Sed haec distinctio rectè explicanda est, ne causa illius, ut sic loquar, inefficaciae quaeratur in absoluto quodam reprobationis decreto, sed in solis hominibus, oblata in Evangelio beneficia amplecti, & vocationi divinae locum dare recusantibus.

Διὰ δόξης καί ἀρετῆς. Vulg. reddidit propriâ gloriâ & virtute. Prosper in Epist. ad Demetriad. & contra Collator. cap. 29. propriâ gloriae virtute. Sed vox ίδίας non habetur in Graeco textu. In paucis Codd. iisque fidei dubiae inventam fuisse hanc lectionem,ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἀρετῇ, memorat Beza in annot. Particulam διὰ quidam censent positam pro πρὸς vel εἰς, ut διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀρετῆς sit idem, quod πρὸς δόξαν καὶ ἀρετὴν, cùm praefixum ב apud Hebraeos significet ἐν, εἰς, πρὸς, διά, περὶ,Rom. 6. v. 4. Existimant igitur, verbis hisce idem significari, quod in proximè praecedentibus per ζωὴν καὶ εὐσέβειαν. Quam enim illic nominaverat ζωὴν, Apostolum hoc loco vocare δόξαν, quamque illic nominaverat εὐσέβειαν, hoc loco vocare ἀρετὴν. Iuxta hanc sententiam exprimeretur his verbis finis vocationis, qui consistit in eo, ut in hac vita bonis operibus ac virtutibus studeamus, & post hanc vitam aeternae gloriae participes reddamur. Eph. 4. v. 1.Ambulate dignè vocatione.

Sed hic προσδιορισμὸς rectiùs refertur ad Deum vocantem, quàm ad homines vocatos, In expositione tamen adhuc quaedam diversitas occurrit.

1. Beda in comm. ad h. l. sic annotat. Propriâ gloriâ & virtute nos vocavit, quia non Angelum ad salvationem nostram, non Arch Angelum misit, non in nobis aliquid meriti boni, pro quo salvaremur, invenit, quin pottus infirmos & inglorios cernens, suâ nos virtute recuperavit & gloriâ.

2. Dionys. Carthus. existimat, insinuare Filium DEIαὐτοπροσώπωςac in propria gloria suae maiestate cum humana Natura coniuncta venisse, ut nos redimeret, ac ad se vocaret. Uterque insistit vulgatae versioni, quae habet propriâ gloriâ & virtute.

3. Quidam per gloriam intelligunt maiestatem illam Christi, de quâ inv. 17. & seqq. agit Apostolus: per potentiam intelligunt virtutem, quam Christus in miraculis demonstravit, per utrumque enim Evangelium, quo vocati sumus confirmavit.

4. Salmeron eodem ferè modo per gloriam & virtutem intelligit Christi divinitatem ac maiestatem, cùm Apostolorum vocatio non fuerit facta sine miraculo, in quo Christi gloria & maiestas splenduit.Luc. 5. v. 10.

5. Idem affert alium sensum, quem priori praefert: Perfecta, inquit, Christi iustitia, quâ conversatus est in terra, & eius gloria, quam viderunt Discipuli ante & post passionem, & in transfiguratione & resurrectione & miraculis eius splendens vocavit Apostolos & per illos omnes. Sed utrique Salmeronis expositioni adversatur, quòd Petrus hic non loquatur de vocatione speciali ad Apostolatum, sed de vocatione generali, & omnibus fidelibus communi ad Christianismum.

6 Quidam & gloriae & virtutis nomen referunt ad Evangelium, quippe quod gloria & virtus Dei dicaturRom. 1. v. 16.2. Cor. 3. v. 8.1. Tim. 1. v. 11.

7. Per virtutem plerique intelligunt DEI potentiam, ut gloria & potentia per usitatum Hebraismum ac figuramένδιαδὺςsit idem, quod gloriosa DEI potentia,ἀρετὴenim in DEO est idem, quodἡ θεία δύναμις, inquit Hesychius.

8. Sed quia δύναμις ab ἀρετῇ significatione differt, cumque vocatio non tam potentiae, quàm gratiae & misericordiae divinae in Scripturis tribuatur, ideo ἀρετῆς nomen rectiùs accipitur sensu eo, quo Petrus in priore Epistola cap. 2. v. 9. illud usurpat, videl. pro Φιλανθρωπία, καὶ Χρηστότητι τοῦ Θεοῦ, ut eam vocat Apostolus, Tit. 3. v. 4. pro DEI benignitate, misericordia & clementia, quam in gratuita vocatione demonstravit. Illam cùm perpetuis laudum praeconiis celebrare debeamus, sicut etiam in loco modo allegato Petrus dicit, quòd virtutes eius, qui nos vocavit ad lumen admirabile, annunciare debeamus, ideò coniungitur ei h. l. δόξα, sensu eo, quòd sit virtus gloriosa, hoc est, perpetuò â nobis glorificanda. Syrus habet nomen [מיתרותא] quo etiam paulò pòst in v. 5. utitur, quando iubemur in fide exhibere virtutem, ubi Dionys.

comméntator annotat, esse hoc nomen generale omnium actionum & operum bonorum.

V 4. Δι' ὧν τὰ μέγιστα ἡμῖν καὶ τίμια ἐπαγγέλματα δεδώρηται.

Δι' ὧν. 1. Quidam Codices Latini habent per quem, qui in Graeco procul dubio legerunt δι'οὗ, quam lectionem innuit Athanasius orat. 2. contra Arian. eamque genuinam censent Lorinus & Cornelius â Lapide in comm. Robertus Stephanus annotavit, unum Codicem habuisseδι' ὅνper quem sc. Christum, in quo omnes DEI promissiones suntναί καί Αμὴν2. Cor. 1. v. 20. 2. Beda in comm. h. l. legit, per quam, (sc. θεοῦ ἐπίγνωσιν) ex quo colligit, quòd quantò quis perfectiùs DEUM cognoscit, tantò altiùs promissorum eius magnitudinem sentiat. Eodem modo etiam legit Ambrosius, vel potiùs Prosper Epist. 33. ad Demetriadem. 3. Sed unius Codicis, vel etiam paucorum Codicum lectio pluribus ac probatioribus Codicibus non est praeferenda. Illi verò habent δι' ὧνper quae, sc. gloriam & virtutem suam Deus maxima & preciosa promissa nobis donavit h. e. φιλανθρωπία & benignitas Deum impulit, ut maxima & preciosa nobis donaret.

Verbum δεδώρηται Erasmus accipit passivè, sed rectiùs accipitur activè, quo modò etiam Vulg. reddidit, ut referatur ad DEUM vocantem, cuius in vers. proximè praecedente facta erat mentio.

Per τὰ ἐπαγγέλματα μετωνυμικῶς intelliguntur bona promissa, propriè enim loquendo non donantur promissiones, sed bona quae promissa fuerunt, sic Hebr. 10. v. 26.reportare promissiones, est reportare bona promissa. Sunt autem bona illa promissa, dona spiritualia & caelestia, quae iuxta promissionem Patribus in V. T. factam, ac per Prophetas toties repetitam, Filius DEI in suo adventu & incarnatione allaturus erat, quae sunt generis humani redemtio, reconciliatio cum Deo, peccatorum remissio, in filios Dei adoptio, iustitiae & vitae aeternae donatio, 2. Cor. 1. v. 20.1. Iohan. 2. v. 25. non quòd in V. T. illorum beneficiorum nemo per fidem factus fuerit particeps, cuius contrarium vel solum Abrahae exemplum ostendit, Rom. 4. v. 1. & seqq. sed quia Filius Dei in assumta carne per suam passionem & mortem in N. demùm Test. ea promeruit, passio autem illa Christi profuit, antequam fuit. Syrus reddidit, per quae[שוודעא]cognitiones magnas, & honores vobis dedit. Sed Pococke in comm. monet, scribendum esse[שוודיא]promissiones, cùm ex unius solùm lineolae productione facilis hic fuerit Scribae lapsus. Dicuntur haec ἐπαγγέλματα h. e. promissa bona μέγιστα καί τίμια, respectu habito ad temporalia & corporalia beneficia, de quibus itidem promissiones divinae extant, sed quae cum hisce spiritualibus, caelestibus & aeternis beneficiis nullo modo comparandae.

Ἵνα διὰ τούτων γένηθαι θείας κοινωνοί φύσεως. Exprimitur his verbis finis maximorum istorum, & preciosorum promissorum, qui est θείας φύσεως κοινωνία. Διά τούτων ἐπαγγελμάτων per illa promissa opere ipso impleta & praestita. Lutherus ad totam orationem praecedentem refert, sic reddens, durch dasselbe. In verbo γένηθε transit Apostolus â persona prima, quâ in praecedentibus usus fuerat, ad personam secundam, quod non caret emphasi. Ne quis enim existimaret, solos Apostolos huius honoris & beneficii participes factos, ideo notanter dicit Petrus, credentes, ad quos scribit, ad eiusdem honoris & beneficii consortium pervenisse. Beda in comm. h. l. Mutat repentè personam, quod non fortuitò, sed providenter agit. Ideo, inquit, Dominus nobis, qui Naturâ Iudaei, qui sub lege sumus nati, qui magisterio ipsius & corporaliter imbuti omnia divinae virtutis suae secreta reseravit; ideò nobis, suis videlicet discipulis maxima & preciosa Spiritus sui promissa donavit, ut per haec etiam vos, qui ex gentibus estis, qui eum corporaliter videre nequivistis, divinae suae Naturae donaret esse participes, nobis sc. vos quae ab ipso audivimus docentibus, vos per eius mysteria consecrantibus. In quo verò consistat illa τῆς θείας φύσεως κοινωνία, in quaest. paulò pòst explicabitur.

Ἀποφυγόντες τῆς ἐν κόσμῳ ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ φθορᾶς. Participium ἀποφυγόντες, quidam vertunt conditionaliter, si effugeritis, quomodo etiam Lutherus reddidit, so ihr fliehet die vergängliche Lust. Illi enim demum sunt & manent divinae Naturae consortes, qui fugiunt corruptionem, quae per pravam concupiscentiam in mundo dominatur, quâ ratione Petrus idem diceret, quod Iohannes 1. Epist. 1. v. 5.Deus lux est & tenebrae non sunt in eo ullae,v. 6.si dixerimus, quòdκοινωνίανhabeamus cum ipso, & in tenebris ambulamus, mentimur,v. 7.Si autem in luce ambulamus, sicut ipse in luce est,κοινωνίανhabemus ad invicem. Deus est summa puritas, mundicies incorruptibilis. Si dixerimus a. quòd κοινωνίαν habeamus cum ipso, & corruptis ac pravis carnis concupiscentiis cum mundo indulgemus, mentimur. Si autem fugiamus eius, quae in mundo est, concupiscentiae corruptionem, sicut & ipse purus est & incorruptus, κοινωνίαν habemus ad invicem.

Sed rectiùs dicitur, τό ἀποφυγόντες h. l. non tàm conditionaliter & hypotheticè, quàm assertivè & categoricè vertendum esse, hoc modo: Cùm effugeritis, vel postquam effugistis concupiscentiae corruptionem, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit, [כד ערקין]cùm fugeritis corruptionem concupiscentiarum. Apostolus enim nondum versatur in exhortando, sed in praedicando divina beneficia, ex qua praedicatione postea demum exhortationem infert. Docet igitur, per illam τῆς θείας φύσεως κοινωνίαν, hoc beneficium credentibus in Christum obtigisse, quòd effugerint carnis & mundi concupiscentias, quibus postea cap. 2. v. 19. opponit eos, qui sunt δοῦλοι τῆς φθορᾶς & v. 20. qui inquinationibus mundi, quas effugerant, iterum sunt impliciti.

Per φθορὰν 1. Quidam intelligunt interitum seu exitium, cùm videatur Apostolus bina binis opponere voluisse, nimirùmφθορὰν τῇ ζωῇ, καί τῇ δόξῃ, ἐπιθυμίανveròεὐσεβείᾳ καί ἀρετὴin v. 3.quo sensu etiamφθορᾶςnomen accipiendum esse putant cap. 2. huius Epist. v. 19.

2. Quidam existimant, perφθορὰνhîc intelligi turpitudinem illam, quâ per foedas & illicitas libidines humana Natura dehonestatur, ac corrupitur, cùm haec Epistola Simoni Mago, & eius sectatoribus, foedas & spurcas carnis libidines permittentibus imò docentibus sit opposita.

3. Sed rectiùs dicitur, per φθορὰν in genere intelligi universum pravae concupiscentiae genus, ut ostendit additum vocabulum ἐπιθυμίας. Neque enim solùm â foedis libidinibus, sed ab omnibus carnis operibus sedulò caveant, caveri certè debent, qui per fidem in Christum ὑιοθεσίας participes facti, ac per Spiritum Sanctum sunt renati & renovati, Gal. 5, v. 24. Qui Christi sunt, crucifixerunt carnem cum affectibus & ἐπιθυμίαις. Hanc generalem φθορᾶς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ corruptionis in concupiscentiâ h. e. corruptae & pravae concupiscentiae significationem probat locus parallelus c. 2, v. 19. & 20. Postquam enim dixerat, pseudo doctores illos, de quibus agit, esse δούλους τῆς φθορᾶς, ἐξηγητικῶς subiicit, eos implicariμιάσμασιinquinamentis mundi, quae effugerant.

Voculam φθορᾶς cum ἐπιθυμίᾳ coniunctam, quidam accipiunt passivè, utφθορὰ ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳsit idem, quodφθαρτικὴ ἐπιθυμίαcorruptibilis ac citò transitura concupiscentia Luth. die vergängliche Lust. Sed rectiùs accipitur activè, pro concupiscentia hominem corrumpente ac perdente, si frena illi securè laxentur. Illud ἐν κόσμῳ ideò additur, quia pravae illae concupiscentiae hominibus carnalibus & mundanis dominantur, cùm per Spiritum illis minimè resistant. Nec absurdè cogitatur, simul respectum haberi ad voculam καλέσαντος in v. praeced. Quia enim pii electi & vocati sunt de mundo,Iohan. 10, v. 19. ideò non ampliùs sectantur pravas concupiscentias, quae in mundo dominantur, & quibus homines mundani securè indulgent.

Quaeritur hoc loco, quid per illamτῆς θείας φύσεως κοινωνίανApostolus intelligat; Resp. 1. Verè credentes dicuntur Naturae divinae consortes, ratione renovationis ac novarum qualitatum, quas Spiritus Sanctus in cordibus eorum efficit, ac per eas amissam, per lapsum, divinam imaginem in illis restaurat. Postquam enim dixerat Apostolus, ut efficiamini divinae Naturae consortes, subiungit, fugientes eam, quae in mundo est, concupiscentiae corruptionem. Nimirum renovationi Spiritus opponuntur prava carnis desideria, pravae concupiscentiae, quae per Spiritum in renatis sunt mortificandae, ut divinae Naturae consortes maneant. De hac interiore piorum renovatione loquuntur haec dicta Apostolica. 2. Corinth. 4. vers. 16.Interior noster homo de die in diem renovatur.Ephes. 4. vers. 23.Renovamini Spiritu mentis vestrae.vers. 24. Et induite novum hominem, qui secundùm Deum creatus est in iustitia & sanctitate veritatis.Coloss. 3, vers. 9.expoliantes veterem hominem cum actibus suisvers. 10.& induentes novum eum, qui renovatur in agnitionem, secundùm imaginem eius, qui creavit illum. Atque haec est illa DEI conformitas & Christi formitas, de qua pii veteres toties loquuntur, quae non consistit in essentiali quadam substantiae nostrae, in DEI vel Christi Naturam, conversione, sed in qualitatum mutatione, & imaginis divinae instauratione. Dionysius de caelesti Hierarch. cap. 1. ἡ σωτηρία οὐχ ἑτέρως γενέσθαι δύναται μὴ θεουμένων τῶν σωζομένων, ἡ δὲ θέωσις ἐστὶν ἡ πρὸς θεὸν, ὡς ἐφικτὸν, ἀφομοίωσις τὲ καὶ ἕνωσις. Interpres Dionysii reddidit cum Deo commistio, sed in Graeco nihil de mistione habetur. Basilius hom. 10. in hexaëm. Τὶς ἔστι Χριστιανισμὸς; θεοῦ ὁμοίωσις κατὰ τὸ ἐνδεχόμενον ἁνθρώπου φύσει Niceph. lib. 1. Histor. Eccles. cap. 22. Quemadmodum omni Doctori ille finis propositus est, ut discipulum, quoad eius fieri potest, disciplinae communicatione sibi reddat persimilem: Sic Christo constitutum est, quantum humana per mittit fragilitas, unumquemque per Evangelium ad se accedentem, sibi ipsi conformare, atque ita conformatos filios exhibere Patri. Quantum quisque habet Christi formitatis, sive cum Christo conformitatis, tantum habet verae Christianitatis.

Praeter hanc interiorem verè piorum renovationem, respexit Apostolus 2. ad Filii Dei incarnationem, quae in Vet. Test. per Prophetas promissa, ac proinde μέγιστον καὶ τίμιον ἐπάγγελμα meritò censetur. Per eam verè facti sumus θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως, quia Filius DEI, qui iuxta assumtam carnem nobis factus όμοούσιος, in personae unitate est verus Deus, Patri caelesti iuxta suam Deitatem όμοούσιος, inde dicimur caro de carne eius, & os de ossibus eius,Ephes. 5, vers. 3. Naturae consanguinitate ac proximâ carnis propinquitate ipsi coniuncti, sicut fratres Iosephi de fratre dicunt. Caro nostra est,Gen. 27, v. 37. Iren. lib. 5. cap. 1. p. 316. Filius DEI propter immensam dilectionem factus est quod nos sumus, ut nos perficeret, quod est ipse. Gregor. Nazianz. orat. 38. f. 620. πτωχεύει τὴν ἑμὴν σάρκα, ἳνα ἑγὼ πλουτήσω τὴν αὐτοῦ θεότητα.Carnis meae paupertatem subit, ut ego divinitatis ipsius opes consequar. Athanasius orat. 5. contra Arian. pag. 103. DEUS factus est homo, ut nos in seipso Deificaret, quod ipsum repetit in Ecclesia ad Adelphium contra Arianos pag. 333. Ambrosius lib. 5. de fide cap. 5. CHRISTUS nostrae fragilitatis in carne se praebuit consortem, ut nos in virtute sua divinae faceret Naturae consortes. Idem Epist. 38. docet, consortes divinae Naturae nos fieri per Christum, in Christo enim Natura nostra facta est consors divinae, quia eidem unita est arctissimè in eadem hypostasi Verbi. Augustinus lib. 9. de Civ. Dei cap. 15. Beatus & beatificus DEUS factus particeps humanitatis nostrae, compendium praebuit participandae divinitatis suae. lib. 21. de C. D. cap. 15. Unicus Naturâ DEI Filius, propter nos, misericordiâ factus est filius hominis, ut nos Naturâ filii hominis, filii DEI per illum gratiâ fieremus. cap. 16. Factus est particeps mortalitatis nostrae, ut nos participes faceret divinitatis suae. serm. 9. de temp. Factus est DEUS homo, ut homo fieret DEUS. Anshelmus lib. de excell. Virg. Mariae cap. 12. Ad hoc DEUS noster factus est frater noster, ut quemadmodum ipse dignatus est consors fieri nostrae humanitatis: sic nos mereamur consortes fieri suae divinitatis.

3. Ad gratuitam in filios Dei adoptionem. Si illi dicuntur genus Dei,Act. 17. v. 29. h. e. generis divini consortes, qui â Deo creati sunt homines rationales, intelligendi & volendi facultate praediti, quantò magis divinae Naturae, suo modo, consortes dici possunt, qui sunt ex Deo nati.1. Ioh. 4. v. 7.& in filios Dei adoptatiIoh. 1, v. 9. De Magistratu dicitur Psal. 82, v. 6.Ego dixi, Dii estis & filii excelsi omnes. ubi Dii dicuntur, qui sunt filii Dei, & ad quos sermo Dei factus.Ioh. 10. v. 35. quantò igitur magis illi possunt dici Dii h. e. divinae Naturae consortes, qui per fidem in Christum, facti sunt DEI filii, & coheredes Christi, sicque participant Naturam DEI, quomodo filii participant Naturam patris. Sicut Deus, cum produxit Adamum, quem Locas vocat Dei filium cap. 3. v. ult. inspiravit in faciem eius, & dedit ei vitam humanam ac animalem,Gen. 2. v. 7. sic cùm aliquem in filium recipit, participem eum facit vitae Spiritualis, quae est ex DEO,Ephes. 4. v. 18. ac communicat ei divinas quasdam proprietates, & ius ad omnem DEI hereditatem. Donatus nobis est Christus cum omni suo merito, ac cum beneficiis suis omnibus, per quae acceptâ iustitiâ imputatâ, adoptione in filios, regeneratione Spiritus Sancti ex vita aeterna ex filiis irae reddimur filii gratiae, & ad imaginem DEI transformamur. Inde Ambros. lib. 1. de Spiritu Sancto c. 6. locum hunc Apostolicum exponit, de spirituali commercio adoptionis gratiae, quod per Spiritum Sanctum fiat in nobis.

4. Ad spiritualem cum Christo unionem. Ad eam itidem applicari potest dictum Apostolicum, Ephes. 5. v. 30.membra sumus corporis eius, de carne eius, & de ossibus eius. Ut enim Adamus de coniuge divinitus sibi adducta dicit Gen. 2. v. 23.Haec est caro de carne mea & os de ossibus meis: ita Paulus typum ad antitypum applicans, verbis hisce spiritualem & arctissimam Christi & Ecclesiae unionem exprimit, ad Ecclesiam autem pertinent omnes credentes, tanquam vera & viva illius membra. Formale istius unionis non consistit in eo, quòd Christus iuxta assumtam Naturam humanam sit nobis όμοούσιος, cùm hoc beneficium sit omnibus hominibus commune, contrà verò mystica unio sit verè credentium duntaxat propria: sed in eo, quòd Christus per fidem nos sibi inserit, filios DEI, membra corporis sui mystici, ac heredes vitae aeternae efficit, adeoque incarnationis & passionis suae fructum nobis applicat, sicut testantur dicta. Iohann. 14, v. 23.Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, & Pater meus diliget & eum, ad eum veniemus, & mansionem apud eum faciemus.1. Cor. 6, v. 15.Nescitis, quoniam corpora vestra membra sunt Christi.Galat. 2, v. 20.Christus in me vivit.Eph. 3, v. 17.Christus per fidem habitat in cordibus nostris. Theophylactus in cap. 14. Iohann. In vobis sum, ut caput in membris; & vos in me, sicut membrae in capite. Simon de Cassia lib. 12. in Evangel. cap. 3. Sumus in Christo in unitate fidei, dilectionis & gratiae, velut rami in arbore, radii in Sole. rivi in fonte, membra sub uno capite. Lutherus in comm: h. l. Tom. 2. Germ. Ien. f. 395. Quid est Natura DEI? aeterna veritas, iustitia, sapientia, aeterna vita, pax, gaudium & voluptas, & quicquid boni nominari potest. Qui ergo Naturae divinae particeps fit, ille haec omnia consequitur, ut vivat in aeternum, ut aeternam pacem, gaudium & voluptatem obtineat, ut sit mundus, iustus & omnipotens contra Diabolum, peccatum & mortem. Quemadmodum DEO non potest hoc auferri, quo minùs sit aeterna vita, & veritas aeterna: ita quoque per fidem Christo unitis vita aeterna eripi nequit. Nemo potest pios opprimere, nisi Deum ipsum opprimat.

5. Ad gratio sam Spiritus Sancti inhabitationem.1. Cor: 3, v. 16.Nescitis, quia templum DEI estis, & Spiritus DEI habitat in vobis?1. Cor. 6. v. 19. An nescitis, quòd corpus vestrum sit templum Spiritus sancti, qui in vobis est? Spiritus Sanctus non est separatus â donis suis sanctificantibus, sed in templo illo, quòd donis suis exornat, etiam ipse habitat. Cùm ergo Spiritus Sanctus sit unus verus cum Patre & Filio Deus, ideò etiam per gratiosam illam Spiritus Sancti inhabitationem Naturae divinae consortes reddimur. 1. Cor. 6. v. 17.Qui Domino adhaeret, est unus Spiritus cum eo, est DEO unitus per Spiritum Sanctum, ac regitur â Spiritu Sancto,1. Iohann. 3, v. 24.In hoc scimus, quoniam manet in nobis, ex Spiritu, quem dedit nobis,cap. 4, vers. 3.In hoc cognoscimus, quoniam in eo manemus, & ipse in nobis, quoniam de Spiritu suo dedit nobis. Irenaeus lib. 5. cap. 2. pag. 317. Dominus effudit Spiritum Patris in adunitionem & communicationem DEI & hominum, ad homines quidem deponens DEUM per Spiritum, ad DEUM autem rursus imponens hominem per suam incarnationem. Basilius in homil. de Spiritu Sancto dicit, sanctos propter inhabitantem Spiritum Sanctum esse Deos, atque inde probat, Spiritum Sanctum esse DEUM per essentiam. Necesse est, inquit, divinum esse Spiritum, & ex DEO esse, qui Diis divinitatis est causa. Athanasius in Dial. 1. de S. Trinit. Reddimur divinae Naturae participes ex eo, quòd Spiritum Sanctum participamus. Si autem ex participatione Spiritus Sancti evadimus divinâ Naturâ praediti, nonne multò magis est divinae Naturae Spiritus ille, qui haec in nobis efficit. Ambrosius lib. 1. de Spiritu Sancto cap. 6. Quis audeat dicere, discretum â DEO Patre & Christo esse Spiritum Sanctum, cum per ipsum ad imaginem & similitudinem DEI esse mereamur, & per ipsum fiat, quemadmodum Petrus Apostolus dixit, ut divinae simus consortes Naturae, in quo utique non carnalis successionis hereditas est, sed adoptionis gratiae Spirituale commercium.

6. Ad corporis & sanguinis Christi in Eucharistia communicationem. Christus corpus & sanguinem suum non solùm spiritualiter, sed etiam Sacramentaliter in Eucharistia nobis manducandum & bibendum exhibet, ut nos sibi arctissimè coniungat. 1. Cor. 10, v. 16.Panis, quem frangimus, nonne estκοινωνίαcorporis Christi, Poculum, cui benedicimus, nonne estκοινωνίαSanguinis Christi? Quia verò Filius DEI hoc suum corpus, quod mediante pane manducandum, & hunc suum sanguinem, quem mediante vino in Eucharistia bibendum nobis exhibet, in divinae suae personae sublimitatem evexit, ideò etiam hac corporis & sanguinis Christi κοινωνίᾳ per veram fidem factâ θείας φύσεως κοινωνία efficimur. Cyrillus Hierosolym. Catech. mystag. 4. SicΧριστοφόροιerimus, cùm eius corpus & sanguinem in membra nostra receperimus, atque divinae Naturae consortes efficiemur. Cyrillus Alexandr. lib. 6. in Iohann. cap. 17. Perinde ac si quis liquefactae cerae aliam ceram infuderit, alteram cum altera per totum commiscet: ita necesse est, si quis carnem & sanguinem Domini recipit, cum ipso coniungi, ut Christus cum eo, & ipse cum Christo inveniatur. lib. 10. cap. 13. Non negamus, recta nos fide, caritateque sincerâ Christo spiritualiter coniungi, sed nullam nobis coniunctionis rationem, secundùm carnem cum illo esse, id profectò pernegamus, idque â divinis scripturis alienum dicimus. ibid. Communicatione corporis & sanguinis Christi ipse est in nobis & nos in ipso. Gelasius in lib. adv. Eutych. & Nestor. ideò panem & vinum Eucharisticum dicit in divinam transire substantiam, quod per ea divinae Naturae consortes efficiamur, communicato nobis corpore & sanguine Christi.

7. Ad arctissimam cum DEO in vita aeterna coniunctionem. Obscura illa & imperfecta DEI cognitio, quae in hac vita per verbum, & Spiritus Sancti illummationem nobis obtingit, hoc efficit, ut cum ipso dicamur habere κοινωνίαν1. Ioh. 1. v. 6. Quanto igitur intuitiva DEI visio, quae clarissimam & perfectissimam DEI cognitionem complectitur, in κοινωνίαν longè uberiorem & arctiorem cum DEO nos reponet. unde manifestationem illam, quae in vita aeterna sequitur, Christus exponit per μονὴν sive mansionem Patris caelestis, adeoque totius Sacrosanctae Trinitatis in electis Ioh. 14, v. 23. quò etiam pertinet dictum Apostolicum 1. Ioh. 3, v. 2.Cùm apparuerit in gloria sua, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum, sicut est. Nazianzenus orat. 4. De Theolog. Non erimus ampliùs, ut in hac vita,οὐδὲν ὅλως θεοῦ ἣ ὁλίγοι ἐν ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς φέροντεςnihil omnino DEI aut parum in nobis habentes,ἀλλ'ὅλοι θεοειδεῖς, ὅλου θεοῦ χωρητικοὶ καὶ μόνουtoti DEO similes & conformes, totiusque DEI capaces. Idem orat. 42. dicit, hominem divinitatem consequi, ut claritatem DEI videat. uti Nicetas. Deificatio omnis actionis & contemplationis est terminus. ubi per Deificationem intelligit Dei visionem. Idem in orat. funebri ad Patrem ὅπου γενόμενοι θεός αὐτός (ἵνα τολμήσεις ἔπω) χόντες ὅλην τῆς ἁγίας Τριάδος τὴν ἔλλαμψιν. Ioh. Huss. in 1. Ioh. 3. Tunc erimus Dii participatione, non consortio aequalitatis, sed participationis per gratiam in hoc, per gloriam in futuro seculo.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Si divina virtus omnia, quae ad vitam & pietatem pertinent, nobis donavit, ergò nihil ex nobis & viribus nostris, in rebus ad salutem nostram pertinentibus, operari possumus 2. Cor. 3. v. 5. Inde Prosper in Epist. ad Demetr. & contra Collatorem cap. 29. ex voce δεδωρημένης colligit, omnia, quae pietatis sunt, etiam ipsa virtutum semina, esse gratuita Dei dona. Nunquid, ait, qui virtutum semina, quae naturaliter habemus inserta, opitulatione suâ excitavit in nobis? sed, ait, qui nunc omnia nobis, quae ad vitam, & pietatem pertinent, donavit, quod dicendo cuius virtutis initium in Natura posuit, quod non ab eo collatum sit, qui cuncta donavit. Opponendum hoc Pontificiorum merito de congruo.

2. Apostolus in vers. 3. fidem definit per ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Notandum hoc contra Bellarmin. qui lib. 1. de Iustif. cap. 7. disputat, fidem meliùs definiri per ignorantiam, quàm per notitiam, Atqui ἐπίγνωσις non est ignorantia, sed cognitio ac notitia. Estius in h. l. per agnitionem Filii, id est, per fidem, quâ in eum credimus. Lorinus ad v. 14. huius cap. Non ignoro, de fide ipsa nomen scientiae nonnunquam dici.

3. Corruptio mundi non est extra nos, sed in nobis, quia concupiscentia prava est in nobis. Rom. 7. v. 18.Iac. 1. v. 14. Ergo per secessum in Monasterium non effugimus illam, quae in mundo est, concupiscentiam.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Beza in annot. ad v. 4. Perθείαν φύσιν negat intelligi ipsam Deiοὐσίαν,sed per eam certas qualitates intelligendas esse dicit, quas virtus Dei in nobis efficit. Existimat insuper, eos, qui credentes ipsius divinae Naturae consortes esse factos dicunt, erroribus Serveti patrocinari, qui quandam divinae essentiae in pios transfusionem imaginatus est. Piscator in Schol. h. l. itidem per θείαν φύσιν intelligit divinas animi qualitates, referentes Naturam Dei, videl. caelestem sapientiam & sanctitatem. Resp. 1. Etiam ipsi non solùm Serveti transfusionem, quâ DEI substantiam mutabilem, & rerum omnium partem facit, sed etiam Weigel. & Methistarum somnia, quibus essentialem quandam animarum, quin & corporum nostrorum in divinam Naturam conversionem introducunt, repudiandam ac damnandam iudicamus, dicentes ex Cypriano serm. de Cen. Dom. Nostra & ipsius coniunctio nec miscet personas, nec unit substantias (per essentialem quandam conversionem vel transfusionem) sed affectus consociat & confoederat voluntates. Apostolus dicit Ephes. 3. v. 17.Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus nostris. Atqui nec inhabitans in habitaculum, nec habitaculum in inhabitantem mutatur. Unio duarum Naturarum personalis in Christo nullam introducit mutationem essentialem, quanto minus spiritualis unio transmutationem unitorum inferet? 2. Concedimus & hoc, divinae Naturae consortes nos dici, ratione renovationis & novarum qualitatum, quas Spiritus Sanctus in cordibus nostris efficit. 3. Sed quòd praeter illam renovationem, & imaginis divinae instaurationem, nihil aliud in hoc l. Apostolico per κοινωνίας θείαν φύσεως intelligatur, hoc verò negamus. Contrarium enim ex dictis patet.

2. Socinus in animad. Posnan. Defens. p. 136. sic scribit. Sumusκοινωνοὶdivinae Naturae, vel certè aliquando futuri tales, tunc videlicet, cùm beatâ immortalitate donabimur in resurrectione iustorum, propter quam etiam filii DEI erimus.Luc. 20. vers. 36. Resp. κοινωνία illa non solùm in vita aeterna, sed etiam in hac vita credentibus obtingit, ut docet tùm hic noster locus, tùm dictum Apostolicum 1. Cor. 1. vers. 9.Fidelis DEUS, per quem vocati estisεἰς κοινωνίανFilii eius.1. Iohann. 1. v. 3. ut κοινωνίαnostra sit cum DEO & cum Filio eius Iesu Christov. 27.Si in luce ambulamus, sicut ipse in luce est,κοινωνίαhabemus mutuam (Idem iudicandum de eo, quod Ambros. Epist. 38. hoc consortium divinae Naturae accipit de rationalis Naturae dono, quodque Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovin. per virginitatem nos divinae Naturae consortes fieri asserit. Atqui κοινωνία illa θαίας φύσεως est & solorum & omnium verè fidelium.)

3. Quidam tempore Gersonis imaginati sunt, se per contemplationem ita uniri DEO, ut reipsa ipsorum Natura in abysso profundo divinitatis submergatur, puta humanitas annihiletur & tota transeat in divinitatem, cui opinioni gemellus est error Methisticus de essentiali nostra cum Christo unione. Atqui aliud est κοινωνία, aliud μεταποιΐα.

4. Andreas Osiander ex hac divinae Naturae κοινωνίᾳ inferre voluit, nos iustificari iustitiâ DEI essentiali in nobis habitante. Resp. Quòd divinae Naturae consortes efficiamur, Petrus dicit; sed quòd divinae Naturae consortio & inhabitatione iustitiae essentialis coram DEO iustificemur, hoc non est doctrina Petri, sed glossa Osiandri.

5. Quidam Pontificii ex hoc loco invocationem sanctorum statuminare conantur, concludentes hoc modo. Qui divinae Naturae sunt consortes, illi etiam cultus divini, religiosae scil. invocationis meritò consortes censentur. Atqui sancti defuncti sunt divinae Naturae consortes. Ergo. Resp. 1. ipsimet Pontificii videri nolunt, quod sanctis defunctis tribuant cultum merè divinum, sed humano ac civili maiorem, divino autem inferiorem sive intermedium, ut loquitur Bellarminus; vel cultum externum, ut loquitur Costerus. 2. Petrus de sanctis in terra viventibus testatur, quod divinae Naturae per Christum consortes sint facti. Quòd si ergo ex illa θειας φύσεως κοινωνιά inferri posset religiosae invocationis cultus, consequens foret, sanctos in terris adhuc viventes religiosè invocari posse. 3. Pii dicuntur divinae Naturae consortes, non quòd sint Dii per participationem, ut loquitur Bellarmin. de beat. sanct. cap. 9. sed per regenerationem, renovationem, adoptionem in filios, imaginis divinae instaurationem, gratiosam Dei inhabitationem &c. ut superiùs ostendimus.

6. Bellarminus lib. 2. de iustif. cap. 5. statuit, divinae Naturae nos consortes fieri per caritatem, utpote per quam reddamur DEI filii, qui autem sunt DEI filii, illi sunt divinae Naturae consortes. Illud se evincere posse putat ex duobus Scripturae dictis 1. Iohann. 3. v. 1.Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis DEUS, ut filii DEI nominemur & simus!cap. 4. v. 7.Caritas ex DEO est & omnis qui diligit, ex DEO natus est & cognoscit DEUM.v. 8.Qui non diligit, non novit DEUM, quoniam DEUS caritas est. Resp. 1. concedimus, caritatem pertinere ad illam θείας φύσεως κοινωνίαν, de qua Apostolus agit. Pertinet enim ad renovationem & imaginis divinae instaurationem, in qua θείας φύσεως κοινωνίαν consistere, superiùs diximus. 2. Concedimus & hoc, quòd adoptio in filios sive υἱοθεσία pertineat ad illam θείας φύσεως κοινωνίαν, uti itidem superiùs monuimus.

3. Negamus verò, per caritatem nos reddi DEI filios, quia caritas non est υἱοθεσίας causa, sed potiùs signum & effectum. 1. Iohann. 3. v. 14.Scimus, quoniam translati sumus â morte ad vitam, quia fratres diligimus. Fidei Scriptura hoc tribuit, quòd sit υἱοθεσίας medium. Iohann. 1. v. 12.Quotquot receperunt eum, dedit illis potestatem filios DEI fieri, his qui credunt in nomen eius.Gal. 3. v. 26.Omnes filii DEI estis per fidem in Christo Iesu. 4. in loco 1. Iohann. 3. vers. 1. non agitur de caritate, quâ nos diligimus Deum, sed de caritate, quâ Deus nos diligit. 1. Iohann. 4. vers. 7. Caritas non statuitur causa regenerationis ex DEO & υἱοθεσίας, sed eius signum & effectus.

7. Lorinus Ies. in hunc locum sic commentatur. Probatur ex hoc loco, iustitiam nostram esse donum permanens & internum, sicut & nomen Naturae significat non solam externam denominationem vel non imputationem: inde est, quòd iustificatio dicitur regeneratio,Tit. 3. v. 5.& nova creaturaGalat. 6. vers. 15.Iacob. 1. vers. 18. Resp. Quod Bellarminus lib. 2. de Iustif. cap. 5. Osiandro, ex hoc loco evincere conanti, nos iustificari per illam iustitiam, quâ Christus non ut homo, sed ut DEUS essentialiter iustus est, respondet, idipsum etiam Lorino opponere possumus. Apostolus Petrus dicit, nos divinae Naturae consortes fieri, sed per illud consortium divinae Naturae nos coram DEO iustificari, non est sententia Petri, sed glossa Lorini; perinde ut Bellarminus scribit, Apostolus non dicit, nos effici divinae consortes per inhabitationem iustitiae essentialis, haec enim est glossae Osiandri, non sententia Petri. Manifestum est ex textu, Apostolum hîc non loqui de gratiâ iustificante vel iustificationis modo, sed de dono, per gratiam, & iustificationis consequente.

8. Salmero ex v. 4. colligit, nos non futuros divinae Naturae consortes sine nostra voluntate & cooperatione. Resp. loquitur Apostolus de renatis, qui per Spiritum divinitus sibi datum & possunt & debent carnis concupiscentias mortificare.

Observat. I. Per cognitionem Christi, h. e. per veram in Christum fidem omnia, quae ad vitam & pietatem spectant, nobis donantur.

2. Vocatio est opus gloriosae Dei gratiae. 2. Tim. 1. v. 9. Deus gloriam suam miserendo & vocando, potentiam parcendo maximè demonstrat.

3. Ut Paulus Eph. 1. v. 19. & 20. potentiam DEI in collatione fidei celebrat: ita Petrus divinae potentiae collationem beneficiorum spiritualium tribuit.

4. Fides est donum DEI gratuitum, non â meritis vel viribus hominum profectum.

5. Leo serm. de nativ. Agnosce, ô Christiane, dignitatem tuam; & divinae consors factus Naturae noli in veterem vilitatem degeneri conversatione recidere. Memento, cuius capitis & corporis sis membrum. Reminiscere, quia erutus de potestate tenebrarum translatus es in DEI lumen & regnum; per Baptismatis Sacramentum Spiritus Sancti factus es templum; noli tantum habitatorem pravis de te actibus effugere & Diaboli te iterum subiicere servituti, quia precium tuum sanguis CHRISTI.

6. Beda in comm. h. l. Bene dicit, concupiscentiam mundi habere corruptionem, ideoque fugiendam esse, quia est & incorruptibilis concupiscentia, de qua canitur. Concupivit & deficit anima mea in atria Domini.

7. Prava concupiscentia fons est tùm corruptionis mortuorum, tùm exitii & interitus aeterni.

8. Ambrosius lib. 10. Epist. 84. Si omnia, quae ad vitam & pietatem pertinent, DEUS nobis divinâ suâ virtute donavit, nihil magis fugiendum est, quàm appetitus huius concupiscentiae, quae virtutem negat divini operis amore propriae dignitatis. Et cùm aliae cupiditates ea tantum bona, quibus adversantur, imminuant, haec dum omnia ad se trahit, simul universa corrumpit. Loquitur autem Ambrosius in specie de superbia.

## 1:5-7
Connection. From the preaching of divine benefits as well as promises, both of which are by far the most ample, the Apostle now deduces an exhortation to constancy and progress, both in faith and in the pursuit of piety: therefore, the general proposition of the whole Epistle is contained in these three verses.

Disposition. In this exhortation the Apostle: 1. enumerates by degrees those virtues to the progress of which he exhorts those to whom he writes. 2. confirms his exhortation with several arguments.

Exposition of the text. Καί αὐτό τοῦτο δέ σπουδὴν πᾶσαν παρεισενέγκαντες. Those who take the particle ὡς in v. 3. as a particle of comparison, in this place ἀνανταπόδοτον they supply that through the particle οὕτως, in this way: Just as GOD has honored you with many and great benefits: so it is right that you in turn honor Him with duties and obsequies. But we have warned above that the particle ὡς is more correctly rendered there as after, since.

Concerning the words, αὐτό τοῦτο the particle περί, or κατά, or πρός, is to be understood, so that the sense may be: And indeed, bringing in all solicitude to this very thing, or applying every effort. Caietanus, Gagneius, and Cornelius â Lapide also understand the word ποιεῖτε. And do this very thing, namely, with all care and diligence applied. But the former exposition is simpler.

The preposition παρὰ in the participle παρεισενέγκαντες seems to some to have respect to that gift of GOD, of which mention was made in v. 3. & 4. so that the sense may be: Besides that gift of GOD, you also bring every effort to the preservation and increase of those gifts, concerning which matter we shall see what is to be determined in ἐκδικήσει. The Syriac interpreter seems to have taken the word παρεισενέγκαντες likewise as ἀποφυγέντες in the preceding verse indicatively, categorically, and assertively, for he rendered it thus: And furthermore, when you have introduced all diligence to this very thing. But the word ἐπιχορηγήσατε, by which this participle is governed shows that the Apostle in this place is not indicating what they have done, but is exhorting to that which they ought to do. Ἐπιχορηγήσατε ἐν τῇ πιστει ὑμῶν τὴν ἀρετὴν. The word ἐπιχορηγεῖν signifies to supply, to subminister, to add, likewise to supply even more, to suggest, to provide. 2. Cor. 9. v. 10. ἐπιχορηγῶν σπέρμα τῷ σπείραντι. Gal. 3. v. 5. ἐπιχορηγῶν ἡμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα. The Syrian rendered it by [אוסף] he added, Luther, reichet dar.

Robertus Stephanus teaches that the preposition ἐν is not found in certain Codices, by which reasoning the sense would be. Supply to faith virtue. But the more approved Codices have it added. Moreover, ἐν is placed for εἰς, so that the sense may be, Add to your faith virtue. Vatablus thinks, it is a Hebraism to say in faith for of faith, and thus also the particle ἐν in the following should be translated, to virtue knowledge, but examples of this Hebraism are deservedly desired.

The little word ἀρετὴν the Syrian rendered by [מיתרותא] which. Some render it by abundance, since [יתר] among other things signifies, he abounded. The sense therefore would be, that they ought to grow daily in faith, just as he says in cap. 3. v. 18. Grow in the knowledge of Christ. But Pococke rightly warns that the noun [מיתרותא] formed from the root [יתר] conveniently expresses τὴν ἀρετὴν according to the usage of the Syrians and is a general name for all good works and actions, which exposition the following things entirely require. When therefore the Apostle requires that they supply virtue in faith, he warns that it is not sufficient to boast of faith: but that the same must be demonstrated by holiness of life and Christian virtues, as the fruits of true faith. Beda in comm. h. l. He placed virtue for good conversation, which is rightly to be joined to faith, lest it be idle and dead without works. Luther in h. l. You have a good inheritance and a fertile field, therefore do not permit tares to grow in it,

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἀρετῇ τὴν γνῶσιν. By τὴν γνῶσιν in this place is understood prudence, which moderates and directs all virtues, so that in their exercise we may neither sin in excess nor in defect, nor wander from the due end, in which sense the word γνώσεως is used 1. Cor. 8. v. 6.2. Cor. 6. v. 6.1. Petr. 3. v. 7. which Paul also calls ἐπίγνωσιν Rom. 10. v. 2. Luther in h. l. γνῶσις consists in this, that the external life and of faith Whoever acts with reason acts with virtue. Because, therefore, prudence is the eye of all virtues, without which virtues easily degenerate into vices, for that reason the Apostle teaches that prudence must be joined to virtue.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ γνώσει τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. ἐγκράτεια is a virtue which restrains not only the desire for food, drink, and lusts, but also vicious affections, anger, avarice, ambition, and envy. Chrysostom, homily 2 on chapter 1 of Titus. ἐγκρατῆ εἶπεν (ὁ Ἀπόστολος) εὸν πάθους κρατοῦντα καὶ γλώττης, καὶ χειρὸς, καὶ ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκολάστων, τοῦτο γὰρ ἔστιν ἐγκράτεια. Gagnaeus on this passage, from Oecumenius. ἐγκράτεια it signifies not only abstinence and temperance, but also continence and moderation from all illicit things. For since knowledge puffs up 1. Cor. 8. v. 1., therefore he requires that moderation of mind be joined with it, so that we may be wise εἰς τὸ σωφρωνεῖν. Rom. 12. vers. 3.. Luther on this passage: Continence ought not only to be exercised in food and drink, but also in the whole external conversation, in words, deeds, and gestures, so that every excess in adornment and clothing may be avoided. To which can be referred that which Gal. 5. v. 22., for one ἐγκρατείας word in the Vulgate version, three virtues and as it were distinct fruits of the Holy Spirit are placed, namely modesty, continence, and chastity. Especially, however, ἐγκράτεια moderates the use of food and drink, and restrains lusts and luxuries, whence it is rightly translated by temperance. Budaeus rendered it continence, namely τῆς γαστρὸς καί οἴνου καὶ συνουσίας.. The Syrian ἐγκράτειαν in this passage translates it by [מחמסננותא], which Pococke renders perseverance, since Dionysius comments on this passage thus: The Apostle adds that we should persist or persevere in the profession and faith which we have received. But 1. they themselves admit that this word does not occur elsewhere in the entire Syriac version of the N.T. 2. They admit that the root [חמסן], from which this word draws its origin, signifies not only to endure, to sustain 1. Thess. 1. v. 1. ἐπιμένειν to persist, to persevere 1. Tim. 4. vers. 16. Hebr. 3. v. 14. but also κρατεῖν to hold fast strongly 2. Thess. 2. v. 15. and ἐγκρατεύεσθαι to contain oneself. Therefore it can rightly be rendered by continence or temperance. 3. That which the Greek text evidently shows, in which is not held the word ὑπομονῆς, but ἐγκρατείας.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐγκρατεία τὴν ὑπομονὴν. He commands that patience be added to continence. For it is not only required of the pious that they moderate the desires of food and drink, which is proper to continence, but also that they bear injuries and afflictions with an even mind, which is proper to Patience. Both pertain to the mortification and crucifixion of the flesh with its affections and concupiscences, which the Apostle requires of all who are Christ's, Gal. 5. v. 24. Those who do not walk according to the custom of this age, the world hates and persecutes them; here, therefore, there is need of patience. The Syrian for ὑπομονῇ places the name [מסברנותא] which signifies not only patience, but also perseverance, from the root [סבר] which corresponds to the Hebrew שבר in Piel, he sustained, tolerated, persevered. For without perseverance, neither continence nor the remaining virtues are of any profit.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ὑπομονῇ τὴν εὐσέβειαν He commands that piety, or the zeal for piety and religious worship toward God, be joined to patience, because true Christian patience is distinguished from the phantom of patience shining in the Heathen in this, that the truly pious in the cross look toward the providence of God, and toward the promises concerning liberation from the cross and the most bountiful reward to follow in eternal life. The Syrian rendered εὐσέβειαν as [דחלת אלהא] the fear of GOD, by which appellation συνεκδοχικῶς the whole worship of GOD is accustomed to be described.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ εὐσεβείᾳ τὴν φιλαδελφίαν, He commands that brotherly love be joined to piety, lest anyone boast that he worships God, who meanwhile is destitute of brotherly love. He who sins against a man, by that very fact sins against GOD Num. 5. v. 6., inasmuch as He has forbidden by His law to sin against a man. 1. Iohann. 4. vers. 20. If anyone says that he loves God, and hates his brother, he is a liar. For he who does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love GOD whom he does not see? v. 21. And this commandment we have from Him, that he who loves God, should love his brother also. Just as we love God as the most benign father for His own sake: so let us love His children, our brothers, i.e., all who confess Christ, for His sake. The Syrian rendered τὴν φιλαδελφίαν as [רחמת אחותא] intimate love of brotherhood or of brothers. [רחם] indeed is from רחם which signifies womb. Therefore, such love is denoted as is that of a mother toward a son whom she has carried in her womb.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ τὴν ἀγάπην. He joins charity to brotherly love, so that it may be signified that not only brothers and those of the household of faith, but all men entirely, even enemies, are to be loved Gal. 6. v. 10. Let us work good unto all, especially however unto those who are of the household of faith. Therefore not unto those of the household of faith alone.

Q. 1. What does the Apostle understand by ἀρετὴν in this place? 1. Flacius and Cornelius à Lapide, following Jerome in chapter 63 of Isaiah, say that by ἀρετὴν is understood the vigor of virtue, strength, and fortitude for overcoming all arduous things, so that the faithful, according to this admonition of Peter, may not be sluggish and weak in faith and Christian life, but eager and strong. For the confirmation of this exposition, Salmero urges that it is absurd to enumerate virtue in general among the species, namely faith, knowledge, abstinence, patience. 2. Some think that by the name ἀρετῆς is specially designated justice toward one's neighbor, with which those who are endowed are called good men. 3. But we have warned above that, with the name ἀρετῆς taken generally, virtues of every kind are understood here, through which true faith exerts itself, so that thus the Apostle proceeds from the genus to certain species.

Q. 2. Is there a certain gradation in this Apostolic exhortation to virtues? Some think the particle ἐν in these words of the Apostle is placed, according to a customary Hebraism, for διά through, in the sense that in this septenary number of virtues the latter is to be supplied through the former, by which reason there would always be a certain causality in the former with respect to the latter, which is what usually happens in the Rhetorical figure which they call κλίμακα. According to this hypothesis, that ladder of virtues distinguished by seven degrees is explained thus. 1. Supply in your faith virtue, that is, fortitude, because faith produces fortitude and confers strength for performing those things which are to be done from the doctrine of Christ. 2. In virtue, knowledge, because virtue produces knowledge, since true knowledge consists in experience, so that he who has been able to perform something, then at last knows for certain (which he did not know before, when he believed) that it could be performed. 3. In knowledge, temperance, because knowledge produces temperance, since, confirmed by this knowledge, a man proceeds to the goal, the same success hoping for in the rest, and therefore he abstains from bodily pleasures, which war against the soul, lest, being hindered by them, he be defrauded of the palm. 4. In temperance, patience. For because the desires, which we previously served, when we rebel against them with temperance, vex us with the desire for themselves, therefore there is need of patience, so that we may bear that pain bravely and constantly. 5. In patience, the fear of GOD. For because we know that this pain, which must be borne in resisting desires, is greater than our strength, therefore we invoke the Lord, that He may train our hands for war, which invocation and trust is piety. 6. In the fear of GOD, brotherly love. For having obtained benefits from GOD through this piety, when we desire to love GOD in return for them, and to render thanks to Him, but because we can confer nothing upon Him, nor does He need our goods, we turn our love toward those whom He Himself loves, and commends to us, namely the pious, and we do good to them out of love. 7. In brotherly love, charity. For because this love, with which we pursue GOD and furthermore our brothers on account of GOD's benefits toward us, is imperfect, therefore it never ceases to grow, until it arrives at perfection, thus the love of GOD is that charity called by Peter. Socinus in his explanation of the Places of Scripture p. 115 brings forward such a connection of this gradation. From the assent applied to the preaching of the Gospel, it ought to proceed that a Christian man afterwards conducts himself manfully, and takes up strength. Hence he seeks true and solid knowledge and science of divine things, from which it is born that he restrains himself from every desire of the flesh, and in this does violence to himself, endures and perseveres, which the word contains ὑπομονὴ. Now it is not only continent, which is a virtue toward oneself. Or it can also be explained thus, he does not harm others, but also becomes more pious, that is, With the pleasures of the flesh spurned, and the care of worldly things cast aside, he turns himself wholly to GOD and religion. Thus affected, he loves his brothers and exercises charity, and does not refuse to lay down his life for his brother.

But anyone sees that this is forced, if anyone should try to demonstrate that in this gradation the prior virtue is always the cause of the posterior, such as also is that which Socinus understands by faith as naked assent, when nevertheless the Apostle uses the word πίστεως here in the same signification in which it is used in v. 1., namely for justifying faith, which embraces knowledge, assent, and trust, and that which by virtue they understand fortitude and strength, although in the Greek it is not δύναμις, but ἀρετὴ,, which word the Apostle uses here in the same meaning in which it is used v. 3., although virtues exist in GOD by way of essence, but in the pious by way of accidents. It is therefore more simply established that the little word ἐν in this place signifies the same as with, so that not so much the origin of one virtue from another is described, as a certain collection of most beautiful and principal virtues, and thus one should not labor greatly over the reason for the order. Flacius in his commentary on this place: In this gradation, not so much the sequence of natural things, as the necessary conjunction of all these virtues with faith is to be regarded. In that meaning the prefix ב is used Gen. 32. v. 1. With my staff I passed over the Jordan, 1. Sam. 1. v. 24. with three bullocks. Psal. 2. v. 11. Serve the Lord with fear. Psal. 60. v. 12. with our armies. Ose. 4. v. 3. with the beast of the field and the bird (thus the LXX rendered it) cap. 5. v. 6. with their flock, Matth. 25. v. 16. He went, who had received five talents, and worked with them. Actor. 7. v. 38. This is he, who was in the Church, i.e., with the Church in the wilderness. In the same way the Syrian also rendered the particle ἐν in this place. Add to your faith, or above your faith, for he uses the preposition [על]. Meanwhile, we do not deny that there is a certain connection in these seven degrees of virtues, which is usefully investigated, even if the former is not always the cause of the latter. For this is certain, that faith is placed in the first position in this catalog because it is the basis and foundation of all Christian virtues, without which it is impossible to please GOD Hebr. 11. v. 6. and from which whatever is not, is sin. Rom. 14. v. 23.

Q. 3. What is understood by γνῶσιν in this place? Some understand by γνῶσιν a more abundant knowledge of divine mysteries, through which we may grow in faith, in which meaning this word is accepted in cap. 3. seqq. v. 18. Grow ἐν γνώσει of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Cyril accepts it thus in this place. 2. Oecumenius in his commentary says that by γνῶσιν it is signified that we ought not only to believe the mysteries of faith, but also to attain them to some extent by understanding. 3. Luther in his German version seems to accept it concerning Christian prudence and moderation, through which we may be able to win brothers for Christ. For thus he rendered it: In der Tugend Bescheidenheit.

4. But in his commentary he understands with us prudence, the moderator of all virtues. Dionysius the Carthusian on this place: By knowledge is understood discretion, which is the directress and charioteer of the virtues, teaching us to observe moderation, the appropriate place, the suitable time, so that all things may be done in order, and we may tend along the royal road, so that our service may be reasonable.

Q. 4. Why the Apostle wishes ἐγκράτειαν? to be joined to knowledge? Resp. 1. Bede in his commentary gives this reason. In knowledge, abstinence, so that when they have learned to do good, they may immediately abstain from evils, lest the knowledge of heavenly things should result in vain, if one has neglected to restrain himself from earthly allurements. 2. Some think, that the Apostle makes mention of continence for this reason, because the Gentiles did not judge simple fornication between an unmarried man and an unmarried woman to be a sin. 3. It is answered most simply, that the Apostle joins temperance with prudence for this reason, because prudence cannot have a place without temperance. A prudent soul is said to dwell in a dry place and σωφροσύνη is said q. σώζουσα τὴν φρόνησιν.

Q. 5. Why the Apostle wishes godliness to be joined to patience? 1. Augustine, book 10 of The City of God, chapter 1, says, εὐσέβειαν godliness, although it properly pertains to God, is nevertheless often used in works of mercy, because these things are wonderfully pleasing to God. Hence by godliness some in this place understand kindness, beneficence, mercy. Bede in his commentary on this passage: So that towards those whom he patiently tolerates, he may also be godly, according to that of the Apostle: Charity is patient, is kind. Lorinus on this passage: Perhaps by εὐσέβειαν from the common notion, Peter wished to understand kindness and works of mercy. For it is not enough for a Christian to bear injuries and torments inflicted upon him, unless he also bears a godly, kind, and beneficent mind towards those who inflict these things. But the Apostle treats of these virtues pertaining to the second table of the Decalogue in the following sections. 2. Some give this reason for the connection, that afflictions render a man humble, and compel him to flee to God through prayers, and to implore His help. 3. Luther on this passage: teaches that godliness is joined with patience for this reason, because in all things which we do or suffer, we ought to seek solely the honor and service of God, not our own honor or advantage. 4. It is answered most simply, that in patience godliness is required to be supplied for this reason, so that hoping in God, and religiously worshipping Him, we may expect deliverance from all adversities in filial confidence.

Q. 6. Why does the Apostle require ἀγάπην φιλαδελπίᾳ to be joined? Resp. 1. Some wish, that brotherly love should be joined to charity for this reason, so that it may be signified that brothers ought to be loved not with a carnal or secular love, but with a spiritual one, that is, on account of God to be loved above all things, which love Scripture everywhere ἀγάπην calls. 2. With this exposition agrees what some establish, that by ἀγάπην is understood the love, by which we are carried toward God, so that because we love the brethren, that may be done on account of the love of God. Bede in his commentary on this passage: He calls charity specifically that by which we love the Creator, which, as the degrees of virtues progress, is deservedly joined to the love of brotherhood, because neither can GOD be perfectly loved without the neighbor, nor the neighbor without GOD. 3. Some by φιλαδελφίαν understand an affection of the mind: by ἀγάπην the duties which proceed from that affection. For he truly loves, who in reality helps those whom he loves. Luke 10. v. 37. 4. But it is more rightly established that by ἀγάπην is understood the general love by which we embrace all men, the reason for which the Apostle wishes φιλαδελφίᾳ to be joined to it, we have explained above.

Ἔλεγχος. Because this Apostolic precept, by which he commands ἐν τῇ γνώσει τὴν ἐκράτειαν to be supplied, is general, pertaining not only to the unmarried, but also to the married, from this it is gathered that Bellarmine very ἀπαιδεύτως in his book on Clerics, chapter 19, concludes thus: Paul Titus 1. v. 8. requires from the Ministers of the Church ἐγκρατείαν. Therefore they ought to abstain from marriage. But not only the present Apostolic passage, but also other sayings of Scripture, Sirach 26. v. 20. Gal. 5. v. 23. testify that ἐγκράτειαν can also have a place in the married.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. From the participle παρεισενέγκαντες the Papists gather the powers of free will in spiritual matters. Lorinus on this passage: The Greek participle signifying those who brought in or brought in alongside something else, who contributed to that, or with another effort and labor, denotes the concurrence and cooperation of our free will. Estius on this passage: This passage makes for the cooperation of free will with the grace of GOD, which nevertheless that very cooperation is entirely to be attributed to the help of GOD, working in us both to will and to perform. Phil. 2. v. 13. Cornelius à Lapide on this passage: This word signifies that grace by itself alone does not suffice for salvation, but that the cooperation of free will is required, so that it may be inferred also by striving with the efficacy of our will. Response 1. παρεισφέρειν is read only once in the New Testament. But it is known that compound words are often used for simple ones, so that an emphasis cannot always be sought in a compound word. 2. Peter here speaks of the reborn; that they are συνέργους, of the grace of GOD we willingly concede. Augustine, book 2 on the merit of sins, chapter 5, after he had proved from prayers that the help of grace is necessary, adds: Nor yet is this matter to be dealt with by prayers alone, so that it may not be inferred by striving also with the efficacy of our will. A helper for our God is called, nor can he be helped, unless he who also attempts something of his own accord, because God does not work our salvation in us as in senseless stones, or as in those in whose nature he did not establish reason and will. However, the question between us and the Papists is not about the reborn and converted, but about the natural powers of free will both before conversion and in conversion itself. 3. If the entire cooperation of free will is to be attributed to the help of God, working in us to will and to perform, as Estius writes in this place; and if τὸ παρὰ signifies that the will cannot work anything by its own powers in these acts, but receives all powers to work them from grace, as Cornelius à Lapide writes in this place, and declares it by the simile of iron made fiery, then certainly free will, even after conversion, does not act by its own natural powers, but by new powers gifted by the Holy Spirit. 4. Therefore, the Apostle by no means intends that we ought to contribute something of our own to God's grace and faith, but that it is not enough to boast of faith, but that it must also be demonstrated by virtues and good works, as if by its fruits.

2. Estius, on the same verse 5, notes: Peter therefore requires that we join the works of virtues to faith, lest faith be empty, unformed, and dead. Cornelius à Lapide, ibid.: Faith is enervated and weak, unless it is supported by virtue. Response: good works are not the form of faith, but its necessary consequence and effect. Gal. 5. v. 6. It is said by James cap. 2. v. ult. faith without works is dead, because good works testify to the life of faith, just as breathing does to the life of the body. By equal reasoning, good works do not add a soul or powers to faith, but rather faith adds all dignity and strength to good works. Rom. 14. v. ult. Hebr. 11. v. 6.

3. Lorinus, on the same verse, notes thus: Abbas Esaias gathers from this place the necessity of good works for salvation besides faith, as does Pope Sixtus the Third. Response: true faith, although it justifies without works, yet it is not without works. Although good works are together with faith, and indeed are necessarily joined with faith, provided faith is true and living, yet they do not justify together with faith, but the power of justifying in the order of instrumental cause belongs to faith alone.

4. The same Lorinus, ibid., comments thus: Theology is useful and even necessary for the Church, not for individuals, just as an equally explicit faith is not required from individuals. Whence heretics wrongly gather from this knowledge that the notion of implicit faith is a mere fabrication. Response: 1. by γνῶσιν Lorinus admits that by Cyril and Oecumenius in the Apostolic text is understood of mysteries The knowledge of Christ, the science of the secret mysteries of God, by Arius the science of the sacred Scriptures. 2. He confesses also this, that the word of knowing is sometimes used concerning the knowledge of faith. 3. Since therefore the Apostle commands γνῶσιν, to be joined to faith, and truly this precept of the Apostle is general, pertaining to all Christians whatsoever, it is a consequence that the faith of all Christians whatsoever ought to have γνῶσιν joined to it, and accordingly is to be defined not so much by ignorance as by knowledge. 4. Although indeed there are certain degrees of that knowledge, and Theology, that is, that accurate knowledge of divine mysteries which ought to be in the Doctors of the Church, is not required of all Christians, yet the pious ought not to be content with implicit faith, which is nothing other than negligence in knowing divine mysteries, but they ought to make greater progress daily in the knowledge of God and of the Savior Jesus Christ.

5. Salmero on verse 7 notes thus: Observe that the beginning of our salvation is faith, but the perfection is charity, which is called by Paul the bond of perfection. Col. 3. 14. In the same way Estius: The crown of virtues is therefore concluded in charity, because that is the form, perfection, and complement of all virtues. Resp. 1. Charity is not the form of justifying faith, but ἐνέργεια effective, or an effect, joined with it by a perpetual and indissoluble covenant. Gal. 5. v. 6. Iac. 2. v. 18. 2. The proper and specific form of justifying faith is the fiducial apprehension of the Mediator Christ, and of his benefits, which are offered to us in the word of the Gospel. 3. In the exercises of Christian piety, which are observed in the justified, we concede that charity is greater than faith 1. Cor. 13. v. 13. not because it informs faith, or enters into the act of justification, or justifies more than faith, but both because of the breadth of the object, for faith has to do with God alone and the Mediator Christ, whereas charity is referred to God and neighbor: and because of its perpetual duration, because in eternal life vision will succeed faith, fruition will succeed hope, but charity will endure and will be fully perfected. 4. Charity is called πλήρωμα of the law Rom. 13. v. 10. because all divine precepts are referred to charity, as Augustine speaks in Enchir. c. 121, yet not any kind of love, but a perfect love, absolute in all its parts, is to be considered the fulfillment of the whole law. 5. Charity Col. 3. v. 14. is called συνδεσμὸς τῆς τελειότητος, not because charity renders us perfect to stand before the judgment of God, but because individual believers, as members of one mystical body, are so perfected through charity that nothing is lacking to any, but necessary things are supplied to individuals from mutual fellowship with the other members.

Observation 1. The ladder of virtues is begun by faith, and is terminated in charity, because the whole of Christianity is completed by faith and charity. Ignatius Epist. 7. τὸ ὅλον πίστις ἡ εἰς τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἀγάπη πρὸς τὸ ὁμόφυλλον. 2. Between the virtues there is a most tight connection, which is mystically signified Cant. 7. v. 1. by the necklaces, fashioned by the hand of the craftsman. For just as in a golden necklace, which has been fashioned by the hand of a skilled craftsman, any ring is connected with the rest in such a way that the individual ones are joined in turn and with the rest as a whole: so in the pursuit of virtues, which cannot stand and be exercised without the special help of the supreme craftsman, each one of the virtues is most tightly connected to another virtue, and the individual ones with all, just as in this place they are placed before our eyes by the Apostle as if in the form of a precious necklace.

3. Bede in his commentary adapts to this ladder of virtues, what is said about the building constructed on the mountain in the Prophetic vision Ezech. 40. v. 34. And its ascent was by eight steps.

4. Faith is placed in the first position in this catalog of virtues for this reason, because it is the base and foundation of all Christian virtues without which it is impossible to please GOD, Hebr. 11. v. 6. and whatever is not from faith, is sin. Rom. 14. v. 23. Origen lib. 1. in Ioh. tom. 2. fol. 3. Just as nothing is delightful to men without light: so nothing is delightful and acceptable to GOD without the light of faith. Gregory Nazianzen orat. 13. p. 347. Without faith no action can be fruitful. August. lib. 19. de Civ. DEI cap. 25. No true virtue before GOD without faith. Epist. 143. Faith is the mother and root of good works. Alcuin lib. 1. de Trin. cap. 1. Faith is the foundation of all good things. Lombard lib. 3. sentent. dist. 40. & 41. from Ambrose; Faith is the mother of good will and just action; from Gregory, it is the vestibule, through which one arrives at good works.

5. Bernard serm. 49. in Cant. Practical knowledge or Spiritual prudence is the charioteer of all virtues.

6. Some shadow of that most beautiful συζυγίας between continence and patience was seen even by the Philosophers of the Heathens, whose precept this was, ἀνέχου καὶ ἀπέχου sustain and abstain. Epictetus in Gellius lib. 17. N. A. c. 19.

7. Gregory part. 3. Curae Pastoral. admon. 20. Unless abstinence were for the most part to shake the minds of those abstaining from the bosom of tranquility, Peter would by no means, while he was saying: Supply in your faith virtue, in virtue knowledge, and in knowledge however temperance, he would immediately vigilantly join, saying. In temperance however patience, for he foresaw that patience was lacking to those who are temperate, which he admonished to be present to them.

8. Bede in this place. It is necessary that patience always accompany temperance, so that whoever has learned to restrain himself from the pleasures of the world, may firmly sustain all adverse things of it, namely from the right and from the left, fortified by the weapons of righteousness. which the interlinear Gloss repeats.

9. Dorotheus doctrine 6. Let each one strive to the best of his ability to cleave to his neighbor. For the more he shall have cleaved to his neighbor in love and benevolence, the more also he will cleave to GOD. Bernard in meditations chapter 5. column 1195. If we love GOD, let us also love his image. The same in the book on loving GOD. In order that your righteousness may be made perfect in the love of the neighbor, it is necessary to have God in it, otherwise he who does not love God cannot love his neighbor purely. It is necessary therefore that God be loved first, so that the neighbor may also be loved in God.

10. Bede in this place. In godliness he commands to minister the love of brotherhood, so that each one may bestow the works of godliness upon his adversaries with no regard for any other thing, except only for brotherly love; procuring this namely with the whole intention, that those whom he cannot convert by teaching only or by rebuking, he may convert to the effect of godliness by praying or by doing good.

11. Tertullian to Scapula, chapter 1. To love friends is for everyone; but to love enemies is for Christians alone.

12. Irenaeus book 4. against heresies chapter 27. Show yourself apt and useful to all to your neighbor, not looking at their malice, but perfecting your own goodness.

13. Basil sermon on the Institution of Monks. Just as GOD indiscriminately imparts light to all: so the imitators of GOD ought to communicate the ray of their charity equally to all.

Latin:

Connexio. Ex praedicatione divinorum tùm beneficiorum, tùm promissorum, quorum utraque longè sunt amplissima, Apostolus iam deducit exhortationem ad constantiam & profectum, tùm in fide, tùm in studio pietatis: Continetur ergo in his versiculis tribus propositio generalis totius Epistolae.

Dispositio. In hac exhortatione Apostolus. 1. per gradus enumerat illas virtutes, ad quarum profectum eos, ad quos scribit, hortatur. 2. exhortationem suam aliquot argumentis confirmat.

Textus expositio. Καί αὐτό τοῦτο δέ σπουδὴν πᾶσαν παρεισενέγκαντες. Qui particulam ὡς in v. 3. ut particulam similitudinis accipiunt, hoc loco ἀνανταπόδοτον illud per particulam οὕτως ad-implent, hoc modo. Sicut DEUS multis & magnis vos honoravit beneficiis: ita aequum est, ut ipsum vicissim honoretis officiis & obsequiis. Sed monuimus superiùs, particulam ὡς rectiùs ibi reddi postquam, siquidem.

Circa verba, αὐτό τοῦτο sub intelligenda particula περί, vel κατά, vel πρός, ut sit sensus. Et verò ad hoc ipsum omnem solicitudinem subinferentes, vel omne studium adhibentes. Caietanus, Gagneius & Cornelius â Lapide subintelligunt etiam verbum ποιεῖτε.Et hoc ipsum scil. facite omni curâ & diligentiâ adhibitâ Sed prior expositio est simplicior.

Praepositio παρὰ in participio παρεισενέγκαντες quibusdam videtur respectum habere ad illam DEI donationem, cuius facta fuit mentio v. 3. & 4. ut sit sensus. Praeter illam DEI donationem vos quoque omne studium conferte ad donorum illorum conservationem atque augmentum, quâ de re quid statuendum, videbimus in ἐκδικήσει. Syrus interpres verbum παρεισενέγκαντες itidem ut ἀποφυγέντες in versu praeced. videtur accepisse indicativè, Categoricè & assertivè, sic enim reddidit, Et hoc porrò ipsum cùm omnem diligentiam introduxeritis. Sed verbum ἐπιχορηγήσατε, â quo hoc participium regitur, ostendit, Apostolum hoc loco non indicare, quid fecerint, sed exhortari ad id, quod facere debent. Ἐπιχορηγήσατε ἐν τῇ πιστει ὑμῶν τὴν ἀρετὴν. Verbum ἐπιχορηγεῖν significat suppeditare, subministrare, adiicere, Item adhuc amplius suppeditare, suggerere, praestare. 2. Cor. 9. v. 10.ἐπιχορηγῶν σπέρμα τῷ σπείραντι.Gal. 3. v. 5.ἐπιχορηγῶν ἡμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα. Syrus reddidit per [אוסף]addidit, Lutherus, reichet dar.

Praepositionem ἐν Robertus Stephanus docet in quibusdam Codicibus non haberi, quâ ratione foret sensus. Ministrate fidei virtutem. Sed probatiores Codices eam habent additam. Ponitur autem ἐν pro εἰς, ut sit sensus, Adiicite ad fidem vestram virtutem. Vatablus putat, Hebraismum esse, dicere in fide pro fidei, & sic etiam particulamἐνin seqq. verti debere, virtuti scientiae, sed huius Hebraismi exempla meritò desiderantur.

Voculam ἀρετὴν Syrus reddidit per [מיתרותא] quod. Nonnulli reddunt per abundantiam, cùm [יתר] inter caetera significet, abundavit. Sensus ergo foret, quòd in fide quotidie crescere debeant, sicut in cap. 3. v. 18. dicit. Crescite in cognitione Christi. Sed Pococke rectè monet, nomen [מיתרותא] formatum ex rad. [יתר] commodè ex Syrorum usu exprimere τὴν ἀρετὴν ac esse generale nomen omnium operum & actionum bonarum, quam expositionem sequentia omninò requirunt. Quando ergo Apostolus requirit, ut subministrent in fide virtutem, monet, quòd non sufficiat de fide gloriari: sed eandem sanctitate vitae & virtutibus Christianis, tanquam verae fidei fructibus, demonstrandam esse. Beda in comm. h. l. Virtutem pro conversatione bona posuit, quae fidei rectê iungenda est, ne sine operibus otiosa sit & mortua. Lutherus in h. l. Habetis bonam hereditatem & fertilem agrum, ergo non permittite, ut in eo crescant zizania,

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἀρετῇ τὴν γνῶσιν. Per τὴν γνῶσιν h. l. intelligitur prudentia, quae virtutes omnes moderatur ac dirigit, ut in earum exercitio nec in excessu, nec in defectu peccemus, nec â debito fine aberremus, quo sensu vox γνώσεως usurpatur 1. Cor. 8. v. 6.2. Cor. 6. v. 6.1. Petr. 3. v. 7. quam etiam Paulus vocat ἐπίγνωσινRom. 10. v. 2. Lutherus in h. l. γνῶσιςin eo consistit, ut vitam externam & fidei virtutem quis cum ratione agat. Quia ergo prudentia est oculus omnium virtutum, absque qua virtutes facilè in vitia degenerant, ideò virtuti prudentiam coniungendam esse, Apostolus docet.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ γνώσει τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. ἐγκράτεια est virtus, quae non solùm cupiditatem cibi, potus, ac libidines, sed etiam vitiosos affectus, iram, avaritiam, ambitionem, invidiam refrenat. Chrysostomus homil. 2. in cap. 1. Tit. ἐγκρατῆ εἶπεν (ὁ Ἀπόστολος) εὸν πάθους κρατοῦντα καὶ γλώττης, καὶ χειρὸς, καὶ ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκολάστων, τοῦτο γὰρ ἔστιν ἐγκράτεια. Gagnaeus in hoc loc. ex Oecumenio. ἐγκράτειαnon modò abstinentiam & temperantiam, sed ab omnibus illicitis continentiam & moderationem significat. Cùm enim scientia inflet1. Cor. 8. v. 1. ideò cum ea animi moderationem coniungi requirit, ut sa-piamus εἰς τὸ σωφρωνεῖν.Rom. 12. vers. 3. Lutherus in hunc locum. Continentia non solum debet exerceri in cibo ac potu, sed etiam in tota conversatione externa, in verbis, factis & gestibus, ut caveatur omnis excessus in ornatu & vestibus. Quò referri potest, quod Gal. 5. v. 22. pro una ἐγκρατείας voce in vulgata versione virtutes tres & velut distincti Spiritus Sancti fructus ponuntur, videlicet modestia, continentia & castitas. Cumprimis tamen ἐγκράτεια usum cibiac potus moderatur, libidines & luxus refrenat, undè rectè vertitur per temperantiam. Budaeus reddidit continentiam, scil. τῆς γαστρὸς καί οἴνου καὶ συνουσίας. Syrus ἐγκράτειαν h. l. vertit per [מחמסננותא] quod Pococke reddit perseverantiam, cùm Dionysius in h. l. sic commentetur. Adiungit Apostolus, ut persistamus seu perseveremus in professione & fide, quam accepimus. Atqui 1. fatentur ipsimet, vocem hanc alibi in tota N. T. versione Syriaca non occurrere. 2. fatentur, radicem [חמסן] unde haec vox originem trahit, significare, non solùm perferre, sustinere1. Thess. 1. v. 1.ἐπιμένεινpersistere, perseverare.1. Tim. 4. vers. 16.Hebr. 3. v. 14. sed etiam κρατεῖνfortiter retinere2. Thess. 2. v. 15. & ἐγκρατεύεσθαιcontinere se. Ergo rectè reddi potest per continentiam sive temperantiam. 3. id quod textus Graecus evidenter ostendit, in quo non habetur vox ὑπομονῆς, sed ἐγκρατείας.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐγκρατεία τὴν ὑπομονὴν. Continentiae iubet adiungere patientiam. Non solùm enim â piis requiritur, ut cupiditates cibi & potus moderentur, quod est proprium continentiae, sed etiam iniurias & afflictiones aequo animo ferant, quod est proprium Patientiae. Utrumque pertinet ad mortificationem & crucifixionem carnis cum suis affectibus & concupiscentiis, quam ab omnibus, qui Christi sunt, requirit Apostolus, Gal. 5. v. 24.Qui non ambulant more huius seculi, illos mundus odio habet & persequitur, hîc ergo opus patientiâ. Syrus pro ὑπομονῇ ponit nomen [מסברנותא] quod significat non solùm patientiam, sed etiam perseverantiam â rad. [סבר] quae respondet Hebraeorum שבר in Piel. sustinuit, toleravit, perseveravit. Absque perseverantia enim nec continentia, nec reliquae virtutes quidquam prosunt.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ ὑπομονῇ τὴν εὐσέβειαν Patientiae pietatem sive studium pietatis ac religiosi erga Deum cultus coniungendum esse praecipit, quia vera Christianorum patientia in eo â simulachro patientiae in Ethnicis relucente distinguitur, quodverè pii in cruce respiciunt ad Dei providentiam, & ad promissiones de liberatione ex cruce & largissima remuneratione in vita aeterna secutura. Syrus εὐσέβειαν reddidit, [דחלת אלהא]timorem DEI, quâ appellatione συνεκδοχικῶς totus DEI cultus describi solet.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ εὐσεβείᾳ τὴν φιλαδελφίαν, Pietati fraternam caritatem coniungi iubet, ne quis glorietur, se Deum colere, qui fraternâ caritate interim destituitur. Qui peccat contra hominem, eo ipso peccat contra DEUM Num. 5. v. 6. quippe qui contra hominem peccare lege suâ prohibuit. 1. Iohann. 4. vers. 20.Si quis dixerit, se diligere Deum, & fratrem suum oderit, mendax est. Qui enim non diligit fratrem suum quem videt, DEUM quem non videt, quomodo potest diligere?v. 21.Et hoc mandatum habemus ab eo, ut qui diligit Deum, diligat & fratrem suum. Sicut Deum amamus velut benignissimum patrem propter seipsum: ita filios ipsius, nostros fratres, h. e. omnes, qui Christum confitentur, diligamus propter ipsum. Syrus τὴν φιλαδελφίαν reddidit [רחמת אחותא]intimum amorem fraternitatis sive fratrum.[רחם] enim est ex רחם quod uterum significat. Denotatur ergo talis dilectio, qualis est matris erga filium, quem in utero suo gestavit.

Ἐν δὲ τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ τὴν ἀγάπην. Fraterno amori coniungit caritatem, ut significetur, non solùm fratres & domesticos fidei, sed omnes omninò homines, etiam inimicos diligendos esse Gal. 6. v. 10.Operemur bonum ad omnes, maximè autem ad domesticos fidei. Ergo non ad solos fidei domesticos.

Q. 1. Quid perἀρετὴνApostolus h. l. intelligat? 1. Flacius & Cornelius â Lapide secuti Hieronymum in cap. 63. Esai. per ἀρετὴν dicunt intelligi virtutis vigorem, robur ac fortitudinem ad omnia ardua superanda, ut fideles iuxta hoc Petri monitum in fide & vita Christiana non sint segnes ac debiles, sed alacres & fortes. Pro confirmatione huius expositionis Salmero urget illud, quòd absurdum sit, inter species videl. fidem, scientiam, abstinentiam, patientiam, enumerare virtutem in genere. 2. Quidam nomine ἀρετῆςspecialiter designari censent iustitiam erga proximum, quâ qui praediti sunt, boni viri nominantur. 3. Sed monuimus superiùs, nomine ἀρετῆς generaliter accepto, omnis generis virtutes hîc intelligi, per quas vera fides sese exerit, ut sic â genere progrediatur Apostolus ad certas species.

Q. 2. An in hac exhortatione Apostolica ad virtutes sit quaedam gradatio? Particulamἐν in hisce Apostoli verbis quidam censent positam, iuxta usitatum Hebraismum proδιάper, sensu eo, quòd in hoc septenario virtutum numero posterior subministranda sit per priorem, quâ ratione in priore semper foret quaedam causalitas respectu posterioris, id quodin figura Rhetorica, quamκλίμακαvocant, plerumque usu venit. Iuxta hanc hypothesin scala ista virtutum septem gradibus distincta sic explicatur. 1. Sub ministrate in fide vestra virtutem h. e. fortitudinem, quia fides parit fortitudinem & confert vires ad ea praestanda, quae ex Christi doctrina facienda sunt. 2. In virtute scientiam, quia virtus parit scientiam, siquidem vera scientia in experientia consistit, ut qui aliquid praestare potuit, tùm demum certò sciat, (quod antea, cùm crederet, nesciebat) id praestari potuisse. 3. In scientia temperantiam, quia scientia parit temperantiam, siquidem hâc scientiâ confirmatus homo pergit ad metam, eundem successum sperans in reliquis, ideoque abstinet se â voluptatibus corporeis, quae contra animam militant, ne ab iis impeditus palmâ defraudetur. 4. In temperantia patientiam. Quia enim cupiditates, quibus antea servivimus, cùm adversùs eas temperantiâ rebellamus, vexant nos desiderio sui, ideo opus est patientiâ, ut illum dolorem fortiter, constanterque feramus. 5. In patientia timorem DEI. Quia enim scimus, dolorem hunc, qui in resistendo cupiditatibus ferendus est, maiorem esse viribus nostris, ideo Dominum invocamus, ut manus nostras ad bellum erudiat, quae invocatio & fiducia est pietas. 6. In timore DEI amorem fraternitatis. Hac enim pietate â DEO beneficia consecuti, cùm propter illa DEUM redamare, eique gratiam referre cupimus, sed quia ei nihil conferre possumus, neque enim bonis nostris indiget, convertimus amorem nostrum in eos, quos ipse amat, nobisque commendat, videl. pios, iisque ex amore benefacimus. 7. In amore fraternitatis caritatem. Quia enim amor hic, quo Deum & porrò fratres nostros propter DEI in nos beneficia prosequimur, imperfectus est, ideò nunquam crescere desinit, donec perveniat ad perfectionem, sic amor DEI est caritas illa â Petro appellata.
