Salmero in his commentary: We elicit from this passage that all the heretics of our time are vain, who, against so many testimonies of the Apostles, and indeed most evident ones, magnify and exalt a naked and solitary faith. For what does it profit to apprehend by faith that CHRIST died for you, unless you trust and rely upon Him? But how will the mind be able to trust in Him whom it does not love? Faith therefore without charity cannot justify. Bellarmine, book 4 on justification, chapter 7, § last, urges this, that Augustine in his book on faith and works, chapter 14, testifies that Peter, John, James, and Jude direct their intention primarily to this, that they may prove that good works are necessary for the salvation of justified men, and that faith alone does not suffice, as some at that time had begun to preach from the Epistles of Paul, which were poorly understood. Estius on this passage: That faith can exist without works, but does not profit, he gathers from this, that Peter studiously exhorts to good works in this Epistle, on account of those who, from the Epistles of Paul poorly understood, were neglecting works, content with faith alone. Lorinus urges the same on this passage. Resp. 1. We do not neglect good works, nor do we say they should be neglected. 2. But rather, together with the Apostle and from the Apostle, we studiously exhort to good works. 3. Teaching that a true and living faith, by which we are justified before GOD, cannot exist without good works. 4. And so we say that those err gravely who persuade themselves that they have true faith, although they neglect the pursuit of good works. 5. But what kind of consequence is this? True faith is not without good works. Therefore it does not justify without works? One must absolutely distinguish between the presence of good works, and the efficiency of good works, which distinction Bellarmine himself acknowledges in book 4 on Justification, chapter 7. 6. One must also distinguish between a true justifying faith, and a vain persuasion of faith. The Apostolic exhortation to the pursuit of good works fights not against the former, but against the latter. 7. For Peter attacks the vain persuasion of those who imagine for themselves such a justifying faith as does not bear the fruits of good works. Therefore he teaches the contrary of that which Estius attributes to him. 8. Lorinus in his commentary on 2 Peter 3, v. 13, about to adduce the statement of Augustine in his book on faith and good works, chapter 25, rightly warns that Augustine is arguing against those void of works with only a profession of faith. Note what he says, with only a profession of faith, because the profession can indeed be separated from works, but true and living faith is never without good works. 9. Lorinus objects, that contradictory things are taught by us, since we sometimes assert that faith alone justifies, and that God requires nothing else from us than that we believe; but sometimes we say that the faith by which we are said to be justified works charity, perseverance, and innocence. Resp. These things, however, do not conflict in the least. For it is one thing for faith to justify without works; it is another for faith to be without works. True and living faith is not without works, yet works do not concur together with faith to effect justification. Those things which are joined together do not immediately concur ἐνεργητικῶς to one and the same effect.

2. From the same verse the Papists gather, that an abundance of good works can be performed by the faithful, so far is it from the case that every work of man is a sin. Estius in comm. Resp. 1. That truly pious men and those believing in Christ can perform an abundance of good works, none of us denies. Of Tabitha it is said Acts 9. v. 36. that she was full of good works; of Cornelius Acts 10. v. 2. that he did many alms and prayed to GOD always. 1. Tim. 6. v. 18. the Apostle requires of the rich of this world, that they become rich in good works. 2. Also, none of us says that every work of man is formally a sin. 3. But we do teach this, that the good works of no man (Christ θεανθρώπῳ alone excepted) are so perfect that they fully satisfy the divine law. One must therefore distinguish between the abundance of good works and their absolute perfection. 4. We also teach this, that the good works of the pious, because of the remnants of sin still clinging in their flesh, are unclean and contaminated by the stain of sin, which adhering uncleanness likewise does not take away the abundance of good works, but their absolute purity.

3. Lorinus on the same verse annotates thus: καθιστάναι is to effect, to render, to place, to set, furthermore to set before, to confirm, to establish, to strengthen, to give fruitful strength, to protect, to restore, to institute, and as it were to instruct, and to teach, to commit as in war, or for war, to compose and to settle, to bring back to good fruit, all of which show the power of good works and the great confidence which they generate before the judgment and in the judgment itself, concerning which some explain the following words. In the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. In Greek εἰς τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν, which case of the accusative, since it indicates a future knowledge, favors the exposition concerning judicial knowledge.

Resp. 1. It is forced to understand ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ in this place as the day of judgment, since the Apostle is dealing with the knowledge of Christ that befalls the pious in this life, that is, with faith in Christ. 2. Although all those meanings of the word καθιστάναι may be accommodated here, (concerning some of which, however, it could not undeservedly still be asked,) yet it could not yet be proven from them either that good works are merits properly so called, or that confidence on the day of judgment is to be placed in them. For it is one thing for the pious to be fruitful in good works, and for most generous rewards to be promised to them by grace; but it is another thing for the pious to acquire those rewards for themselves by the merits of their works. The former Scripture asserts, the latter it denies. 3. Lorinus himself prefers this sense, that through the works of virtues we are not rendered unfruitful in faith or in the knowledge of Christ.

4. The same Lorinus comments thus on the same verse. The word fruit denotes the reason of goodness and merit in the works of the just, which are exercised by them with the grace of GOD by their own free will. There is no similarity in it with fruit in that, just as this proceeds from seed or a plant: so a good work proceeds naturally and necessarily from the just: although there is also a certain similar reason, insofar as cultivation is necessary in both cases, which we do not apply except freely and spontaneously.

Resp. 1. Firm arguments are not drawn from parabolic expressions, unless Scripture itself shows the application; nor are comparisons to be extended beyond the third point for which they are employed. 2. When good works are compared to fruits, the merit of good works is not denoted, but their necessity and utility. Good fruits are necessarily required to demonstrate the goodness of the tree, and their utility is greatest. Thus good works are required so that the goodness of the person may be recognized from them; they also have a far greater use. 3. We rather invert the argument taken from the appellation of fruit. Just as sowing is not the meritorious cause of the harvest, nor planting the cause of the fruits, but they obtain that by the blessing of GOD: so good works are not the meritorious cause of heavenly rewards, but these follow those by the blessing of GOD. 4. Nor is there any reason for Lorinus to urge the free cultivation required in natural and spiritual fruits. For fruits are not the wages of that cultivation by merit, but only a consequence.

5. Add, that the cultivation necessary for spiritual fruits does not proceed, nor can it proceed, from the natural powers of free will, but from new powers gifted by the Holy Spirit, so that man is more bound to GOD on account of that cultivation, than that GOD is rendered a debtor to him. Compare Jerome in chapter 6 of Galatians upon the words: He who sows in the Spirit &c. where among other things he writes thus: That is likewise to be observed, that he who sows in the flesh, is placed with the addition of his own flesh. But he who sows in the Spirit, is not said to sow in his own Spirit, but simply in the Spirit. For he who sows good things, sows not anything in his own, but in the Spirit of GOD, from whom he is also to reap eternal life.

5. The same Lorinus at v. 9 annotates thus: Heretics, who rejoice in the light of faith alone, and wish to be only Gnostics or knowers, are blind. Resp. It is evident from what was said in ἐκδικ. the first.

6. The same Lorinus ibid. from the word purgation gathers, that no trace of sin remains in the reborn. Resp. One must distinguish between the formal and material of sin, or the guilt and the incentive. The guilt or the formal is taken away by purgation, but not the material or the incentive. Renewal mortifies and diminishes the incentive, yet it does not take it away completely and by the root.

7. The Vulgate version in v. 10. inserted through good works, in which way the Council of Trent also alleges this Apostolic passage, and the Syriac version has this προσδιορισμὸν added. Following the authority of the Vulgate version, the Papists gravely accuse Luther on this account, because in the German version he did not express this προσδιορισμὸν. Lorinus says, Luther expunged that, through good works.

Resp. 1. It is not held in the Greek Codices, except in a few, which Robert Stephanus brings forward, into which it was translated from the Latin version. Beza mentions that he found in two manuscript Greek codices διὰ καλῶν ἔργων, but those were of more recent writing. 2. Cajetan, Erasmus, Vatablus, Clarius, Adam, Gagneius establish, that those two words through good works are superfluous. 3. The Bibles of Isidorus Clarius, Bishop of Foligno, printed at Venice in the year 1557, exclude those words. The Bibles of the Royal work likewise omit them. 4. Estius says, Perhaps Peter did not add these, about which however he says he does not wish to contend. That indeed is Luther's is sufficient for a defense. 5. Even if we grant to the greatest extent what Estius urges and is not denied by us, that by the pursuit of good works our calling and election is made firm, and therefore that προσδιορισμὸν, must be understood as implied, yet from that it cannot be inferred that it ought to have been inserted into the text by Luther, because the scope of Luther was by no means to adorn a paraphrase, but a version. 6. Lorinus for the insertion of those words brings forward Mark the Monk, who lived in the year of Christ 300 and a little more, who reads them, Item Anthony Melissa, who although he does not read the works, yet understands this passage concerning works, sermon 1. volume 5. Library part 7. but we respond, it is one thing to have a genuine reading of the text, another to have an exegetical explanation of the same. 9. Some from the following pronoun ταῦτα attempt to prove that in the preceding words it must be read entirely διὰ καλῶν ἔργων, for these, namely, doing good works. But we have warned above, that by ταῦτα, can be understood the virtues enumerated in v. 5. 6. & 7.

8. Cornelius à Lapide on the same verse annotates thus. Peter speaks of election to faith and grace, consequently however of election to glory, not antecedent and absolute, but consequent and conditional.

Resp. If these things are understood as opposed to the absolute decree of election, which the Calvinists defend, we easily agree. But if concerning a certain mutable election, from which a man might again fall away, we deny our vote.

9. From the same verse Gabriel Vasquez, Gregory of Valencia, Luis de Molina in commentaries on Thomas, Cornelius à Lapide in commentary on this place labor to prove, that election to glory is made by GOD from the foreseen merits of each one. For since the Apostle commands to make election firm through good works, from that it seems to follow that election depends on the foreseeing of good works. Lorinus on this place That exhortation of Peter makes it so that calling and election depend on our works. And afterwards. It must remain fixed that God both foreknew, and indeed also predestined these and those to be his own through faith and work.

Respond. 1. That election does not depend on the foreseeing of merits, we have given confirmation in its own place with many arguments, namely from the naming of election, its causes, end, and time, from the consistency of the decree and its execution, from the nature of good works, etc. 2. Nor can the contrary be proved from this place, because the Apostle here does not treat of the causes of election, but of the certainty of election with respect to us. He teaches from where we can be certain that we are in the number of the elect, but not for what causes God has chosen us. 3. Thence Estius himself at this place comments thus, It is not consequent from the words of Peter, that election depends upon good works, which he himself confirms with evident sayings of the Apostle, Eph. 1. he chose us, that we should be holy chap. 2. created in good works, which God prepared, that we should walk in them. 4. Estius indeed adds, that election according to something depends upon good works, insofar as, namely, eternal happiness, to which we are chosen, is not given to adults, unless they keep the commandments of God, and insofar as that eternal happiness depends upon good works, as a reward from merit. But the former is ambiguous, the latter false. That eternal happiness, to which we are chosen, is not given to adults, unless they keep the commandments of God, can be taken in a double sense. Either that it may be a description of the object, to whom, namely, eternal happiness is given, or that it may be a description of the cause, on account of which the same is given. We concede the proposition taken in the former sense, but from it it cannot yet be inferred, that election depends upon good works as upon a cause. For the condition of an object is not immediately the cause of that thing, which is attributed to the object. Taken in the latter sense the proposition is false and contrary to Scripture, which we say also of the latter assertion of Estius, that eternal happiness depends upon good works, as a reward from merit. For Scripture does not attribute this to our merits, but to the merit of Christ alone, that on account of that eternal happiness falls to those believing in him, nor does it anywhere preach a reward of merit, but of grace. 5. We shall say nothing here about another certain ambiguity, lurking in the words of Estius, when he says, that eternal happiness, to which we are chosen, is not given to adults, unless they keep the commandments of GOD. For either this is understood of the perfect and in all numbers absolute fulfillment of the law, or of the inchoate observation of the divine commandments. If he understands the former, we deny that it has a place in the infirmity of this life in the reborn, whence also by the works of the law no flesh is justified before GOD. Rom. 3. v. 20. If the latter, we do not gainsay the assertion of Estius. 6. If eternal happiness to which we are chosen, is given on account of the merits of our good works, it is false, that election does not depend upon good works, and thus Estius contradicts himself. The reason of the connection depends upon the most exact agreement of the decree and the execution. On account of which causes God in time saves and glorifies man, on account of the same from eternity he has constituted him to save and to glorify. But according to the assertion of Estius, on account of the merits of good works, GOD in time saves and glorifies man. Therefore, also on account of the merits of good works, He determined from eternity to save and to glorify him, that is, He elected him to salvation, and consequently, election depends upon good works. 7. We oppose the same to the remaining Papists, who deny that election was made from the foreknowledge of good works, and yet defend the merits of works, namely, that they contradict themselves. Barradius, Tom. 3, Conc. Evang., lib. 4, cap. 19, pag. 303: GOD does not predestine either on account of works foreseen, or on account of the good use of the will. He does, however, predestine that we should have good works and the good use of the will; otherwise, if we do not have good works and the good use of the will, we shall be reprobate. Lorinus on this place: God calls and elects because He wills, not on account of those works. But in order that the called, the elected, the predestined may arrive there where He Himself wills, He has decreed among the means and conditions those same works, for the doing of which He might provide efficacious grace.

10. Cornelius à Lapide on the same verse annotates thus: From these words of St. Peter, the Doctors gather that not only election to glory, but also predestination itself to grace depends upon the cooperation of free will, even if this is not the cause of that. Thus Gregory of Valencia, 1. p. q. 23. Disp. 1. punct. 4. Lorinus on this place: We would strive in vain, unless there were free will in us. Response: It is one thing to make the calling firm through good works, but another thing for the calling to depend upon good works, or upon the cooperation of free will. The Apostle asserts the former, for those who are zealous for good works are confirmed by that fact, that they are led by the Spirit of GOD, and therefore are children of GOD: but the latter cannot be inferred from that, because all Scripture testifies that the calling is a work of mere divine grace, that it does not depend upon the cooperation of free will, as if upon a merit of congruity. Meanwhile, we willingly concede that those who stubbornly resist the operation of the Holy Spirit are not ordinarily converted to GOD; nor are those saved who, after regeneration, indulge in the concupiscences of their flesh, and have received the grace of GOD in vain.

11. Lorinus and other Papists attempt to prove the uncertainty of grace from the same verse, for in this way they gather: If the certainty of calling is to be sought through good works, therefore also that of justification. But if the certainty of justification depends upon good works, it is a consequence, first, that man is not certain of his own justification, as soon as he is justified. Secondly, that the certainty of justification does not depend on faith alone. Thirdly, that our justification is not certain with the certainty of faith, which is infallible, but of works, which is conjectural.

Resp. 1. We concede that justification must be made firm through the pursuit of good works, but we deny that no other principle of this certainty is given, as is evident from what was said in ἐλέγχω the third. 2. By the name of good works, one must understand not only external good works, but also interior renewal, a serious purpose of a holy life, and other spiritual motions excited by the Holy Spirit. 3. By good works we are commanded to make our calling firm, not so that the calling, which was previously uncertain, may become certain, but so that the certainty of that which is certain may be shown by good works. For βεβαιοῦν is not always used of a thing which is primarily uncertain, but also of that which, even if it be certain in itself, is nevertheless confirmed more and more. Mark 16. verse 20.Rom. 15. v. 8. If therefore the certainty of the calling does not depend absolutely on good works, much less does the certainty of justification.

12. The same Lorinus from the words, Give more diligence, gathers works of supererogation. Not improbably, he says, some are said to be indicated, that by works of supererogation the calling and election are rendered more certain, and that for those wishing to procure such certainty for themselves, it is necessary not to be content with the simple observation of the commandments, but to direct their effort higher.

Resp. 1. Both Peter and the whole Scripture are ignorant of works of supererogation, as is taught in its place. 2. The Apostolic precept is general, pertaining to all Christians. But works of supererogation are not required of all by way of a precept. 3. Lorinus himself acknowledges that the little word μᾶλλον is not of increasing, but of correcting, so that the sense may be: Rather give diligence or strive, that through good works you may establish yourselves in your calling and election. 4. If there were a discussion here about works of supererogation, it would follow that only Religious have the certainty of their calling and election. But the Papists will not concede this consequence, attributing to all the truly pious that conjectural certainty, concerning which they think Peter is dealing in this place.

13. The same Lorinus at this place annotates thus: Luther expunged those words by good works, just as he also expunged,1. Thess. 4. v. 3.that you abstain concerning fornication, and fromEphes. 6. v. 13.he blotted out what is prescribed concerning perfection, which seemed too heavy and troublesome to him.

Resp. 1. What is to be determined concerning προσδιορισμὸς, through good works was explained above. 2. In 1. Thess. 4. v. 3. & Eph. 6. v. 13. he did not strike out anything of those things which are held in the Greek text; but neither did he omit any of them in the vernacular version, but expressed them most faithfully, as αὐτοψία testifies.

14. The same Lorinus gathers from this place both the necessity of good works, which the word σπουδάζειν, also proves, and also the goodness of just works, truly and properly so called, since they are suitable to the calling and election.

Resp. 1. That Προσδιορισμός, through good works, is not an undoubted part of the authentic text. 2. We do not deny the necessity of good works by reason of coexistence with faith, but the necessity by reason of coefficient, and indeed meritorious, action. 3. Nor do we deny the goodness of works, but their absolute perfection and purity.

15. The Calvinists strive to elicit from this place that true faith and the zeal for good works flowing from it are proper to the elect in such a way that they belong to them alone and uniquely, from which they further infer that faith once received cannot be lost again. Beza on this place. Purpose, election, calling, sanctification, and justification cohere in an individual bond. Piscator on this place. Good works are the very reason by which election and calling are made firm in the minds of the faithful, while, namely, they reason from their own effects to the procreating cause. For good works can proceed only from the elect and effectively called.

Resp. 1. We have demonstrated in its place that faith once held can be lost, and that the terms 'regenerate' and 'elect' are not convertible, since some who are regenerate are not elect, namely those who, through sins against conscience, lose faith and regeneration again. 2. Nor can the contrary be demonstrated from this Apostolic saying. For although we are confirmed concerning faith, and consequently concerning election, from good works as from certain signs, yet the certainty of election does not depend on the testimony of good works alone, but also on other principles, as is evident from what has been said. 3. Nor does the certainty of present faith suffice for the certainty of election, but the certainty of perseverance is also required, or faith of the persevering, since only those persevering in faith until the very end of life are the elect.

16. Lorinus on the word πταίσητε notes thus, quite imperiously: Caietanus, Catharinus, Vatablus, and Salmero do not please me, who prefer that we use the word for slipping rather than for sinning, and to explain it concerning the loss of grace, of vocation, of election. These things are joined with sin, but it is better, as far as it can be done, to defend the side of our Interpreter. But yet 1. it is not so much about the authority of the Latin Interpreter as it is about the genuine exposition of the Greek text that it behooves us to be concerned. 2. The word πταίειν does not properly signify to sin, but to slip, to stumble.

17. The same Lorinus on v. 11 comments thus: Before the coming of Christ, this entrance (into the heavenly kingdom) was open to no one, but just as the entrance to the earthly Paradise after sin, had been closed to Adam, Gen. 3. v. 24. so the perception of happiness was granted to no one. He, who did not count it robbery to be equal with GOD, Phil. 2. v. 6. and immediately from the Baptism which He received, saw the heavens opened, Matth. 3. v. 16. He admitted the thief into Paradise, that is, into the beatific vision of GOD, which, wherever it may be perceived, is Paradise: but since Christ was about to present Himself to the just and to the thief himself on that day in the limbo of the just or in the bosom of Abraham, as Maldonatus rightly teaches in Matt. 27. v. 3., not well enough refuted by Thomas Malvenda in his book on Paradise, chapter 91.

Resp. 1. The Limbo of the Fathers is not only ἄγραφος, but also ἀντίγραφος, as was demonstrated in its place. 2. Nor can that fictitious limbo be propped up from this passage. For what is the consequence; To the pious in the N. T. an entrance into the kingdom of God is ministered abundantly. Therefore, were the pious in the O. T. excluded from entrance into the kingdom of God? Do we wish to conclude in this way also? To the pious in the New T. the Holy Spirit is given. Therefore, did the pious in the O. T. not receive the Holy Spirit? To the pious in the N. Test. rewards are given not only of the future life, but also of this life. 1. Timoth. 4. v. 8. Therefore, did the Pious of the O. T. not receive the rewards of this life? 3. Lorinus says, before the coming of Christ, entrance into the kingdom of GOD was open to no one. But other Papists say, before Christ's ascension into the heavens, entrance into the heavenly kingdom was open to no one. 4. But how was the beatific vision of God granted to the thief in the limbo of the Fathers, when the Fathers in limbo are said to be excluded from the beatific vision of God, and thus subject to the punishment of loss. 5. It is entirely the Blood of Christ that is the key of Paradise, as Jerome speaks in the Epistle to Heliodorus, which Lorinus urges for the assertion of limbo, but the Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world,Apoc. 13. v. 8. and the passion of Christ was profitable before it existed.

18. Guilielmus Estius from the same verse gathers the merits of good works. For after he had said, that that saying of Paul fits this place.2. Cor. 9. v. 6.He who sows in blessings, shall also reap from blessings, he adds. Sentences of this kind signify the proportion of merits and rewards before God. These things are to be observed against the Sectarians of our time, who deny the merits of good works. Likewise against the ancient heretic Jovinian, who took away the disparity of virtues and rewards. Lorinus in the same way. This is the greatest fruit of good works, the power of entering into the possession of everlasting happiness through the abundant and copious grace, which is supplied by God to those exercising themselves in the said works, although they themselves merit for themselves through the same.

Resp. 1. We have confirmed in its place with many arguments that good works are not merits of eternal life properly so called. What is clearer than the Apostolic saying Rom. 6. v. 23.The wages of sin is death, τὶ δὲ χάρισμα but the gratuitous gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord? 2. That there is no proportion of our merits before God is evidently gathered from Rom. 8. v. 18.I reckon therefore, that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory, which shall be revealed in us.2. Cor. 4. v. 17. Τὸ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν, καθ' ὑπερβολὴν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν αἰώνιον βάρος δόξης κατεργάζεται. But if there is no proportion between our sufferings and the rewards of eternal life, much less will there be a proportion between our good works and the rewards of eternal life, because to suffer evils is more than to do good. Hence the Scholastics themselves say, God rewards good things above what is condign, and punishes evil things below what is condign. 3. Nor can the contrary be proven from this Apostolic place. For neither are good works and the rewards of eternal life compared as meritorious cause and effect, but as antecedent and consequent. Those who are rich in good works will be rich in heavenly rewards, not from the merit of their works, but from the gratuitous gift of God promising. 4. Hence the reward promised to the good works of the pious is called, ἀνταπόδοσις τῆς κληρονομίας. Col. 3. v. 24. because it is such a reward, as is an ample inheritance, which falls to one adopted as a son, which is given after obedience, but not because of obedience. 5. Lorinus on this passage annotates thus: To the abundance of grace corresponds a greater store of blessedness; it also overflows for the sake of example to others, the better each one is. Likewise, abundance in the said entrance can designate the firm possession of blessedness. Finally, it seems that Simon's error is being countered, that Christ is not sufficient and that entrance into heaven can be hindered by his angels. But also, abundance hints at the access of new grace for those who make good use of what has been received. To him who has, it shall be given. If we embrace these expositions, no patronage for the merits of works will accrue from this place. 6. Campianus in his 8th reason attempts to smear us with the error of Jovinian concerning the parity of sins. This also, he says, is worn out in this dregs of the Protestants, that sins are equal: by this scale, that innkeeper who killed a rooster would not have sinned less against God than one who killed a man. But Estius absolves us from him in this place, separating the error of Jovinian from our opinion; Bellarmine also absolves us in book 3 of Justification, chapter 16, in the beginning. The Lutherans, he says, do not say, as far as I know, that virtues are equal or sins equal, nor do they deny that a man can grow in hope, love, and other virtues.

Latin:

Connexio. Pergit Apostolus in explicanda utilitate, profectum in virtutibus enumeratis consequente, ac expositae in versu praeced.

duplici utilitati addit tertiam, quae est finis fidei nostrae vita aeterna. 1. Pet. 1. v. 5. & 9.

Textus expositio. οὕτω γὰρ sc. Si vocationem & electionem vestram firmam faciatis, & â gravioribus lapsibus diligenter caveatis, praeoccupati autem â lapsu, citò resurgatis. Gal. 6. v. 1.

Πλουσίως ἐπιχορηγηθήσεται ὑμῖν ἡ εἴσοδος εἰς τὴν αἰώνιον βασιλείαν τοῦ κυρίου ὑμῶν, καὶ σωτῆρος Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Voculam πλουσίως Vulg. reddidit abundanter, significat a. propriè opulenter,Col. 3. v. 16.1. Tim. 6. v. 17.Tit. 3. v. 6. Syrus reddidit. [עתיראית]opulenter, affatim, â rad. [עתר]multiplicavit ex Hebr. עשרditatus, locupletatus fuit. Ambros. lib. 3. de fide cap. 6. legit abundantiùs, ut significetur, Deum nostra opera abundantiùs & magis remunerari, quam ipsa in se merentur.

Verbum ἐπιχορηγέσεται Vulg. reddidit, ministrabitur, utens simplice pro composito subministrabitur. Syrus habet verbum [מתיהבא]dabitur vobis introitus in regnum aeternum h. e. habebitis liberum & apertum ingressum in regnum aeternum Domini & Salvatoris nostri Iesu Christi. Pro εἰς τὴν αἰώνιον βασιλείαν quidam Codd. legunt ἐπουράνιον βασιλείαν. Ambrosius d. l. & Idacius contra Varimadum legunt, in aeternum imperium. Idem Ambrosius legit, Dei & Domini nostri Salvatoris Iesu Christi, atque exeo contra Arianos argumentatur, Patris ac Filii regnum non esse divisum sed aequale, idemque amborum, ac proinde consubstantiales esse, cùm non possit Patris, quem dicunt Ariani Filio maiorem esse, ius regni minoris esse, nec Filii si minor est secundum divinitatem, regnum esse aequale.

Caeterum in verbo ἐπιχορηγηθήσεται respicit Apostolus ad v. 5. in quo dixerat, ἐπιχορηγήσατε in fide virtutem; & ad vers. 8. in quo dixerat, ταῦτα γὰρ ὑμῖν ὑπάρχοντα καὶ πλεονάζοντα. Hoc ergo vult dicere. Si subministraveritis in fide virtutem, & reliqua priùs enumerata, sicque divites fueritis in bonis operibus, Deus ex gratia opulenter vobis suppeditabit ingressum in aeternum Christi regnum, sicque divites eritis in praemiis caelestibus, quae â Domino & Salvatore nostro Christo vobis ex gratia conferentur. Si fidem bonis operibus demonstrabitis, suppeditabitur vobis fidei incrementum, & in fide perserverantia, ut in via mandatorum divinorum, tanquam in studio ad propositam metam decurratis, sed & cor vestrum laetitiâ implebitur, & fortitudine, & ardenti desiderio verae gloriae, ut possitis firmam facere electionem vestram.

Q. 1. Quare bona opera fructibus arborum comparentur? Resp. 1. ob testimonium. Sicut bonitas fructuum testatur de bonitate arboris: Sic opera bona testantur de interiore renovatione cordis. 2. ob beneplacitum. Sicut fructus boni suâ suavitate gustum hominis afficiunt: sic bona opera DEO placent. 3. ob periculum. Sicut arbor infrugisera excinditur, & in ignem mittitur: sic destituti operibus bonis, sunt ignis infernalis materia.

Q. 2. Anμυωπάζωνrectiùs vertatur lusciosus, vel, manu palpans? Resp. 1. μυωπάζων deducitur â nomine μύωψ, cum μυωπάζων nihil aliud sit, quàm μύωξ εἰμὶ. Quinam autem dicantur μύωπες, cognosci potest ex loco Aristotelis in Problem. sect. 31. ubi quaerit, διὰ τὶ οἱ μύωπες συνάγοντες τὰ βλέφαρα ὁρῶσιν; cur μυωπεςcontractis palpebris videant? ac postea subiungit: οἱ ἐκ γενετῆς τὰ μὲν ἐγγυς βλέποντος, τὰ δὲ ἐξ ἀποστάσεως οὐχ ὁρῶντες, sc. μύωπεςdicuntur; quod ab ortu primo proxima quidem vident, romota vero non vident. Postmodum addit, ἐναντία δὲ πάσχουσιν οἱ γηρῶντος τοῖς μυωπάζουσιν, τὰ γὰρ ἐγγὺς μὴ ὁρῶντος τὰ πόῤῥωθεν βλέπουσι.At senibus vitium huic contrarium accidit, siquidem senes admota non videntes, longè reducta vident. Propter hunc Aristotelis locum Rob. Stephanus in Thesauro Graecae linguae, & in Concordantiis N. T. censet, μυωπάζων commodissimè verti, nihil procul cernens, quâ ratione dicti Apostolici sensus foret. Cui virtutes hae non adsunt, is lusciosus est, atque eo modo caecutit, ut rebus mundanis, utpote proximis aciem oculorum intendat, ad caelestia verò, utpote procul posita, eam dirigere nequeat. 2. Ad hanc significationem participii μυωπάζων referri posset, quòd iuxta etymologiam, sive ipsam compositionem μυωπάζων dicitur q. μύων ὦπα seu ὦπας,qui connivet oculis. Qui enim procul posita videre nequeunt, oculos parumper ex parte claudunt, & connivent, ut aciem illorum eò intendere possint. Favet etiam huic significationi, quod Budaeus tradit, Dionysium Arcopagitam uti hoc verbo pro coecutio, quodque Gellius lib. 4. N. A. cap. 2. dicit, μύωπαâ Latinis vocari lusciosum. 3. Sed cùm praecesserit nomen τυφλὸς, quod absolutè & simpliciter significat coecum, ideò per μυωπάζων h. l. non potest intelligi, qui lusciosus est vel coecutit, vel conniventibus oculis videt, vel procul posita videre nequit, talis siquidem non potest vocari caecus, cùm adhuc videat, licet aliquo oculorum seu visus vitio laboret. Rectiùs igitur μυωπάζων redditur manu palpans, quod est proprium coecorum, qui non solùm manibus, sed etiam pedibus palpitando viam quaerunt. 4. Proinde Erasmus deducit hoc nomen â μυῶνâ muribus, qui extra cavernas nihil vident, sed parietem, aut tabulam, aut si quid aliud obvium fuerit, sequi solent, donec cavum nacti fuerint. Robertus Stephanus existimat, Erasmum in hac etymologia apertè deceptum fuisse, cùm tamen ipse Stephanus agnoscat, μυωπίαν usurpari de murium cavernula, ex μῦς & ὀπὴ, mutato ο in ω sic dicta, in qua significatione vox μυωπία usurpatur ab Aristotele de animalibus lib. 6. μυωπίας ὕες ἀνορύττουσι, & ab Aeliano, qui de muribus sic scribit, καὶ μελλούσης τῆς οἰκίας ἀπολισθαίνειν, ἀπολείπουσι τὰς μυωπίας αὐτῶν. Graeca Scholia μυωπάζων exponunt per τυφλώττεινexcoecatum esse, more coecorum viam praetentare, ac metaphoram ductam statuunt â subterraneis muribus, quos talpas vocant, quòd perpetuò coeci sint. 5. Sensus ergo dicti Apostolici hic est. Cui enumeratae virtutes non adsunt, is coecus est, coeci instar manu palpat, nesciens quò iter suum dirigat. Procul dubio respicit Apostolus ad locum Mosaicum, Deut. 28. vers. 28,Percutiet te Dominus amentiâ & coecitate & stupore cordisv. 29.& palpabis in meridie, quem admodum palpat coecus in caligine. Estius huic collationi opponit, quòd eo loco sint diversae dictiones in Graeco, quibus ista palpatio significetur. Atqui si vel maximè hîc non habeat locum parallelismus verborum, tamen parallelismus rerum, qualis etiam statui potest in aliis Scripturae dictis, cum hoc loco Apostolico collatis. Iob. 5. vers. 14.Per diem incurrent tenebras & q. in nocte, sic palpabunt in meridie.cap. 12. v. 25.Palpabunt q. in tenebris & non in luce, & errare eos faciet q. ebrios.Esai. 59. v. 10.Palpavimus sicut coeci parietem & veluti absque oculis attrectavimus, impegimus in meridie. 6. Quidam, ut obtineant, cum, cui desunt enumeratae virtutes, diverso respectu dici coecum ac lusciosum, sive oculis conniventem, adducunt locum Paulinum 1. Cor. 8. v. 2. tanquam huic nostrò parallelum, ut sit sensus. Quamvis existimet, se aliquid videre ac scire, tamen reverâ nihil videt ac scit, quo ferè sensu Christus Pharisaeis dicit,Iohan. 9. v. 41.Quia dicitis, videmus, peccatum vestrum manet. Sed manifestum est, τὸ μυωπάζειν non κατὰ δόξαν, sed κατ' ἀληθείαν illis, de quibus Apostolus loquitur, tribui. 7. Quidam existimant, paerticipiumμυωπάζωνper quandam quasi correctionem nominiτυφλὸςsubiici, q. d. Apostolus. Coecus est, aut si non prorsus coecus, lusciosus, instar lusciosi caecutit, ut qui non rectè aspiciat atque aestimet beneficium purgationis â peccatis. Sed hac ratione inserenda fuisset particula disiunctiva ἢ τυφλὸς ἔστι ἢ μυωπάζων. Iam verò Apostolus per appositionem dicit τυφλὸς ἔστι μυωπάζων. Ergo μυωπάζων non significat aliquid minus quàm τυφλὸς.

Q. 3. De qua peccatorum purgatione Apostolus loquatur? 1. Quidam volunt, Apostolum in specie respicere ad purgationem illam peccatorum, quae fit in Baptismo, & vetera peccata vocari ea, quae fuére ante Baptismum commissa. Oecumenius in h. l. Cùm cognoverit, dum purgatus fuit sancto Baptismate, se multitudine peccatorum fuisse ablutum ac liberatum, & ex ea ablutione sanctitatem se accepisse, cùm deberet sobriè agere & dare operam, ut sanctificationem sibi conservaret, sine qua Deum nemo videbit, ipse oblivioni hoc mandavit. Gloss. ordin. Ille peccat mortaliter, videtur oblitus pacti, quod in Baptismo cum DEO iniit. 2. Sed rectiùs dicitur, Apostolum in genere loqui de peccatorum remissione, sive in Baptismo, sive post Baptismum in vera paenitentia per fidem ea fuerit impetrata. Eo enim fine Deus ex gratia tùm in Baptismo, tum etiam post Baptismum in vera paenitentia per fidem peccata nobis remittit, ut in posterum â peccatis abstineamus, ac in vera sanctitate & iustitia DEO serviamus, Luc. 1. v. 74. sicut Christus homini â se sanato dicit, Iohan. 5. vers. 14.Ecce, sanus factus es, inposterum noli ampliùs peccare, ne deterius quid tibi contingat. Quotquot igitur prioribus peccatis sese rursus implicari patiuntur, meritò dicuntur prioris illius purgationis obliti, cùm non observent, nec adimpleant finem, propter quem prior illa peccatorum purgatio ipsis ex gratia obtigerit, quae est damnabilis ignorantia ἀχαριστία, cuius exaggerationem in cap. 2. v. 20. & seqq. Apostolus subiungit.

Q. 4. An de certitudine vocationis & electionis respectu nostri vel aliorum Apostolus loquatur? Resp. 1. Beda, ut & Scholia Graeca, respectu aliorum vocationem & electionem firmam faciendam esse dicunt, ut sit sensus. Certam facite aliis hominibus electionem & vocationem vestram, ut illi integritatem vitae vestrae, probitatemque morum atque praestantiam bonorum operum liquidò cernentes agnoscant, & fateri cogantur, vocationem & electionem vestram, h. e. disciplinam fidei & re igionis Christianae, ad quam â DEO vocati & electi estis, & quam colitis ac profitemini, esse veram & sanctam & â DEO profectam. Eodem modo exponunt Hugo, Dionys. Carthus. Glossa ordinaria & alii. 2. Sed consequentia ostendunt, de certitudine vocationis & electionis respectu nostri Apostolum agere: sequitur namque, Haec enim facientes non peccabitis aliquando, sic enim abundanter vobis ministrabitur ingressus in regnum caelorum. 3. Locus ergo huic nostro parallelus est. 2. Corinth. 13. vers. 5.Vosipsos probate, an sitis in fide, an non cognoscitis vosmetipsos, quia Christus in vobis est, nisi fortè reprobi estis?

Q. 5. An de electione ad gratiam, an verò ad gloriam Apostolus loquatur? Resp. 1. Quidam existimant, per ἐκλογὴν h. l. intelligi electionem ad gratiam, quae est eadem cum κλήσει. Ambrosius Catharinus negat, h. l. sermonem esse de praedestinatis, quia nec Petrus praedestinatos sciebat, ad quos scribebat, nec si sciebat, interearat, illis id revelare. Statuit igitur, Petrum loqui de illa electione, per quam de multa hominum turba eripiuntur aliqui & diriguntur ad notitiam fidei & Christi. Hanc explicationem Lorinus dicit sibi non displicere. 2. At si de hac ad gratiam electione Apostolus loqueretur, praeponendum fuisset nomen ἐκλογῆς, & ἐξηγητικῶς subiungendum nomen κλήσεως, sensu eo. Studete firmam facere electionem h. e. vocationem vestram. Quia verò praeponitur nomen κλήσεως, quod denotat vocationem in tempore, ideò nomen ἐκλογῆς rectiùs accipitur de electione, quae facta est ab aeterno ad gloriam, hoc sensu. Operam date sedulam, ut vocationem vestram, quâ in tempore ad regnum gratiae vocati estis; & electionem, quâ ab aeterno ad regnum gloriae electi estis, certam ac firmam faciatis.

Εναντιοφανειαι 1. Cui haec non adsunt, coecus est,v. 9. Sed Iohann. 9. v. 14. Christus dicit Pharisaeis. Si coeci essetis, non haberetis peccatum.

Resp. 1. Lorinus sic conciliat, Petrum fortassè meliùs dixisse, coecatum esse, quàm coecum. At hoc est corrigere textum. 2. Christus illos vocat coecos, qui coecitatem suam nativam & acquisitam agnoscunt, ac per ipsum, utpote mundi lucem, illuminari expetunt, ut ostendit oppositio.

2. Haec enim facientes, non offendetis aliquando.v. 10. At Iac. 3. v. 2.πολλὰ πταίουσιν ἅπαντες. Resp. 1. Iacobus loquitur de lapsibus infirmitatis, â quibus per paenitentiam statim quis resurgit. Prov. 24. v. 16.Septies in die cadit iustus & resurgit. (Quamvis hoc dictum directè & propriè videatur agere de liberatione ex calamitatibus. Confer Tarnov. in Exercit. p. 49. edit. prioris.) Petrus verò loquitur de lapsibus eiusmodi, â quibus per paenitentiam homo non resurgit. 2. Nimirum τὸ πταίειν commune est tùm maioribus & gravioribus; tùm minoribus & levioribus lapsibus; ac significat, non solùm offendere & impingere, sed etiam labi & corruere, adeoque ita cadere, ut quis non resurgat. Apud Aristidem πταίσαντες τῶν μαχῶν h. e. ἐν μάχαις dicuntur, qui in praelio succubuerunt. Pro ratione igitur subiectae materiae de gravioribus vel levioribus lapsibus est accipiendum. Beda in h. l. de maioribus peccatis dicit, quae quicunque egerit, non habet haereditatem in regno DEI & Christi, & â quibus omnis, qui supradictis virtutibus se manciparit, immunis Domino permanet. 3. Ex quo etiam apparet, quid Salmeroni respondendum sit, qui ex h. l. colligit, hominem posse esse sine peccato.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Tertiâ iam vice in v. 8. Apostolus mentionem facit τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιγνώσεως, per quam intelligit fidem in Christum. v. 2. expotat, ut gratia & pax illis, ad quos scribit, multiplicetur in agnitione Domini nostri Iesus Christi.v. 3.Per agnitionem eius, qui vocavit nos, omnia, quae ad vitam & pietatem faciunt, nobis donata esse, asserit. In hoc v. 8. docet, quòd cognitio illa Christi in bonis operibus nos fertiles reddere debeat. In fine Epistolae cap. 3. v. 18.

admonet eos, ut crescant in gratia & agnitione Christi. Quia ergo toties Apostolus fidem definit per γνῶσιν καί ἐπίγνωσιν, ex eo manifestum, quàm absurdus sit Bellarminus, quando lib. 1. de Iusti. cap. 7. sub finem statuit, fidem meliùs definiri per ignorantiam, quàm per notitiam.

2. Ex v. 9. contra Anabaptistas & Calvinianos colligi potest, eos, qui peccatorum suorum purgationem consecuti sunt, posse iterum illis involvi, ac proinde fide, per quam purgationis illius participes facti sunt, ac gratiâ Dei, quae cum peccatorum remissione individuo nexu coniuncta est, iterum excidere. Nec obverti potest, fidem illorum non fuisse veram, quia purgatio peccatorum nemini obtingit, nisi per veram & vivam fidem. Tossanus exponit tantùm de oblatione huisu beneficii in verbo Evangelii, eiusdemque significatione in Baptismo. Sed manifestum est, Apostolum non de solâ oblatione, sed etiam de collatione huius beneficii, adeoque de peccatorum remissione per fidem olim acceptâ, sed per peccata contra conscientiam iterum amissâ loqui.

3. Ex v. 10. colligitur, verè pios & in Christum credentes posse esse de electione sua certos, non quidem certitudine absoluta, h. e. ex absoluto Dei decreto dependente, sed ordinatâ, h. e. dependente â Dei proposito, per Christum in Evangelio nobis manifestato. Sic enim ex h. l. concludimus. Qui electionem suam possunt & debent firmam facere, illi possunt esse de electione sua certi. Verè in Christum credentes possunt ac debent electionem suam firmam facere. Ergo verè in Christum credentes possunt esse de electione sua certi. Inde Thomas in comm. ad h. l. rectè sic commentatur. Ut per bona opera sc. exteriora certam faciatis, h. e. ostendatis vestram vocationem ad fidem ex tempore, & electionem per praedestinationem ab aeterno, ut sc: certi sitis, vos vocatos & â Deo electos.

Contrarium statuit Concilium Tridentinum sess. 6. cap. 12. & eius decisioni inhaerentes Pontificii, Gregorius de Valentia Tom. 1. Disp. 1. q. 23. punct. 6. assert. 4. Bellarminus lib. 3. de iustif. cap. 12. Becanus tract. 1. Theol. Schol. cap. 14. q. 6. §. 6. Cornelius â Lapide in cap. 16. Levit. Bened. Iustin. in comm. Phil. 2. v. 12. Lorinus & Estius in h. l. Pererius disp. 8. in cap. 8. Rom. Illorum igitur exceptiones examinandae veniunt.

Bellarm. d. lib. cap. 9. §. ult. excipit, hoc testimonium non posse afferri pro nostra de certitudine electionis sententia. 1. cùm certitudinem priorem esse velimus operibus, non posteriorem. 2. cùm certitudo, quae ex operibus nascitur, non possit esse fidei, sed coniecturalis 3. cum Apostolus non tàm loquatur de certitudine ex parte subiecti, quàm ex parte obiecti. Id enim monet, ut per bona opera certam h. e. ratam & firmam vocationem & electionem faciamus. Nam cùm DEUS nos elegerit, ut essemus sancti, Eph. 1. illi electionem suam confirmant & certam reddunt, qui sancti & immaculati fieri student, & in caritate magis ac magis, Deo adiuvante proficiunt.

Resp. 1. Bonorum operum nomine vel intelliguntur tantùm bona opera externa, vel interior renovatio. Prioritas alia est ordinis, alia temporis. Certitudo alia est gratiae & fidei praesentis, sive iustificationis: alia gloriae & fidei perseverantis sive electionis. Utraque pendet vel â testificatione Spiritus Sancti interiori, vel â testimonio bonorum operum exteriori. Certitudo prior est bonis operibus, si quaeratur de bonis operibus externis, de prioritate temporis, & de certitudine, quae pendet â testimonio bonorum operum exteriori. Certitudo posterior est bonis operibus, si quaeratur de renovatione, quae cum regeneratione individuo nexu est coniuncta, de prioritate ordinis & de certitudine, quae pendet â testificatione Spiritus interiori. 2. Certitudo coniecturalis est ἀντικείμενον ἐν προσκειμένῳ. 3. Apostolus agit omninò de certitudine ex parte obiecti, requirit enim, ut credentes certam faciant electionem suam, utique non apud Deum, sed in suis mentibus, ut firmiter statuere possint, se esse in numero electorum.

2. Estius, Pererius, Lorinus, Iustinianus d. l. excipiunt, βεβαίανrectiùs verti firmam quàm certam, ut sit sensus, constanti bonorum operum studio firmari ac stabiliri hominem Christianum, ne â sua vocatione & electione, h. e. ab eo ad quod vocatus & electus est, excidat, quo sensuApoc. 3. v. 11.dicitur. Tene quod habes, ne alius accipiat coronam tuam. Probat hoc ex eo, quiaβεβαίανpropriè significat firmam, & quia firmitati opponitur lapsus in parte proximè sequente, cum certitudini dubitatio vel incertitudo opponi deberet.

Resp. non agnoscimus oppositionem inter firmum & certum, 1. quia firmitas includit certitudinem. Quod alicui est firmum, illud etiam eidem est certum. Firmitas est stabilimentum rei; certitudo stabilimentum conceptus, rei in mente respondentis. 2. Vulgata versio h. l. βεβαίαν reddidit certum; ab eius autoritate Pontificii per Concilium Tridentinum discedere non audent. 3. Syrus reddidit per [שריר] quod significat, firmum, solidum, certum, stabilem. 4. Ubicunque in Scripturis usurpatur vox βεβαία, ibi non solùm firmitatem significat, sed etiam certitudinem connotat. Sic Rom. 4. v. 16.firma promissio est etiam certa promissio. 2. Cor. 1. v. 7.firma spes est etiam certa spes. Vidit hoc Estius, ideò textum Apostolicum sic παραφράζει.Diligentiùs operam date, ut vocationem vestram, quâ per DEI gratiam vocati estis, & electionem, quâ ab aeterno electi & praedestinati estis, ad hereditatem regni caelestis, certam firmamque faciatis.

Et postea: Redditur autem certa & firma vocatio & electio cuiusque per bona opera. Et interiectis aliquot, postquam dixisset, propriùs explicari mentem Apostoli, siβεβαίανvertatur, firmam, subiungit. Veruntamen sive certitudinem, sive firmitatem hîc intelligas, satis patet ex sensu, quem dedi, verba Petri nihil adiuvare eos, qui fidem ab unoquoque specialem exigunt suae electionis, quâ nimirum certissimè statuat, se esse electum, quae non est fides, sed temeraria praesumtio; & doctrina, quâ docentur homines ad fidem istam specialem ipsos teneri, tantum abest, ut fidei sit doctrina, ut contrà sit perdita & perditrix haeresis, â Patribus Concilii Tridentini damnata.

3. Aliter igitur excipit Estius; certam cuiusque vocationem & electionem fieri per bona opera, quia studium bonorum operum signum est electionis certum suo modo h. e. in genere signorum benè probabilium: sic enim usurpari frequenter solet certitudo, Pererius d. l. n. 37. concedit. assiduâ exercitatione hominis in bonis operibus certam ei posse fieri iustificationem eius, non tamen certitudine fidei divinae, cui nullo modo potest subesse falsum sed humanâ quadam & morali certitudine.

Resp. 1. iam ante diximus, nos non statuere electionis certitudinem absolutam, sed ordinatam. 2. Certitudo illa non tantùm dependet ex bonis operibus ex quibus velut ex certis signis confirmamur, quòd simus verè fideles & â Deo electi. 1. Ioh. 3. v. 18. & 19. sed etiam ex aliis fundamentis paulò pòst enumerandis, inter quae eminet interior testificatio Spir. S. Rom. 8. v. 16.Ipse Spir. testimonium reddit Sp. nostro, quòd simus filii Dei. 3. Hoc Spiritus testimonium non est probabile tantùm & incertum, sed infallibile & certissimum 4. Ergo certitudo haec non est tantùm coniecturalis, ut Bellarminus loquitur, nec in genere signorum benè probabilium, ut Estius loquitur, sed certitudo propriè dicta, qualis est rerum firmarum & infallibilium. 5. Estius nullo exemplo, ostendit, in genere signorum benè probabilium locum habere certitudinem propriè sic dictam, distincta enim sunt τεκμήρια signa certa, & εἰκότα signa probabilia ac verisimilia. Estius ipse in comm. Rom. 8. v. 38. concedit, quod homo verè credens & pius caetui electorum se annumerare possit ac debeat, idque tantò maiori fiducia, quanto plura ac maiora in se percipit electionis signa.

4. Lorinus sic excipit. Magnam cum probabilitate & verisimilitudine coniunctam, ut omnes hîc expositores notant, fiduciam ingenerant opera bona, sed pium timorem & diligentem tuendae salutis curam relinquunt ac exigunt etiam. Resp. pius ille sive filialis timor, & diligens tuendae salutis cura, â nobis non negatur, nec per certitudinem fidei excluditur.

5. Est & haec Lorini exceptio, non tam nobis, quàm aliis vocationem & electionem fieriβεβαίανcertam & compertam per bona opera. Resp. quid de hac expositione statuendum sit, vidimus superiùs. Ac si aliis vocatio & electio nostra potest fieri certa, multò magis nobis ipsis.

Cùm ergò evictum sit ex hoc loco Apostolico, pios de electione sua posse & debere esse certos, iam porrò explicandum, quâ ratione de electione sua certi esse possint. 1. Extra controversiam hîc non agitur de certitudine electionis apud DEUM, sed de certitudine in cordibus piorum, quia apud DEUM electio fuit certa, cùm actu nondùm existerent credentes, ac apud ipsum electio semper est firma & immobilis, propter voluntatis immutabilitatem. Esai. 46. vers. 10.Rom. 11. v. 29.2. Timoth. 2. v. 19. etiam ab aeterno antequam quidquam boni agant credentes. Rom. 9. v. 11. 2. Electio ex Dei ordinatione est eorum, qui beneficia passione & morte Christi parta, inque verbo Evangelii sibi oblata, fide amplectuntur, & in fide ad finem usque vitae perseverant. Qualis ergo certitudo fidei & perseverantiae, talis etiam certitudo electionis. 3. De fide sua verè pios in Christum credentes certos esse posse, manifestum est ex loco Apostolico 2. Cor. 13. v. 5.Vos metipsos tentate, an sitis in fide, vos ipsos probate. An non cognoscitis vos ipsos, quòd Christus Iesus in vobis est, nisi fortè reprobi estis. Utique ergò verè pius certò scire potest, se verae fidei & per consequens etiam beneficiorum Christi esse participem. 4. Potest autem quis esse certus de sua fide tum â priori, videlicet ratione causarum, quae sunt gratia DEI in ordine causae Principalis; verbum & sacramenta in ordine causarum instrumentalium. Causis illis in actu positis & non impeditis, h. e. quando verbum audimus, sacramentis utimur & Spiritui Sancto obicem non ponimus, sequitur effectus, sc. ipsa fides; tum â posteriori, videlicet ab effectis & consequentibus fidei, quae sunt renovatio interior, (quae cognoscitur ex lucta carnis & Spiritus Gal. 5. v. 17. siquidem ea non nisi in renatis & verè credentibus locum habet) peccatorum displicentia & detestatio, Spiritus Sanctus interior testificatio, studiosa legis divinae observatio, dilectionem DEI & proximi, patientiam in cruce, & alia bonorum operum exercitia complectens. Ex istorum bonorum operum exercitio intelligimus, quòd Spiritu DEI agamur, quia bona opera sunt fructus Spiritus,Gal. 5. v. 22.Qui autem Spiritu DEI aguntur, illi sunt filii DEI.Rom. 8. v. 14. utique per fidem Iohan. 1. v. 9. Beda in h. l. Qui fidei Sacramentis, quae praeceperunt, bona quoque opera perseveranter adiungunt, isti suam vocationem & electionem certam intuentibus facient. 5. De hoc cognitionis medio loquuntur multa scripturae dicta. Rom. 8. v. 14.Qui Spiritu DEI aguntur, hi sunt filii DEI.v. 16.ipse Spiritus testimonium reddit Spiritui nostro, quòd simus filii DEI.Gal. 5. v. 24.Qui Christi sunt, crucifigunt carnem cum concupiscentiis & affectibus.1. Iohann. 2. v. 3.In hoc scimus, quod cognoverimus eum, si mandata eius observemus.v. 5.Qui servat verbum eius, verè in eo caritas DEI perfecta est. In hoc scimus, quoniam in ipso sumus.cap. 3. v. 14.Scimus, quoniam translati sumus de morte in vitam, quoniam diligimus fratres.v. 24.In hoc scimus, quòd maneat in nobis, ex Spiritu, quem dedit nobis.cap. 5. vers. 10.Qui credit in Filium DEI, habet testimonium DEI in seipso. 6. Nec solùm de fide, sed etiam de perseverantia fidei verè in Christum credentes certi esse possunt, non quidem absolutè, sed suo modo. Fundamenta illius certitudinis sunt duorum generum; quaedam ex parte DEI, quaedam ex parte nostra. Ex parte DEI, primò bona DEI voluntas & infallibilis eius promissio. Quia promisit Deus, se non tantùm velle in nobis bonum incipere, sed etiam perficere,Phil. 2. v. 12. inde certi esse possumus, quòd in fide nos sit conservaturus. Secundò, Dei virtus & ipsius potestas, 2. Tim. 1. vers. 12.Scio cui credidi & certus sum, quia potens est depositum meum servare in diem illum, 3. Dei fidelitas. 1. Cor. 1. v. 9.Fidelis Deus, per quem vocati estis in societatem Filii eiusv. 8.qui & confirmabit vos usque in finem sine crimine.cap. 10. v. 3.Fidelis Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis. Ex parte nostra, primò seria DEI invocatio. Quia promisit Deus, se preces nostras exauditurum, & quae ad salutem sunt necessaria nobis daturum, ideò petentes â Deo perseverantiam, de ea certi esse possumus. 1. Ioh. 5. v. 14.Si quid petiermus secundum voluntatem ipsius, audit nos. Secundò, continuata mediorum usurpatio. Per quae media Deus fidem primò in nobis accendit, per eadem media, videlicet verbi auditum & Sacramentorum usum, eandem in nobis augebit & conservabit, proinde ex usu illorum mediorum de perseverantia certi esse possumus. Tertiò, serium Spiritui Sancto non resistendi, nec in peccata mortalia consentiendi propositum. Possunt renati per gratiam Spiritus Sancti cavere peccata mortalia, proinde per firmum ea cavendi propositum de perseverantia possunt esse certi. August. de bono perseverantiae cap. 22. Ipsam obediendi perseverantiam â Patre luminum sperare debetis & quotidiants orationibus poscere, atque hoc faciendo confidere, non vos esse â praedestinatione populi eius alienos, quia etiam hoc ut faciatis, ipse largitur. Ex his omnibus facilè colligi potest, qualem electionis certitudinem statuamus, & ex quibus fundamentis illam certitudinem deducamus, ac proinde quid statuendum sit de eo, quòd ex solo bonorum operum studio aliqui eam arcessant.

4. Ex vers. 10. iterum evinci potest, renatos & iustificatos per peccata contra conscientiam posse excidere gratia DEI & salute. Si enim tum demum renati non labuntur, quando bonis operibus studere sedulò pergunt, sequitur quòd â studio bonorum operum cessantes labantur & excidant. Opponendum hoc errori Anabaptistarum & Calvinianorum, qui iam olim in Ioviniano Romae damnatus, ut refert Hieronymus lib. 2. contra Iovianian. uti etiam in Aficano quodam Concilio.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Ex vers. 8. Pontificii colligunt, fidem veram posse esse sine bonis operibus, sed non prodesse. Salmero in comm. Elicimus ex hoc loco, vanos esse omnes nostri temporis haereticos, qui contra tot Apostolorum testimonia, & quidem evidentissima, fidem nudam & solam magnificant & exaltant. Quid enim iuvat, CHRISTUM pro te mortuum per fidem apprehendere, nisi ei fidas & innitaris? quomodo autem animus fidere poterit ei, quem non diligit? fides ergo sine caritate non potest iustificare. Bellarminus lib. 4. de iustific. cap. 7, §. ult. hoc urget, quòd Augustinus lib. de fide & operibus cap. 14. testetur, Petrum, Iohann. Iacobum & Iudam intentionem suam eò potissimum dirigere, ut probent, opera bona iustificatis hominibus ad salutem esse necessaria, neque fidem solam sufficere, ut quidam eo tempore ex Epistolis Pauli malè intellectis praedicare coeperant. Estius in h. l. Fidem sine operibus esse posse, sed non prodesse, colligit ex eo, quòd Petrus studiosè in hac Epistola ad bona opera exhortetur, propter illos, qui ex Epistolis Pauli malè intellectis opera negligebant, solâ fide contenti. Idem urget Lorinus in h. l. Resp. 1. Nos opera bona non negligimus, nec negligenda esse dicimus. 2. Sed potiùs unà cum Apostolo & ex Apostolo studiosè ad bona opera exhortamur. 3. Docentes, veram & vivam fidem, quâ coram DEO iustificamur, non posse esse sine bonis operibus. 4. adeoque graviter illos errare dicimus, qui sibi persvadent, se habere veram fidem, licet studium bonorum operum negligant. 5. Quae verò haec est consequentia. Vera fides non est sine bonis operibus. Ergo non iustificat sine operibus? Distinguendum omninò inter bonorum operum praesentiam, & inter bonorum operum efficientiam, quam distinctionem Bellarminus ipse agnoscit lib. 4. de Iustif. cap. 7. 6. Distinguendum etiam inter fidem veram iustificantem, & inter inanem fidei persuasionem. Non contra illam, sed contra hanc pugnat Apostolica ad studium bonorum operum exhortatio. 7. Petrus enim inanem eorum persvasionem impugnat, qui talem fidem iustificantem sibi imaginantur, quae non ferat bonorum operum fructus. Contrarium ergo potiùs illius docet, quod Estius ipsi tribuit. 8. Lorinus in comm. 2. Petr. 3. v. 13. adducturus dictum Augustini lib. de fide & bon. oper. cap. 25. rectè monet, Augustinum disputare adversus operibus vaevos cum sola professione fidei. Nota, quod dicit, cum sola professione fidei, quia professio quidem fidei ab operibus separari potest, vera autem & viva fides nunquam est sine bonis operibus. 9. Excipit Lorinus, pugnantia â nobis doceri, cùm modò asseramus, fidem solam iustificare, nihilque aliud Deum â nobis requirere, quàm ut credamus; modò verò dicamus, fidem, quâ iustificari dicimur, operari caritatem, perseverantiam, innocentiam. Resp. haec verò minimè pugnant. Aliud enim est fidem iustificare sine operibus; aliud fidem esse sine operibus. Fides vera & viva non est sine operibus, interim opera non concurrunt unà cum fide ad iustificationem efficiendam. Non statim ea quae coniuncta sunt, ad unum eundemque effectum ἐνεργητικῶς concurrunt.

2. Ex eodem vers. colligunt Pontificii, â fide libus praestari posse bonorum operum abundantiam, tantum abesse, ut omne opus hominu sit peccatum. Estius in comm. Resp. 1. verè pios & in Christum credentes praestare posse bonorum operum abundantiam, nemo nostrûm negat. De Tabitha dicitur Actor. 9. v. 36.quòd fuerit plena bonis operibus; de Cornelio Actor. 10. v. 2.quòd fecerit eleemosynas multas & deprecatus fuerit DEUM semper.1. Tim. 6. v. 18.â divitibus huius seculi requirit Apostolus, ut divites fiant in bonis operibus. 2. Nemo etiam nostrûm dicit, omne opus hominis esse formaliter peccatum. 3. Hoc verò docemus, nullius hominis, (solo Christo θεανθρώπῳ excepto) opera bona tam perfecta esse, ut legi divinae plenè satisfaciant. distinguendum igitur inter bonorum operum copiam, & eorundem perfectionem absolutam. 4. Docemus & hoc, quòd bona opera piorum propter reliquias peccati in carne ipsorum adhuc haerentes sint immunda & peccati labe contaminata, quae adhaerens immundities itidem non tollit bonorum operum abundantiam, sed absolutam eorundem puritatem.

3. Lorinus ad eund. vers. sic annotat: καθιστάναιest efficere, reddere, ponere, locare, praeterea coràm statuere, firmare, stabilire, roborare, fructuosum robur dare, tueri, restituere, instituere, ac veluti erudire, & docere, committere tanquam in bello, sive ad bellum, componere ac sedare, ad bonam frugem reducere, quae omnia ostendunt vim bonorum operum ac fiduciam magnam, quam ingenerant ante iudicium & in ipso iudicio, de quo aliqui exponunt verba sequentia. In Domini nostri Iesu Christi cognitione. Graecèεἰς τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν,qui casus accusandi cum indicet futuram cognitionem, favet expositioni de cognitione iudiciaria.

Resp. 1. coactum est, per ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ h. l. intelligere diem iudicii, cùm Apostolus agat de cognitione Christi ea, quae piis in hac vita obtingith. e. de fide in Christum. 2. Quamvis omnia illa verbi καθιστάναι significata hûc accommodentur, (de quorum tamen quibusdam non immeritò adhuc quaeri poterat,) nondum tamen ex illis probari posset, vel quòd bona opera sint merita propriè dicta, vel quod fiducia in die iudicii in illis collocanda. Aliud enim est, pios in bonis operibus esse fructuosos, iisdemque ex gratia largissima praemia esse promissa; aliud vero pios operum suorum meritis illa praemia sibi acquirere. Prius Scriptura asserit, posterius negat. 3. Lorinus ipse praefert hunc sensum, quòd per opera virtutum non reddamur in fide seu in cognitione Christi infrugiferi.

4. Idem Lorinus ad eundem vers. sic commentatur. Denotat fructus vox rationem bonitatis & meriti in operibus iustorum, quae cum DEI gratia exercentur ab ipsis liberâ voluntate. Non est in eo similitudo cum fructu, quòd ut hic ex semine aut planta: sic naeturaliter & necessariò proficiscatur â iustis opus bonum: quanquam & similis quaedam ratio est, quatenus cultura utrobique necessaria est, quam non nisi liberè ac sponte adhibemus.

Resp. 1. Ex parabolicis locutionibus non ducuntur firma argumenta, nisi ipsa Scriptura monstret applicationem; nec comparationes extendendae sunt ultra tertium, propter quod adhibentur. 2. Quando bona opera comparantur fructibus, non denotatur meritum bonorum operum, sed eorum necessitas & utilitas. Fructus boni necessariò requiruntur ad demonstrandam arboris bonitatem, eorundemque maxima est utilitas. Sic bona opera requiruntur, ut ex illis personae bonitas agnoscatur; eadem etiam habent usum longè maximum. 3. Invertimus potiùs argumentum, ex appellatione fructus petitum. Quemadmodum sementis non est causa meritoria messis, nec plantatio fructuum, sed DEI benedictione illam hi consequuntur: sic bona opera non sunt causa meriotoria praemiorum caelestium, sed DEI benedictione ad illa haec consequuntur. 4. Nec est, quod Lorinus urgeat liberam culturam, in fructibus naturalibus & Spiritualibus requisitam. Fructus enim non sunt culturae illius merces ex merito, sed tantùm consequentia.

5. Adde, quòd cultura ad spirituales fructus necessaria non proficiscatur, nec proficisci possit ex naturalibus liberi arbitrii viribus, sed ex novis à Spiritu sancto donatis viribus, ut sic homo propter illam culturam magis obstringatur DEO, quàm ut DEUS illius debitor reddatur. Confer Hieronymum in cap. 6. Gal. super verba. Qui a. seminat in Spiritu &c. ubi inter caetera sic scribit. Illud pariter observandum, quod qui seminat in carne, cum additamento suae carnis ponitur. Qui autem seminat in Spiritu, non dicitur in Spiritu suo, sed simpliciter in Spiritu seminare. Qui enim bona seminat, non in suo quippiam, sed in DEI Spiritu seminat, de quo & vitam messurus est aeternam.

5. Idem Lorinus ad v. 9. sic annotat. Haeretici, qui gaudent in sola fidei luce, & Gnostici seu cognoscentes tantùm volunt esse, coeci sunt. Resp. patet ex dictis in ἐκδικ. prima.

6. Idem Lorinus ibid. ex voce purgationis colligit, nullum in renato superesse peccati vestigium. Resp. Distinguendum inter peccati formale, & materiale, sive reatum, & formitem. Reatus sive formale tollitur per purgationem, non autem materiale sive fomes. renovatio fomitem mortificat, & minuit, non tamen penitus ac radicitus tollit.

7. Vulgata versio in v. 10. inseruit per bona opera, quo modo etiam locum hunc Apostolicum allegat Concilium Tridentinum, & additum habet hunc προσδιορισμὸν versio Syriaca. Versionis vulgatae authoritatem secuti Pontificii Lutherum hoc nomine graviter accusant, quòd in versione Germanica hunc προσδιορισμὸν non expresserit. Lorinus dicit, Lutherum illud, per bona opera, expunxisse.

Resp. 1. Non habetur in Codicibus Graecis, nisi in paucis, quos adducit Robertus Stephanus, in quos ex Latina versione fuit translatus Beza memorat se reperisse in duobus MStis codd. Graecisδιὰ καλῶν ἔργων, sed illi fuêre recentioris scriptionis. 2. Caietanus Erasmus, Vatablus, Clarius, Adamus, Gagneius statuunt, duas illas voces per bona epera superfluere. 3. Biblia Isidori Clarii Episcopi Fulginatis, Venetiis Ann. 1557. impressa, illas voces excludunt. Biblia operis Regii itidem eas praetermittunt. 4. Estius dicit, Fortè Petrus haec non addidit, de quo tamen se contendere nolle, asserit. Id vero Lutheri patrocinio sufficit. 5. Si vel maximè concedamus, quod Estius urget & â nobis non negatur, per studium bonorum operum firmam fieri vocationem & electionem nostram, ac proinde subintelligendum esse illumπροσδιορισμὸν, ex eo tamen nondum potest inferri, debuisse eum â Luthero textui inseri, quia scopus Lutheri minimè fuit, paraphrasin, sed versionem adornare. 6. Lorinus pro insertione illarum vocum adducit Marcum Monachum, qui vixit anno Christi 300. pauloque ampliùs, qui eas legat, Item Antonium Melissam, qui etsi non legat opera, tamen de operibus hunc locum intelligat, serm. 1. tom. 5. Biblioth. par. 7. sed respondemus, aliud est genuina textus lectio, aliud exegetica eiusdem explicatio. 9. Quidam ex seq. pronomine ταῦτα evincere conantur, in verbis praecedentibus omninò legendumδιὰ καλῶν ἔργων,haec enim sc. bona opera facientes, Sed monuimus superiùs, per ταῦτα, intelligi posse virtutes in v. 5. 6. & 7. enumeratas.

8. Cornelius â Lapide ad eund. versic. sic annotat. Petrus loquitur de electione ad fidem & gratiam, consequenter tamen de electione ad gloriam, non antecedente & absoluta, sed consequente & conditionatâ.

Resp. Si haec intelliguntur opposita absoluto electionis decreto, quod Calviniani propugnant, facilè suffragamur. Sed si de mutabili quadam electione, ex qua homo iterum possit excidere, suffragium denegamus.

9. Ex eodem versiculo Gabriel Vasquez, Gregorius de Valentia, Ludovicus Molina in comm. Thom. Cornel. â Lapide in comm. h. l. evincere laborant, electionem ad gloriam â DEO fieri ex praevisis cuiusque meritis. Cùm enim Apostolus per bona opera electionem firmam facere iubeat, ex eo videtur sequi, quòd electio ex praevisione bonorum operum pendeat. Lorinus ad h. l. Ista Petri adhortatio facit, ut vocatio & electio pendeant ab operibus nostris. Et postea. Manere fixum debet, Deum & praenovisse, imò & praedestinavisse hos & illos fide & opere suos futuros.

Respond. 1. Electionem non pendere ex praevisione meritorum, suo loco multis confirmatum dedimus argumentis, videlicet ex appellatione electionis, causis, fine & ex tempore eiusdem, ex convenientia decreti & executionis, ex bonorum operum Natura, &c. 2. Nec potest contrarium ex hoc loco probari, quia Apostolus hîc non agit de electionis causis, sed de certitudine electionis respectu nostri. Docet, unde possimus esse certi, quòd simus in numero electorum, non autem ob quas causas Deus nos elegerit. 3. Inde Estius ipse ad h. l. sic commentatur, Non est ex verbis Petri consequens, electionem pendere â bonis operibus, quod ipsum confirmat evidentibus dictis Apostoli, Eph. 1. elegit nos, ut essemus Sancti cap. 2. creati in operibus bonis, quae praeparavit Deus, ut in illis ambulemus. 4. Subiungit quidem Estius, electionem secundùm aliquid â bonis operibus dependere, quatenus sc. aeterna felicitas, ad quam electi sumus, non datur adultis, nisimandata Dei servantibus, & quatenus aeterna illa felicitas pendet â bonis operibus, tanquam merces â merito. Sed prius est ambiguum, posterius falsum. Aeternam felicitatem, ad quam electi sumus, non dari adultis, nisi mandata Dei servantibus, duplici sensu accipi potest. Vel ut sit descriptio obiecti, quibus sc. aeterna felicitas detur, vel ut sit descriptio causae, propter quam eadem detur. Priore sensu acceptam propositionem concedimus, sed ex ea nondum inferri potest, electionem pendere â bonis operibus tanquam â causa. Conditio enim obiecti non statim est illius rei causa, quae obiecto tribuitur. Posteriore sensu accepta propositio falsa est & Scripturae contraria, quod ipsum de posteriore Estii assertione, quòd aeterna felicitas pendeat â bonis operibus, tanquam merces â merito, dicimus. Scriptura enim non nostris meritis, sed solius Christi merito hoc tribuit, quòd propter illud credentibus in ipsum aeterna felicitas obtingat, nec uspiam mercedem meriti, sed gratiae praedicat. 5. Nihil hîc dicemus de alia quadam ambiguitate, in verbis Estii latente, quando dicit, aeternam felicitatem, ad quam electi sumus, non dari adultis, nisi mandata DEI servantibus. Vel enim hoc intelligitur de perfecta & numeris omnibus absoluta legis impletione, vel de in choata mandatorum divinorum observatione. Si priorem intelligit, negamus, eam in huius vitae infirmitate in renatis locum habere, unde etiam ex operibus legis coram DEO non iustificatur omnis caro. Rom. 3. v. 20. Si posteriorem, non refragamur Estii assertioni. 6. Si felicitas aeterna ad quam electi sumus, datur propter bonorum operum nostrorum merita, falsum est, quòd electio non pendeat â bonis operibus, sicque Estius sibiipsi contradicit. Ratio connexionis pendet ab exactissima decreti & executionis convenientia. Propter quas causas Deus in tempore hominem salvat & glorificat, propter easdem ab aeterno eum constituit salvare & glorificare. Sed iuxta assertionem Estii propter merita bonorum operum DEUS in tempore hominem salvat & glorificat. Ergo etiam propter merita bonorum operum ab aeterno eum salvare & glorificare constituit, h. e. ad salutem elegit, & per conseq. electio â bonis operibus pendet. 7. Idem opponimus reliquis Pontificiis, qui negant electionem factam ex praevisione bonorum operum, & tamen merita operum propugnant, videlicet quòd sibi ipsis contradicunt. Barradius Tom. 3. Conc. Evang. lib. 4. cap. 19. pag. 303. Non praedestinat DEUS aut propter opera praevisa, aut propter bonum arbitrii usum. Praedestinat tamen, ut bona opera & bonum arbitrii usum habeamus, alioqui si bona opera, arbitriique bonum usum non habeamus, reprobi erimus. Lorinus ad h. l. Vocat & elegit Deus, quia vult, non propter illa opera. Ut autem illuc perveniant vocati, electi, praedestinati, quò ipse vult, inter media conditionesque decrevit eadem opera, quibus faciendis gratiam praebeat efficacem.

10. Cornelius â Lapide ad eund. vers. sic annotat. Ex hisce S. Petri verbis colligunt Doctores, non tantùm electionem ad gloriam, sed etiam ipsam praedestinationem ad gratiam pendere â cooperatione liberi arbitrii, etiamsi haec illius non sit causa. Ita Gregorius de Valentia. 1. p. q. 23. Disp. 1. punct. 4. Lorinus ad h. l. Frustra satageremus, nisi esset in nobis liberum arbitrium. Resp. aliud est vocationem firmam facere per bona opera, aliud verò vocationem pendere â bonis operibus, vel â cooperatione liberi arbitrii. Prius asserit Apostolus, qui enim bonis operibus student, ex eo confirmantur, quòd Spiritu DEI agantur, ac proinde sint filii DEI: sed ex eo non potest inferri posterius, quia tota Scriptura testatur, vocationem esse opus merae gratiae divinae, quòd non pendeat â cooperatione liberi arbitrii, tanquam â merito congrui. Interim libenter concedimus, illos ordinariè non converti ad DEUM, qui Spiritus Sanctus operationi pertinaciter resistunt; nec illos salvari, qui post regenerationem concupiscentiis carnis suç indulgent, & gratiam DEI in vacuum acceperunt.

11. Lorinus & alii Pontificii ex eod. vers. incertitudinem gratiae probare conantur, hoc enim modo colligunt. Si per bona opera quaerenda est certitudo vocationis, ergo & iustificationis. Atqui si certitudo iustificationis pendet â bonis operibus, consequens est, primò, hominem non esse certum de sua iustificatione, mox ut est iustificatus. Secundè, certitudinem iustificationis non pendere â sola fide. Tertio, iustificationem nostram non esse certam certitudine fidei, quae est infallibilis, sed operum, quae est coniecturalis.

Resp. 1. Iustificationem faciendam esse firmam per studium bonorum operum, concedimus, sed nullum aliud certitudinis huius principium dari negamus, uti constat ex dictis in ἐλέγχω tertio. 2. Bonorum operum nomine non tantùm intelligenda sunt bona opera externa, sed etiam renovatio interior, serium vitae sanctae propositum, ac alii motus spirituales â Spiritu Sancto excitati. 3. Per bona opera iubemur firmam facere vocationem, non ut vocatio, quae priùs incerta erat, fiat certa, sed ut quae certa est, eius certitudo bonis operibus ostendatur. βεβαιοῦν enim non semper usurpatur de re, quae primò est incerta, sed etiam de ea, quae etsi per se certa sit, tamen magis magisque confirmatur. Marc. 16. vers. 20.Rom. 15. v. 8. Quòd si ergo vocationis certitudo non pendet absolutè â bonis operibus, multò minùs certitudo iustificationis.

12. Idem Lorinus ex verbis, Magis satagite, colligit opera supererogationis. Non improbabiliter, inquit, aliqui dicuntur indicari, per opera supererogationis reddi magis certam vocationem & electionem, atque volentibus huiusmodi certitudinem sibi comparare, opus esse non simplici mandatorum observatione contentum esse, sed conatum altiùs dirigere.

Resp. 1. Opera supererogationis & Petrus & tota Scriptura ignorat, ut suo loco docetur. 2. Praeceptum Apostolicum est generale, ad omnes Christianos pertinens. Atqui opera supererogationis non requiruntur ab omnibus per modum praecepti. 3. Lorinus ipse agnoscit, voculamμᾶλλονnon esse augentis, sed corrigentis, ut sit sensus. Potiùs satagite vel studete, ut per bona opera in vocatione & electione vos stabiliatis. 4. Si de operibus supererogationis hîc esset sermo, consequens foret, solos Religiosos habere vocationis & electionis suae certitudinem. At consequens hoc non concedent Pontificii, tribuentes omnibus verè piis certitudinem illam coniecturalem, de qua Petrum hoc loco agere arbitrantur.

13. Idem Lorinus ad h. l. sic annotat. Lutherus expunxit illa verba per bona opera, sicut etiam expunxit,1. Thess. 4. v. 3.ut abstineatis â fornicatione, & exEphes. 6. v. 13.delevit, quod de perfectione praescribitur, quae ipsi nimis gravis ac molesta visa est.

Resp. 1. Quid de προσδιορισμὸς, per bona opera, statuendum sit, superiùs fuit expositum. 2. In 1. Thess. 4. v. 3. & Eph. 6. v. 13. nihil quidquam eorum expunxit, quae in Graeco textu habentur; sed nec in vernacula versione quidquam eorum omisit, sed fidelissimè expressit, ut αὐτοψία testatur.

14. Idem Lorinus ex hoc loco colligit tùm bonorum operum necessitatem, quam etiam probet verbumσπουδάζειν,tùm verè & propriè dictam operum iustorum bonitatem, cùm sint vocationi & electioni apta.

Resp. 1. Προσδιορισμός ille, per bona opera, non est textus authentici pars indubitata. 2. Operum bonorum necessitatem ratione coëxstientiae cum fide non negamus, sed necessitatem ratione coëfficientiae, & quidem meritoriae. 3. Nec operum bonitatem negamus, sed absolutam perfectionem & mundiciem.

15. Calviniani ex hoc loco elicere satagunt, veram fidem & ex ea promanans bonorum operum studium electis esse eo modo proprium, ut ipsis solis & unicè competat, ex quo porrò inferunt, fidem semel acceptam iterum amitti non posse. Beza in hunc locum. Individuo nexu coharent propositum, electio, vocatio, sanctificatio & iustificatio. Piscator in h. l. Bonae opera sunt ipsa ratio, quâ electio & vocatio in mentibus fidelium firma efficitur, dum scil. illae ratiocinantur ex propriis effectis ad causam procreantem. Etenim bona opera non nisi ab electis & efficaciter vocatis proficisci possunt.

Resp. 1. Demonstravimus suo loco, fidem semel habitam amitti posse, nec esse terminos convertibiles, renatos & electos, cùm quidam renati non sint electi, videlicet illi, qui per peccata contra conscientiam fidem, & renovationem iterum amittunt. 2. Nec potest contrarium ex hoc dicto Apostolico demonstrari. Quamvis enim ex bonis operibus, tanquam ex certis signis, confirmemur de fide, & consequenter de electione, tamen non ex solo bonorum operum testimonio certitudo electionis pendet, sed etiam ex aliis principiis, ut ex dictis patet. 3. Nec sufficit ad certitudinem electionis certitudo fidei praesentis, sed etiam requiritur certitudo perseverantiae, sive fidei perseverantis, cùm non nisi in fide ad finem usque vitae perseverantes sint electi.

16. Lorinus ad verbum πταίσητε satis pro imperio sic annotat. Non placent mihi Caietanus, Catharinus, Vatablus, Salmero, qui malunt, nos uti verbo labendi quam peccandi, & exponere de iactura gratiae, vocationis, electionis. Sunt haec cum peccato coniuncta, sed praestat, quoad fieri potest, tueri partes Interpretis nostri. Atqui 1. non tàm de autoritate Interpretis Latini, quàm de genuina textus Graeci expositione nos convenit esse solicitos. 2. Verbum πταίειν propriè non significat peccare, sed labi, impingere.

17. Idem Lorinus ad v. 11. sic commentatur. Ante adventum Christi nulli patuit hic introitus (in regnum caeleste) sed sicut Paradisi terrestris post peccatum, Adae clausus erat aditus, Gen. 3. v. 24. ita nulli felicitatis perceptio concedebatur.
