Ex voce tabernaculi videri posset statuminari Platonicorum error, qui statuerunt, corpus humanum merè extrin secum esse veluti custodiam & sepulchrum animae, quodσῶμαdicaturπαρὰ τὸ σώζεινservare & custodire; vel quasiσῆμαh. e. sepulchrum. Atqui corpus aequè est hominis pars essentialis ac ipsa anima rationalis, sed & Christus non animam solùm, sed etiam corpus redemit, illudque unà cum anima caelestis gloriae ac felicitatis particeps reddet.

3. Lorinus in comm. v. 14. memorat. Alexandrum Papam 2. Petro Damiano movisse quaestionem, cur Apostolicae Sedis Antistes nunquam diutiùs viveret, sed intra breve temporis spacium diem clauderet extremum, adeò ut post Petrum Apostolum, qui per quinque circiter annorum lustrah. e. ferè per 25. annos praesedit, nemo postmodùm Romanorum Pontificum hoc spacium Praesulatus aequaverit, apud Petrum Damianum lib. 1. Epist. 17. Respondit a. Damianus, hoc iudicii caelestis ordinem disposuisse, ut humano generi metum mortis incuteret, & quàm despicienda sit temporalis vitae gloria in ipso gloriae Principatu ac veluti Sole deliquium patiente evidenter ostenderet. Lorinus alias addit rationes. Ipsum per se tantum pondus & sollcitudo omnium. Ecclesiarum illis quidem qui aestiment in & se suscipiant, vitae cursum imminuere potest: & aliâ ex parte benignus Deus adeò gravatos non sinit opprimi, sed ecyùs exonerat. Denique hac ratione fieri potest, ut minus appetant homines quam ferè certi sunt haud diu duraturam dignitatem. Quid si hac etiam in re Petri dignitatis Deus haberi rationem voluit, propter quam nec ullus in Pontificatu gerere Petri nomen post illum voluit.

Atqui 1. Petrum Romae per 25. annos Pontificem egisse, falsum est. 2. Pontifices Rom. esse Petri in Sede Papali successores, aequè verum. 3. Posterioribus seculis de temporali potiùs dominio, quàm de Ecclesiae salute Pontifices fuêre soliciti. 4. Omittitur ratio principalis, quòd plerique Pontifices veneno ê medio tollantur, ut aliis ad dignitatem illam pateat aditus, unde proverbio iactatur. Venenum mors Pontificum. 5. Panormitanus censet, impios Pontifices morte praematurâ propterea ê medio tolli, ne flagitiis suis Ecclesiam scandalizent & perturbent.

4. Salmero Disp. 1. in hanc Epist. Tom. 6. p. 112. ex eo, quòd Petrus Romae Martyrio coronatus fuerit, colligit, quod haec Epistola Romae fuerit scripta, quâ de re quid statuendum sit, in prolegomenis fuit expositum. Colligit insuper ex eo aliud, quod maioris est momenti. Petrus, inquit, sanguinis sui ac crucis merita pro Romanis obtulit, & perficacissimae intercessionis suae patrocinium in perpetuum est pollicitus. Sicut etiam Paulus gentium Apostolus & doctor in eadem urbe Dominum glorificavit, ut urbem, quam doctrinâ & signis illustraverat, sanguinis quoque sui meritis locupletaret, & quasi eorum advocatus perpetuò causam eorum apud Deum ageret.

Resp. 1. Salmero Petro tale quid tribuit, quod soli Christo competit. Is enim solus sanguinis sui ac crucis merita pro Romanis & omnibus hominibus obtulit, & efficacissimae intercessionis patrocinium credentibus in perpetuum est pollicitus. 2. Quinimò Salmero plus tribuit Petro quam Christo. Ex eo, quòd Petrus Romae mortuus, colligit, Petrum efficacissimae suae intercessionis patrocinium in perpetuum Romanis esse pollicitum, id quod alibi sic explicat, eos, qui Romanam Petri sedem tenent, in doctrina errare non posse, sed perpetuâ Spiritus Sancti assistentiâ gaudere. Atqui ne de Christo quidem Hierosolymis mortuo dici potest, quod Hierosolymitanae sedis Episcopus ex eo infallibilitatem fuerit sortitus. 3. De duobus Prophetis & testibus contra Antichristum pugnaturis Apoc. 11. v. 8. dicitur, corpora eorum iacebunt in platea civitatis magnae, quae vocatur spiritualiter Sodoma & Aegyptus, ubi & Dominus eorum crucifixus est. At num dicemus, etiam illos Prophetas sanguinis sui ac mortis merita pro incolis illius urbis obtulisse?

5. Iohannes Gagnaeus ad v. 15. sic annotat. Non puto, unquam repeririἔχεινpro posse alteri infinitivo iunctum. Fortassis Petrus cùm praemisissetἔχειν,ob longum hyperbatum iam non memor praedicti verbi adiecit rursumποιεῖσθαι,sufficere enim potest alterutrum. Dabo operam, ut post exitum meum horum memoriam habeatis vel efficiatis. Similia occurrunt apud Salmeronem Disp. 2. in hanc Epistolam.

Resp. 1. Lorinus in comm. h. l. rectè scribit, se nullo modo illud de oblivione Petri velle dicere. 2. Quia haec Gagnae futilis coniectura in ipsum Spiritum sanctum principalem Scripturae autorem est iniuria, ac parum distat â blasphemia. Quod si enim Petrus dictante Spiritu Sancto hanc Epistolam conscripsit, certè si immemor praedicti verbi ἔχειν adiecit rursum ποιεῖσθαι, utique ipse Spiritus sanctus oscitantiae accusatur. 3. Causa, quae Gangnaeum movit, ut sic statueret, nulla est. Quod si enim verbum ἔχω in aliis modis usurpatum cum alio infinitivo coniungi potest, quidni etiam in infinitivo positum cum alio verbo infinitivi modi coniungi posset? At prius multis exemplis confirmari potest. Iohan. 8. v. 6.ἵνα ἔχωσι κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.Actor. 4. v. 14.οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν.Eph. 4. v. 28.ἵνα ἔχῃμεταδιδόναι.2. Iohann. vers. 13.πολλὰ ἔχων ὑμῖν γρὰφειν. Demosth. pro Corona. οὐκ ἔχειν ἀπολύσασθαι τὰ κατηγοροῦμενα δόξω.Videbor non posse diluere obiecta.

6. Salmero Disp. 21. in 1. Cor. 13. & Disp. 2. in 2. Petri. Gregorius de Valentia Tom. 3. Disp. 6. q. 2. punct. 9. Franciscus Turrianus lib. 2. pro Epist, Pontif. cap. 13. Nodinus in cap. 8. Exod. Iodocus Coccius Tom. 1. lib. 5. Thesauri art. 4. p. 471. Laurentius Fauntaeus de invoc. sanctor. th. 79. Iosephus Acosta conc. 2. in festo Ioh. Apostoli. Suarez. Tom. 2. in Thom. q. 37. Disp. 23. sect. 2. Bellarm. lib. 1. debeat. sanct. cap. 18. Costerus in Enchir. cap. 14. Cottonus lib. 1. Instit. cap. 15. Ludovicus Richeomus de sanctis cap. 10. Petrus de bollo de authen. probatione Christiani sacrificii. Fevardentius, Catharinus, Lorinus, Cornelius â Lapide in comm. h. l. ex vers. 15. evincere conantur, sanctos post obitum curam gerere viventium, ac proinde religiosè invocandos esse,

Resp. 1. constat ex textus genuina expositione superiùs allata, Apostolum non promittere, quòd in precibus suis eorum, ad quos scribit, meminisse velit, sed quòd monumenta Epistolarum relinquendo operam dare velit, ut fideles etiam post mortem suam eorum memoriam retineant, quae ex ipso, dum in vivis adhuc erant, audierant. 2. Hanc expositionem confirmant non solùm Glossa ordinaria, Thomas de Aquino, Lyranus, Hugo Cardinalis, Dionysius Carthusianus, sed etiam ex recentioribus Pontificiis Caietanus, Erasmus, Guillaudus, Emanuel Saa. Estius in comm. huius loci, inde Lorinus ipse ad h. l. sic annotat. Magis communis Expositorum sententia est, significare Petrum, se, quia brevi sibi ex hac vita discedendum sit, curare velle, ut hoc Epistolarum & monitorum in iis tàm salutarium resinquat monumentum, ne illis unquam excidat de memoria. 3. Pulchrè Guillandus in h. l. Quemadmodum optimi Praeceptores discipulis, quorum studio sissimi sunt, ne animo excidant, quae pia & sancta ab illis didicerunt, ut non solùm his, sed & posteris omnibus prodesse possint docendo, literas & virtutum monumenta â se scripta, veluti animorum componendorum specula tradere solent: ita & noster Apostolus ipsis Asianis, quin potius toti Ecclesiae Christianae destinare, & ceu Testamento delegare voluit hanc Epistolam, quâ animum divinum, purum, sincerum & integrum non modò perspiciant, sed etiam ipso mortuo habeant, quod doctrinae olim ab ipso traditae admoneat. 4. Haec expositio manifestè elicitur ex scopo & contextu. v. 12. dicit Apostolus, non negligam vos semper commonefacere de his etiam scientes & confirmatos in praesenti veritate.v. 13. subiicit. Iustum autem arbitror, quamdiu sum in hoc tabernaculo, excitare vos in commonefactione.v. 15. addit, Dabo autem operam habere vos identidem etiam post exitum meum, ut horum memoriam faciatis. Hîc quilibet videt, scopum & sensum Apostoli esse, quòd exponere velit, quid in vivis adhuc existens facturus sit, ut fideles eorum, quae ab ipso didicerant, perpetuam memoriam etiam post mortem suam retinere possint, non autem quid post mortem suam facere velit. 5. Cornelius â Lapide cogitur fateri, hunc sensum esse valde planum, facilem & obvium; nec tamen in eo acquiescit, sed planè novam profert expositionem, ἔχειν, inquit, significat impellere, agere, dirigere, incitare, q. d. agam, dirigam, & impellam vos, ut horum reminiscamini. Petrus enim est auriga Ecclesiae, fideles agens & agitans ad bonum, etiam cùm in caelis DEO fruitur. Quamvis verò haec significatio verbi ἔχειν sit planè insolens & infrequens, tamen si de usu Scripturae Petrinae hoc accipatur, rem ipsam concedere possumus. 6. Salmero huic nostrae expositioni obiicit, quod iuxta eam Petrus ter idem dixisset. Atqui Petrus primò in genere dicit, ad suum officium pertinere, ut illos commonefaciat, deinde in specie explicat, tùm quid adhuc in corporis tabernaculo constitutus facere velit, tùm quod memoriale huius suae commonefactionis etiam post mortem ipsis relinquere cogitet. 7. Bellarminus d. 1. §. Quartus locus &c. talem huius loci profert paraphrasin. Dabo autem operam & frequenter habere vos, nimirum commendatos, sive in animo post obitum meum, ut horum memoriam faciatis. Sed cui persvadebit Bellarminus hanc personarum enallagen? Petrus loquitur de memoria sanctorum fidelium, ad quos scribit, Bellarmin. verò de Petri recordatione hoc exponit. Committit etiam fallaciam compositionis & divisionis, dividendo ea, quae in textu Apostolico sunt coniuncta. Ex verbo enim ἔχειν dependent sequentia μνήμην ποιεισθ.Dabo operam, ut habeatis, cuius post obitum meum recordemini: ac verbum ἔχειν non refertur ad Petrum, sed ad eos, ad quos scribebat, sc. non ut Petrus ipsos habeat, sed ut ipsi habeant eorum memoriam. Quis unquam sic locurus est. Operam dabo, ut habeam vos h. e. ut habeam vestrûm curam. 8. Franciscus Turrianus d. l. agnoscit quidem, τὸ ἐχεινvertendum esse, ut possitis, nonἵνα ἔχω ὑμᾶς, sed ἵνα ὑμεῖς ἔχητε. At illud, post obitum meum, refert ad verbum σπουδάσω, quae est manifesta textus perversio. Quomodo etiam sanctis post mortem convenit σπουδάζειν; 9. Salmero, Bellarminus, Coccius, Lorinus, dictis locis provocant ad Scholia Graeca apud Oecumenium, menium, in quibus dicatur, quòd aliqui veteres non ineptè hinc collegerint, sanctos post obitum curam genere viventium. Sed dissimulant, quòd Oecumenius illi expositioni nostram praeferat. Locus integer sic habet. Nonnulli per hyperbaton intelligunt hoc modo. Dabo autem operam & post meum exitum, vos habere semper sive indies & continuè horum memoriam, volentes ex hoc ostendere, quòd etiam post mortem sancti eorum meminerint, quae hîc pro viventibus perfecerunt. Alii verò simpli iter tractantes illud dictum ita intelligunt. Dabo operam & semper habere vos post meum exitum, ut horum mentio fiat h. e. ne miremini, neque grave ducatis, assiduam de his fieri vobis mentionem. Non enim condemnans ruditatem vestram hoc facio, sed per continuam de his doctrinam perseverans, & immobile vobis exhibeo horum sub sidium, ut his confirmati habeatis etiam post meum obitum vivam ac indelebilem horum doctrinam. 10. Ante Oecumenium, cuius aetas incidit in seculum decimum, nullus hunc esse loci illius sensum divinavit. Producitur quidem Chrysostomi Oratio in Principes Apostolorum, in qua implorat Petri & Pauli patrocinium, ac postulat, ut suas hac de re promissiones expleant, rationem afferens hanc, quòd Petrus dixerit. Studebo post meum adventum memoriam vestri facere. Sed quid de hac Chrysostomo attributa oratione statuendum sit, mox videbimus. 11. Haec omnia expendens Bellarminus d. l. fatetur, argumentum ex hoc loco pro religiosa sanctorum invocatione ductum, non esse evidens, sed tantùm probabile. Demus enim, ex hoc loco evinci posse, quod sancti defuncti memoriam gerant eorum, quae in his terris egerunt, quodque in genere pro viventibus in his terris orent, num ex eo statim inferri poterit, sanctos defunctos esse religiosè invocandos? 12. Quinimò Estius disertis verbis argumentum illud, quod alii Pontificii pro astruenda sanctorum invocatione ex h. l. ducunt, repudiat. Quidam, inquit, Catholici Scriptores ex his Petri verbis probari posse putant, intercessionem sanctorum pro vivis, facientes hunc sensum. Dabo operam, ut post meum obitum vestri sim memor, Deum videlicet oraturus pro vobis, ut habeatis horum, quae scribo, memoriam. Sic accepit Chrysostomus sermone in Petrum & Paulum, si tamen eius est totus, nam sub finem mirè variat. Nec citat Petri verba, ut apud ipsum leguntur, sed hoc modo. Studebo post meam dimissionem vestri memoriam facere. Oecumenius etiam huius meminit interpretationis, sed alteram praefert ut simpliciorem. Certè non congruebat, ut diceret. Dabo operam, curabo,σπουδάσω,cùm illud sancti faciant absque curâ & solicitudine. Iam quid attinet statuere velle doctrinam certissimam argumento incerto, cùm alia certissima nequaquam de sint? Igitur observanda hîc & laudanda solicitudo Petri, quâ satagit, ut etiam se mortuo recta doctrina maneat apud fideles, & ad posteros transmittatur. 13. Meritò autem Estius sermonem illum de Petro & Paulo, qui extat Tom. 5. oper. Chrysostomi, suspecti accusat. Casaubonus in Exercit. adver. Baronium p. 169. de eo sic scribit. Prae pudore haec homilia encomiastica in Principes Apostolorum, Petrum & Paulum, operibus Chrysostomi non fuit inserta, nam Scripturis eius autor abuititur & falsat. Petre & Paule orate pro nobis sine intermissione, promisistis enim. Tu Paule quando dixisti. Venite mecum & bonis non deficiemur, Tu Petre, dabo operam, ut post obitum meum horum memoriam faciatis.

7. Thomas Bozius de signis Ecclesiae lib. 18. cap. 3. ex hoc loco primatum Rom. Pontificis miro artificio probare satagit. Quomodo, inquit, Petrus operam dedit, ut post obitum suum Ecclesiae cunctae semper commonerentur? nam speciatim se id facturum pollicetur. Et quis unquam Petri nomine id egit? hoc enim necesse, alioquin non magis Petrus quàm quivis ad haec operam posuisse dicetur. Duo sunt igitur necessaria, & ut aliquis hoc egerit, & ut egerit ex praescripto ipsius met Petri. Atqui solus Rom. Pontifex hoc confecit. Ergo de mandato Petri ius ipse habet in omnes Ecclesias commonendi & videndi, ut illae memores sint mandatorum Petriac DEI. Et advertendum illud, incipiam semper commonere. Ergo iam moriturus inquit se incipere. Incepit autem per literas & alias huiusmodi vias: Ergo per easdem prosecutus est, ut progressus initio respondeat.

Resp. 1. Nullus veterum vel recentiorum Interpp. in comm. h. l. quidquam de Rom. Pont. primatu somniavit. 2. Quae verò haec συνέχεια. Petrus post obitum suum commonefacit cunctas Ecclesias. Ergo hoc exequitur per Pontifices Romanos? imò verò per has ipsas Epistolas, in perpetuum totius Ecclesiae usum scriptas, illud praestat, uti multi ex ipsis Pontificiis Interpp. hunc versiculum ad μνημόσυνον Epistolarum accommodant. Audiamus solum Estium, is postquam talem proposuisset huius loci paraphrasin. Quin &

curam atque operam adhibebo, ut post meum decessum omni tempore possitis horum, de quibus nunc scribo, memoriam vobis renovare; subiicit, id autem fecit, relinquendo illis monumentum suarum Epistolarum, quibus saepe relectis futurum esset, ut praeceptorum ac monitorum eius nunquam obliviscerentur. 3. Demus verò, Petrum per Episcopos Romanos commonere omnes Ecclesias: num ex eo consequens, quòd per solos Rom. Pontifices hoc praestat? quinimò per omnes fideles Ecclesiae Doctores illud praestat. Omnes enim Apostolorum, & sic etiam Petri successores sunt, inquit Hieron. in Epist. ad Evagrium. 4. Demus ex hypothesi, per solos Romanos Episcopos commonefactionem illam fieri, nondum tamen ex eo confirmaretur primatus Monarchicae potestatis, sed tantùm ordinis & dignitatis. 5. Ne ipse quidem Petrus primatum Monarchicum sibi arrogavit, sed se vocat συμπρεσβύτεραν1. Epist. 5. vers. 1. ac prohibet κατακυριεύειν τῶν κλήρων. v. 3. quantò igitur minùs illis, per quos Petrus commonefaciendi partes exequitur, primatus Monarchicus hoc nomine competet? 6. Pontifices Romani non omnibus temporibus Ecclesias universas de veritate caelesti commonefecerunt, cùm quandoque fuerint haeretici, vel haereticorum fautores, quandoque in officio desides, quandoque ad docendi munus prorsus inepti. Quod si ergo Petrus promisisset, sese Ecclesias per Pontifices Romanos semper commonefacturum, praedictioni non respondisset eventus, nec promissioni complementum. 7. Quotquot Pontificii ex hoc loco invocationem sanctorum defunctorum probare conantur, illi statuere coguntur, Petrum, quod hoc loco promittit, per seipsum, non per alios vicarios, & personas intermedias praestare. 8. Nec est, quod Bozius urgeat verbum incipiam in v. 12. est enim vitium vulgatae versionis, cùm in Graeco sit, οὐκ ἀμελήσω, quâ de re ex versiculi illius expositione superius tradita indicium fieri potest.

Observationes. 1. Non sufficit, mysteria fidei & morum doctrinam semel auditoribus tradere, sed perpetuâ commonefactione & exhortatione opus est, inde Rom. 12. v. 7. & 8.διδάσκων καὶ παρακαλῶν coniunguntur. Beda in h. l. Quare vult illos semper commonere de bonis operibus, quos habere scientiam dicit, & de praesentia veritatis esse confirmatos? nisi fortè ob hoc, ut scientiam, quam norunt, operibus exerceant & veritatem, cuius praesentiâ confirmati sunt, fixâ mente custodiant, ne quando per magistros erroris excidant â simplicitate & castitate fidei. Confer. Esai. 58. v. 1.c. 62. v. 6.1. Tim. 4. v. 13.2. Tim. 4. v. 2.

2. Nemo adeò peritus & confirmatus in veritate fidei sibivideri debet, ut putet, se non amplius commonefactione indigere. 1. Cor. 13. v. 8.Frequenter oportet reminisci, quod mundus iste cogit oblivisci, inquit Thomas Angelicus in h. l. ex Bernahardo.

3. Anima nostra in hac vita habitat in corpore, tanquam in tabernaculo: in vita aeterna habitabit in corpore glorificato tanquam in templo. Tabernaculum foederis extruebatur in deserto, per quod desertum praefiguratur praesens seculum, in quo tanquam peregrini & aliò tendentes, duntaxat ad tempus in mortali isto corpore moramur. Templum verò extructum erat Hierosolymae, quae est typus vitae aeternae, in qua velut in patria fixam habebimus sedem, nec unquam metuenda ampliùs erit animae & corporis dissolutio, h. e. animae â corporis habitaculo discessio. 2. Cor. 5. v. 1.Scimus, quoniam si terrestris domus nostra tabernaculi huius dissoluta fuerit, aedificationem ex DEO habeamus domum non manufactam aeternam in caelis. Inde Paulus Philip. 1. vers. 23. dicit, se teneri desiderioεἰς τὸ ἀναλύσαιad migrandum, videlicet ex transitorio corporis tabernaculo ad caeleste habitaculum.

4. Quamvis credentes sint filii lucis,Luc. 16. v. 8. & filii diei1. Thess. 5. vers. 5. nec dormiant sicut coeteri,vers. 6. qui veterno peccacorum sunt sopiti, tamen quandoque etiam ipsi dormitant Matth. 25. vers. 5. ac periculum ipsis imminet, ne somno opprimantur: requiritur igitur â fidelibus Ecclesiae doctoribus, ut eos excitent & ad perpetuam vigiliam hortentur. 2. Timoth. 1. vers. 6.ἀναμιμνήσκω σε ἀναζωπορεῖν τὸ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ. Lutherus in h. l. Wir sind alle mit dem alten faulen Sack beladen/ mit unsern Fleisch und Blut / das wil immerdar den Holtzweg / zeugt uns immer zu sich herrunder / daß die Seele leichtlich entschläfft. Darümb muß man immer treiben und anhalten / wie ein Haußvater das Haußgefinde treibet / daß es nicht faul werde / ob sie gleich wol wissen was sie thun sollen.

5. Beda in hunc locum & ex eo Glossa ordin. Pulcherrimè B. Petrus obitum suum depositionem tabernaculi dicit, quia nimirum sic est perfectis DEI famulis carnis retinacula exuere, sicut viatoribus confecto itinere domum propriam pro habitatione tabernaculi adire, sicut positis in expeditione fugato hoste vel prostrato ad patriam redire. Solam namque sibi domum, solum municipatum, solam patriam norunt in caelis.

6. Tabernaculum illud nostrum quandoque citò removetur, ut Pastoris tuguriolum.Esai. 38. v. 12. maturè ergo nos praeparemus. Quò proprior meta, eò celerior sit cursus.

7. Simeon senex mortem suam vocat ἀπὸλυσινdissolutionemLuc. 2. vers. 29.quasi necessitate quadam vinculorum in hac vita teneretur non voluntate, inquit Ambrosius de bono mortis cap. 2. Paulus vocat ἀνάλυσιν2. Timoth. 4. vers. 6.resolutionem, regressionem.

8. Israëlitarum ex Aegytiaca servitute liberatio vocatur ἡ ἔξοδος, ut ostendit ἐπιγραφὴ libri secundi Mosaici, & Hebr. 11. vers. 12. Eò respicit Petrus, quando mortem suam vocat ἔξοδον. Talis ἔξοδος est mors omnium verè piorum, quia anima nostra, quamdiu in corpore moratur, miserâ captivitate ac servitute premitur, Rom. 7. v. 14.23. 24. sed quando ex corpore egreditur, tunc ex vinculis illis liberatur. Psal. 142. v. 8.

9. Fideles Ecclesiae Doctores omni studio in id incumbere debent, ut doctrinae caelestis integritas ad posteros propagetur. Actor. 20. vers. 28.Attendite vobis & universo gregi, v. 29. Scio quoniam intrabunt post discessionem meam lupi graves,1. Tim. 6. v. 20.O Timothee depositum custodi.2. Tim. 1. v. 14.Bonum depositum custodi per Spiritum Sanctum.2. Tim. 2. v. 2.Quae audivisti â me per multos testes, haec commenda fidelibus hominibus, qui idonei erunt & alios docere. Lyranus in h. l. Bonus Pastor desiderat & quaerit salutem sui gregis, non solum pro tempore suo, sed etiam pro futuro.

10. Inter causas alias, propter quas Deus verbum suum priùs vivâ voce praedicatum in Scripturas redigi voluerit, est etiam memoriae humanae imbecillitas. Petrus h. l. dicit, se operam daturum, ut post suum discessum possint eorum, de quibus scribit, memoriam semper habere, id praestitit relinquendo illis monumenta suarum Epistolarum. Confer Eusebium lib. 2. Hist. cap. 34. lib. 3. cap. 24. lib. 6. cap. 13.

11. Scripturae librum non semel tantùm legere, sed relegere & meditari debemus, eo enim fine Prophetae & Apostoli apud Ecclesiam scripta sua deposuerunt.

## 1:13
Connection. He seeks a second reason for the admonition from his Apostolic office, because it is incumbent upon an Apostle and any faithful Doctor of the Church, not only to teach the ignorant, but also to put those instructed in the faith in remembrance.

Exposition of the text. Δίκαιόν δε ἡγοῦμαι. By τό δίκαιον is understood in this place, that which by reason of office is incumbent upon someone. In that meaning this word is taken Eph. 6. vers. 1. Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is δίκαιον that is, by reason of office and status this is required of you. Phil. 1. vers. 7. Paul says of himself καθὼς ἔστι δίκαιον ἐμοὶ to think this of you all. In the same signification the answer given by Christ to John the Baptist can be conveniently taken. Matth. 3. v. 15.

Thus it becomes us to fulfill all righteousness, that is, it is incumbent upon me by reason of my Mediatorial office, and it is δίκαιον, to receive Baptism, and as the Lamb of GOD, burdened with the sins of the whole world, to approach this saving fountain: it is incumbent upon you by reason of your office and it is δίκαιον, not to deny the Baptism of repentance: meanwhile we do not deny that in the phrase to fulfill all righteousness, more things are altogether contained.

Ἡγούμαι He did not only think, but he knew, that this was just and necessary, if he wished to satisfy his duty. Therefore, this mode of speaking also pertains to modesty and the conciliation of benevolence.

Ἐφ' ὅσον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ σκηνώματι. Concerning ἐφ' ὅσον one must understand χρόνον. By τό σκήνωμα he understands his body, in which the soul dwells for some time as if in a certain tabernacle, whence the Syrian, explaining the metaphor, rendered it [בפגרא הנא] in this body. The appellation is taken from 2. Cor. 5. v. 1. & 4. where Paul likewise calls the body τό σκῆνος a tabernacle, & from Esai. 38. v. 12. where King Hezekiah complains, my life is taken away and rolled up from me, like the tabernacles of shepherds. Eusebius also imitated this mode of speaking in book 2 of Ecclesiastical History, chapter 25, περὶ τῶν τύπων ἔνθα τῶν εἰρημένων Ἀποστόλων τὰ ἱερὰ σκηνώματα κατατέθειται, where he speaks of the bodies of the Holy Apostles.

Διεγείρειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ὑπομνήσει. Vulgate to stir you up, more correctly to stir you up by putting you in remembrance, that is, through admonition, for ἐν ὑπομνήσει is placed for Διὰ ὑπομνήσεως, according to the customary Hebraism. Therefore, he shows a twofold end of his writing. The former is ὑπόμνησις, through which the doctrine of the faith already handed down to them is recalled to memory. The latter is δίεγερσις, through which they are stirred up to constancy in the faith, and to the pursuit of good works. But there lies in the word διεγείρειν a metaphor drawn from those who rouse someone from sleep. Matth. 4. v. 38. Luc. 8. v. 24.Ioh. 6. v. 18. Symmachus Iob. 3. v. 8. rendered the Hebrew ערר as διεγείρειν which Theodotion translates ἐξυπνίσαι. The sense therefore: I think it just to stir you up as if you were sleeping and sluggish.

Latin:

Connexio. Rationem commonefactionis alteram petit ex officio suo Apostolico, quia Apostolo & cuivis fideli Ecclesiae Doctori in cumbit, non solùm ignorantes docere, sed etiam in fide institutos commonefacere.

Textus expositio. Δίκαιόν δε ἡγοῦμαι. Per τό δίκαιον intelligitur hoc loco, quod ratione officii alicui incumbit. In eo significatu accipitur vox ista Eph. 6. vers. 1.Filii oboedite parentibus vestris in Domino, hoc enim estδίκαιον id est, ratione officii & status id à vobis requiritur. Phil. 1. vers. 7. Paulus de se dicit καθὼς ἔστι δίκαιον ἐμοὶhoc sentire de omnibus vobis. In eadem significatione commodè accipi potest responsum Christi Iohanni Baptistae datum. Matth. 3. v. 15.

Sic decet nos implere omnem iustitiam h. e. mihi ratione officii Mediatorii incumbit, ac δίκαιον est, Baptismum accipere, ac tanquam agnum DEI, peccatis totius mundi onustum, ad hunc salutarem fontem accedere: tibi ratione officii incumbit ac δίκαιον est, peccat. Baptismum non denegare: interim non negamus, in phrasi implere omnem iustitiam, plura omninò contineri.

Ἡγούμαι Non arbitrabatur solùm, sed sciebat, hoc esse iustum & necessarium, si suo vellet muneri satisfacere. Ergo & hic loquendi modus pertinet ad modestiam & benevolentiae conciliationem.

Ἐφ' ὅσον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ σκηνώματι. Circa ἐφ' ὅσον subintelligendum χρόνον. Per τό σκήνωμα intelligit suum corpus, in quo anima velut in tabernaculo quodam aliquandiu habitat, unde Syrus metaphoram explicans, reddidit [בפגרא הנא]in hoc corpore. Desumta est autem appellatio ex 2. Cor. 5. v. 1. & 4. ubi Paulus itidem corpus vocat τό σκῆνοςtabernaculum, & ex Esai. 38. v. 12. ubi Ezechias Rex conqueritur, vitae seriem ablatam & convolutam à se, quasi tabernacula Pastorum. Imitatus etiam est hunc modum loquendi Eusebius lib. 2. Histor. Ecclesiast. cap. 25. περὶ τῶν τύπων ἔνθα τῶν εἰρημένων Ἀποστόλων τὰ ἱερὰ σκηνώματα κατατέθειται, ubi de corporibus Sanctorum Apostolorum loquitur.

Διεγείρειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ὑπομνήσει. Vulg. suscitare vos, rectiùs excitare vos incommonefactione id est, per commonefactionem, ponitur enim ἐν ὑπομνήσει pro Διὰ ὑπομνήσεως, iuxta usitatum Hebraismum. Duplicem ergo ostendit scriptionis suae finem. Prior est ὑπόμνησις, per quam doctrina fideiiam antè ipsis tradita in memoriam revocatur. Posterior est δίεγερσις, per quam ad constantiam in fide, & studium bonorum operum excitantur. Latet verò in voce διεγείρειν metaphora ducta ab illis, qui è somno aliquem excitant. Matth. 4. v. 38. Luc. 8. v. 24.Ioh. 6. v. 18. Symmachus Iob. 3. v. 8. Hebraeum ערר reddidit διεγείρειν quod Theodotio vertit ἐξυπνίσαι. Sensus igitur: Iustum arbitror, suscitare vos tanquam dormiturientes ac torpescentes.

## 1:14
Connection. 1. This is a new reason, and the same the third, through which the Apostle adds weight to his exhortation, namely: because he is now near to death, and therefore all the more solicitous for the salvation of those to whom he writes. He had touched upon this reason briefly in the preceding verse, as long as I am in this tabernacle, but here he explains it more fully. The less time remains, with the end of my life now approaching, to perform the parts of my Apostolic office, the more studiously it is incumbent upon me to fulfill them.

2. The Apostle also explains the principle of knowledge, whence he knows that he will shortly put off the tabernacle of his body, namely, from the revelation of Christ.

Exposition of the text. Εἰδὼς, ὅτι ταχινή ἐστιν ἡ ἀπὸθεσις τοῦ σκηνώματος μου. The Vulgate rendered the participle εἰδὼς as certain. But it properly signifies knowing or since I know, in which way the Syriac also rendered [כד ידע אנא] since I know.

Ὅτι ταχινὴ. The Vulgate rendered κατὰ πόδα as that the putting off of this tabernacle is swift. The sense is, I know that it will shortly come to pass that this tabernacle of mine is put off: or also actively, that I shall put off this tabernacle of mine. The Apostle persists in the metaphor; and because he had called his body in the verse immediately preceding τὸ σκήνωμα, therefore he calls his death the putting off of the tabernacle, which Paul in the same sense 2. Cor. 5. v. 1. calls κατὰλυσιν τῆς ἐπιγείου οἰκίας τοῦ σκήνους. The Syriac, explaining the metaphor in its own words, rendered it, since I know, that [דעונדנא דפגרי] the departure of my body will be soon.

καθὼς καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐδήλωσε μοι. The Vulgate rendered the little word καθὼς as according as, but it properly signifies in the manner that. The Syriac rendered it [איכנא] As.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Nova haec est ratio, eademque tertia, per quam Apostolus exhortationi suae pondus addit, videl. quia morti iam sit vicinus, ac proinde eò magis de eorum, ad quos scribit, salute solicitus. Hanc rationem brevibus attigerat in vers. praeced. quamdiu sum in hoc tabernaculo, hîc vero pleniùs eam exponit. Quò minus temporis, appropinquante iam vitae meae fine, ad peragandas muneris mei Apostolici partes restat, eò studiosiùs illas adimplere mihi incumbit.

2. Explicat etiam Apostolus principium cognitionis, unde sciat, se brevi tabernaculum corporis sui depositurm, videl. ex revelatione Christi.

Textus expositio. Εἰδὼς, ὅτι ταχινή ἐστιν ἡ ἀπὸθεσις τοῦ σκηνώματος μου. Participium εἰδὼς Vulg. reddidit, certus. Sed propriè significat Sciens vel cùm sciam, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit [כד ידע אנא]cùm sciam ego.

Ὅτι ταχινὴ. Vulg. κατὰ πόδα reddidit, quod velox est depositio tabernaculi huius. Sensus est, Scio, brevi futurum esse, ut deponatur tabernaculum hocce meum: vel etiam activè, ut deponam tabernaculum hoc meum. Persistit Apostolus in metaphora; & quia corpus suum in versu proximè praecedente vocaverat τὸ σκήνωμα, ideò mortem suam vocat depositionem tabernaculi, quam Paulus eodem sensu 2. Cor. 5. v. 1. vocat κατὰλυσιν τῆς ἐπιγείου οἰκίας τοῦ σκήνους. Syrus metaphoram propriis verbis explicans reddidit, cùm sciam, quod [דעונדנא דפגרי]obitus corporis mei citò sit futurus.

καθὼς καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐδήλωσε μοι. Voculam καθὼς Vulg. reddidit, secundum quod, sed propriè significat quemadmodum. Syrus reddidit [איכנא]Sicut.

## 1:15
Connection 1. He explains the fourth cause of his admonition and exhortation, namely that those faithful to whom he writes may have μνημόσυνον of the doctrine delivered to them even after his death.

2. Because he had called his body σκήνωμα in verse 13 and had called his death ἀπόθεσιν τοῦ σκηνώματός. in verse 14, he therefore persists in the metaphor and in this verse calls his death ἔξοδον an exodus, that is, of the soul from the tabernacle of the body; and he promises that he will endeavor that they may be able, even after his departure from this life, at all times to remember those things of which he writes, which he accomplished by leaving them a monument of his Epistles.

Exposition of the text. Σπουδάσω δὲ καὶ ἐκὰστοτε ἔχειν ὑμᾶς μετὰ τὴν ἐμὴν ἔξοδὸν τὴν τοὺτων μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι. The adversative δὲ seems to be put for the illative οὖν. For he deduces this cause of his admonition from the preceding.

Σπουδάσω The Vulgate translates, I will endeavor. The Greek verb includes the meaning of study and diligence, I will apply all care and effort, I will strive solicitously. The Syriac refers it to those to whom the Apostle writes. [יצפו] Take care. But all the Greek codices have the verb in the first person singular, so that it may refer to the writer, namely to Peter. This verb, however, looks back to verse 10 preceding. Σπουδάσατε Give diligence, that you may make your calling and election sure; σπουδάσω, in my place I will give diligence that the means of this thing may be supplied to you, namely the doctrine comprised in writing. Do your duty in your place, I will be wanting neither to you nor to my office.

The Vulgate rendered the little word ἐκάστοτε. as frequently; Pagninus, individually. But it properly signifies at all times, repeatedly, always. The Syriac rendered it, [אמינאית] perpetually, concerning which word it was spoken above in verse 12. Luther rendered it, allenthalben. Erasmus [rendered] this adverb He referred it to the preceding word σπουδάσω,, for thus he translates, I will always take care: with any opportunity offered, I will take care, as Piscator rightly translates. But it is more rightly referred to the following word ἔχειν,, for one about to die shortly could not conveniently say, I will take care at all times. Luther ich wil aber Fleiß anthun / daß ihr allenthalben habet.

Concerning the word ἔχειν, some establish ἔλλειψιν,, for it seems to them that that you may have the opportunity and means must be understood. But we are compelled by no necessity to establish ἔλλειψιν here, for it is known that it is frequent among the Greeks that ἔχειν to have is placed for δύνασθαι to be able.

By Ἔξοδον exit, departure he understands his own death, which is nothing other than the departure of the soul from the tabernacle of the body and from the exile of this world into the heavenly fatherland. Without a doubt, the Apostle looks with this word to the passage Luke 9. verse 31. where the death of Christ is likewise described by ἔξοδον. Compare Wisdom 7. verse 6. Sirach 38. verse 25.

Τὴν τουτων μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι. By ταῦτα he understands those things of which he had treated up to this point, namely, concerning faith in Christ and the pursuit of good works, for he had exhorted them up to this point to the progress of both. The sense is, I will take care that you may be able to make, or that you may have wherewith you may make, a remembrance of the Apostolic doctrine, always, everywhere, and individually, even when after the death of the Apostles you will no longer be able to have their living voice. And μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι, is more than μνεῖαν,, for it signifies to preserve the memory of some thing, and thus it includes not only the memory of some thing, but also a monument by which that memory is renewed and preserved. But as to what the Apostle did so that they could make mention of them even after his death, we explained above, namely, because he left them these two Epistles, the frequent and constant reading of which could recall those salutary warnings to memory.

Latin:

Connexio 1. Quartam commonefactionis & exhortationis suae causam exponit, videlicet ut fideles illi, ad quos scribit, etiam post mortem ipsius habeant μνημόσυνον doctrinae sibi traditae.

2. Quia corpus suum in vers. 13. vocaverat σκήνωμα & in vers. 14. mortem suam vocaverat ἀπόθεσιν τοῦ σκηνώματός. ideò persistit in metaphora & in hoc vers. mortem suam vocat ἔξοδον egressum, sc. animae ex corporis tabernaculo; ac promittit, se operam daturum, ut possint etiam post suum ex hac vita discessum omni tempore eorum, de quibus scribit, meminisse, id quod praestitit, monumentum Epistolarum ipsis relinquendo.

Textus expositio. Σπουδάσω δὲ καὶ ἐκὰστοτε ἔχειν ὑμᾶς μετὰ τὴν ἐμὴν ἔξοδὸν τὴν τοὺτων μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι. Adversativa δὲ poni videtur pro illativa οὖν. Hanc enim commonefactionis suae causam ex praecedentibus deducit.

Σπουδάσω Vulg. vertit, operam dabo. Verbum Graecum includit significationem studii & diligentiae, omnem curam & operam adhibebo, solicitè enitar. Syrus refert ad eos, ad quos scribit Apostolus. [יצפו]Curate. Sed Graeci Codd. omnes habent verbum primae personae numeri singularis, ut referatur ad scriptorem, videl. ad Petrum. Respicit autem hoc verbum ad vers. 10. praecedentem. Σπουδάσατεoperam date, ut vocationem & electionem vestram firmam faciatis; σπουδάσω, meo loco operam dabo, ut suppetant vobis huius rei media, videlicet doctrina scripto comprehensa. Vos vestro loco officium facite, ego nec vobis nec meo muneri deero.

Voculam ἐκάστοτε. Vulgata reddidit frequenter; Pagninus, Sigillatim. Sed propriè significat omni tempore, identidem, semper. Syrus reddidit, [אמינאית]perpetuò de qua voce dictum superiùs vers. 12. Luth. reddidit, allenthalben. Erasmus hoc adverbium retulit ad praecedens verbum σπουδάσω, sic enim vertit, dabo semper operam: quavis occasione oblatâ, operam dabo, ut Piscator rectè vertit. Sed rectiùs refertur ad sequens verbum ἔχειν, nec enim brevi moriturus commodè dicere poterat, Curabo omni tempore. Lutherus ich wil aber Fleiß anthun / daß ihr allenthalben habet.

Circa verbum ἔχειν quidam statuunt ἔλλειψιν, videtur enim ipsis subintelligendum, ut habeatis occasionem & media. Sed nullâ necessitate cogimur, ut ἔλλειψιν hîc statuamus, notum enim est, frequens apud Graecos esse, ut ἔχεινhabere ponatur pro δύνασθαιposse.

Per Ἔξοδονexitum, discessum intelligit suam mortem, quae nihil aliud est, quàm animae ex corporis tabernaculo, & ex huius mundi exilio in caelestem patriam discessus. Procul dubio respicit Apostolus hac voce ad locum Luc. 9. vers. 31. ubi mors Christi itidem per ἔξοδον describitur. Confer Sap. 7. vers. 6.Sirac. 38. vers. 25.

Τὴν τουτων μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι. Per ταῦτα intelligit ea, de quibus hactenus egerat, videlicet de fide in Christum & studio bonorum operum, ad utriusque enim profectum eos fuerat hactenus exhortatus. Sensus est, operam dabo, ut possitis facere, vel ut habeatis, unde faciatis memoriam doctrinae Apsotolicae, semper, ubique, & sigillatim, etiam quando post obitum Apostolorum vivam illorum vocem non ampliùs habere poteritis. Ac plus est μνήμην ποιεῖσθαι, quàm μνεῖαν, significat enim conservare memoriam alicuius rei, sicque includit non solùm rei alicuius memoriam, sed etiam monumentum, quo memoria illa renovatur & conservatur. Quod verò fecerit Apostolus, ut etiam post mortem suam possent eorum mentionem facere, exposuimus superiùs, videl. quia reliquit illis duas hasce Epistolas, quarum crebra & frequens lectio salutaria illa monita in memoriam revocare potuit.

## 1:16
Connection 1. After the Apostle had exhorted those to whom he writes to constancy and progress in the pursuit of virtues, he now further exhorts them to constancy and progress in the faith, by the argument that the doctrine of the faith which they had embraced is of immovable truth and certainty, which he proves both by αὐτοψίᾳ the majesty of Christ in the transfiguration, and by προφητείᾳ the Old Testament.

2. He therefore commends the doctrine delivered by him to those to whom he writes by its authority, because he delivered to them not human figments, but divine oracles.

3. When the Apostle had indicated the end of his writing, which is that it might always stand as a μνημόσυνον and testimony of sound doctrine, he now further confirms the certainty of that doctrine, which he amplifies by the opposition of ingeniously devised fables.

4. The particle αἰτιολογικὴ γὰρ shows that Peter wishes to say this: If I had taught human dreams and fables, imminent death could have warned me to repent and to change my opinion. But the things which I have taught are right, wherefore I shall not cease to inculcate them. Oecumenius favors this reason for the connection.

Exposition of the text. Οὐ γάρ σεσοφισμένοις μύθοις ἐξακολουθήσαντες ἐγνωρίσαμεν ὑμῖν τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν. By τοὺς μύθους σεσοφισμένους some determine that sermones arte compositos are to be understood. Gagnaeius in this place: Cùm μῦθος non fabulam modò, verùm etiam orationem significet, videtur mihi Petri sensus esse, quod non affabrè, compositâ & eleganti oratione usus illis praedicavit. Sic enim Graeca Scholia exponunt, ut sit idem sensus cum Paulo, quod non in doctis humanis sapientiae verbis illis Christi veritatem praedicârit. 1. Cor. 2. v. 4. ad quem locum etiam marginales Concordantiae ubique nos remittunt. But because the name μύθοι is nowhere in the New Testament otherwise it is used for fables.1. Tim. 1. v. 4.c. 4. v. 7.2. Tim. 4. v. 4.Tit. 1. v. 14. & because here it is not so much a matter of the form of teaching as of the matter of the doctrine, as the latter part of the opposition shows, therefore this name is more correctly rendered by fables. The Syrian rendered it by [מתלא] which signifies parables, proverbs, fables, from the root [מתל] from the Hebrew משל he assimilated, he spoke parabolically.

The participle σεσοφισμένοις descends from σοφίζασθαι, whose active σοφίζειν is taken in a good sense 2. Tim. 3. v. 15. Sacred letters are able to make you σοφίσαι wise unto salvation, and the LXX use it for בין in Hiphil. he understood, he perceived, he caused to understand,1. Sam. 3. v. 8. for חכם he was wise, he showed wisdom,Deut. 32. v. 28.1. Reg. 4. vers. 31.Ps. 18. v. 8.Psal. 104. v. 22.Psal. 119. v. 98.Prov. 8. v. 33.Eccles. 2. v. 15. & 19cap. 7. v. 24. Sometimes, however, it is taken in a bad sense, Eccles. 7. v. 17. μηδὲ σοφίζου περισσὰ be not overwise.Sirach. 7. v. 5. παρὰ βασιλεῖ μὴ σοφίζου, do not seem to yourself to be overwise before the King.cap. 10. vers. 29. μὴ σοφίζου ποιῆσαι τὸ ἔργον σου. Do not wish to seem wise in doing your work.cap. 32. vers. 6. ἀκαίρως μὴ σοφίζου. Do not wish to seem wise importunately.cap. 37. vers. 23. ὁ σοφιζόμενος ἐν λόγοις is he who sophistically deals in words, whom today we call a Sophist. For the same reason it is also taken in a bad sense in this place, namely not for true wisdom, but for a phantom and appearance of wisdom. For they are σεσοφισμένοι μύθοι fables composed with art, and subtly devised, having only μόρφωσιν of wisdom, neatly and aptly composed to deceive others. Among profane writers σοφίζεσθαι likewise sometimes signifies to devise something sharply and ingeniously. Aristoph. in Nubib. ἀεὶ καινὰς ἰδέας εἰσφέρων σοφίζομαι, I always bring some new ideas, sharply and cleverly devised by me. It is also accepted in a bad sense for to devise deceitfully and fraudulently, to invent craftily and cunningly. Demosth pro Corona. εἶθα σοφίζεται. In the same signification Gregory Nazianzen uses this verb. orat. de sacro pasch. σοφίσαι τι καὶ σὺ περὶ τὴν ἀπαίτησιν devise something craftily also you concerning the petition, which latter signification is proper to this place. For those whom he calls in this place σεσοφισμένους μύθους, he calls them later cap. 2. v. 3. πλαστοὺς λόγους. From these it can easily be judged what must be determined concerning that which Oecumenius says in his commentary, that Peter means this, that he by no means used ἀνθρωπίνῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ καλλιεπημένοις λόγοις, οἷς καταγοητεύσοιτο αὐτῶν τὴν ἀκοὴν human wisdom and ornate words, by which he might have deceived their hearing as if by tricks. 1. Cor. 2. v. 1. & seqq. And likewise concerning that which Drusius thinks, that by this participle σεσοφισμένοις the Hebrew is expressed מחכמים which is had Proverb. 30. vers. 24. wise, wisely instructed. But 1. Cor. 2. vers. 1. & seqq. concerns the form of teaching, but here it concerns the matter of the doctrine; Proverb. 30. vers. 24. מחכמים is taken in a good sense, but here σεσοφισμένοι is taken in a bad sense. The Syrian rendered it [דעבידין באומנותא] fables fashioned in artifice, or artificially.

Τὴν δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν. The Vulgate rendered it, power and presence, for which latter word some Latin codices viciously read foreknowledge. But the name of power is also ambiguous, for sometimes the Vulgate Interpreter expressed through it the Greek name ἀρετὴν, as in this very chapter v. 3. & 5. but sometimes δύναμιν: more rightly therefore, for the sake of avoiding ambiguity, he would have rendered it through potency, just as the Syrian also translates it through [חילה] παρουσία not only signifies presence, but also advent, Matth. 24. vers. 3. & 27. 1. Corinth. 15. vers. 23. cap. 16. vers. 17. but whether it is more rightly expressed in this place by presence or advent, we shall see in the questions. Ἀλλ' ἐπόπται γενηθέντες τῆς ἐκείνου μεγαλειότητος. The Vulgate rendered it, but having become spectators of his greatness. But the Greek ἐπόπται is more rightly rendered inspectors, than spectators, because to speculate, is properly to see and observe things at a distance. Budaeus in his commentaries on the Greek language, page 338, teaches, ἐπόπτας that those were formerly called arbiters of sacred things, who preceded in dignity μύστας that is, initiated into sacred things, which meaning can in some way be accommodated to this place, because Peter speaks of the singular privilege of the transfiguration, seen by himself, John, and James, the three principal Apostles. The word ἐποπτεύειν, from which ἐπόπτης is formed, and which Peter alone uses in the New Testament, it signifies some attentive inspection undertaken with care.

By μεγαλειοτηζα is understood the glory and majesty of Christ, which shone forth in Him during all that time in which He lived with the Apostles on these lands. John 1. verse 14. ἐθεασάμεθα. We beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father. The author of the book on the wonders of Scripture, Tom. 3. August. book 3. chapter 10. The divinity lying hidden in the body granted to those seeing from the outside a small portion of its light to be beheld, as much as they were able. He uses the cognate word μεγαλωσύνης concerning Christ in the Epistle Hebrews chapter 1. v. 3. & chapter 8. v. 1. The word μεγαλειότητος itself, however, is used concerning the miracles of Christ Luke 9. v. 43., indeed from which His divine majesty and power shone forth. But especially, as is evident from what follows, Peter looks to the manifestation of the majesty and glory of Christ made in the transfiguration Matthew 17. v. 2.Mark 9. v. 2.Luke 9. v. 18. and appeals to αὐτοψίαν,, namely that together with James and John, his fellow Apostles, he beheld with his own eyes the very glory and majesty of Christ in the transfiguration, which αὐτοψίαν he opposes to those who dared to call into doubt the preaching of the Apostles concerning the second coming of Christ, since that transfiguration and ἔνδειξις of the majesty of Christ was a prelude and prefiguration of the glory to be publicly exhibited in the second coming and to be beheld by all at some time.

Latin:

Connexio 1. Postquam ad constantiam & profectum in studio virtutum eos, ad quos scribit, exhortatus fuerat Apostolus, iam porrò eos ad constantiam & profectum in fide hortatur, argumento eo, quòd doctrina fidei, quam amplexi fuerant, sit immotae veritatis ac certitudinis, id quod probat tum αὐτοψίᾳ maiestatis Christi in transfiguratione, tùm προφητείᾳ Veteris Testamenti.

2. Commendat ergo doctrinam illis, ad quos scribit, â se traditam ab autoritate, quòd non humana figmenta, sed divina oracula ipsis tradiderit.

3. Cùm finem scriptionis suae Apostolus indicasset, qui est, ut illa tanquam μνημόσυνον & testimonium sanae doctrinae semper extaret, iam porrò certitudinem illius doctrinae confirmat, quam ab oppositione fabularum ingeniosè excogitatarum amplificat.

4. Particula αἰτιολογικὴ γὰρ ostendit, Petrum hoc dicere velle. Si humana somnia & fabulas docuissem, mors imminens potuisset me commonere ad resipiscendum & ad mutandam sententiam. Sed recta sunt, quae docui, quare non desinam ea inculcare. Huic connexionis rationi favet Oecumenius.

Textus expositio. Οὐ γάρ σεσοφισμένοις μύθοις ἐξακολουθήσαντες ἐγνωρίσαμεν ὑμῖν τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν. Per τοὺς μύθους σεσοφισμένους quidam intelligendos esse statuunt sermones arte compositos. Gagnaeius in h. l. Cùmμῦθοςnon fabulam modò, verùm etiam orationem significet, videtur mihi Petri sensus esse, quod non affabrè, compositâ & eleganti oratione usus illis praedicavit. Sic enim Graeca Scholia exponunt, ut sit idem sensus cum Paulo, quod non in doctis humanis sapientiae verbis illis Christi veritatem praedicârit.1. Cor. 2. v. 4.ad quem locum etiam marginales Concordantiae ubique nos remittunt. Sed quia nomen μύθοι nuspiam in Nov. Test. aliter usurpatur quâ pro fabulis.1. Tim. 1. v. 4.c. 4. v. 7.2. Tim. 4. v. 4.Tit. 1. v. 14. & quia hîc non tàm de docendi forma, quàm de doctrinae materia agitur, ut oppositionis pars posterior ostendit, ideò rectiùs hoc nomen per fabulas redditur. Syrus reddidit per [מתלא] quod significat parabolas, proverbia, fabulas, â rad. [מתל] ex Hebr. משלassimilavit parabolicè locutus est.

Participium σεσοφισμένοις descendit â σοφίζασθαι, cuius actirum σοφίζειν in bonam partem sumitur 2. Tim. 3. v. 15.Sacrae literae possunt teσοφίσαιad salutem, ac LXX. eo utuntur pro בין in Hiphil. intellexit, animadvertit, intelligere fecit,1. Sam. 3. v. 8. pro חכםsapiens fuit, sapientiam praestitit,Deut. 32. v. 28.1. Reg. 4. vers. 31.Ps. 18. v. 8.Psal. 104. v. 22.Psal. 119. v. 98.Prov. 8. v. 33.Eccles. 2. v. 15. & 19cap. 7. v. 24. Quandoque tamen in malam partem sumitur, Eccles. 7. v. 17.μηδὲ σοφίζου περισσὰne sis nimium sapiens.Sirach. 7. v. 5.παρὰ βασιλεῖ μὴ σοφίζου,apud Regemne videaris tibi nimiùm sapiens.cap. 10. vers. 29.μὴ σοφίζου ποιῆσαι τὸ ἔργον σου.Ne velis videri sapiens in faciendo opus tuum.cap. 32. vers. 6.ἀκαίρως μὴ σοφίζου.Importunè ne velis videri sapiens.cap. 37. vers. 23.ὁ σοφιζόμενος ἐν λόγοις est is, qui in verbis sophisticatur, quem hodie Sophistam appellamus. Pari ratione etiam hoc loco in malam partem sumitur, videlicet non pro vera sapientia, sed pro sapientiae simulachro & specie. Sunt enim σεσοφισμένοι μύθοι fabulae arte compositae, ac subtiliter excogitatae, habentes tantùm μόρφωσιν sapientiae, ad alios fallendum concinnè & aptè compositae. Apud profanos scriptores σοφίζεσθαι itidem quandoque significat argutè & ingeniosè aliquid comminisci. Aristoph. in Nubib. ἀεὶ καινὰς ἰδέας εἰσφέρων σοφίζομαι,semper novas aliquas ideas affero, argutè & solerter â me excogitatas. Accipitur etiam in malam partem pro dolosè & fraudulenter excogitare, vafrè & callidè comminisci. Demosth pro Corona. εἶθα σοφίζεται. In eadem significatione utitur hoc verbo Gregorius Nazianzenus. orat. de sacro pasch. σοφίσαι τι καὶ σὺ περὶ τὴν ἀπαίτησινvafrè quiddam excogita & tu de petitione, quae posterior significatio est huius loci propria. Quos enim hoc loco vocat σεσοφισμένους μύθους, illos postea cap. 2. v. 3. vocat πλαστοὺς λόγους. Ex his facilè iudicari potest, quid statuendum de eo, quod Oecumenius in comm. dicit, Petrum hoc velle, se minimè usumἀνθρωπίνῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ καλλιεπημένοις λόγοις, οἷς καταγοητεύσοιτο αὐτῶν τὴν ἀκοὴνhumanâ sapientiâ & ornatis verbis, quibus quasi praestigiis deceperit ipsorum auditum.1. Cor. 2. v. 1. & seqq. Itemque de eo, quod Drusius putat, participio hocσεσοφισμένοιςexpressum Hebraeumמחכמיםquod habeturProverb. 30. vers. 24.sapientes, sapienter instituti. Sed 1. Cor. 2. vers. 1. & seqq. de docendi forma, hîc verò de doctrinae materia agitur; Proverb. 30. vers. 24.מחכמים in bonam, hîc verò σεσοφισμένοι in malam partem accipitur. Syrus reddidit [דעבידין באומנותא]confectas in artificio, sive artificiosè fabulas.

Τὴν δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν. Vulg. reddidit, virtutem & praesentiam, pro quo posteriore quidam Codd. Latini vitiosè legunt praescientiam. Sed & virtutis nomen est ambiguum, quandoque enim Vulg. Interpres per illud expressit Graecum nomen ἀρετὴν, ut in hoc ipso capite v. 3. & 5. quandoque verò δύναμιν: rectiùs ergo vitandae ambiguitatis causâ reddidisset per potentiam, sicut & Syrus vertit per [חילה]παρουσία non solùm significat praesentiam, sed etiam adventum,Matth. 24. vers. 3. & 27.1. Corinth. 15. vers. 23.cap. 16. vers. 17. an verò hoc loco rectiùs per praesentiam vel adventum exprimatur, videbimus in quaestionibus. Ἀλλ' ἐπόπται γενηθέντες τῆς ἐκείνου μεγαλειότητος. Vulg. reddidit, sed speculatores facti illius mag nitudinis. Sed Graecum ἐπόπται rectiùs redditur inspectores, quàm speculatores, quia speculari, propriè est longinqua videre & observare. Budaeus in comm. Graec. ling. pag. 338. docet, ἐπόπταςolim dictos fuisse arbitros sacrorum, qui dignitate praecesseruntμύσταςh. e. initiatos sacris, quae significatio huic loco quodammodo accommodari potest, quia loquitur Petrus de singulari privilegio transfigurationis, â se, Iohanne & Iacobo tribus praecipuis Apostolis visae. Verbum ἐποπτεύειν, ex quo ἐπόπτης formatur, quove solus Petrus in Novo Testamento utitur, attentam aliquam inspectionem cum cura susceptam significat.

Per μεγαλειοτηζα intelligitur Christi gloria & maiestas, quae in ipso eluxit toto illo, quo cum Apostolis in his terris ver satus est, tempore. Iohann. 1. vers. 14.ἐθεασάμεθα.Vidimus gloriam eius, gloriam quasi unigeniti â Patre. Autor lib. de mirabilibus Scripturae Tom. 3. August. lib. 3. cap. 10. Divinitas latens in corpore luminis sui portiunculam conspiciendam foris videntibus quantam poterant, concessit. Cognatâ voce μεγαλωσύνης de Christo utitur Epist. Hebr. cap. 1. v. 3. & cap. 8. v. 1. Ipsa autem μεγαλειότητος vox de miraculis Christi usurpatur Luc 9. v. 43. quippe ex quibus divina ipsius maiestas & potentia reluxit. Cumprimis vero, ut constat ex sequentibus, respicit Petrus ad manifestationem maiestatis & gloriae Christi factam in transfiguratione Matth. 17. v. 2.Marc. 9. v. 2.Luc. 9. v. 18. ac provocat ad αὐτοψίαν, quòd sc. unâ cum Iacobo & Iohanne CoApostolis suis ipsammet Christi gloriam & maiestatem in transfiguratione oculis suis conspexerit, quam αὐτοψίαν opponit illis, qui praedicationem Apostolorum de secundo Christi adventu in dubium vocare ausi fuêre, cùm transfiguratio illa ac maiestatis Christi ἔνδειξις fuerit praeludium ac praefiguratio gloriae, in secundo adventu publicè exhibendae & ab omnibus olim conspiciendae.

## 1:16-18 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place 1. Is it read correctly in most Latin Codices v. 16: having followed unlearned fables? Resp. Leo IX, Epistle 1 to Michael, Emperor of Constantinople, ch. 13, Hugo the Cardinal, Lyranus, the Carthusian, Caietanus, Titelmanus, Primaticcius in this place, Maldonatus on John 15, v. 27, and not a few Latin Codices indeed read it so. Nor did it appear how fables could be called learned. But the Pontificals themselves acknowledge that it is read more correctly as learned fables, in which way even corrected Latin Codices read it today. Salmero on this place. The reading which the Greek letter offers is more probable, namely σεσοφισμένους i. e. learned, that is, fables composed with artifice & eloquence, and thus Jerome reads in ch. 3. to the Galatians. Gagnaeius in this place. Instead of unlearned fables, in Greek it is σεσοφισμένους that is, learned and composed with rhetorical artifice, whence I think the Interpreter translated learned, as certain Codices have it, but it was added by a sciolist scribe. Lorinus in this place. We value the Pontifical authority very much in this matter, which now in the amended Bibles commands us to read it thus. Gagnaeius, Catharinus, Vatablus, Clarius, Salmeron, Arias, and Lucas Brugensis also agree in this. Estius in this place. In many Codices unlearned was read instead of learned, but the Roman correctors restored to us the true reading from more faithful Codices consistent with the Greek. Would that they would correct the Latin version from the Greek text in other places!

Q. 2. Who are those σεσοφισμένοι μὺθοι, of whom the Apostle v. 16. speaks? Resp. 1. Christophorus a Castro in Comm. Baruch 3. n. 12. discourses thus. Mythologists were called interpreters & explainers of fables, which most learned poets invented, under the coverings of which they hid a certain wisdom, for they signified both divine and natural things, and those pertaining to morals under them, and for that reason Peter calls them learned fables, which Clement lib. 6. Recognit. in the person of Apion said to have a certain cognate & Philosophical reason, which could be explained through allegory, of which kind were the fables about the various transfigurations of Jupiter. i. e. of the air. For the Metamorphosis of the Lord JESUS is not it was such, but true and glorious. Castrius therefore thinks that the fables of the Gentiles concerning the metamorphosis of their gods are opposed in turn to the Apostolic account of the metamorphosis of Christ. But because Peter opposes fables to heavenly doctrine in general, it is therefore better, by taking that name generally, to understand any human inventions devised by whatever artifice. Lorinus in this place: We could call all external and foreign doctrines fables, Ps. 119. v. 85. which they tell in Hebrew is כרו the proud dig, through which they might cast us into pits, for the same name שחות with a point on the right, means pits; on the left, it signifies trifles and absurdities. 2. For what learned fables the Apostle understands can be gathered both from parallel passages and from the object of this writing. The parallel passages are 1. Tim. 1. v. 4. μηδὲ προσέχειν μύθοις καὶ ἀπέρανταις γενεαλογίαις, where by μύθους are understood Jewish fables, as appears from the following word γενεαλογίαις, in which the Jews detained themselves through scrupulous and useless questions. cap. 4. v. 7. τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ. 2. Timoth. 4. vers. 4. ἀπό μέν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσι. Ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μὺθους ἐκτραπήσονται. Tit. 1. v. 14. μὴ προσέχοντες ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοι, καἰ ἐντολαῖς ἀνθρώπων. The object of the writing are those converted from the Jews and Gentiles. Therefore he understands Jewish and Ethnic fables. The fables of the Jews occur in great abundance in the fourth book of Esdras and in the Talmudic books. The fables of the Gentiles are proposed everywhere in Hesiod's Theogony, Ovid's Metamorphoses, and elsewhere. 3. Afterwards the Simonians, Gnostics, Valentinians, and other heretics imitated them, who fashioned many fables about GOD, about Angels, and about aeons. Concerning the Gnostics, Augustine in the book on heresies, chapter 6, writes thus: They hand down dogmas full of most fabulous inventions, etc., and those who believe them, they make not to possess much knowledge, as they think, but to vanish into much, if I may say so, fabulosity. Oecumenius in this place determines that the Valentinians are indicated, who βυθοὺς καὶ σιγην devised depths and silence: but that it is likely that they had already begun to arise at that time.

Q. 3. Does the little word παρουσία in v. 16. denote the first or rather the second coming of Christ? Resp. 1. Vatablus, Caietanus, Clarius, Salmero, Erasmus, Gagnaeius, Fevardentius, Saa, etc., in their commentaries on this place accept it concerning the first coming of Christ, namely concerning the coming and presence Of Christ through the incarnation, to which exposition conforms that which Melchior Canus, book 12 of the Locorum, chapter 14, understands as virtue or power, that by which the Word was made flesh; presence, by which he dwelt among us John 1. v. 14. Lorinus in this place: By the name of presence I comprehend the whole economy of Christ in the flesh, by virtue I understand more properly miracles. Cornel. à Lapide in this place: He strikes at Simon Magus, who was selling himself for Christ, and was calling himself the power of God, Acts 8. v. 10. as if to say: We preach that Christ is the power of God, not Simon Magus. 1. Cor. 1. v. 23. Those who embrace this opinion understand by παρουσίαν the coming of the Son of God into the flesh, concerning which it is said 1. Tim. 1. v. 15. that Christ Jesus ἦλθεν came into the world to save sinners; by δύναμιν they understand that divine force of Christ, which exerted itself in miracles, but especially in the resurrection. Rom. 1. v. 4. Some also join δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν in such a way that, according to a Hebraism, it is the same as powerful coming, that is, a coming undertaken to exercise power. Now Christ exercised his power in his first coming, both by effectively persuading what he was teaching, and by confirming his doctrine with miracles, and by overcoming the Devil through his passion and death, and by gloriously rising from the dead by his own power. 1. John 3. v. 8. 2. But this Apostolic passage is more correctly understood of the second coming of Christ. 1. Because the word παρουσίαν is nowhere used in the N. T. concerning the first coming of Christ, but always concerning the second coming. Matt. 24. v. 3. 27. 37. & 39. 1. Cor. 15. v. 23. 1. Thess. 2. v. 19. cap. 3. v. 13. cap. 4. v. 15. cap. 5. v. 23. 2. Thess. 2. v. 1. & 8. James 5. v. 7. & 8. 1. John 2. v. 28. The first coming of Christ is called ἔλευσις Acts 7. v. 52. εἰσοδος Acts 13. v. 24. the second παρουσία & ἐπιφάνεια, 1. Tim. 6. v. 14. 2. Tim. 4. v. 1. & 8. Tit. 2. v. 13. 2. In the same signification Peter uses the word παρουσίας in this very Epistle cap. 3. v. 4. Where is the promise of his coming? v. 12 expecting τὴν παρουσίαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας 3. The scope of this Epistle proves the same. For it is evident from chapter 3 that, among other things, he wished to forearm those to whom he writes against mockers, calling the second coming of Christ into doubt. 4. The first coming of Christ was rather of weakness and humility than of power and majesty: but the second will be in glory and power. 5. The transfiguration of Christ, to which the Apostle appeals in the following verse, was a prelude of the majesty and glory in which Christ in the second coming he will show himself to be visible. 6. Thence Lorinus, departing from the remaining Papists in this part, comments on this place thus: Nor does it displease, if we interpret the second coming by presence, which will be in majesty and power, and of which the transfiguration was a certain type, of which mention is subjoined. Certainly a little before v. 10. & 11. he had exhorted to good works, so that thus an entrance might be abundantly ministered into the eternal kingdom: he had also made mention just before of his own death, and there is a kinship between death and judgment.

Q. 4. What is that magnificent glory in v. 17. from which the voice was brought? Resp. 1. Some accept that saying from heaven, which is the throne of divine majesty and glory, since in the Baptism of Christ the same voice ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν is said to have been brought Matth. 3. v. 7. and since in this place in v. 18. seq. it is said. And we heard that voice ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθείσαν. But Matthew and Mark say in the transfiguration that this voice came ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης from a cloud. 2. More rightly, therefore, it is said that that voice is said to have been brought from magnificent glory, i.e., from the most magnificent and most glorious GOD the Father, because the heavenly Father through it magnificently and gloriously demonstrated his peculiar presence. 3. Some establish that by that magnificent glory is understood that lucid cloud, which, as is evident from the description of the Evangelists, overshadowed not only Christ, but also Moses and Elijah who were present, so that the sense may be: from magnificent glory i.e. from the lucid and clear cloud, which was an index of divine glory i.e. of GOD the Father, who from it uttered the voice, from which they further collect that the heavenly Father manifested his presence in that lucid cloud, as if in a certain external symbol, just as otherwise in the O. T. he revealed himself several times in a lucid cloud. But it is said more rightly that the lucid cloud in this θεοφανείᾳ was a symbol of the presence of the Holy Spirit, who, as he manifested himself in the Baptism of Christ in the form of a dove, so in the transfiguration he manifested himself in a lucid cloud, so that by this reason also some external symbol of presence may be attributed to the third person of the Godhead.

Q. 5. Whether this voice was of the Father alone, or indeed of the whole Trinity? Resp. one must distinguish between the formation of the voice and the appropriation. That is to be attributed to the whole Trinity. August. lib. 4. de Trinit. cap. 21. The Trinity worked together both the voice of the Father and the flesh of the Son and the dove of the Holy Spirit. Fulgentius de fide ad Petrum cap. 9. Hold that voice, by which God the Father alone spoke, and that flesh, by which the only-begotten God alone was made man; and that dove, in whose form the Holy Spirit descended upon Christ, are works of the whole most holy Trinity, etc. But this pertains to the Father alone. August. serm. 63. on the word of the Lord The Trinity made the dove from heaven, but the dove pertains to the Holy Spirit alone. The Trinity made the voice from heaven, but the voice pertains to the Father alone.

Q. 6. Recently in the Latin version v. 16. let it be added. Hear him? Resp. 1. Although all three Evangelists add these words in the description of the transfiguration of Christ, from which it is without doubt that the author of the Vulgate version brought the same here, nevertheless in the Greek -odd in this place they are not held, therefore they are not a genuine and Canonical part of this chapter. It is indeed certain that this voice was added by the heavenly Father at the transfiguration of Christ, so that He might make manifest that Christ is that great Prophet, of whom Moses, who was present at the transfiguration, had prophesied, and had predicted that He was to be heard by all, Deut. 18. vers. 18. nevertheless Peter, not content with the prior words of the paternal voice, did not wish to add these latter ones, as being already most known to those to whom he was writing.

Q. 7. Which was that holy mountain, on which Christ was transfigured? Resp. 1. The Evangelists do not express that specifically, but only say this, that it was a high mountain. 2. Some therefore establish that it was Lebanon, that highest mountain of Palestine, of which frequent mention is made in the Holy Scriptures. Jacobus Faber Stapulensis in ch. 9. of Mark. Franciscus Lucas Brugensis in ch. 17. of Matthew. Which they think they can prove from Marc. 9. v. 30. And departing from there they passed through Galilee, from which they gather, the transfiguration was not done in Galilee, in which Mount Tabor was situated, but in the parts of Caesarea Philippi, and thus on a nearby mountain of Lebanon. 3. The more common opinion, however, establishes that Christ was transfigured on Mount Tabor, which is a round and sublime mountain in the plains of Galilee, as Jerome describes it in comm. on Hosea 5, where he also teaches that it was otherwise called Ithabyrium. Josephus in book 4 of the Jewish War ch. 2. records, its height rises up to the thirtieth stadium, but it has a plain of twenty stadia on the summit. This is the opinion of Cyril of Jerusalem catech. 12. Jerome Epist. 27. in the Epitaph of Marcella. Damascene in the sermon on the transfiguration of the Lord. Euthymius in Psalm. 88. Bede on the holy places chapter 17. Philo of Carpathos in his commentary on the Canticles, which is confirmed by both the preceding and following histories among the Evangelists, which show, that these things were done in Galilee, because immediately after the transfiguration he descended to Capernaum, which city is near Mount Tabor. Matth. 17. v. 23. 4. Nor can the contrary be gathered from Marc. 9. v. 30. because παραπορεύεσθεν signifies, to pass through quickly, secretly, and in passing to pass through/ but not to pass by or to pass over, to move around.

Ἐναντιοφανείας. 1. The voice of the Father in this place is said to have been brought from heaven v. 18. But Matth. 17. v. 5. it is said to have sounded from a cloud. Resp. That miraculous cloud was descending from heaven, from the cloud that voice of the Father was brought down, therefore that voice was also brought down from heaven. 2. The voice of the heavenly Father in the transfiguration is described thus: This is my beloved Son, but that voice was heard from a cloud, which was an external symbol of the Holy Spirit. Therefore the Son is called the Son of the Holy Spirit. Resp. The cloud was an external symbol of the Holy Spirit, the voice heard from the cloud was an external symbol of the Father. Therefore he who speaks from the cloud calls Christ his beloved Son, but not he whose external symbol is the cloud from which the voice is heard.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. To those fables, by which the truth and sincerity of heavenly doctrine is opposed, are deservedly referred the Papistical fables, noted in the mirror of Vincent, in the Historical work of Antoninus, in the Golden Legend, in the sermons of the Disciple on the seasons, in the Histories of Jacobus de Voragine, in the Dormisecure and other writings of this flour or rather of this bran. Concerning the Golden Legend, Melchior Canus pronounces in book 11 of the Commonplaces, chapter 6, §. But the law etc. that a man of iron mouth, of leaden heart, and certainly of a mind little severe and prudent, wrote it.

2. Christ is the natural, only-begotten, and eternal Son of God, and consequently true God with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Hilary, book 3 on the Trinity, p. 26. Many are sons, but this Son is not such as they. For this is the true and proper and only-begotten Son, by origin, not by adoption; by truth, not by naming; by birth, not by creation. Leo the Great, sermon on the transfiguration. This is my beloved Son, whom Deity does not separate from me, power does not divide, eternity does not distinguish. This is my Son, not adoptive but proper; not created from elsewhere, but begotten from me, nor made comparable to me from another nature, but born equal to me from my own essence.

3, From the words which are added in the Vulgate version v. 17. and are held in Matth. 17. v. 5., Hear him, we gather thus. The voice brought from heaven says concerning Christ alone, Hear him. Therefore, the Roman Pontiffs are not to be heard if they bring forth anything beyond or against the doctrine of Christ. Estius objects to this place 1. that it was said by the Lord to the disciples Luc. 10. v. 16. He who hears you, hears me, and he who rejects you, rejects me. Resp. 1. properly and principally this saying deals with the Apostles. 2. Secondarily and consequently it can also be accommodated to other Doctors of the Church, but with this limitation, if they bring forth things conformable to the doctrine of Christ, Matth. 23. v. 17. Do not be called Masters, because your one Master is Christ. cap. 28. v. 20. teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. Rom. 16. v. 16. Observe those who cause dissensions and scandals παρὰ τὴν διδαχὴν contrary to the doctrine which you have learned. Gal. 1. v. 8. If we or an Angel from heaven evangelize to you παρ' ὅ besides that which we have evangelized to you, let him be anathema. 1. Tim. 6. v. 3. If anyone ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ and does not acquiesce to the sound words of Christ etc. v. 4. he is proud, knowing nothing. 3. Therefore, the Prelates of the Church are to be heard, but insofar as they hear Christ speaking in the Scriptures.

2. Lorinus objects, that it is not prohibited by these words that we should hear Moses and Elias, since Christ afterwards referred the Jews to Moses Ioh. 5. v. 45. and introduced Abraham promising riches, that his brothers might hear Moses and the Prophets here Luc. 16. v. 30. and frequently confirmed his doctrine, as did his disciples by the testimony of the same. Therefore, it cannot be elicited from these words that no one at all is to be heard besides Christ. Resp. the voice of Moses, the Prophets, and the Apostles is not opposed to the voice of Christ, but subordinated to the same; therefore, when Christ alone is commanded to be heard, not Moses, not the Prophets, not the Apostles, but those who bring a doctrine foreign to the Scriptures are excluded.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Estius gathers from the words Hear him in v. 17., because the heavenly Father commanded that his Son, whom he gave to the world as Redeemer, should also be heard as teacher, preceptor, and legislator, therefore deservedly by the Council of Trent. sess. 6. can. 21. anathema is said to those who establish that Christ Jesus was given by God to men as a Redeemer, in whom they might trust, and not also as a legislator, whom they might obey. Resp. 1. none of us denies that Christ can be called a legislator in that sense and respect, because at once with the Father and the Holy Spirit he implanted the law in the hearts of men at the first creation, promulgated the command concerning not eating the fruit of the forbidden tree, and was present at the solemn repetition of the law on Mount Sinai. 2. It is also certain that Christ can be called a legislator, in that sense and respect, that in the ministry of his preaching he proposed to his hearers not only the Gospel concerning the gratuitous remission of sins, but also the law, and vindicated the same from Pharisaical corruptions and restored it to its pristine splendor.

3. Far be it, therefore, that anyone should wish to deny that Christ is to be heard obediently when he repeats the law of God and exhorts us to the pursuit of good works.

4. But this is in question, Whether Christ in his own Mediatorial office is a legislator, who came into the world for that end, that he might promulgate certain new laws and render the Mosaic law more perfect, which we deny, but the Papists affirm, yet they can prove it neither from this passage, nor from other sayings of Scripture.

2. Lorinus comments thus on the same verse: It matters little if we make the Angel the immediate former of the voice, just as also of the cloud, for he spoke in the place of the Father. Resp. Nay, indeed, it matters a great deal that we establish both the voice and the cloud as the immediate work of God, otherwise the mystery of the Trinity will not be able to be firmly proven from this θεοφανεία. The ancient fathers attribute the formation of the voice and the cloud not to an Angel, but to the Most Holy Trinity, as is evident from the sayings of Augustine and Fulgentius cited above.

3. From the fact that the mountain on which Christ was transfigured is called holy, and that other places also are called holy, the Papists attempt to establish their pilgrimages to the places of the Saints. Bellarmine, book 3, on the worship of Saints, chapter 8. Resp. 1. The Apostle calls that mountain of Galilee, on which the transfiguration of Christ was made, holy, not because of any peculiar holiness inherent in that place, of which those who travel to it might become participants, but because of the divine manifestation made in it, in which sense also the place in which the Lord appeared to Moses Exod. 3. v. 5. and Josh. c. 5. v. 15. is called holy. The holy Prophets and Apostles spoke of holy things on this mountain. Christ, that Holy of Holies Dan. 9 v. 24., received glory and honor from the Father on this mountain; nay, the whole most holy Trinity in a peculiar manner on this mountain manifested itself. 2. Salmero thinks that by the epithet of holiness an allusion is made to the name of Mount Tabor. טהור for it signifies pure, clean, etc. With this hypothesis standing, no support for pilgrimages to the places of the saints will come from this appellation. 3. That certain places and parts of the earth are said to be cursed on account of sin, Gen. 3. v. 17.cap. 4. v. 11. and are said to be holy, that happens on account of the preaching of the word and the exercise of divine worship. Thus, that Jerusalem is called the holy city,Matth. 4. v. 5. is explained for that reason Esai. 31. vers. 9. because there was in it the fire and hearth of Jehovah, that is, because ignitions and sacrifices were offered there by the command of GOD. Therefore, wherever the word of GOD is preached, there the holiness of a place cannot be lacking, nor is it necessary that pilgrimages be undertaken to the places of the saints.

Observations. 1. The foundation of our faith is not the ingeniously devised commentaries of men, but the divine oracles.

2. All other sciences are said to be in a certain way fables, except for sacred Scripture, and this on account of four things which are found in a fable. First, the fable itself seems to have falsehood. Second, obscurity. Third, novelty. Fourth, uselessness. But sacred Scripture has the purity of truth, against the first; the clarity of speech, against the second; the antiquity of the matter, against the third; the fruitful utility, against the fourth. Iohann. Huss. in comm. h. l.

3. The first coming of Christ was indeed one of infirmity, the second of majesty: meanwhile, however, even in his first coming, Christ sometimes exerted certain rays of divine majesty and power, communicated to him according to his human Nature.

4. The Apostles are eyewitnesses αὐτόπται καὶ ἐπόπται Iohan. 1. v. 14.Actor. 10. vers. 41.1. Iohan. 1. v. 1. Therefore their testimony is worthy of faith.

5. Because Peter, James, and John were to see the agony of Christ in the garden, they therefore had to be encouraged beforehand by the vision of the glory of Christ, lest they be scandalized.

6. Christ received glory from his heavenly Father, but he did not receive glory from men Ioh. 5. v. 41. nay, when he was glorified by men in his royal entry, he nevertheless sought to be glorified by the Father. Iohann. 12. v. 28. so let us also not seek glory among men, but among God. Ioh. 5. v. 44.

7. The glory which Christ received from the Father in the transfiguration is not some finite glory, but truly divine and infinite glory, because it is the glory as of the only-begotten of the FatherJohn 1. v. 14., whence in that very glorification this voice sounds from heaven: This is my beloved Son. But Christ received that glory according to his human nature from the Father, because it shone forth from his body like solar rays through his garments. Therefore, to Christ according to his human nature, truly divine and infinite glory was communicated, whence the Greek Fathers say that Christ βολίδας τῆς θεότητος ἐκ σαρκὸς σου θεολαμπούσης emitted.

9. Oecumenius in his commentary on this place notes that the heavenly Father testified publicly concerning his Son manifested in the flesh with an audible voice from heaven on three occasions in all. First, in the Baptism, which testimony is describedMatt. 3. v. 17.Mark 1. v. 11.Luke 3. v. 22.Secondly, in the transfiguration, which testimony is describedMatt. 17. verse 5.Mark 9. v. 7.Luke 9. v. 35. & in this place of Peter. Thirdly, a little before the passion, when a voice came from heaven, saying: I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again, which testimony is described John 12. v. 28.

9. The voice of the heavenly Father heard in the transfiguration was an infallible testimony concerning the origin and mission of this heavenly Teacher. John 3. v. 31.He who comes from heaven is above all.chap. 6. v. 38.I have descended from heaven, not that I might do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. Moreover, Moses, Elijah, Peter, James, and John stand by, so that it may be intimated that both the Law and the Prophets in the Old Testament and the Apostles in the New Testament testify concerning Christ, and that he alone is to be heard by all.

10. This most highly commends the authority of Prophetic Scripture, that GOD speaking from heaven uses no other words than those of Scripture. Thus all the words of this Voice brought down from heaven are taken from the writings of the Old Testament, whence also a little later Peter adds v. 19: We have a more firm Prophetic word &c.
