For that which the heavenly Father says, This is my Son, that is taken from Ps. 2. v. 7.You are my Son,Prov. 30. v. 4.What is his name, and what is the name of his Son? That this Son is called ὁ ἀγαπητὸς, is taken from the types of the Old Testament. For concerning Isaac, who was a type of Christ, God says Gen. 22. v. 2.Take your only Son τὸν ἀγαπητὸν. Concerning Solomon, who likewise was A type of Christ, it is said 2. Sam. 12. v. 25. that David called him Jedidiah because of the Lord, i. e. because the Lord loved him, as is had in the preceding verse 24. That which the heavenly Father says concerning this Son, in whom I am well pleased, is taken from Esai. 42. v. 1., which passage Matthew also cap. 12. v. 18. alleges, and in express words accommodates to Christ. From these O. T. passages, as from their proper seat, a complete exposition of that paternal voice can be sought.

11. When God looks upon the human race lying in sins according to the law, He sees mere abomination, Psal. 14. v. 2. & He utters that sad voice, it repenteth me that I have made man, Genes. 6. vers. 6. but when He beholds believers in His beloved Son, then He has good pleasure in them because of that beloved Son of His.

12. Because Esai. 42. v. 1. the heavenly Father says concerning the person of Christ, in him my soul is well pleased: therefore because of this beloved Son He also says concerning the Church. Esai. 62. v. 4. Thou shalt be called my good pleasure in her, because the Lord has good pleasure in thee.

13. In this address of the heavenly Father is proposed the sum of the whole doctrine concerning the person, office, benefits, and their application of Christ. Concerning the person of Christ the heavenly Father testifies that this son of Mary is His only-begotten, natural, and proper Son, and therefore in the unity of person true GOD and true MAN, which differs very far from all adoptive sons, inasmuch as they are ψιλοὶ ἄνθρωποι, and are loved by the Father only in this natural and only-begotten Son of GOD and because of Him. The benefits are signified by these words, in whom I am well pleased. The mode of application is added Matth. 17. v. 5. that He is to be heard and faith in Him is to be conceived from the word.

14. That mountain, on which Christ is transfigured, is called holy. Doubtless Christ, that holy of holies Dan. 9. v. 24. sanctifies all things by His advent and His gracious presence. When therefore through faith He prepares a dwelling place for Himself in our hearts Eph. 3. v. 17. He also sanctifies us. Iohann. 17. v. 19. I sanctify myself for them, that they also may be sanctified in the truth.

14. Christ delighted in mountains, He preached on a mountain, Matth. 5. vers. 1. He prayed on a mountain Matth. 14. vers. 23. He fed the crowds on a mountain Matth. 15. vers. 29. on a mountain, that is in the upper room of the city In Jerusalem, built upon Mount Sion, He instituted and celebrated the Eucharist, on a mountain He was crucified, on a mountain He offered Himself to be seen by the disciples after the resurrection Matth. 26 v. 16. from a mountain He ascended into heaven Actor. 1. vers. 12. for He is that mystical Bridegroom, of whom it is said Cant. 2. vers. 8. Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills. Origen. homil. 3. in Cant.

16. On Mount Tabor Christ held a sermon concerning the beatitudes, as Jerome establishes in chapter 5 of Matthew, because after the sermon is finished Christ is said to have descended into Capernaum, neighboring Mount Tabor. Luc. 7. vers. 1. Thus, therefore, on the same mountain He both showed the way of blessedness, and proposed a certain mirror of the same in the transfiguration.

17. Tertullian, book 4 against Marcion, chapter 22. It was fitting that the New Testament be signed on that elevation (on the mountain) on which the Old had been written. And a little before. I recognize the form of the place, for the Creator had also initiated the former people at the mountain both by vision and by His voice.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco 1. Recténe in plerisque Codd. Latinis v. 16. legatur: indoctas fabulas secuti? Resp. ita quidem legunt Leo IX. Epist. 1. ad Michaëlem Constantinopolitanum Imp. cap. 13. Hugo Cardinalis, Lyranus, Carthusianus, Caietanus, Titelmanus, Primaticcius in h. l. Maldonatus in Ioh. 15. v. 27. & Codd. Latini non pauci. Neque enim apparebat, quomodo fabulae possent dici doctae. Sed agnoscunt ipsimet Pontificii, rectiùs legi doctas fabulas, quo modo etiam correcti Codd. Latini hodie legunt. Salmero in hunc locum. Probabilior est lectio, quam Graeca litera porrigit, nempeσεσοφισμένους i. e. doctas, h. e. artificio & eloquentiâ compositas fabulas, & ita legit Hieronymus in cap. 3. ad Galatas. Gagnaeius in h. l. pro indoctas fabulas Graecè estσεσοφισμένουςid est, doctas & rhetorico artificio compositas, unde puto Interpretem vertisse doctas, prout quidam Codd. habent, sed â sciolo librario additum. Lorinus in h. l. Plurimi hac in re facimus Pontificiam autoritatem, quae nunc in emendatis Bibliis nos ita legere iubet. Conveniunt & in hoc Gagnaeius, Catharinus, Vatablus, Clarius, Salmeron, Arias, Lucas Brugensis. Estius in h. l. In multis Codd. legebatur indoctas pro doctas, sed veram lectionem ex Codicibus fide lioribus consentaneam Graeco nobis restituerunt epanorthotae Romani. Utinam verò in aliis locis versionem Latinam ex textu Graeco corrigerent!

Q. 2. Quinam sint illiσεσοφισμένοι μὺθοι,de quibus Apostolus v. 16. loquitur? Resp. 1. Christophorus â Castro in Comm. Baruch. 3. n. 12. sic disserit. Mythologi dicebantur Interpretes & explicatores fabularum, quas Poëtae doctissimi confinxerunt, sub quarum integumentis sapientiam quandam occultarunt, nam & res divinas & naturales, & ad mores pertinentes sub illis significabant, & propterea Petrus illas vocat doctas fabulas, quas Clemens lib. 6. Recognit. in persona Apionis aiebat habere rationem quandam cognatam & Philosophicam, quae per allegoriam exponi posset, cuiusmodi erant fabulae de variis Iovis. i. e. aëris trans figurationibus. Nam Metamorphosis Domini IESU non fuit talis, sed vera & gloriosa. Censet ergo Castrius, opponi invicem fabulas gentilium de metamorphosi suorum Deorum, & relationem Apostolicam de metamorphosi Christi. Sed quia Petrus doctrinae caelesti in genere opponit fabulas, ideò praestat, nomine illo generaliter accepto, quaevis commenta humana quocunque artificio excogitata intelligere. Lorinus in h. l. Omnes externas & alienas doctrinas appellare possismus fabulationes,Ps. 119. v. 85.quas narrant in Hebr. estכרוfodiunt superbi, per quas nos deiiciant in foveas, nam idem nomenשחותcum puncto in dextro, foveas; in sinistro, significat nugas & ineptias. 2. Quas enim Apostolus intelligat doctas fabulas, colligi potest tùm ex locis parallelis, tùm ex scriptionis huius obiecto. Loca parallela sunt 1. Tim. 1. v. 4.μηδὲ προσέχειν μύθοις καὶ ἀπέρανταις γενεαλογίαις, ubi per μύθους intelliguntur fabulae Iudaicae, ut apparet ex subiecta voce γενεαλογίαις, in quibus per scrupulosas & inutiles quaestiones Iudaei sese detinebant. cap. 4. v. 7.τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ.2. Timoth. 4. vers. 4.ἀπό μέν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσι. Ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μὺθους ἐκτραπήσονται.Tit. 1. v. 14.μὴ προσέχοντες ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοι, καἰ ἐντολαῖς ἀνθρώπων. Obiectum scriptionis sunt conversi ex Iudaeis & gentilibus. Ergo Iudaicas & Ethnicas fabulas intelligit. Iudaeorum fabulae in libro quarto Esdrae & in Thalmudicis libris magnâ copiâ occurrunt. Gentilium fabulae in Hesiodi Theogonia, Ovidii metamorphosi, & alibi pasim proponuntur. 3. Illos postmodùm imitati Simoniani, Gnostici, Valentiniani & alii haeretici, qui de DEO, de Angelis, de aeonibus complures fabulas confinxerunt. De Gnosticis Augustinus lib. de haeresibus cap. 6. sic scribit. Tradunt dogmata fabulo sissimis plena figmentis, &c. & illos qui eis credunt, faciunt non multâ, ut putant, scientiâ pollere, sed multâ, ut ita dicam, fabulositate vanescere. Oecumenius in h. l. statuit indicari Valentinianos, quiβυθοὺς καὶ σιγηνcomminiscebantur, profunda & silentium: verisimile autem esse, eos illo tempore iam suboriri caepisse.

Q. 3. An voculaπαρουσίαin v. 16. primum vel secundum potiùs Christi adventum denotet? Resp. 1. Vatablus, Caietanus, Clarius, Salmero, Erasmus, Gagnaeius, Fevardentius, Saa &c. in comm. h. l. accipiunt de primo Christi adventu, videlicet de adventu & praesentia Christi per incarnationem, cui expositioni conforme est illud, quod Melchior Canus lib. 12. Locorum cap. 14. virtutem seu potentiam intelligit eam, quâ Verbum caro factum; praesentiam, quâ habitavit in nobisIoh. 1. v. 14. Lorinus in h. l. Praesentiae nomine Oeconomiam totam Christi in carne comprehendo, per virtutem intelligo magis propriè miracula. Cornel. â Lapide in h. l. Perstringit Simonem Magum, qui se pro Christo venditabat, seque vocabat virtutem Dei,Act. 8. v. 10.q. d. Nos praedicamus Christum esse Dei virtutem, non Simonem Magum.1. Cor. 1. v. 23. Qui hanc sententiam amplectuntur, per παρουσίαν intelligunt adventum Filii Dei in carnem, de quo 1. Tim. 1. v. 15. dicitur, quòd Christus Iesusἦλθενvenerit in mundum, peccatores salvos facere; per δύναμιν intelligunt divinam illam vim Christi, quae in miraculis, cumprimis verò in resurrectione sese exeruit. Rom. 1. v. 4. Quidam etiam δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν eo modo coniungunt, ut iuxta Hebraismum sit idem, quod potens adventus h. e. adventus ad potentiam exercendam susceptus. Exeruit autem Christus suam potentiam in primo adventu, tùm efficaciter persuadendo quae docebat, tùm doctrinam suam miraculis confirmando, tùm per passionem & mortem suam Diabolum vincendo, tùm gloriosè ex mortuis propriâ virtute resurgendo,1. Ioh. 3. v. 8. 2. Sed rectiùs de secundo Christi adventu hic locus Apostolicus intelligitur. 1. quia vox παρουσίαν nuspiam in N. T. de primo Christi adventu, sed semper de secundo adventu usurpatur. Matth. 24. v. 3.27.37. & 39.1. Cor. 15. v. 23.1. Thessal. 2. v. 19.cap. 3. v. 13.cap. 4. v. 15.cap. 5. v. 23.2. Thess. 2. v. 1. & 8.Iac. 5. v. 7. & 8.1. Ioh. 2. v. 28. Primus Christi adventus vocatur ἔλευσιςAct. 7. v. 52.εἰσοδοςAct. 13. v. 24. secundus παρουσία & ἐπιφάνεια,1. Tim. 6. v. 14.2. Tim. 4. v. 1. & 8.Tit. 2. v. 13. 2. In eadem significatione utitur Petrus voce παρουσίας in hac ipsa Epistola cap. 3. v. 4.Ubi promissio adventus eius? v. 12. expectantesτὴν παρουσίαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας 3. Eandem probat scopus huius Epistolae. Constat enim ex cap. 3. quod inter coetera eos, ad quos scribit, praemunire voluerit contra empaectas, secundum Christi adventum in dubium vocantes. 4. Primus Christi adventus potiùs fuit infirmitatis & humilitatis, quàm virtutis & maiestatis: secundus autem erit in gloria & virtute. 5. Transfiguratio Christi, ad quam Apostolus in v. seq. provocat, fuit praeludium maiestatis & gloriae, in qua Christus in secundo adventu sese conspicuum exhibiturus. 6. Inde Lorinus â reliquis Pontificiis hac in parte discedens ad h. l. sic commentatur. Nec displicet, si per praesentiam interpretemur adventum secundum, qui erit in maiestate & virtute, ac cuius transfiguratio typus quidam fuit, de qua mentio subiicitur. Certè paulò antè v. 10. & 11.hortatus fuerat ad bona opera, ut sic abundanter ministraretur introitus in aeternum regnum: meminerat quoque proximè de obitu suo, est autem cum morte, iudicioque cognatio.

Q. 4. Quaenam sit magnifica illa gloria in v. 17. ex qua vox delata? Resp. 1. Quidam illud accipiunt dictum de caelo, quod est thronus divinae maiestatis & gloriae, cùm in Baptismo Christi eadem voxἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶνdelata dicaturMatth. 3. v. 7.cumque hoc loco inv. 18. seq. dicatur. Et nos audivimus vocem illamἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθείσαν. Sed Matthaeus & Marcus dicunt in transfiguratione vocem hanc venisse ἐκ τῆς νεφέληςex nube. 2. Rectiùs ergo dicitur, quòd vox illa dicatur delata â magnifica gloria, h. e, â magnificentissimo & gloriossimo DEO Patre, quia Pater caelestis per eam magnificè & gloriosè peculiarem suam praesentiam demonstravit. 3. Quidam statuunt, per magnificam illam gloriam intelligi nubem illam lucidam, quae, uti constat ex Evangelistarum descriptione, non solùm Christum, sed etiam Mosen & Eliam prae sentes obumbravit, ut sit sensus: â magnifica gloria h. e. ex nube lucida & clara, quae index erat divinae gloriae h. e. DEI Patris, qui ex ea vocem edebat, ex quo porrò colligunt, Patrem caelestem in lucida illa nube, velut in externo quodam symbolo suam praesentiam manifestasse, sicut aliàs in V. T. in nube lucida aliquoties sese revelavit. Sed rectius dicitur, nubem lucidam in hac θεοφανείᾳ fuisse Symbolum praesentiae Spiritus sancti, qui ut in Baptismo Christi manifestavit se in specie columbae, sic in transfiguratione manifestavit se in nube lucida, ut hac ratione etiam tertiae Deitatis personae externum aliquod praesentiae Symbolum tribuatur.

Q. 5. An haec vox fuerit solius Patris, an verò totius Trinitatis? Resp. distinguendum est inter vocis formationem & appropriationem. Illa toti Trinitati tribuenda. August. lib. 4. de Trinit. cap. 21. Trinitas simul operata est & vocem Patris & carnem Filii & columbam Spiritus sancti. Fulgentius de fide ad Petrum cap. 9. Tene illam vocem, quâ solus locutus est Deus Pater, & illam carnem, quâ solus homo factus est unigenitus Deus; & illam columbam, in cuius specie Spiritus sanctus super Christum descendit, opera esse totius sacrosanctae Trinitatis &c. Haec verò soli Patri competit. August. serm. 63. de verbo Domini Trinitas fecit de caelo columbam, sed non pertinet nisi ad solum Spiritum sanctum. Trinitas fecit de caelo vocem, sed non pertinet vox nisi ad solum Patrem.

Q. 6. Recéne in versione Latina v. 16. addatur. Ipsum audite? Resp. 1. Quamvis omnes tres Evangelistae in descriptione transfigurationis Christi haec verba addant, ex quo dubio procul factum, quòd autor vulgatae versionis eadem huc retulerit, tamen in Graecis -odd hoc loco ea non habentur, proinde non sunt huius capitis pars genuina & Canonica. Certum quidem est, hanc vocem in transfiguratione Christi fuisse â Patre caelesti additam, ut manifestum faceret, Christum esse magnum illum Prophetam, de quo Moses, qui in transfiguratione praesens erat, vaticinatus fuerat, ac ipsum ab omnibus audiendum esse praedixerat, Deut. 18. vers. 18. tamen Petrus non contentus prioribus vocis paternae verbis, haec posteriora, utpote iam ante illis, ad quos scribebat, notissima adiicere noluit.

Q. 7. Quis fuerit sanctus ille mons, in quo Christus transfiguratus? Resp. 1. Evangelistae in specie illud non exprimunt, sed hoc solùm dicunt, fuisse montem excelsum. 2. Quidam ergo statuunt, fuisse Libanum montem illum Palaestinae altissimum, cuius crebra in Scripturis sacris fit mentio. Iacobus Faber Stapulensis in cap. 9. Marci. Franciscus Lucas Brugensis in cap. 17. Matth. quod probare se posse putant ex Marc. 9. v. 30.Et inde profecti praetergrediebantur Galilaeam, ex quo colligunt, transfigurationem non in Galiaea, in qua situs fuit mons Thabor, sed in partibu, Caesareae Philippi, adeoque in vicino monte Libani factam. 3. Communior tamen sententia statuit, Christum in monte Thabor fuisse transfiguratum, qui mons est in Galilaeae campestribus rotundus ac sublimis, ut eum describit Hieronymus in comm. Oseae 5 ubi etiam docet, fuisse eum aliàs dictum Ithabyrium. Iosephus libro 4 de Bello Iudaico cap. 2. memorat, altitudinem eius ad trigesimum usque stadium assurgere, in vertice autem viginti stadiorum planiciem habere. Haec est sententia Cyrilli Hiero solymitani catech. 12. Hieronymi Epist. 27. in Epitaph. Marcellae. Damasceni in serm. de transfig. Domini. Euthymii in Psalm. 88.Bedae de locis sanctis cap. 17. Philonis Carpathii in comm. Cantic. quam confirmant & antecedentes & sequentes Historiae apud Evangelistas, quae ostendunt, Haec esse facta in Galilaea, quia mox â transfiguratione descendit Capernaum, quae urbs vicina monti Thabor.Matth. 17. v. 23. 4. Nec potest contrarium colligi ex Marc. 9. v. 30. quia παραπορεύεσθεν significat, celeriter, latenter & in transcursu pertransire durchziehen/ non autem praetergredi sive praeterire, umbzichen.

Ἐναντιοφανείας. 1. Vox Patris hoc loco dicitur allatad è caelo v. 18. AtMatth. 17. v. 5.dicitur ex nube sonuisse. Resp. nubes illa miraculosa descendebat ex caelo, ex nube deferebatur vox illa Patris, ergo etiam ex caelo vox illa fuit delata. 2. Vox Patris caelestis in transfiguratione audita sic describitur. Hic est Filius meus dilectus, At vox illa fuit audita ex nube, quae erat externum Symbolum Spiritus Sancti. Ergo Filius dicitur Spiritus Sancti Filius. Resp. nubes fuit Symbolum externum Spiritus Sancti, vox ex nube audita fuit Symbolum externum Patris. Ergo is, qui ex nube loquitur, vocat Christum dilectum Filium suum, non autem is cuius Symbolum externum est nubes, ex qua vox auditur.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Ad fabulas illas, quibus doctrinae caelestis veritas & sinceritas opponitur, meritò referuntur fabulae Papisticae, in speculo Vincentii, in Historiali Antonini, in Legenda aurea, in sermonibus Discipuli de tempore, in Historiis Iacobi de Voragine, in Dormisecurè & aliis huius farinae vel potiùs furfuris scriptis annotatae. De Legenda aurea pronunciat Melchior Canus lib. 11. Locor. comm. cap. 6. §. Lex verò &c. quod eam scripserit homo ferrei oris, plumbei cordis, animi certè parùm severi ac prudentis.

2. Christus est naturalis, unigenitus & aeternus Dei Filius, ac proinde verus cum Patre & Spiritu sancto Deus. Hilarius lib. 3. de Trinit. p. 26. Multi nos fuii, sed non talis hic est Filius. Hic enim verus & proprius & unigenitus est Filius, origine, non adoptione; veritate, non nuncupatione; nativitate, non creatione. Leo Magnus serm. de transfigur. Hic est Filius meus dilectus, quem â me non separat Deitas, non dividit potestas non discernit aeternitas. Hic est Filius meus, non adoptivus sed proprius; non aliunde creatus, sed ex me genitus, nec de alia Natura mihi factus comparabilis, sed de mea essentia mihi natus aequalis.

3, Ex verbis, quae in vulgata versione v. 17. adduntur & Matth. 17. v. 5. habentur, Hunc audite, sic colligimus. De solo Christo vox caelitus delata dicit, Ipsum audite. Ergo Pontifices Romani non sunt audiendi, si praeter vel contra doctrinam Christi aliquid proferant. Excipit 1. Estius ad h. l. â Domino dictum esse discipulisLuc. 10. v. 16.Qui vos audit, me audit, & qui vos spernit, me spernit. Resp. 1. propriè & principaliter hoc dictum agit de Apostolis. 2. Secundariò & consequenter etiam ad alios Ecclesiae Doctores accommodari potest, sed cum hac limitatione, si proferant doctrinae Christi conformia, Matth. 23. v. 17.Ne vocemini Magistri, quia Magister vester unus est Christus.cap. 28. v. 20.docentes eos servare, quae ego praecepi vobis.Rom. 16. v. 16.Observate eos qui dissensiones & offendiculaπαρὰ τὴν διδαχὴνpraeter doctrinam, quam didicistis, faciunt.Gal. 1. v. 8.Si licet nos aut Angelus de caelo evangelizet vobisπαρ' ὅpraeter id, quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit.1. Tim. 6. v. 3. Si quis ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ& non acquiescit sanis sermonibus Christi &c. v. 4. superbus est, nihil sciens. 3. Audiendi ergo Ecclesiae Praesules, sed quatenus Christum in Scripturis loquentem audiunt.

2. Lorinus excipit, non prohiberi his verbis, quò minùs audiamus Mosen & Eliam, cum Christus postea remiserit Iudaeos ad MosenIoh. 5. v. 45.ac Abrahamum induxerit divitire spondentem, ut audirent fratres eius hîc Mosen & ProphetasLuc. 16. v. 30.ac crebrò confirmaverit doctrinam suam, nec non discipuli eius testimonio eorundem. Ergo non posse ex his verbis elici, nullum penitus audiendum esse praeter Christum. Resp. vox Mosis Prophetarum & Apostolorum non est opposita voci Christi, sed eidem subordinata, igitur quando solus Christus audiri iubetur, non Moses, non Prophetae, non Apostoli, sed qui alienam â Scripturis doctrinam afferunt, excluduntur.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Estius ex verbis Ipsum audite in v. 17. colligit, quia Pater caelestis Filium suum, quem mundo Redemtorem dedit, etiam audiri tanquam doctorem, praeceptorem & legislatorem praecepit, ideò meritò â Concilio Tridentino. sess. 6. can. 21. anathema dici illis, qui statuunt, Christum Iesum â Deo datum fuisse hominibus, ut Redemtorem, cuifidant, non etiam ut legislatorem, cui oboediant. Resp. 1. nemo nostrûm negat, Christum posse dici legislatorem sensu & respectu eo, quod unâ cum Patre & Spiritu sancto legem cordibus hominum in primâ creatione indiderit, mandatum de non comedendo vetitae arboris fructu promulgaverit, ac solenni legis repetitioni in monte Sinai interfuerit. 2. Certum & hoc est, Christum posse dici legislatorem, sensu & respectu eo, quòd in ministerio praedicationis suae non solùm Evangelium de gratuita peccatorum remissione, sed etiam legem auditoribus suis proposuerit, eandemque â corruptelis Pharisaicis vindicaverit & pristino nitori restituerit.

3. Absit igitur, ut quisquam negare velit, Christum esse obedienter audiendum, quando legem Dei repetit & ad bonorum operum studium nos exhortatur.

4. Hoc vero in quaestione est, An Christus in proprio suo officio Mediatorio sit legislator, qui eo fine in mundum venerit, ut novas quasdam leges promulgaret ac legem Mosaicam perfectiorem redderet, quod nos negamus, Pontificii vero affirmant, sed nec ex hoc loco, nec ex aliis Scripturae dictis probare possunt.

2. Lorinus ad eundem. vers. sic commentatur. Parum refert, si Angelum formatorem vocis faciamus immediatum, sicut & nubis, loquebatur enim vice Patris. Resp. imò verò plurimùm refert, ut & vocem & nubem immediatum Dei opus statuamus, aliàs Trinitatis mysterium ex hac θεοφανεία firmiter probari haud poterit. Piiveteres formationem vocis & nubis non Angelo, sed Sacrosanctae Trinitati tribuunt, ut constat ex dictis Augustini & Fulgentii superiùs citatis.

3. Exeo, quòd mons, in quo Christus transfiguratus est, dicitur sanctus, quodque alia etiam loca dicuntur Sancta, Pontificii suas peregrinationes ad loca Sanctorum statum inare conantur. Bellarmin. lib. 3. de cultu Sanct. cap. 8. Respon. 1. Montem illum Galilaeae, in quo Christi transfiguratio fuit facta, Apostolus vocat Sanctum, non propter Sanctitatem aliquam peculiarem loco illi inhaerentem, cuius participes fieri possint, qui ad illum proficisountur, sed propter divinam manifestationem in eo factam, quo sensu etiam locus, in quo Dominus Mosi Exod. 3. v. 5. & Ios. c. 5. v. 15. apparuit, sanctus vocatur. Sancti Prophetae & Apostoli in hoc monte de sanctis rebus locuti sunt. Christus sanctus ille Sanctorum Dan. 9 v. 24. in hoc monte â Patre gloriam & honorem accepit; quinimò tota sacrosancta Trinitas in hoc monte peculiariratione sese manifestavit. 2. Salmero existimat epitheto sanctitatis alludi ad nomen montis Thabor.טהורenim significat purum, mundum &c. Stante hac hypothesi nihil subsidii peregrinationibas ad loca sanctorum ex hac appellatione accedet. 3. Quòd certa quaedam loca ac partes terrae propter peccatum maledictae, Gen. 3. v. 17.cap. 4. v. 11. dicuntur sanctae, id fit propter verbi praedicationem & cultus divini exercitium. Sic quod Ierusalem dicitur civitas sancta,Matth. 4. v. 5. eius rei causa exponitur Esai. 31. vers. 9. quia fuit in ea Iehovae ignis ac focus, h. e. quia ignitiones & sacrificia ex DEI mandato ibi fuêre oblata. Ergo ubicunque verbum DEI praedicatur, ibi sanctitas loci non potest desiderari, nec est necesse, ut ad loca sanctorum peregrinationes suscipiantur.

Observationes. 1. Fidei nostrae fundamentum non sunt hominum commenta ingeniosè excogitata, sed divina oracula.

2. Omnes aliae scientiae dicuntur quodammodo fabulae, exceptâ sacra Scripturâ, & hoc propter quatuor, quae in fabula inveniuntur. Primò ipsa fabula videtur habere falsitatem. Secundò, obscuritatem. Tertiò, novitatem. Quartò. inutilitatem. Sacra verò Scriptura habet veritatis puritatem, contra primum; sermonis claritatem, contra secundum; rei antiquitatem, contra tertium; fructuosam utilitatem, contra quartum. Iohann. Huss. in comm. h. l.

3. Primus Christi adventus fuit quidem infirmitatis, secundus maiestatis: interim tamen etiam in primo suo adventu Christus quosdam divinae maiestatis & potentiae, sibi secundùm humanam Naturam communicatae, radios quandoque exeruit.

4. Apostoli sunt testes oculati αὐτόπται καὶ ἐπόπταιIohan. 1. v. 14.Actor. 10. vers. 41.1. Iohan. 1. v. 1. Ergo testimonium ipsorum est fide dignum.

5. Quia Petrus, Iacobus & Iohannes agonem Christi in horto visuri erant, ideò visione gloriae Christi priùs animari debuerunt, ne scandalizarentur.

6. Christus â Patre suo caelesti accepit gloriam, ab hominibus autem non accepit gloriam Ioh. 5. v. 41. quinimò cum in regio suo ingressu ab hominibus glorificaretur, tamen â Patre glorificari periit. Iohann. 12. v. 28. sic & nos non quaeramus gloriam apud homines, sed apud Deum. Ioh. 5. v. 44.

7. Gloria, quam in transfiguratione Christus â Patre accepit, non est gloria aliqua finita, sed verè divina & infinita gloria, quia est gloria velut unigeniti â PatreIoh. 1. v. 14. unde in ipsa glorificatione sonat haec vox de caelo. Hic est Filius meus dilectus. At gloriam illam Christus secundum humanam Naturam â Patre accepit, quia ex ipsius corpore instar radiorum solarium per vestes reluxit. Ergo Christo secundum humanam Naturam gloria verè divina & infinita est communicata, unde Graeci Patres dicunt, quòd Christus βολίδας τῆς θεότητος ἐκ σαρκὸς σου θεολαμπούσηςemiserit.

9. Oecumenius in comm. h. l. notat, quòd Pater caelestis tribus omninò vicibus voce audibili è caelo de Filio suo in carne manifestato publicè testificatus sit. Primò in Baptismo, quae testificatio describiturMatth. 3. v. 17.Marc. 1. v. 11.Luc. 3. v. 22.Secundò, in transfiguratione quae testificatio describiturMatth. 17. vers. 5.Marc. 9. v. 7.Luc. 9. v. 35. & in hoc loco Petrino. Tertiò, paulò ante passionem, quando vox de caelo venit, dicens: Et glorificavi, & iterum glorificabo, quae testificatio describitur Ioh. 12. v. 28.

9. Vox Patris caelestis in transfiguratione audita, fuit infallibile testimonium de caelestis huius Doctoris origine & missione. Ioh. 3. v. 31.Qui de caelo venit, est super omnes.cap. 6. v. 38.Descendi de caelo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem eius, qui misit me. Adstant insuper Moses, Elias, Petrus, Iacobus & Iohannes, ut innuatur, & legem & Prophetas in V. & Apostolos in N. T. de Christo testari, ipsum solum ab omnibus audiendum esse.

10. Hoc maximè commendat Scripturae Propheticae autoritatem, quod DEUS ê caelo loquens, non aliis quàm Scripturae verbis utitur. Sic omnia huius Vocis caelitus delatae verba ex scriptis V. T. sunt desumta, unde etiam paulò pòst subiungit Petrus v. 19. Habemus firmiorem Propheticum sermonem &c. Nam quod Pater caelestis dicit. Hic est Filius meus, illud desumtum ex Psal. 2. v. 7.Tu es Filius meus,Prov. 30. v. 4.Quod nomen eius, & quod nomen Filii eius? Quòd hic Filius vocatur ὁ ἀγαπητὸς, desumtum est ex typis V. T. De Isaaco enim, qui fuit Christi typus, dicit Deus Gen. 22. v. 2.Tolle Filium tuum unicumτὸν ἀγαπητὸν. De Salomone, qui itidem fuit Christi typus, dicitur 2. Sam. 12. v. 25. quòd David eum vocaverit Iedidah propter Dominum i. e. quia Dominus dilexit eum, ut habetur v. praeced. 24. Quod de hoc Filio dicit Pater caelestis, in quo mihi complacitum est, illud desumtum ex Esai. 42. v. 1. quem locum etiam Matthaeus cap. 12. v. 18. allegat, ac disertis verbis ad Christum accommodat. Ex hisce V. T. locis, tanquam ex propria sede, integra paternae illius vocis expositio peti potest.

11. Quando Deus genus humanum in peccatis iacens iuxta legem aspicit, meram videt abominationem, Psal. 14. v. 2. & tristem illam vocem emittit, paenitet me fecisse hominem,Genes. 6. vers. 6. sed quando credentes in dilecto Filio suo intuetur, tunc in illis propter dilectum illum Filium suum habet beneplacitum.

12. Quia Esai. 42. v. 1. de persona Christi dicit Pater caelestis, in eo complacitum est animae meae: ideò propter hunc dilectum Filium etiam de Ecclesia dicit. Esai. 62. v. 4.Vocaberis beneplacitum meum in ea, quoniam beneplacitum habet Dominus in te.

13. In hac concione Patris caelestis proponitur summa totius doctrinae de Christi persona, officio, beneficiis & eorum applicatione. De persona Christitestatur Pater caelestis, quod hic Mariae filius, sit filius suus unigenitus, naturalis ac proprius, & proinde in personae unitate verus DEUS & verus HOMO, quod longissimè differat ab omnibus adoptivis filiis, quippe qui sunt ψιλοὶ ἄνθρωποι, ac non nisi in hoc naturali & unigenito DEI Filio & propter illum â Patre diliguntur. Beneficia significantur his verbis, in quo mihi complacuit. Modus applicationis additur Matth. 17. v. 5. quòd sit audiendus & ex verbo fides in ipsum concipienda.

14. Mons ille, in quo Christus transfiguratur, vocatur sanctus. Nimirum Christus, sanctus ille sanctorumDan. 9. v. 24. omnia suo adventu & suâ gratiosâ praesentiâ sanctificat. Quando ergo per fidem in cordibus nostris habitaculum sibi parat Eph. 3. v. 17. etiam nos sanctificat.Iohann. 17. v. 19.Ego pro eis meipsum sanctifico, ut etiam ipsi sint sanctificati in veritate.

14. Christus montibus delectatus fuit, in monte praedicavit,Matth. 5. vers. 1. in monte oravit Matth. 14. vers. 23. in monte turbas pavit Matth. 15. vers. 29. in monte, hoc est in cenaculo urbis Hierosolymae, super montem Sion extructae, Eucharistiam instituit & celebravit, in monte crucifixus est, in monte discipulis post resurrectionem se conspiciendum praebuit Matth. 26 v. 16. ex monte in caelum ascendit Actor. 1. vers. 12. est enim Sponsus ille mysticus, de quo Cant. 2. vers. 8. dicitur. Ecce iste venit saliens in montibus, transiliens colles. Origen. homil. 3. in Cant.

16. In monte Thabor Christus sermonem habuit de beatitudinibus, ut statuit Hieronymus in cap. 5. Matth. quia finito sermone Christus dicitur descendisse in Capernaum, monti Thabor vicinum.Luc. 7. vers. 1. Sic ergo in eodem monte & viam beatitudinis ostendit, & speculum quoddam eiusdem in transfiguratione proposuit.

17. Tertullianus lib. 4. adv. Marcion. cap. 22. Oportebat in eo suggestu (in monte) consignari N. T. in quo conscriptum erat Vetus. Et paulò antè. Agnosco formam loci, nam & pristinum populum apud montem & visione & voce suâ creator initiaverat.

## 1:17
Connection. 1. He proves what he had said in the verse immediately preceding, that he had been ἐπόπτην τῆς μεγαλειότητος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, from the fact that he had been αὐτακουστὴς of a voice having descended from heaven, through which honor and glory had been conferred upon Christ.

2. He confirms the certainty of Christian doctrine from the authority and majesty of CHRIST, from whom he had received it: He confirms the authority and majesty of CHRIST from the glory and honor conferred upon him in the transfiguration, in which he was constituted the public Doctor of the whole world by the voice of the heavenly Father.

Exposition of the text. Λαβὼν γὰρ παρὰ θεοῦ Πατρὸς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν. The Greek λαβὼν, which the Vulgate rendered, receiving, has nothing to which it may be referred. It must be said, therefore, either that according to a customary Hebraism the substantive verb λαβὼν ἐτύγχανε, was receiving is to be understood; or that the participle is placed in the stead of the verb ἔλαβε he received, as Oecumenius notes and Vatablus repeats; or that the nominative of the participle is taken for the genitive absolute, so that the sense may be, when he had received, just as the Syrian also rendered it. [כד גיר נסב] for when he received.

Τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν Some establish that one and the same thing is signified in this place, in the sense that Christ received glorious honor from his heavenly Father, but it is more correctly said that two distinct things are signified. For Δόξα denotes that glory which shone forth from the body of Christ in the transfiguration, which the Evangelists describe in this way. Matth 17. vers. 2. μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν his face shone as the sun, and his garments became white as snow. Marc. 9. v. 3. his garments became shining and exceeding white as snow, such as a fuller upon earth cannot make white. Luc 9. vers. 29. ἐγγένετο τὸ εἰδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λεύκων ἐξαστράπτων. So great was the glory of the body, so great the splendor, so great the brightness, that it exerted itself through the garments themselves, which were otherwise dark and not at all diaphanous. But Τιμὴ denotes that excellent honor with which CHRIST was affected by his heavenly Father by a voice fallen from heaven, which exposition the following words prove. The Syrian δόξαν rendered by [תשבוחתא] from the root [שבח] he glorified, he celebrated with praises, Iohann. 16. vers. 14. but τιμὴν by [איקרא] from the root [יקר] he was heavy in authority or price, honorable, precious.

Φωνῆς ἐνεχθείσης αὐτῷ τοιᾶσδε ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης. The Vulgate rendered, by a voice coming down to him of this kind from the magnificent glory. But ἐνεχθείσης is properly carried or brought, as the Vulgate Interpreter himself rendered in the verse immediately following. But what kind of voice he understands he immediately explains, namely that which was delivered from heaven at the transfiguration of Christ. Therefore, the things which Drusius, book 1, page 6, brings forward from the Rabbis concerning בת קול the daughter of the voice (a certain mode of divine revelation, and the same one most used in the second temple after the death of Malachi, the last Prophet), and refers the reader to them in the exposition of this passage, are clearly foreign to this place. For this voice of the heavenly Father was clear, articulate, public, and heard by all present on the mountain.

Ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης. The Syrian rendered it after the glory adorned with his majesty. But the Apostle explains by these words the origin of that voice, through which heavenly honor was attributed to Christ. August. tract. 35. in John The Trinity formed the voice from the magnificent power, but that indicated the Father alone. Peter further recounts that voice word for word.

Οὑτὸς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς μου ἀγαμητὸς, εἰς ὅν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα. The Apostle recites the voice of the heavenly Father in the way in which it is described in Matthew, except that for ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα he says εἰ ὃν εὐδόκησα, which is the same by reason of sense, whence Matth. 12. v. 18. that sentence is brought forth in the same way as in this place, εἰς ὅν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου.

In the repetition of the article, ὁ υἱὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς there is great emphasis. This is that son of mine, that beloved one, which shows that Christ is not an adoptive, but a natural, proper, and only-begotten Son of God.Ioh. 1. v. 14.cap. 3. v. 16.Rom. 8. v. 32 etc.

Ὁ ἀγαπητὸς, does not only signify that this Son is intimately and in the highest degree loved by GOD the Father, (for how would he not be loved by the Father, who is begotten from eternity from his very substance, and is the substantial image of the Father?) but also that in him, through him, and on account of him, those who are adopted into sons by God the Father through faith in him are loved by GOD, as the Apostle explains, Eph. 1. v. 6. ἐχαρίτωσεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἠγαπημένῳ, and Christ Ioh. 17. v. 26. in his prayer προαγωνίῳ says in most sweet words. I pray Father, that the love with which you love me, may also be in them or towards them. The Syrian rendered it, [ברי חביבא] from the Syriac root [חבב] he cherished in his bosom, he held in delights, he loved most tenderly, in which respect the Son is said to be in the bosom of the Father,Ioh. 1, v. 18. and therefore ὁ ἀγαπητὸς of vehement love it has the signification, and it does not signify so much a beloved one, as a dear and lovable one. Cyprian, Epist. 63, chap. 6, translates most beloved.

Εἰς ὅν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα. The word Εὐδοκεῖν is used very frequently not only among the LXX Interpreters, but also in the New Testament for that which is, to be of a benevolent and inclined affection toward some thing or person, to be delighted and to rest in something. Theodoret on Psalm 5 notes, that the sacred scriptures call the good will of GOD εὐδοκίαν his love and affection toward us. With which agrees that of Jerome on chapter 1 of Ephesians, that εὐδοκία it properly signifies good pleasure, because not everything that has pleased can also immediately please well. Moreover, this phrase embraces the whole οἰκονομίαν, of our salvation, which consists in this, that since on account of sin all men are guilty of divine wrath and eternal damnation, no access is open to any for reconciliation with GOD, for the remission of sins, and for eternal life, except through this Son, through whom the heavenly Father is appeased and reconciled to the whole human race, upon whom when he looks, he lays aside all wrath and offense, in whom he has as it were deposited all his good pleasure, so that he who desires reconciliation with GOD, the remission of sins, and eternal life, may find grace in him alone. Augustine, book 2 de consens. Evang. chap. 14, expresses the emphasis thus, I have established my pleasure in you, through you I have decreed to fulfill what pleases me, so that henceforth I may not say, it repents me that I have made man. John 8, verse 29. I always do the things that are pleasing to him. Gloss. ordin. Through whom I have shown my good pleasure, and in him, who is pleasing and is mine, I have found it. But the safest and best explanation is gathered from parallel places of scripture. Isaiah 42, verse 1. from which these words are taken, the word רצה is had, which signifies to have good will toward someone, to hold something as grateful and acceptable, to rest in someone. It is signified, therefore, that the εὐδοκία of the heavenly Father rests in this Son, so that outside of him no one can become a participant of his εὐδοκίας: Luke 2, v. 14. when Christ was born on earth the Angels sing, ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία because, namely, he was born through whom the human race was to be reconciled to the heavenly Father. Luke 12, verse 32. it is called the εὐδοκία, of GOD because he wills to give the kingdom to those believing in CHRIST. Ephesians 1, verse 5. it is called εὐδοκία τοῦ θελήματος τοῦ θεοῦ, because he predestined us unto the adoption of sons through CHRIST. verse 9. It is called the ευδοηια, of GOD because He made known the mystery of His will concerning our salvation in the Gospel. Philip. 1. vers. 13. It is called the εὐδοκία, of GOD which works in us both to will and to do. Because therefore in CHRIST is all the εὐδοκία, of the Father, therefore all those benefits come to us through CHRIST and for the sake of CHRIST. The Syrian has the word [צבא] which signifies good pleasure, complacency, and inclination of mind.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Probat, quod in vers. proximè praeced. dixerat, se fuisse ἐπόπτην τῆς μεγαλειότητος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ex eo quod fuerit αὐτακουστὴς vocis caelitus delapsae, per quam honor & gloria Christo fuerit collata.

2. Certitudinem doctrinae Christianae confirmat ab autoritate & maiestate CHRISTI, â quo illam acceperit: Autoritatem & maiestatem CHRISTI confirmat â gloria & honore in transfiguratione ipsi collato, in qua publicus totius orbis Doctor voce Patris caelestis fuerit constitutus.

Textus expositio. Λαβὼν γὰρ παρὰ θεοῦ Πατρὸς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν. Graecum λαβὼν, quod Vulg. reddidit, accipiens, non habet quò referatur. Dicendum igitur, vel quod iuxta usitatum Hebraismum subintelligendum sit verbum substantivum λαβὼν ἐτύγχανε,accipiens fuit; vel quòd participium ponatur loco verbi ἔλαβεaccepit, ut notat Oecumenius & repetit Vatablus; vel quòd nominativus participii sumatur pro genitivo absoluto, ut sit sensus, cùm accepisset, sicut & Syrus reddidit. [כד גיר נסב]cùm enim accepit.

Τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν quidam statuunt, unum idemque hoc loco significare, sensu eo, quòd Christus gloriosum honorem â Patre suo caelesti acceperit, sed rectiùs dicitur, duo distincta significari. Δόξα enim notat gloriam illam, quae in transfiguratione ex Christi corpore refulsit, quam Evangelistae hoc modo describunt. Matth 17. vers. 2.μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶνresplenduit facies eius, sicut Sol, vestimenta autem eius facta sunt alba, sicut nix.Marc. 9. v. 3.vestimenta eius facta sunt splendentia & candida nimis velut nix, qualia fullo non potest super terram candida facere.Luc 9. vers. 29.ἐγγένετο τὸ εἰδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λεύκων ἐξαστράπτων. Tanta fuit corporis gloria, tantus splendor, tantus fulgor, ut per ipsas vestes alioqui obscuras ac minimè diaphanas sese exereret. Τιμὴ verò denotat eximium illum honorem, quo CHRISTUS â Patre suo caelesti voce caelitus delapsa fuit affectus, quam expositionem probant verba sequentia. Syrus δόξαν reddidit per [תשבוחתא] â rad. [שבח]glorificavit, encomiis celebravit,Iohann. 16. vers. 14.τιμὴν verò per [איקרא] â rad. [יקר]gravis fuit autoritate vel precio, honorabilis, preciosus.

Φωνῆς ἐνεχθείσης αὐτῷ τοιᾶσδε ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης. Vulg. reddidit, voce ad eum de lapsa huius cemodi â magnificâ gloria. Sed ἐνεχθείσης propriè est delata vel allata, ut in vers. proximè sequente ipse vulgatus Interpres reddidit. Qualem verò vocem intelligat, statim exponit, videlicet eam, quae in transfiguratione Christi fuit caelitus delata. Proinde, quae de בת קולfilia vocis (modo quodam divinae revelationis, eodemque infimo post mortem Malachiae ultimi Prophetae in secundo templo maximè usitato) Drusius lib. 1. praeterit. pag. 6. ex Rabinis adducit, & ad ea in expositione huius loci lectorem remittit, sunt ab hoc loco planè aliena. Fuit enim haec vox Patris caelestis clara, articulata, publica, ab omnibus in monte praesentibus audita.

Ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης. Syrus reddidit post gloriam maiestate sua decoram. Sed Apostolus his verbis exponit originem illius vocis, per quam Christo caelestis honor fuit attributus. August. tract. 35. in Ioh. De magnifica potestate vocem formavit Trinitas, sed illa Patrem indicabat solum. Vocem illam Petrus verbatim porrò recenset.

Οὑτὸς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς μου ἀγαμητὸς, εἰς ὅν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα. Recitat Apostolus vocem Patris caelestis eo modo, quo describitur apud Matthaeum, nisi quod pro ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα dicit, εἰ ὃν εὐδόκησα, quod ratione sensus idem est, unde Matth. 12. v. 18. eodem modo, quo hoc loco, sententia ista effertur, εἰς ὅν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου.

In repetitione articuli, ὁ υἱὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς est magna emphasis. Hic est ille filius meus ille dilectus, quae ostendit, Christum non esse adoptivum, sed naturalem, proprium, & unigenitum Dei Filium.Ioh. 1. v. 14.cap. 3. v. 16.Rom. 8. v. 32 &c.

Ὁ ἀγαπητὸς, non solùm significat, hunc Filium esse intimè & in summo gradu â DEO Patre dilectum, (quomodo enim non diligeretur â Patre, qui est ab aeterno ex ipsius substantia genitus, ac est substantialis imago Patris?) sed etiam quòd in ipso, per ipsum, & propter ipsum â DEO diligantur, quicunque per fidem in ipsum â Deo Patre in filios adoptantur, ut exponit Apostolus, Eph. 1. v. 6.ἐχαρίτωσεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἠγαπημένῳ, ac Christus Ioh. 17. v. 26. in oratione sua προαγωνίῳ suavismis verbis inquit. Oro Pater, ut dilectio, quâ me diligis, sit etiam in eis vel erga eos. Syrus reddidit, [ברי חביבא] â rad. Syriaca [חבב]in sinu fovit, in delitiis habuit, tenerrimè dilexit, quo respectu Filius dicitur esse in sinu Patris,Ioh. 1, v. 18. ac proinde ὁ ἀγαπητὸς vehementis amoris significationem habet, nec tam dilectum, quàm carum & amabilem significat. Cyprianus Epist. 63. cap. 6. vertit dilectissimum.

Εἰς ὅν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα. Verbum Εὐδοκεῖν non solùm apud LXX. Interpp. sed etiam in Nov. Test. frequentissimè usurpatur pro eo quod est, benevolo & propenso esse erga aliquam rem vel personam affectu, in aliquo oblectari & acquie scere. Theodoretus in Psal. 5. notat. sacras literas bonam DEI voluntatem appellareεὐδοκίανamorem & dilectionem eius erga nos. Cum quo congruit illud Hieronymi in cap. 1. Ephes. quod εὐδοκίαpropriè significet beneplacitum, quia non statim omne quod placuit, etiam beneplacere potest. Complectitur autem haec phrasis totam salutis nostrae οἰκονομίαν, quae in eo consistit, quod cùm propter peccatum omnes homines sint rei irae divinae & aeternae damnationis, nulli ad reconciliationem cum DEO, ad remissionem peccatorum, & vitam aeternam pateat aditus, nisi per hunc Filium, per quem Pater caelestis toti generi humano est placatus & reconciliatus, in quem cùm intuetur, omnem iram & offensionem deponit, in quem omne suum beneplacitum quasi deposuit, ut in eo solo gratiam inveniat, qui reconciliationem cum DEO, peccatorum remissionem & vitam aeternam desiderat. Augustin. lib. 2. de consens. Evang. cap. 14. emphasin sic exprimit, placitum meum in te constitui, per te decrevi implere, quod mihi placet, ut deinceps non dicam, paenitet me fecisse hominem.Iohann. 8. vers. 29.Quae placita sunt ei, facio semper. Gloss. ordin. Per quem beneplacitum meum ostendi, & in eo, quod placet & meum est, inveni. Sed tutissima & optima explicatio colligitur ex parallelis scripturae locis. Esai. 42. vers. 1. ex quo haec verba sunt desumta, habetur verbum רצה quod significat bonam voluntatem erga aliquem habere, gratum & acceptum aliquid habere, in aliquo requiescere. significatur ergo, quòd Patris caelestis εὐδοκία in hoc Filio recumbat, ut extra illum nemo eius εὐδοκίας particeps fieri possit: Luc. 2. v. 14. nato in terris Christo canunt Angeli, ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία quia sc. natus erat is, per quem genus humanum erat Patri caelesti reconciliandum. Luc. 12. vers. 32. vocatur DEI εὐδοκία, quòd velit credentibus in CHRISTUM dare regnum. Ephes. 1. vers. 5.εὐδοκία τοῦ θελήματος τοῦ θεοῦ vocatur, quod praedestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per CHRISTUM. vers. 9. Vocatur DEI ευδοηια, quòd notum fecit mysterium voluntatis suae de salute nostra in Evangelio. Philip. 1. vers. 13. vocatur DEI εὐδοκία, quod operatur in nobis velle & perficere. Quia ergo in CHRISTO est omnis Patris εὐδοκία, ideò omnia illa beneficia per CHRISTUM & propter CHRISTUM nobis obtingunt. Syrus habet verbum [צבא] quod beneplacitum, complacentiam & animi propensionem habuit significat.

## 1:18
Connection. He applies the history of the transfiguration to his purpose, namely, to confirm that he has not delivered human dreams, but divine oracles to those to whom he writes, and he gravely inculcates that he himself, together with two other Co-Apostles, John and James, not only beheld the glory of Christ with his own eyes, but also heard the voice brought from heaven.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ ταύτην τὴν φωνὴν ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν σὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ ἁγίῳ, The pronoun ταύτην and the article τὴν placed before the word φωνὴν have ἔμφασιν ἀναφορικὴν. which the Syrian expressed in this way. [לה להנא קלא] we heard that very voice.

Ἠκούσαμεν. He uses the plural number on account of the other two Co-Apostles who were present at the same time, namely James and John, Matth. 17. vers. 6. just as John also, one of the number of them, speaks in the plural about this vision of glory, 1. Epist. 1. v. 1. That which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, this we announce to you, which passage is parallel to this one of ours.

Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν. Ioh. Huss. in comm. h. l. He does not say uttered, because it did not sound from the mouth of an animal, nor was it formed by natural instruments, but brought from heaven, i. e. coming down or sent down to the earth. σὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες. He testifies that he not only heard the voice brought from heaven and testifying concerning Christ, but also that he was present together with Him on the mount. The voice could have reached those further away, just as that other voice likewise brought from heaven. And I have glorified it and will glorify it again. I will glorifyJohn 12. verse 28. the crowd had heard, but Peter, for the sake of greater confirmation, says that he himself heard that voice present on the mountain.

Ἐν τῷ ὅρει τῷ ἁγίῳ on that holy mountain, he determinately denotes the certain mountain on which the transfiguration took place.

Latin:

Connexio. Historiam transfigurationis applicat ad suum institutum, videlicet ut confirmet, se non humana somnia, sed divina oracula iis, ad quos scribit, tradidisse, ac graviter inculcat, quòd ipse un à cum aliis duobus CoApostolis, Iohanne & Iacobo, non solùm gloriam Christi oculis suis conspexerit, sed etiam vocem caelitus delatam audiverit.

Textus expositio. Καὶ ταύτην τὴν φωνὴν ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν σὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ ἁγίῳ, Pronomen ταύτην & articulus τὴν praemissa voci φωνὴν habent ἔμφασιν ἀναφορικὴν. quam Syrus expressit hoc modo. [לה להנא קלא]illam ipsam vocem audivimus.

Ἠκούσαμεν. Utitur numero multitudinis propter alios duos CoApostolos, qui simul praesentes fuerunt, Iacobum scil. & Iohannem, Matth. 17. vers. 6. quemadmodum etiam Iohannes unus ex illorum numero in plurali de hac visione gloriae loquitur, 1. Epist. 1. v. 1.Quod audivimus, quod vidimus oculis nostris, quod perspeximus hoc annunciamus vobis, qui locus est huic nostro parallelus.

Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν. Ioh. Huss. in comm. h. l. Non dicit prolatam, quia non sonuit ex ore animalis, nec instrumentis naturalibus fuit formata, sed de caelo allatam, i. e. devenientem vel demissam ad terramσὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες. Testatur, se non solùm audivisse vocem caelitus delatam & de Christo testificantem, sed etiam unà cum ipso in monte praesentem fuisse. Potuisset longiùs ad absentes vox pervenire, sicut alteram illam vocem itidem caelo delatam. Et clarificavi & iterum clarificaboIohann. 12. vers. 28. turba audiverat, sed Petrusmaioris confirmationis ergo dicit, se in ipso monte praesentem vocem illam audivisse.

Ἐν τῷ ὅρει τῷ ἁγίῳin monte illo sancto, determinatè certum montem denotat, in quo facta fuit transfiguratio.

## 1:19
Connection. After he had demonstrated the immovable certainty of the doctrine handed down to those to whom he writes, by living voice and by letters, by the αὐτοψία of the majesty of Christ and the αὐτοψία of the voice brought down to Him from heaven: now furthermore he confirms the same by the προφητείᾳ, of the Old Testament, to which that doctrine is in every respect conformable.

Exposition of the text. καὶ ἔχομεν βεβαιότερον τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον is in this place a particle of exaggeration, Furthermore, moreover, also.

ἔχομεν. He speaks in the first person plural, joining himself with the faithful to whom he writes, not so much for the sake of modesty, as for the sake of demonstrating the ὁμονοίας in faith, so that he may show that both his faith and that of those to whom he writes rest upon one and the same immovable foundation.

By λόγον προφητικὸν Erasmus understands the voice of the heavenly Father. But the consequences refute this new exposition, which evidently testify that by this λόγον is understood the word comprised in the writings of the Prophets, because the Apostle asserts that the converted Jews attend to it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, and he adds, that prophecy was not at any time brought by human will, but holy men of GOD spoke being inspired by the Holy Spirit, all of which can be understood only of Prophetic Scripture.

Βεβαιότερον. Since heavenly doctrine, by whomever it may finally be brought forth, is always of the same truth and firmness, nor can it be said that the prophecies of the O. T. are truer and more certain than the voice of the heavenly Father heard in the transfiguration, to which Peter had appealed in the preceding verses, and since the faith of the Apostles in the N. T. is no less than that of the Prophets in the O. T. Eph. 2. v. 20., a not light scruple arises, in what sense the Prophetic word is said to be βεβαιότερος:, but we shall satisfy this doubt later in the questions.

Ὧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες. In the Greek text a certain transposition of words occurs here. For this was the natural series. To which Prophetic word, namely, attending, or while you attend, by reading namely the writings of the Prophets and inquiring from them the truth of the Apostolic doctrine, you do well. A similar transposition of words exists 1. Petr. 3. v. 21. ᾧ καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σώζει βάπτισμα.

The Vulgate rendered the word προσέχειν in this place, to attend. August. in Psalm. 51. Exposit. 2. in Psal. 87. tractat. 23. in Iohann. serm. 74. de diversis cap. 5. serm. 237. de temp. Prosper in lib. Dimid. temp. cap. 12. to intend. It includes in its meaning a diligent and certain attentive study toward some thing and a singular attention of the mind, Matth. 7. vers. 15.cap. 10. v. 17.cap. 16. vers. 6.Luc. 12. v. 1.cap. 17. v. 3. But it signifies not only to apply the mind and attend, but also to obey, to remain, to persist: Therefore the Apostle requires both a sedulous investigation and meditation of the Scriptures Ioh. 5. v. 39. ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφὰς. 1. Tim. 4. v. 13. πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει: and a conformation of life to the norm of the written word, Iohann. 13. v. 17. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them. Iacob. 1. vers. 22.

Be doers of the word and not hearers only, etc. then constant perseverance in doctrine drawn from the Scriptures 2. Timoth. 3. v. 14. Continue in those things which you have learned. Hebr. 3. v. 14. We have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm unto the end. The Syrian, persisting in the metaphor of a lamp, rendered it [חירין אנתון] looking back at you. For those who walk in darkness look back eagerly toward the light that meets them.

Ὡς λύχνῳ φαίνοντι ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ. Λύχνος properly is a lighted lamp, such as is a candle, a torch, a lamp. Matth. 5. vers. 15. Neither do they light λύχνον and put it under a bushel, but upon a candlestick, that it may shine to all who are in the house. Marc 4. vers. 21. Does the (it is inferred) λύχνος, come to be put under a bushel, or under a bed, is it not that it may be put upon a candlestick? Luc. 8. vers. 16. No one, λύχνον when he has lighted a lamp, covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed, but puts it upon a candlestick, that they who enter may see the light. cap. 11. vers. 33. No one, λύχνον when he has lighted a lamp, puts it in a secret place, nor under a bushel, but upon a candlestick, that they who enter in may see the light. All these things show the genuine meaning of τοῦ λύχνου, namely that it is a lighted lamp, and indeed lighted for that purpose, that it may dispel the darkness of the night, and shine to all who are in the house, or the room into which it is brought. Most beautifully, however, do these things agree with Scripture, which, since it draws its origin from GOD, who is αὐτόφως light itself and Φῶς ἀρχέγονον original light, therefore it also is like a clear and bright lamp, providing light to all who are in the house of GOD, which is the Church, 1. Timoth. 3. v. 15.

Ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ. The Vulgate rendered it, in a dark place. Augustine in sermon 74 on diverse subjects, chapter 5, and elsewhere here and there cites in an obscure place. The Syrian rendered it [באתרא עמוטא] in a place of darkness, that is, dark and gloomy. Αὐχμηρὸς properly signifies squalid, because squalor adheres to dark places.

Ἕως ἡ ἡμέρα διαυγάσῃ καὶ φωσφόρος ἀνατείλῃ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν. The Vulgate rendered it, until the day dawns, for which some Latin codices viciously read shines forth. Concerning the first member, some establish the pronoun must be understood ὑμῖν: but it is more correctly said that the sentence is completed in the latter member, namely in the words ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν. But what is understood here by the name of the day and of Phosphorus, we shall see a little later.

Latin:

Connexio. Postquam immotam doctrinae eis, ad quos scribit, vivâ voce & literis traditae certitudinem αὐτοψία maiestatis Christi & αὐτοψία vocis ê caelo ad ipsum delatae demonstraverat: iam porrò eandem confirmat V. T. προφητείᾳ, cui doctrina illa ex asse sit conformis.

Textus expositio. καὶ ἔχομεν βεβαιότερον τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον est hoc loco particula exaggerantis, Praeterea, insuper, etiam.

ἔχομεν. Loquiturin persona prima plurali, seipsum coniungens cum fidelibus ad quos scribit, non tàm modestiae, quàm demonstrandae in fide ὁμονοίας causâ, ut ostendat, & suam & eorum, ad quos scribit, fidem unico eodemque immoto niti fundamento.

Per λόγον προφητικὸν Erasmus intelligit vocem Patris caelestis Sed novam hanc expositionem refellunt consequentia, quae evidenter testantur, per hunc λόγον intelligi verbum in scriptis Prophetarum comprehensum, quia Apostolus asserit, conversos Iudaeos illi attendere velut lucernae lucenti in loco caliginoso, ac subiungit, non esse humanâ voluntate allatam aliquando prophetiam, sed Spiritu sancto inspiratos locutos esse sanctos DEI homines, quae omnia non nisi de Prophetica Scriptura intelligi possunt.

Βεβαιότερον. Cùm doctrina caelestis, â quocunque tandem proferatur, semper sit eiusdem veritatis & firmitatis, nec dici possit, prophetias V. T. veriores & certiores esse voce Patris caelestis in transfiguratione audita, ad quam Petrus in praecedentibus provocaverat, cumque non minor sit fides Apostolorum in N. quàm Prophetarum in V. T. Eph. 2. v. 20. in de non levis oritur scrupulus, quo sensu Propheticus sermo dicatur βεβαιότερος: sed huic dubitationi postea in quaestionibus satisfaciemus.

Ὧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες. In textu Graeco hîc occurrit quaedam verborum traiectio. Naturalis enim series haec erat. Cui scilicet sermoni Prophetico attendentes, sive dum attenditis, legendo scilicet Prophetarum scripta & ex illis veritatem doctrinae Apostolicae inquirendo, benefacitis. Similis verborum traiectio extat 1. Petr. 3. v. 21.ᾧ καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σώζει βάπτισμα.

Verbum προσέχειν Vulg. hoc loco reddidit, attendere. August. in Psalm. 51. Exposit. 2. in Psal. 87. tractat. 23. in Iohann. serm. 74. de diversis cap. 5. serm. 237. de temp. Prosper in lib. Dimid. temp. cap. 12. intendere. includit in sua significatione diligens & attentum quoddam studium in rem aliquam ac singularem animi attentionem, Matth. 7. vers. 15.cap. 10. v. 17.cap. 16. vers. 6.Luc. 12. v. 1.cap. 17. v. 3. Non solùm autem significat, animum adhibere & attendere, sed etiam obtemperare, permanere, persistere: Requirit igitur Apostolus tùm sedulam Scripturarum indagationem & mediationem Ioh. 5. v. 39.ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφὰς.1. Tim. 4. v. 13.πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει: tùm vitae ad normam verbi scripti conformationem, Iohann. 13. v. 17.Haec si sciveritis, beati si feceritis.Iacob. 1. vers. 22.

Estote factores verbi & non auditores tantùm &c. tum constantem in doctrina ex Scripturis hausta perseverantiam 2. Timoth. 3. v. 14.Permane in iis, quae didicisti.Hebr. 3. v. 14.Participes Christi facti sumus, si initium fiduciae usque ad finem firmum retineamus. Syrus in metaphora lucernae persistens reddidit [חירין אנתון]respicientes vos. Qui enim in tenebris ambulant, ad lucem sibi obviam cupidè respiciunt.

Ὡς λύχνῳ φαίνοντι ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ. Λύχνος propriè est lucerna accensa, qualis est candela, fax, lampas. Matth. 5. vers. 15.Non accenduntλύχνον & ponunt eum sub modio, sed super candelabrum, ut luceat omnibus, qui sunt in domo.Marc 4. vers. 21.Nunquid venit (infertur) λύχνος,ut sub modio ponatur, aut sublecto, nonne ut super candelabrum ponatur?Luc. 8. vers. 16.Nemoλύχνονaccendens operit eum vase, aut subtus lectum ponit, sed super candelabrum ponit, ut intrantes videant lumen.cap. 11. vers. 33.Nemoλύχνονaccendens, in abscondito eum ponit, neque sub modio, sed supra candelabrum, ut qui ingrediuntur, lumen videant. Haec omnia genuinam significationem τοῦ λύχνου ostendunt, quòd scilicet sit lucerna accensa, & quidem eo fine accensa, ut noctis tenebras discutiat, & omnibus, qui sunt in domo, vel conclavi, cui infertur, luceat. Pulcherrimè autem haec Scripturae congruunt, quae cum â DEO, qui est αὐτόφωςlux ipsa & Φῶς ἀρχέγονον lux originaria, originem suam trahat, ideò ipsa quoque est instar lucernae clara & lucida, omnibus qui sunt in domo DEI, quae est Ecclesia,1. Timoth. 3. v. 15. lucem praestans.

Ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ. Vulg. reddidit, in loco caliginoso. Augustinus serm. 74. de divers. cap. 5. & alibi passim citat in obscuro loco. Syrus reddidit [באתרא עמוטא]in loco caliginis hoc est caliginoso ac tenebricoso. Αὐχμηρὸς propriè significat squalidum, quia locis tenebricosis squalor adhaeret.

Ἕως ἡ ἡμέρα διαυγάσῃ καὶ φωσφόρος ἀνατείλῃ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν. Vulg. reddidit, donec dies illucescat, pro quo quidam Codd. Latini vitiose legunt elucescat. Circa prius membrum quidam statuunt, subintelligendum pronomenὑμῖν: sed rectiùs dicitur, sententiam compleri in membro posteriore, videlicet in verbis ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν. Quid verò diei ac Phosphori nomine hîc intelligatur, paulò post videbimus.

## 1:19-21 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. In what sense is the Prophetic word said to be firmer than the Apostolic testimony concerning the transfiguration of Christ? Resp. 1. Erasmus, Gagnaeius, and others maintain that the comparative is used in this place for the positive. We can, says Gagnaeius, take 'firmer' not comparatively, but positively, in the way it is often taken both in Greek and in Latin, the Syrian in the same way. [ואית לן דשרירא דנביותא אף מלתא] And we have the word of prophecy as firm (certain, truthful). Luth. Wir haben ein festes Prophetischs Wort. But that the positive is put for the comparative, the comparative for the superlative, and likewise the positive for the superlative can be demonstrated by examples; but that the comparative is put for the positive, of this either no examples or rare ones are given. Act. 7. v. 21. καινότερον is put for καινὸν. 2. Some think the comparative is put for the superlative. We have a firmer word, i. e., a most firm word. Examples of this enallage occur everywhere in the Scriptures of the N. T. Matth. 11. v. 11. ὁ μικρότερος the least in the kingdom of heaven. cap. 22. v. 13. σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον they are the outermost darkness, cap. 23. v. 11. ὁ μείζων ὑμῶν he who is greatest among you. Marc. 4. vers. 21. 32. Mustard is μικρότερον the least among all seeds and becomes μεῖζον the greatest among all. Iohann. 10. v. 29. The Father is μείζων the greatest among all. cap. 13. v. 27. do more quickly, i. e., most quickly. Act. 25. v. 10. κάλλιστος you know very well. 1. Cor. 13. v. 13. μείζων the greatest is charity. cap. 15. vers. 19. ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων, most miserable of all men. Sirach. 1. v. 4. wisdom προτέρα πάντων i. e. πρώτη. 2. But since one must not depart from the letter without an urgent necessity, therefore it is more correctly maintained that the proper meaning of the comparative is to be retained, this hypothesis standing, furthermore

Q. 2. With respect to what is the Prophetic word established as firmer? Resp. 1. Some Greek codices read τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον, instead of τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον so that the sense may be, We have a firmer, viz., vision and voice of the heavenly Father heard in the transfiguration of Christ than the Prophetic words. But the genuine reading has τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον, which produces a clearly contrary sense. 2. Some therefore think regard is had to verse 16. in which mention is made of σεσοφισμένων μύθων, than which the Prophetic word is far more certain and firmer, as being to all Jews and gentiles to be preferred by a very long interval to fables and all human traditions and doctrines. But the comparison of the Prophetic word, that is, the divine word, with Jewish and Ethnic fables, that is, with the doctrine of demons, is exceedingly harsh. 3. Some think that regard is had to the miraculous transfiguration of Christ, and the appearance of Moses and Elijah in it, than both of which the Prophetic word is said to be firmer, since miracles do not provide as solid a foundation of faith as the word of GOD itself, to which could be referred the Apostolic saying Gal. 1. v. 8. Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed, where the Gospel preached by the Apostles is preferred to the preaching of angels, upon which passage Chrysostom comments thus, page 973, Comm. edition: The Apostle prefers the Scriptures to angels, and that very congruously: since angels, however great, are nevertheless servants and ministers. But all the Scriptures came to us not from servants, but from the Lord of all, GOD. Proclus, in his sermon on faith to the Armenians, p. 15, citing this passage of the Apostle, adds, λειτουργεῖν γὰρ Ἄγγελος ἐτάχθη, οὐ δογματίζειν, the angel is placed in the order of ministering, not of prescribing dogmas. But even if in a certain respect the preaching of the Apostles could be preferred to the preaching of angels, nevertheless no reason seems able to be given why, in itself and through itself, the Prophetic word should be preferred to either the voice of the heavenly Father or the miraculous transfiguration of Christ in terms of firmness. And even if we should wish to say that the Prophetic word is therefore called firmer than the miraculous transfiguration of Christ, and the appearance of Moses and Elijah, because miracles do not provide as solid a foundation of faith as the word of God itself: the difficulty is still not removed, because it is manifest from the text that the Prophetic word is said to be firmer not only with respect to the miraculous transfiguration of Christ, but also with respect to the paternal voice brought from heaven in that transfiguration. 4. Akin to this exposition is that which Cornelius à Lapide brings forward in this place, that faith and the light of faith, showing that the oracles of the Prophets are divine and proceeded from GOD, is firmer and more certain than all science, demonstration, and sensitive vision, and any ocular and auricular testimony, and thus the Prophetic word was firmer not only than others, but even to Peter himself than his own vision and hearing. And yet, from that hearing of Peter, its object cannot be excluded, namely the voice of the heavenly Father. Therefore, the difficulty still remains, How can the Prophetic word, by the voice of the heavenly Father heard by Peter, be said to be more firm? Cornelius replies; although the voice of the Father was objectively and in itself most certain and most true, equally with the oracles of the Prophets, nevertheless subjectively, insofar as it was sensibly received and resounded in the ears of Peter, it was not as certain and firm as the visions of the Prophets: for hearing, and every sense, can be deceived, but a Prophetic vision cannot be deceived, because it occurs through a supernatural and divine light. And yet it cannot be denied that, together with the hearing of that voice, a supernatural and divine light of faith shone into the mind of Peter, so that he might believe with a divine, certain, and indubitable faith that this voice was true and proceeded from GOD. 5. Some therefore respond, the words of the Apostle are not to be taken in a distributive sense, as if the Prophetic word is said to be more firm than the voice of the heavenly Father simply; but in a complex sense, so that it is said to have been made more firm and more certain now, the voice of the heavenly Father itself attesting to the sayings of the Prophets, more firm, I say, than itself, but not than the word of the heavenly Father or the Apostles. Oecumenius explains it in almost that way. But by this reasoning it should have been said to Peter: Therefore we now have a more firm Prophetic word. 6. Erasmus, as we have already warned before, brings forth a clearly new exposition. For by the Prophetic word he understands the very voice of the heavenly Father brought from heaven, since the Father himself by that heavenly voice was in a certain way the Prophet and herald of his Son. This Prophetic word, he says, i.e., the voice of the heavenly Father, was more firm than the word of the Prophets, whom they venerated, which sense Erasmus thinks is the genuine one of this passage, and he follows the same in his Paraphrase. But it is manifest from the context that by the Prophetic word is not understood the voice of the heavenly Father, but the word of the Prophets of the O. T. contained in their writings. 7. Lyranus thinks that the Prophetic word of David (Psal. 2. vers. 7. You are my Son, to which the Apostle here appeals) is said to be more firm than the word of the remaining Prophets, because David was an excellent Prophet above the rest. Other Prophets saw the truth revealed to them in imaginary visions, but David through the intellect without such images. And yet Peter here does not speak specifically about the word of one Prophet, namely David, but in general about the whole Prophetic word noted in the writings of the Prophets. 8. Most simply, therefore, it is answered that the Prophetic word, i.e., the Testimony of the Old Testament of the Prophets in their it is said to be more firm as comprised in writings, not indeed by the very voice of the heavenly Father heard in the transfiguration of Christ, but by the Apostolic testimony concerning that voice of the heavenly Father and concerning the transfiguration of Christ; nor is it said to be more true on that account, but only more firm; nor is it said to be more firm in itself and through itself, nor absolutely and simply, but with respect had to those to whom the Apostle writes, concerning which matter it is to be held thus. Something is said to be firm either in itself, because it is immovable and immutable of truth, by this reason every word of GOD is equally firm, whether it be brought forth by the Prophets in the Old or by the Apostles in the New Testament; or in the mind of the man assenting to that truth, or still inquiring about it. In this latter way the Prophetic discourse was more firm than the testimony of the Apostles to those to whom the Apostle writes in this place. For there were among them those converted from Judaism, among whom the writings of the Prophets were in the highest authority, as being confirmed and strengthened by the consensus of so many centuries; but the preaching of the Apostles had not yet reached that sublime pinnacle of authority among them, whence Peter, after he had proved the truth of Christian doctrine by the voice of the Father, brought from heaven in the transfiguration of CHRIST, and heard by himself and his two co-Apostles James and John, not content with this domestic testimony, appeals to the discourse of the Prophets, which he calls more firm, because among those to whom he writes, it was of greater authority and veneration.

He confirms this exposition. 1. The perpetual custom of Christ and the Apostles in the New Testament, by which they confirm their doctrine from the oracles of the Old Testament, as often as they had business with the Jews, as we showed above verse 12.. Chrysostom homily 52 on chapter 26 of Acts. Paul, lest he seem to be the teacher himself, brings forward the Prophets and Moses. And a little before. Since he alone saw, he again confirms his words by the authority of the Prophets. But the authority proving is always greater than the authority to be proved, at least among those for whose sake the proof is instituted. 2. The Bereans are commended by the Holy Spirit for this reason, Acts 17. verse 11. because having heard the preaching of the Apostles, they searched the Scriptures daily (certainly the Prophetic ones) whether these things were so, as they were preached by Paul and Silas. Ἀνακρίνοντες is placed there for συγκρίνοντες, because they compared with the doctrine of Paul the Prophetic Scriptures, so that from that mutual comparison they might gather the consensus. Chrysostom in his commentary on that place. οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἀλλὰ μετ' ἀκριβείας ἀνηρεύνον τὰς γραφάς. Τοῦτο γὰρ ἔστι τὸ ἀνέκρινον βουλόμενοι ἀπ' αὐτῶν πληροφορίαν μᾶλλον περὶ τοῦ πάθους λαβεῖν. They did not search the Scriptures simply, but with diligence: for this is what that means, they judged, for they wished to procure for themselves a full persuasion concerning the passion. Theophylact on this place. Searching, whether they might be found τῶν παλαιῶν Προφητῶν λόγοις συνάδοντα. 3. The pious Ancients confirm the same exposition. Augustine, tractate 35 on John. Because we were not there (on the holy mount), and that voice from heaven (in the transfiguration brought to Christ) we did not hear then, Peter himself says to us. And we have a more certain Prophetic word. For the Lord Jesus Christ, foreseeing that certain impious men would exist, who would slander his miracles by attributing them to magic arts, sent the Prophets ahead beforehand. The same, sermon 27 on the word of the Apostle. Who among us would not wonder that the Prophetic word was called more certain by the Apostle than the voice brought from heaven? He said more certain indeed, not better. For that word from heaven is as true as the Prophetic word; as good, as useful. What then is more certain, except that in which the hearer is more confirmed. Bede in his commentary on this place. If anyone should think that our testimony is to be disbelieved, that we saw the divine glory of our Redeemer in secret, that we heard the voice of the Father made to him, certainly no one will dare to contradict the Prophetic word, no one will dare to doubt concerning this, which all testify to be true, having been inserted into the divine Scriptures long ago. Humbert of Silva Candida, Bishop of Silva Candida, in his book on unleavened bread. The first Master of the Church professes the authority of the O.T. to be firmer than that voice which he heard made over the transfigured Lord. But let us understand him to have said firmer, not indeed simply, but by reason of those who believed only in the Old Testament. Thomas Aquinas, Hugh the Cardinal, Lyra, Dionysius the Carthusian, and certain of the more recent Papists embrace the same exposition. Cajetan in Opuscula, Volume 2, tractate 1, chapter 1, asserts two things: first, that Peter wished to add the Prophetic as divine, as firmer and more certain than his own testimony as human (which, however, is not to be accepted in that sense, as if the testimony of Peter in itself and absolutely were merely human; but that it could be held as such by those to whom he was writing, and therefore to the Prophetic word, as to more firm, namely with respect to the hearers he sent them away. Secondly, that certainty must be had by divine testimony, not human, in judging matters of faith. Confer the same in the commentary on this place. Erasmus in his Annotations on the Recognitions testifies that he would by no means object if the opinion of Augustine concerning this passage were more pleasing to anyone. Salmero on this place: The word of the Prophets is called more firm than the vision of the transfiguration, because the things which the Apostles were then doing or saying among the faithful Jews were not of as great authority as the ancient Scriptures, which had been confirmed and proven, and raised to the highest pinnacle of authority. Barradius, Vol. 1, Concordance of the Gospels, book 1, chapter 17: The Prophetic word is more firm than the Apostolic, not indeed compared with the revelation, but compared with the men who are called to the faith. For they gather that it is the true faith which is confirmed by the most ancient and received testimonies of so many Prophets. Lorinus in his commentary Acts 26, v. 22: Peter calls the Prophetic word more firm than the transfiguration of Christ himself, which he had seen, that is, more apt for convincing the Jews, who receive the Prophets. Similar things occur in Gretser, Vol. 1, Defense of Bellarmine, in the treatise on recognizing Canonical Scripture, chapter 7, p. 1908, and Estius in his commentary on this place of the Apostolic.

Q. 3. Whether λόγου Προφητικοῦ by this name the Apostle understands some certain Prophetic saying of the O.T.? Bede, and from him Lyranus, Gagnaeius, and Cornelius à Lapide determine that Peter by this name looks to the Davidic oracle Ps. 2, v. 7 You are my Son, today I have begotten you. But it is more correctly said that Peter is speaking in general about all the prophecies of Moses and the Prophets, which treat of the person, office, and benefits of the promised Messiah. Salmero on this place: Peter did not produce any single passage, because Scripture testified to it everywhere.

Q. 4. What is understood by the day dawning and the morning star rising? Resp. 1. By the day dawning, most of the Ancients understand the day of the final judgment and the last coming of Christ, which κατ' ἐξοχὴν is called ἡ ἡμέρα, that day, indeed as that which will begin for us, but will not be finished; which will dawn, but will never grow dark; which no night will follow; after which also there will be no other day, but mere eternity. Matt. 7, v. 22 chap. 24, v. 36 chap. 26, v. 29 Luke 21, v. 34 2 Thess. 1, v. 10 2 Tim. 1, v. 18 2 Tim. 4, 18 where it is called ἡμέρα ἐκείνη; 1 Thess. 5, verse 4 Heb. 10, v. 25 where it is simply called ἡ ἡμέρα. Basil on chapter 13 of Isaiah, p. 464: That day is peculiarly called the day on account of the continuous union of his own state and perpetual tranquility. For it will be intercepted by no night, nor will any evening circumscribe it with a fixed limit, because on that day, on which the hidden things of darkness have hitherto lain concealed, they will be brought forth into the open light. According to this hypothesis, what is said here concerning the Prophetic word must also be accepted concerning the Apostolic word, and indeed concerning the whole of Holy Scripture, so that the sense is that the whole time of the present life is a certain obscure night, surrounded by the darkness of errors and ignorance, but that God, out of His immense mercy, has kindled for us the light of Holy Scripture, the guidance and light of which we ought to follow for so long, until the time of the future age succeeds, and that most august day, the beginning of most blessed eternity, in which we shall no longer need the aid of Scripture and the light kindled in it, but shall be advanced to the intuitive and beatific vision of GOD. 1. Cor. 13. v. 12. We see now through a glass in a dark manner, but then face to face. 2. This exposition is served by the fact that the name φωσφόρου is rendered in the Syriac version by [שמשא] which signifies Sun, and which, as Suidas testifies, denotes Sun to the Greeks, for it is its nature φωσφορεῖν to shine and to bring in the day. For Christ, that true Sun of righteousness Mal. 4. v. 2. and bright and morning star Apoc. 22. v. 16. coming in His glory on that last day, will bring the meridian radiance of divine knowledge and the light of day most clearly to the elect: and just as the light of the morning star and the dawn proceeds from the Sun: so the glory of the blessed will proceed from the glory of Christ, and indeed in that last coming of Christ to judgment the blessed will begin to shine in heaven like stars and morning stars. Dan. 12. v. 3. Apoc. 2. v. 28. etc. 3. The pious ancients follow the same exposition: Augustine in Psalm 51: As long as we walk by a lamp, it is necessary that we live with fear; but when our day has come, that is, the manifestation of Christ, then we also shall appear with Him in glory. The same, tract. 35 on John: Because in comparison with that light, to which we are to come, it is still night, even the day in which we are, hear Peter the Apostle etc. We have, he says, a more certain prophetic word, to which you do well to attend as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts. When therefore our Lord Jesus Christ has come, and as the Apostle Paul also says, has illuminated the hidden things of darkness etc. then, such a day being present, lamps will not be necessary. φωσφόρος

The Prophet will not be read by us, the Book of the Apostle will not be opened, the testimony of John will not be sought, we will not even need the Gospel itself.
