Moreover, the comparison is instituted not between the Israelites in the O. T. and the Gentiles in the N. T., but between the Israelites in the O. T. and the Christians in the N. T., since such false teachers existed not only among the Gentiles, but also among the Jews converted to Christ, and thus among both called by the general name of Christians, indeed they arose from them Acts 20. v. 30 whom the Syriac in this place calls [מלפנא דגלא] lying teachers, i.e., architects of lies, from the root [דגל] he lied. Places parallel to this one of ours are Matt. 7. v. 15.chap. 24. vers. 11. & 24.Mark 13. vers. 22.Luke 21. vers. 8.Acts 20. v. 29. & 30.1. Tim. 4. v. 1. & seqq. Tit. 3. vers. 1. & 5. οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. For παρεισάξουσι, which is future, some codices read in the present παρεισάγουσιν. But Many and more approved codices have the future, in which way the Vulgate Interpreter also rendered they will introduce. The Greek παρεισάξουσι properly signifies they will subintroduce, stealthily, secretly and deceitfully introducing, pretending the appearance of piety and the name of the Church, and at the same time it is hinted that they are not going to deny the Christian doctrine entirely, but are going to subintroduce false dogmas alongside it, which is what the preposition of the decomposed verb παρὰ. denotes. Parallel passages are Gal. 2. v. 4. δὶα τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους because of false brothers subintroduced, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον who had subintroduced to spy out our liberty, where they are called παρείσακτοι, as if παρὰ παρατήρησιν εἰσαχθέντες, who insinuate themselves into some assembly without observation, or with no one observing and noticing. The same are called παρεισέρχεσθαι i.e. παρὰ παρατήρησιν εἰσέρχεσθαι etc. which can be beautifully applied to the subintroduction of lost and destructive sects, of which Christ speaks in the parable Matth. 13. v. 25.. While men slept, his enemy came and oversowed tares. Jude in his Epistle, which is of the same argument as this 2nd chapter of the latter Petrine v. 4., speaks thus concerning the same false teachers: παρεισέδυσαν τινες ἄνθρωποι certain men have subintroduced, where παρεισδύναι has the same force, i.e. to creep in secretly and as if doing something else, to enter stealthily, by their own judgment, that is, not by another's legitimate mission. For such ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι for the most part insinuate themselves without a legitimate calling.

Αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. Some think that the word ἀπωλείας was added for the sake of restriction, since αἱρέσεως is a little word ἐκ τῶν μέσων, signifying an opinion which one has chosen for himself, whether true or false. But we will demonstrate below that heresy is always taken in a bad sense; therefore it is more correctly said that the little word ἀπολείας was added not for the sake of restriction, but of description. Moreover, they are called αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, according to a common Hebraism, destructive heresies, lost and authors of perdition. Erasmus rendered it, pernicious sects. Just as men of bloods Psalm. 55. v. 23. are called those who are bloodthirsty and shed human blood: so sects of perdition are called those which are lost and bring about perdition or destruction. Luther verderbliche Secten The Syrian [ארסיס דאבדנא] heresies of perdition.

Καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσοντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι. Vulg. denying the Lord who bought them. But in the Greek there is the participle denying. Some join this participle ἀρνούμενοι with the more remote member, in this way: There will be false teachers among you, and denying the Lord who bought them. But it is more correctly joined with the closer member, they will bring in sects of perdition, denying the Lord who bought them, that is, by that very fact, that they will introduce sects of perdition, they will deny their Lord, by whom they were redeemed, if not in express words, yet in the very act; if not directly, yet through those things which follow from their impious doctrine.

By τὸν ἀγοράσοντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην he understands Christ, who with his blood, as he redeemed the whole human race, so also he redeemed those by whom he is denied. Acts 20. v. 28.1. Cor. 6. v. 20.chap. 7. v. 23. ἠγοράσθη τι τιμῆς you were bought with a dear price.Apoc. 5. v. 9. ἠγοράσας τῷ θεῷ ἡμᾶς τῷ αἵματι σου, for the blood of Christ is that dear price of redemption of which the Apostles speak. Moreover, the impiety of these false teachers is exaggerated by this reasoning, that they do not fear by the introduction of destructive sects to deny him by whom they were bought with a dear price, and there is in this periphrasis of Christ the Redeemer some silent argument. Christ bought them with his precious blood. Therefore they ought not to have denied him by the introduction of destructive sects. A parallel passage is held in the Epist. of Jude v. 4. Certain men have crept in, transferring the grace of our GOD εἰς ἀσέλγειαν (just as also Peter in the following verses says, many will follow their ἀσελγείας ) and the only δεσπότην God and our Lord Jesus Christ ἀρνούμενοι.

Ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν. He had said that those false teachers would bring in αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. he explains that concerning the destruction of those false teachers themselves, nor yet does he exclude the destruction of those who follow those false teachers, as is evident from v. 20. and the following of this chapter, to which pertains the saying of Christ Luke 6. v. 39.When a blind man leads a blind man, both fall into the pit. The Syrian rendered it, bringing upon their souls swift destruction.

By Ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν some think is signified unexpected ruin. For that which is unexpected and unlooked for, that is swift and suddenly it seems to happen, even if it happens after a long time. But the proper meaning of swiftness can also be retained, in the sense that such false teachers are to perish eternally, and indeed sooner than they think, since they promise themselves in their hypocrisy not only a tranquil and long-lived life on this earth, but also eternal happiness. For thus Peter himself explains a little later v. 3.. οἷς τό κρῖμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει. Jude in his Epistle v. 4. expresses that thus. οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τό κρῖμα. Calvinists explain that concerning the absolute decree of reprobation to eternal damnation. But Peter in this place expressly asserts that they bring upon themselves by their own fault destruction that is, they summon it. Either, therefore, this must be accepted concerning the prophecies of the O.T., that the Prophets had already long ago prophesied in their writings that false teachers would disturb the Church and bring destruction upon themselves: or if we wish to adapt this statement of Jude to the decree of reprobation, so that it is a metaphor drawn from those who, for the sake of memory, write down and record in notebooks what they have proposed to do, it must necessarily be added that that reprobation was not made out of a certain absolute hatred, but by a consequent and judicial will, punishing with most just judgment the impiety and obstinacy of the false teachers foreseen from eternity.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Quia sub finem praecedentis capitis mentionem fecerat Apostolus sanctorum DEI hominum h. e. sanctorum V. T. Prophetarum, qui acti & impulsi â Spiritu Sancto divina oracula protulerunt, ac viam salutis hominibus monstrarunt, commodùm addit, unà cum his tempore V. T. exortos fuisse falsos Prophetas.

2. Hac occasione vaticinium profert de falsis doctoribus, etiam N. T. tempore exorituris, quos diligenter cavendos esse innuit, quando eos vocat mendaciorum architectos, qui & se & sequaces suos in exitium perducant.

3. Exhortatus fuerat eos, ad quos scribit, ad constantiam in fide & veritatis caelestis confessione, meritò igitur eos praemonet de cavendis falsis doctoribus, qui â veritate ad errores homines pertrahunt.

4. Commendaverat Apostolus sub finem praecedentis capitis Scripturae Propheticae & Apostolicae suis τεκμηρίοις confirmatae sedulam & attentam lectionem, iam porrò ostendit, quis illius Doctrinae usus sit futurus. Praedicit enim, exorituros falsos Doctores, â quibus ne fideles seducantur, Scripturam sacram tanquam Cynosuram ipsos sequi oportet.

Textus expositio. Ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ Ψευδοπροφήται ἐν τῷ λαῷ. Vocula ηαι respectum habet ad proximè praecedentia. Non solùm veri Prophetae fuerunt â DEO ad populum Israëliticum missi, de quibus hactenus egi, sed etiam ingesserunt se Pseudoprophetae.

Pro ἐν τῷ λαῷ Syrus habet [בעלמא]in mundo. Sed intelligitur determinatè certus populus, videlicet Israëliticus qui in V. T. erat populus Dei, quae expositio colligitur ex addito articulo τῷ λαῷ.

Ἐγένοντο. Non dicit, illos falsos Prophetas â DEO missos fuisse, sed extitisse, nimirum quia ἄκλητοι καὶ αὐτόκλητοι venerunt.

Ὡς καὶ ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι. Vulg. reddidit, Sicut & in vobis erunt Magistri mendaces. Graecum ὡς comparationem notat. Similiter etiam inter vos erunt falsi Doctores, nam ἑν ὑμῖνin vobis est hoc loco idem, quod inter vos, iuxta usitatum Hebraismum, quamvis etiam apud Ciceronem occurrat, amicitiam non nisi in bonis i. e. inter bonos esse posse. Instituitur autem comparatio non inter Israëlitas in V. & gentiles in N. Test. sed inter Israëlitas in V. & Christianos in N. T. siquidem non solùm inter gentiles, sed etiam inter Iudaeos ad Christum conversos, adeoque inter utrosque generali Christianorum nomine appellatos extiterunt, imò ex ipsis exorti sunt tales falsi Doctores Act. 20. v. 30 quos Syrus h. l. vocat [מלפנא דגלא]magistros mendaces h. e. mendaciorum architectos, â rad. [דגל]mentitus fuit. Loca huic nostro parallela sunt Matth. 7. v. 15.cap. 24. vers. 11. & 24.Marc. 13. vers. 22.Luc. 21. vers. 8.Actor. 20. v. 29. & 30.1. Tim. 4. v. 1. & seqq. Tit. 3. vers. 1. & 5.οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. Pro παρεισάξουσι, quod est futurum, quidam Codd. legunt in praesenti παρεισάγουσιν. Sed plures & probatiores Codd. habent futurum, quo modo etiam reddidit Vulg. Interp. introducent. Graecum παρεισάξουσι propriè significat subintroducent, furtim, clam & sub dolè introducent, speciem pietatis & nomen Ecclesiae praetendentes, ac simul innuitur, quòd non sint penitus doctrinam Christianam abnegaturi, sed praeter illam falsa dogmata subintroducturi, id quod notat praepositio verbi decomposit παρὰ. Loca parallela sunt Gal. 2. v. 4.δὶα τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφουςpropter subintroductos falsos fratres,οἵτινες παρεισῆλθονqui subintroierant explorare libertatem nostram, ubi παρείσακτοι dicuntur, quasi παρὰ παρατήρησιν εἰσαχθέντες, qui praeter animadversionem, sive nemine observante ac animadvertente, in caetum aliquem se insinuant. Iidem dicuntur παρεισέρχεσθαι h. e. παρὰ παρατήρησιν εἰσέρχεσθαι &c. id quod pulchrè accommodari potest ad subintroductionem sectarum perditarum & exitialium, de qua Christus in parabola Matth. 13. v. 25. dicit. Cum dormirent homines, venit inimicus & superseminavit Zizania. Iudas in sua Epistola, quae cum hoc 2. cap. posterioris Petrinae est eiusdem argumenti v. 4. de iisdem Pseudo doctoribus sic loquitur. παρεισέδυσαν τινες ἄνθρωποιsubintroierunt quidam homines, ubi παρεισδύναι eandem vim habet, q. d. latenter ac velut aliud agendo irrepere, furtim intrare, proprio sc. arbitrio, non alterius missione legitimâ. Tales enim ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι utplurimùm sine vocatione legitimâ sese insinuant.

Αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. Quidam existimant, vocem ἀπωλείαςrestrictionis causâ esse additam, cumαἱρέσεωςvocula sitἐκ τῶν μέσων,significans opinionem, quam quis sibi delegerit, sive veram, sive falsam. Sed demonstrabimus inferiùs, haeresin semper in malam partem accipi, rectiùs igitur dicitur, voculam ἀπολείας non restrictionis, sed descriptionis causâ esse adiectam. Dicuntur autem αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, iuxta usitatum Hebraismum, haereses exitiales, perditae & perditionis autores. Erasmus reddidit, sectas pernitiosas. Sicut viri sanguinumPsalm. 55. v. 23. dicuntur, qui sunt sanguinarii & sanguinem humanum effundunt: Sic sectae perditionis dicuntur, quae sunt perditae & perditionem sive exitium adducunt. Lutherus verderbliche Secten Syrus [ארסיס דאבדנא]haereses perditionis.

Καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσοντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι. Vulg. negant cum, qui emit eos, Dominum. Sed in Graeco est participium negantes. Quidam participium hoc ἀρνούμενοι coniungunt cum membro remotiore, hoc modo. Erunt in vobis falsi Doctores, & Dominum, qui eos mercatus est, negantes. Sed rectiùs coniungitur cum membro propinquiore, subintroducent sectas perditionis, Dominum qui eos emit, negantes h. e. eo ipso, quòd sectas perditionis introducent, Dominum suum, â quo redemti sunt, negabunt, si non expressis verbis, tamen ipso facto; si non directè, tamen per ea, quae ex impia illorum doctrina consequuntur.

Per τὸν ἀγοράσοντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην intelligit Christum, qui suo sanguine, ut totum genus humanum, ita quoque illos, â quibus negatur, redemit. Actor. 20. v. 28.1. Cor. 6. v. 20.cap. 7. v. 23.ἠγοράσθη τι τιμῆςcaro precio emti estis.Apoc. 5. v. 9.ἠγοράσας τῷ θεῷ ἡμᾶς τῷ αἵματι σου, sanguis enim Christi est carum illud redemtionis precium, de quo Apostoli loquuntur. Exaggeratur autem hac ratione falsorum istorum Doctorum impietas, quòd non vereantur sectarum exitialium introductione negare eum, â quo caro precio sunt redemti, ac inest huic periphrasi Christi Redemtoris tacitum aliquod argumentum. Christus illos precioso suo sanguine mercatus est. Ergo non debebant eum introductione sectarum exitialium negare. Locus parallelus habetur in Epist. Iudae v. 4. Subintroierunt quidam homines, DEI nostri gratiam transferentesεἰς ἀσέλγειαν (perinde ut etiam Petrus v. seqq. dicit, multi sequentur ipsorumἀσελγείας) & solumδεσπότηνDeum ac Dominum nostrum Iesum Christumἀρνούμενοι.

Ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν. Dixerat, illos falsos Doctores subintroducturos αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας. illud de proprio illorum pseudodoctorum exitio exponit, nec tamen excludit exitium illorum, qui Pseudodoctores illos sequuntur, ut constat exv. 20. & seqq. huius capitis, quò pertinet dictum Christi Luc. 6. v. 39.Quando coecus coecum ducit, ambo in foveam cadunt. Syrus reddidit, afferentes super animas suas celerem perditionem.

Per Ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν quidam significari putant inopinatum interitum. Quod enim inopinatum atque inexpectatum est, id celeriter ac subito videtur accidere, etiam si post multum tempus accidat. Sed potest etiam propria significatio celeritatis retineri, sensu eo, quòd eiusmodi falsi Doctores sint in aeternum perituri, & quidem opinione sua citiùs, cùm sibi in sua hypocrisi non tantùm vitam in his terris tranquillam & longaevam, sed etiam aeternam felicitatem polliceantur. Ita namque Petrus ipse paulò pòst v. 3. explicat. οἷς τό κρῖμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει. Iudas in sua Epistola v. 4. illud sic effert. οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τό κρῖμα. Calviniani illud exponunt de absoluto reprobationis ad aeternam damnationem decreto. Sed Petrus h. l. disertè asserit, quòd sibiipsis suapte culpâ perditionem superducant h. e. accersant. Vel igitur de vaticiniis V. T. hoc accipiendum, quòd Prophetae iam olim in scriptis suis vaticinati fuerint, falsos Doctores Ecclesiam turbaturos, ac sibiipsis exitium superducturos: vel si ad reprobationis decretum hoc Iudae effatum accommodare velimus, ut sit metaphora ducta ab iis, qui memoriae causâ in Codicillis describunt & consignant, quae sibi proposuerunt, agere, necessariò addendum, quòd reprobatio illa non sit facta ex absoluto quodam odio, sed voluntate consequente & iudiciariâ, impietatem & pertinaciam falsorum Doctorum ab aeterno praevisam, iustissimo iudicio puniente.

## 2:1-2 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Who were those False Prophets in the O. T. of whom Peter v. 1. speaks. Resp. 1. They were the Priests of Baal, who obtained the greatest authority, especially in the times of Ahab, in the kingdom of Israel. 1. Reg. 18. v. 19.cap. 22. v. 22. 2. Those who in the times of Isaiah, Jeremiah, and other holy men of GOD opposed themselves, defended idolatry, and promised temporal happiness to the Israelite people against the will of GOD, such as were Zedekiah 1. Reg. 22. v. 11. Hananiah Ierem. 28. v. 1. and all those of whom the Prophets complain in general. Esai. 9. v. 15.Ierem. 2. v. 8.cap. 5. v. 31.cap. 6. v. 13. and 14.cap. 14. v. 14.cap. 23. v. 25.Thren 2. v. 14. etc. 3. To the same class belong the sects of the Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes, etc.

Q. 2. Who are those false Teachers, of whose coming Peter prophesies. Resp. 1. Some maintain that Peter is speaking of heretics who had already arisen in the Church in the time of the Apostles, or certainly immediately after the times of the Apostles, and namely of the Gnostics, whose impiety and impurity Epiphanius describes in book 1. against heresies, Tom. 2. heresy 26. for to them it properly applies, what the Apostle says 2. Ep. 2. v. 19. that they promise liberty to others, when they themselves are slaves of corruption.v. 19. 2. But some think, that Simon Magus is understood with his followers, whose carnal and filthy family was disseminated into many heresies. Estius in the Prolegomena of this Epistle.

3. Some understand this of the Nicolaitans, of whom John makes mention in the Apocalypse chap. 2. v. 6. as also Irenaeus book 1. chap. 27. Epiphanius book 1. tom. 2. heresy 25. Eusebius book 3. of Ecclesiastical History chap. 26. For they taught, among other things, that wives ought to be common.

Those who maintain that it is treated here of the Simonians and Nicolaitans, but not of the Gnostics, use this argument, that the heresy of the Gnostics is later than the times of the Apostles. But now Peter speaks of heretics already arisen in his own time in the Church, which they prove by such an argument. Peter and Jude speak of the same heretics, as a mutual comparison shows. But Jude speaks of heretics who had already arisen in his own time in the Church. Certain men, he says, have crept in, turning the grace of God into lasciviousness. Therefore Peter also speaks of such heretics.

4. But indeed because firstly Peter uses words of future time, παρεισάξουσι, ἔσονται ἐξακολουθήσουσι, ἐμπορεύσονται, etc. Secondly, his Epistle is Catholic, written for the use of the whole Church; and as Peter himself testifies 2. Epist. 1. vers. 15. to this end, that even after his death the faithful might have a memorial of the doctrine delivered by him, and might be fortified by the same against false teachers, therefore this Apostolic admonition is to be understood not only of heretics already arisen in the time of the Apostles, but also of all heretics of all times, who are conformed to those ancient ones both by the falsity of their doctrine and by the impiety of their life, for all of them precipitate both themselves and their followers into destruction, therefore they are to be avoided by all with the greatest zeal. Hence Bede in his commentary applies this prophecy of Peter to Arius, Photinus, Manichaeus, Apollinaris, and Pelagius.

5. We say therefore, that not only the Simonians, Nicolaitans, Gnostics, Borborites mentioned from this very chapter, last verse, and other heretics of this bran, who either in the very times of the Apostles, or a little after the times of the Apostles, troubled the Church, and led many into destruction by their false dogmas, are understood, but also that the Apostolic admonition can and ought to be understood of the heretics of the following, nay even of these our most recent times.

Q. 3. What is understood by the way of truth in v. 2. ? Resp. 1. Some understand Christ, who John 14. v. 6. says of himself, I am the way, the truth and the life; for the curses which are cast upon Christian doctrine redound upon Christ himself, the principal author of this doctrine, and thus become blasphemies. 2. But it is simpler, by the phrase ὁδὸς way of truth, to understand in the Hebrew manner heavenly truth, or doctrine divinely revealed, as is evident from other places of Scripture. Acts 9. v. 2. chap. 19. v. 9. & 23. chap. 22. v. 4. chap. 24. v. 14. the Christian religion is called and with προσδιορισμῷ ὁδὸς σωτηρὶας way of salvation, because it leads to eternal life, Acts 16. verse 17. it is also called ὁδός τοῦ Κυρίου. Acts 18. verse 25. ὁδὸς τοῦ θεοῦ chap. of the same v. 26. because it is revealed by GOD and leads us to GOD. In this very chapter 2. of the Epistle of Peter. v. 15. it is called ἡ ὁδός εὐθεῖα straight way, because it leads us to life without error and detours.

Ἐναντιοφανεία. Christ in this place is said to have bought those who bring upon themselves swift destruction. But Christ John 10. v. 15. says that he gives his life for his sheep. chap. 17. v. 19. that he sanctifies himself for those whom the Father has given to him. The elect Rev. 5. v. 9. celebrate as a peculiar benefit that he redeemed them to GOD in his blood. Resp. 1. One cannot always proceed from an affirmative to an exclusive. Christ died for his sheep, but not for his sheep alone. 2. That indefinite proposition, that Christ died for his sheep, Scripture elsewhere explains by a universal, that he died for all men, that he gave himself ἀντίλυτρον for all, 1. Tim. 2. v. 6. 3. The merit of Christ is considered either with respect to acquisition alone, or with respect to acquisition and application together. In the former respect Christ is said to have died for all, but in the latter for those who through faith become partakers of that merit.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Peter predicts, that false teachers will come, who will bring in sects of perdition. Paul Acts 20. v. 29. in the same way. After my departure grievous wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock. v. 30. From among yourselves men will arise speaking perverse things. Therefore, one must not simply believe teachers in the Church, but only so far as their dogmas are conformable to the Prophetic and Apostolic writings. For the privilege of infallibility does not belong to them equally as to the Prophets and Apostles, therefore one must judge of their doctrine from the word of GOD.

Bellarmino objects in book 2 on Councils, chapter 6, last section: Peter describes heretics under the name of false Prophets, who, resisting the doctrine which is preserved by the Bishops presiding in the Church by ordinary succession, do not fear to introduce sects, so that they may lead away disciples after them and make a name for themselves on earth. I respond: the hypothesis is false, that the assistance of the Holy Spirit and the truth of doctrine are simply tied to the personal and local succession of Bishops. For Bellarmino himself admits in book 4 on the Church, chapter 8, section: Add lastly, etc., all the Patriarchal Churches, the Antiochene, the Hierosolymitan, the Alexandrian, and the Constantinopolitan, have had manifest heretics for long periods of time. He indeed excepts the Roman See, but Ecclesiastical History testifies that Zepherinus the Montanist, Liberius the Arian, and Honorius the Monothelite presided even over that one. Therefore, the local and personal succession of Bishops is not the norm of true doctrine in the Church, because Paul says that wolves would succeed them, but the Prophetic and Apostolic Scripture, to which Peter had also referred those to whom he writes in the preceding verses. Whoever departs from this rule introduces a destructive sect.

2. Salmero in his commentary on this place rightly weighs the emphasis of προσδιορισμού, added in the Apostolic text, ἐγένοντο ἐν ἡμίν. I ponder, he says, that word 'among you' that is among you or from you, because Paul spoke thus Acts 20, verse 30 From among yourselves men will arise speaking perverse things. In the same way Lorinus in his commentary on this place: Among you and from you they will arise, as Paul predicted Acts 20, v. 30 and John 1, Epistle 2, v. 2. With these sayings, cited by Salmero and Lorinus, must be joined the parallel passages Matthew 13, v. 25 While men were sleeping, the enemy of the householder came and oversowed Tares in the midst of the wheat. 1 Cor. 11, v. 19 It is necessary that there be heresies among you. But all these things must be opposed to the Papists, who always repeat that our assembly cannot be the true Church, since in it some seducers are from time to time stirring up trouble. And yet Satan scatters his Tares especially in the field of the Lord, in the midst of the good wheat, not in wild, rocky, or thorny places. Therefore, those very Tares of Satan testify that the good field itself and the good seed of Christ are present here.

3. Peter says that in the N.T. false teachers will come, just as in the O.T. there were False Prophets. Therefore, the danger to the Church of the N.T. is equally imminent from them as it is imminent to the Church of the O.T. from these. Therefore, it is false what Bellarmine writes in the said place, §. finally, etc. It is not permitted to transfer everything that is said in the Scriptures against the Prophets and Priests of the O. T. to the Priests of the N. T., especially those gathered in a Council. For the Church has more certain and greater promises of GOD than the Synagogue. Matt. 16. upon this rock I will build my Church 1. Tim. 3. the pillar and ground of the truth Luke 22. I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

4. Peter says that those false teachers, bringing upon themselves swift destruction, deny him who bought them. Therefore Christ died on the altar of the cross for all, and thus even for those who perish in their errors and sins, and satisfied for their sins.

They object. 1. Polanus, Tossanus, Piscator, and other Calvinists, that this is said not κατ' ἀλήθειαν, but κατὰ δόξαν, partly because they persuade themselves that they are in the number of those redeemed by Christ and boast that they are Christians: partly because others judge out of charity that they are truly faithful and therefore redeemed by Christ. I respond: this exposition is heretical. For 1. Peter does not say, denying him, by whom either they themselves or others think they are bought, but he says absolutely and simply, denying him who bought them. 2. In this very chapter vers. 18. & 20. Peter asserts that some of those who perish had previously ὄντως truly escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ. Therefore they truly believed in CHRIST, and consequently Christ ὄντως also satisfied for their sins. For he for whom Christ did not satisfy cannot find the remission of his sins through faith. 3. If those things which are simply asserted in the Scriptures κατὰ δόκησιν are permitted to be interpreted, CHRIST will be man only κατὰ δόκησιν, will have suffered and died κατὰ δόκησιν, and thus all articles of faith will be able to be called into doubt.

2. The same Polanus and others object, that this is to be understood regarding the magnitude or sufficiency of the price, but not regarding the efficacy, which they prove with this argument. Upon whom the wrath of GOD remains, they are not redeemed by Christ. The wrath of GOD remains upon the reprobate John 3. v. 36. Therefore the reprobate are not redeemed by Christ. I respond 1. If they were to accept that distinction between the sufficiency of the price and the efficacy in the sense in which it is used by the Scholastics, namely, that Christ, as far as it depends on him, gave a most sufficient price of redemption for all, but that not all become participants of that benefit, the fault and cause of that matter resides in the reprobate themselves, because, to wit, they do not apply to themselves the benefits of Christ offered in the Gospel, then we would by no means reject the distinction brought forward. 2. But they explain that distinction in an erroneous sense, such that the value of expiating the sins of all men would not indeed have been lacking to the death of Christ, if it had been destined for this by God, but this counsel and this will never existed for God and Christ. Bucan. in loc. pag. 396. If you consider the power of the blood of Christ, it suffices for the redemption of all; but if you look at the eternal purpose and counsel of GOD, and the will of the Mediator, He died for the elect alone. Robertus Bishop of Salisbury in Exercit. pag. 31. He asserts that Christ willed to satisfy for all by the dignity of the price, but by the will of the purpose only for the elect pag. 36. By human affection alone Christ died for all men. 3. Thence Beza in Thes. Theol. de Praedest. th. 13. & part. 2. Resp. ad Colloq. Mompelg. pag. 217. Piscator Disp. de praedest. th. 109. in Apol. Disp. de causa meritoria Iustificat pag. 107. 108. part. 3. Resp. ad amicam Collation. Vorstii pag. 11. in annot. 1. Tim. 2. pag. 26. reject that distinction, and simply deny that Christ died for all. 4. So that the whole matter may be clearer, we proceed thus. Sufficiency is twofold. First, potential or possible, by which Christ is said to have been able indeed to satisfy for the sins of all men, but by a certain absolute good pleasure of GOD to have willed not to. Secondly, actual, by which we say that Christ, according to the counsel of GOD the Father, actually redeemed all men universally, and restored life and salvation to them. The Calvinists posit the former sufficiency, we the latter. By efficiency here is understood the application of the merit of Christ and the bestowal of acquired salvation, which we easily concede to be particular. For Paraeus burdens us with calumny in Iren. p. 245, writing that we teach that Christ, as much regarding efficacy as regarding sufficiency λύτρου died not only for the elect, the faithful, and those to be saved, but also for the reprobate, the unfaithful, the damned, and those to be damned. But this is in question, from what it comes to pass that the efficacy or application of the merit of Christ is particular? The Calvinists establish that the cause is to be sought in the absolute decree of reprobation, but we in the fault and incredulity of men. 5. From these it can easily be judged what is to be established concerning the dissertation of Chamier, Tom. 3. Panstrat. lib. 9. cap. 9. §. 21. In this, he says, controversy, sufficiency is a certain power: but efficacy is the act of that power. Whence who does not see it is prompt, that those who are actually redeemed, they are also effectively that they have been redeemed, and therefore not only sufficiently? so that one may rightly wonder in what sense Windekius said that the reprobate are understood to be actually bought by Christ, in that he laid out a price for them, whether it be applied or not. For how can he be actually, if there is no application? unless perhaps he says this, that the reprobate were not actually redeemed, but that Christ did that from which the reprobate could have been bought, which even if ἄκυρον it is, yet if it pleases the Sophists, let it be so, for it does not please me λογομαχεῖν: yet it will be true, if they could have been redeemed, that they were not redeemed. Resp. It is false that the reprobate cannot be said to be actually redeemed because the benefit of redemption is not applied to them. A Christian ruler can pay the price of redemption to the Turkish Emperor for captives, who nevertheless may not wish to leave captivity. Those captives are actually redeemed, and yet the benefit of redemption is not applied to them. Leo, Epistle 83. The shedding of the just blood for the unjust was so powerful in privilege, so rich in price, that if the whole body of captives believed in their Redeemer, no tyrannical chains would hold them. 6. The argument of Polanus concludes nothing, because the major premise is false. Upon whom the wrath of GOD remains, to them indeed as such the benefit of redemption is not applied: meanwhile, however, the acquisition of this benefit pertains to them, of which thing an evident proof is that the benefits, brought forth by the passion and death of Christ, are offered to all men, and therefore even to the reprobate in the word of the Gospel.

3. Others among the Calvinists object, that the Apostle does not say that the Lord Jesus bought those false prophets, but simply asserts that the Lord δεσπότης bought them, which word in the N. T. is for the most part attributed to GOD the Father, or generally to GOD. Epist. Iud. v. 4. Resp. 1. Even if the word δεσπότηου here designated God the Father, the Son nevertheless ought not at all to be excluded from this redemption, nor could he be, on account of the ταυτότητα. essence. 2. Not only the Father or God in general, but also Christ specifically is called δεσπότης in the N. T. Act. 2. v. 24. Apoc. 6. v. 10. 3. It does not follow, in the Epistle of Jude v. 4, God is called δεσπότης and Christ κύριος. Therefore only God the Father, or God in general is called δεσπότης, and not Christ: otherwise from 1. Cor. 8. vers. 6. it could be gathered that the Father is God, and not Lord; that Christ is Lord, and not God.

4. Molinaeus in the Anatomy of Arminianism, chap. 29, p. 422, objects, that it is not a question here of redemption from eternal death, but of liberation from ignorance and error, and from the darkness of the age through the light of the Gospel. Resp. 1. Peter 1. Ep.

1. vers. 18. & 19. he explains himself clearly enough, that he understands the redemption made through the blood of Christ. 2. The parallel passage proves the same Apoc. 5. v. 9. 3. If they have been freed from the darkness of the age through the light of the Gospel. Therefore also from death, as is gathered from this very chapter v. 20. 4 For those who are freed from the error and darkness of the age through the light of the Gospel, to them are offered in the word of the Gospel the benefits prepared by the passion and death of Christ. To those to whom the benefits acquired by the passion and death of Christ are offered, for them also Christ has suffered and died. 5. Estius the Papist in his commentary on this place objects thus, it is indeed well gathered from these words that Christ redeemed certain reprobates, namely those who were made participants of his redemption according to some effects, of which kind were those of whom Peter speaks, as being regenerated through faith in Baptism and having obtained the forgiveness of sins, although they afterwards relapsed into the old servitude of sin: yet it is not to be gathered from this that the effect of redemption extends to all men entirely. Resp. 1. Scripture does not assert that only certain reprobates were redeemed by Christ, but uses universal terms, teaching that Christ tasted death for all,Rom. 5. v. 8.2. Cor. 5. v. 14.1. Tim. 2. v. 6.Hebr. 2. v. 9. it also uses the collective term world, teaching that Christ satisfied for the sins of the whole world,Iohann. 1. v. 29.cap. 4. vers. 42. it adds moreover μερισμὸν, teaching that Christ is the propitiation not only for ours, but also for the sins of the whole world,1. Iohann. 2. v. 2. Rightly therefore Cornelius à Lapide in his commentary on 2. Petr. 3. v. 9. writes thus. They err who think that Christ did not suffer for all, but only for the predestined. Thus thought the Predestinarians of old, Arnobius on Psalm 146, Faustus book 2 de lib. arb. chapters 14 and 16, Remigius of Lyons in his book against the three Epistles of the three Bishops, and some moderns. But Holy Scripture and all the Fathers everywhere teach the contrary. &c. 2. When Scripture makes mention of reprobates specifically and asserts that Christ died for them, it nowhere adds a restriction that he died for only some reprobates, but not for all. Rom. 14. v. 15.1. Cor. 8. v. 11. and in this place. 3. That those reprobates who were regenerated through Baptism, but afterwards relapsed into the former servitude of sin and were involved in eternal destruction, were redeemed through Christ, is proven effectively from the received benefit of regeneration: but from this it cannot be inferred by a contrary sense that those who were not regenerated through Baptism were also not redeemed through Christ.

For it can be proven from other principles that even those were redeemed by Christ. 4. It is said ambiguously that the effect of redemption extends to all men whatsoever. For it is a question either of the acquisition or of the application of this benefit. If in the former sense, the assertion is true; but if in the latter, it is false.

5. Peter uses the word ἀγοράζειν. concerning the work of redemption performed by Christ. Therefore, in it, satisfaction for our sins intervened, namely, that which was made by Christ. For where λύτπον or a price is paid, satisfaction is performed. This must be opposed to the Photinians, who deny the satisfaction of Christ.

They object. 1. That the word redemption is metaphorical, and signifies nothing other than a simple liberation, which was made without an intervening true price of satisfaction. Socin. against Covetus page 75. Catech. Racov. chapter 8. page 270. Resp. 1. Peter not only uses the word ἀγοράζειν, but also expresses the price of redemption, namely, that it is the blood of Christ, of that lamb immaculate, 1. Epist. 1. v. 18. & 19. The same price is expressed Apoc. 5. v. 9. You have redeemed us with your blood. 2. We therefore urge the confession of Socinus in Synopsis on Justification page 7. The word to redeem signifies to liberate by a given price, indeed if you look at the force of the word itself, it declares a purchase entirely, which cannot be done without a price: as also that of Smaltzius in Exam. 156. of errors, error 51. page 16. We confess that the blood of Christ is the true price of our redemption and had the force of a price in redeeming us, because the blood of Christ truly performed for us that which a price performs in redeeming some captive. Therefore, one must not depart from this propriety of the word without an urgent cause. 3. We conclude, however, in this way. Wherever the requirements of a properly so-called redemption are given, there also a properly so-called redemption is given. In the liberation of the human race from the power of Satan, all the requirements of a properly so-called Redemption are given. First, the object of redemption is given, that is, the captives, who are all men Zach. 9. v. 11. Gal. 3. verse 10. Second, the person, who redeems the captive, the principal cause, who is Christ our Redeemer, our propitiatory, Rom. 3. v. 24. Third, the instrumental cause, namely λύτρον or the redemptive price, which is the precious blood of Christ Zach. 9. v. 11. Eph. 1. v. 7. Coll. 1. v. 14. Fourth, the captivity, which is the term from which of our redemption, under which is understood both the judge or Lord of the prison, and the keeper of the prison, and the prison itself, and its adjuncts. The judge is GOD himself, angry, or the wrath & judgment of God Rom. 5. v. 9.Gal. 3. v. 13. The keeper of the prison is the Devil, from whose power Christ has redeemed us, Os. 13. v. 14. The prison is hell Zach. 9. v. 11. Os. 13. v. 14. &c. The adjuncts of the prison are the snares of our sins Luc. 1. v. 74.Heb. 2. v. 14. &c. Fifthly, the liberty into which we are asserted, which is the term to which of our liberation Luc. 1. v. 14. 4. Therefore, one must distinguish between bodily redemption, which can be done in any way even without the intervention of a price, and spiritual, which cannot be done except by the shedding of blood. Hebr. 9. v. 22. Likewise between judicial redemption and extrajudicial; the latter can be accomplished without λύτρῳ, but the former truly never.

2. Schmalzius in Exam. 157. errorum c. 51. p. 16. objects, that not all the requirements of a properly called redemption are present, since there is no one to whom the blood of Christ was given for us Error. 53. p. 17. No price was given to God for us, since God himself expended Christ for our sake. Now if he wished him to be given to himself as a price, could he not have retained him and not given him? unless we wish to say that God plays in his divine actions.

Resp. 1. The words of the Apostle are clear. Eph. 5. vers. 2. Christ delivered himself up for us as a victim and an offering to GOD.Hebr. 9. v. 14.Christ offered himself through the eternal Spirit blameless to GOD, from which we conclude thus. To whom the propitiatory sacrifice was offered for the sins of the whole world, to him also the price of our redemption was offered. But the propitiatory sacrifice was offered to GOD for the sins of the whole world. Therefore. 2. One must consider in this place the wonderful tempering of justice and mercy in God. That he gave his only-begotten Son to us, who would pay λύτρον for us, and that he accepted this λύτρου exhibition, as if we ourselves had performed it, is of mercy; that he did not remit the debts of sins except with the intervention of a full and perfect satisfaction, is of justice. 3. Although God the Father himself procured our redemption, yet because he procured it through the Son, he could altogether receive the price. Compare Nazianzen orat. 42. in Sanctum Pascha, p. 691.

6. Against the absolute decree of reprobation, defended by the Calvinists, we weave such an argument from these words of the Apostle. Those who bring destruction upon themselves, when they have been bought with a dear price for salvation and life, they are not rejected by an absolute decree of reprobation. But false teachers bring destruction upon themselves, when they are bought at a dear price for salvation and life, as Peter asserts in this place and parallel passages confirm. Hos. 13. v. 9.Luke 7. v. 30.Acts 13. v. 46. Therefore they are not rejected by an absolute decree of reprobation. But the same judgment applies to the rest of the damned.

7. The Apostolic admonition pertains not only to the ancient heretics, who troubled the Church in the times of the Apostles or a little after the time of the Apostles, and led many into destruction with their false dogmas, but also to the seducers of our time. Thus

First, the Papists have brought in sects of perdition, because not content with the Apostolic doctrine contained in the sacred writings, they have brought in many false dogmas besides, such as the merits of works, the sacrifice of the Mass, purgatory, the religious invocation of saints, etc. The word παρειάξουσι hints that false teachers are to introduce new errors secretly and dissemblingly under the name of Christ and Catholic doctrine; that has indeed been abundantly fulfilled in the Papal kingdom, because the Pope does everything under the name of Christ and the Holy Spirit. The Papist teachers also introduced the sects of the Thomists, Scotists, Occamists, etc., opposing one another with mutual contentions; they introduced multiple Monastic orders, by which they have rent the unity of the Church. The same have denied the Lord who bought them. For although they do not seem in open words to deny the person, or office, or benefits of Christ, yet because they deny the real communication of divine idioms, which is the immediate consequence of the personal union, they indirectly deny the personal union. Because they defend the sacrifice of the Mass, they indirectly and consequently deny the perfection and sufficiency of the Sacrifice offered on the altar of the cross. They twist the Protoevangelium Gen. 3. v. 15. concerning the seed of the woman who would crush the head of the Serpent to Mary, whom they join to Christ as a partner in the work of redemption. Dietenberg. in v. Bibl. Dieselbe wird dir den Kopff zertreten. Moreover, because they teach that men obtain eternal life by the merits of their own works, and satisfy for the punishments of their sins, and furthermore can perform works of supererogation, and can communicate the same to others, by that very fact they indirectly and consequently deny the Mediatorial office of Christ. In the Little Flowers of St. Francis, as reported by Vagerius in the annotations to the Index of books

prohibited in the year 1559, fol. 9, it is read, that Mary by the merit of her virginity saved all women until the times of a certain Clare, a contemporary of St. Francis, just as Christ himself by the merit of his passion saved all men until the times of the same Francis. Thence Luther in his book against the falsely named Spiritual Estate, Vol. 2, Jena, German, fol. 211, writes thus concerning this Apostolic passage: These words cannot be understood otherwise than of Bishops and Ecclesiastical Leaders among the people. We see that besides the doctrine of Christ, they have erected and introduced into the world doctrines of men, sects, orders, and various Estates, which outside the common way of the Christian faith hand down peculiar works and modes of living, through which Christ, who bought us, is denied. In his commentary on this place, same Vol., fol. 402: It is the proper work of Christ to take away sins; this they attribute to their own works. They are those of whom Christ says: Many will come in my name, saying, I am Christ. They do not say, I am called Christ, but I am Christ, because they seize for themselves that office which belongs solely to Christ, they cast him down from the throne of the Mediator and place themselves in it.

Secondly, the Calvinists likewise deny the real communication of idioms and introduce a Nestorian tearing apart of the person; they deny that Christ according to his human Nature, exalted to the right hand of GOD, governs all things in heaven and on earth presently and powerfully; they deny that Christ made satisfaction for all the sins of the whole world.

Thirdly, the Photinians deny that Christ is true God by Nature: they deny ἀποτόμως the satisfaction of Christ; they deny that the righteousness of Christ is imputed to us by faith. Therefore, this thunderbolt of Apostolic admonition strikes them all.

8. Many are said by the Apostle to be about to follow the destructive dogmas and the impurity of life of false teachers, v. 2, with which prediction the parallel prophecies of Christ and the Apostles in the New Testament agree. Matthew 24, verse 11. Many false prophets will arise and will seduce many. 2 Thessalonians 2, verse 11. GOD will send them the efficacy of error or effective errors. 1 Timothy 4, verse 1. In the last times some will depart from the faith, which the circumstances of the text show will be ἀποστασίαν almost Universal. Apocalypse 13, verse 8. All who inhabit the earth, whose names are not written in the book of life, adored the beast. chapter 17, verse 2. With that great harlot the Kings of the earth have committed fornication, and those who inhabit the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her prostitution.chap. 19. verse 2.The great whore has corrupted the earth with her prostitution. Therefore, amplitude is not a proper and genuine mark of the Church. This must be opposed to Bellarmine, who in book 4 of On the Church, chapter 7, § 1, counts amplitude and the multitude of adherents among the marks of the Church: as also Jakob Reihing, while still a Papist, who in Walls of Babylon, foundation 11, p. 298, argues thus. Those Doctors are to be heard, whose hearers are much more numerous. The multitude of the faithful shows us better Doctors. In this part, the Papists conform themselves to the Arians, who boasted of the multitude of their followers, whence the Emperor Constantius the Arian objected to Liberius the orthodox Bishop. What part of the world are you? in Theodoret, book 2 of Ecclesiastical History, chapter 16, and to the Eutychians, of whom the same Theodoret writes in the Opuscula published under the name of Athanasius, that μόνω πλήθει τοῦ λόγου τὴν ἰσχύν ἀπονέμουσι they claimed the force of reason for the multitude alone, to whom he himself replies, the strength of truth is always immense, κἀν παρ' ὀλίγοις εὑρίσκηται, however much it may be found among the few.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Estius, on verse 1, warns that false Doctors are not called by the Apostle False-prophets, by which name he had called the false teachers of the Old Testament, but false Masters, the reason for which variation he assigns as this, that the time of the Old Testament was properly PropheticLuke 16. verse 16.The Law and the Prophets were until John, since in the Old Testament mysteries were predicted, which is the work of Prophets so called in the strict sense; but in the New Testament the predicted things are explained, which is the work of Masters. In almost the same way Lorinus on this passage, who after he had said, ψευδοδισκάλους that they are the same whom the Apostle had previously called False-prophets, since it was the duty of Prophets to teach, afterwards adds. Peter seems to designate those whom the Hebrews called Prophets as Masters in the voice of the Church alone, although there were not lacking to the Church its own Prophets, and in those first beginnings of it, it is recorded that there were Prophets and Doctors at Antioch,Acts 13. verse 1.

But 1. this observation does not sufficiently agree with the usage of Holy Scripture, since CHRIST also in the New Testament calls them false Doctors Ψευδοπροφήτας Matthew 7. verse 15.chap. 24. verse 11. & 24.Mark 13. verse 22. which nomenclature they also imitate Luke Act, 13. v. 6. & John 1. Epist. 4 v. 1.Apoc. 16. v. 13.chap. 19. v. 20.chap. 20. v. 10. 2. namely, because προφητεύειν in the phrase of Scripture not only signifies to predict future things, but also to expound Prophetic Scripture, as Estius acknowledges in the commentary on the preceding chapter, v. 20, which signification he proves from Rom. 12. v. 6.1. Cor. 13. v. 2. & 8.chap. 14. v. 6.1. Thess. 5. v. 20.Apoc. 11. vers. 6. 3. Estius indeed objects, that this is the general acceptance of prophecy; but that prophecy taken in the strict sense is the prediction of future things. But these are two distinct significations of one word, both of which properly belong to it, if we look to the use of Scripture, and not to the Etymology of the word. 4. Luther in the commentary on this place, Tom. 2. Ien. Germ. fol. 401, brings forward another observation, which is deservedly opposed to Estius. It was done by the singular counsel of GOD, that in Papal Academies there were Doctors called, who were to be set over Ecclesiastical offices, so that it could be understood that they are here censured by the Apostle under the name of false doctors, whence he does not call them false Prophets, & false Apostles, but false doctors.

2. Lorinus on the same verse comments thus. I have warned in the comm.Acts 24. vers. 14.that from Ecclesiastical use heresy sounds badly, although sometimes among our writers it has a good use. Estius in the same way. Although heresy by the use of the whole Church is now long since taken in a bad sense, yet among profane authors, and even in sacred Scripture, the word is neutral, signifying an opinion which one has chosen for himself, whether true or false. Hemmingius on this place. Although heresy is a neutral word, as that which is taken now in a good, now in a bad sense: yet more often by the use of Scripture, because it denotes dissension, it is taken in a bad sense.

Resp. 1. In the Biblical phrase the word heresy is always taken in a bad sense. Acts 5. v. 17.chap. 15. v. 5.1. Cor. 11. v. 19.Gal. 5. v. 20. 2. Some passages are indeed brought forward to the contrary, in which it seems to be taken in a good sense, but to them one can easily answer from the circumstances of the text. Acts 24. v. 5. Tertullus, the Orator of the Jews, says of Paul. We have found this man a pestilent author τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως where by the heresy of the Nazarenes is understood the religion of the Christians. And yet Tertullus & the Jews held that for a most pestilent heresy. Acts 24. vers. 14. Paul says to the Governor. I confess to you, that according to this way, which they call αἵρεσιν, I serve the God of my fathers. But Paul does not call the Christian religion a heresy simply and in his own sense, but in the sense of others, for he expressly adds, ἥν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν. Act. 26. v. 5. κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος. But Pharisaism was in truth a pernicious heresy, yet he calls it the most exquisite heresy, because by their hypocrisy they strove to procure for their sect a singular reputation for holiness, when the Sadducees were Epicureans, and the Essenes were removed from common conversation. Actor. 28. vers. 22. περὶ μὲν γὰρ αἱρέσεως ταύτης &c. But those Jews held the Christian religion to be a damnable sect, whence they add, We hear that this sect is spoken against everywhere. 3. In the version of the LXX Interpreters, the word heresy is taken for a very bad purpose Gen. 49. v. 6. Although indeed in Levit. 22. vers. 18. & 21. it is taken for the spontaneous affection of an offering, and in 1. Maccab. 8. vers. 30. for a spontaneous and free change, nevertheless it cannot be proven from that, that when taken for doctrine it is used in a good sense. 4. Let it be certain, therefore, that the name of heresy when taken for doctrine is always taken in a bad sense, namely for a depraved and false opinion, which someone chooses for himself by his own wit and private judgment, and embraces it against the truth revealed in Scripture. In the same way it is also taken in the writings of the ancients, and thus in ecclesiastical phraseology. Tertullian, book on prescription against heresies, chapter 6: Heresies are so called from the Greek word for the interpretation of choice, which one uses either to institute or to receive them. Therefore he also said that the heretic is condemned by himself, because he chose for himself that in which he is condemned: but it is not permitted for us to introduce anything from our own judgment, nor to choose what someone has introduced from his own judgment. We have the Apostles of the Lord as authors, who did not themselves choose anything of their own judgment to introduce, but faithfully assigned to the nations the discipline received from Christ. From the same book, chapter 37: Whence are heretics strangers and enemies to the Apostles, if not from the diversity of doctrine, which each one of his own judgment either brought forth or received against the Apostles? Jerome on chapter 5 of Galatians: Heresy is called in Greek from choice, because, to wit, each one chooses for himself that discipline which he thinks is better. Whoever, therefore, understands Scripture otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit demands, by whom it was written, although he may not have departed from the Church, yet he can be called a heretic. Leo the First, Epistle 10 to Flavian: Who not to the Prophetic voices, not to the Apostolic letters, not to the Evangelical authorities, but they return to themselves, they incur the foolishness of heresy, and therefore they exist as Masters of error, because they were not disciples of truth. Bede in comm. h. l. Which Sect is called heresy in Latin, in Greek, when someone with foolish obstinacy never ceases to follow the error which he once began, which who does not know to be the property of heretics?

3. Lorinus on v. 2. annotates thus. Luther, an apostate of a religious Order, taught what he was doing, that intercourse is just as necessary as eating, drinking, sleeping: and that it is more than a commandment for all, from which no one can be exempted. Increase and multiply: and that if a wife is unwilling, another maidservant should even be called in. Resp. these ἐγκλήμασι have been satisfied at length in the place concerning marriage and in the Catholic Confession. Luther does not deny that the gift of virginity is given to some by God, but he denies that it is placed in the judgment of any man. Nor does he speak of promiscuous intercourse with a maidservant, but of the legitimate separation of a refractory wife.

4. Cornelius à Lapide on the same verse comments thus. Thomas More, to someone objecting that very many were betaking themselves to Luther's sect, and therefore it seemed true, wittily replied. There is no more miracle in men running to Luther than in rocks falling downward from a height. For most run and rush to gluttony, Venus, and the liberty of the flesh which Luther permits, nay, teaches.

Resp. 1. Luther neither taught nor permits these vices of the flesh, but detested them. 2. He truly taught the mortification and crucifixion of the flesh with its concupiscences, which he requires from all who are truly pious. 3. As many as receive the Evangelical doctrine preached by Luther expose themselves to the hatreds and persecutions of the world.

Observations. 1 The Apostolic prediction concerning future false teachers warns us of the Tyranny of Satan, that he does not allow the Church to be quiet, but always attempts to disturb it either by heresies or by persecutions.

2. It is not enough to hand down sound doctrine, but it is also necessary to forewarn and forearm the hearers against false teachers.

3. False Prophets arise within the very people of God. 1. Cor. 11. v. 19. There must be heresies among you. Wolves rush into the very sheepfold. Matth. 7. v. 15. Act. 20. v. 29.

4. Heresy is a clandestine and hidden subintroduction, so that it may deceive the more, whence heretics are compared to foxes in the vineyard of the Church secretly creeping in Cant. 2. v. 15. but when they find applause and acquire strength, they degenerate into lions violently rushing into the Church.

5. By the word παρεισάγειν is also denoted the crafty cunning of false teachers, by which they know how to insinuate themselves into the minds of men through smooth speech and specious words.

6. Heresies are referred to among the works of the flesh Gal. 5. v. 20. deservedly therefore they are called destructive, bringing about perdition. But also the leader, the chorus-master, and the instigator of heretics is the Angel of the abyss Abaddon καὶ ἀπολλύων. Apoc. 9. v. 11.

7. Bede in this place: Heretics deny the Lord, who bought them with the price of his blood, because they preach him not as the truth shows him, but as they fashion him for themselves.

8. The denial of the Lord happens in three ways; by profession, in which way Jews, Turks, and Gentiles deny Christ; by doctrine, in which way heretics, perverting and pertinaciously attacking the fundamental articles of the Christian faith, deny him; and by morals and by life, in which way Epicureans deny him by the impiety of their life.

9. Christ is our Lord by a double right. By the right of creation, because he created us with the Father and the Spirit; and by the right of redemption, because he claimed us for his own possession when we were reduced into the captivity of sin and Satan.

10. Deviation from the truth and a fall into heresies is easy, therefore the spirits are to be tested, and one must not believe every spirit. 1. Ioh. 4. v. 1.

11. John Huss in this place: The doctrine of heretics is corruptive of the truth, introductive of falsehood, and infective and seductive of the faithful.

12. Only the Christian doctrine is the way of truth revealed by him who is the primary truth, bringing a true and salutary θεογνωσίαν and showing the way of salvation.

13. This apostolic prophecy was fulfilled in the Papacy, which propagated itself far and wide through almost the whole world: and in Monasticism, which was received everywhere with great applause into the Church; and indeed in the multitude of Mass-sacrificing priests. Through the Popish teachers also the way of truth is blasphemed, because they burden the Evangelical doctrine with exquisite insults and calumnies and proclaim all those who depart from the Roman see to be heretics.

14. Those who, either by the approval of errors or by the impiety of their life, scandalize those who are outside the Church, cause the Christian religion to be ill-spoken of, and the name of God to be blasphemed among the nations. Rom. 2. v. 24.1. Tim. 6. v. 1.Tit. 2. v. 5.Iac. 2. v. 3. & 7.

15. Jerome in chapter 52 of Isaiah, Just as the Lord speaks to the disciples in the Gospel, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven: so on the contrary, when we have done evil works, the name of God is blasphemed among the nations on our account.

16. Bede in this place, The way of truth is blasphemed by heretics, not only in those whom they associate, having led them into their heresy, but also in those whom they incite through their most impure deeds and sacrifices or execrable mysteries which they perform in hatred of the Christian name, with the unskilled thinking that all Christians are enslaved to such outrages.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quinam fuerint illi Pseudoprophetae in V. T. de quibus Petrus v. 1. loquitur. Resp. 1. fuerunt Sacerdotes Baal, qui maximam autoritatem, Achabi praesertim temporibus, in regno Israëlis obtinebant. 1. Reg. 18. v. 19.cap. 22. v. 22. 2. Illi qui temporibus Esaiae, Ieremiae & aliorum Prophetarum sanctis DEI hominibus sese opposuerunt, idololatriam propugnarunt, ac felicitatem temporalem contra DEI voluntatem populo Israëlitico policiti fuerunt, quales fuêre Sedecias 1. Reg. 22. v. 11. Hananias Ierem. 28. v. 1. & omnes illi, de quibus Prophetae in genere conqueruntur. Esai. 9. v. 15.Ierem. 2. v. 8.cap. 5. v. 31.cap. 6. v. 13. & 14.cap. 14. v. 14.cap. 23. v. 25.Thren 2. v. 14. &c. 3. Ad eandem classem pertinent sectae Pharisaeorum, Saducaeorum, Essaeorum &c.

Q. 2. Quinam sint falsi illii Doctores, de quorum adventu Petrus vaticinatur. Resp. 1. Quidam statuunt. Petrum loqui de haereticis iamdum Apostolorum tempore, vel certè statim post Apostolorum tempora in Ecclesia exortis, ac nominatim de Gnosticis, quorum impietatem & impuritatem Epiphanius lib. 1. adv. haeres. Tom. 2. haeres. 26. describit; illis enim propriè convenire, quod Apost. dicit 2. Ep. 2. v. 19. illos libertatem aliis promittere, cùm ipsi sint servi corruptionis.v. 19. 2. Quidam vero existimant, intelligi Simonem Magum cum suis sectatoribus, cuius carnalis & spurca familia in plures haereses fuit disseminata. Estius in Proleg. huius Epist.

3. Quidam de Nicolaitis hoc accipiunt, quorum mentionem facit Iohannes in Apocalypsi cap. 2. v. 6. uti etiam Irenaeus lib. 1. cap. 27. Epiphanius lib. 1. tom. 2. haeres. 25. Eusebius libro 3. Hist. Eccles. cap. 26. Illi enim inter alia docuerunt, uxores debere esse communes.

Qui de Simonianis & Nicolaitis, non autem de Gnosticis hîc agistatuunt, argumento utuntur eo, quòd Gnosticorum haeresis Apostolorum temporibus sit posterior. Iam vero Petrum loqui de haereticis iamdum suo tempore in Ecclesia exortis, id quod probant tali argumento. Petrus & Iudas de iisdem haereticis loquuntur, ut ostendit mutua collatio. Atqui Iudas loquitur de haereticis, qui iamdum suo tempore in Ecclesia fuêre exorti. Subintroierunt, inquit, quidam homines, Dei gratiam in luxuriam transferentes. Ergo etiam Petrus de talibus haereticis loquitur.

4. Sed enim quia primò Petrus utitur verbis futuri temporis, παρεισάξουσι, ἔσονται ἐξακολουθήσουσι, ἐμπορεύσονται, &c. Secundò, Epistola eius est Catholica in usum totius Ecclesiae scripta; & ut Petrus ipse testatur 2. Epist. 1. vers. 15. fine eo, ut etiam post obitum ipsius fideles doctrinae â se traditae memoriale habere, eodemque contra falsos doctores muniri possent, ideò non solùm de haereticis iamdum Apostolorum tempore exortis, sed etiam de omnibus omnium temporum haereticis, qui tùm doctrinae falsitate, tùm vitae impietate antiquis illis conformes sunt, haec Apostolica commonefactio accipienda, omnes enim & se & sequaces suos in exitium praecipitant, ab omnibus igitur summo studio cavendum. Inde Beda in comm. hoc Petri vaticinium ad Arium, Photinum, Manichaeum, Apollinarium & Pelagium applicat.

5. Dicimus ergo, non solùm Simonianos, Nicolaitas, Gnosticos, Borboritas ex hoc ipso c. v. ult. dictos, & alios huius furfuris intelligi haereticos, qui vel ipsis Apostolorum temporibus, vel paulò post Apostolorum tempora Ecclesiam turbarunt, & falsis suis dogmatibus multos in exitium perduxerunt, sed etiam de sequentium, quinimò etiam de nostrorum novissimorum istorum temporum haereticis commonefactionem Apostolicam & posse & debere accipi.

Q. 3. Quid per viam veritatis in v. 2. intelligatur? Resp. 1. Quidam per viam veritatis intelligunt Christum, quiIoh. 14. v. 6.de seipso dicit, Ego sum via, veritas & vita; maledicta enim quae doctrinae Christianae ingeruntur, in ipsum Christum doctrinae huius autorem principalem redundant & sic fiunt blasphemiae. 2. Sed simplicius est, per viam veritatis phrasi Hebraicâ intelligere veritatem caelestem, seu doctrinam divinitus patefactam, ut constat ex aliis Scripturae locis. Act. 9. v. 2.cap. 19. v. 9. & 23.cap. 22. v. 4.cap. 24. v. 14. religio Christiana vocatur ὁδὸς & cum προσδιορισμῷ ὁδὸς σωτηρὶαςvia salutis, quia perducit ad vitam aeternam, Actor. 16. vers. 17. vocatur etiam ὁδός τοῦ Κυρίου.Actor. 18. vers. 25.ὁδὸς τοῦ θεοῦcap. eiusd. v. 26. quia est â DEO patefacta & ad DEUM nos ducit. In hoc ipso cap. 2. Epist. Petri. v. 15. vocatur ἡ ὁδός εὐθεῖαvia recta, quia sine errore & ambagibus ad vitam nos perducit.

Ἐναντιοφανεία.Christus hoc loco dicitur emisse eos, qui celerem interitum sibiipsis superinducunt. At ChristusIohann. 10. v. 15.dicit, se animam dare pro ovibus suis.cap. 17. v. 19.sanctificare se pro illis, quos Pater ipsi dederit. ElectiApoc. 5. v. 9.tanquam peculiare beneficium celebrant, quòd redemerit ipsos DEO in sanguine suo. Resp. 1. ab affirmativa non potest semper procedi ad exclusivam. Christus mortuus est pro ovibus suis, sed non pro solis suis ovibus. 2. Indefinitam illam propositionem, quòd Christus pro ovibus suis mortuus sit, Scriptura alibi exponit per universalem, quòd pro omnibus hominibus mortuus sit, quòd dederit seipsum ἀντίλυτρον pro omnibus, 1. Tim. 2. v. 6. 3. Meritum Christi consideratur vel respectu solius acquisitionis, vel respectu acquisitionis & applicationis simul. Priore respectu Christus dicitur pro omnibus mortuus, posteriore verò pro illis, qui per fidem meriti illius participes fiunt.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Petrus praedicit, venturos falsos doctores, qui subintroducturi sint sectas perditionis. Paulus Actor. 20. v. 29. eodem modo. Intrabunt post meum discessum lupi graves in vos, non parcentes gregi. v. 30. Ex vobis ipsis exurgent viri loquentes perversa. Ergo Doctoribus in Ecclesia non est simpliciter credendum, sed eatenus tantùm, quatenus ipsorum dogmata Propheticis & Apostolicis scriptis sunt conformia. Neque enim illis aequè ut Prophetis & Apostolis infallibilitatis privilegium competit, ideò de ipsorum doctrina ex verbo DEI iudicandum.

Excipit Bellarminus lib. 2. de Concil. cap. 6. §. ultimo. Petrum describere haereticos sub nomine falsorum Prophetarum, qui repugnantes doctrinae, quae per Episcopos ordinariâ successione in Ecclesia praesidentes conservatur, sectas non metuunt introducere, ut abducant discipulos post se & faciant sibi nomen in terra. Resp. falsa est hypothesis, quòd ad personalem & localem Episcoporum successionem Spiritus Sancti assistentia & doctrinae veritas sit simpliciter alligata. Fatetur enim ipse Bellarminus lib. 4. de Eccles. cap. 8. §. Adde ultimò &c. omnes Ecclesias Patriarchales, Antiochenam, Hierosolymitanam, Alexandrinam & Constantinopolitanam, habuisse per longa tempora manifestos haereticos. Excipit quidem Romanam Sedem, sed & illi Zepherinum Montanistam, Liberium Arianum, Honorium Monotheletam praefuisse, Ecclesiastica Historia testatur. Ergo localis & personalis Episcoporum successio non est norma doctrina verae in Ecclesia, quia Paulus dicit, lupos sibi successuros, sed Scriptura Prophetica & Apostolica, ad quam etiam in praecedentibus Petrus eos, ad quos scribit, remiserat. Quicunque ab hac regula discedit, sectam exitialem introducit.

2. Salmero in comm. h. l. meritò expendit emphasin προσδιορισμού, in textu Apostolico additi, ἐγένοντο ἐν ἡμίν.Pondero, inquit, illud verbum in vobis h. e. inter vos velex vobis, quia ita Paulus locutus estActor. 20. vers. 30.Ex vobis ipsis exurgent viri loquentes perversa. Eodem modo Lorinus in comm. h. l. Inter vos & ex vobis exsurgent, ut praedixit PaulusAct. 20. v. 30. & Iohannes 1. Epist. 2. v. 2. Cum his dictis, â Salmerone & Lorino citatis, coniungenda sunt loca parallela Matth. 13. v. 25.Cùm dormirent homines, venit inimicus patris familiâs & super seminavit Zizania in medio tritici.1. Cor. 11. v. 19.Oportet esse haereses inter vos. Opponenda verò haec omnia Pontificiis, qui semper ingeminant, nostrum coetum non posse esse veram Ecclesiam, cùm in ea subinde aliqui seductores tumultuentur. Atqui Satan sua Zizania potissimùm in agro Domini, in medio boni tritici spargit, non in sylvestribus, saxosis aut spinosis locis. Ergo illa ipsa Satanae Zizania testantur, hîc adesse etiam ipsum bonum agrum & bonam Christi sementem.

3. Petrus dicit, in N. T. venturos falsos doctores, perinde ut in V. T. fuerunt Pseudoprophetae. Aequè igitur ab illis Ecclesiae N. T. periculum imminet, ut ab his V. T. Ecclesiae imminuit. Falsum ergò est, quod Bellarminus d. l. §. denique &c. scribit. Non licet omnia, quae dicuntur in Scripturis adversùs Prophetas & Sacerdotes V. T. transferre ad Sacerdotes N. T. praesertim in Concilio congregatos. Certiores enim & maiores DEI promissiones habet Ecclesia, quàm Synagoga.Matth. 16.super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam1. Tim. 3.columna & firmamentum veritatisLuc. 22.Rogavi pro te, ne deficeret fides.

4. Petrus dicit, falsos illos doctores celerem perditionem sibiipsis superducentes, negare eum, qui ipsos emit. Ergo Christus pro omnibus, adeoque etiam pro illis, qui in erroribus & peccatis suis pereunt, in ara crucis mortuus est & pro peccatis eorum satisfecit.

Excipiunt. 1. Polanus, Tossanus, Piscator & alii Calviniani, hoc dictum esse nonκατ' ἀλήθειαν,sedκατὰ δόξαν,tùm quiae ipsi sibi persuadent, se esse in numero redemtorum â Christo ac se Christianos esse gloriantur: tùm quia alii ex caritate iudicant, illos esse verè fideles & proinde â Christo redemtos. Respond. haec expositio est haeretica, Nam. 1. Petrus non dicit, negantes eum, â quo vel ipsi vel alii putant se esse emtos, sed absolutè & simpliciter dicit, negantes eum, qui ipsos emit. 2. In hoc ipso cap. vers. 18. & 20. Petrus asserit, quosdam eorum, qui pereunt, priùs ὄντωςverè effugisse inquinamenta mundi per cognitionem Christi. Ergo verè in CHRISTUM crediderunt, & per consequens etiam Christus ὄντως pro peccatis ipsorum satisfecit. Pro quo enim Christus non satisfecit, ille non potest per fidem peccatorum suorum remissionem invenire. 3. Si ea, quae in Scripturis simpliciter asseruntur, κατὰ δόκησιν licet interpretari, CHRISTUS erit homo tantùm κατὰ δόκησιν, erit passus & mortuus κατὰ δόκησιν, adeoque omnes fidei articuli in dubium vocari poterunt.

2. Idem Polanus & alii excipiunt, esse hoc intelligendum quoad magnitudinem seu sufficientiam pretti, non autem quoad efficaciam, id quod probant hoc argumento. Super quos manet ira DEI, illi non sunt â Christo redemti. Super reprobos manet ira DEIIoh. 3. v. 36.Ergo reprobi non sunt â Christo redemti. Resp. 1. Si distinctionem illam inter precii sufficientiam, & efficaciam eo sensu acciperent, quo â Scholasticis adhibetur, videlicet, quòd Christus, quantum in ipso est, pro omnibus sufficientissimum redemtionis precium dederit, quòd autem non omnes fiant illius beneficii participes, eius rei culpam & causam haerere in ipsis reprobis, quia scil. oblata in Evangelio Christi beneficia sibi non applicant, tùm distinctionem allatam minimè repudiaremus. 2. Sed distinctionem illam sensu erroneo sic explicant, quòd morti quidem Christi non defuisset valor expiandi omnium hominum peccata, si ad hoc â Deo fuisset destinata, sed hoc consilium & hanc voluntatem Deo & Christo nunquam constitisse. Bucan. in loc. pag. 396. vim sanguinis Christi ressicias, ad redemtionem omnium sufficit; si verò propositum consiliumque DEI aeternum, voluntatemque Mediatoris intuearis, pro solis electis mortuus est. Robertus Episcopus Sarisber. in Exercit. pag. 31. Christum pro omnibus satisfacere voluisse asserit dignitate precii, sed voluntate propositi tantùm pro electis pag. 36. Solo affectu humano Christus mortuus est pro omnibus hominibus. 3. Inde Beza in Thes. Theol. de Praedest. th. 13. & part. 2. Resp. ad Colloq. Mompelg. pag. 217. Piscator Disp. de praedest. th. 109. in Apol. Disp. de causa meritoria Iustificat pag. 107. 108. part. 3. Resp. ad amicam Collation. Vorstii pag. 11. in annot. 1. Tim. 2. pag. 26. distinctionem illam repudiant, ac simpliciter negant, Christum pro omnibus esse mortuum. 4. Ut ergo tota res sit dilucidior, sic progredimur. Sufficientia duplex est. Primò potentialis vel possibilis, quâ Christus dicitur potuisse quidem satisfacere pro omnium hominum peccatis, sed absoluto quodam DEI beneplacito noluisse. Secundò actualis, qua Christum iuxta consilium DEI Patris actu redemisse omnes in universum homines, eisque vitam & salutem reparasse dicimus. Priorem sufficientiam ponunt Calviniani, nos posteriorem. Per efficientiam hic intelligitur applicatio meriti Christi & collatio salutis acquisitae, quam particularem esse, facilè concedimus. Calumniâ enim nos onerat Paraeus in Iren. p. 245. scribens, nos docere, quòd Christus tàm quoad efficaciam, quàm quoad sufficientiamλύτρουnon solùm pro electis, fidelibus & salvandis, sed etiam pro reprobis, infidelibus, damnatis & damnandis sit mortuus. Sed id in quaestione est, ex quo fiat, quòd efficacia sive applicatio meriti Christi sit particularis? Calviniani statuunt, causam quaerendam esse in absoluto reprobationis decreto, nos verò in culpa & incredulitate hominum. 5. Ex his facilè iudicari potest, quid statuendum de disseratione Chamieri Tom. 3. Panstrat. lib. 9. cap. 9. §. 21. In hac, in quit, controversia sufficientia est potentia quaedam: at efficacitas actus eius potentia. Unde quis non videt prom tum, qui actu redemti sunt, eos etiam efficaciter redemtos esse, ideoque non tantum sufficienter? ut meritò subeat mirari, quo sensu Windekius dixerit, intelligi reprobos actu Christi emtos, quo precium pro iis exposuerit, sive applicetur, sive non. Nam qui potest actu, si nulla sit applicatio? nisi fortè ita dieat, non actu redemtos reprobos, sed id egisse Christum, unde potuissent reprobi emi, quod et siἄκυρονest, tamen si Sophistis placet, esto sanè, non enim libetλογομαχεῖν:tamen verum erit, si potuerint redimi, non fuisse redemtos. Resp. falsum est, non posse dici reprobos actu redemtos, propterea quòd redemtionis beneficium ipsis non applicetur. Potest Dynasta Christianus pro captivis Imperatori Turcico precium redemtionis persolvere, qui tamen ex captivitate nolint exire. Illi captivi actu sunt redemti, & tamen beneficium redemtionis illis non applicatur. Leo Epist. 83. Effusio pro iniustis sanguinis iusti tàm potens fuit ad privilegium, tàm dives ad precium, ut si universitas captivorum in Redemtorem suum crederet, nullum Tyrannica vincula retinerent. 6. Argumentum Polani nihil concludit, quia Maior est falsa. Super quos manet ira DEI, illis quidem quâ talibus non applicatur beneficium redemtionis: interim tamen acquisitio huius beneficii ad illos spectat, cuius rei evidens probatio est, quod beneficia, passione & morte Christi parta, omnibus hominibus, adeoque etiam reprobis in verbo Evangelii offeruntur.

3. Alii ex Calvinianis excipiunt, Apostolum non dicere, quòd Dominus Iesus istos Pseudoprophetas sit mercatus, sed simpliciter asserere, quòd Dominusδεσπότηςeos emerit, quae vox in N. T. utplurimùm DEO Patri, aut generaliter DEO attribuatur.Epist. Iud. v. 4. Resp. 1. Si vel maximè vox δεσπότηου hîc Deum Patrem designaret, Filius tamen ab hac redemtione excludi minimè deberet, nec posset, propter essentiae ταυτότητα. 2. Non solus Pater vel Deus in genere, sed & Christus specialiter in N. T. dicitur δεσπότηςAct. 2. v. 24.Apoc. 6. v. 10. 3. Non sequitur, in Epistola Iudae v. 4. Deus dicitur δεσπότης & Christus κύριος. Ergo solus Deus Pater, vel Deus in genere dicitur δεσπότης, non autem Christus: aliàs ex 1. Cor. 8. vers. 6. colligi posset, Patrem esse Deum, & non Dominum; Christum esse Dominum, & non Deum.

4. Molinaeus in Anatome Arminianismi cap. 29. p. 422. excipit, non agi hîc de redemtione â morte aeternae, sed de liberatione ab ignorantia & errore, ac â tenebris seculi per lucem Evangelii. Resp. 1. Petrus 1. Ep.

1. vers. 18. & 19. seipsum satis luculentè explicat, quòd intelligat redemtionem factam per sanguinem Christi. 2. Idem probat locus parallelus Apoc. 5. v. 9. 3. Si per lucem Evangelii liberati sunt à tenebris seculi. Ergo etiam â morte, ut colligitur ex hoc ipso capite v. 20. 4 Qui enim per lucem Evangelii liberantur ab errore & tenebris seculi, illis in verbo Evangelii beneficia, passione & morte Christi parata, offeruntur. Quibus beneficia passione & morte Christi parta offeruntur, pro illis etiam Christus passus & mortuus est. 5. Estius Pontificius in comm. h. l. sic excipit, benè quidem ex his verbis colligi, Christum redemisse quosdam reprobos, nimirum eos, qui redemtionis eius secundùm aliquos effectus facti sunt participes, cuiusmodi erant, de quibus Petrus loquitur, utpote per fidem in Baptismo regenerati & peccatorum veniam consecuti, licet postea in veterem peccati servitutem relapsi: non tamen hinc colligendum, ad omnes omninò homines effectum redemtionis extendi. Resp. 1. Scriptura non quosdam tantum reprobos esse â Christo redemtos asserit, sed utitur terminis Universalibus, docens, Christum pro omnibus mortem gustasse,Rom. 5. v. 8.2. Cor. 5. v. 14.1. Tim. 2. v. 6.Hebr. 2. v. 9. utitur etiam termino collectivo mundi, docens, Christum pro totius mundi peccatis satisfecisse,Iohann. 1. v. 29.cap. 4. vers. 42. addit insuper μερισμὸν, docens, Christum esse propitiationem non tantùm pro nostris, sed etiam pro totius mundipeccatis,1. Iohann. 2. v. 2. Meritò igitur Cornelius â Lapide in comment. 2. Petr. 3. v. 9. sic scribit. Errant, qui censent, Christum non pro omnibus esse passum, sed tantùm pro praedestinatis. Ita senserunt olim Praedestinatiani, Arnobius in Psal. 146. Faustus lib. 2. de lib. arb. cap. 14. & 16. Remigius Lugdunensis lib. contra tres Epistolas trium Episcoporum & moderni nonnulli. Verùm contrarium Scriptura sacra & Patres omnes passim docent. &c. 2. Quando Scriptura in specie mentionem reproborum facit ac pro illis Christum mortuum esse asserit, nuspiam addit restricionem, quòd pro aliquibus tantùm reprobis, non autem pro omnibus mortuus sit. Rom. 14. v. 15.1. Cor. 8. v. 11. & hoc loco. 3. Reprobos illos, qui per Baptismum fuêre regenerati, postea verò in pristinam peccati servitutem prolapsi, & aeterno exitio involuti, per Christum fuisse redemtos, efficaciter ex percepto regenerationis beneficio probatur: sed ex eo non potest â contrario sensu inferri, quòd qui per Baptismum non fuêre regenerati, etiam per Christum non sint redemti.

Ex aliis enim principiis probari potest, etiam illos fuisse â Christo redemtos. 4. Ad omnes omninò homines effectum redemtionis extendi, ambiguè dicitur. Vel enim de acquisitione, vel de applicatione huius beneficii agitur. Si priore sensu, vera est assertio; sin posteriore, falsa.

5. Petrus de opere redemtionis per Christum praestito utitur verbo ἀγοράζειν. Ergo in eo intercessit satisfactio pro peccatis nostris per Christum sc. facta. Ubi enim λύτπον sive precium solvitur, satisfactio praestatur. Opponendum hoc Photinianis, satisfactionem Christi negantibus.

Excipiunt illi. 1. Redemtionis vocem esse metaphoricam, ac nihil aliud significare quàm simplicem liberationem, quae absque interveniente vero satisfactionis precio facta sit. Socin. contra Covetum pag. 75. Catech. Racov. cap. 8. pag. 270. Resp. 1. Petrus non solùm utitur verbo ἀγοράζειν, sed etiam exprimit redemtionis precium, quòd sc. sit sanguis Christi, agni illius immaculati, 1. Epist. 1. v. 18. & 19.
