Idem precium exprimitur Apoc. 5. v. 9.Redemisti nos tuo sanguine. 2. Urgemus ergo confessionem Socini in Synopsi de Iustif. pag. 7. Redimendi verbum precio dato liberare significat, imo si ipsius verbi vim spectes, emtionem omninò declarat, quae sine precio fieri nequit: ut & Smaltzii in Exam. 156. errorum err. 51. pag. 16. Fatemur, sanguinem Christi verum precium esse redemtionis nostrae & vim precii in nobis redimendis habuisse, quia verè id nobis praestitit sanguis Christi, quod precium in aliquo redimendo captivo praestat. Ab hac ergo verbi proprietate sine urgente causa non est discendendum. 3. Concludimus autem hoc modo. Ubicunque dantur propriè dictç redemtionis requisita, ibi etiam datur propriè dicta redemtio. In liberatione generis humani ex potestate Satanae dantur omnia propriè dictae Redemtionis requisita. Datur primò redemtionis obiectum h. e. captivi, qui sunt omnes homines Zach. 9. v. 11.Gal. 3. vers. 10. Secundò persona, quae captivum redimit, causa se principalis, quae est Christus Redemtor noster, propitiatorium nostrum, Rom. 3. v. 24. Tertiò causa instrumentalis, videlicet λύτρον seu precium redemtivum, quod est preciosus Christi sanguis Zach. 9. v. 11.Eph. 1. v. 7. Coll. 1. v. 14. Quartò captivitas, quae est terminus â quo nostrae redemtionis, sub qua intelligitur tùm iudex seu Dominus carceris, tùm custos carceris, tùm carcer ipse, eiusque adiuncta. Iudex est ipse DEUS iratus, sive ira & iudicium Dei Rom. 5. v. 9.Gal. 3. v. 13. Custos carceris est Diabolus, â cuius potestate Christus nos redemit, Os. 13. v. 14. Carcer est infernus Zach. 9. v. 11. Os. 13. v. 14. &c. Adiuncta carceris sunt laquei peccatorum nostrorum Luc. 1. v. 74.Heb. 2. v. 14. &c. Quintò libertas in quam asserimur, quae est terminus ad quem nostrae liberationis Luc. 1. v. 14. 4. Distinguendum proinde inter redemtionem corporalem, quae quocunque modo etiam sine precii interventu fieri potest, & spiritualem, quae non nisi sanguinis effusione fieri potest. Hebr. 9. v. 22. Item inter redemtionem iudicialem, & extraiudicialem, haec sine λύτρῳ peragi potest, illa verò nunquam.

2. Schmalzius in Exam. 157. errorum c. 51. p. 16. excipit, non adesse omnia propriè dictae redemtionis requisita, cùm nemo sit, cui sanguis Christi datus sit pro nobis Error. 53. p. 17. Deo non est datum ullum precium pro nobis, cùm ipse Deus Christum nostri causâ impenderit. Iam si eum sibi dari voluit pro precio, nonne retinere eum & non dare potuit? nisi Deum ludere in actionibus suis divinis dicere velimus.

Resp. 1. Verba Apostoli sunt diserta. Eph. 5. vers. 2. Christus tradidit se ipsum pro nobis victimam & oblationem DEO.Hebr. 9. v. 14.Christus obtulit seip sum per Spiritum aeternum inculpabilem DEO, ex quibus sic concludimus. Cui oblatum est sacrificium propitiatorium, pro totius mundi peccatis, illi etiam oblatum est redemtionis nostrae precium. Atqui DEO fuit oblatum sacrificium propitiatorium pro totius mundi peccatis. Ergo. 2. Considerandum hoc loco mirabile temperamentum iustitiae & misericordiae in Deo. Quod Filium suum unigenitum nobis dedit, qui pro nobis λύτρον solveret, quodque hanc λύτρου exhibitionem, ac si nos ipsi eam praestitissemus, acceptavit, est misericordiae; quod non nisi interveniente plenâ & perfecta satisfactione peccatorum debita dimisit, est iustitiae. 3. Licet Deus Pater redemtionem nostram ipsemet procuraverit, tamen quia per Filium eam procuravit, precium accipere omninò potuit. Confer Nazianzenum orat. 42. in Sanctum Pascha, p. 691.

6. Contra absolutum reprobationis decretum, â Calvinianis propugnatum, tale ex his Apostoli verbis nectimus argumentum. Qui sibimetipsis perditionem accersunt, cùm ad salutem & vitam sint caro precio emti, illi non sunt absoluto reprobationis decreto reiecti. At falsi Doctores sibiipsis perditionem accersunt, cùm sint ad salutem & vitam caro precio emti, ut hoc loco Petrus asserit & confirmant loca parallela. Os. 13. v. 9.Luc. 7. v. 30.Act. 13. v. 46. Ergo non sunt absoluto reprobationis decreto reiecti. Idem verò iudicium de reliquis damnatis.

7. Non solùm ad pristinos haereticos, qui temporibus Apostolorum vel paulò post Apostolorum tempore Ecclesiam turbarunt, & falsis suis dogmatibus multos in exitium perduxerunt, commonefactio Apostolica pertinet, sed etiam ad nostri temporis seductores. Sic

Primò Pontificii subintroduxerunt sectas perditionis, quia non contenti doctrinâ Apostolicâ in sacris literis comprehensa multa insuper falsa dogmata superinduxerunt, qualia sunt merita operum, sacrificium Missae, purgatorium, religiosa invocatio sanctorum &c. Verbum παρειάξουσι innuit, quòd falsi doctores latenter & dissimulanter sub nomine Christi & Catholicae doctrinae novos errores sint introducturi; id verò in regno Papali abundè impletum, quia Papa omnia sub nomine Christi & Spiritus sancti agit. Introduxerunt etiam Pontificii doctores sectas Thomistarum, Scotistarum, Occamistarum &c. mutuis concertationibus sese invicem oppugnantium; introduxerunt multiplices ordines Monasticos, quibus Ecclesiae unitatem sciderunt. Negarunt iidem Dominum, qui eos emit. Quamvis enim verbis apertis non videantur Christi personam, vel officium, vel beneficia negare, tamen quia realem divinorum idiomatum communicationem, quae est immediatum unionis personalis consequens, negant, indirectè unionem personalem negant. Quia Missae sacrificium propugnant, perfectionem & sufficientiam Sacrificii in ara crucis oblati indirectè & consequenter negant. Protevangelium Gen. 3. v. 15. de semine mulieris contrituro caput Serpentis ad Mariam detorquent, quam Christo in opere redemtionis sociam adiungunt. Dietenberg. in v. Bibl. Dieselbe wird dir den Kopff zertreten. Quinimò quia docent, homines suorum operum meritis vitam aeternam obtinere, ac pro peccatorum suorum poenis satisfacere, insuper etiam opera supererogationis praestare, eademque aliis communicare posse, eo ipso Mediatorium Christi officium indirectè & consequenter negant. In Flosculis S. Francisci referente Vagerio in annot. ad Indicem libror.

prohib. ad annum 1559. fol. 9. legitur, Mariam merito virginitatis suae servasse omnes feminas ad tempora cuiusdam Clarae contemporaneae S. Francisci, sicut ipse Christus merito passionis suae servavit omnes viros usque ad tempora eiusdem Francisci. Inde Lutherus in lib. contra falsò dictum Statum spiritualium Tom. 2. Ien. Germ. f. 211. de hoc loco Apostolico sic scribit. Haec verba non possunt aliter quam de Episcopis & Ecclesiasticis Praesidibus in populo accipi. Videmus, quod praeter doctrinam Christi, doctrinas hominum sectas, ordines, varios Status erexerint & in mundum introduxerint, qui extra communem Christianae fidei viam peculiaria opera & modos vivendi tradunt, per quod Christus, qui nos emit, negatur. In comm. h. l. Tom. eod. fol. 402. Proprium Christi opus est, peccata tollere, hoc tribuunt suis operibus. Illi sunt, de quibus Christus dicit. Multivenient in nomine meo, dicentes, Ego sum Christus. Non dicunt, ego vocor Christus, sed ego sum Christus, quia officium illud, quod in solidum Christo competit, ad sese rapiunt, de throno Mediatoris ipsum deturbant ac sese in illum collocant.

Secundò, Calviniani itidem negant realem idiomatum communicationem ac Nestorianam personae divulsionem introducunt; negant Christum secundum humanam Naturam ad dextram DEI exaltaetum omnia in caelo ac terra praesenter & potenter gubernare; negant Christum pro omnibus totius mundi peccatis satisfecisse.

Tertiò, Photiniani negant, Christum esse verum Naturâ Deum: negant ἀποτόμωςsatisfactionem Christi; negant iustitiam Christi fide nobis imputari. Illos ergo omnes hoc fulmen Apostolicae commonefactionis per cellit.

8. Multi dicuntur ab Apostolo falsorum doctorum exitialia dogmata & vitae immunditiem sectaturi v. 2. cum quâ praedictione congruunt parallela Christi & Apostolorum in Nov. Test. vaticinia. Matth. 24. vers. 11.Multi Pseudoprophetae surgent & seducent multos.2. Thessal. 2. vers. 11.mittet illis DEUS efficaciam erroris sive efficaces errores.1. Timoth. 4. vers. 1.In novissimis temporibus discendent quidam à fide, quam fore ἀποστασίαν penè Universalem ostendunt textus circumstantiae. Apoc. 13. vers. 8.Adoraverunt bestiam omnes, qui inhabitant terram, quorum nomina non sunt scripta in libro vitae.cap. 17. vers. 2.Cum meretrice illa magna fornicati sunt Reges terrae, & inebriati sunt, qui inhabitant terram, de vine prostitutionis eius.cap. 19. vers. 2.Meretrix magna corrupit terram prostitutione suâ. Ergo amplitudo non est propria & genuina Ecclesiae nota. Opponendum hoc Bellarmino, qui lib. 4. de Eccles. cap. 7. §. 1. amplitudinem ac multitudinem adhaerentium inter notas Ecclesiae numerat: uti etiam Iacobo Reihingio adhuc Pontificio, qui in Muris Babylon. fund. 11. p. 298. sic disserit. Illi Doctores audiendi, quorum auditores multò plures. Multitudo fidelium meliores nobis ostendit Doctores. Pontificii hac in parte sese conformant Arianis de multitudine sectatorum gloriantibus, unde Imp. Constantius Arianus Liberio Episcopo orthodoxo obiiciebat. Quota pars tu es orbis terrarum? apud Theodoretum lib. 2. Hist. Eccles. cap. 16. ac Eutychianis, de quibus idem Theodoretus in Opusculis Athanasii nomine editis scribit, quod μόνω πλήθει τοῦ λόγου τὴν ἰσχύν ἀπονέμουσιsoli multitudini vim rationis vendicârint, quibus ipse respondet, immensum semper esse veritatis roburκἀν παρ' ὀλίγοις εὑρίσκηται,quantumvis apud paucos reperiatur.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Estius ad vers. 1. monet, falsos Doctores non vocari ab Apostolo Pseudoprophetas, quo nomine falsos Vet. Test. doctores appellaverat, sed falsos Magistros, cuius variationis rationem assignat eam, quod tempus Vet. Test. fuerit propriè ProphetumLuc. 16. vers. 16.Lex & Prophetae usque ad Iohannem, siquidem in Vet. Test. mysteria praedicebantur, quod est Prophetarum stricto nomine sic appellatorum; at in Nov. Test. praedicta explicantur, quod est Magistrorum. Eodem ferè modò Lorinus in hunc locum, qui postquam dixerat, ψευδοδισκάλουςesse eosdem, quos prius dixerat Apostolus Pseudoprophetas, cùm Prophetarum fuerit docere, postea subiungit. Videtur Petrus, quos magistros suos Hebraei Prophetas nominabant, in Ecclesiae sola Magistri voce nuncupare, licet nec de fuerint Ecclesiae sui Prophetae, primisque illis eius initiis commemorantur Antiochiae fuisse Prophetae & Doctores,Actor. 13. vers. 1.

Atqui 1. haec observatio non satis congruit usui Scripturae Sacrae, siquidem CHRISTUS etiam Nov. Test. falsos Doctores vocat ΨευδοπροφήταςMatthaei 7. versu 15.cap. 24. vers. 11. & 24.Marc. 13. vers. 22. quam nomenclaturam etiam imitantur Lucas Act, 13. v. 6. & Iohannes 1. Epist. 4 v. 1.Apoc. 16. v. 13.cap. 19. v. 20.cap. 20. v. 10. 2. nimirum, quia προφητεύειν phrasi Scripturae non solum significat futura praedicere, sed etiam Scripturam Propheticam exponere, ut agnoscit Estius in comm. cap. praeced. v. 20. quam significationem probat ex Rom. 12. v. 6.1. Cor. 13. v. 2. & 8.cap. 14. v. 6.1. Thess. 5. v. 20.Apoc. 11. vers. 6. 3. Regerit quidem Estius, hanc esse prophetiae acceptionem generalem; prophetiam verò stricto nomine acceptam esse futurorum praedictionem. Sed haec sunt duo distincta unius vocis significata, quorum utrumque propriè ei competit, si Scripturae usum, non autem vocis Etymologiam respiciamus. 4. Lutherus in comment. h. l. Tom. 2. Ien. Germ. fol. 401. aliam profert observationem, quae Estio meritò opponitur. Singulari DEI consilio factum, quod in Academiis Papalibus Doctores sint vocati, qui Ecclesiasticis officiis erant praeficiendi, ut intelligi posset, illos nomine falsorum doctorum ab Apostolo hîc perstringi, unde non vocat eos falsos Prophetas, & falsos Apostolos, sed falsos doctores.

2. Lorinus ad eund. vers. sic commentatur. Admonui in comm.Actor. 24. vers. 14.ex usu Ecclesiastico malè sonare haeresin, licet interdum apud Scriptores nostros habeat usum bonum. Estius eodem modo. Haeresis quamvis usu totius Ecclesiaeiam olim in malam partem accipiatur, tamen apud prophanos autores, atque etiam in Scriptura sacra vocabulum medium est, significans opinionem, quam quis sibi delegerit seu veram, seu falsam. Hemmingius in h. l. Haeresis etsi medium vocabulum est, ut quod nunc in bonam, nunc in malam partem accipiatur: tamen saepius usu Scripturae, quia dissensionem notat, in malam partem accipitur.

Resp. 1. phrasi Biblicâ haereseos vox semper in malam partem accipitur. Actor. 5. v. 17.cap. 15. v. 5.1. Cor. 11. v. 19.Gal. 5. v. 20. 2. Afferuntur quidem in contrarium quaedam loca, in quibus videtur in bonam partem accipi, sed ad ea ex circumstantiis textus facilè responderi potest. Actor. 24. v. 5. Tertullus Iudaeorum Orator de Paulo dicit. Invenimus hunc hominem pestiferum autoremτῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως ubi per haeresin Nazaraeorum intelligitur religio Christianorum. Atqui illam Tertullus & Iudaei pro pestilentissima haeresi habebant. Actor. 24. vers. 14. inquit Paulus ad Praefidem. Confiteor tibi, quòd secundùm viam hanc, quam vocantαἵρεσιν, patrio DEO servio. At non simpliciter & suo sensu Paulus Christianam religionem haeresin vocat, sed sensu aliorum, disertè enim addit, ἥν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν.Act. 26. v. 5.κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος. At Pharisaismus reverâ erat perniciosa haeresis, vocat autem exquisitissimam haeresin, quia hypocrisi sua singularem sanctitatis opinionem sectae suae conciliare studebant, cùm Sadducaei essent Epicuraei, Esseni â conversatione vulgari semoti. Actor. 28. vers. 22.περὶ μὲν γὰρ αἱρέσεως ταύτης &c. At Iudaei illi religionem Christianam habebant pro damnabili secta, unde addunt, Audimus, quòd ubique huic Sectae contradicatur. 3. In LXX. Interpp. versione haereseos vox sumitur pro pessimo proposito Gen. 49. v. 6. Quamvis vero Levit. 22. vers. 18. & 21. accipiatur de spontaneo oblationis affectu,1. Maccab. 8. vers. 30. de spontanea & libera mutatione, tamen ex eo non potest probari, quòd de doctrina acceptum in bonam partem usurpetur. 4. Certum igitur esto, haereseos nomen pro doctrina acceptum semper in malam partem accipi, videlicet pro prava & falsa opinione, quam quis proprio suo ingenio & privato arbitrio sibi eligit, eamque contra veritatem in Scriptura patefactam amplectitur. Eodem modo etiam in scriptis veterum, adeoque phrasi Ecclesiasticâ accipitur. Tertullianus lib. de praescript. adversus haereses cap. 6. Haereses dictae Graecâ voce ex interpretatione electionis, qua quis sive ad instituendas, sive ad suscipiendas eas utitur. Ideò & sibi damnatum dixit haereticum, quia & in quo damnatur, sibi elegit: nobis verò nihil ex nostro arbitrio inducere licet, sed nec eligere, quòd aliquis de arbitrio suo induxerit. Apostolos Domini habemus autores, qui nec ipsi quidquam ex suo arbitrio, quòd inducerent, elegerunt, sed acceptam â Christo disciplinam fideliter nationibus adsignaverunt lib. eiusd. cap. 37. Unde extranei & inimici Apostolis haeretici, nisi ex diversitate doctrinae, quam unusquisque de suo arbitrio adversus Apostolos aut protulit aut recepit? Hieronymus in cap. 5. Gal. Haeresis Graecè ab electione dicitur, quod sc. eam unusquisque sibi eligat disciplinam, quam putat esse meliorem. Quicunque igitur aliter Scripturam intelligit, quàm sensus Spiritus sancti flagitat, quo scripta est, licet ab Ecclesia non recesserit, tamen haereticus appellari potest. Leo primus Epist. 10. ad Flavianum. Qui non ad Propheticas voces, non ad Apostolicas literas, non ad Evangelicas autoritates, sed ad seipsos recurrunt, haereseos insipientiam incurrunt & ideò Magistri erroris existunt, quia veritatis discipuli non fucrunt. Beda in comm. h. l. Quae Secta Latinè, Graecè dicitur haeresis, cùm quis stultâ obstinatione errorem quem semel coepit, semper sectari nullatenus cessat, quod haereticorum proprium esse quis nescit?

3. Lorinus ad v. 2. sic annotat. Lutherus religiosi Ordinis Apostata, quod faciebat, docebat etiam, aequè concubitum esse necessarium ac edere, bibere, dormire: & plus quàm praeceptum esse omnibus à quo nullus eximi possit. Crescite & multiplicamini: & ut si uxor nolit, alia etiam ancilla advocetur. Resp. hisce ἐγκλήμασι in loco de coniugio & in Confess. Catholica prolixè satisfactum. Virginitatis donum quibusdam divinitus esse datum Luth. non negat, sed in cuiusvis hominis arbitrio illud positum esse negat. Nec de promiscuo cum ancilla concubitu, sed de legitima refractariae uxoris separatione loquitur.

4. Cornelius à Lapide ad eund. vers. sic commentatur. Thomas Morus cuidam obiicienti, plurimos ad Lutheri sectam sese conferre, ideoque eam videri veram argutè respondit. Non plus miraculi est, homines ad Lutherum currere, quam saxa ex alto deorsum ruere. Plerique enim currunt & ruunt ad gulam, Venerem & libertatem carnis quàm permittit, imò docet Lutherus.

Resp. 1. haec carnis vitia Lutherus nec docuit, nec permittit, sed detestatus est. 2. Docuit vero mortificationem & crucifixionem carnis cum suis concupiscentiis ab omnibus verè piis requirit. 3. Quotquot Evangelicam doctrinam à Luthero praedicatam suscipunt odiis & persecutionibus mundi sese exponunt.

Observationes. 1 Praedictio Apostolica de venturis falsis doctoribus admonet nos de Tyrannide Satanae, quod Ecclesiam non sinat esse quietam, sed semper eam conetur vel haeresibus vel persecutionibus turbare.

2. Non sufficit sanam doctrinam tradere, sed oportet etiam contra falsos doctores auditores praemonere ac praemunire.

3. In ipso Dei populo exurgunt falsi Prophetae. 1. Cor. 11. v. 19.Oportet esse haereses inter vos. Lupi in ipsum ovile irruunt. Matth. 7. v. 15.Act. 20. v. 29.

4. Haeresis est subintroductio clancularia & occulta, quo magis decipiat, unde haeretici comparantur vulpibus in Ecclesiae vineam clam irrepentibus Cant. 2. v. 15. quando autem applausum inveniunt & vires acquirunt, degenerant in leones violentè in Ecclesiam irruentes.

5. Per verbum παρεισάγειν etiam denotatur veteratoria falsorum doctorum astutia, quâ per blandiloquentiam & speciosos sermones animis hominum sese insinuare norunt.

6. Haereses referuntur inter opera carnis Gal. 5. v. 20. meritò ergo vocantur exitiales perditionem afferentes Sed & Dux, choragus & incentor haereticorum est Angelus abyssi Abaddonκαὶ ἀπολλύων.Apoc. 9. v. 11.

7. Beda in h. l. Haeretici Dominum, qui eos sanguinis sui precio emit, negant, quia illum, non qualem veritas ostendit sed qualem ipsi sibi fingunt, praedicant.

8. Abnegatio Domini fit tribus modis; professione, quo modo Iudaei, Turcae & gentiles Christum negant; doctrinâ quo modo haeretici fundamentales fidei Christianae articulos pervertentes ac pertinaciter oppugnantes eum negant; & moribus ac vita, quo modo Epicuraei vitae impietate eum negant.

9. Christus duplici iure est noster Dominus. Iure creationis, quia cum Patre & Filio nos creavit; & Iure redemtionis, quia in captivitatem peccati & Satanae redactos nos sibi in peculium asservit.

10. Proclivis est à veritate deviatio & in haereses prolapsus, probandi igitur Spiritus, nec cuivis Spiritui credendum.1. Ioh. 4. v. 1.

11. Ioh. Huss. in h. l. Doctrina haereticorum est veritatis corruptiva, falsitatis introductiva & fidelium infectiva ac seductiva.

12. Sola doctrina Christiana est via veritatis ab eo, qui est prima veritas, revelata, veram & salutarem θεογνωσίαν afferens & viam salutis monstrans.

13. Impletum est hoc Apostolivaticinium in Papatu, qui longè lateque per totum fere orbem sese propagavit: ac Monachismo, qui magno applausu in Ecclesiam fuit ubivis locorum receptus; quin & in sacrificulorum Missificantium multitudine. Per Pontificios etiam doctores via veritatis blasphematur, quia doctrinam Evangelicam exquisitis convitiis & calumniis onerant & quotquot à sede Romana discedunt, illos omnes haereticos proclamant.

14. Qui vel approbatione errorum, vel vitae impietate eos, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam, scandalizant, faciunt ut Christiana religio malè audiat, & nomen Dei inter gentes blasphemetur. Rom. 2. v. 24.1. Tim. 6. v. 1.Tit. 2. v. 5.Iac. 2. v. 3. & 7.

15. Hieronymus in cap. 52. Esai. Quo modo in Evangelio discipulis loquitur Dominus, luceat lumen vestrum coram hominibus, ut videant opera vestra bona, & glorificent Patrem vestrum, qui in caelis est: sic è contrario cùm mala opera fecerimus, nomen Dei propter nos in gentibus blasphematur.

16. Beda in h. l. Via veritatis per haereticos non solùm in eis, quos suae haeresi eductos (addictos) associant, sed in eis quoque quos per impurissima sua facta & sacrificia vel mysteria execranda quae faciunt in odium Christiani nominis concitant, existimantibus imperitis omnes Christianos huiusmodi flagitiis esse mancipatos.

## 2:2
Connection. 1. He brings forward the reason for his admonition. Because there would be many followers of the false teachers, therefore a forewarning against them was necessary.

2. In order to sharpen and exaggerate his admonition, he shows that the danger of destruction threatens not only the seducers, but also the seduced.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταίς ἀσελγείαις. For ἀσελγείαις indeed the Greek Codices read ἀπωλείαις from v. 1. in which way also Henry Stephanus in the Greek Concordance, as also Vatablus, Cajetan, Clarius etc. read. But by ἀπωλείας destructions μετωνυμικῶς destructive dogmas and manifold errors, by which they lead men with them into destruction, would be understood. To this reading it supports [the view] that in the preceding verse mention was made twice of ἀπωλείας, and in vers. 3. following, the Apostle again uses this name. Luther followed the same reading in the vernacular version. Viel werden nachfolgen ihrem Verderben. The sense therefore would be: As false Teachers bring destruction upon themselves: so many will run into the same destruction with them, following their dispositions and morals.

But other Codices read ἀσελγείαις, which reading seems to some to be preferable to the former. 1. Because, as Robert Stephanus notes, more and more approved Codices read thus. Beza in the annotations to this place: This reading is confirmed by the authority of the Complutensian edition and six other Codices. 2. The Syriac Interpreter seems to have read in the same way, who rendered it by [טנפותא] uncleanness from the root [טנף] he defiled, he polluted. 3. As also the Vulgate version, which rendered it, lasciviousnesses. 4. A parallel passage supports this reading. Jude Epist. v. 4. Παρεισέδυσαν γὰρ τινες ἄνθρωποι &c τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριν μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον δεσπότην θεὸν &c ἀρνούμενοι. 5. In this very second chapter v. 18. Peter likewise attributes ἀσελγείας. to these false Teachers. 6. One is not properly or customarily said to follow another's destruction, although by following his morals he goes to his own destruction together with him.

But neither reading is opposed to the analogy of faith or to the context, and both agree with the underlying matter. For those false Teachers have many followers of their destructive errors and imitators of their lasciviousnesses. Concerning the word ἀσελγείας it was spoken of 1. Petr. 4. v. 3.

Δι' οὓς ἡ ὁδός τῆς ἀληθείας Βλασφημηθήσεται. Some connect the relative pronoun οὑς with the more remote [antecedent], namely with the false Teachers, of whom mention had been made v. 1. in the sense that by the false Teachers seducing others the way of truth is blasphemed, while they harass the true and orthodox confession of faith with curses. But it is more correctly connected with the latter member, so that it is taken of those who allow themselves to be seduced by the false Teachers, in the sense that the Gentiles blaspheme the Christian Doctrine when they see dissensions in Doctrine and scandals of morals flourishing among Christians. Esai. 52. v. 5.Ezech. 36. v. 23.Rom. 2. v. 24. The name of GOD is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you. The Syriac notably expressed this, rendering the text thus: And many will go away, after their uncleanness, those for whom the way of truth shall be blasphemed.

For ἡ ὁδός τῆς ἀληθείας certain Codices in the possession of Rob. Stephanus read δόξα τῆς ἀληθείας. But the former reading is the genuine one. By the way of truth is understood the Doctrine divinely revealed, which is the true and straight way to heaven.

Βλασφημηθήσεται. The Syriac has the word [גדף] he blasphemed, he assailed with reproaches, with contumelies. The name blasphemy is accepted in the Scriptures in two ways, either strictly and properly for a reproach against God: or generally and loosely for any curse and reproach even against one's neighbor. In this place it is put in the former signification. For when the Gentiles see that Christians are divided among themselves into so many Sects, and that many under the Christian name ἀσελγείας καί τὰς τῆς σαρκὸς ἐπιθυμίας freely follow them, they tear apart with reproaches the true and sound Doctrine, which indirectly and consequently redound upon God Himself, the author of this Doctrine.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Commonefactionis suae rationem profert. Quia multi falsorum Doctorumerunt sectatores, ideò necessaria fuit adversus illos praemonitio.

2. Ut commonefactionem suam acuat & exaggeret, ostendit, non solùm seductoribus, sed etiam seductis periculum exitii imminere.

Textus expositio. Καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταίς ἀσελγείαις. Pro ἀσελγείαις quidem Graeci Codd. legunt ἀπωλείαις ex v. 1. quo modo etiam Heinricus Stephanus in Concord. Graecis, uti etiam Vatablus, Caietanus, Clarius &c. legunt. Intelligerentur autem per ἀπωλείαςexitiaμετωνυμικῶςdogmata exitialia ac multiplices errores, quibus homines secum in exitium abducunt. Huic lectioni suffragetur, quod in vers. praeced. bis facta fuerit mentio ἀπωλείας, ac in vers. 3. seq. Apostolus denuò hoc nomine utatur. Eandem lectionem secutus est Lutherus in vers. vernacula. Viel werden nachfolgen ihrem Verderben. Sensus ergo foret. Sicut falsi Doctores sibi ipsis exitium pariunt: sic plerique in idem cum illis exitium current, eorum ingenia & mores sectantes.

Alii verò Codices legunt ἀσελγείαις, quae lectio videtur quibusdam priori praeferenda. 1. Quia, ut Robertus Stephanus annotat, plures & probatiores Codd, ita legunt. Beza in annot. ad h. l. Haec lectio confirmatur Complutensis editionis & sex praeterea Codicum autoritate. 2. Eodem modo legisse videtur Interpres Syrus, qui reddidit per [טנפותא]immunditiem â rad. [טנף]inquinavit, polluit. 3. Uti etiam vulgata versio, quae reddidit, luxurias. 4. Suffragatur huic lectioni locus parallelus. Iud. Epist. v. 4. Παρεισέδυσαν γὰρ τινες ἄνθρωποι &c τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριν μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον δεσπότην θεὸν &c ἀρνούμενοι. 5. In hoc ipso secundo cap. v. 18. Petrus falsis istis Doctoribus itidem tribuit ἀσελγείας. 6. Non propriè nec usitatè quis dicitur sequi alterius perditionem, licet eius mores sectando unà cum ipso eat se perditum.

Sed neutra lectio vel analogiae fidei, vel contextui adversatur, ac utraque substratae rei convenit. Falsi enim illi Doctores multos habent errorum suorum exitialium sectatores & lasciviarum suarum imitatores. De voce ἀσελγείας dictum fuit 1. Petr. 4. v. 3.

Δι' οὓς ἡ ὁδός τῆς ἀληθείας Βλασφημηθήσεται. Pronomen relativum οὑς quidam coniungunt cum remotiore, cum falsis scil. Doctoribus, quorum mentio facta fuerat v. 1. sensu eo, quòd per falsos Doctores alios seducentes via veritatis blasphemetur, dum veram & orthodoxam fidei confessionem maledictis exagitent. Sed rectiùs coniungitur cum membro posteriore, ut accipiatur de illis, qui â falsis Doctoribus sese patiuntur seduci, sensu eo, quòd gentiles Doctrinam Christianam blasphement, quando vident, dissidia in Doctrina & scandala morum inter Christianos vigere. Esai. 52. v. 5.Ezech. 36. v. 23.Rom. 2. v. 24.Nomen DEI per vos inter gentes blasphematur. Syrus notanter hoc expressit, textum sic reddens. Et multi abibunt, post immunditiam eorum, illi propter quos via veritatis blasphemabitur.

Pro ἡ ὁδός τῆς ἀληθείας quidam Codd. apud Rob. Stephanum legunt δόξα τῆς ἀληθείας. Sed prior lectio est genuina. Intelligitur autem per viam veritatis Doctrina divinitus patefacta, quae est vera & recta ad caelum via.

Βλασφημηθήσεται. Syrus habet verbum [גדף]blasphemavit, convitiis, contumeliis incessit. Nomen blasphemiae dupliciter in Scripturis accipitur, vel strictè & propriè pro convitio in Deum: vel generaliter & laxè pro quovis maledicto & convitio etiam in proximum. Hoc loco in priore significatione ponitur. Quando enim gentiles vident, Christianos inter se tot Sectis scindi, ac multos sub nomine Christiano ἀσελγείας καί τὰς τῆς σαρκὸς ἐπιθυμίας liberè sectari, veram & sanam Doctrinam conviciis proscindunt, quae indirectè & consequenter in ipsum Deum Doctrinae huius autorem vergunt.

## 2:3
Connection. 1. To the prediction concerning the coming of false teachers, he adds a graphic description of the same, and in the first place he touches upon their covetousness. Indeed, ἀσέλγεια,, of which mention is made in the preceding verse, could also be referred to the marks of false teachers, but because the reading of the Greek Codices varies, therefore this part of the description is deservedly referred to verse 19.

2. To the description of this first vice in false teachers, he adds a repetition of the destruction which most certainly awaits them, and thus he explains that which he had said in verse 1, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ ἐν πλεονεξία πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται. ἐν is placed for διὰ by a customary Hebraism. Πλεονεξία by the force of the name signifies a desire always to have more, which is proper to the covetous and παθογνωμονικόν a vice. Luc. 12. v. 15. Christ expresses the emphasis of this word thus. Beware from πλεονεξία, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν εινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτοῦ. They are therefore πλεονεκταὶ, who constitute the highest good ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν who, not content with those things which are obtained through legitimate means, always desire to heap up more. πλουτεῖν βουλόμενοι, as speaks. The Apostle 1. Tim. 6. v. 9. thence Col. 3. vers. 5. ἐπιθυμία κακὴ and πλεονεξία are joined. Augustine, book 3, On Free Choice, chapter 17, and book 12, On the Trinity, chapter 9, defines avarice as wanting more than is enough, (or than the measure of Nature requires for being preserved in its own kind). The Syrian in this place has the word [עלובותא] from the root [עלב], which is not only used for πλεονεκτεῖν 1. Thessal. 4. v. 6.2. Cor. 7. v. 2. but also for ἀδικεῖν to treat with injury, 1. Cor. 6. v. 8. because the avaricious are injurious toward their neighbor, not fearing to defraud and circumvent him.

By πλαστοὺς λόγους are understood fictitious and flattering words, speeches artificially composed for deceiving. For the word πλάτεσθαι the LXX, among other meanings, use for בדא to lie, to bring forth a lie from the heart and thought to the mouth. 3. Reg. 12. v. 33. and πλάττειν among the Greeks signifies to fashion, to invent. Demosth. τοιαῦτα πλάττεσθαι τολμάτε. Among Herodian πλασαμένη is opposed to τῷ ἀληθεύουσα πλαστολάλος or πλαστολόγος is he who speaks things fashioned or feigned. The interpreter of the Syriac text, Etzelius and Pococke, rendered it by the second case, In avarice of words fallaciously fashioned. But it can also be rendered in that way, as it is in the Greek, In avarice with words fallaciously fashioned, for thus the Syrian has [דמלא דבדיא] from the root בדא he fashioned, he lied. Luther. Mit erdichteten Worten.

Ἐμπορεύσανται ὑμᾶς. Ἐμπορεύσθαι placed absolutely signifies to trade, to merchandise. Iac. 4. v. 3. thence ἐμπορία merchandise, trade, Matth. 22. v. 5. but here it is used with the accusative of the person, examples of which phrase rarely occur elsewhere in the Scriptures. Genes. 34. vers. 10. it is used with the preposition ἐπὶ, ἐμπορεύεσθε ἐπ' αὐτῆς, namely γῆς Genes. 42. v. 34. with the dative, τῇ γῇ ἐμπορεύεσθαι. Os. 12. vers. 1. with the preposition εἰς ἔλαων εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐνεπορεύοτο. Gen. 34. v. 21. it is indeed used with the accusative, but not of the person, but of the thing. Ἐμπορευέσθωσαν αὐτὴν namely γῆν Prov. 3. v. 14. ἐμπορεύεσθαι αὐτὴν namely σοφίαν. Ezech. 27. vers. 21. it is used with the accusative of the person, κριοὺς, ἐν οἷς ἐνεπορεύοντο σε rams, in which they traded with you are or have exercised trade. But neither is this passage plainly parallel to ours, for the pronoun σε denotes the object of trade, but not the material, whereas in this Apostolic passage it denotes the material of trade. Through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you that is, they will make gain out of you, they will abuse you for their own gain, they will abuse you like cattle for market and gain, just as Pliny says in book 29 of Nat. Hist. chap. 1. that unskilled physicians trade in souls Luth. Sie werden an euch handthieren. The sense therefore is, under the guise of piety they will deceive you and fleece you of money, they will prepare their own advantage from your disadvantage; they will suppose that godliness is gain. 1. Tim. 6. vers. 5. The Syrian rendered it. [נתתגרון בכון] they will exercise trade in you. The root is [אגר] in Ithpehal, to trade, to gain. The metaphor is drawn from greedy merchants, who commend their wares with feigned and lying words, so that they may sell them at a higher price, according to πολυθρήλλυτον that saying. He praises wares who wishes to push out goods. Jude in the parallel passage says of them, that they admire persons for the sake of gain. v. 16.

Οἵς τὸ κρῖμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν μὴ νυστὰζει. By το ητιμα in the customary meaning in the Scriptures is understood τὸ κατάκριμα damnation, as the added word ἀπωλείας ἐξηγητικῶς shows. It is said therefore that the damnation of these false teachers does not idle and their destruction does not slumber, because although God may seem to connive for a time, yet their punishment will most certainly and sooner than expected follow, for which he had said above, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν.

Ἔκπαλαι properly signifies from of old. Luth. vor langst her. Syr. [מן קדים] Regard is therefore had both to the divine reprobation, by which on account of foreseen final perseverance in error and impiety they are adjudged to eternal destruction by the just judgment of GOD, Esai. 30. v. 33.Matth. 25. v. 41. and to the Prophetic predictions, in which destruction is foretold for such false Doctors; and to the approach of damnation, which is closer than false teachers might think and is to be put into execution shortly. Dionys. Carthus. in h. l. The judgment of reprobation long ago foretold concerning them in the holy Scriptures is neither revoked nor ended. Jude in his Epistle v. 4 expresses that member thus, οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο χρῖμα, the sense of which words we have explained above.

Moreover, in the words ἀργεῖν & νυστάζειν there are elegant metaphors. He who is idle and slumbers, he puts off what is incumbent upon him to perform. Therefore the Apostle denies that the damnation of these false teachers is idle and that their destruction slumbers, because at the time divinely appointed and thus sooner than they think, it will overwhelm them. Beda in comm. refers to the beginning of punishments in this life and their eternal duration. Since, he says, it signifies time long past, yet the word of the present tense does not cease, nothing else seems to be understood, except that the judgment of the destruction of the impious has already begun long ago, which presently torments them always and will never cease with any end. Hugo & Glossa interlin. say, that the sentence is true concerning those still living on account of the remorse of conscience, which is no small part of hell.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Praedictioni de falsorum doctorum adventu subiungit graphicam eorundem descriptionem ac primo loco perstringit eorum avaritiam. Poterat sanè etiam ἀσέλγεια, cuius in vers. praeced. fit mentio, ad notas falsorum doctorum referri, sed quia Codicum Graecorum lectio variat, ideo haec descriptionis pars meritò refertur adv. 19.

2. Descriptioni primi huius vitii in falsis Doctoribus subiungit repetitionem exitii, quod ipsos certissimè maneat, sicque explicat illud quod vers. 1. dixerat, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν.

Textus expositio. Καὶ ἐν πλεονεξία πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται. ἐνponitur proδιὰper usitatum Hebraismum.Πλεονεξίαex vi nominis significat studium semper plus habendi, quod avaris est proprium & παθογνωμονικόν vitium. Luc. 12. v. 15. Christus vocis huius emphasin sic exprimit. Cavete â πλεονεξία, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν εινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτοῦ. Sunt ergo πλεονεκταὶ, qui summum bonum constituunt ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν qui non contenti iis, quae per legitima media obtingunt, plura semper congerere desiderant. πλουτεῖν βουλόμενοι, ut loquitur Apostolus 1. Tim. 6. v. 9. inde Col. 3. vers. 5.ἐπιθυμία κακὴ ac πλεονεξία coniunguntur. August. lib. 3. de lib. arb. cap. 17. & lib. 12. de Trinit. cap. 9. definit avaritiam plus velle, quàm sat est, (seu quàm exigit Naturae in suo genere conservandae modus) Syrus h. l. habet vocem [עלובותא] â rad. [עלב] quae non solùm usurpatur pro πλεονεκτεῖν1. Thessal. 4. v. 6.2. Cor. 7. v. 2. sed etiam pro ἀδικεῖνiniuriâ afficere,1. Cor. 6. v. 8. quia avari in proximum sunt iniurii, ipsum defraudare ac circumvenire non metuentes.

Per πλαστοὺς λόγους intelliguntur verba fictitia & blanda, sermones ad decipiendum artificiosè compositi. Verbo enim πλάτεσθαι LXX. inter alia significata utuntur pro בדאmentiri, mendacium educere ex corde & cogitatione ad os. 3. Reg. 12. v. 33. ac πλάττειν apud Graecos significat confingere, comminisci. Demosth. τοιαῦτα πλάττεσθαι τολμάτε. Apud Herodianum πλασαμένη opponitur τῷ ἀληθεύουσα πλαστολάλος vel πλαστολόγος est, qui ficta vel simulata loquitur. Syriaci textûs Interpres Etzelius & Pococke reddiderunt per casum secundum. In avaritia verborum fallaciter fictorum. Sed potest etiam eo modo reddi, ut est in Graeco. In avaritia verbis fallaciter fictis, sic enim habet Syrus [דמלא דבדיא] â rad. בדאeffinxit, mentitus est. Lutherus. Mit erdichteten Worten.

Ἐμπορεύσανται ὑμᾶς. Ἐμπορεύσθαι absolutè positum significat negotiari, mercari.Iac. 4. v. 3. inde ἐμπορίαmercatura negotiatio,Matth. 22. v. 5. hîc verò usurpatur cum accusativo personae, cuius phraseos exempla alibi in Scripturis rarò occurrunt. Genes. 34. vers. 10. usurpatur cum praepositione ἐπὶ, ἐμπορεύεσθε ἐπ' αὐτῆς sc. γῆςGenes. 42. v. 34. cum Dativo, τῇ γῇ ἐμπορεύεσθαι.Os. 12. vers. 1. cum praepositione εἰς ἔλαων εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐνεπορεύοτο.Gen. 34. v. 21. usurpatur quidem cum accusativo, sed non personae, verùm rei. Ἐμπορευέσθωσαν αὐτὴν sc. γῆνProv. 3. v. 14.ἐμπορεύεσθαι αὐτὴν sc. σοφίαν.Ezech. 27. vers. 21. usurpatur cum accusativo personae, κριοὺς, ἐν οἷς ἐνεπορεύοντο σεarietes, in quibus tecum mercati sunt vel negotiationem exercuerunt. Sed nec hic locus nostro est planè parallelus, nam pronomen σε denotat negotiationis obiectum, non autem materiam, verùm in hoc loco Apostolico materiam negotiationis denotat. Per avaritiam fictis sermonibus vos negotiabuntur h. e. quaestum ex vobis facient, ad quaestum suum vobis abutentur, vobis tanquam pecoribus ad nundinationem & quaestum abutentur, sicut Plinius dicit lib. 29. Nat. Hist. cap. 1. imperitos Medicos animas negotiari Luth. Sie werden an euch handthieren. Sensus ergo est, sub specie pietatis vos decipient & pecuniâ emungent, ex vestro incommodo suum parabunt commodum; pietatem quaestum existimabunt. 1. Tim. 6. vers. 5. Syrus reddidit. [נתתגרון בכון]mercaturam exercebunt in vobis. Rad. est. [אגר] in Ithpehal, mercari, lucrari. Metaphora ducta est ab avaris mercatoribus, qui verbis fictiis & mendacibus merces suas commendant, ut eò maiori precio eas vendant, iuxta πολυθρήλλυτον illud. Laudat venales qui vult extrudere merces. Iudas in loco parallelo de illis dicit, quòd mirentur personas quaestus causâ. v. 16.

Οἵς τὸ κρῖμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν μὴ νυστὰζει. Per το ητιμα usitatâ in Scripturis significatione intelligitur τὸ κατάκριμαdamnatio, ut vox ἀπωλείας ἐξηγητικῶς addita ostendit. Dicitur ergo falsorum istorum doctorum damnatio non otiari ac exitium ipsorum non dormitare, quia quamvis Deus ad tempus videatur connivere, poena tamen ipsorum certissimè & opinione citiùs sit secutura, Pro quo superius dixerat, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν.

Ἔκπαλαι propriè significat ex antiquo. Luth. vor langst her. Syr. [מן קדים] Respectus igitur habetur tum ad divinam reprobationem, quâ ob praevisam finalem in errore & impietate perseverantiam iusto DEI iudicio aeterno exitio sunt adiudicati, Esai. 30. v. 33.Matth. 25. v. 41. tum ad praedictiones Propheticas, in quibus eiusmodi falsis Doctoribus exitium est praenunciatum; tum ad damnationis appropinquationem, quod propiùs absit, quàm falsi doctores existiment & brevi sit executioni mandanda. Dionys. Carthus. in h. l. Reprobationis iudicium dudum de eis praenunciatum in sanctis Scripturis non est revocatum neque finitum. Iudas in sua Epist. v. 4. illud membrum sic exprimit, οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο χρῖμα, quorum verborum sensum exposuimus superiùs.

Coeterum in verbis ἀργεῖν & νυστάζειν elegantes sunt metaphorae. Qui otiatur ac dormitat, ille, quod peragendum sibi incumbit, differt. Negat ergo Apostolus, damnationem horum falsorum doctorum otiari & eorum exitium dormitare, quia tempore divinitus constituto adeoque opinione citiùs eos opprimet. Beda in comm. refert ad initium poenarum in hac vita & aeternam carum durationem. Cùm, inquit, iam olim tempus praeteritum significet, non cessat autem verbum praesentis temporis sit, non aliud intelligendum videtur, nisi quia iam olim coepit iudicium perditionis impiorum, quod eos praesentialiter semper excruciat nullo unquam fine cessabit. Hugo & Glossa interlin. dicunt, de viventibus adhuc veram esse sententiam ob conscientiae remorsum, qui pars gehennae non nulla est.

## 2:3-5 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Whether by ἀπώλειαν in v. 3. the Devil can be understood? Hugo Cardinalis, the Ordinary Gloss, and Johannes Huss in his commentary on this place maintain this, since the Devil is the author of all perdition, who for that reason is called by the Hebrew name Ἀβαδδῶν, and the Greek Ἀπολλύων Apoc. 9. v. 11. Also Asmodeus Tob. 3. v. 8. from the root שמד he was lost, destroyed, devastated, and Judas is called son τῆς ἀπωλείας, of the Devil John 17. v. 12. Therefore, what is said of η απωλεια not to slumber, they accept in this way, that the Devil does not sleep nor slumber, because he is not pressed by the weight of flesh, and by his will, if not in reality, he always solicits us to sin and perdition. But this meaning of ἀπωλείας is foreign to this place and to the Scriptures, for son of perdition is not the son of the Devil, but a lost man devoted to destruction, that is, adjudged to damnation by the just judgment of GOD.

Q. 2. Whether by chains of darkness the pride of evil Angels is to be understood? Bede affirms this, for he comments thus on v. 4. The ropes of hell are the very boasting of pride, by which the Angels of that Spirit swelled against the creator, since ropes are called the cables by which sailors hang their sails, so that with a blowing breeze they leave the tranquility of the harbor and entrust themselves to the always ambiguous waves of the sea, to which ropes the efforts of unclean Spirits are fittingly compared, who, as soon as they were driven by the breath of pride and raised themselves against the creator, were snatched into the depths of the abyss by the very efforts of their own elation. He also says that some copies have roaring of hell, which adapts to the voice of either proud elation, or wailing in punishments. But the Greek σειραὶ in general signifies chains, and the Apostle is not dealing here with the fault, but with the punishment of evil Angels, as the whole context shows.

Q. 3. What is to be understood by τάρταρον, of which mention is made in the participle ταρταρώσας, and into which the fallen Angels are said to have been cast?

Resp. 1. Tertullian in Apologeticus ch. 22, Chrysostom in homily 11 on 1 Thessalonians, Jerome on ch. 6 of Ephesians, Augustine in q. 26 on Numbers, Theodoret in book 4 of Greek Affections, etc., understand by tartarus, in which evil Angels are held by chains of darkness, the dark and thick air, into which the Demons have been thrust as if into a prison and in which they are held until the day of judgment. Paterius explains the reason for the name in his Exposition of this Epistle, in the works of Gregory. The name of hell, he says, is attributed to this air, just as to the height of the heaven properly so called, just as the earth, which is lower, and the deep hell can be understood in relation to the height of this same air. 2. In order to establish this, they are moved by the Apostolic passage Eph. 6. vers. 12. Κοσμοκράτορες τοῦ σκότους αἰῶνος τούτου the rulers of the darkness of this world, upon which passage Nicolaus Fullerus comments thus in book 3 of his Miscellanea Sacra, chapter 14: By τὸ σκότος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου is understood this lowest globe, which mortals inhabit, this dark world, as the Syriac Interpreter translates by hypallage. Everything here is full of dense gloom, if they are compared with the most brilliant splendor of the starry heaven, which exposition seems to be able to be established from Ephes. 2. vers. 2. where the Devil is called ἄρχων τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἄερος. The evil Angels are also called Ephes. 6. vers. 12. τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρὶας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις in those things which are under heaven, i. e., in the air, as Jerome and Haymo explain. The Syriac rendered it, Evil spirits, which are under heaven. But because in the Greek there is not ὑπουρανίοις, but ἐπουρανίοις, from there some explain, in the sublime place of the air, which with respect to us is referred to ἐπουράνια . Jerome in chapter 6 of Ephesians: In heavenly places, not that demons dwell in heavenly places, but because the air above receives this name. Augustine in book 8 of De Civitate Dei, chapter 22: Devils dwell in this air, because having been cast down from the sublimity of the higher heaven by the merit of their unretractable transgression, they are condemned in this place suitable to them as if in a prison. Bede in his commentary on this place: The Angels received this hell, i. e., the lower dark air, as a prison penally. For as far as the sublimity of heaven is concerned, the space of this air can now be called hell. 3. We willingly concede that evil Angels dwell in the air, move and disturb the same, and produce meteors in it at an unusual time by the permission of GOD; but we deny that by tartarus and chains of darkness in this Petrine passage the air is understood. For firstly, by τάρταραν is nowhere signified air, but the lowest and most profound seat of the infernal regions, which in other places of Scripture is called abyss Luc. 8. vers. 31. Rom. 10. vers. 7. Apoc. 9. vers. 1. cap. 11. vers. 7. cap. 17. v. 8. cap. 20. v. 1. & 3. hence Lorinus writes on this place: the name of hell is taken for air too harshly and without another example. Compare Oecumenius on this passage. Secondly, in the parallel passage Iudae vers. 6. chains of darkness are called everlasting chains under darkness. But Demons are not in the air, but in hell with everlasting chains under darkness bound. Although indeed the Syrian there renders [באסוראלא ידיעא] unknown bonds or invisible, and Origen homily 9 on Matthew heavy bonds, nevertheless the Greek codices constantly read δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις, in which sense Cyril of Alexandria also interpreted that place in Habakkuk 3, no. 49, for whom the mist of darkness is reserved for all ages. Thirdly, the word ζόφου of mist, fits hell very well, which is a dark prison; this air is sometimes misty, but sometimes also serene.

Q. 4. What was the sin of the evil Angels? Resp. 1. Most of the Ancients assert that it was Pride. Methodius in Revelations Tom. 1. Orthodox p. 100. There was no one more worthy than Lucifer among the standing Angels. He, weighing the eminence of his Nature and the depth of his knowledge, grew proud against his creator to such an extent that he wished to make himself equal to GOD. Ambrose book 10. Epist. 84. Pride took its beginning from the Devil, who, because he was pleased with his own power and dignity which he had received from his creator, and compared himself to the glory of his author, was cast down from heavenly sublimity with those Angels whom he had drawn into the consent of his impiety. Compare Augustine book 12. de Civ. DEI chapter 1. book 11. de Genes. ad lit. chapter 13. Fulgentius book 1. ad Monimum page 38. Reuchlin in q. 10. Athanasius. Luther in comm. Gen. 1. Ludovicus Vives in book 12. of Augustine de Civ. DEI chapter 6. and 2. They prove this opinion from Job 41. verse 25.Isaiah 14. verse 12.Ezekiel 28 verse 12.Tobit 4. verse 14.Sirach 10. verse 14.Luke 10. verse 18.1. Timothy 3. verse 6.Apocalypse 12. verse 7.& from the ancient nature of the Devil. Because the Devil dislodged the first parents from the degree of their concreated happiness by breathing the poison of pride into them, so that they would dare to affect equality with GOD in wisdom, and even today he tries to instill pride into all of Adam's descendants, it is probably gathered from that, that he himself also fell from his happy state through pride. For he knows that GOD is perpetually like Himself and therefore will punish similar sins in a similar way. 3. Some judge that that pride of Lucifer and the evil Angels consisted in this, that they were too pleased with themselves in their beauty and excellence; others in this, that they did not want to depend on GOD, but to live for themselves and be sufficient for themselves; others in this, that they wanted to arrogate blessedness to themselves, and to attain it by their own powers, not by the powers of GOD; others in this, that they wished to be preferred to the other Angels, and to be subject to no one at all; others in this, that they sought the hypostatic union of the Word, so that it might be conferred upon one of the order of Angels, for instance Lucifer their Prince, not upon any man, for instance Christ. Suarez. lib. 6. de Angelis cap. 18. n. 13. Lorinus in h. l. 4. But indeed, since it cannot be proved directly and apodictically from the cited sayings of Scripture that pride was the sin of the evil Angels, therefore we embrace τὸ ἐπέχειν here, especially when it is asked specifically in what the formal object and proper reason of that pride consisted. Irenaeus lib. 2. cap. 49. Neither has any Scripture reported the cause of the angelic fall, nor does the Apostle say it, nor did the Lord teach it. The author of the book on the wonders of Scripture among the works of Augustine lib. 1. cap. 2. The true Physician did not wish to indicate how the angelic wound was made, while He did not intend to cure it afterwards, and He kept silent on how he was cast out by the sentence of vengeance, whom He in no way recalled through repentance. 5. Our Apostle, as also John 1. Epist. 3. v. 8. describe the angelic fall with the general word ἁμαρτάνειν, from which it is gathered that they had transgressed the law proposed to them by GOD the creator, because πᾶσα ἡ ἁμαρτία ἔστιν ἀνομία. Christ Ioh. 8. v. 44. says that he did not stand in the truth, where by truth is understood both true goodness, holiness, justice, and the concreated integrity of Nature, from which the love of truth arose; and also concreated happiness, for in both he did not stand, but fell from it into guilt and misery. Jude, in a place parallel to this one of ours, says concerning the Devils that they did not keep τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν but left their own οἰκητήριον: in which saying the fall of the Angels is described, first ἀποφατικῶς and negatively, that they did not keep their ἀρχὴν. By that some understand origin and principle, so that the sense is, they did not keep their original condition, their justice and concreated goodness; some the dignity of order, so that it is hinted that not a few even from the more excellent Angels apostatized, whence the Apostle establishes principalities and powers among the evil Angels, Eph. 6. v. 12. Oecumenius and others take it concerning the heavenly principality, looking back to which Luther translates, Sie haben ihre Fürstenthumb nicht behalten. There are indeed still ἀρχαὶ among the evil Angels Eph. 6. v. 12. but infernal, not heavenly; some simply explain it thus, they failed through pride from With the due subjection of their Prince, GOD. Secondly καταφατικῶς and affirmatively that they left their οἰκητήριον.. Some take that to mean the heavenly dwelling, in the sense that because of the crime of divine high treason they were forced to leave their original dwelling. But because the punishment for the fall is finally treated in the following words, it is therefore more correctly understood in this way, that since the heavenly armies had previously been placed by Jehovah Zebaoth in a certain station, they, having become deserters, abandoned it. οἰκητήριον could also be taken to mean GOD Himself, from whom they defected through sin. As God wished to dwell in them through grace and intimate presence: so they also ought to have dwelt in GOD through prompt and constant obedience. But they abandoned this οἰκητήριον, having been basely turned away from GOD the Creator.

Q. 5. Why did God not spare the sinning Angels, when nevertheless He spared men and provided for them a Redeemer? Resp. The pious ancients bring forward various reasons, but they are not of equal strength. 1. Because man sinned out of fragility and infirmity, the Devil out of malice. Iren. lib. 4. cap. 78. p. 313. Damascenus lib. 2. Orth. fid. cap. 3. Cassianus Collat. 4. cap. 3. says, The Angel sinned with full will on account of the highest perspicacity of his mind. 2. Because man sinned having been seduced and persuaded by another, but the Devil with no one instigating, but by his own will. Iren. lib. 3. cap. 33. p. 222. Gregorius lib. 4. moral. cap. 10. & lib. 9. cap. 36. Anselmus lib. 2. Cur Deus homo cap. 36. lib. 4. cap. 19. Bernhardus serm. 1. de Adventu. 3. Because in man sinning there was the substance of flesh, in the Angel a spiritual Nature. Gregorius lib. 4. moral. cap. 9. 4. Because in the fall of the Angels not the whole Angelic Nature perished, but with the first man sinning the whole human Nature perished. Therefore, so that the whole human race might not perish, divine mercy exhibited a remedy. Chrysost. homil. 1. de Adam & Eva, Augustinus or whoever else is the author in Enchir. c. 29. 5. Because all things were created for the sake of man, therefore God did not wish this work of His to be destroyed by the Devil. Theodoret. lib. 6. de div. provid. 6. Because if man were to perish entirely, for whose sake this visible world was created, it could not be repaired by another rational Nature, which perhaps, being inferior to the human, cannot be created, but man could fill the ruins of the Angels. Anselm. lib. 1. Cur Deus homo cap. 16. & 17. Alcuinus prooem. lib. 3. de Trinit. 7. Because it was less fitting that the destroyers of human Nature, out of the hatred with which they pursued God directly, to return into favor with Him, by which very thing, lest they should be too puffed up, it pleased Him that men be set free. Athanasius on the Incarnation. Leo sermon 2 on the Nativity 8. Some of the more recent ones add that by this reason more was bestowed upon human nature than upon angelic; because more angels were saved, lest they should fall, and fewer were permitted to fall; but of men more perish, fewer are saved. In this, however, human nature is honored above the angelic, that the Son of GOD did not take hold of angels but the seed of Abraham. Hebr. 2. v. 16. It is better to acknowledge with a grateful heart the φιλανθρωπίαν of GOD in the remedy provided for the human race, than to scrutinize the depth of divine judgments too curiously beyond the limits of the Word.

Q. 6. What is that righteousness of which Noah acted as a herald? Resp. 1. This is certain, that he did not preach civil or human righteousness, such as even outside the Church has a place among the saner Gentiles, since he was a Doctor of the Church in the signs, one from the number of the Patriarchs. 2. Some therefore take the name δικαιοσύνης of the righteousness of GOD, the avenger of human crimes, which Noah preached not only by words, but also by deed, namely by the very construction of the ark, because that construction of the ark was a public testimony that, on account of the exuberance of sins, a flood was impending over the world, in which all who had not entered the ark were to perish. To this can be accommodated what is said Hebr. 11. v. 7. concerning Noah, that not only through the preaching of repentance and the threatening of the encroaching flood, but also through the ark itself, that is, through the construction of the ark, he condemned the world; for by building the ark, in which he would be preserved with his house at the time of the flood, he showed that those threats would not be empty, and thus by the very deed or example he preached the righteousness of GOD, and condemned the impious and incredulous men. 3. Some take it of the righteousness of works, that he exhorted the antediluvian men that they should send a message to the sins in which they were securely indulging, and, having been converted to God, should pursue righteousness, in which part he shone before them by his own example, when it is said of him Gen. 6. vers. 9. that he was a just and perfect man in his generations and walked with GOD, that is, that he lived in the true fear of GOD, and led a holy life. Bede on this passage: He names Noah a herald of righteousness, because by doing the works of righteousness he showed to all who were looking on how one ought to live before GOD, etc. In the building of the ark, with his mouth indeed silent, but with the most prompt devotion of his heart, he obeyed the commands heavenly things. Josephus, book 1 of Antiquities, chapter 3: Noah, bearing the deeds of those (men of his own age, who neither paid the customary honors to GOD, nor observed human laws) with annoyance and indignation, urged them to change their mind and works for the better. But when he saw that they did not obey him, and were entirely succumbing to the sweetness of vices, fearing that they might kill him and his family, he withdrew and migrated with his own people into another region. 4. Although we do not entirely disapprove of the second and third opinion, for without a doubt Noah preached the divine justice as the avenger of crimes, and exhorted them to pursue the justice of works, nevertheless the discourse here is principally and chiefly about the justice of faith, as is evident from the parallel passage Heb. 11. verse 7. By faith Noah, having received an oracle concerning those things which were not yet seen, εὐλαβηθεὶς moved with godly fear, prepared an ark for the salvation of his house, by which he condemned the world, and became heir of the justice which is by faith, that is, he was justified before GOD by faith and constituted an heir of eternal life. From which we conclude thus. Of whatever justice Noah was constituted an heir, of that same justice he was also a herald. But the justice by faith is that justice of which Noah was constituted an heir. Therefore, he was also a herald of the justice by faith. Lorinus on this passage: That Noah preached about the coming of the Messiah, who κατ' ἐξοχὴν is called the Just, I easily believe. That the predecessors of Noah also did this, even from Adam, Irenaeus indicates book 2, chapter 9, and Athanasius in the Epistle that the Nicene Synod etc., and the Hebrews themselves in Reuchlin, book 1, of the Cabala.

For that reason, therefore, Noah was a herald of justice. 1. That he might seriously exhort men to perform repentance through the preaching of the law and the denunciation of the imminent flood, for without that, the justice of faith has no place. 2. That through the preaching of the promise concerning the Messiah he might inculcate the justice of faith, teaching that the justice which is valid before GOD must be sought solely in the promised Messiah, the crusher of the infernal serpent, and must be accepted by faith. He preached this justice of faith not only with words, but also by the very deed itself, because in the construction of the ark the mystery of Baptism and of preservation against the flood of divine wrath was prefigured through CHRIST, that true ark of salvation, to whom we can flee by true faith 1. Pet. 3. verse 20. and 21. 3. That he might teach that that faith through the study of good works is to be demonstrated, and consequently also that the righteousness of works is to be pursued. He likewise preached this righteousness of a good conscience not only by words, but also by the very deed, namely by the example of his obedience toward GOD, whence Hebr. 11. vers. 7. the honor and fear of GOD εὐλάβεια is attributed to him, because he did not treat the divine threats concerning the destruction of the human race by the flood with indifference, but, having complied with the divine command, he built an ark as a refuge against the waters of the flood.

Q. 7. Whether some from the number of those who perished in the waters of the flood were saved?

Q. 8. Whether all who were preserved in the ark were righteous? These two questions were dealt with in the exposition of Genesis.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. ChristIoh. 8. v. 44.speaks μοναδικῶς, The Devil did not stand in the truth. Peter in this place, as also Jude v. 6. speak πληθυντικῶς He did not spare the Angels who sinned.

Resp. The name Devil taken κυρίως is used concerning evil Angels 1. ἀτόμως for the Prince and head of evil Spirits,Matth. 25. v. 41.Apoc. 12. v. 9.whom they call Beelzebub or Lucifer. 2. συναγωγικῶς for the whole band of evil Angels, Luc. 8. v. 12.Act. 10. v. 38.Eph. 6. vers. 12. Whether the name of Devil is taken in the former or the latter way in the saying of Christ, it does not oppose our Apostolic passage. Scripture speaks of evil Angels in the singular number for this reason, because they constitute a certain society and kingdom under one head. Add that the name is singular in termination but plural in meaning. Others respond, the name of DevilIoh. 8. v. 44.is not taken exclusively but authoritatively, so that it signifies the Prince of Devils, and yet the remaining Devils are not excluded.

2. Peter concludes thus. GOD did not spare the Angels who sinned. Therefore He will not spare men who sin. But the sin of the Angels is greater than the sin of man.

Resp. John Huss in his commentary on this passage If sin is compared to sin, then the consequence is not valid, but if the Angelic Nature is compared to human Nature, then the consequence is perfectly valid, by saying thus: He does not spare the more worthy. Therefore He will not spare the less worthy.

3. The evil Angels are said to have been cast down into hell and bound in it with chains of darkness. But they wander about through the orb of the earthJob 1. v. 7.chap. 2. v. 2.they dwell in the air,Eph. 6. v. 12.

Resp. 1. After the fall they were indeed thrust into hell. Meanwhile, before the day of judgment, God permits them to go out onto the earth Rev. 9. v. 1.c. 12. v. 12. and to tempt men, and to vex the impious. 2. Some therefore bring this forward for the reconciliation of these sayings, that although many Demons dwell in the air, yet many also are detained in the prison of hell. 3. One must distinguish between the ordinary and extraordinary place of the Angels. The ordinary place of the evil Angels is hell, to which all were adjudged after the fall and into which they were cast. The extraordinary place before the day of judgment is the air, the sea, the earth, etc., where those evil Spirits dwell; and indeed they prefer to dwell in those places than in hell, because they propagate and extend their kingdom more in them. 4. Although those dwelling in the air are not ἐν τῷ ποῦ in hell, yet they are not entirely free from hellish torments, whence Bede on chapter 3 of James says, Demons, wherever they go, wherever they live, carry their hell with them (the name of hell being taken, to wit, for a state of misery.) Gloss. ordin. on chapter 3 of James. Just as Gehenna always burns: so the Devil, wherever he may be, whether in the air or under the earth, always carries with him the torments of his flames. Thomas explains the reason in p. 1. q. 64. art. 4. ad 3. on account of the troublesome apprehension of their being bound in a certain place, which the will flees and about which it grieves. Some, however, think that the real and true fire of hell is present to individual Demons in the air for their part. 5. Meanwhile, in ποῦ hell they seem to sustain greater torments, whence Luke 8. v. 31. they solicitously pray that it might not be commanded them to go into the abyss. Also on the day of judgment their torments will be increased more, whence Matt. 8. v. 29. they say to Christ: Have you come here to torment us before the time! For just as the punishments of the impious will receive the greatest increase in the reunion of souls with bodies; so also the torments of the Devils will be increased on the day of judgment, because then no exit will be open to them anymore from the hellish prison. Rev. 20. v. 10. & seqq. 6. That Jude calls those chains, by which evil Angels are bound and constricted under darkness, eternal, that can be understood of their perpetual anguish and horror, by which, like evildoers shut up in prison, they are constricted and await that horrible final judgment.

4. Peter calls the antediluvian world ancient. But the same world existed before the flood and after the flood. Resp. The world preceding the flood, by a comparison made to that in which we are, is called ἀρχαῖος, not as if God had founded a new universe of things; but because through the flood such a conversion and confusion of all things was made, that the restoration of the world following the flood is not undeservedly considered a certain new creation.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. The Apostolic prophecy concerning the avarice of false teachers, by which under the appearance of piety they are to fleece men of money, has been most clearly fulfilled in the Papacy. For whence come the public complaints of the whole Christian world concerning the Simony of the Roman Curia! Francesco Petrarca in his Dialogue on avoiding the Roman Curia writes, At Rome Simon Magus has revived with his spouse Simonia. In the book whose title is Onus Ecclesiae, such a complaint exists: Ambition and Simony now reign everywhere in the Clergy, so that today that of the Prophet is verified. From the least even to the greatest, namely all Clerics, they study avarice. Before the name of Luther was heard, the Italian Raphael Volaterranus wrote at Rome, Priesthoods are bestowed in place of a reward, and the spiritual treasure is held for gain and for trade. Matthew Paris in Henry 3 calls the Roman Pontiffs fishers not of men, but of coins; not of Christ, but of the treasury. Aeneas Sylvius Epist. 66 to Johannes Peregalius. The Roman Curia gives nothing without money, the very impositions of hands and the gifts of the Holy Spirit are sold, nor is the remission of sins bestowed, unless to the moneyed. What, moreover, are Indulgences other than nets for money? Hence Cajetan writes thus on this Petrine passage. Not far from these are the preachers of gain (of Indulgences) who abuse the devotion of the Christian people for gain, who dare to preach ignorantly or rashly that those paying a Carolinus or a ducat for a promulgated pecuniary Indulgence are in that state as if they had then been baptized, and similarly, that they free one soul from purgatory, for these are monsters and negotiations concerning the Christian people, the Christian religion knows not these figments. Claudius Espensaeus, Theologian of Paris, in his Epistle to Titus, Digression 2, p. 69. The Scholiast of the Rules of Innocent VIII now calls the Apostolic Chamber the mother of money, now acknowledges all things at Rome to be venal, now does not hide that many things are established and conceded for the sake of indirectly extorting money. p. 78 he adduces the saying of Volaterranus cited above. The penitentiary tax is a public instrument of Papal avarice. But also the Papal mass-priests sell Masses for a price;

The monks falsely claim that they can communicate their works of supererogation to others through the intervention of money, etc.

2. In v. 4. an evident testimony is held, that there are evil Angels, otherwise called Demons and Devils. This must be opposed to the Sadducees, the Dositheans, and the heretics of our age, the Anabaptists, the Libertines, and the David-Georgians.

3. The casting down of the Devils into hell and the eternal chains cast upon them must be opposed to Origen, who taught that Demons were at some time to be liberated and saved, book 1. περὶ ἀρχῶν chapter 6. Ambrosiaster in his commentary on Eph. 3 asserts, that some of the Demons were liberated by Paul from error, sin, and the tyranny of Lucifer. Against this, Augustine most truly in book 21 of The City of God, chapter 23, says: Let it be held fixed and immovable that the Devil and his angels will have no return to justice and the life of the saints, because the Scripture, which deceives no one, says that God did not spare them, and thus they were predamned by Him among the impious, so that they were thrust into the prisons of the darkness of hell to be kept and to be punished at the final judgment, when eternal fire will receive them, where they will be tormented for ever and ever.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lorinus on v. 3 annotates thus: It is sufficiently evident that avarice alone was the cause for Luther to depart from the Church and to forge heresy, because he saw himself deprived of the profit which he was taking from the promulgation of Indulgences, the duty of this matter having been transferred from his Augustinians to the Dominicans, by the will of the Archbishop of Mainz.

Response 1. Does such great avarice therefore fall even upon monks bound by a vow of poverty and having nothing of their own in the world, so that, driven by it, they even stir up heresies? 2. Are Papal Indulgences therefore traps for money and nets of avarice? 3. Other Papal writers explain the true cause for which Luther began to attack Indulgences, that it was the abuse of Papal Indulgences, the abuse of ecclesiastical power, and the corruptions of doctrine and morals which had publicly prevailed, etc., the testimonies of which have been brought forward in the Catholic Confession, book 1, part 1, chapter 7, etc. 4. Lorinus himself acknowledges this, who a little later on this very verse annotates thus: Rightly do Thomas the Angelic, Cajetan, and Catharinus here rebuke the Preachers, who are especially devoted to profit, as the Second says, undoubtedly encountering the origin of the Lutheran error, if they do this under the pretext of promulgated Indulgences. 3. Salmero in his enarrations on verse 4 disputes against certain Scholastics, who From these words of Peter, If He spared not the angels that sinned, they gather that the demons sinned in such a way at first, that GOD granted them no delay of time for repentance. He answers their argument, however, in this way: 1. That that phrase, GOD spared not the angels that sinned, proves rather the contrary, namely that He could have spared them and had a mind prepared to spare them, provided they had repented. They prove this from a comparison of the passage Job 9. v. 28. I feared all my works, knowing that Thou dost not spare the offender, where it is not signified that one who is actually offending incurs damnation, but that he immediately merits damnation by that act, unless he returns to GOD by way of repentance. 2. That Peter adds in the same place, And spared not the original world. Likewise, He reduced the cities of the Sodomites and Gomorrahites to ashes. Therefore, just as He did not immediately cast the pre-diluvian men and the citizens of Sodom into hell when they sinned, but granted them a time of repentance: so also He granted the fallen angels time and place to repent, if they wished. 3. If GOD had not given them a space to repent, He would have dealt with them more out of the rigor of justice than out of kindness and long-suffering. But they prove the contrary by the benefits with which He heaped them in their first creation, when He adorned them with excellent and supernatural gifts. 4. He brings forward certain revelations. 5. Sayings of the Fathers, Cyril of Jerusalem, Catech. 9. Illum. Gregory of Nyssa, book 1, Philos. chap. 3. Basil on chap. 14 of Isaiah. Jerome on chap. 1 of Ephesians. 6. He reduces this opinion to an absurdity. If immediately, as the angel sinned, he fell, and the fall was for him what death is for us, it will follow that no angel would have been damned except for one sin only, when nevertheless man can perform repentance and find mercy after myriads of sins; it will follow, moreover, that there were many men who sinned more gravely than the angels in heaven. If, therefore, He did not deny a time of repentance to men, would He not much less grant indulgence to the angels, who sinned less? 7. The sin of the angel does not seem to have made his will inflexible and immutable, from the fact that he sees all things without discursive reasoning, both the principles and the conclusions which arise from them, and as they say, he adheres to whatever thing, and adheres immovably. For it could be objected, because we also see first principles and the conclusions necessarily deduced from them, and yet our will is not immutable, to which self-love or φιλαυτία is always present, which can bend the will toward some evil appearing under the guise of the honorable. Cornelius à Lapide comments on this verse thus. Some Doctors think that the demons, as soon as they fell, are in sin, to have been at the end of their way, and therefore not to have been able to rise again through repentance. We, concerning this question: 1. We use the statement of Augustine, book 1, de peccat. merit. & remiss., last chapter: Where a most obscure matter is disputed, without the help of certain and clear documents of the divine Scriptures, human presumption ought to restrain itself, affirming nothing rashly in this or that direction. 2. Salmeron himself is compelled in a certain way to admit this, whence to the question, If the Angels could have done penance for their sin, why among so many myriads of Angels who fell, did none repent? he answers, that this is a great mystery of divine wisdom, nor can we render a reason for everything. And afterwards he adds: It seems difficult to define any certain opinion about these things. 3. If a time of repentance had been given to them, a Redeemer would also have been given to them. But Salmeron himself fears to affirm that Christ was given to the Angels as Mediator and Redeemer. If a few, he says, some from the evil Angels had existed, thus saved, I would say, there would have been no need for Christ to be the Redeemer of the Angels through his blood just as of men. 4. Damascenus, book 2, Orth. fid., chapter 3, discourses thus: An Angel is ἀνεπίδεκτος μετανοίας, ὅτι καὶ ἀσώματος, ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τήν τοῦ σώματος ἀσθένειαν τῆς μετανοίας ἔτυχε; chapter 4: ὅπερ ἔστι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ὁ θάνατος, τοῦτο τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις ἡ ἔκπτωσις μετὰ γὰρ τὴν ἔκπτωσιν οὐκ ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς μετάνοια, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ ἀνθρώποις μετὰ τὸν θάνατον. 5. Salmeron, equally with all the Jesuits, swore by the words of Thomas. But he, p. 1, q. 64, art. 2, disputes: the very Nature of the Angelic will is so constituted, that what it has once chosen with full deliberation, it can no longer turn away from, nor choose that which it has once turned away from. 6. Lorinus on this place annotates thus: Although to Scotus, 2, dist. 6, q. 2, to Gabriel ibid., q. 1, art. 2, and to Salmeron it seems that the Angels could have, if they wished, repented, nevertheless many deny this, using that from Damascenus and Nyssenus or Nemesius, 1, Phil., chapter 2: What death is to men, this the fall is to Angels, after which there is no place for repentance, just as there is not for man after death. In the same opinion besides these two Fathers is Cassianus, collat. 4, chapter 13 and 14, the Author de mirabilib. Scripturae, book 1, chapter 2, Gregory, book 2, moral., chapter 3, al. 4, Isidorus, book 1, de summo bono, chapter 12, sent. 11, Fulgentius, de fide, chapter 3, Prosper, book de dimid. temp., chapter 2, and 1, de vita contempl., chapter 3. Some bring forward the reason, because GOD confers the first grace solely by the merit of Christ to his enemies, but he did not wish to for the Angels, as to give a Redeemer to men, etc. And afterwards: That which Salmeron says, that from these words, he did not spare, it could be gathered that God spares, I concede, yet not that He had a mind prepared for sparing. Nor indeed does the other passage Job 9. v. 28. I feared all my works, knowing that you would not spare the offender, denote only that one deserves damnation, and that it must be incurred, unless the sinner returns to God by way of penance, but the sense is, where God has determined to punish, there is no one who can pray away the punishment or resist, according to that 1. Sam. 15. v. 29. The Triumpher in Israel will not spare, and will not be moved by repentance. Nor does the argument hold either from other examples of the flood and the Pentapolis, which are here subjoined, or from the commendation of divine mercy, or from I know not what divine revelation, (these are Salmeron's arguments) For the revelation is uncertain, why grace to repent was offered not to Angels, but to men. I also see no inconvenience in conceding that some Angels were damned for fewer and lesser sins than men, although to the latter, not to the former, was given the faculty of repenting. Nyssenus or Nemesius is said to assert this in vain (citing Salmeron) since he openly compares the fall of the Angels into sin with the death of men. Neither in Basil, nor in Jerome do I read what hinders our opinion, and it is certain that Jerome often speaks according to the opinion of others. All these things Lorinus, refuting Salmeron professedly.

3. The same Lorinus at this place from the word ταρταρώσας gathers, that there will be future vicissitudes of extreme cold and extreme heat in hell, since ταρταρίζειν is to freeze with a hellish cold. Resp. what is to be determined concerning this matter was set forth in the tract on Hell §. 71. Abulensis q. 558. on Matthew. Dominicus a Soto 4. dist. 50. q. un. art. 4. deny that there is cold among the infernal regions.

4. Cornelius a Lapide at the same verse annotates thus. Many heresiarchs have had demons as companions and familiars. Luther in his book on the private Mass and to the Elector of Saxony confesses that he had consumed more than a bushel of salt with the Devil, and had received from him arguments by which he might attack the Mass. These, like many other things, Cornelius a Lapide transcribed from Lorinus in his commentary on verse 15, where he inculcates the same in as many words. Resp. 1. Luther does not speak of a familiar and friendly association with a Demon, but of the daily stake of Diabolical temptations fixed in his flesh. 2. Cor. 12. v. 7. 2. Nor did Luther first learn from Satan the arguments by which solitary Masses were to be attacked, but he noticed their strength in the interior temptation of the Devil.

5. Gagnaeus in his exposition of v. 5 brings forward two things, both of which are unworthy of assent. First he says, that the vulgate interpreter perhaps read ἀρχικὸν primogenium, when he rendered it, Original.
