Secondly he says, that it seems to him, that ἀρχαῖος in this place does not signify so much ancient, as rude and unskilled, so that the sense is. If God did not spare that age, still rude and unskilled, and almost ignorant of divine things, what is He going to do to false Teachers, who have turned aside from the way of the truth that was understood. Concerning this opinion of Gagnaeus, Lorinus on this verse discourses thus. Salmeron and Fevardentius approve of this; I by no means, since the received and customary notion of ἀρχαίου is prior for ancient, old, aged, pristine, and that more often than for rude or foolish and inept, which τὸ ἀρχαϊκὸν. also signifies. Read Budaeus in his commentaries on the Greek language and the Author of the Thesaurus (Henricus Stephanus) who τὸ ἀρχικὸν explain it as desirous of commanding, imperious. Certainly I do not find it for ancient. And afterwards, The interpreter renders the same word ἀρχαίου in Latin as ancient in many places of the N. T.Matt. 5. v. 21.27.33.Luke 9. v. 8.Acts 15. v. 7.21.chap. 21. v. 16.Apoc. 12. v. 9.chap. 20. v. 2.to omit Old. And he very wisely placed the epithet of original in this place, to designate the men of the first age, which they reckon from the transgression of the parents up to the time of the flood.

6. Iodocus Coccius in Vol. 1 of the Thesaurus, book 7, art. 3, p. 796, attempts to demonstrate from this Apostolic passage, that from the foundation of the world up to the present time there has always been one President and Monarch of the Church in a perpetual succession. In a primacy and Monarchy of this kind, he says, Noah obtained the eighth place, who after the death of his grandfather Methuselah lived, and alone presided over the Church for 350. years, whence 2. Pet. 2. he is called the eighth preacher of righteousness. To our exposition, that Noah is said to have been saved as the eighth, that is, with seven others, he opposes this. If this Scripture were to be understood in such a way, for what reason is he called the eighth and not the first? For Noah was the first to enter the ark, the first to go out of it, he was first in age, first in dignity; among those eight souls Ham was impious, such an encomium cannot be attributed to four wives.

Resp. 1. We have proven above from the phrase customary to the Greeks and from a comparison of the parallel passage 1. Pet. 3. verse 20, our exposition that Noah is said to have been saved as the eighth, because he was saved in the ark with seven others. 2. Lyranus, Ambrose, Catharinus, Cajetan, Gagnaeus, Guillandus, Lorinus, Salmero, Saa, and many other Papists follow the same. Estius in his commentary writes thus concerning it. He calls him the eighth not from Adam, from whom he is found to be the tenth, but because only eight souls were preserved, in which number was Noah, and indeed as a head, who is therefore called the eighth, in a manner of speaking also common in everyday usage. Cornelius à Lapide on this passage: Noah is called the eighth, namely of those who were saved through the ark, for Peter alludes to that which he said Epist. 1. cap. 3. v. 20. Eight souls were saved through water. Others from Josephus book 1. Antiq. ch. 4. & 5. judge that Noah was the eighth herald of righteousness, because he followed seven generations, in which the descendants of Seth cultivated righteousness and holiness. Others judge him to be called the eighth, because he was born in the eight-hundredth year (not from the creation of the world, for he was born from it in the year 1056, but) from the beginning of the impiety and corruption of the world, which had lasted before Noah for seven hundred years. Others invent seven other heralds of righteousness in that age, whom Scripture might express, of whom Noah was the eighth. But the first sense is genuine. 3. It is objected in vain to this exposition that the seven remaining souls saved in the ark were not heralds of righteousness, because the little word ὄγδοον is not to be joined with the noun κύρηκα but with the verb ἐφύλαξε. 4. Let us grant that Noah was the chief Doctor of the Church placed over all the rest, can it be inferred immediately from that that he was the Monarch of the Church? One is a primacy of order and dignity, another of Monarchical power. 5. To whom also will Coccius be able to persuade that a herald of righteousness is the same as a Monarch of the Church? and likewise that in so many centuries from the beginning of the world up to the flood there were only eight heralds of righteousness? Let him acknowledge, therefore, that the little word ὄγδοον ought not to be joined with the noun κήρυκα. 6. And even if it were granted in the highest degree that Noah was the Monarch of the Church and indeed by right of succession, must the same immediately obtain in the N. T.? Let the Sacerdotal succession be brought back, therefore, let the sacrifices from animals be brought back, let the Levitical Ceremonies and all Mosaic laws be brought back.

7. Lorinus on these words annotates thus: Rightly does Andradius refute Chemnitz (Payva) book 2. for the Council of Trent, inventing I know not what revelations in Noah concerning a fuller declaration of heavenly doctrine, and for that reason called a herald of righteousness by Peter, when the true knowledge of heavenly things had already perished entirely and the force of traditions was not sufficient, for the History of Genesis narrates nothing of the sort, nor does Peter hint at it here.

Resp. The words of Chemnitz have it thus in Exam. Conc. Trident. part. 1. on Sacred Scripture p. 13. After the death of Adam not only the posterity of Cain, but also the sons of Elohim, who had received the traditions of heavenly doctrine, They corrupted their ways, in which corruption there was without doubt the principal adulteration of the word of GOD. For thus God says: My Spirit shall not strive in man forever. And He adds the cause, because they are flesh and the imagination of the human heart is evil. Therefore, the heavenly doctrine in the original world was handed down as if by hand by living voice without writing: but because the imagination of the human heart is evil, the purity of the word was at length not faithfully preserved through the traditions of the living voice, but corrupted and adulterated, nay, at length plainly lost, etc. But there, by peculiar revelations to Noah, added to the stupendous miracles in the flood, God restored the collapsed purity of doctrine, preserved it, and added a fuller declaration of it both before and after the flood; And He confirmed Noah by those miracles as a herald of Righteousness, so that he might be the guardian of the purity of doctrine, and hand it down by living voice by hand to posterity. These things D. Chemnitius, in which not even Momus himself would have found anything to criticize.

Observations. 1. Let the Ministers of the Churches learn that both any vices whatsoever, and especially avarice, ought to be banished from them. Luke 12. v. 15.1. Thessal. 2. v. 5. & 6.Acts 20. v. 33.2. Cor. 4. v. 2. Bonaventura in chapter 12 of Luke. A preacher of truth above all things ought to avoid the vice of greed, otherwise he will not be a preacher of truth, but a flatterer. Indeed whoever is eager for avarice or popular applause, never teaches about piety with fruit, which is a distich of Fabricius. Concerning heretics, Jerome says in book 3 on Zechariah, chapter 14, that they do all things for the sake of gain and glory; on the contrary, however, Chrysostom pronounces concerning the Apostles in homily 47 on Matthew, that a true and unfeigned contempt for glory and money rendered the Apostles great and effective persuaders.

2. Just as Peter pronounces concerning heretics in this place, that they trade with their hearers with feigned words, like merchants who entice buyers with smooth speech so that they may sell their wares more dearly: so Paul pronounces concerning them 2. Cor. 2. v. 17. that they peddle the word of GOD. In Greek it is καπηλεύειν, which is proper to those who sell food or drink, whose main concern is accustomed to be to sell spoiled things for sincere ones, to adulterate wine with the pouring in of water, Isaiah 1. v. 22. Chrysostom in 2. Cor. 2. This is to peddle, when someone (for the sake of capturing gain) adulterates wine; when someone sells water or other such things for money, which he ought to give for free.

3. This very metaphorical formula of speaking used concerning false Doctors hints that the care of souls is in itself and by itself a kind of the most honorable ἐμπορίας or most excellent business, through which souls are gained for Christ, Luc. 19. v. 13. πραγματεύσασθε, Trade until I come.

4. Just as God does not delay the promise, 2. Petr. 3. v. 9. so also He does not delay the threat, although He may sometimes seem to defer the fulfillment of both His promises and His threats.

5. Augustine, On the Nature of the Good against the Manichaeans, chapter 33, rightly gathers from this passage that the evil angels were not created evil by GOD, but were made evil by sinning. Bede in his commentary on this passage: In that which the Apostle says, that God did not spare the sinning angels, it is to be noted that those evil angels were not created evil by GOD, but were made evil by sinning. They are not evil by nature, but by choice and their own sin, as defined in the Council of Carthage 4, chapter 1, and the Council of Braga, chapter 7.

6. Fulgentius, On Faith, chapter 3, concludes beautifully thus: Without grace a man cannot repent, because the evil angel could have done so much more, whose nature, the less it is burdened by the weight of an earthly body, the more it would have been endowed with this faculty.

7. The same Fulgentius, book 2 to Trasimundus, chapter 2, concludes from the fall of the angels: The angelic nature was not suitable for repairing the human, since that nature testifies by the evidence of its own consubstantial ruin that it is in need of help.

8. The chains by which evil angels are held bound after the fall signify: 1. that they are restrained by divine power, so that they cannot harm men without the permission of God. 2. that they have fallen from a state of happiness into extreme misery, and from created liberty into servitude.

9. Those chains are called chains of darkness: 1. because by the divine will and power they are held captive and bound under darkness, that is, in hell, so that they cannot leave it without the permission of God. The bonds of darkness are dark bonds, that is, the bonds of hell, in which there is perpetual darkness. 2. because they are deprived of all consolation, joy, and hope of liberation, whence Jude says, that they are reserved in eternal chains under darkness. Augustine, book 21, On the City of GOD, chapter 23: Let it be held fixed and immovable that the Devil and his angels will have no return to justice and the life of the saints, because Scripture, which deceives no one, says of them that God did not spare, etc. The entire passage ἐλέγχῳ 3 was cited above.

10. On the day of judgment, not only impious men, but also evil Angels will hear the sentence of condemnation, their wickedness being manifested before the blessed Angels and men, their power being utterly trampled upon, and their pride being publicly mocked.

11. Augustine, tract. 95 in John. Let not the hard pride of mortals think that it is spared; it must be terrified by the punishment of the Angels. If GOD so turns away from the uncleanness of sin, that those golden vessels of the Angelic Nature, adorned with the most precious gems of most brilliant gifts, for the very reason that He saw they had contracted the uncleanness and rust of pride, He crushed with the eternal sentence of condemnation as with an iron rod and cast into the dunghill of hell forever; what do you believe will become of man, who is a vessel of clay and earth, when he has been defiled by the uncleanness and filth of sins?

12. The flood is a public and evident testimony concerning the truth of divine threats; concerning the severity of divine wrath against sins; concerning the power and majesty of GOD, by which He can arm all Elements and all creatures against the impious; concerning the kindness of GOD toward the pious, by which He can miraculously preserve them in a public πανολεθρίᾳ.

13. The ministry of Noah and other faithful Doctors of the Church is a public proclamation of righteousness.

14. Bede in comm. on this passage weaves such an allegory. For this reason he makes mention of the number eight, so that he may secretly insinuate that the time of the flood signifies the crisis of the final examination, when, with all the reprobate condemned, all the just will receive the glory of perpetual life. For there are six ages of the present world: the seventh age is even now being spent in that life where the souls of the saints enjoy the happy Sabbath, that is, eternal rest; the eighth is to come at the time of the resurrection of all and the Universal judgment.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. An perἀπώλειανin v. 3. possit intelligi Diabolus? Ita statuunt Hugo Cardin. Gloss. ordinaria, Iohannes Huss in comm. h. l. cùm Diabolus sit omnis perditionis autor, qui propterea vocatur Hebraico nomine Ἀβαδδῶν, Graeco ἈπολλύωνApoc. 9. v. 11. Item Asmodaeus Tob. 3. v. 8. â rad. שמדperditus, destructus, devastatus fuit, ac Iudas vocatur filiusτῆς ἀπωλείας,DiaboliIohann. 17. v. 12. Quod ergo η απωλεια dicitur non dormitare, illud sic accipiunt, quòd Diabolus non dormiat neque dormitet, quia mole carnis non premitur, ac voluntate si minùs reipsâ, semper nos solicitat ad peccatum & perditionem. Sed haec significatio ἀπωλείας ab hoc loco & â Scripturis est aliena, filius enim perditionis non est filius Diaboli, sed homo perditus & exitio devotus h. e. iusto DEI iudicio damnationi adiudicatus.

Q. 2. An per catenas caliginis intelligatur malorum Angelorum superbia? Affirmat Beda, sic enim ad v. 4. commentatur. Rudentes inferni sunt ipsa superbiae iactantia, quâ Angeli eius Spiritus contra conditorem intumuit, cum rudentes dicantur funes, quibus nautae vela suspendunt, ut flante aurà portûs tranquillitatem relinquant, seseque ambiguis semper ponti fluctibus credant, quibus convenienter rudentibus immundorum Spirituum conamina comparantur, qui mox, ut flatu superbiae impulsi, se adversus conditorem erexerunt, ipsis elationis suae conatibus in abyssi profunda sunt rapti. Dicit etiam, quaedam exemplaria habere rugientibus inferni, quod ad vocem vel superbae elationis, vel eiulatus in poenis accommodat. Sed Graecum σειραὶ in genere significat catenas, nec de culpa, sed de poena malorum Angelorum Apostolus hoc loco agit, ut totus contextus ostendit.

Q. 3. Quid perτάρταρον,cuius mentio fit in participioταρταρώσας,& in quem Angeli lapsi dicuntur proiecti, sit intelligendum?

Resp. 1. Tertullianus in Apologet. cap. 22. Chrysostomus homil. 11. in 1. ad Thessal. Hieronymus in cap. 6. Ephes. Augustinus q. 26. in Num. Theodoretus lib. 4. Graecar. affection. &c. per tartarum, in quo mali Angeli catenis caliginis detinentur, intelligunt aërem caligino sum & crassum, in quem velut in carcerem detrusi sint Daemones & in quo detineantur usque ad diem iudicii. Rationem appellationis explicat Paterius in Exposit huius Epist. apud Gregorium. Tribuitur, inquit, nomen inferni aëri huic, quemadmodum ad celsitudinem propriè dicti caeli, sicut quemadmodum ad eiusdem aëris altitudinem terra, quae inferius est, intelligi & infernus profundus potest. 2. Ut sic statuant, moventur loco Apostolico Eph. 6. vers. 12.Κοσμοκράτορες τοῦ σκότους αἰῶνος τούτουrectores tenebrarum huius seculi, in quem locum sic commentatur Nicol. Fullerus lib. 3. Miscell. sacror. cap. 14. Perτὸ σκότος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτουintelligitur globus hic infimus, quem mortales incolunt, tenebrosus hic mundus, ut per hypallagen vertit Syrus Interpres. Densae caliginis hîc plena sunt omnia, si conferantur cum clarissimo caeli stelliferi fulgore, quae expositio stabiliri posse videtur exEphes. 2. vers. 2.ubi Diabolus vocaturἄρχων τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἄερος. Vocantur etiam Angeli mali Ephes. 6. vers. 12.τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρὶας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοιςin illis quae sub caelo i. e. in aëre, ut exponunt Hieronymus & Haymo. Syrus reddidit, Spiritus mali, qui sunt sub caelo. Quia verò in Graeco non est ὑπουρανίοις, sed ἐπουρανίοις, inde quidam explicant, in sublimi scilicet aëris loco, qui respectu nostri adἐπουράνιαrefertur. Hieronymus in cap. 6. Eph. In caelestibus, non quòd daemones in caelestibus commorentur, sed quod supranos aër hoc nomen accipit. Augustinus lib. 8. de civ. DEI cap. 22. Diaboli in hoc aëre habitant, quia de caeli superioris sublimitate deiecti merito irregressibilis transgressionis in hoc sibi congruo velut carcere praedamnantur. Beda in comm. h. l. Angeli poenaliter hunc infernum i. e. inferiorem caliginosum aërem, tanquam carcerem acceperunt. Quantum enim ad sublimitatem caeli iam huius aëris spacium dici infernus potest. 3. Nos libenter concedimus, Angelos malos in aëre versari, eundem movere ac turbare, inque eo meteora inusitato tempore DEI permissione producere; sed negamus, per tartarum & catenas caliginis in hoc loco Petrino intelligi aërem. Nam primò per τάρταραν nuspiam aër, sed ima & profundissima inferorum sedes significatur, quae in aliis Scripturae locis vocatur abyssusLuc. 8. vers. 31.Rom. 10. vers. 7.Apoc. 9. vers. 1.cap. 11. vers. 7.cap. 17. v. 8.cap. 20. v. 1. & 3. inde Lorinus in h. l. scribit: nomen inferni pro aëre duriùs accipitur & sine alio exemplo. Confer Oecumenium in hunc locum. Secundò, in loco parallelo Iudae vers. 6.catenae caliginis dicuntur vincula aeterna sub caligine. At Daemones non sunt in aëre, sed in inferno vinculis aeternis sub caligine constricti. Quamvis verò Syrus ibi reddat [באסוראלא ידיעא]vinculis incognitis seu invisibilibus, & Origenes homil. 9. in Matth. vinculis gravibus, tamen Graeci Codd. constanter legunt δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις, quo sensu etiam locum illum interpretatus est Cyrillus Alexandrinus in Habac. 3. n. 49. quibus caligo tenebrarum in omnia secula est reservata. Tertiò, vox ζόφουcaliginis, optimè congruit inferno, qui est tenebricosus carcer, hic aër quandoque caliginosus est, quandoque verò etiam serenus.

Q. 4. Quodnam fuerit malorum Angelorum peccatum? Resp. 1. Plerique ex Veteribus Superbiam fuisse asserunt. Methodius in Revelat. Tom. 1. Orthodox p. 100. Lucifero non fuit dignior inter stantes Angelos. Is eminentiam suae Naturae & profunditatem suae scientiae perpendens in suum creatorem superbivit in tantum, quod DEO se aequare voluit. Ambrosius lib. 10. Epist. 84. Superbia â Diabolo sumsit exordium, qui quoniam suâ, quam â creatore acceperat, potentiâ & dignitate sibi placuit, seque autoris sui gloriae comparavit, cum iis Angelis, quos in consensum impietatis suae traxerat, â caelesti sublimitate deiectus est. Confer August. lib. 12. de Civ. DEI cap. 1. lib. 11. de Genes. ad lit. cap. 13. Fulgentium lib. 1. ad Monimum pag. 38. Reuchlinum in q. 10. Athanasii. Lutherum in comm. Gen. 1. Ludovicum Vivem in lib. 12. Augustini de Civ. DEI cap. 6. &. 2. Hanc sententiam probant ex Iob. 41. vers. 25.Esai. 14. vers. 12.Ezech. 28 vers. 12.Tob. 4. vers. 14.Sirach. 10. vers. 14.Luc. 10. vers. 18.1. Timoth. 3. vers. 6.Apocal. 12. vers. 7.& ex antique Diaboli ingenio. Quia Diabolus primos parentes ex concreatae felicitatis gradu deturbavit, venenum superbiae illis afflando, ut aequalitatem cum DEO in sapientia affectare auderent, & adhuc hodie omnibus Adae posteris superbiam instillare conatur, ex eo probabiliter colligitur, etiam ipsum per superbiam è felici suo statu decidisse. Scit enim, DEUM sui perpetuò esse similem ac proinde similia peccata similiter puniturum. 3. Superbiam illam Luciferi ac malorum Angelorum quidam in eo sitam fuisse censent, quòd sibi in sua pulchritudine & excellentia nimis placuerint; alii in eo, quòd noluerint pendere â DEO, sed sibi vivere & sufficere; alii in eo, quòd voluerint beatitudinem sibi arrogare, suisque eam, non DEI viribus assequi; alii in eo, quòd voluerint coeteris Angelis praeferri, & nulli omninò subesse; alii in eo, quòd ambiverint unionem hypostaticam Verbi, ut illa uni ex Angelorum ordine, puta Lucifero suo Principi conferretur, non homini alicui, puta Christo. Suarez. lib. 6. de Angelis cap. 18. n. 13. Lorinus in h. l. 4. Sed enim cùm ex allatis Scripturae dictis directè & apodicticè probari nequeat, superbiam fuisse malorum Angelorum peccatum, ideo τὸ ἐπέχειν hîc amplectimur, praesertim quando in specie quaeritur, in quo formale obiectum & propria ratio illius superbiae constiterit. Irenaeus lib. 2. cap. 49. Causam lapsus Angelici neque Scriptura aliqua retulit, neque Apostolus dicit, nec Dominus docuit. Autor libri de mirabil. Scripturae apud Augustinum lib. 1. cap. 2. Angelicum vulnus verus Medicus qualiter factum sit, indicare noluit, dum illud postea curare non destinavit & qualiter sit eiectus per sententiam vindictae, reticuit, quem per paenitentiam nullo modo revocavit. 5. Apostolus noster, uti etiam Iohannes 1. Epist. 3. v. 8. generali verbo ἁμαρτάνειν lapsum Angelicum describunt, ex quo colligitur, quòd legem â DEO creatore sibi propositam fuerint transgressi, quia πᾶσα ἡ ἁμαρτία ἔστιν ἀνομία. Christus Ioh. 8. v. 44. dicit, quòd non steterit in veritate, ubi per veritatem intelligitur tum vera bonitas, sanctitas, iustitia ac concreata Naturae integritas, ex qua veritatis amor exortus; tum felicitas concreata, in utraque enim non stetit, sed ab ea in culpam & miseriam prolapsus est. Iudas in loco huic nostro parallelo de Diabolis dicit, quod non servaverintτὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴνsed reliquerint suumοἰκητήριον: in quo dicto describitur lapsus Angelorum, primò ἀποφατικῶς ac negativè, quòd non servaverint suam ἀρχὴν. Per illam quidam intelligunt originem ac principium, ut sit sensus, non servaverunt originalem suam conditionem, suam iustitiam & bonitatem concreatam; quidam dignitatem ordinis, ut innuatur, ex praestantioribus quoque Angelis non paucos apostatasse, unde Apostolus inter malos Angelos statuit principatus & potestates,Eph. 6. v. 12. Oecumenius & alii accipiunt de principatu caelesti, quò respiciens Lutherus vertit, Sie haben ihre Fürstenthumb nicht behalten. Sunt quidem adhuc inter Angelos malos ἀρχαὶEph. 6. v. 12. sed infernales, non caelestes; quidam simpliciter sic exponunt, defecerunt per superbiam â Principis sui DEI debitâ subiectione. Secundò καταφατικῶς & affirmativè quòd reliquerint suum οἰκητήριον. Quidam illud accipiunt de domicilio caelesti, sensu eo, quòd ob crimen laesae maiestatis divinae pristinum suum domicilium relinquere fuerint coacti. Sed quia de poena lapsus in verbis seqq. demùm agitur, ideò rectiùs accipitur hoc modo, quod cùm priùs fuerint exercitus caelestes â Iehovah Zebaoth in certa statione collocati, transfugae facti illam deserverint. Posset etiam οἰκητήριον accipi de DEO ipso, â quo per peccatum defecerunt. Ut Deus in ipsis voluit habitare per gratiam & intimam praesentiam: sic debebant etiam ipsi in DEO habitare per promtam & constantem oboedientiam. Sed hoc οἰκητήριον deserverunt, â DEO creatore turpiter aversi.

Q. 5. Quare Deus Angelis peccantibus non pepercerit, cùm tamen hominibus pepercerit ac de Redemtore illis prospexerit? Resp. pii veteres varias afferunt rationes, sed quae non sunt aequalis roboris. 1. quia homo peccavit ex fragilitate & infirmitate, Diabolus ex malitia. Iren. lib. 4. cap. 78. p. 313. Damascenus lib. 2. Orth. fid. cap. 3. Cassianus Collat. 4. cap. 3. dicit, Angelus ob summam mentis perspicacitatem plenâ voluntate peccavit. 2. quia homo ab alio seductus & persuasus peccavit, Diabolus verò nullo instigante, sed propriâ voluntate. Iren. lib. 3. cap. 33. p. 222. Gregorius lib. 4. moral. cap. 10. & lib. 9. cap. 36. Anselmus lib. 2. Cur Deus homo cap. 36. lib. 4. cap. 19. Bernhardus serm. 1. de Adventu. 3. Quia in homine peccante erat carnis substantia, in Angelo spiritualis Natura. Gregorius lib. 4. moral. cap. 9. 4. Quia in Angelorum lapsus non tota Angelica Natura periit, at primo homine peccante tota Natura humana periit. Ne ergo totum genus humanum perir et, divina misericordia remedium exhibuit. Chrysost. homil. 1. de Adam & Eva, Augustinus vel quicunque alius autor in Enchir. c. 29. 5. Quia omnia propter hominem condita, ideò noluit Deus hoc opificium suum â Diabolo destrui. Theodoret. lib. 6. de div. provid. 6. Quia si homo penitus interiret, propter quem hic aspectabilis mundus conditus est, non posset reparari per aliam Naturam rationalem, quae fortassis inferior quàm humana, condi nequit, potuit verò ruinas Angelorum homo replere. Anselm. lib. 1. Cur Deus homo cap. 16. & 17. Alcuinus prooem. lib. 3. de Trinit. 7. Quia minùs decuit, destructores humanae Naturae ex directo, quo Deum prosequebantur, odio in gratiam redire cum ipso, quâ ipsâ de re ne se nimium efferrent, placuit homines liberari. Athanasius de in carnat. Leo serm. 2. de nativ. 8. Quidam ex recentioribus addunt, quòd hac ratione plus praestitum humanae Naturae quàm Angelicae; quia plures Angeli servati sunt, ne caderent, pauciores cadere permissi sunt; homines vero plures pereunt, pauciores salvantur. In eo tamen Natura humana prae Angelica honorato, quòd Filius DEI non Angelos sed semen Abrahae assumserit.Hebr. 2. v. 16. Praestat, grato corde DEI φιλανθρωπίαν in remedio generi humano praestito agnoscere, quàm profunditatem divinorum iudiciorum curiosiùs extraverbi limites scrutari.

Q. 6. Quaenam sit illa iustitia, cuius praeconem egit Noahus? Resp. 1. Certum hoc est, non civilem aut humanam iustitiam ipsum praedicasse, qualis etiam extra Ecclesiam apud saniores gentiles locum habet, cùm fuerit in signis Ecclesiae Doctor, unus ex numero Patriarcharum. 2. Quidam ergò nomen δικαιοσύνης accipiunt de iustitia DEI, scelerum humanorum vindice, quam non solum verbis, sed etiam facto, videlicet ipsâ extructione arcae Noahus praedicavit, quia extructio illa arcae fuit publicum testimonium, propter delictorum exuberantiam imminere mundo diluvium, in quo omnes, qui arcam non fuerint ingressi, sint perituri. Eò accommodari potest, quod Hebr. 11. v. 7. de Noaho dicitur, quòd non solùm per praedicationem paenitentiae & comminationem de ingruente diluvio, sed etiam per ipsam arcam, hoc est, per extructionem arcae damnaverit mundum, aedificando enim arcam, in qua tempore diluvii cum domo sua conservaretur, ostendit, comminationes illas non fore inanes, sicque ipso facto seu exemplo iustitiam DEI praedicavit, & impios ac incredulos homines condemnavit. 3. Quidam accipiunt de iustitia operum, quòd exhortatus fuerit homines antediluvianos, ut peccatis, quibus securè indulgebant, nuncium mitterent & ad Deum conversi iustitiam sectarentur, quà in parte suo illis praeluxit exemplo, cùm de ipso dicaturGen. 6. vers. 9.quòd fuerit vir iustus ac perfectus in generationibus suis ac cum DEO ambulaverit, hoc est, quod in vero DEI timore vixerit, ac vitam sanctam egerit. Beda in hunc locum: Iustitiae praeconem Noë cognominat, quia iustitiae opera faciens cunctis intuentibus, qualiter coram DEO vivendum esset, ostendit &c. In arcae fabrica ore quidem silente, sed cordis devotione promtissimâ iussis obtemperavit caelestibus. Iosephus lib. 1. antiq. cap. 3. Noë facta illorum (sui seculi hominum, qui nec DEO consuetos honores persolvebant, nec humana iura servabant) molestè & indignè ferens suadebat, ut in melius mentem ac opera sua transmutarent. Verùm cùm videret, illos sibi non parere, totosque vitiorum dulcedini succumbere, veritus ne se & familiam suam interimerent, secedens cum suis in aliam regionem migravit. 4. Quamvis verò secundam & tertiam sententiam non omninò improbemus, procul enim dubio Noahus iustitiam divinam scelerum vindicem praedicavit, & ad sectandam operum iustitiam ex hortatus est, tamen de fidei iustitia principaliter ac potissimùm hîc sermo est, ut constat ex loco parallelo Hebr. 11. vers. 7.Fide Noë accepto oraculo de iis, quae nondum videbantur,εὐλαβηθεὶςex vero DEI timore praeparavit arcam in salutem domus suae, per quam damnavit mundum, & illius quae per fidem est iustitiae, heres constitutus est, hoc est, fide coram DEO iustificatus & heres vitae aeternae constitutus est. Ex quo sic concludimus. Cuius iustitiae heres Noahus constitutus est, eiusdem etiam iustitiae praeco fuit. Atqui iustitia per fidem est illa iustitia, cuius heres Noahus fuit constitutus. Ergo etiam iustitiae per fidem fuit praeco. Lorinus in hunc locum de Messiae, quiκατ' ἐξοχὴνnominatur Iustus, adventu praedicasse Noahum, facilè credo. Id praecessores quoque Noae iam inde ab Adam fecisse, Irenaeus indicat lib. 2. cap. 9. & Athanasius in Epist. quod Nicena Synodus &c. & Hebraei ipsi apud Reuchlinum lib. 1. Cabalae.

Ea igitur ratione Noahus fuit iustitiae praeco. 1. ut homines per praedicationem legis & denunciationem imminentis diluvii ad paenitentiam agendam seriò exhortaretur, absque ea enim fidei iustitia locum non habet. 2. Ut per praedicationem promissionis de Messia fidei iustitiam inculcaret, docens, iustitiam, quae coram DEO valet in promisso Messia, serpentis infernalis contritore, unicè quaerendam & fide acceptandam esse. Hanc sidei iustitiam non solùm verbis, sed ipso etiam facto praedicavit, quia in arcae extructione praefiguratum fuit mysterium Baptismatis ac conservationis contra irae divinae diluvium per CHRISTUM veram illam salutis arcam, ad quam verâ fide confugere possumus 1. Petr. 3. vers. 20. & 21. 3. Ut doceret, fidem illam per studium bonorum operum esse demonstrandam, ac proinde etiam operum iustitiam sectandam esse. Hanc iustitiam bonae conscientiae itidem non solùm verbis, sed etiam ipso facto, videlicet suae erga DEUM oboedientiae exemplo praedicavit, unde Hebr. 11. vers. 7. ipsi tribuitur εὐλάβεια DEI honor ac timor, quod divinas comminationes de perditione generis humani per diluvium non susque deque habuerit, sed mandato divino obsecutus arcam in refugium contra diluvii aquas extruxerit.

Q. 7. An quidam ex eorum numero, qui in aquis diluvii perierunt, fuerint salvati?

Q. 8. An omnes, qui in arca conservati, fuerint iusti? De hisce duabus quaestionibus in enarratione Geneseos fuit actum.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. ChristusIoh. 8. v. 44.loquiturμοναδικῶς,Diabolus non stetit in veritate. Petrus hoc loco, ut & Iudas v. 6. loquunturπληθυντικῶςAngelis, qui peccaverunt, non pepercit.

Resp. nomen Diaboli acceptum κυρίως de malis Angelis usurpatur 1. ἀτόμως pro Principe & capite malorum Spirituum,Matth. 25. v. 41.Apoc. 12. v. 9.quem Beelzebub vel Luciferum vocant. 2. συναγωγικῶς pro tota malorum Angelorum caterva, Luc. 8. v. 12.Act. 10. v. 38.Eph. 6. vers. 12. Sive priore, sive posteriore modo in dicto Christi nomen Diaboli accipiatur, non adversatur loco nostro Apostolico. Ideò verò Scriptura de malis Angelis loquitur in numero singulari, quia sub uno capite quandam societatem & regnum constituunt. Adde quòd nomen terminatione singulare significatione sit plurale. Alii respondent, nomen DiaboliIoh. 8. v. 44.non accipi exclusivè sed autoritativè, ut significet Diabolorum Principem, nec tamen reliqui Diaboli excludantur.

2. Petrus sic concludit. DEUS non pepercit Angelis peccantibus. Ergo nec hominibus peccantibus parcet. Atqui peccatum Angelorum maius est peccato hominis.

Resp. Iohannes Huss in comm. h. l. Si comparatur peccatum peccato, tunc non valet consequentia, sed si comparatur Natura Angelica Naturae humanae, tunc consequentia optimè valet, sic dicendo. Digniori non parcit. Ergo nec minùs digno.

3. Dicuntur mali Angeli in tartarum praecipitati & vinculis caliginis in eo constricti. At circumvagantur per orbem terrarumIob. 1. v. 7.cap. 2. v. 2.versantur in aëre,Eph. 6. v. 12.

Resp. 1. Post lapsum in infernum quidem detrusi sunt. interim ante diem iudicii Deus permittit illos exire in terram. Apoc. 9. v. 1.c. 12. v. 12. ac homines tentare, impios v. vexare. 2. Quidam ergo ad conciliationem horum dictorum id afferunt, quòd quamvis multi Daemones in aëre versentur, tamen multi quoque in inferni carcere detineantur. 3. Distinguendum inter locum Angelorum ordinarium, & extraordinarium. Ordinarius malorum Angelorum locus est infernus, cui omnes post lapsum sunt adiudicati & in eum praecipitati. Extraordinarius ante diem iudicii locus est aër, mare, terra &c. ubi mali illi Spiritus versantur; & quidem in illis locis versari malunt, quam in inferno, quia regnum suum in illis magis propagant & extendunt. 4. Quamvis vero in aëre versantes non sint ἐν τῷ ποῦ infernali, tamen ab infernalibus cruciatibus non sunt penitus liberi, unde Beda in cap. 3. Iac. dicit, Daemones quocunque abeant, ubicunque degant, suum secum circumferre infernum (inferni scil. nomine pro statu miseriae accepto.) Gloss. ordin. in cap. 3. Iacobi. Sicut gehenna semper ardet: sic Diabolus ubicunque sit vel in aëre vel sub terra, semper secum fert tormenta flammarum suarum. Rationem exponir Thomas p. 1. q. 64. art. 4. ad 3. ob apprehensionem molestam suae certo in loco alligationis, quam refugit voluntas & de qua dolet. Quidam tamen censent, realem ac verum ignem inferni singulis in aëre Daemonibus pro sua parte praesentem esse. 5. Interim in ποῦ infernali maiores videntur sustinere cruciatus, unde Luc. 8. v. 31. solicitè precantur, ne imperetur illis, ut in abyssum irent. In die quoque iudicii cruciatus ipsorum magis augebuntur, unde Matth. 8. v. 29. Christo dicunt: Venisti huc nos torquere ante tempus! Ut enim impiorum supplicia in animarum cum corporibus redunitione maxima capient incrementa; ita quoque Diabolis in die iudicii cruciatus augebuntur, quia tunc ex infernali carcere ipsis nullus patebit ampliùs exitus. Apoc. 20. v. 10. & seqq. 6. Quòd Iudas vincula illa, quibus mali Angeli sub caligine ligati atque constricti sunt, nominat aeterna, illud accipi potest de perpetuo ipsorum angore & horrore, quo instar maleficorum in carcere conclusorum constricti horribile illud iudicium novissimum expectant.

4. Petrus mundum antediluvianum vocat antiquum. Atqui idem mundus fuit ante diluvium & post diluvium. Resp. Mundus diluvium praecedens comparatione ad eum factâ, in quo nos sumus, vocatur ἀρχαῖος, non quasi novam rerum universitatem Deus condiderit; sed quia per diluvium tanta fuit facta rerum omnium conversio & confusio, ut mundi instauratio diluvium insecuta pro nova quadam creatione haud immeritò censeatur.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Vaticinium Apostolicum de avaritia falsorum doctorum, quâ sub pietatis specie homines pecuniâ sint emuncturi, in Papatu clarissimè est impletum. Unde enim publicae totius orbis Christiani querelae de Simonia Curiae Romanae! Franciscus Petrarcha in Dial. de Rom. Curia vitand. scribit, Romae Simonem Magum cum coniuge sua Simonia revixisse. In libro, cui titulus, Onus Ecclesiae, extat talis querela: Ambitio & Simonia in Clero iam ubique regnat, ut hodie verificetur illud Prophetae. A minore usque ad maiorem, omnes scil. Clerici, avaritiae student. Ante auditum Lutheri nomen Raphaël Volaterranus Italus Romae scripsit, Sacerdotia tribui mercedis loco, spiritualemque thesaurum quaestui haberi ac negotiationi. Matthaeus Paris in Henrico 3. Rom. Pontifices vocat piscatores non hominum, sed nummorum; non Christi, sed fisci. Aeneas Sylvius Epist. 66. ad Iohan. Peregalium. Curia Romana sine pecunia nihil dat, ipsae manuum impositiones & Spiritus sancti dona venduntur, nec remissio peccatorum, nisi nummatis impenditur. Quid insuper aliud sunt Indulgentiae, nisi retia pecuniarum? Inde Caietanus ad hunc locum Petrinum sic scribit. Non longè ab istis sunt praedicatores quaestus (Indulgentiarum) qui abutuntur populi Christiani devotione ad quaestum, qui ignoranter aut temerè praedicare audent, quòd solventes Carolinum aut ducatum promulgatâ Indulgentia pecuniariâ sint in eo statu, ac si tunc baptizati fuissent, & similiter, quòd liberant animam unam ê purgatorio, haec enim monstra sunt & negotiationes de Christiano populo, nescit Christiana religio haec figmenta. Claudius Espensaeus Theol. Parisiensis in Epist. ad Titum Digress. 2. p. 69. Innocentii octavi Regularum Scholiastes modò Cameram Apostolicam pecuniarum matrem appellat, modò venalia Romae omnia agnoscit, modò multa statui, concedique pecuniae indirectè extorquendae causâ, non dissimulat. p. 78. adducit dictum Volaterrani superiùs citatum. Taxa paenitentiaria est publicum Papalis avaritiae instrumentum. Sed & Papales sacrificuli Missas precio vendunt;

Monachi opera supererogationis interventu pecuniae aliis sese communicare posse mentiuntur &c.

2. In v. 4. evidens habetur testimonium, quòd dentur mali Angeli, Daemones & Diaboli aliàs dicti. Opponendum hoc Sadducaeis, Dositheanis & nostri aevi haereticis, Anabaptistis, Libertinis & Davidgeorgianis.

3. Diabolorum in tartarum abiectio & aeterna vincula illis iniecta opponenda sunt Origeni, qui Daemones aliquando liberandos & salvandos esse docuit, lib. 1. περὶ ἀρχῶν cap. 6. Ambrosiaster in comm. Eph. 3. asserit, aliquos ex Daemonibus per Paulum liberatos ab errore, peccato & Luciferi Tyrannide. Contra verissimè Augustinus lib. 21. de Civ. DEI cap. 23. Teneatur fixum & immobile, nullum regressum ad iustitiam vitamque sanctorum Diabolum & Angelos eius habituros, quiae Scriptura, quae neminem fallit, dicit, eis Deum non pepercisse, & sic ab illo esse inter impios praedamnatos, ut carceribus caliginis inferni retrusi traederentur servandi, atque ultimo iudicio puniendi, quando eos aeternus ignis excipiet, ubi cruciabuntur in secula seculorum.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lorinus ad v. 3. sic annotat. Satis constat, solam Luthero avaritiam ab Ecclesia discendendi & haere sin cudendi causam fuisse, quòd quaestu se privatum videret, quem ex Indulgentiarum promulgatione capiebat, translato huius rei munere ab Augustinianis suis ad Dominicanos, Moguntini Archiepiscopi voluntate.

Resp. 1. Ergone etiam in Monachos paupertatis voto adstrictos, ac nihil proprii in mundo habentes, tanta cadit avaritia, ut eâ impulsi etiam haereses excitent? 2. Ergone Indulgentiae Papales sunt pecuniarum aucupia & avaritiae retia? 3. Veram causam, ob quam Lutherus Indulgentias impugnare coepit, exponunt alii Scriptores Pontificii, quòd fuerit abusus Indulgentiarum Papalium, abusus potestatis Ecclesiasticae, corruptelae doctrinae & morum, quae publicè invaluerant &c. quorum testimonia adducta sunt in Confess. Cathol. lib. 1. part. 1. cap. 7. &c. 4. Agnoscit hoc Lorinus ipse, qui paulò pòst ad hunc ipsum vers. sic annotat. Meritò Thomas Angelicus, Caietanus & Catharinus hîc Praedicatores reprehendunt, quaestui vacantes maximè, ut Secundus ait, occurrens procul dubio Lutherani erroris origini, si promulgatae Indulgentiae praetextu id faciant. 3. Salmero in enarr. vers. 4. disputat contra quosdam Scholasticos, qui ex verbis hisce Petri, Si Angelis peccantibus non pepercit, colligunt, Daemones ita primò peceasse, ut nullam temporis moram ad resipiscentiam illis DEUS contulerit. Respondet autem ipsorum argumento hoc modo 1. Phrasin illam, DEUS Angelis peccantibus non pepercit, potiûs contrarium probare, nempé quòd potuerit parcere & animum paratum habuerit illis parcendi, modò resipuissent. Probant hoc ex collatione loci Iob. 9. v. 28.Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens, quòd non parcis omni delinquenti, ubi non significatur, actu delinquentem damnationem incurrere, sed statim illo actu damnationem mereri, nisi per viam paenitentiae ad DEUM revertatur. 2. Petrum ibidem subiungere, & originali mundo non pepercit. Item, Civitates Sodomaeorum & Gomorrhaeorum in cinerem redegit. Ut ergo homines ante diluvianos ac cives Sodomorum, non statim ubi peccarunt, in tartarum praecipitavit, sed tempus paenitentiae ipsis concessit: ita quoque Angelis lapsis tempus & locum paenitendi, si vellent, concessit. 3. Si DEUS non dedisset illis spacium paenitendi, potiùs ex rigore iustitiae, quàm ex benignitate & longanimitate cum ipsis egisset. Contrarium verò probant beneficia, quibus eos in prima creatione cumulavit, quando excellentibus & supernaturalibus donis eos decoravit. 4. Adducit quasdam revelationes. 5. Dicta Patrum, Cyrilli Hierosolym. Catech. 9. Illum. Gregorii Nysseni lib. 1. Philos. cap. 3. Basilii in cap. 14. Esai. Hieronymi in cap. 1.Ephes. 6. Deducit hanc sententiam ad absurdum. Si statim, ut Angelus peccavit, cecidit, & casus fuit illi, quod nobis mors, sequetur quòd nullus Angelus nisi pro uno tantùm peccato damnatus fuisset, cùm tamen homo post myriades peccatorum paenitentiam agere & misericordiam invenire possit; sequetur insuper, multos homines fuisse, qui graviùs, quam Angeli in caelo, peccaverunt. Si ergo hominibus non denegavit paenitentiae tempus, multò minus Angelis, qui minùs peccaverunt, non tribueret Indulgentiam? 7. Angeli peccatum non videtur inflexibilem & immutabilem eius voluntatem effecisse, ex eo, quòd omnia videt sine discursu, & principia, & conclusiones, quae ex illis oriuntur, & ut dicunt, cuicunque rei inhaeret, et immobiliter haeret. Obiici enim posset, quia nos etiam videmus prima principia & conclusiones necessariò ex illis deductas, nec tamen immutabilis est nostra voluntas, cui amor proprius sive φιλαυτία semper adest, quae potest inflectere voluntatem ad malum aliquod sub specie honesti apparens. Cornelius â Lapide ad h. vers. sic commentatur. Nonnulli Doctores censent, Daemones mox ut lapsi sunt in peccatum, fuisse in viae suae termino, ideoque non potuisse per paenitentiam resurgere. Nos de hac quaestione 1. Usurpamus dictum Augustini lib. 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. ult. Ubi de re obscurissima disputatur, non adiuvantibus divinarum Scripturarum certis clarisque documentis, cohibere se debet humana praesumtio, nihil in hanc, vel illam partem temerè affirmando. 2. Cogitur hoc quodammodo Salmeron ipse fateri, unde ad quaestionem, Si potuerunt Angeli paenitentiam agere de peccate, quare inter tot myriades Angelorum, qui ceciderunt, nullum paenituit? respondet, hoc esse magnum arcanum divinae sapientiae, nec nos posse de omnibus rationem reddere. Et postea subiicit. Difficile esse videtur, certam aliquam sententiam de his definire. 3. Si tempus paenitentiae ipsis datum fuisset, etiam Redemtor ipsis fuisset datus. Christum verò Angelis Mediatorem & Redemtorem esse datum, ipse Salmeron affirmare reformidat. Si pauci, inquit, aliqui ex malis Angelis extitissent, ita salvi, dicerem, non opus fuisse, Christum perinde esse Angelorum per suum sanguinem Redemtorem atque hominum. 4. Damascenus lib. 2. Orth. fid. cap. 3. sic disserit. Angelus estἀνεπίδεκτος μετανοίας, ὅτι καὶ ἀσώματος, ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τήν τοῦ σώματος ἀσθένειαν τῆς μετανοίας ἔτυχε; cap. 4. ὅπερ ἔστι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ὁ θάνατος, τοῦτο τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις ἡ ἔκπτωσις μετὰ γὰρ τὴν ἔκπτωσιν οὐκ ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς μετάνοια, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ ἀνθρώποις μετὰ τὸν θάνατον. 5. Salmeron, aequè ac omnes Iesuitae, iuravit in verba Thomae. Isverò p. 1. q. 64. art. 2. disputat, ipsam Naturam voluntatis Angelicae ita comparatam esse, ut quod semel cum plena deliberatione elegit, aversari ampliùs nequeat, neque id eligere, quod semel est aversata. 6. Lorinus ad h. l. sic annotat. Etsi scoto 2. dist. 6. q. 2. Gabrieli ibid. q. 1. art. 2. & Salmeroni videatur, potuisse Angelos, si vellent paenitere, plures tamen hoc negant, usurpantes illud ex Damasceno & Nysseno vel Nemesio 1. Phil. cap. 2. Quod hominibus mors, hoc Angelis esse lapsum, post quemnon sit paenitentiae locus, ut neque homini post mortem. In eadem sententia praeter hos duos Patres est Cassianus collat. 4. cap. 13. & 14. Autor de mirabilib. Scripturae lib. 1. cap. 2. Gregorius lib. 2. moral. cap. 3. al. 4. Isidorus lib. 1. de summo bono cap. 12. sent. 11. Fulgentius de fide cap. 3. Prosper lib. de dimid. temp. cap. 2. & 1. de vita contempl. cap. 3. Rationem aliqui afferunt, quia primam gratiam solo Christi merito confert DEUS inimicis suis, noluit autem Angelis, sicut hominibus Redemtorem dare &c. Et postea: Quod ait Salmeron, ex verbis istis, non pepercit, colligi potuisse, Deum parcere, concedo, non tamen quòd habuerit animum paratum parcendi. Nec sanè alter locusIob. 9. v. 28.Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens, quòd non parceres delinquenti, denotat solùm mereri damnationem, eamque incurrendam, nisi peccator per viam paenitentiae ad Deum revertatur, sed sensus est, ubi statuerit Deus punire, non esse, qui deprecari poenam possit vel obsistere, iuxta illud1. Sam. 15. v. 29.Triumphator in Israël non parcet, & paenitudine non flectetur. Nec argumentum valet aut ab aliis exemplis diluvii & Pentapolis, quae hîc subiiciuntur aut à commendatione divinae misericordiae, aut â ne scio quâ divinâ revelatione, (Salmeronis haec sunt argumenta) Nam revelatio incerta, cur non Angelis, sed hominibus oblata sit gratia ad paenitendum. Nil quoque video incommodi, concedere, nonnullos Angelos paucioribus ac minoribus pro peccatis damnatos, quàm homines, licet istis, non illis data sit paenitendi facultas. Nyssenus vel Neme sius frustrà id asserere dicitur (citante Salmerone) siquidem apertè comparat lapsum Angelorum in peccatum cum morte hominum. Nec in Basilio, nec in Hieronymo lego, quod sententiae nostrae officiat, certumque est, Hieronymum saepe loqui ex aliorum sententia. Haec omnia Lorinus, Salmeronem ex professo refellens.

3. Idem Lorinus ad h. l. ex voce ταρταρώσας colligit, in inferno futuras vicissitudines summi frigoris, summique caloris, cùmταρταρίζεινsit tartareo frigere frigore. Resp. quid hac de re statuendum sit, expositum fuit in tract. de Inserno §. 71. Abulensis q. 558. in Matth. Dominicus â Soto 4. dist. 50. q. un. art. 4. negant, apud inferos frigus esse.

4. Cornelius â Lapide ad eund. versic. sic annotat. Multi haeresiarchae habuerunt Daemonas paredros & familiares. Lutherus lib. de Miss. angul. & ad Elect. Saxon. fatetur, se cum Diabolo plus quam modium salis assumsisse, ab eoque argumenta accepisse, quibus Missam oppugnaret. Haec ut alia plura transcripsit Cornelius â Lapide ex Lorino in comm. v. 15. ubi eadem totidem verbis inculcat. Resp. 1. Lutherus non loquitur de familiari & amico cum Daemone consortio, sed de quotidiano tentationum Diabolicarum palo, carni suae infixo. 2. Cor. 12. v. 7.2. Nec Lutherus â Satana argumenta, quibus Missas solitarias oppugnaretur, primùm didicit, sed eorum robur in interiori Diaboli tentatione animadvertit.

5. Gagnaeus in expos. v. 5. duo affert, quorum utrumque assensu indignum. Primò dicit, vulgatum interpretem fortassè legisseἀρχικὸνprimogenium, cùm reddiderit, Originalem. Secundò dicit, sibi videri, quòdἀρχαῖος h. l. non tam antiquum significet, quàm rudem & imperitum, ut sit sensus. Si Deus seculo illi rudi adhuc & imperito, rerumque divinarum penè ignaro non pepercit, quid facturus est falsis Doctoribus, qui â via veritatis intellecta deflexerunt. De hac Gagnaei opinione Lorin. ad h. versum sic disserit. Hoc approbant Salmeron ac Fevardentius; ego nullo modo, cùm recepta sit ac usitata notioἀρχαίουprior pro antiquo, prisco, vetusto, pristino, idque saepiùs quàm pro rudi vel stulto & inepto, quod significat quoqueτὸ ἀρχαϊκὸν.Lege Budaeum in comm. ling. Graecae & Autorem Thesauri (Henricum Stephanum) quiτὸ ἀρχικὸνexplicant imperandi cupidum, imperiosum. Certè pro antiquo non invenio. Et postea, Interpres eandem vocemἀρχαίουreddit Latinè antiqui pluribus locis N. T.Matth. 5. v. 21.27.33.Luc. 9. v. 8.Act. 15. v. 7.21.cap. 21. v. 16.Apoc. 12. v. 9.cap. 20. v. 2.ut omittam Vetus. Ac valde sapienter hoc loco posuit originalis epithetum, ut designaret homines aetatis primae, quam â parentum censent transgressione usque ad tempus diluvii.

6. Iodocus Coccius Tom. 1. Thesauri lib. 7. art. 3. p. 796. ex hoc loco Apostolico demonstrare conatur, ab orbe condito usque ad praesens tempus perpetuâ successione semper fuisse unum Ecclesiae Praesidem & Monarcham. In huius modi primatu & Monarchia, inquit, Noë octavum locum obtinuit, qui post obitum avi Mathusalem vixit, & solus praefuit Ecclesiae 350. annis, unde 2. Petr. 2. octavus praeco iustitiae dicitur. Expostioni nostrae, quòd Noah dicatur servatus octavus h. e. cum aliis septem, hoc opponit. Si ita Scriptura haec esset intelligenda, quâ ratione dicitur octavus & non primus? Primus enim Noah arcam ingreditur, primus eâdem egreditur, primus erat aetate, primus dignitate; inter octo illas animas Cham erat impius, quatuor uxoribus tale encemium tribui nequit.

Resp. 1. Expositionem nostram, quòd Noah dicàtur servatus octavus, quia cum aliis septem in arca fuit servatus, superiùs ex phrasi Graecis usitata & ex collatione loci paralleli 1. Petr. 3. vers. 20. comprobavimus. 2. Eandem sequuntur Lyranus, Ambrosius, Catharinus, Caietanus, Gagnaeus, Guillandus, Lorinus, Salmero, Saa & alii Pontificii complures. Estius in comm. de ea sic scribit. Octavum vocat non ab Adamo, â quo decimus reperitur, sed quia octo tantum animae conservatae fuerunt, quo in numero erat Noah, & quidem tanquam caput, qui proinde octavus dicitur, modo loquendi etiam vulgaribus usitato. Cornelius â Lapide in h. l. Dicitur Noë octavus, sc. eorum, qui per aream salvati sunt, alludit enim Petrus ad id, quod dixit Epist. 1. cap. 3. v. 20.Octo animae salvae factae sunt per aquam. Alii ex Iosepho lib. 1. Antiq. cap. 4. & 5. censent, Noë fuisse octavum praeconem iustitiae, quia secutus est septem generationes, quibus posteri Seth coluerunt iustitiam & sanctitatem. Alii octavum dici censent, quia natus est anno octingentesimo (non â creatione mundi, ab ea enim natus est anno 1056. sed) ab inchoata impietate & corruptione mundi, quae ante Noë duraverat per septingentos annos. Alii septem alios praecones iustitiae illo aevo comminiscuntur, quos Scriptura exprimat, quorum octavus fuerit Noë. Sed primus sensus est genuinus. 3. Huic expositioni frustra obvertitur, quòd septem animae reliquae servatae in arca non fuerint praecones iustitiae, quia vocula ὄγδοον non coniungenda cum nomine κύρηκα sed cum verbo ἐφύλαξε. 4. Demus, Noahum fuisse praecipuum Ecclesiae Doctorem reliquis omnibus praepositum, num ex eo stastatim inferri poterit, fuisse Ecclesiae Monarcham? alius primatus est ordinis & dignitatis, alius Monarchicae potestatis. 5. Cui etiam persuadere poterit Coccius, iustitiae praeconem esse idem, quod Ecclesiae Monarcham? itemque in tot seculis ab initio mundi usque ad diluvium octo tantùm iustitiae praecones fuisse? Agnoscat ergo, voculam ὄγδοον cum nomine κήρυκα coniungi non debere. 6. Ac si vel maximè detur, Noam fuisse Ecclesiae Monarcham & quidem iure successionis, num idem statim in N. T. obtinere debet? Reducatur ergo successio Sacerdotalis, reducantur sacrificia ex animalibus, reducantur Leviticae Ceremoniae & omnes leges Mosaicae.

7. Lorinus ad h. v. sic annotat. Meritò Chemnitium refellit (Andradius) Payva lib. 2. pro Conc. Trid. nescio quas comminiscentem revelationes in Noë de pleniori caelestis doctrinae declaratione, proptereaque praeconem â Petro appellatum iustitiae, cùm iam periisset omninò vera caelestium rerum cognitio & vis traditionum non sufficeret, nam nil tale aut Genesis Historia narrat, aut hîc innuit Petrus.

Resp. Verba Chemnitii sic habent in Exam. Conc. Trident. part. 1. de Script. sacra p. 13. Post mortem Adami non tantùm posteritas Caini, verùm etiam filii Elohim, qui traditiones doctrinae caelestis acceperant, corruperunt vias suas, in qua corruptione absque dubio praecipuae fuit adulteratio verbi DEI. Ita enim Deus inquit. Non disceptabit Spiritus meus in homine in perpetuum. Et causam addit, quia caro sunt & figmentum cordis humani malum. Fuit igitur doctrina caelestis in originali mundo vivâ voce sine scripto quasi per manus tradita: sed quiae cordis humani figmentum malum est, puritas verbi per traditiones vivae vocis tandem non fide liter fuit conservata, sed corrupta & adulterata, imò tandem planè amissa &c. Ibi verò peculiaribus revelationibus ad Noë, addidis stupendis in diluvio miraculis, puritatem doctrinae collapsam Deus restituit, conservavit & pleniorem eius declarationem addidit & ante & post diluvium; Et Noë illis miraculis confirmavit in praeconem Iustitiae, ut custos esset puritatis doctrinae, & illam vivâ voce per manus traderet posteris. Haec D. Chemnitius in quibus quod carpat, ne ipse quidem Momus invenerit.

Observationes. 1. Discant Ecclesiae Ministri, tum quaevis vitia, tum cumprimis avaritiam ab ipsis exulare debere. Luc. 12. v. 15.1. Thessal. 2. v. 5. & 6.Actor. 20. v. 33.2. Cor. 4. v. 2. Bonaventura in cap. 12. Lucae. Praedicator veritatis super omnia vitare debet vitium cupiditatis, alîoqui non erit veritatis praedicator, sed adulator. Nimirum quis quis avaritiae studet aut popularibus auris, cum fructu nunquam de pietate docet, quod est Fabricii distichon. De haereticis dicit Hieronymus lib. 3. in Zach. cap. 14. quod omnia lucri & gloriae causâ faciant; contrà verò de Apostolis pronunciat Chrysostomus homil. 47. in Matth. quod verus & non simulatus gloriae ac pecuniae contemtus Apostolos reddiderit magnos & efficaces persuasores.

2. Sicut de haereticis Petrus hoc loco pronunciat, quod fictis verbis de auditoribus suis negotientur, instar mercatorum, qui blando sermone emtores illiciunt, ut merces suas cariùs vendant: ita Paulus de illis pronunciat 2. Cor. 2. v. 17. quòd verbum DEI cauponentur. In Graeco est καπηλεύειν, quod est proprium eorum, qui esculenta aut potulenta venditant, quorum studium consuevit esse praecipuum, vitiata pro sinceris vendere, vinum affusione aquae adulterare, Esai. 1. v. 22. Chrysostomus in 2. Cor. 2. Hoc est cauponari, cum quis (lucri captandi causa) vinum adulterat; cùm quis aquam vel huiusmodi alias res pecuniâ vendit, quas gratis dare debebat.

3. Haec ipsa loquendi formula metaphorica de falsis Doctoribus usurpata subinnuit, curam animarum esse in se ac per se genus honestissimae ἐμπορίας sive negotiationis praestantissimum, per quod animae Christo lucrifiunt, Luc. 19. v. 13.πραγματεύσασθε,Negotiemini, donec veniam.

4. Sicut Deus non tardat promissionem,2. Petr. 3. v. 9. ita quoque non tardat comminationem, quamvis & promissionum & comminationum suarum impletionem quadoque differre videatur.

5. Augustinus de Natura boni adv. Manich. cap. 33. ex hoc loco rectè colligit, malos Angelos non â DEO conditos malos, sed peccando factos esse malos. Beda in comm. h. l. In eo, quod dicit Apostolus, Deum Angelis peccantibus non pepercisse, notandum, quia ipsi mali Angeli non â DEO conditi mali, sed peccando facti sunt mali. Naturâ mali non sunt, sed electione & proprio peccato, ut definitum in Concil. Carthag. 4. cap. 1. & Bracarensi cap. 7.

6. Fulgentius de fide cap. 3. pulchrè sic concludit. Sine grattâ non potest homo paenitere, quia multò magis Angelus malus potuisset, cuius Natura quantò minùs gravatur terreni corporis pondere, tantò magis hac esset praedita facultate.

7. Idem Fulgentius lib. 2. ad Trasimund. cap. 2. ex Angelorum lapsu concludit. Naturam Angelicam non fuisse idoneam ad humanam reparandam, quoniam illa se iuvaminis egenam consubstantialis ruina documento testatur.

8. Catenae, quibus mali Angeli post lapsum tenentur constricti, significant. 1. quòd divinâ potentiâ coërceantur, ne possint absque permissione Dei hominibus nocere. 2. quod ex statu felicitatis in extremam miseriam ex libertate concreatâ in servitutem sint prolapsi.

9. Catenae illae vocantur catenae caliginis. 1. quia divinâ voluntate ac potentiâ sub caligine h. e. in inferno captivi & vincti tenentur, ut absque Dei permissione ex illo nequeant exire. Vincula caliginis sunt vincula caliginosa h. e. vincula inferni, in quo perpetuae tenebrae. 2. quia privati sunt omni consolatione, laetitiâ ac spe liberationis, unde Iudas dicit, illos aeternis vinculis sub caligine reservari. Augustinus lib. 21. de civ. DEI cap. 23. Teneatur fixum & immobile, nullum regressum ad iustitiam vitamque sanctorum Diabolum & Angelos eius habituros, quia Scriptura, quae neminem fallit, dicit de eis, Deum non pepercisse &c. Integer locus ἐλέγχῳ 3. superiùs fuit adductus.

10. In die iudicii non solùm homines impii, sed etiam Angeli mali damnationis sententiam audient, nequitiâ ipsorum coram beatis Angelis & hominibus manifestatâ, potentiâ eorum prorsus conculcatâ ac superbiâ publicè illusâ.

11. Augustinus tract. 95. in Iohann. Ne sibi parci existimet superbia dura mortalium, de supplicio superborum terrenda est Angelorum. Si DEUS immunditiem peccati ita aversatur, ut vasa illa aurea Angelicae Naturae preciosissimis donorum fulgentissimorum gemmis ornata, eo ipso, quod vidit immunditiem & aeruginem superbiae contraxisse, aeternâ damnationis sententia tanquam virgâ ferrea contrivit & in sterquilinium inferni in aeternum proiecit; quid futurum credis de homine, qui vas est fictile & terreum, cùm peccatorum immunditiâ ac sordibus fuerit inquinatum?

12. Diluvium est publicum & evidens testimonium de comminationum divinarum veritate; de irae divinae adversùs peccata severitate; de DEI potentia & maiestate, quâ omnia Elementa, creaturas omnes contra impios armare potest; de DEI erga pios benignitate, quâ in publica πανολεθρίᾳ mirabiliter illos servare potest.

13. Noahi & aliorum fidelium Ecclesiae Doctorum ministerium est publicum iustitiae praeconium.

14. Beda in comm. h. l. talem texit allegoriam. Idcircò octavi numeri facit mentionem, ut occultè insinuet, quia tempus diluvii discrimen significet examinis ultimi, quando damnatis omnibus reprobis omnes iusti gloriam vitae perpetis accipient. Sex etenim sunt praesentis seculi aetates: septima etiam nunc agitur aetas in illa vita, ubi animae sanctorum Sabbato felici, id est, requie perfruuntur aeternâ, octava est ventura tempore resurrectionis omnium & Universalis iudicii.

## 2:4
Connection. He confirms the certainty of the destruction foretold for the false teachers with three examples, the first of which is of the evil Angels, who through their apostasy from GOD cast themselves headlong into eternal destruction.

Exposition of the text. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς Ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο. Some suspect εἰ to have crept in for καὶ. But the Greek Codices consistently read εἰ. Therefore in this verse and the two following ἀνανταπόδοτον, is to be understood, for with Cassian lib. 12. Instit. cap. 4. οὐδ' ἐκείνοις φείσεται, he will much less spare miserable little men. A similar ἀνανταπόδοτον occurs Rom. 9. vers. 22. & 23. Moreover, in the words of the Apostle is an argument drawn from the lesser to the greater. If God did not spare the Angels, he will much less spare men. The Apostle shows the connection v. 11. where he calls the Angels ἰσχύει καὶ δυνάμει μείζονας.

The Vulgate rendered the participle ἀμαρτησὰντων in the present tense, peccantibus [sinning], but in the Greek it is an aorist, having the meaning of the past, who have sinned.

In the phrase μὴ ἐφείσατο there is μείωσις,, for it says little, but signifies far more. God did not spare the evil Angels, but brought forth an irrevocable sentence of damnation against them, and gave the same to execution. Compare the things said above in cap. 1. v. 8.

Ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν ἐτηρημένους. The Apostle had said, that God did not spare the Angels, i. e., that He punished them most severely, (for the negated is put for the contrary affirmed.) Now furthermore he explains that punishment, what kind it was.

Σειρὰ, which some derive from σύρω I draw, signifies a chain or also a rope. The LXX use it for חלב a rope, from which one can in no way extricate himself. Prov. 5. v. 22. they are called σειρεὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ropes, by which sinners are entangled and bound and stick fast σειραὶ therefore ζόφου are chains of darkness, from which it easily appears that the noun σειρὰς is taken metaphorically here so that the sense is He bound them with darkness as if with certain chains. Jude in the parallel passage just cited explains the phrase thus: δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρεικεν He has reserved them in eternal chains under darkness. It is therefore a metaphor drawn from robbers and other evildoers, who, bound with chains, are thrown into a foul and dark prison, in which they are kept until the time of judgment and punishment. By the same reasoning God cast the apostate Angels into hell, in which they are reserved in chains of darkness, as Peter speaks, or in eternal chains under darkness, as Jude speaks. The Vulgate version rendered σειραῖς by cables, which are nautical ropes, strong and valid, but the Greek simply signifies ropes or chains. ζόφον the same Vulgate version rendered by hell, so that it is a metonymy of the adjunct for the subject, darkness for a dark hell. But in the parallel passage Epist. Iudae v. 6. ζόφον κατὰ πόδα it rendered by darkness. The Syrian rendered [בששלתא דעמטנא] in chains of darkness. For [ששלתא] is the same as [שלשלא] with the [ל] elided, a chain. Iob. 20. cap. 36. v. 8.

[עמטנא] indeed is darknessActs 2. v. 20.c. 13. v. 11. from the root [עמט] to be darkened, to be dark. The other Syrian seems to have retained the Greek words, so that he might better express the Greek truth, as Pococke advises in the notes to the Syriac paraphrase on this place.

Augustine in book 11 of The City of God chapter 33, and book 21 chapter 23, and in The Nature of the Good chapter 33, and Fulgentius in book 2 to Thrasimundus, read prisons instead of chains, of which version Bede also makes mention in his commentary, and Paterius in the exposition of this Epistle among the works of Gregory cites this passage thus: But thrusting them into the dark prisons of hell, he delivered them to be reserved for judgment to be tormented. But Ludovicus Vives in his annotations to Augustine's book on The City of God rightly advises, that interpreter placed prisons, for enclosures, by which demons are prohibited from exiting, such as those were in the circus, by which horses were restrained before they ran. It can also be a metonymy of the container for the thing contained; of the prison for the chains in the prison.

Ταρταρώσας. This word occurs nowhere else in the Scriptures, but it is deduced from ταρταρος, from which, as also from the context of this place, its meaning is gathered, namely that it is the same as εις ταρταραν ριπτειν to cast into Tartarus, as Homer speaks in the Iliad θ. to send to the impious Tartarus, as Virgil speaks having imitated Homer. The words of Homer himself are thus: Ἡμιν ἑλὼν ῥίψω εἰς τάρταρον ἠερόεντα Τῆλε μάλ' ᾗχι βάθεστον ὑπὸ χθονός ἔστιβέροθρον. Ἔνθα σιδήρειαι του πύλαι καὶ χάλκεος οὐδός. But they deduce the name itself τάρταρος from ταράσσω or διά τὸ ταραχώδες ἐκεῖ τοῦ ἄερος or because by its opaque darkness or even by cold ταράσσει καὶ ταρβεῖν ποιεῖ it terrifies and makes one tremble. The Syrian rendered the word ταρταρώσας as [עגן בתחתיתא] he concluded, he detained in the lowest places, with the explanation taken from the passage Apoc. 20. v. 1.I saw an Angel &c. having a great chain in his handv. 2.& he apprehended the Dragon the ancient serpent, which is the Devil, and bound him &c.v. 3.& cast him into the abyss and shut him up. The other Syrian retained the Greek ταρταρώσας.

Παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τετηρημένους. The Vulgate rendered it, he delivered them to be reserved for judgment to be tormented. But in the Greek there is nothing which corresponds to the participle to be tormented. Let him answer. Indeed Robertus Stephanus cites certain Greek Codices, in which it is read, εἰς κρὶσιν κολαζομένους τηρεῖν to be reserved for judgment to be punished, which participle also occurs in Augustine book 11 de Civ. DEI chapter 33, de Nat. boni chapter 33, and in Fulgentius book 2 ad Thrasim. but it was added to the text by them for the sake of illustration, for the Greek Codices which have it are fewer and of doubtful authority.

For Τετηρημένους kept, certain Greek Codices read τηρουμένους to be kept, or who are kept. From this Gagnaeus gathers, that for τηρουμένους at that time, when the vulgate version was adorned, there was read τειρουμένους afflicted, vexed, for which the Interpreter placed to be tormented. But this conjecture is fallacious, since in the parallel place Jude v. 6. the same verb τετήρηκεν is held placed in the past, which confirms the customary reading of our Codices τετηρημένους. Therefore εἰς κρίσιν τετήρηκεν, is the same, which phrase Jude uses, and παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τετηρημένους, which phrase Peter uses in this place. Jude in the said place added, εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας, by which he points out the day of the final judgment, from which also the Syrian in this place ἐξηγήσεως for the sake of it added, [לדינאדשונקא] for the judgment of torment, unless we prefer to say, this, as also many other things, was taken from the vulgate version, which added the participle to be tormented.

Moreover, that the fallen Angels are said to be by chains of darkness ταρταρωσάμενοι some accept that in the sense that by most strong chains, as it were, they were dragged down from heaven into hell, and in it until the day of judgment are detained as if in a certain dark prison, by which reason that σειραῖς ζόφου is accepted as an ablative of instrument and is referred to the participle ταρταρώσας, which sense the Vulgate Interpreter also seems to have followed, who rendered, dragged down to hell by ropes of the infernal regions. But it is more correctly said, those words σειραῖς ζόφου are to be joined with the verb παρέδωκε or with the participle τετηρημένους, so that the sense may be, he delivered them reserved by chains of darkness, that is, consigned to a dark prison, and in it to be reserved until the day of judgment, which exposition the parallel place of Jude v. 6 confirms. He reserved the fallen Angels for the judgment of the great day with eternal bonds under darkness.

Latin:

Connexio. Confirmat exitii falsis doctoribus praenunciati certitudinem tribus exemplis, quorum primum est Angelorum malorum, qui per suam â DEO apostasiam in aeternum exitium seipsos praecipites dedêre.

Textus expositio. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς Ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο. Quidam suspicantur εἰ pro καὶ irrepsisse. Sed Graeci Codices constanter legunt εἰ. Est ergo in hoc versiculo & duobus sequentibus ἀνανταπόδοτον, subintelligendum enim cum Cassiano lib. 12. Instit. cap. 4. οὐδ' ἐκείνοις φείσεται,multò minùs miseris homuncionibus parcet. Simile ἀνανταπόδοτον occurrit Rom. 9. vers. 22. & 23. Caeterùm in verbis Apostoli est argumentum ductum â minore ad maius. Si Deus Angelis non pepercit, multò minùs hominibus parcet. Connexionem ostendit Apostolus v. 11. ubi Angelos vocat ἰσχύει καὶ δυνάμει μείζονας.

Participium ἀμαρτησὰντων Vulg. in praes. reddidit, peccantibus sed in Graeco est aoristus, praeteriti significationem habens, qui peccaverunt.

In phrasi μὴ ἐφείσατο est μείωσις, parum enim dicit, sed longè plus significat. Non pepercit Deus malis Angelis, sed irrevocabilem damnationis sententiam in illos protulit, eandemque executioni dedit. Confer dicta superius in cap. 1. v. 8.

Ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν ἐτηρημένους. Dixerat Apostolus, Deum Angelis non pepercisse i. e. gravissimè punivisse, (ponitur enim negatum pro contrario affirmato.) iam porrò poenam illam explicat, qualis illa fuerit.

Σειρὰ, quod quidam deducunt â σύρωtraho, significat catenam vel etiam funem. LXX. utuntur pro חלבfunis, ex quo sese explicare quis minimè potest. Prov. 5. v. 22. dicuntur σειρεὶ ἁμαρτιῶν funes, quibus peccatores impliciti & vincti haerent σειραὶ ergo ζόφου sunt catenae caliginis, ex quo facilè apparet, nomen σειρὰς metaphoricè hic accipi ut sit sensus caligine velut quibusdam catenis eos constrinxit. Iudas in loco parallelo modò citato phrasin sic explicat. δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρεικενvinculis aeternis sub caligine eos reservavit. Est ergo metaphora ducta â latronibus & aliis maleficis, qui catenis vincti in tetrum ac tenebricosum carcerem coniiciuntur, in quo usque ad tempus iudicii & supplicii adservantur. Pariratione Deus Angelos apostatas in tartarum praecipitavit, in quo catenis tenebrarum, ut Petrus loquitur, sive catenis aeternis sub caligine, ut Iudas loquitur, reservantur. Vulg. versio σειραῖς reddidit per rudentes, qui sunt funes nautici, fortes ac validi, sed Graecum simpliciter significat funes vel catenas.ζόφον eadem Vulg. versio reddidit per infernum, ut sit metonymia adiuncti pro subiecto, caligo pro inferno calignoso. Sed in loco parallelo Epist. Iudae v. 6.ζόφον κατὰ πόδα reddidit per caliginem. Syrus reddidit [בששלתא דעמטנא]in catenis caliginis. Nam [ששלתא] est idem quod [שלשלא] eliso [ל]catena.Iob. 20.cap. 36. v. 8.

[עמטנא] verò est caligoAct. 2. v. 20.c. 13. v. 11. â rad. [עמט]obscurari, obscurum esse. Alter Syrus Graeca vocabula retinuisse videtur, ut Graecam veritatem meliùs exprimeret, monente Pococke in notis ad paraph. Syr. h. l.

Augustinus lib. 11. de Civ. DEI cap. 33. ac lib. 21. cap. 23. de Natura boni cap. 33. ac fulgentius lib. 2. ad Thrasim. pro catenis legunt carceribus, cuius versionis etiam Beda in comm. meminit, ac Paterius in expos. huius Epist. apud Gregorium locum hunc sic adducit. Sed carceribus caliginosis inferni retrudens tradidit in iudicium cruciandos reservari. At Ludovicus Vives in annotat. ad August. lib. de Civ. DEI rectè monet, carceribus, pro claustris Interpretem illum posuisse, quibus exire Daemones prohibentur, quales erant illi in circo, quibus equi antequam currerent, coercebantur. Potest etiam esse metonymia continentis pro contento; carceris pro catenis in carcere.

Ταρταρώσας. Verbum hoc in Scripturis nuspiam alibi occurrit, deducitur autem â ταρταρος, ex quo, uti etiam ex contextu huius loci, eius significatio colligitur, quòd scilicet idem sit ac εις ταρταραν ριπτεινin tartarum proiicere, ut loquitur Homerus Iliad. θ.ad impia tartara mittere, ut Virgilius Homerum imitatus loquitur. Verba ipsa Homerisic habent. Ἡμιν ἑλὼν ῥίψω εἰς τάρταρον ἠερόεντα Τῆλε μάλ' ᾗχι βάθεστον ὑπὸ χθονός ἔστιβέροθρον. Ἔνθα σιδήρειαι του πύλαι καὶ χάλκεος οὐδός. Ipsum verò nomen τάρταρος deducunt â ταράσσω vel διά τὸ ταραχώδες ἐκεῖ τοῦ ἄερος vel quoniam opacis suis tenebris aut etiam frigore ταράσσει καὶ ταρβεῖν ποιεῖ exterret & tremefacit. Syrus verbum ταρταρώσας reddidit [עגן בתחתיתא]conclusit, detinuit in infimis, explicatione desumtâ ex loco Apoc. 20. v. 1.Vidi Angelum &c. habentem catenam magnam in manu suav. 2.& apprehendit Draconem serpentem antiquum, qui est Diabolus, & ligavit eum &c.v. 3.& misit eum in abyssum & clausit. Alter Syrus Graecum ταρταρώσας retinuit.

Παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τετηρημένους. Vulg. reddidit, tradidit cruciandos in iudicium reservari. Sed in Graeco nihil est, quod participio cruciandos respondeat. Sanè Robertus Stephanus citat Codd. quosdam Graecos, in quibus legatur, εἰς κρὶσιν κολαζομένους τηρεῖνin iudicium puniendos reservari, quod participium etiam occurrit apud Augustinum lib. 11. de Civ. DEI cap. 33. de Nat. boni cap. 33. & apud Fulgentium lib. 2. ad Thrasim. sed illustrationis gratiâ ab illis textui est adiectum, Graeci enim Codd. qui illud habent, pauciores sunt & dubiae fidei.

Pro Τετηρημένουςservatos quidam Codd. Graeci legunt τηρουμένουςservandos, sive qui servantur. Ex eo colligit Gagnaeus, pro τηρουμένουςeo tempore, quo vulgata versio fuit adornata, lectum fuisseτειρουμένουςafflictos, vexatos, pro quo Interpres posuerit cruciandos. Sed coniectura haec fallax est, cùm in loco parallelo Iudae v. 6. habeatur idem verbum τετήρηκεν in praeterito positum, quod confirmat usitatam Codicum nostrorum lectionem τετηρημένους. Idem ergo est εἰς κρίσιν τετήρηκεν, quâ phrasi utitur Iudas & παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τετηρημένους, quâ phrasi h. l. utitur Petrus. Iudas d. l. addidit, εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας, per quam diem extremi iudicii indigitat, ex quo etiam Syrus hoc loco ἐξηγήσεως causâ addidit, [לדינאדשונקא]in iudicium tormenti, nisi malimus dicere, hoc, ut & alia plura, desumtum esse ex vers. vulgata, quae addidit participium cruciandos.

Coeterùm quòd Angeli lapsi dicuntur catenis caliginis ταρταρωσάμενοι illud quidam sensu eo accipiunt, quod validissimis qs. catenis, ê caelo in infernum detracti sint, inque eo ad diem iudicii velut in obscuro quodam carcere detineantur, quâ ratione illudσειραῖς ζόφουaccipitur ut ablativus instrumenti ac refertur ad participiumταρταρώσας, quem sensum etiam secutus videtur Vulgatus Interpres, qui reddidit, rudentibus inferni in tartarum detractos. Sed rectius dicitur, verba illa σειραῖς ζόφου coniungenda cum verbo παρέδωκε vel cum participio τετηρημένους, ut sit sensus, tradidit eos catenis caliginis reservatos, h. e. carceri tenebricoso mancipatos, inque eo usque ad diem iudicii reservandos, quam expositionem confirmat locus parallelus Iudae v. 6. Angelos lapsos in iudicium magnae diei vinculis aeternis sub caligine reservavit.

## 2:5
Connection. 1. This is another example of divine wrath proposed in the antediluvian men, namely in the ancient world, which was in the times of Noah, by which Peter confirms that those false teachers will by no means escape judgment and destruction.

2. He inserts indeed ἀντιθετικῶς an example of divine grace, proposed in Noah, whom GOD wonderfully preserved together with his family in the ark at the time of the flood. For just as by the example of divine wrath, proposed in the men destroyed by the flood, he wished to terrify false teachers and their followers and invite them to repentance; so by the example of divine grace proposed in Noah, preserved at the time of the flood, he wished to console and lift up those who remain constant in the truth and on this account experience the hatreds and persecutions of the world.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο. The Vulgate rendered it, he did not spare the original world. But it rendered the same word ἀρχαῖος Matth. 5. vers. 21. and elsewhere throughout as ancient, in which way it ought to have rendered it here also. He did not spare the ancient or primitive world. By the name of world, however, are understood the men dwelling in the world, and by the name of the ancient or primitive world, those men who lived before the flood and miserably perished, overwhelmed by the waters of the flood. The Syriac rendered it [עלמא קדמיא] the former world, so that the antediluvian world is understood as the former, the postdiluvian as the latter. The particle εἰ must be understood and supplied regarding this member from the preceding verse, If God did not spare the ancient world.

Ἀλλ' ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξε. The little word ὄγδοον is to be referred to the word ἐφύλαξεν he preserved the eighth, that is, together with seven others who were with him in the ark, namely his wife, three sons, and three daughters-in-law. Plutarch on Pelopidas, εἴς οἰκίαν δωδέκατος κατελθὼν the twelfth having entered the house, that is, with eleven companions. Polybius book 16. Διονησιδώρος τρίτος ἀτενήξατο he swam out with two others. Bede in his commentary on this book: It is clear to all that Noah was born in the tenth generation from Adam, but he calls him the eighth, because eight men escaped the flood, of whom he was one. The Apostle undoubtedly refers to that which in the former Epistle chap. 3. vers. 20. in the ark built in the days of Noah eight souls were saved. One of the Syrian Interpreters expressed it by the cardinal number [דתמניא] the eighth, but the other by the ordinal [תמיניא]

In the word κήρυκος there is emphasis, for it signifies a public herald, whose προσκείμενα are 1. to be sent away by another and indeed by a Ruler to announce something. 2. to be fortified with public authority. 3. to announce something with a public and clear voice. All these things suit Noah, who was a Teacher sent by GOD, and surrounded with singular authority, and who intrepidly announced to the incredulous and impious world divine threats concerning the imminent flood. The Syrian has the noun [כרוזא] which signifies a herald and preacher. Acts 15. v. 21. 1. Tim. 2. v. 7.

Κατακλυσμόν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας. The flood is called by the Hebrews מבול Gen. 6. v. 17. which R. Solomon derives from בלה he confounded, because through it all these lower things were confounded. R. D. Kimhi derives it from נבל to wither, to flow down, in that the powers of things born from the earth were thereby greatly diminished, and that the flood caused flowers and fruits to flow down from the trees. The Greek κατακλυσμὸς signifies an inundation or a washing away, i.e., a huge flooding of waters, ἀπὸ τοῦ κατακλύζειν, which is to wash away, to cleanse, to overwhelm. The Syrian renders [טופנא] inundation.

By κόσμον ἀσεβῶν is understood that whole multitude of the impious, which lived in the times immediately preceding the flood, and by their sins brought the waters of the flood upon themselves, in which way the little word κόσμου is almost taken James 3. v. 6. The participle ἐπάξας the Vulgate rendered bringing in, but in the Greek it is an aorist, after he had brought in.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Alterum hoc est divinae irae exemplum in hominibus antediluvianis, in prisco scil. mundo, qui fuit Noë temporibus, propositum, quo Petrus confirmat, falsos illos doctores iudicium & exitium minimè effugituros.

2. Inserit verò ἀντιθετικῶς exemplum gratiae divinae, propositum in Noaho, quem DEUS unà cum familia sua tempore diluvii mirabiliter in arca custodivit. Ut enim exemplo irae divinae, in hominibus per diluvium perditis proposito, falsos doctores & eorum asseclas terrere & ad paenitentiam invitare; ita exemplo gratiae divinae proposito in Noaho tempore diluvii conservato eos, qui in veritate constantes manent & hoc nomine mundi odia & persecutiones experiuntur, consolari & erigere voluit.

Textus expositio. Καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο. Vulg. reddidit, mundo originali non pepercit. Sed eandem vocem ἀρχαῖοςMatth. 5. vers. 21. & alibi passim reddidit per antiquus, quo modo etiam h. l. reddere debebat. Mundo antiquo vel prisco non pepercit. Intelliguntur autem nomine mundi homines in mundo degentes & nomine mundi antiqui prisci illi homines, qui ante diluvium vixerunt, ac diluvii aquis obruti miserè perierunt. Syrus reddidit [עלמא קדמיא]mundo priori, ut mundus antediluvianus intelligatur prior, postdiluvianus posterior. Subaudienda autem ac reperenda circa hoc membrum ex versiculo praecedente particula εἰSi Deus prisco mundo non pepercit.

Ἀλλ' ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξε. Vocula ὄγδοον referenda ad verbum ἐφύλαξενservavit octavum hoc est unà cum septem aliis, qui cum ipso erant in arca videlicet uxor, tres filii & tres nurus. Plutarchus de Pelopida, εἴς οἰκίαν δωδέκατος κατελθὼνduodecimus ingressus domum, id est, cum undecim comitibus. Polybius lib. 16. Διονησιδώρος τρίτος ἀτενήξατοcum duobus aliis enatavit. Beda in comm. hunc l. Constat omnibus, quia Noë decimâ ab Adam generatione natus est, sed octavum eum nominat, quia octo homines diluvium evaserunt, ê quibus ille unus erat. Respicit procul dubio Apostolus ad id, quod in priore Epistola cap. 3. vers. 20. in arca diebus Noë fabricatâ octo animas servatas esse. Unus ex Syris Interpretibus expressit per numerum Cardinalem [דתמניא]octavum, alter verò per ordinalem [תמיניא]

In voce κήρυκος emphasis est, significat enim publicum praeconem, cuius προσκείμενα sunt 1. ablegari ab alio & quidem â Dynasta ad aliquid annunciandum. 2. munitum esse publicâ autoritate. 3. publicâ & clarâ voce aliquid denunciare. Haec omnia Noaho conveniunt, qui fuit Doctor â DEO missus, ac singulari autoritate circumdatus, quique incredulo & impio mundo intrepidè divinas comminationes de imminente diluvio denunciavit. Syrus habet nomen [כרוזא] quod praeconem ac praedicaetorem significat. Act. 15. v. 21.1. Tim. 2. v. 7.

Κατακλυσμόν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας. Diluvium Hebraeis vocatur מבולGen. 6. v. 17. quod R. Salomo deducit â בלהconfudit, quia per illud omnia haec inferiora fuêre confusa. R. D. Kimhi deducit â נבלmarcescere, defluere, eò quòd vires terrâ nascentium eodem fuerint plurimum diminutae, quòdque diluvium fecerit, ut flores & fructus ex arboribus defluerent. Graecum κατακλυσμὸς significat illuviem vel illuvionem, h. e. ingentem aquarum inundationem, ἀπὸ τοῦ κατακλύζειν, quod est proluere, mundare, obruere. Syrus redd. [טופנא]inundatio.
