Per κόσμον ἀσεβῶν intelligitur tota illa impiorum multitudo, quae temporibus diluvium proximè antegressis vixit, suisque peccatis aquas diluvii sibi superinduxit, quo ferè modo vocula κόσμου accipitur Iac. 3. v. 6. Participium ἐπάξας vulg. reddidit inducens, Sed in Graeco est aoristus, postquam induxisset.

## 2:6
Connection. This is the third example by which Peter confirms that false teachers and their followers, impious men, will not escape the judgment of GOD, namely the example of the Sodomites and the remaining inhabitants of the Pentapolis, which Jude also uses in Epist. v. 7.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Φομόῤῥας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν. The little word εἰ is also to be understood in this verse from v. 4. preceding. For the sentence still hangs: it must also be understood in this ἀνανταποδότῳ consequent, that indeed He will punish the false teachers also.

Sodom (in the plural) Gomorrah (in the singular) Admah, Zeboiim & Zoar, the five cities, called the Pentapolis from that, had deserved to be consumed on account of the sins of their inhabitants by sulfur & fire sent down from heaven; and in the former four the judgment of God was given execution, as appears from Gen. 19. v. 24.Deut. 29. v. 23.Oseae. 11. v. 8.Iudae v. 7. where Admah & Zeboiim are joined to Sodom & Gomorrah, but the fifth, namely Zoar, was preserved by the prayers of Lot, as is evident from Gen. 19. v. 21. To that horrible example of divine wrath Peter in this place refers those to whom he writes, so that from it they may gather that those who are joined to the Sodomites in guilt will also be their partners in punishment.

Πὸλεις τεφρώσας. The Vulgate rendered reducing to ashes. But in the Greek it is properly, having reduced to ashes, or after he had reduced to ashes. The verb τεφρόω occurs nowhere in the Scriptures other than in this place, but it signifies I reduce to ashes, whence the 1st aorist of the active verb τεφρώσας (which Peter uses in this place) is explained by Suidas ἐμπρήσας, σποδώσας; τεφρωθεὶς in the passive it is reduced to ashes, turned to ash. Luther rendered zu Aschen gemacht / it could also be rendered eingeäschert. The Syrian has [אוקד] from the root [יקד] he set on fire, he burned, for those things which are burned are reduced to ashes. The other Syrian translates by [דחיא] which Dionysius interprets, he made them ashes or rather dust very fine & thin. Psal. 35. v. 5.

Καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν by overturning or by subversion he condemned, he punished by overturning from the foundations. Luther Er hat sie umbgekehret und verdammet. καταστρέφειν is to subvert, to overturn. Matth. 21. v. 12.Marc. 11. v. 15. which verb the LXX use concerning the destruction of the Sodomites Gen. 19. v. 25.29.Deut. 29. v. 23.Esai. 13. v. 19.Ierem. 49. vers. 17.cap. 50. v. 40. thence καταστροφὴ, by which word the same ones use for איד destruction, perdition, devastation Iob. 21. v. 17. for הפכה which verb Moses Gen. 19. v. 29. & in this place the Syrian use in the description of the Sodomitic destruction.

Ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν τεθεικὼς. Some establish such a distinction between ὑπὸδειγμα καὶ παράδειγμα, that παράδειγμα is an example of imitation, ὑπόδειγμα but a monument or warning of a thing to be avoided. Whence they think that Peter used the word ὑποδείγματος, not παραδείγματος. But this distinction is not perpetual. Christ John 13. verse 15. & James chap. 5. v. 10. also use the word ὑποδείγματος for an example of imitation. This observation is more elegant, that the word ὑποδείγματος in this place includes the meaning of a type, in which sense it is used Heb. 8. v. 5. chap. 9. v. 23. For that Sodomite subversion was a typical example, prefiguring the punishment of hellfire, which awaits all the impious, which explanation is gathered from the parallel passage Jude v. 7. ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γομόῤῥα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις &c. πρόκεινται τεῖγμα πυρός αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι.

Μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν The Vulgate rendered it, of those who are going to act impiously. It is more correctly rendered an example (of his wrath & of punishment most certainly prepared) for the impious who were to follow, or for those who might wish to act impiously, he set. The Syriac, when he set a demonstration for the impious who were to be. Luther. Den Gottlosen / die hernach kommen werden.

Latin:

Connexio. Tertium hoc est exemplum, quo Petrus confirmat, falsos doctores & eorum asseclas, homines impios, DEI iudicium non evasuros, videlicet exemplum Sodomitarum & reliquorum Pentapoleos inhabitatorum, quo etiam utitur Iudas Epist. v. 7.

Textus expositio. Καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Φομόῤῥας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν. Vocula εἰ etiam in hoc versiculo subaudienda ex v. 4. praeced. Pendet enim adhuc sententia: subintelligendum etiam in hoc ἀνανταποδότῳ consequens, utique & falsos doctores puniet.

Sodoma (in plurali) Gomorrha (in singulari) Adama, Seboim & Segor quinque civitates, Pentapolis ex eo dictae, propter peccata in colarum sulphure & igne caelitus demisso absumi meruerant; ac in prioribus quatuor iudicium Dei executioni fuit datum, ut apparet ex Gen. 19. v. 24.Deut. 29. v. 23.Oseae. 11. v. 8.Iudae v. 7. ubi Adama & Seboim Sodomis & Gomorrhae coniunguntur, sed quinta, videlicet Segor, precibus Lothi fuit conservata, ut constat ex Gen. 19. v. 21. Ad horribile illud irae divinae exemplum Petrus hoc loco eos, ad quos scribit, remittit, ut ex eo colligant, illos, qui Sodomitis coniunguntur in culpa, fore etiam ipsorum socios in poena.

Πὸλεις τεφρώσας. Vulg. reddidit in cinerem redigens. Sed in Graeco propriè est, in cinerem redactas, vel postquam in cinerem redegisset. Verbum τεφρόω nuspiam in Scripturis alibi quàm hoc loco occurrit, significat autem in cinerem redigo, unde aoristus 1. verbi activi τεφρώσας (quo Petrus h. l. utitur) apud Suidam exponitur ἐμπρήσας, σποδώσας; τεφρωθεὶς in passivo est in cinerem redactus, cinefactus. Luth. reddidit zu Aschen gemacht / posset etiam reddi eingeäschert. Syrus habet [אוקד] â rad. [יקד]succendit, combussit, quae enim comburuntur, in cinerem rediguntur. Alter Syrus vertit per [דחיא] quod Dionysius interpretatur, fecit eos cineres vel potius pulverem valde minutum & tenuem.Psal. 35. v. 5.

Καταστροφῇ κατέκρινενeversione sive subversione damnavit, funditus evertendo punivit. Luth. Er hat sie umbgekehret und verdammet.καταστρέφειν est subvertere, evertere. Matth. 21. v. 12.Marc. 11. v. 15. quo verbo de excidio Sodomorum LXX utuntur Gen. 19. v. 25.29.Deut. 29. v. 23.Esai. 13. v. 19.Ierem. 49. vers. 17.cap. 50. v. 40. inde καταστροφὴ, quâ voce iidem utuntur pro אידinteritus, perditio, vastitasIob. 21. v. 17. pro הפכה quo verbo Moses Gen. 19. v. 29. & h. l. Syrus in descriptione excidii Sodomitici utuntur.

Ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν τεθεικὼς. Quidam inter ὑπὸδειγμα καὶ παράδειγμα tale discrimen statuunt, quòdπαράδειγμαsit exemplum imitationis,ὑπόδειγμαverò monimentum sive monitorium rei vitandae. unde existimant, Petrum singulari consilio usum voceὑποδείγματος,nonπαραδείγματος. Sed discrimen hoc non est perpetuum. Christus Ioh. 13. vers. 15. & Iacobus cap. 5. v. 10. voce ὑποδείγματος etiam pro imitationis exemplo utuntur. Concinnior haec est observatio, quòd ὑποδείγματος vox hoc loco includat significationem typi, quo sensu usurpatur Hebr. 8. v. 5.cap. 9. v. 23. Subversio enim illa Sodomitica fuit exemplum typicum, praefigurans poenam ignis infernalis, quae manet omnes impios, quae explicatio colligitur ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 7.ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γομόῤῥα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις &c. πρόκεινται τεῖγμα πυρός αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι.

Μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν Vulg. reddidit, eorum, qui impiè acturi sunt. Rectiùs redditur exemplum (irae suae & poenae certissimè paratae) impiis secuturis, vel illis, qui impiè agere velint, posuit. Syrus, cùm demonstrationem impiis, qui futuri essent, posuit. Luther. Den Gottlosen / die hernach kommen werden.

## 2:6-9 Questions and observations
Observations. 1. The monuments of the Sodomite conflagration are the apples which grow in that region today. For the whole Sodomite land remained scorched after that conflagration; and the apples, which that region produces, entice with their external appearance, but at the touch of the hands they vanish into embers or ashes, as if the original fire still exists there. Egesippus book 4 of the History of the destruction of the city, chapter 18. You may see there apples green in appearance, formed clusters of grapes, so that they generate in those looking at them a desire for eating; if you take them, they crack open and are resolved into ash, and stir up smoke, as if they were still burning. Augustine book 21 of the City of GOD, chapter 5. They write that apples are indeed born in the soil of Sodom, and reach the appearance of maturity, but when tested by a bite or pressure, they vanish into smoke and embers as the skin cracks open. Ordinary Gloss on this place. These cities were reduced to fire in a twofold way, because both first He reduced them with the surrounding lands to ash through a conflagration: and when the waves of the dead sea later covered the places of the conflagration, He wished to preserve the region situated around them as a species of ancient punishment. For there grow most beautiful apples, which also generate a desire for eating in those looking at them; if you pluck them, they crack open and are resolved into ash, and stir up smoke, as if they were still burning. Similar things occur not only among Ecclesiastical writers, Tertullian in Apology, chapter 40, the Author on the wonders of scripture, book 1, chapter 10, Orosius book 1 of Histories, chapters 5 and 6, but also profane ones, Solinus chapter 48, Cornelius Tacitus book 21 of Histories, Pliny book 5 of Natural History, chapter 16, Strabo book 16, Aristotle book 2 of Meteorology.

2. In the Sodomite conflagration a type of infernal fire is proposed, Jude Epistle verse 7, because the impious, who insist on the footsteps of the Sodomites, are to be cast at some time into the lake of fire and sulfur. Apoc. 19. vers. 20. Bede in the commentary on this place: The fire, which punished the Sodomites once, shows clearly what the impious are to suffer without end. Salvianus book 2 on providence teaches, GOD wished to declare in the present that which is the future judgment, when He sent hell from heaven upon the impious people.

3. By sulfur the stench of sins was signified and punished; by fire the heat of lust. Gregory book 4 of morals, chapter 10.

4. Those who are afflicted with punishments by the Magistrate, παραδειγματίζονται Matth. 1. vers. 19. examples are established, by looking to which others may guard themselves from similar offenses. For the same end GOD sends punishments upon the Sodomites and other impious ones. Thence men are so often referred to this example of divine wrath proposed in the Sodomitic conflagration. Deut. 29. v. 23.cap. 32. v. 32.Psal. 107. v. 34.Esai. 1. v. 9.cap. 3. v. 9.cap. 13. v. 19.Ierem. 23. v. 14.cap. 49. v. 18.cap. 50. v. 40. Threnor. 4. v. 6. Ezech. 16. v. 46.Oseae. 11. v. 8.Amos. 4. v. 11.Soph. 2. v. 9.Matth. 10. v. 15.cap. 11. v. 23.Luc. 10. v. 12.cap. 17. v. 29.Rom. 9. v. 29.Apoc. 11. v. 8. book 4. Esdr. cap. 2. v. 8.

5. Therefore, Histories concerning public punishments for sins are admonitions concerning punishments imminent on account of sins, unless by serious repentance they are averted in time. For GOD is immutable and always remains the same.Psal. 102. v. 28.

6. There is no region so pleasant and cultivated, to which devastation does not threaten, if its inhabitants indulge in notorious and public crimes. Lev. 18. v. 28. GOD turns a fruitful land into saltiness because of the wickedness of those dwelling in it, says the Royal Prophet Psal. 107. v. 34. Before the subversion, Sodom and Gomorrah were like the Paradise of the Lord.Gen. 13. v. 10. but on account of the sins of the inhabitants they were reduced to ashes.

7. It is grave and troublesome for the pious to dwell in the midst of the impious, since their life and morals differ greatly. Psal. 120. v. 5. & 6.Ezech. 2. v. 6.Sap. 2. v. 15. & 16.

8. Chrysostom on Psalm 11. Therefore we admire Abraham, therefore Lot, therefore Moses, because they appeared as stars in the deep night, and as roses among thorns, and sheep among innumerable wolves. ibid. As nothing is more difficult than to drive a ship in the opposite direction when the wind is blowing back and the heat is holding it: so nothing is more laborious than to struggle strenuously against those impelling one to evil and to be promoted into good. Gregory book 1. moral. cap. 1. It is not very praiseworthy to be good with the good, but to be good with the bad. For just as it is of a graver fault not to be good among the good: so it is of immense praise to have been good even among the bad. Hence Peter extolled Lot with great praises, because he found a good man among the reprobate &c. hence the holy Church is praised by the voice of the Bridegroom, when it is said to her: As a lily among thorns: so is my beloved among the daughters,Cant. 2. v. 2. Bernard sermon 48. on Cant. It is no mediocre title of virtue, To live among the wicked and to retain the brightness of innocence among the malicious. To move among thorns and not be harmed in the least, is of divine power, not of your virtue.Apoc. 2. vers. 13.

9. Therefore, by the example of Lot we are warned, that we do not allow ourselves to be moved by the multitude of sinners, so that we might be involved in the same impiety with them, but rather that we shine in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, as lights. Phil. 2. v. 15.

10. The pious are tormented by the wicked works of the impious for three reasons. For they grieve first at the insult to GOD, with which the impious afflict Him. Secondly, at the tyranny of Satan, by whom they are led as captives. Thirdly, at the eternal damnation of the impious, to which they render themselves liable.

11. Even to the saints cling the infirmities of the flesh, on account of which, however, they are not cast away by GOD, nor do they lose the name of the righteous. Lot offers his daughters to the Sodomites, he weaves delays in his departure, etc., yet he is called righteous.

12. On account of the pious, GOD also does good to their relatives and friends. Not only Lot, but also his wife and daughters are freed from the Sodomite fire, and indeed the same benefit is offered to his sons-in-law. Actor. 27. v. 24. The Angel of the Lord says to Paul, GOD has granted you all who sail with you.

13. Chrysostom, homily 2 on repentance, explaining what kind of person Job was in the land of Uz, that is, living in a region given over to idolatry, speaks of him thus: He was a dove in the midst of hawks, a sheep in the midst of wolves, a star in the midst of clouds, a lily in the midst of thorns, a sprout of righteousness in a town of iniquity. The same can be said of Lot living among the Sodomites.

14. The souls of the righteous are tormented by the wicked works of the impious, which they are forced to experience with their eyes and ears. For where there is true love of GOD, there also is zeal for righteousness. Psal. 119. v. 53.Trembling has seized me because of the impious who forsake your law. v. 158. I saw the transgressors and I pined away, because they did not keep your words.2. Cor. 11. v. 29. Paul says, on account of the scandals and apostasy of others he is burned. Compare Ezech. 9. v. 4. Those who can hear horrible blasphemies against GOD with a calm mind and behold abominable crimes without indignation, in them the zeal for justice and piety is extinguished. But another Spirit, another affection reigns in the pious.

15. The soul of Lot was tormented from day to day. Indeed, the pious are compelled to complain with Asaph, Psal. 73. vers. 14.I have been plagued all the day, and my chastisement is renewed every morning. But let them consider, that also the mercies of GOD are new every morning.Thren. 3. vers. 23.

16. August. in the preface to Psal. 69.For neither did that holy Lot in Sodom suffer bodily persecution from anyone, etc. his persecution was the evil deeds of the Sodomites. From there he proves that the persecutions of wicked scandals are worse than those of tyrants who slaughter bodies.

17. To despise the ministers of the word, and to afflict them, is a sin of such a kind, on account of which punishments are drawn upon a whole region.

18. Beda in h. l. It is to be noted, that Blessed Peter in this place follows the example of the Lord's teaching. For the Lord himself also in the Gospel, speaking of the day of judgment, brings to memory the sudden arrival of either the flood or the Sodomite fire, where the just were delivered, but the reprobate were caught in the snare of unexpected destruction.

19. The pious βασανίζουσι in this age, the impious in the future. Luc. 16. vers. 23.when he was ἐν βασάνοις. Apoc. 14. vers. 11.And the smoke βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν ascends in the age. But there is a great βασανισμὸν difference between the two. To the pious it is sent βασανισμὸς for testing, to the impious for damnation. The βασανισμὸς of the former is temporal, but that of the latter is eternal.

20. The providence and kindness of GOD shines forth most especially from the fact that He knows how to preserve the pious in public calamities. Psal. 26. v. 9.Psal. 34. v. 20.Psal. 91. v. 7.Ierem. 38. v. 2.cap. 45. v. 5.Ezech. 9. v. 6.Amos. 3. v. 12.

21. The pious are not preserved from all distresses and adversities, but are delivered out of them, so that the help of GOD may be more illustrious. Thus Abraham was delivered out of Ur of the Chaldeans Gen. 11. v. 31.Iudith. 5. v. 6. Jacob from his brother Esau Gen. 27. v. 32. Joseph out of the pit Gen. 37. v. 28. and out of prison Gen. 41. v. 2. David out of the hands of Saul 1. Sam. 18. and of Absalom 2. Sam. 18. the three children out of the Babylonian furnace v. 49. Daniel out of the lions' den. Dan. 6. v. 22.

22. In three ways especially does God his beloved out of calamities snatches away. For either He calls them to Himself from this life before public calamities and punishments for sins may rush in, or He miraculously preserves the pious immune from them in public calamities, or He infuses interior consolation into their hearts, by which they may sustain themselves, even if they are most greatly involved in the same calamities in a time of war or plague,

23. Johannes Huss in comm. h. l. When you pass through the waters, the rivers will not cover you. Behold the deliverance of Noah. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned. Behold the deliverance of Lot. Esai. 43. v. 2.

24. The impious, even if they may delight for a time, are reserved for eternal torments. That which delights them is momentary; that which torments is eternal.

Latin:

Observationes. 1. Incendii Sodomitici monumenta sunt poma, quae in illa regione hodie nascuntur. Tota enim terra Sodomitica post incendium illud torrida perseveravit; & poma, quae regio illa profert, externâ specie blandiuntur, sed ad manus tactum in favillas, cineresve evanescunt, q. pristinus adhuc ignis illic existat. Egesippus lib. 4. Hist. de excid. urbis cap. 18. Spectes illic specie poma viridantia, formatos uvarum racemos, ut edendi generent spectantibus cupiditatem; si capias, fatiscunt ac resolvuntur in cinerem, fumumque excitant, q. adhuc ardeant. August. lib. 21. de Civ. DEI cap. 5. Poma in solo Sodomorum gigni quidem scribunt, & ad maturitatis faciem pervenire, sed morsu, pressuve tentata in fumum ac favillam corio fatiscente evanescere. Gloss. ordin. in h. l. Hae civitates dupliciter in ignem sunt redactae, quia & primò eas per incendium cum adiacentibus terris in cinerem redegit: & cùm loca incendii postmodùm mortui maris undae contexerint, servare adhuc voluit regionem circa positam speciem priscae poenae. Naescuntur enim poma pulcherrima, quae & edendi cupiditatem spectantibus generant; si carpas, fatiscunt & resolvuntur in cinerem, fumumque excitant, q. adhuc ardeant. Similia occurrunt non solum apud Scriptores Ecclesiasticos, Tertullian. in Apolog. cap. 40. Autorem de mirabilibus script. lib. 1. cap. 10. Orosium lib. 1. Histor. cap. 5. & 6. sed etiam profanos, Solinum cap. 48. Cornelium Tacitum lib. 21. Histor. Plinium lib. 5. N. H. cap. 16. Strabonem lib. 16. Aristotelem lib. 2. Meteor.

2. In Sodomitico incendio proponitur typus ignis infernalis, Iudae Epist. vers. 7. quòd impii, qui vestigiis Sodomitarum insistunt, in stagnum ignis ac sulphuris aliquando coniiciendi sint. Apoc. 19. vers. 20. Beda in comm. huius loci: Ignis, qui Sodomitas semel puniit, ostendit patenter, quid impii sint sine sine passuri. Salvianus lib. 2. de provid. docet, in praesenti illud quod futurum est, voluisse DEUM declarare iudicium, quando super impium populum gehennam misit ê caelo.

3. Sulphure significatus & punitus fuit peccatorum fetor; igne libidinis ardor. Gregorius lib. 4. moral. cap. 10.

4. Qui â Magistratu suppliciis afficiuntur, παραδειγματίζονται Matth. 1. vers. 19. exempla statuuntur, ad quae alii respicientes â similibus delictis sibi caveant. Eodem fine DEUS Sodomitis & aliis impiis poenas immittit. inde toties ad hoc irae divinae exemplum in Sodomitico incendio proposicum homines remittuntur. Deut. 29. v. 23.cap. 32. v. 32.Psal. 107. v. 34.Esai. 1. v. 9.cap. 3. v. 9.cap. 13. v. 19.Ierem. 23. v. 14.cap. 49. v. 18.cap. 50. v. 40. Threnor. 4. v. 6. Ezech. 16. v. 46.Oseae. 11. v. 8.Amos. 4. v. 11.Soph. 2. v. 9.Matth. 10. v. 15.cap. 11. v. 23.Luc. 10. v. 12.cap. 17. v. 29.Rom. 9. v. 29.Apoc. 11. v. 8. lib. 4. Esdr. cap. 2. v. 8.

5. Proinde Historiae de publicis peccatorum poenis sunt commonefactiones de imminentibus propter peccata suppliciis, nisi per seriam paenitentiam maturè eadem avertantur. DEUS enim est immutabilis ac semper manet idem ipse.Psal. 102. v. 28.

6. Nulla est regio tam amaena & exculta, cui non immineat vastatio, si illius habitatores sceleribus notoribus & publicis indulgeant. Lev. 18. v. 28.Ponit DEUS terram frugiferam in falsuginem propter malitiam inhabitantium in ea, inquit Regius Propheta Psal. 107. v. 34. Ante subversionem Sodoma & Gomorrha erant sicut Paradisus Domini.Gen. 13. v. 10. sed propter incolarum peccata in cineres sunt redacta.

7. Grave ac molestum est piis, in medio impiorum habitare, cùm vita & mores ipsorum plurimùm discrepent. Psal. 120. v. 5. & 6.Ezech. 2. v. 6.Sap. 2. v. 15. & 16.

8. Chrysostomus in Psal. 11. Propterea admiramur Abrahamum, propterea Lothum, propterea Mosen, quòd velut in profunda nocte stellae apparebant, & tanquam rosae inter spinas, & oves inter lupes innumerabiles. ibid. Ut nihil difficilius, quàm reflante vento & retinente aestu navem in contrarium impellere: sic nihil laboriosius, quâm malis ad malum impellentibus strenuè reluctarî & in honum promoveri. Gregorius lib. 1. moral. cap. 1. Non est valde laudabile, bonum esse cum bonis, sed bonum esse cum malis. Sicut enim gravioris culpae est, inter bonos bonum non esse: ita immensi est praeconii bonum, etiam inter malos extitisse. Hinc Petrus magnis Lothum laudibus extulit, quia bonum inter reprobos invenit &c. hinc sancta Ecclesia Sponsi voce laudatur, cùm ei dicitur. Sicut lilium inter spinas: sic amica mea inter silias,Cant. 2. v. 2. Bernhardus serm. 48. in Cant. Non mediocris titulus virtutis est, inter pravos vivere bonum & inter malignantes innocentiae retinere candorem. Versari inter spinas & minimè laedi, divinae potentiae est, non virtutu tuae.Apoc. 2. vers. 13.

9. Exemplo igitur Lothi monemur, ne multitudine peccantium moveri nos patiamur, ut eidem cum ipsis impietati involvamur, sed luceamus potius in medio nationis pravae & tortuosae, ut luminaria. Phil. 2. v. 15.

10. Pii iniquis impiorum operibus tribus de causis cruciantur. Dolent enim primò de DEI contumeliâ, quâ impii eum afficiunt. Secundò de Satanae Tyrannide, â quo illi velut captivi ducuntur. Tertiò de damnatione impiorum aeterna, cui semetipsos reddunt obnoxios.

11. Etiam sanctis adhaerent infirmitates carnis, propter quas tamen â DEO non abiiciuntur, nec iustorum nomen amittunt. Lothus filias Sodomitis offert, moras in egressu nectit &c. tamen vocatur iustus.

12. Propter pios DEUS etiam cognatis & amicis eorum benefacit. Non solùm Lothus, sed etiam ipsius uxor & filiae ex Sodomitico incendio liberantur, quin & generis ipsius idem beneficium offertur. Actor. 27. v. 24. Angelus Domini dicit Paulo. Donavit tibi DEUS omnes, qui navigant tecum.

13. Chrysostomus homil. 2. de paenit. explicans, qualis fuerit Iobus in terra Hus, h. e. in regione idololatriae dedita habitans, de eo sic loquitur. Columba fuit in medio accipitrum, ovis in medio luporum, stella in medio nubium, lilium in medio spinarum, germen iustitiae in oppido iniquitatis. Idem de Lotho inter Sodomitas habitante dici potest.

14. Animae iustorum torquentur iniquis operibus impiorum, quae oculis & auribus usurpare coguntur. Ubi enim verus DEI amor, ibi etiam iustititiae Zelus. Psal. 119. v. 53.Tremor apprehendit me super impiis derelinquentibus legem tuam. v. 158. Vidi praevaricantes & tabescebam, quia eloquia tua non custodierunt.2. Cor. 11. v. 29. dicit Paulus, propter aliorum scandala & apostasian sese uri. Confer Ezech. 9. v. 4. Qui horribiles in DEUM blasphemias aequo animo audire & abominabilia scelera sine indignatione spectare possunt, in illis iustitiae & pietatis Zelus est extinctus. Alius verò Spiritus, alius affectus regnat in piis.

15. Anima Lothi de die in diemtorquebatur. Nimirum pii cum Asapho conqueri coguntur, Psal. 73. vers. 14.Fui flagellatus tota, die & castigatio mea singulis diebus renovatur. Sed cogitent, etiam miserationes DEI quolibet diluculo esse novas.Thren. 3. vers. 23.

16. August. in praefat. Psal. 69.Neque enim & Loth ille sanctus in Sodomis ab aliquo corporalem consecutionem patiebatur &c. persecutio eius facta mala Sodomitarum erant. Inde probat, peiores esse persecutiones pravorum scandalorum, quàm Tyrannorum, corpora trucidantium.

17. Ministros verbi contemnere, eosque affligere, est eiusmodi peccatum, propter quod toti regioni poenae attrahuntur.

18. Beda in h. l. Notandum, quòd B. Petrus in hoc loco Dominici Magisterii sequitur exemplum. Et ipse enim Dominus in Evangelio de die iudicii loquens subitaneum vel diluvii velignis Sodomitici adventum ad memoriam deducit, ubi iusti liberati, reprobi autem sint inopinatae perditionis laqueo comprehensi.

19. Pii βασανίζουσι in hoc seculo, impii in futuro. Luc. 16. vers. 23.cum essetἐν βασάνοις.Apoc. 14. vers. 11.Eumusβασανισμοῦ αὐτῶνascendit in seculo. Magna verò inter utrumque βασανισμὸν differentia. Piis immittitur βασανισμὸς ad probationem, impiis ad damnationem. Illorum βασανισμὸς est temporalis, horum verò aeternus.

20. DEI providentia & benignitas vel maximè elucet ex eo, quod pios in publicis calamitatibus conservare novit. Psal. 26. v. 9.Psal. 34. v. 20.Psal. 91. v. 7.Ierem. 38. v. 2.cap. 45. v. 5.Ezech. 9. v. 6.Amos. 3. v. 12.

21. Pii non praeservantur ab omnibus angustiis & adversis, sed ex illis liberantur, ut auxilium DEI sit illustrius. Sic liberatus est Abraham ex Ur Chaldaeorum Gen. 11. v. 31.Iudith. 5. v. 6. Iacob de fratre Esau Gen. 27. v. 32. Ioseph ex cisterna Gen. 37. v. 28. & ex carcere Gen. 41. v. 2. David ex manibus Saulis 1. Sam. 18. & Absolonis. 2. Sam. 18. tres pueri ex fornace Babylonica v. 49. Daniel ex lacu leonum. Dan. 6. v. 22.

22. Tribus potissimùm modis Deus dilectos suos ex calamitatibus cripit. Vel enim ex hac vita eos ad se vocat, antequam publicae calamitates & poenae peccatorum ingruant, vel mirabiliter pios in publicis calamitatibus ab illis immunes conservat, vel interiorem consolationem cordibus eorum infundit, quâ sese sustentent, si vel maximè iisdem calamitatibus belli vel pestis tempore involvant ur,

23. Iohannes Huss in comm. h. l. Cum transieris aquas, flumina non operient te. Ecce liberatio Noahi. Cùm ambulaveris per ignem, non adureris. Ecce liberatio Lothi.Esai. 43. v. 2.

24. Impii etiamsi ad tempus delitientur, aeternis cruciatibus reservantur. Momentaneum est, quod ipsos delectat; aeternum, quod cruciat.

## 2:7
Connection. Just as in the second example of divine wrath, namely in the flood, the Apostle ἀντιθετικῶς had inserted an example of divine goodness & grace toward the pious, proposed in the preservation of Noah: so also in this third example of divine wrath, namely in the Sodomite destruction, he likewise inserts an example of divine goodness & grace toward the pious, shining forth in the preservation of Lot. By examples of wrath he terrifies the impious, by examples of grace he consoles the pious.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐῤῥύσατο. Just as he had called Noah, preserved in the flood, a preacher of righteousness: so he calls Lot, preserved in the Sodomite destruction, just; however, both were both just & a preacher of righteousness.

Καταπονούμενον. The word καταπονεῖσθαι, signifies to be oppressed, to be wearied, to be grievously afflicted. Act. 7. vers. 24. An Israelite oppressed by an Egyptian, to whom Moses came for aid, is called καταπονούμενος. 2. Maccab. 8. vers. 2. The Israelite people miserably harassed by enemies is called καταπονούμενος, where the Vulgate rendered, who was trodden down by all. In Laërtius, in the life of Lyco, νόσῳ καταπονηθεὶς is worn out and weakened by disease. The sense, therefore, is that the Sodomites were troublesome and grievously hostile to Lot in many ways, that they afflicted him harshly, and miserably wearied him, worn out with pain. Genes. 19. vers. 8. they themselves say, Now we will do worse to thee than to them; and they did violence to him exceedingly, partly to commit a nefarious crime with him, by dragging him away; partly by attempting to break down the doors, which he had closed behind him. The Syrian rendered, [דמתקפח הוא] who was bruised, or as it were, was beaten with blows. Luth. Sie thaten ihm alles Leid an.

Ὑπὸ τῆς ἀναστροφῆς from the conversation. The Syrian rendered [מן הופכא] which Etzelius translates from perversity. But it is more correctly rendered from the conversation, as it also is in the Greek text. For [הפך] in the Ithpahel [אתהפך] signifies to be occupied, to converse, Matth. 17. v. 22. Iohann. 3. v. 22. meanwhile we do not deny, Prov. 2. v. 14. cap. 16. v. 30. that it is used for perversity, which signification also fits the thing itself, of which it is treated in this place, very well, for the conversation of the Sodomites was depraved and perverse.

Τῶν ἀθέσμων The Vulgate rendered of the nefarious. But ἄθεσμοι are nefarious men, who care for neither law nor divine right, extremely flagitious and wicked men, who nefariously break through the barriers of honest laws. Some take it in the neuter gender, so that by τὰ ἄθεσμα those nefarious crimes which the Sodomites perpetrated are understood. But it is more correctly taken in the masculine gender, so that the Sodomites themselves are called ἄθεσμοι. According to Hesychius ἄθεσμος δίκη is ἄνομος δίκη, and it is said to be done to the same, which is done παρανόμως; According to Suidas ἄθεσμος or ἄθεσμος is ἄδικος. Therefore an opposition is made between Lot δίκαιον and the Sodomites ἀθέσμους or ἀδίκους, whose life and morals since from ἀθέσμως If the justice of Lot δὺς διὰ πασῶν differed, thence Lot was καταπονούμενος. from them. The Syrian translates of those who were [דלא נמוסא] without law. Luth. Die schändlichen Leute.

By Εἰ ἀσελγεία. Some Latin codices read, by injury and by luxurious conversation. Some, by shamelessness. Some, by injustice. The Greek ἀσελγεία properly denotes lasciviousness, impudicity, lusts. Rom. 13. v. 13. they are joined κοίτα καὶ ἀσελγείαι 2. Cor. 12. v. 21. ἀκαθαρσία, πορνεία, ἀσέλγεια. Gal. 5. v. 19. μοιχεία, πορνεία, ἀκαθαρσία, ἀσέλγεια. Eph. 4. v. 19. it is said of the gentiles, they delivered themselves τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης. Sap. 14. v. 26. in the commemoration of the nefarious outrages, committed by gentile idolaters, they are joined ψυχῶν μιασμὸς, γενέσεως ἐναλλαγή, γάμων ἀταξία, μοιχεία καὶ ἀσέλγεια, from the collation of which places, but especially from Gen. 19. v. 5. one can judge concerning the genuine signification of this word. Among profane writers ἀσελγὴς signifies the same as ὑβριστὴς who is petulantly and wantonly injurious: meanwhile as ὑβριστὴς, so also ἀσελγὴς is sometimes specially used for lascivious, who petulantly indulges in lusts and violent rapes. Athenaeus lib. 11. Lucian said ἀσελγέστεροι τῶν ὄνων, for this animal is most lustful. Among Philo lib. 1. de vita Mosis ἀσέλγεια it is used for obscene lust. The Syrian rendered it by [טנפותא] which signifies filth, impurity, uncleanness.

Latin:

Connexio. Sicut in secundo irae divinae exemplo, videlicet in diluvio, Apostolus ἀντιθετικῶς inserverat exemplum divinae bonitatis & gratiae erga pios, in Noahi conservatione propositum: ita quoque in hoc tertio irae divinae exemplo videlicet in excidio Sodomitico, itidem inserit exemplum divinae bonitatis & gratiae erga pios, in Lothi conservatione elucescens. Exemplis irae perterrefacit impios, exemplis gratiae consolatur pios.

Textus expositio. Καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐῤῥύσατο. Sicut Noahum in diluvio conservatum vocaverat iustitiae praeconem: ita Lothum in excidio Sodomitico conservatum vocat iustum; fuit autem uterque & iustus & iustitiae praeco.

Καταπονούμενον. Verbum καταπονεῖσθαι, significat opprimi, fatigari, graviter affligi.Act. 7. vers. 24. Israëlita ab Aegyptio oppressus, cui Moses venit in auxilium, vocatur καταπονούμενος.2. Maccab. 8. vers. 2. Israëliticus populus ab hostibus miserè divexatus vocatur καταπονούμενος, ubi Vulg. reddidit, qui ab omnibus calcabatur. Apud Laërtium in Lycone, νόσῳ καταπονηθεὶς est morbo confectus & debilitatus. Sensus igitur est, quòd Sodomitae multis modis Lotho fuerint molesti ac graviter infensi, quòd duriter eum afflixerint, ac dolore enectum miserè fatigaverint. Genes. 19. vers. 8. ipsi dicunt. Nunc malefaciemus tibi magis quàm illis; & fecerunt vim in ipsum valde, partim ad nefarium flagitium cum eo committendum, ipsum abripiendo; partim fores, quas post se clauserat, effringere conando. Syrus reddidit, [דמתקפח הוא]qui contundebatur, seu q. colaphis caedebatur. Luth. Sie thaten ihm alles Leid an.

Ὑπὸ τῆς ἀναστροφῆςâ conversatione. Syrus reddidit [מן הופכא] quod Etzelius vertit â perversitate. Sed rectiùs redditur â conversatione, quomodo etiam est in textu Graeco. [הפך] enim in Ithpahel [אתהפך] significat versari, conversari,Matth. 17. v. 22.Iohann. 3. v. 22. interim non negamus, Prov. 2. v. 14.cap. 16. v. 30. pro perversitate usurpari, quae significatio etiam rei ipsi, de qua hoc loco agitur, optimè congruit, Sodomitarum enim conversatio erat prava & perversa.

Τῶν ἀθέσμων Vulg. reddidit nefandorum. Sunt autem ἄθεσμοι homines nefarri, qui nec ius, nec fas curant, homines extremè flagitiosi atque improbi, qui legum honestarum repagula nefariè perfringunt. Quidam accipiunt in genere neutro, ut perτὰ ἄθεσμαintelligantur nefaria illa facinora, quae Sodomitae perpetrarunt. Sed rectiùs accipitur in genere masculino, ut ipsi Sodomitae dicantur ἄθεσμοι. Hesychio ἄθεσμος δίκη est ἄνομος δίκη, ac ἀθέσμως eidem fieri dicitur, quod fit παρανόμως; Suidae ἄθεσμος vel ἄθεσμος est ἄδικος. Fit ergo oppositio inter Lothum δίκαιον & Sodomitas ἀθέσμους sive ἀδίκους, quorum vita & mores cùm â Lothi iustitia δὺς διὰ πασῶν distiterint, inde Lothus ab illis fuit καταπονούμενος. Syrus vertit eorum qui erant[דלא נמוסא]sine lege. Luth. Die schändlichen Leute.

EiΕἰ ἀσελγεία. Quidam Codd. Latini legunt, iniuriâ ac luxuriosâ conversatione. Quidam, impuditâ. Quidam, iniustâ. Graecum ἀσελγεία propriè notat lasciviam, impudicitiam, libidines.Rom. 13. v. 13. coniunguntur κοίτα καὶ ἀσελγείαι2. Cor. 12. v. 21.ἀκαθαρσία, πορνεία, ἀσέλγεια.Gal. 5. v. 19.μοιχεία, πορνεία, ἀκαθαρσία, ἀσέλγεια.Eph. 4. v. 19. de gentilibus dicitur, tradiderunt seipsosτῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης.Sap. 14. v. 26. in commemoratione nefandorum flagitiorum, â gentilibus idololatris commissorum, coniunguntur ψυχῶν μιασμὸς, γενέσεως ἐναλλαγή, γάμων ἀταξία, μοιχεία καὶ ἀσέλγεια, ex quorum locorum collatione, praesertim verò ex Gen. 19. v. 5. de genuina huius vocis significatione iudicari potest. Apud profanos Scriptores ἀσελγὴς significat idem quod ὑβριστὴςqui petulanter protervè iniurius est: interim ut ὑβριστὴς, ita quoque ἀσελγὴς specialiter quandoque usurpatur pro lascivo, qui petulanter indulget libidinibus ac violentis stupris. Athenaeus lib. 11. Lucianus dixitἀσελγέστεροι τῶν ὄνων,hoc enim animal est libidinosissimum. Apud Philonem lib. 1. de vita Mosis ἀσέλγεια pro obscaena libidine usurpatur. Syr. reddidit per [טנפותא] quod significat spurcitiem, impuritatem, immunditiem.

## 2:8
Connection. The Apostle had said in the preceding verse that Lot, dwelling among the Sodomites, was just, and that he was gravely afflicted and as it were killed with grief by the lustful and impious conversation of the Sodomites. He declares both more fully in this verse, namely, both the justice of Lot and the wantonness of the Sodomites.

Exposition of the text. Βλέμματι γὰρ γαὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος, ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἐξ ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν. The word ἐβασάνιζεν the Vulgate version and Luther refer to the Sodomites, in the sense that they tormented the righteous soul of Lot with their wicked works. But this version is vehemently opposed by the fact that the word ἐβασάνιζεν is of the singular number, and that the rule of grammar does not seem to admit it, for what is this construction, 'By sight and hearing the righteous, etc., were tormenting the righteous soul with wicked works.'

To the former, some respond that for ἐβασάνιζεν it should be read in the plural ἐβασάνιζον. But all Greek codices consistently read in the singular ἐβασάνιζεν. But if, therefore, Luther's version were to be defended at all, it would have to be said either that it is an enallage of the singular number for the plural, which is frequent in the Scriptures (especially when a certain distribution is connoted. Job 12. v. 7. The beast shall teach i.e., each of the beasts shall teach. Esth. 9. v. 23. The Jews received i.e., each of the Jews received. Prov. 14. v. 1. The wise of women builds the house i.e., each of the wise women. Thus in this place, The Sodomite tormented i.e., each of the Sodomites tormented) or that the construction is referred to the sense, since the nominative governing the verb is not explicitly expressed in this way: The Sodomitic people tormented the soul of Lot.

To the latter, Gagnaeus responds that the nominatives ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐγκατοικῶν are placed for the genitives in this way: By sight and hearing of the righteous one dwelling among them, they were tormenting the righteous soul, which opinion of Gagnaeus also pleases Lorinus in his commentary on this place. But for nominatives to be placed for genitives in the Holy Scriptures is clearly unusual and infrequent. It would therefore be more conveniently answered that there is here a double ἔλλειψιν, both of the substantive verb ἦν, according to the customary Hebraism, in the first part of the verse; and of the relative pronoun οἱ in the latter part of the verse, in this way: By sight and hearing he was righteous, dwelling among those who were tormenting the righteous soul with their wicked works, i.e., Although Lot, dwelling among them, was righteous by sight and hearing, nevertheless they were tormenting his righteous soul with their wicked works.

But simpler and more convenient to the Greek text is the exposition by which the word ἐβασάνιζεν is referred to Lot himself, in the sense that Lot himself tormented his soul with the wicked works of the Sodomites, by hearing and seeing them: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ ἐβασάνιζεν. wherever he might have applied either his eyes or his ears, whatever he might perceive or hear, this very thing miserably tortured him. Which sense the Syrian paraphrast also seems to follow. According to this hypothesis, the article ο placed before the word δίκαιος is δεικτικὸς, that righteous man, namely Lot, tormented his soul.

It is objected to this exposition, that by this reasoning a harsh transposition of words must be established in the text, since those two nouns βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ placed at the beginning of the verse must be joined with ἀνόμοις ἔργοις at the end of the little verse. But besides the fact that hyperbata and transpositions are not unusual in the Apostolic Epistles, we are compelled by no necessity to descend to that harsher transposition. For those words βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ can be joined according to the natural series of the text with the noun ὁ δίκαιος, in the sense that Lot was righteous in sight and hearing, by which reasoning there is no need to establish a hyperbaton. B. Luther joins those words βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ with the participle ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, in this way: Because he was righteous and dwelt among them, so that he was forced to see and hear their crimes, thence his righteous soul was tormented.

In the word ψυχῆς there is a Hebraism: Lot the righteous tormented his righteous soul, that is, himself. Matth. 12. vers. 18.Luc. 1. v. 46.Hebr. 10. v. 38. The emphasis, however, is in the fact that Lot is said to have tormented his righteous soul with the wicked works of the Sodomites: for it is signified that the sword of sorrow passed through his soul when he was forced to behold and hear the crimes of the Sodomites. Luc. 2. vers. 35. In the word ἐβασάνιζεν there is a metaphor, drawn from torments. The Syrian has the word [שנק] he constricted, he distressed, he affected with straits, he tortured. The sense of the little verse therefore is this: For since Lot was righteous, and dwelling among them was forced to see and hear their crimes, from day to day he was excruciating his righteous soul with their wicked works, he was dragging out a life anxious and subject to perpetual sorrows, laboring no less than if he had been placed upon the rack.

Latin:

Connexio. Dixerat Apostolus in versu praeced. Lothum inter Sodomitas habitantem fuisse iustum, eundemque per libidinosam, & impiam Sodomitarum conversationem fuisse graviter afflictum ac dolore qs. enectum. Utrumque in hoc vers. pleniùs declarat, videlicet tum Lothi iustitiam, tum Sodomitarum proterviam.

Textus expositio. Βλέμματι γὰρ γαὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος, ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἐξ ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν. Verbum ἐβασάνιζεν Vulg. versio & Lutherus referunt ad Sodomitas, sensu eo, quòd illi iniquis suis operibus iustam animam Lothi cruciaverint. Sed huic versioni vehementer adversatur, quòd verbum ἐβασάνιζεν est numeri singularis, quòdque ratio Grammaticae eam non videatur admittere, quae enim haec constructio, Aspectu & auditu iustus &c. animam iustam iniquis operibus cruciabant.

Ad prius quidam respondent pro ἐβασάνιζενlegendum esse in pluraliἐβασάνιζον. Sed Graeci Codd. omnes constanter legunt in singulari ἐβασάνιζεν. Quod si ergo Lutheri versio omninò esset defendenda, dicendum foret, vel quòd sit enallage numeri singularis pro plurali, quae in Scripturis frequens (praesertim quando quaedam distributio connotatur. Iob. 12. v. 7.Iumenta docebit i. e. quodlibet iumentorum docebit. Esth. 9. v. 23.Iudaei recepit h. e. quisque Iudaeorum recepit. Prov. 14. v. 1.Sapientes feminarum aedificat domum i. e. quaeque sapientum. Sic hoc loco. Sodomitae cruciavit h. e. quilibet Sodomitarum cruciavit) vel quod constructio referatur ad sensum, cùm nominativus verbum regens disertè non exprimatur hoc modo. Populus Sodomiticus animam Lothi eruciavit.

Ad posterius respondet Gagnaeus, nominativosὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐγκατοικῶνponi pro genitivis hoc modo. Aspectu & auditu iusti inter ipsos habitantis animam iustam cruciabant, quae Gagnaei sententia placet etiam Lorino in comm. h. l. Sed nominativos pro genitivis poni in Scripturis Sacris est planè insolens atque infrequens. Commodiùs ergò responderetur, esse hîc duplicem ἔλλειψιν tum verbi substantivi ἦν, iuxta usitatum Hebraismum, in priore versiculi parte; tum pronominis relativi οἱ in posteriore versiculi parte, hoc modo. Aspectu & auditu iustus erat, habitans inter eos, qui animam iustam iniquis operibus cruciabant, h. e. Quamvis Lothus inter eos habitans aspectu & auditu esset iustus, nihilo tamen minùs iustam ipsius animam iniquis suis operibus cruciabant.

Sed simplicior & textui Graeco convenientior est expositio, quâ verbum ἐβασάνιζεν ad ipsum Lothum refertur, sensu eo, quod Lothus ipse animam suam iniquis Sodomitarum operibus, ea audiendo & videndo cruciaverit: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ ἐβασάνιζεν. quocunque vel oculos vel aures applicuisset, quicquid cerneret vel audiret, hoc ipsum miserè torquebat. quem sensum etiam Syrus paraphrastes sequi videtur. Iuxta hanc hypothesin articulus ο praemissus voci δίκαιος est δεικτικὸς,ille iustus sc. Lothus, animam suam cruciavit.

Opponitur huic expositioni, quòd haec ratione dura verborum traiectio in textu statuenda, cùm duo illa nominaβλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇin principio versus posita cumἀνόμοις ἔργοιςin fine versiculi sint coniungendae. Sed praeter quam quòd hyperbata & traiectiones in Epistolis Apostolicis non sint inusitatae, nullâ cogimur necessitate, ut ad duriorem illam traiectionem descendamus. Possunt enim verba illa βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ iuxta naturalem textus seriem coniungi cum nomine ὁ δίκαιος, sensu eo, quòd Lothus aspectu & auditu fuerit iustus, quâ ratione nullum opus est statuere hyperbatum. B. Lutherus verba illa βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ coniungit cum participio ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, hoc modo. Quia iustus erat & inter eos habitabat, ut cogeretur illorum scelera videre & audire, inde anima ipsius iusta cruciabatur.

In voce ψυχῆς est Hebraismus. Lothus iustus cruciabat animam suam iustam, hoc est, seipsum. Matth. 12. vers. 18.Luc. 1. v. 46.Hebr. 10. v. 38. Emphasis tamen in eo est, quod Lothus animam suam iustam iniquis Sodomitarum operibus cruciasse dicitur: significatur enim, quòd gladius doloris animam ipsius pertransierit, quando Sodomitarum facinora intueri & audire coactus fuit. Luc. 2. vers. 35. In verbo ἐβασάνιζεν est metaphora, â tormentis ducta. Syrus habet verbum [שנק]arctavit, anxit, angustiis affecit, torsit. Sensus ergo versiculi hic est. Cùm enim Lothus esset iustus, & inter illos habitans videre & audire ipsorum scelere cogeretur, de die in diem iustam suam animam iniquis illorum operibus excruciabat, anxiam & doloribus perpetuis obnoxiam vitam trahebat, non minùs laborans, quàm si equuleo fuisset impositus.

## 2:9
Connection. 1. The Apostle transfers the hypothesis to the thesis, and from the history of the flood and the Sodomite destruction, brought forward from the Mosaic Genesis in the preceding verses, he gathers two commonplaces, as we are accustomed to speak today. The former is that the Lord is able to rescue the godly from temptation, just as He saved Noah in the flood, and Lot in the Sodomite conflagration. The latter is that God is able to reserve the unrighteous for the day of judgment, having been removed from the midst through horrible punishment, just as He made manifest by the examples of the men drowned in the flood and the citizens of Sodom.

2. According to this method of connection, the Greek Scholia separate this verse from the preceding ones; and they complete the discourse, which had hung imperfectly from verse 4, in this way. If God did not spare the angels, nor the transgressing men, but saved Noah and Lot, therefore He will not spare the false teachers either, but will hand them over to destruction, but you, who are immune from their contagion, He will save and make safe.

3. It could, however, not absurdly be said that the sentence hanging until now from those words, If God did not spare the angels who sinned, etc. is now finally completed in this way. If God did not spare the angels and transgressing men of old, but reserved them, having been gravely punished, for the final judgment, but rescued Noah and Lot from dangers and adversities, certainly the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from temptation; but to reserve the unrighteous for the day of judgment. In that way, Bede in his commentary connects this verse with the preceding ones. Many, he says, verses are closed with one end, the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from temptation.

Exposition of the text. Οἶδε Κύριος εὐσεβεῖ ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι. By the word οἶδε the Apostle not only refers us to divine knowledge, wisdom, and power, because according to His infinite wisdom and power He has various ways by which He can rescue the godly from temptation; but also to divine grace and good pleasure, because this work, namely the liberation of the godly from dangers, is a work pleasing and acceptable to God. For words of knowledge among the Hebrews more often connote both the affection of the heart and the effect of the work. Psal. 1. v. ult.

By τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς are understood those who, insisting upon the footsteps of Noah and Lot, seek righteousness in Christ through true faith, and testifying to their faith by good works, serve GOD in true fear, study from the heart the righteousness of a good conscience and the holiness of life, and separate themselves from the company of the impious. The Syrian rendered it [דדחלים לה] those who fear him, namely God. For fear is more often used for the whole of divine worship. Gen. 31. v. 53.

For ἐκ πειρασμοῦ some Greek Codices read in the plural number ἐκ πειρασμοὺς, which is more emphatic. Furthermore, by πειρασμοὺς are understood dangers and adversities of every kind, straits of the inner mind and pressures of the body and exterior persecutions, all of which are sent upon the pious for the sake of temptation and probation, just as Peter says 1. Epist. 4. v. 12. that πύρωσις the heat of the cross πρὸς πειρασμὸν is sent. Thus Deut. 7. v. 19. the plagues of Egypt are called temptations. Tob. 2. v. 12. cap. 12. v. 3. the blindness of Tobias is called temptation. Christ Luc. 22. v. 28. calls his adversities temptations, in which he declares that the disciples remained constant with him. Sirach. 27. v. 6. it is called the temptation of tribulation. The Syrian rendered this place [מן אולצנא] from affliction, anguish, oppression, from the root [אלץ] to afflict, to straiten, to narrow.

Ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέρας κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν. Athanasius in the Disputation against Arius in the Council of Nicaea, Vol. 1, p. 83, cites this passage thus: οἶδεν ὁ θεὸς εὐσεβεῖς ῥυέσθαι, ἀνόμους δὲ τηρεῖν εἰς ἡμεραν κρίσεως κιλαζομένους αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ. But without a doubt he wished to cite not the words themselves, but the sentiment of the Apostle.

By ἀδίκους are understood those who, insisting upon the footsteps of the antediluvian men and the Sodomites, wickedly transgress the law of GOD, follow injustice and lusts, and torment the souls of the pious with their iniquitous works. The Syrian rendered it [עולא] from the root [עול] he acted iniquitously and perversely. 2. Cor. 7. v. 2.

By ἡμέραν κρίσεως is understood the day of the extreme and Universal judgment, which Christ will institute in his final coming. Actor. 17. v. 31, In this very Epistle c. 3. v. 7. Peter calls that day ἡμέραν κρίσεως καὶ ἀπωλείας τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνθρώπων. Jude in his Epistle v. 6. calls κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας, the judgment, which will be instituted on that great day.

Κολαζομένους The Vulgate rendered being punished. But in the Greek it is not future, but present, since no Codices read κολασομένους, but all have κολαζαμὲνους. The Syriac [כד משתנקין] after they have been punished; so that the sense may be, giving punishments, namely according to the soul in the underworld; or rather past, so that the sense may be, having been punished, that is, removed from the midst by horrible torment, for κολάζειν signifies to restrain and check the petulance of someone with punishments. Luther, having followed the Vulgate zu peinigen.

Q. In this place. 1. What was the impiety of the Sodomites, on account of which they were so horribly punished? Resp. The Holy Spirit Gen. 19. v. 13. describes it thus. The men of Sodom were evil and sinners before the Lord exceedingly, where their sins are exaggerated in a threefold way 1. by emphatic repetition. They were evil and sinners, which repetition is αὐξητικὴ. 2. By the expression of the divine name. They were sinners before the Lord, that is, most grave and greatest sinners, because those things which are attributed to GOD are great and excellent, Psal. 51. v. 3. or they were sinners before the Lord i. e. openly, publicly, they sinned in the very sight of GOD, Gen. 10. v. 9. or they sinned against the Lord, whose holy laws they nefariously and insolently transgressed, which agrees with the word ἀθέσμων. 3. By the addition of an adverb. They were sinners exceedingly, so much so that even their sins cried out to heaven. The Chaldean Paraphrast rendered it thus. The men of Sodom abused their riches and sinned with their bodies before the Lord exceedingly.

Q. 2. What was their ἀσέλγεια; Resp. It is evident from Gen. 19. v. 5. that they were ἀῤῥενοκοίται καὶ παιδεράσται, which wickedness Sap. 14. v. 26. is called γένεσεως ἐναλλαγὴ. Luther rendered it, Stumme Sünden / that they ought not even to be named before honest and chaste ears, from which place seems to be taken that Apostolic saying Rom. 1. v. 26. The women of the gentiles μετήλλαξεν changed the natural use, into that which is against Nature v. 27. Likewise also the males, having abandoned the natural use of the female, burned in their desires toward one another, males working shame with males. But especially does the parallel passage in the Epistle Jude v. 7. pertain here, in which the Sodomite ἀσέλγεια is described in this way: Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities in a similar manner ἐκπορνεύσασαι poured themselves out into fornication, having been heated up by fornicating, giving themselves over to fornication even to the point of exhaustion, because the preposition ἐκ intensifies the meaning, Sie haben sich ansgehuret / as Luther rightly rendered it: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, when they had gone after different flesh, when they had followed after other flesh, by which words κατ' εὐφημισμὸν the ἀῤῥενοκοίτων crime of the Sodomites is described. He calls it different flesh, because it was created by GOD for a different end and use, Rom. 1. v. 27.

Q. 3. Did any of the adult Sodomites perform penance?

Q. 4. Is it consistent with divine justice that infants and children were also consumed by this fire? Resp. These questions were dealt with in the exposition of chapter 19 of Genesis.

Q. 5. Why does the Apostle impress upon those seducers the example of divine wrath, publicly displayed in the destruction of the Sodomites? Resp. 1. Because in the Scriptures idolatry and heresy are called spiritual fornication and spiritual adultery. Since, therefore, GOD punished Sodomite lusts with fire and brimstone rained down from heaven, Peter leaves it to be gathered from that, that He will also punish with infernal fire those false Teachers who commit spiritual adultery. 2. In the following verses the Apostle attributes to those false Teachers that they have eyes full of adultery, that they entice in the lusts of the flesh, Jude accuses them that they themselves also similarly defile the flesh. Epistle v. 8.

Q. 6. What kind of righteousness was Lot's? Resp. It was. 1. Imputed righteousness, because he hoped in the promised Messiah, and believed that through Him the remission of sins was obtained by him. 2. Inchoate righteousness, because he demonstrated his faith by good works, inasmuch as together with Abraham his uncle he obeyed the divine command and abandoned his idolatrous homeland Gen. 13. v. 1. he received strangers with hospitality Gen. 19. v. 2. he called the Sodomites back from their unspeakable crime v. 7. he wished to free his sons-in-law from the impending Sodomite fire v. 14. he turned his back on all his possessions v. 17. for the preservation of He prayed for Zoar, which are all works of piety and charity, φιλοξενίαν of Lot he commends in the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapter 13, verse 2.

Q. 7. To what deliverance does the Apostle look back? Resp. 1. Lorinus thinks, that regard is had principally to that deliverance by which Lot was snatched by the Angels from the injury and luxurious conversation of the Sodomites, lest those most abandoned men should strive to satisfy their lust either upon his guests or upon his daughters. From the fire, he says, of lust not only Angels, nor one alone, and indeed violently, delivered, etc. The care of lust requires angelic men, and in it great force is required. But that ὑπὸ ἀναστροφῆς does not pertain to the verb ἐῤῥσύατο, but to the participle καταπονούμενον. 2. It is therefore more correctly said that Peter looks back to that deliverance by which the most benign GOD, having sent two Angels, caused Lot together with his wife and two daughters to be led out of Sodom, lest they should be consumed by the Sodomitic fire.

Q. 8. Why did Lot dwell for so long in wicked and flagitious Sodom? Chrysostom, homily 43 on Genesis, refers us to the providence of GOD, who wished to heal the diseases of the Sodomites through the work of Lot as a Physician, even though He foresaw that no fruit would arise from it. Thus, he says, a prudent Physician is accustomed, although he sees that a disease is too grave to be cured by his art, to remit or omit nothing of his duty, but rather to apply all his art the more, so that he may either restore the sick man over a long time, or at least preserve him for a long time, or have a just excuse that he omitted nothing of those things which pertained to his art and office. The providence of GOD also shone forth from this, in that on this occasion the justice and innocence of Lot were brought more into the light on one side; but the malice of the Sodomites and the equity of the divine judgment on the other. But if we look here at Lot himself, he seems to have suffered something human in the choice of Sodom for dwelling and in his longer stay among the Sodomites. Genes. 13. v. 10. Lot, having been given the option by Abraham, lifting up his eyes, saw all the surrounding region of the Jordan, which was entirely watered, before the Lord overturned Sodom and Gomorrah, like the Paradise of the Lord, and like Egypt as one comes to Zoar vers. 11. and Lot chose for himself the region around the Jordan, verse 12, and pitched his tent as far as Sodom. verse 13, but the men of Sodom were the worst. It seems therefore that he had regard rather to the fertility of the region in his choice, than to the quality of the inhabitants.

Q. 9. In what way was Lot righteous in sight and hearing? Resp. 1. Some take that in this sense, that those who saw the conversation of Lot and heard his preaching, could find nothing in either or both to reprehend. Lyranus on this passage: in his life and reputation, justice appeared. 2. Others, however, in this way, that Lot, dwelling in the midst of the Sodomites, nevertheless remained righteous in sight and hearing, that is, that he did not draw the contagion of crimes from them with his eyes or ears, but rather showed the zeal of his justice with modest eyes and chaste ears, being unwilling to discern the crimes of the Sodomites with his eyes, or to hear them speaking impiously before him, and so he utterly abhorred the crimes of the Sodomites with his eyes, ears, and all his senses. Gregory, book 1 of the Morals, chapter 6: He is called righteous in sight and hearing, because the life of the wicked touched the ears and eyes of the righteous not by delighting, but by striking. 3. Bede in his commentary on this passage joins both expositions. He conducted himself, he says, so circumspectly, that neither by the sight of their flagrant acts, nor by hearing them, did he stain the gaze of his chaste mind in anything, but with untiring intention he insisted upon the acts of his justice begun. Or certainly he was righteous in sight and hearing, because those present saw and heard nothing in him except works of justice and utterances, and fame spread nothing about him among the absent, except what pertained to justice. 4. We have indeed warned above, that that βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ is more correctly referred to the participle ἐγκατοικῶν, than to the noun δίκαιος.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Lot is called righteous in verse 7. But how does it accord with this justice, that Gen. 19. verse 7. he offers his daughters to the Sodomites for fornication? Resp. 1. Chrysostom, homily 42 on Genesis, proclaims that deed of Lot as a virtue, greater than hospitality itself. Ambrose, book 1 on Abraham, chapter 6, Augustine, book on lying, chapter 7, Thomas, q. 1 on evil, art. 1, to 14, also seem to praise it. Cajetan on chapter 19 of Genesis discourses on it thus: Lot offered his daughters to the Sodomites with the intention not of redeeming a flagrant act with a flagrant act, but of appeasing the people with hyperbolic submission: for he thought, and reasonably, that the people would not accept such an offering. Lorinus on this passage thinks that if that deed of Lot cannot be praised, it can nevertheless be excused. 2. But it is more correctly said that Lot sinned in this matter, whence The same Augustine, q. 42 in Gen., lib. contra mendac. cap. 9, the interlinear Gloss, Lyranus, and Tostatus in cap. 19 Gen. disapprove of that deed. For although he did this with a good intention, in order to restrain the Sodomites and keep his guests safe from a wicked crime; although he did not even persuade them to fornication, but only offered his daughters to the Sodomites who were burning with lust, yet lesser evils are not to be done, so that greater ones may be avoided Rom. 3. v. 8. nor was Lot the master of the bodies and modesty of his daughters. Therefore he ought not to have offered them for defilement, especially since they were not consenting to this crime and were already betrothed to husbands. But he also ought to have consulted the reputation and modesty of his daughters more than the safety of the strangers, since the daughters were related to him by a closer bond of blood than the strangers. Furthermore, there was a danger that the daughters might consent to the lust of others, on account of the pleasure of delight mixed into that act, nor could it be a lesser sin for the father of the daughters to offer his daughters to be violated than to allow the guests to be violated by a wicked vice. Beautifully, Augustine in the said work: Someone might then have most rightly said to holy Lot: Do whatever you can, so that what you rightly fear does not happen; but do not commit your own great crime, while you shudder more at another's. For however much it may differ between yours and another's; this will nevertheless be yours, and that another's. 3. Meanwhile, however, Lot is called just by the Holy Spirit (just as Augustine also in the preface to Psal. 69. calls him holy. Ephrem Tom. 2. paraen. 9. and 35. proposes him as an example to religious men, in serm. 3. de paenit. he calls him blameless and his life irreprehensible, and in his own sermon he also praises him as just). Firstly, because whatever he sinned in this matter, he later amended through penance. Secondly, he was just before GOD not by inherent and actual justice, but by imputed justice; not by the justice of works, but of faith. Thirdly, with respect to the justice of works begun, he is called just, who has the purpose of doing just things and for the most part does just things. Fourthly; nor did he sin in this matter out of malice, but out of infirmity, namely from a sudden perturbation and lack of counsel, because in a matter so doubtful and perplexing, and in the violent invasion of all the inhabitants of the whole city, no other way occurred to him of consulting for the safety and security of his guests.

2. GOD does not delight in the death of the wicked Ezech. 33. v. 11. not He wills them to perish2. Petr. 3. v. 9.& yet in this place it is said, that He knows how to keep the unrighteous to be punished for the day of judgment that is that it is His will and good pleasure that the impious be punished. I answer: one must distinguish between the antecedent and consequent will of GOD; between the will of mercy and of justice or judicial; between the first and second will. GOD does not delight in the punishments of the impious, out of some absolute hatred against them; nor did He adjudge them to destruction by an antecedent or absolute will: meanwhile, by a consequent and judicial will, He made a decree concerning the perishing of all those who persevere in impiety until the end of their life, which work of His justice He has decreed, wills, and approves. Prov. 1. v. 26.I will laugh at your destruction.

3. The impious are said to be reserved to be punished or for punishment for the day of judgment. But the soul of the rich glutton, departing from the dwelling of the body, was immediately subjected to torments.Luc. 16. v. 23. I answer: 1. It is certain that the souls of the impious are immediately after the death of the body immersed in infernal torments. Gregory, book 4, Dial. 28. If you have believed by the satisfaction of sacred eloquence that the souls of the saints are in heaven: it is necessary that you believe in all respects that the souls of the unrighteous are in hell, because by the retribution of eternal justice, from which the just are already rejoicing, it is necessary in all respects that the unjust be tormented. For just as beatitude gladdens the elect: so it is necessary to believe that from the day of their departure fire burns the reprobate. chapter 29. While the Truth declares the damned rich sinner to be in fire, what wise man would deny that the souls of the reprobate are held by fires? 2. Nor can the contrary be proven from this place: for we have already warned before, that in the Greek text there is κολαζουμένους tormented or punished. 3. If you object, that the devils beseech that they be not tormented before the time,Matth. 8. v. 29.that the judgment is the same concerning impious and damned men, I answer that one must distinguish between the beginnings and the increments of torments. Also between the torments of separated souls, and of souls reunited with bodies. Peter speaks in this place of the beginnings of torments Luc. 16. v. 19. which on the day of judgment will receive the greatest increments, both in evil spirits and in damned men, as much intensively as extensively: hence Bede in his commentary on this place. He says the unrighteous are reserved to be punished for the day of judgment, not because they do not pay penalties for their merits even before the day of judgment when released from the body, but because heavier torments await them in judgment when the body is received, who are now tormented in the soul alone. The same is repeated by Dionysius the Carthusian on this place.

Ἔλεγχος. Lorinus on verse 7 comments thus: That if after Lot escaped into the mountain, he sinned, we elicit a lesson clearly true and especially salutary, that seculars, as the Interlinear Gloss notes on chapter 19 of Genesis, sometimes maintain a state of uprightness among the wicked: but when they ascend to the height of life, having become more negligent, they sin, nor can any places save the soul without the grace of GOD, as Gregory warns book 6, Epistle 4, and it is referred to in dist. 40, c. Quaelibet and homily 9 on Ezekiel, and book 8, Epistle 45, with this example brought forward, be able to save the soul. The words of Gregory are as follows: Any hidden places cannot save the soul without grace, which we sometimes observe even in the very errors of the elect. For Lot was righteous in the very perverse city, but sinned on the mountain. But why do we say these things, when we have known greater ones? For what is more pleasant than Paradise? What is more secure than heaven? And yet man fell from Paradise, and an Angel fell from heaven by sinning. This must be opposed to the opinion of the Papists, that Monasticism is a state of perfection, and that solitary places are means of a holy life. Alphonsus de Castro, book 1 against heresies, chapter 9: I cannot help but be indignant at those Monks who, in order to praise their own institution, do not fear to boast and teach before the people that he who has once taken the habit of that Order cannot err or fail in the faith. Is this not open blasphemy, since by this he seems to attribute more to the habit with which he is clothed than to the faith and grace of GOD. And afterwards: I call God to witness, I do not lie, for in my presence a certain man preaching to the people in a public sermon on the day on which the solemnity of the Saint who had instituted the Order is celebrated, said, wishing to extol his fraternity and society with praises, that he who has once put on the habit of that Order cannot be a heretic. And I have received from many others that they heard the same words from men of the same Order, when a sermon was being made to the people about the same matter.

Ἐκδίκησις. Cornelius à Lapide on verse 7 comments thus: Heresiarchs are handed over to the fires as expiatory sacrifices and purifications of the earth, so that they may not pollute it, but purify it, for they themselves are not rarely bodily, but always mystical Sodomites, because they introduce an adulterous and preposterous faith, for which reason Peter here compares them to the Sodomites.

Resp. 1. The flame of fire in the Papacy does not persist in heresiarchs, but involves also those seduced by heretics. 2. They falsely call those heretics who do not rise in all things to the Roman Pontiff. 3. The bodily punishment of heretics is nowhere commanded in the New Testament, as in its place is demonstrated. 4. If heretics are mystical Sodomites, therefore they will also be punished with mystical fire.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Transfert Apostolus hypothesin ad thesin & ex Historia diluvii & excidii Sodomitici, ex Genesi Mosaica in praecedentibus versiculis adducta, colligit duos locos communes, uti hodie loqui solemus. Prior est, Dominum posse pios de tentatione eripere, sicut Noahum servavit in diluvio, Lothum in incendio Sodomitico. Posterior est, Deum posse iniquos in diem iudicii reservare, per horribile supplicium è medio sublatos, sicut testatum fecit exemplis hominum in diluvio submersorum ac civium Sodo miticorum.

2. Iuxta hanc connexionis rationem Graeca Scholia hunc versiculum â praecedentibus seiungunt; & orationem, quae iam inde â v. 4. imperfectè pependerat, absolvunt hoc modo. Si Deus nec Angelis, nec hominibus transgressoribus pepercit, Noahum verò & Lothum servavit, ergo etiam falsis Doctoribus non parcet, sed exitio illos tradet, vos autem, qui ab illorum contagio immunes estis, servabit & salvos faciet.

3. Posset verò haut absurdè etiam dici, sententiam hactenus pendentem ab illis verbis, Si Deus Angelis, qui peccaverunt, non pepercit, &c. nunc demum absolvi hoc modo. Si Deus Angelis & hominibus transgressoribus olim non pepercit, sed graviter punitos ad iudicium extremum reservavit, Noahum verò & Lothum ex periculis & adversis eripuit, utique novit Dominus pios de tentatione eripere; iniquos verò in diem iudicii reservare. Eo modo Beda in comm. hunc versiculum cum praecedentibus connectit. Multi, inquit, versiculi uno fine clauduntur, novit Dominus pios de tentatione eripere.

Textus expositio. Οἶδε Κύριος εὐσεβεῖ ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι. Verbo οἶδε non solùm remittit nos Apostolus ad divinam scientiam, sapientiam & potentiam, quod pro sua infinita sapientia & potentia varios habeat modos, quibus possit pios ex tentatione eripere; sed etiam ad divinam gratiam & beneplacitum, quòd hoc opus, videlicet liberatio piorum ex periculis sit opus Deo gratum ac placitum. Verba enim notitiae apud Hebraeos & affectum cordis & effectum operis saepiùs connotant. Psal. 1. v. ult.

Per τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς intelliguntur illi, qui Noah & Lothi vestigiis insistentes verâ fide in Christo iustitiam quaerunt, ac fidem suam bonis operibus testantes in vero timore DEO serviunt, iustitiae bonae conscientiae & vitae sanctitati ex animo student, & ab impiorum consortio sese segregant. Syrus reddidit. [דדחלים לה]illos qui timent eum, scilicet Deum. Timor enim saepiùs pro toto cultu divino usurpatur. Gen. 31. v. 53.

Pro ἐκ πειρασμοῦ quidam Codd. Graeci numero multitudinis legunt ἐκ πειρασμοὺς, quod magis emphaticum. Caeterùm per πειρασμοὺς intelliguntur omnis generis pericula & adversa, angustiae animi interioris & pressurae corporis ac persecutiones exteriores, quae omnia tentationis ac probationis causâ piis immittuntur, sicut Petrus dicit 1. Epist. 4. v. 12. quòd πύρωσιςfervor crucisπρὸς πειρασμὸνimmittatur. Sic Deut. 7. v. 19. plagae Aegypti dicuntur tentationes.Tob. 2. v. 12.cap. 12. v. 3. coecitas Tobiae vocatur tentatio. Christus Luc. 22. v. 28. adversitates suas vocat tentationes, in quibus discipulos secum constantes mansisse praedicat. Sirach. 27. v. 6. vocatur tentatio tribulationis. Syrus hunc locum reddidit, [מן אולצנא]ex afflictione, angustia, oppressione, â rad. [אלץ]affligere, arctare, angustare.

Ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέρας κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν. Athanasius in Disput. contra Arium in Concil. Niceno Tom. 1. p. 83. locum hunc sic citat. οἶδεν ὁ θεὸς εὐσεβεῖς ῥυέσθαι, ἀνόμους δὲ τηρεῖν εἰς ἡμεραν κρίσεως κιλαζομένους αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ. Sed dubio procul non ipsa verba, sed sententiam Apostoli citare voluit.

Per ἀδίκους intelliguntur, qui hominum antediluvianorum & Sodomitarum vestigiis insistentes DEI legem nefariè transgrediuntur, iniustitiam & libidines sectantur, ac iniquis suis operibus animas piorum cruciant. Syrus reddidit [עולא] â rad. [עול]inique ac perversè egit.2. Cor. 7. v. 2.

Per ἡμέραν κρίσεως intelligitur dies iudicii extremi & Universalis, quod Christus in novissimo suo adventu instituet. Actor. 17. v. 31, In hac ipsa Epistola c. 3. v. 7. Petrus diem illam vocat ἡμέραν κρίσεως καὶ ἀπωλείας τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνθρώπων. Iudas in sua Epist. v. 6. vocat κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας, iudicium, quod in die illa magna instituetur.

Κολαζομένους Vulg. reddidit cruciandos. Sed in Graeco non est futurum, sed praesens, siquidem nulli Codd. legunt κολασομένους, sed omnes habent κολαζαμὲνους. Syr. [כד משתנקין]postquam fuerint cruciati; ut sit sensus, poenas dantes, videlicet secundùm animam apud inferos; vel potiùs praeteritum, ut sit sensus, punitos, h. e. per horribile supplicium è medio sublatos, κολάζειν enim significat, petulantiam alicuius poenis compescere ac cohibere. Luth. Vulg. secutus zu peinigen.

Q. hoc loco. 1. Quaenam fuerit Sodomitarum impietas, propter quam tam horribiliter puniti? Resp. Spiritus sanctus Gen. 19. v. 13. eam sic describit. Homines Sodomitae erant mali & peccatores coram Domino valde, ubi peccata ipsorum tripliciter exaggerantur 1. per emphaticam repetitionem. Erant mali & peccatores, quae repetitio est αὐξητικὴ. 2. Per nominis divini expressionem. Erant peccatores coram Domino, h. e. gravissimi & maximi peccatores, quia quae DEO tribuuntur, sunt magna & eximia, Psal. 51. v. 3. vel erant peccatores coram Domino i. e. palam, publicè, in ipsius DEI conspectu peccabant, Gen. 10. v. 9. vel peccabant contra Dominum, cuius sanctas leges nefariè & protervè transgrediebantur, quod congruit cum voce ἀθέσμων. 3. Per adverbii adiectionem. Erant peccatores valde, adeò ut etiam ipsorum peccata in caelum clamarent. Chald. Paraphrastes sic reddidit. Homines Sodomae abutebantur divitiis suis & peccabant corporibus suis coram Domino valde.

Q. 2. Qualis fuerit ipsorumἀσέλγεια; Resp. constat ex Gen. 19. v. 5. quòd fuerint. ἀῤῥενοκοίται καὶ παιδεράσται, quod flagitium Sap. 14. v. 26. vocatur γένεσεως ἐναλλαγὴ. Luth. reddidit, Stumme Sünden / quòd coram honestis & castis auribus ne quidem nominari debeant, ex quo loco desumtum videtur illud Apostolicum Rom. 1. v. 26.Feminae gentiliumμετήλλαξενmutarunt naturalem usum, in eum qui est contra Naturam v. 27. Similiter etiam masculi relicto naturali usu feminae exarserunt desideriis suis invicem, masculi in masculos turpitudinem exercentes. Cumprimis verò huc pertinet locus parallelus in Epist. Iud. v. 7. in quo Sodomit. ἀσέλγεια hoc modo describitur. Sodoma & Gomorrha & finitimae civitates simili modoἐκπορνεύσασαιin scortationem effusae, scortando effervefactae, ad defatigationem usque scortationi operam dantes, quia praepositio ἐκ intendit significationem, Sie haben sich ansgehuret / ut Luth. rectè reddidit: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας,cùm abiissent post carnem diversam, cùm sectatae essent alteram carnem, quibus verbis κατ' εὐφημισμὸν describitur Sodomitarum ἀῤῥενοκοίτων flagitium. vocat autem diversam carnem, quia in diversum finem & usum est â DEO condita, Rom. 1. v. 27.

Q. 3. An ex adultis Sodomitis quidam egerint paenitentiam?

Q. 4. An iustitiae divinae congruum sit, etiam infantes & pueros hoc incendio ab sumtos fuisse? Resp. de his quaestionibus in enarratione cap. 19. Genes. fuit actum.

Q. 5. Quare Apostolus exemplum irae divinae, in Sodomitarum excidio publicè editum, seductoribus illis inculcet? Resp. 1. Quia in Scripturis idololatria & haeresis spiritualis scortatio & spirituale adulterium vocantur. Cùm ergo DEUS Sodomiticas libidines igne & sulphure caelitus depluto puniverit, ex eo Petrus colligendum relinquit, ipsum quoque infernali igne puniturum falsos illos Doctores, qui spirituale adulterium committunt. 2. In sequentibus Apostolus falsis illis Doctoribus tribuit, quòd habeant oculos plenos adulterii, quòd pelliciant in concupiscentiis carnis, Iudas eos accusat, quòd ipsi quoque similiter carnem maculent. Epist. v. 8.

Q. 6. Qualis fuerit Lothi iustitia? Resp. fuit. 1. Iustitia imputata, quia speravit in promissum Messiam, ac per illum peccatorum remissionem sibi obtingere credidit. 2. Iustitia in choata, quia fidem suam bonis operibus demonstravit, siquidem unà cum Abrahamo patruo suo divinae iussioni obsecutus patriam idololatricam deservit Gen. 13. v. 1. peregrinos hospitio excepit, Gen. 19. v. 2. Sodomitas â nefando scelere revocavit v. 7. generos suos ex instante incendio Sodomitico liberare voluit v. 14. facultatibus suis omnibus tergum obvertit v. 17. pro conservatione Zoaris oravit, quae omnia sunt pietatis & caritatis opera, φιλοξενίαν Lothi commendat Epist. ad Hebr. cap. 13. v. 2.

Q. 7. Ad quam liberationem Apostolus respiciat? Resp. 1. Lorinus putat, praecipuè respectum haberi ad illam liberationem, quâ Lothus per Angelos ab iniuria & luxuriosa conversatione Sodomitarum ereptus fuit, ne perditissimi isti homines libidinem explere vel in hospites niterentur, vel in filias eius. Ab incendio, inquit, libidinis non nisi Angeli, nec unus solus & quidem violentè liberavit &c. Angelicos homines requirit cura libidinis & in ea vis magna requiritur. Sed illud ὑπὸ ἀναστροφῆς non pertinet ad verbum ἐῤῥσύατο, sed ad participium καταπονούμενον. 2. Rectiùs ergo dicitur, quòd Petrus respiciat ad illam liberationem, quâ benignissimus DEUS missis dubus Angelis Lothum unà cum uxore & duabus filiabus ex Sodoma educi curaverit, ne incendio Sodomitico absumerentur.

Q. 8. Quare Lothus in scelerata & flagitiosa Sodoma tamdiu habîtaverit? Chrysostomus homil. 43. in Genes. remittit nos ad providentiam DEI, qui Lothi ceu Medici operâ morbos Sodomitarum sanare voluit, tametsi praevideret, nullum ex eo fructum oriturum. Sic, inquit, solet prudens Medicus, quamvis videat, morbum graviorem esse, quàm ut arte suâ curari possit, nihil praeterea de officio suo vel remittere, vel praetermittere, sed eò magis omnem artem suam adhibere, ut aegrum aut longo tempore reparet, aut in longum certè tempus conservet, aut iustam habeat excusationem, quod nihil eorum omisserit, quae ad artem, munusque suum pertinebant.
