Eluxit etiam ex eo DEI providentia, quod hac occasione magis in lucem producta fuit Lothi iustitia & innocentia ex parte unâ; Sodomitarum verò malitia & iudicii divini aequitas ex parte altera. Quòd si verò Lothum ipsum hîc respiciamus, videtur in electione Sodomae ad habitandum & in diuturniore apud Sodomitas commoratione aliquid humani passus. Genes. 13. v. 10. Lothus datâ sibi per Abrahamum optione, elevatis oculis vidit omnem circumiacentem regionem Iordanis, quae universa irrigabatur, antequam subverteret Dominus Sodomam & Gomorrham, sicut Paradisus Domini, & sicut Aegyptus venientibus in Segor vers. 11. elegitque sibi Loth. regionem circa Iordanem vers. 12. & tabernaculum sixit usque ad Sodomam. vers. 13. homines autem Sodomitae erant pessimi. Videtur ergo fertilitatem regionis in electione potiùs respexisse, quàm incolarum qualitatem.

Q. 9. Quâ ratione Lothus aspectu & auditu fuerit iustus? Resp. 1. Quidam illud accipiunt hoc sensu, quòd qui Lothi conversationem viderent & praedicationem eius audirent, quod in alterutra vel utraque reprehenderent, invenire non potuerint. Lyranus in hunc locum: in vita & fama eius, iustitia apparebat. 2. Quidam verò hoc modo, quod Lothus in medio Sodomitarum habitans, nihilo minus manserit aspectu & auditu iustus, hoc est, quod nec oculis nec auribus contagium scelerum ab illis hau serit, quinimò pudicis oculis & castis auribus Zelum suae iustitiae ostenderit, nolens Sodomitarum crimina oculis cernere, aut de illis impios coram se loqui, adeoque oculis, auribus & omnibus sensibus â Sodomitarum sceleribus prorsus abhorruerit. Gregorius lib. 1. moral. cap. 6. Aspectu & auditu iustus dicitur, quia iniquorum vita non delectando iusti aures atque oculos, sed feriendo tangebat. 3. Beda in comm. huius loci utramque expositionem coniungit. Tam circumspectè, inquit, se gerebat, ut nec visis eorum flagitiis, nec auditis, in aliquo castae suae mentis fucaret intuitum, sed indefessa intentione caeptis suae iustitiae insistebat actibus. Velcertè aspectu & auditu iustus erat, quia nihil in eo praesentes, nisi iustitiae & opera cernebant & audiebant eloquia, nihil fama de illo per absentes, nisi quod ad iustitiam pertineret, vulgabat. 4. Monuimus verò superius, quòd illud βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ rectiùs referatur ad participium ἐγκατοικῶν, quàm ad nomen δίκαιος.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Lothus in vers. 7. vocatur iustus. At quomodo cum hac iustitia congruit, quodGenes. 19. vers. 7.filias suas Sodomitis ad fornicationem offert? Resp. 1. Chrysostomus homil. 42. in Genes. factum illud Lothi praedicat tanquam virtutem, ipsâ hospitalitate maiorem. Laudare etiam illud videntur Ambrosius lib. 1. de Abraham cap. 6. August. lib. de mendac. cap. 7. Thomas q. 1. de malo art. 1. ad 14. Caietanus in cap. 19. Genes. de eo sic disserit. Loth obtulit filias suas Sodomitis animo non redimendi flagitium flagitio, sed placandi hyperbolicâ submissione populum: putabat enim & rationabiliter, quod populus non acceptaret talem oblationem. Lorinus in h. l. putat, si non laudari, tamen excusari posse illud Lothi factum. 2. Sed rectiùs dicitur, Lothum hac in re peccasse, unde de factum illud improbant idem Augustinus q. 42. in Genes. lib. contra mendac. cap. 9. Glossa interlin. Lyranus, Tostatus in cap. 19. Genes. Quamvis enim hoc fecerit bonâ intentione, ut Sodomitas coërceret, & hospites â nefario flagitio immunes servaret; quamvis etiam fornicationem non suaserit, sed Sodomitis libidine flagrantibus filias tantùm obtulerit, tamen non sunt facienda mala cuipae minora, ut vitentur maioraRom. 3. v. 8. nec fuit Lothus Dominus corporum & pudicitiae filiarum. Ergo non debuit eas stupro offerre, praesertim in hoc flagitium non consentientes & maritis iam desponsatas. Sed & filiarum suarum famae & puditiae magis consulere debuit, quàm indemnitati peregrinorum, cùm propinquiore sanguinis coniunctione filiae ipsum attigerint, quàm peregrini. Periculum insuper erat, ne filiae assentirentur libidini alienae, ob voluptatis delectationem in eo actu admixtam, nec potuit patri filiarum custodi minus peccatum esse, offerre filias violandas, quàm nefando vitio sinere hospites violari. Pulchrè Augustinus d. l. Rectis simè quispiam tunc dixisset sancto Lotho. Age, quicquid potes, ne fiat, quod meriò times; sed noli facere magnum scelus tuum, dum magis horrescis alienum. Quantumlibet enim distet inter tuum & alienum; hoc tamen erit tuum, & illud alienum. 3. Interim tamen Lothus vocatur â Spiritu sancto iustus (sicut etiam Augustinus in praefat. Psal. 69. eum appellat sanctum. Ephrem Tom. 2. paraen. 9. & 35. viris religiosis eum proponit in exemplum, serm. 3. de paenit. vocat eum inculpatum & vitam eius irreprehensibilem, proprio quoque sermone eum laudat ut iustum) Primò, quia quicquid hac in re peccavit, per paenitentiam postea emendavit. Secundò, iustus fuit coram DEO non inhaerente & actuali, sed imputatâ; non operum, sed fidei iustitiâ. Tertiò, respectu inchoatae operum iustitiae iustus vocatur, qui habet propositum iusta faciendi & plerumque iusta agit. Quartò; neque hac in re ex malitia peccavit, sed ex infirmitate, ex subitâ sc. perturbatione & consilii inopia, propterea quòd in re tam ancipiti ac perplexa, inque violenta omnium totius urbis incolarum invasione nullus occurebat modus alius, hospitum indemnitati & incolumitati consulendi.

2. DEUS non delectatur morte impiorumEzech. 33. v. 11.non vult illos perire2. Petr. 3. v. 9.& tamen hoc loco dicitur, quod noverit iniquos in diem iudicii servare cruciandos h. e. quod sit ipsius voluntas & beneplacitum impios cruciari. Resp. disting. inter voluntatem DEI antecedentem & consequentem; inter voluntatem misericordiae & iustitiae sive iudicariam; inter voluntatem primam & secundam. Non delectatur DEUS poenis impiorum, ex absoluto quodam adversus illos odio; nec voluntate antecedente vel absolutâ eos exitio adiudicavit: interim voluntate consequente & iudicariâ decretum fecit de perdendis omnibus illis, qui in impietate ad finem usque vitae perseverant, quod opus iustitiae suae decrevit, vult & approbat. Prov. 1. v. 26.Ridebo in interitu vestro.

3. Impii dicuntur in diem iudicii reservari cruciandi vel ad cruciatum. Atqui anima divitis epulonis ex corporis habitaculo emigrans statim fuit cruciatibus subiecta.Luc. 16. v. 23. Resp. 1. Certum est, animas impiorum statim post corporis mortem cruciatibus infernalibus immergi. Gregor. lib. 4. Dial. 28. Si esse sanctorum animas in caelo, sacri eloquii satisfactione credidisti: oportet, ut per omnia esse credas, & iniquorum animas in inferno, quia ex retributione aeternae iustitiae, ex qua iusti iam gloriantur, necesse est per omnia, ut iniusti crucientur. Nam sicut electos beatitudo laetificat: ita credi necesse est, quod â die exitus sui ignis reprobos exurat. cap. 29. Dum peccatorem divitem damnatum veritas in ignem perhibet, quisnam sapiens reproborum animas teneri ignibus neget? 2. Nec potest contrarium ex hoc loco probari: iam antè enim monuimus, in Graeco textu esse κολαζουμένουςcruciatos vel punitos. 3. Si excipias, Diabolos deprecari, ne ante tempus crucientur,Matth. 8. v. 29.idem iudicium esse de hominibus impiis & damnatis, Resp. distinguendum esse inter cruciatuum initia & incrementa. It. inter cruciatus animarum separatarum, & animarum corporibus iterum unitarum. Petrus hoc loco loquitur de cruciatuum initiis Luc. 16. v. 19. quae in die iudicii tùm in Spiritibus malis, tùm in hominibus damnatis maxima capient incrementa, tam intensivè quàm extensivè: inde Beda in comm. h. l. Iniquos dicit in diem iudicii cruciandos reservari, non quia etiam ante diem iudicii soluti corpore non luant poenas pro meritis, sed quia graviora eos in iudicio tormenta expectent corpore recepto, qui nunc in anima sola cruciantur. Idem repetit Dionys. Carthusianus in hoc loco.

Ἔλεγχος. Lorinus adv. 7. sic commentatur. Quòd si postquam evasit Loth in montem, peccavit, elicimus documentum planè verum & apprimè salutare, seculares, ut annotat Glossa interlin. in cap. 19. Genes. aliquando inter malos statum rectitudinis tenere: cùm verò ad altitudinem vitae ascendunt, negligentiores factos peccare, nec quaelibet loca sine DEI gratia, ut monet Gregorius lib. 6. Epist. 4. & refertur dist. 40. c. Quaelibet & homil. 9. in Ezechiel. & lib. 8. Epist. 45. hoc allato exemplo, animam salvare posse. Verba Gregorii sic habent. Quaelibet occulta loca sine gratia animam salvare non possunt, quod aliquando in ipsis quoque conspicimus erratis electorum. Nam Loth in ipsa perversa civitate iustus fuit, in monte peccavit. Sed ista cur dicimus, cùm maiora noverimus? Quid enim Paradiso iucundius? quid caelo securius? & tamen homo ex Paradiso Angelus de caelo peccando cecidit. Opponendum hoc opinioni Pontificiorum, quod Monachatus sit status perfectionis, quodque loca solitaria sint vitae sanctae media. Alph. de castro lib. 1. adv. haeres. cap 9. Non possum non stomachari in illos Monachos, qui, ut suum institutum laudent, non verentur coram populo iactare ac docere, eum, qui semel habitum illius Ordinis susceperit, non posse in fide errare aut deficere. Nonne haec aperta est blasphemia, cùm per hoc magis tribuere videatur habitui, quo induitur, quàm fidei & gratiae DEI. Et postea. Deum testor, non mentior, nam me praesente quidam in publica concione ad populum praedicans in die, quo agitur solennitas Sancti, qui Ordinem instituerat, dixit, fraternitatem suam ac societatem laudibus extollere volens, eum, qui habitum illius Ordinis semel induerit, non posse esse haereticum. Et ab aliis pluribus accepi, se eadem verba audivisse ab hominibus eiusdem Ordinis, cum de eadem re sermo populo fieret.

Ἐκδίκησις. Cornelius â Lapide ad vers. 7. sic commentatur. Haeresiarchae ignibus traduntur quasi piacula & catharmata terrae, ne eam inquinent, sed expient, ipsi enim non rarò corporales, sed semper mystici sunt Sodomitae, quia fidem adulteram & praeposteram inducunt, quâ de causâ eos Petrus hîc Sodomitis comparat.

Resp. 1. Flamma ignis in Papatu non persistit in haeresiarchis, sed involvit etiam ab haereticis seductos. 2. Haereticos falsò vocant eos, qui non in omnibus Pontifici Romano assurgunt. 3. Corporale haereticorum supplicium in Nov. Test. nuspiam praecipi, suo loco demonstratur. 4. Si haeretici sunt mystici Sodomitae, ergo etiam mystico igne erunt puniendi.

## 2:10
Connection. In this verse the Apostle returns to a graphic description of the false teachers, and recounts the second and third mark of the same, namely, lustfulness and pride, because both vices are familiar to false teachers.

Exposition of the text. Μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ, μιασμοῦ πορευομένους. To be repeated from the preceding verse. οἶδε κύριος εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως τηρεῖν. For the Apostle here adapts the general doctrine handed down in the preceding verse to the false teachers, whom he terrifies with the threat of the final judgment.

Μάλιστα. The Vulgate rendered more, concerning which version Lorinus in h. l. judges thus. The Latin interpreter better expressed the comparison with a comparative adverb. But the Greek properly signifies especially, chiefly, as Jerome translates in lib. 1. adv. Iovinian. The Syriac renders [יתיראית] chiefly, abundantly, excellently. The sense therefore is, that God indeed keeps all the impious to be punished on the day of judgment, but especially those who join an impious life and nefarious crimes with false doctrine by the example of the false teachers themselves.

By τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς πορευομένους, who walk after the flesh, are understood those who follow the flesh, that is, the depraved concupiscences of the flesh, and especially indeed nefarious lusts: whence some judge that by οὐ φημισμὸν,, through a modest synecdoche, the genital member is understood by the name of flesh, or rather the nefarious abuse of that member in illicit intercourse. Ezech. 16. v. 26.cap. 23. vers. 20. Jude in Epist. v. 6. says concerning the Sodomitic crime: ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, which passage is parallel to this one of ours regarding phrase and subject matter. But especially pertinent here is v. 8. of that Epistle. οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσι. Some separate that ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι from the following words and explain it in this way, that they are deluded by dreams, i.e., that swelling with their vain and fictitious dignity they dream that they are I know not whom or what, or that the judgment of the mind in them is as it were oppressed by a certain lethargy. But it can with the best reason be joined with the following words, in the sense that dreaming, i.e., while dreaming they defile the flesh, and thus foul lust exerts itself in impure dreams and the pollution of the flesh even while they are sleeping.

Ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ. The Vulgate rendered it, in the concupiscence of uncleanness. But the Greek properly signifies pollution, just as Jerome also rendered it in the said place. Moreover, ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ is said according to a customary Hebraism for δια ἐπιθυμίας μιασμοῦ in the desire of pollution, i.e., by which they are basely polluted, or through an impure and polluted desire. Vatablus, on account of polluted desire. The Syriac rendered [ברגיגתא דטמאותא] in the concupiscence or desire (for the root is [רגג] he sought, he desired) of pollution or uncleanness, (for the root is [טמא] he was impure, unclean, polluted) Luth. In der unreinen Lust. The preposition ἐν does not denote the way or place where one walks, but the procreating cause from which the walking proceeds, or which impels one to walk.

Καὶ Κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντες. The Vulgate and despise dominion. The Complutensian and Royal Bibles read in the plural κυριότητας,, which reading Jerome also followed in the said place, who cites this text thus: They despise dominions. But the former reading in is to be preferred as more singular. 1. Because it is conformable to more and more approved codices of Robertus Stephanus, Aldus, etc. 2. Because καταφρονεῖν among the Greeks is constructed not with the accusative, but with the genitive. 3. Because Judas in the parallel passage of the Epistle v. 8. has likewise the singular. 4. Because when Judas uses the accusative κυριότητα, he employs the verb ἀθετεῖν, which governs the accusative, κυριότητα ἀθετοῦσι.

But that those false teachers are called κυριότητος καταφρονεῖν, some explain it thus, that they wish to be subject to no one: others indeed in this way, that they despise dominion, that is, the Magistrate. For as 1. Epist. 5. v. 9. ἀδελφότητα calls the assembly of the brethren: so κυρίοτητα calls the assembly of Senators, or the college of any other Magistrates whatsoever. Although indeed the matter comes to the same thing, for he who does not wish to be subject to the Magistrate, he also despises the Magistrate, yet the latter explanation, which is more extensive, is more conformable to the text, as appears from the following words in Peter and Judas. The Syrian has the noun [מרותא] which Eph. 1. v. 21.Col. 1. v. 16. is used concerning dominions, that is, a certain order of Angels, which are called in the same place in Greek κυρίοτητες, from which some maintain that in this place also the discourse is about Angels. But that exposition, as also that which Lyranus brings forward; ( They despise dominion i. e. Christ, who is not only called Lord in the concrete, but also dominion in the abstract on account of the excellence of the Lordship) is clearly foreign to this Apostolic passage.

Τολμηταὶ, αὐθάδεις. Some maintain that there is to be understood ὄντες or οἱ εἰσὶ since they are, or who are, bold. Some understand αὐτοὶ or ἐκεῖνοι. Those bold ones do not fear to blaspheme majesties. Some wish to be understood the relative pronoun οἵτινες and the copulative particle, ηαι, but nothing of these is simply necessary. For these can be taken as said by exclamation σχετλιαστικὴν καὶ ἀγανακτητικὴν, so that they are annexed to the preceding ones abruptly on account of πάθος. Bold, pleasing themselves, they do not shudder to provoke majesties with insults. τολμητὰς some judge that they are called false teachers, because they are eager and bold to undertake those things by which they may promote their own design. But in what respect the Apostle to them boldness may grant, is evident from the following, namely that they do not fear to blaspheme majesties. The Syriac rendered, [מרחא] bold, impudentProv. 14. v. 14.cap. 21. vers. 24. from the root [מרח] he dared, he used boldness, he took confidence. Luther rendered Dürstig.

Αὐθάδεις. The Vulgate rendered, pleasing themselves, as if it were formed from αὐτὸς himself and ἅδειν to please; as if it were pleasing themselves, but despising all others with a high brow. Others derive it from αὐτὸς καὶ ἐν ἑαυτῷ the same in himself, as Hesychius wishes: or as if αὐτὸς ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ the same from himself. For there are in Greek αὐθάδεις stubborn, obstinate, who adhere uniquely to their own preconceived opinions, whom they otherwise call ἰδιογνώμονες, ἰσχυραγνώμονες, which vice, since it arises from pride, therefore the Vulgate version αὐθάδεις elsewhere translates proud.Tit. 1. v. 7. The LXX use this word, Gen. 49. v. 7. for ען tenacious, hardened. The Greek Scholia explain τὸ ἑαυτοῖς ἄρεσκον μεταδιώκοντες, pursuing what pleases themselves. Hesychius makes these synonyms, αὐθάδεις, ὑπερήφανος, θυμώδης, παράνομος, αὐτάρεστος, ἐξουσιαστικὸς. Proud, irascible, lawless, self-pleasing, of one's own right. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian translates impudent, Erasmus; stubborn, and of their own head and sense. The Syriac in this place rendered, [משקלא] elated;Tit. 1. v. 7. αὐθάδη rendered; led by the will of his own soul. Luther most correctly Engensinning.

Δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφειμοῦντες. Jude in the parallel passage v. 8. Epist. δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσι. By δόξας glories or dignities μετωνυμικῶς are understood Emperors, Kings, Princes, who are endowed with the highest glory and majesty in the world. Erasmus in this place By glories are understood those excelling in glory, that is, men endowed with glory and majesty, such as are Kings, Princes, and Magistrates. To which can be referred, that Matth. 4. v. 8.Luc. 4. v. 6. is attributed to the kingdoms of this world δόξα. Those δόξας false Doctors do not fear to blaspheme, because they trample the dignity and power of the Magistrate underfoot and assail him with insults, καταφρονητικῶς ἔχουσι, as the Greek Scholia explain, and for this reason GOD himself, from whom is all ἐξουσία Rom. 13. v. 2. they set themselves against. The participle βλασφημοῦντες is put for the infinitive verb βλασφημεῖν, as is evident from the parallel passage Jude v. 8. through a customary Graecism, because it is familiar to the Greeks to use participles for infinitives. The Syriac rendered it, with what glory or dignity they are not moved, when they blaspheme; another Syriac version rendered the Greek text κατὰ πόδα,, who do not fear to blaspheme glories or Majesties. Luther Sie erzittern nicht die Majestäten zu lästern.

Latin:

Connexio. Redit in hoc versiculo Apostolus ad graphicam falsorum doctorum descriptionem, ac secundam & tertiam eorundem notam recenset, videlicet libidinositatem ac superbiam, quod utrumque vitium falsis doctoribus familiare.

Textus expositio. Μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ, μιασμοῦ πορευομένους. Repetendum ex versu praeced. οἶδε κύριος εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως τηρεῖν. Generalem enim doctrinam in versu praeced. traditam Apostolus hîc accommodat ad falsos doctores, quos iudicii extremi comminatione terret.

Μάλιστα. Vulg. reddidit magis, de qua versione Lorinus in h. l. sic iudicat. Interpres Latinus comparationem comparativo adverbio meliùs expressit. Sed Graecum propriè significat maximè, praecipuè, ut vertit Hieronymus lib. 1. adv. Iovinian. Syr. redd. [יתיראית]praecipuè, abundanter, excellenter. Sensus igitur est, quod Deus omnes quidem impios in diem iudicii puniendos servet, maximè tamen eos, qui cum falsa doctrina vitam impiam & scelera nefaria exemplo falsorum ipsorum doctorum coniungunt.

Per τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς πορευομένους, qui post carnem proficiscuntur, intelliguntur illi, qui carnem, hoc est, pravas carnis concupiscentias, cumprimis verò nefarias libidines sectantur: unde quidam censent per οὐ φημισμὸν, per vere cundam sc. Synecdochen, carnis nomine intelligi membrum genitale, vel potiùs nefarium illius membri in illicito coitu abusum. Ezech. 16. v. 26.cap. 23. vers. 20. Iudas in Epist. v. 6. de scelere Sodomitico dicit: ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, qui locus huic nostro quoad phrasin & rem parallelus. Cumprimis verò hîc pertinet v. 8. illius Epistolae. οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσι. Quidam illud ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι seiungunt â seqq. & hoc modo exponunt, quòd somniis sint delusi, h. e. quod vanâ & commentitiâ suâ dignitate turgentes somnient se nescio quos ac quales esse, vel quòd iudicium mentis in illis quasi quodam veterno sit oppressum. Sed potest optimâ ratione coniungi cum sequentibus, sensu eo, quòd somniantes h. e. inter somniandum carnem maculent, adeoque faeda libido in impuris somniis & pollutione carnis etiam ipsis dormientibus sese exerat.

Ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ. Vulg. reddidit, in concupiscentia immunditiae. Sed Graecum propriè significat pollutionem, quemadmodum etiam Hieronymus d. l. reddidit. Dicitur autem ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ iuxta usitatum Hebraismum pro δια ἐπιθυμίας μιασμοῦin cupiditate pollutionis h. e. quâ turpiter polluuntur, sive per impuram & pollutam cupiditatem. Vatablus, ob pollutum desiderium. Syrus redd. [ברגיגתא דטמאותא]in concupiscentia vel desiderio (radix enim est [רגג]expetivit, desideravit) pollutionis vel immundiciei, (radix enim est [טמא]impurus, immundus, pollutus fuit) Luth. In der unreinen Lust. Praepositio ἐν non notat viam seu locum, ubi ambuletur, sed causam procreantem, â qua ambulatio proficiscitur, seu quae ad ambulandum impellit.

Καὶ Κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντες. Vulg. dominationemque contemnunt. Biblia Complutensia & Regia legunt in plurali κυριότητας, quam lectionem etiam secutus est Hieronymus d. l. qui textum hunc sic citat. Dominationes contemnunt. Sed prior lectio in singulari magis probanda. 1. Quia pluribus & probatioribus Codd. Roberti Stephani, Aldi &c. est conformis. 2. Quia καταφρονεῖν apud Graecos non cum accusativo, sed cum genitivo construitur. 3. Quia Iudas in loco parallelo Epist. v. 8. habet itidem singulare. 4. Quia quando Iudas usurpat accusativum κυριότητα, adhibet verbum ἀθετεῖν, quod accusativum regit, κυριότητα ἀθετοῦσι.

Quod autem falsi isti doctores dicuntur κυριότητος καταφρονεῖν, illud quidam sic explicant, quòd nemini velint subiici: quidam verò hoc modo, quòd dominationem, h. e. Magistratum contemnunt. Ut enim1. Epist. 5. v. 9.ἀδελφότηταvocat coetum fratrum: itaκυρίοτηταvocat coetum Senatorum, aut aeliorum quorumvis Magistratuum Collegium. Quamvis vero res eodem redeat, qui enim Magistratui subiici non vult, is etiam Magistratum contemnit, posterior tamen explicatio, quae latiùs patet, magis conformis est textui, ut apparet ex sequentibus verbis apud Petrum & Iudam. Syrus habet nomen [מרותא] quod Eph. 1. v. 21.Col. 1. v. 16. de dominationibus, hoc est, certo Angelorum ordine 11. surpatur, quae ibidem in Graeco vocantur κυρίοτητες, ex quo quidam statuvut, etiam hoc loco de Angelis sermonem esse. Sed expositio illa, uti etiam ea, quam Lyranus profert; ( Dominationem contemnunt i. e. Christum, qui non solùm dicitur Dominus in concreto, sed etiam dominatio in abstracto propter excellentiam Dominii) est ab hoc loco Apostolico planè aliena.

Τολμηταὶ, αὐθάδεις. Quidam statuunt, subintelligendum esseὄντες vel οἱ εἰσὶcùm sint, vel qui sunt, audaces. Quidam subintelligunt αὐτοὶ vel ἐκεῖνοι.Audaces illi non timent maiestates blasphemare. Quidam subintelligi volutn pronomen relativumοἵτινες & particulam copulativam,ηαι, sed nihil horum est simpliciter necessarium. Possunt enim haec accipi dicta per exclamationem σχετλιαστικὴν καὶ ἀγανακτητικὴν, ut superioribus annectantur ex abrupto propter πάθος. Audaces, sibi placentes non horrent maiestates convitiis lacessere. τολμητὰς quidam censent, falsos doctores dici, quia alacres & audaces sint ad aggrediendum ea, quibus institutum suum promoveant. Sed quo respectu Apostolus ipsis audaciam tribuat, patet ex sequentibus, videlicet quod maiestates blasphemare non reformident. Syrus reddidit, [מרחא]andaces, proterviProv. 14. v. 14.cap. 21. vers. 24. â rad. [מרח]ausus fuit, audaciâ usus fuit, confidentiam sumsit. Lutherus reddidit Dürstig.

Αὐθάδεις. Vulg. reddidit, sibi placentes, quasi formetur ab αὐτὸς ipse & ἅδεινplacere; ac si sit sibiipsis placentes, alios verò quosvis alto supercilio contemnentes. Alti deducunt ab αὐτὸς καὶ ἐν ἑαυτῷidem in seipso, ut vult Hesychius: vel quasi αὐτὸς ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦidem ex seipso. Sunt enim Graecis αὐθάδειςpraefracti, pervicaces, qui praeconceptis suis opinionibus unicè adhaerent, quos aliàs vocant ἰδιογνώμονες, ἰσχυραγνώμονες, quod vitium cùm ex superbia oriatur, ideò vulg. versio αὐθάδεις alibi vertit superbos.Tit. 1. v. 7. LXX. hac voce utuntur, Gen. 49. v. 7. pro עןpertinax, obfirmatus. Graeca Scholia exponunt τὸ ἑαυτοῖς ἄρεσκον μεταδιώκοντες,quod ipsis placet, persequentes. Hesychius haec facit synonyma, αὐθάδεις, ὑπερήφανος, θυμώδης, παράνομος, αὐτάρεστος, ἐξουσιαστικὸς.Superbus, iracundus, exlex, sibi placens, proprii iuris. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. vertit procaces, Erasmus; praefracti, suique capitis & sensus. Syrus h. l. reddidit, [משקלא]elatos;Tit. 1. v. 7.αὐθάδη reddidit; ductum in voluntate animae suae. Lutherus rectissimè Engensinning.

Δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφειμοῦντες. Iudas in loco parallelo v. 8. Epist.δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσι. Per δόξας glorias sive dignitates μετωνυμικῶς intelliguntur Imperatores, Reges, Principes, qui summâ in mundo gloriâ ac maiestate praediti. Erasmus in h. l. Per glorias intelliguntur praecellentes gloriâ h. e. viri gloriâ ac maiestate praediti, quales sunt Reges, Principes ac Magistratus. Quò referri potest, quòd Matth. 4. v. 8.Luc. 4. v. 6. regnis huius mundi tribuitur δόξα. Illas δόξας falsi Doctores non metuunt blasphemare, quia dignitatem & potestatem Magistratus pedibus conculcant & convitiis eum incessant, καταφρονητικῶς ἔχουσι, ut Graeca Scholia exponunt, & hac ratione DEO ipsi, â quo est omnis ἐξουσίαRom. 13. v. 2. sese opponunt. Participium βλασφημοῦντες ponitur pro verbo infinitivo βλασφημεῖν, ut constat, ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 8. per usitatum Graecismum, quia Graecis familiare est, participiis uti pro infinitivis. Syrus reddidit, qua gloriâ vel dignitate non moventur, cum blasphemant; alter v. Syrus Graecum textum κατὰ πόδα, reddidit, qui glorias sive Maiestates non metuunt blasphemare. Lutherus Sie erzittern nicht die Majestäten zu lästern.

## 2:10-13 Questions and observations
Observations. 1. Let all the lustful, adulterers, fornicators, and effeminate; let all also who are despisers of the Magistracy, blasphemers against this holy ordinance of GOD, know that a most certain punishment hangs over them, unless they have timely repented. 1. Corinth. 6. v. 9.Gal. 5. v. 19.

2. Bede in his commentary on this passage: By those who walk after the flesh in concupiscence, the Apostle understands fornicators, who, on account of the guilt of their corruption, will suffer greater torments in judgment than the general wicked. By those who despise dominion, he understands the proud and arrogant, who themselves also are about to pay heavier punishments than the general ones.

3. The holy angels are powerful in strength and virtue. 2. Kings 19. v. 35.Psal. 104. verse 20. Let this strength of theirs confirm us, that they can most powerfully protect us against the Devil and all his instruments 2. Kings 6. v. 16.Matth. 26. v. 53.

4. Kings and Princes, even if they sin, are not to be assailed with curses and insults, but their divine office is to be honored, and their persons are to be committed to the judgment of GOD.

5. Just as Peter compares false teachers to φυσικοῖς ζώοις, in whom Nature alone rules: so Jude in the parallel passage of his Epistle v. 19. calls them ψυχικούς, because they are not ruled by the Spirit of GOD, but follow only the guidance of reason, or indeed sometimes the appetite of the flesh. Tertullian the Montanist, having rendered this name into Latin, called the Catholics Psychics.

6. Moreover, the Apostle compares false teachers to brute animals in that they are ruled neither by counsel, nor by reason, much less by the Spirit of GOD, but are carried by a blind impulse toward beastly lusts and pleasures. Irenaeus, book 5, chapter 8, adapts to this the passage Psal. 49. v. 13. He is compared to the senseless beasts.

7. Truly, flagitious men become brutish through beastly lusts and other graver offenses, when they do not even restrain vicious appetites with the bridle of reason, let alone with the governance of the Spirit. Hence Peter, a little later, compares them to swine and dogs v. 22. Thus Jerem. 5. v. 8. like fed horses they neighed every one after his neighbor's wife. Ezech. 23. v. 20. Flesh their flesh is like the flesh of horses, and their issue is like the issue of donkeys.Apoc. 22. v. 15.Outside (beyond the heavenly Jerusalem) are dogs.

8. It is the characteristic of false teachers to blaspheme those things which they do not understand, whereas on the contrary the truly pious say: What I read, I believe; what I do not grasp, I revere. Bede in his commentary on this passage: While they themselves serve the corruption of the flesh, they nevertheless blaspheme the conduct of those who live chastely; while they themselves are held by insane errors, they do not cease to disparage those who are sound in judgment.

9. Augustine, book 13 of The City of God, chapter 12, makes four species of death. The first is the death of the soul, when it is deprived through sins of GOD, who is the life of the soul, as the soul is the life of the body. The second is the death of the body, when it is deprived of the soul. The third is another death of the soul, when it, separated both from GOD and from the body, is punished. The fourth and final death is that of the whole man, when the soul without GOD will suffer eternal punishments with the body. All those who follow in the footsteps of those of whom Peter speaks here incur these species of death.

10. Nothing is more foolish than to prefer momentary pleasures to eternal happiness. The point of time which we live is short, and yet in this point eternity is acquired or lost.

11. False teachers and flagitious men are stains upon the Church, nay, cancers, since because of them the Church has a bad reputation among the infidels.

12. With false doctrine are usually joined frauds and impostures, through which it is propagated.

Latin:

Observationes. 1. Omnes libidinosi, adulteri, scortatores, molles; omnes etiam Magistratus contemtores in hanc sanctam DEI ordinationem blasphemi sciant, certissimum sibi imminere supplicium, nisi maturè paenitentiam egerint. 1. Corinth. 6. v. 9.Gal. 5. v. 19.

2. Beda in comm. h. l. Per eos, qui post carnem in concupiscentia ambulant, fornicatores intelligit Apostolus, qui pro reatu suae corruptionis maiora in iudicio, quam generales iniqui tormenta patientur. Per illos, qui dominationem contemnunt, superbos & arrogantes intelligit, qui & ipsi graviora generalibus sint supplicia luituri.

3. Angeli sancti pollent robore ac virtute. 2. Reg. 19. v. 35.Psal. 104. vers. 20. Hoc illorum robur confirmet nos, quod contra Diabolum & omnia ipsius organa potentissimè nos tueri possint 2. Reg. 6. v. 16.Matth. 26. v. 53.

4. Reges & Principes, etiamsi delinquant, non sunt maledictis & convitiis incessendi, sed officium ipsorum divinum honorandum, personae DEI iudicio committendae.

5. Sicut Petrus falsos doctores comparat φυσικοῖς ζώοις, in quibus sola Natura dominatur: sic Iudas in loco parallelo Epist. v. 19. eos vocat ψυχικούς, quia non reguntur DEI Spiritu, sed rationis ductum tantummodò sequuntur, imò quandoque carnis appetitum. Tertullianus Montanista nomine isthoc Latinitate donato abusos Catholicos vocavit Psychicos.

6. Confert autem Apostolus falsos doctores brutis animalibus eò, quod nec consilio, nec ratione, nedum Spiritu DEI regantur, sed caeco ad belunias libidines & voluptates ferantur impetu. Irenaeus lib. 5. cap. 8. hûc accommodat locum Psal. 49. v. 13.Comparatus est iumentis insipientibus.

7. Nimirum homines flagitiosi per brutales libidines & alia delicta graviora obbrutescunt, cùm vitiosos appetitos sensitivi motus nequidem rationis freno, tantum abest, ut Spiritus regimine coërceant. Inde Petrus paulò post eos porcis & canibus comparat v. 22. Sic Ierem. 5. v. 8.instar equorum saturatorum unus quisque ad uxorem proximi sui hinniebant.Ezech. 23. v. 20.Caro eorum sicut equorum caro, & fluxus eorum sieut fluxus afinorum.Apoc. 22. v. 15.Foris (extra caelestem Hierosolymam) canes.

8. Falsorum doctorum proprium est, ea, quae non intelligunt, blasphemare, cùm contrà verè pii dicant. Quod lego, credo; quod non assequor, minor. Beda in comm. h. l. Cùm ipsi corruptioni carnis serviant, nihilominus conversationem eorum, qui castè vivunt, blasphemant; cùm ipsi vesanis teneantur erroribus, eis, qui sanum sapiunt, detrahere non cessant.

9. Augustinus lib. 13. de C. D. cap. 12. facit quatuor mortis species. Prima est mors animae, quando illa per peccata privatur DEO, qui est vita animae, ut anima est vita corporis. Secunda est mors corporis, quando illud privatur animâ. Tertia est alia mors animae, quando illa & â DEO & â corpore separata punitur. Quarta & novissima mors est totius hominis, quando anima sine DEO cum corpore aeternas poenas luet. Omnes hasce mortis species incurrunt, qui vestigiis illorum, de quibus Petrus hîc loquitur, insistunt.

10. Nihil stolidius, quàm momentaneas voluptates aeternae felicitati praeferre. Punctum temporis quod vivimus, & tamen in hoc puncto aeternitas acquiritur vel amittitur.

11. Falsi doctores & homines flagitiosi sunt Ecclesiae maculae, imò carcinomata, cùm propter illos Ecclesia apud in fideles malè audiat.

12. Cum falsa doctrina plerunque coniunctae sunt fraudes & imposturae, per quas ea propagatur.

## 2:11
Connection. The Apostle exaggerates the pride of the false teachers, by which they do not shrink from despising dominion and blaspheming majesties, from the opposite example of Angelic modesty, in which there is an argument from the greater to the less.

Exposition of the text. ὅπου Ἄγγελοι ἰσχύι καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες. The Vulgate rendered the little word ὅπου as where, introducing obscurity into the text by this reasoning. Lorinus in his commentary says, it is various, ὅπου either it denotes the place, which it properly signifies, namely hell or another, in which the evil Angels are punished: or it has the force of a cause, namely for which sins, which were previously enumerated and are committed by men, they are persuaded by Demons, or it is the same as when, since, after. But Lorinus rightly advises, that this last exposition is to be preferred to the former ones. For the context proves it, and the Greek ὅπου also obtains this meaning elsewhere. Mark 4. verse 15. ὅπου 1. Corinthians 3. verse 3. ὅπου ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος where the Vulgate rightly rendered it, when there is jealousy among you. The LXX use this little word in the same meaning Proverbs 26. verse 20. באין נרגן ὅπου οὐκ ἔστιν ὀξύθυμος, when there is no whisperer. Henri Estienne in the Index of the Thesaurus under the word ὅπου. Just as the Latin 'ubi' is sometimes put for 'since', 'when'; so also ὅπου among the Greeks, which he proves with examples taken from Plutarch, Lucian, Isocrates, and Demosthenes. Therefore Luther translates it rightly. So doch die Engel. Estius says, the Vulgate Interpreter for that reason did not wish in this place ὅπου to render it by 'when', lest the same thing be said twice in so few words, because it follows, since they are greater. But it would have been better, in the following, to use another word, (even if they are greater, however they may be greater) than to bring darkness upon the text. By Angels some understand evil Angels, who are also elsewhere absolutely called Angels Rom. 8. vers. 38.1. Cor. 6. vers. 3. But that holy and good Angels are understood here by this name placed absolutely, is evident from the parallel passage in the Epistle of Jude, verse 9, where mention is made of Michael the Archangel. He calls them Apostles greater in strength and power. This comparison is explained in three ways. 1. Some think regard is had to δόξας or Magistrates, whom false teachers blaspheme. 2. Some refer it to evil Angels, with whom the good have a controversy and dispute.Jude v. 9. 3. Some to false teachers, whose audacity and pride the Apostle exaggerates, because they dare such a thing, which not even the Angels themselves, greater than them in strength and virtue, do. which exposition we prefer to the others.

Οὐ φέρουσι κατ' αὐτῶν βλάσφημον κρίσιν. The Vulgate rendered, they do not bring against themselves an execrable judgment. But in the Greek it is, they do not bring against themselves a blasphemous or railing judgment.

For κατ' αὐτῶν some Codices have καθ' ἑαυτῶν against themselves, that is, against one another, one against another, which reading most greatly agrees with the scope and context; and even if κατ' αὐτῶν, is read, that nevertheless must be taken as placed for καθ' ἑαυτῶν entirely. The Syriac in the same way. They do not bring [עליהון] against themselves a judgment of blasphemy. that is, blasphemous. That παρὰ Κυρίῳ which is held inserted into the Greek text in the Complutensian and Royal Codices, is entirely omitted in the Vulgate version, as also in the Syriac Paraphrase. Lucas Brugensis testifies, however, that in certain ancient Latin Codices it is held added, which read, they do not bring against themselves from the Lord an execrable judgment. Concerning the genuine sense of this passage we shall see in the questions.

Latin:

Connexio. Exaggerat Apostolus superbiam falsorum doctorum, quâ dominationem, contemnere & maiestates blasphemare non reformidant ab oppositio Angelicae modestiae exemplo, cui in est argumentum â maiori ad minus.

Textus expositio. ὅπου Ἄγγελοι ἰσχύι καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες. Voculam ὅπου Vulg. reddidit, ubi, obscuritatem hac ratione textui inferens. Lorinus in comm. varius est,ὅπου inquit, aut locum, quem propriè significat, inferni sc. aliumve denotat, in quo Angeli mali puniuntur: aut vim causae habet, nempe pro quibus peccatis, quae priùs erant numerata & ab hominibus fiunt, suadentur â Daemonibus, aut idem est atque cùm, quando, postquam. Sed rectè monet Lorinus, postremam hanc expositionem prioribus esse praeferendam. Eam enim probat contextus, & hanc significationem Graecum ὅπου etiam alibi obtinet. Marc. 4. vers. 15.ὅπου1. Corinth. 3. vers. 3.ὅπου ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος ubi Vulg. rectè reddidit, cùm sit inter vos Zelus. LXX. in ead. significatione hac voculâ utuntur Proverb. 26. vers. 20.באין נרגןὅπου οὐκ ἔστιν ὀξύθυμος,cùm non adfuerit susurro. Henricus Stephanus in Indice Thesauri in voce ὅπου.Sicut Latinum ubi ponitur interdum pro quandoquidem, cùm; ita etiamὅπουapud Graecos, id quod exemplis ex Plutarcho, Luciano, Isocrate & Demosthene petitis probat. Rectè igitur Lutherus vertit. So doch die Engel. Estius dicit, Vulg. Interp. propterea noluisse hoc locoὅπουreddere per cùm, ne bis diceretur idem in tam paucis verbis, quia sequitur, cùm sint maiores. At satiùs fuisset, in sequentibus alio uti verbo, (etiamsi sint maiores, utut sint maiores) quàm tenebras textui inferre. Per Angelos quidam intelligunt malos Angelos, qui & alibi absolutè vocantur Angeli Rom. 8. vers. 38.1. Cor. 6. vers. 3. Sed sanctos & bonos Angelos hoc nomine absolutè posito hîc intelligi, patet ex loco parellelo Iudae Epist. vers. 9. ubi mentio fit Michaëlis Arch Angeli. Illos vocat Apostolos robore & potentiâ maiores. Comparatio haec tripliciter exponitur. 1. Quidam putant respectum haberi adδόξαςsive Magistratus, quos falsi doctores blasphemant. 2. Quidam referunt ad malos Angelos, cum quibus bonis est controversia ac disceptatio.Iudae v. 9. 3. Quidam ad falsos doctores, quorum audaciam ac superbiam exaggerat Apostolus, quòd tale quid audeant, quod ne ipsi quidem Angeli robore ac virtute eis maiores faciant. quam expositionem reliquis praeferimus.

Οὐ φέρουσι κατ' αὐτῶν βλάσφημον κρίσιν. Vulg. reddidit, non portant adversum se execrabile iudicium. Sed in Graeco est, non ferunt adversus se iudicium blasphemum sive maledicum.

Pro κατ' αὐτῶν quidam Codd. habent καθ' ἑαυτῶνadversus seipsos, h. e. adversus se mutuò, alius adversus alium, quae lectio scopo & contextui maximè congruit; ac si vel maximè legatur κατ' αὐτῶν, illud tamen pro καθ' ἑαυτῶν positum omninò accipiendum. Syrus eodem modo. Non afferunt[עליהון]adversus se iudicium blasphemiae. hoc est blasphemum. Illud παρὰ Κυρίῳ quod in Complutensibus & Regiis Codd. textui Graeco insertum habetur, in vulg. versione, ut & in Syriaca Paraphrasi penitus est omissum. Testatur tamen Lucas Brugensis, in antiquis quibusdam Codd. Latinis haberi additum, qui legunt, non portant adversum se â Domino execrabile iudicium. De genuino huius loci sensu videbimus in quaestionibus.

## 2:12
Connection, 1. The Apostle continues to exaggerate the proud audacity of those false teachers, of whom he treats, from the adjunct of stupidity and blindness, in respect of which he compares them to brute animals, rushing to their own destruction, on which occasion he predicts destruction for the false teachers for the third time. 2. This stupid blindness could also be taken as some new vice and mark of the false teachers, for the Apostle continues to describe their most corrupt morals.

Exposition of the text. οὗτοι δὲ ὡς ἄλογα ζῶα φυσικὰ &c. οὗτοι δὲ, viz. ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι of whom he has treated at length until now. He institutes an opposition between the holy Angels, who do not bring a railing judgment against evil Angels, even though they have deserved such a thing: and those false teachers, who do not even shrink from blaspheming what they are ignorant of.

Ὡς ἄλογα ζῶα. The Vulgate rendered it, as irrational cattle; Erasmus more correctly, brute animals, in which way the Vulgate Interpreter himself in a parallel passage Jude v. 12. rendered it. The Syrian translates [חיותא חרשתא] Etzel. animals of the woods, more correctly, mute animals, in which way also certain Latin Codices read Jude v. 12. For a brute is devoid of both reason and speech. Pococke on the Syriac Paraphrase on this passage annotates thus. It seems to be common to the Syrians with the Arabs, that they call an irrational being mute, but a rational being speaking, because speech is surely among the chief acts of the rational soul.

Φυσικὰ. Some join this little word with the following words γεγενημένα εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν, so that the noun φυσικὰ is placed for an adverb φυσικῶς, and the sense may be, naturally born for capture and slaughter. Erasmus on this passage, He said naturally for capture, just as we say, born to learn, for that which is, composed by nature. The Vulgate Interpreter seems to follow this sense, who rendered the two words φυσικὰ γεγενημένα with a single word naturally, as also Luther, who translates this passage thus. Sie sind wie die unvernünfftigen Thier / die von Natur darzu geboren sind/ daß sie gefangen und geschlachtet werden.

This exposition, as regards the underlying matter of which it treats, contains nothing absurd. For GOD who is the author of created Nature and Natura naturans, as they say, created brute animals, as much quadrupeds as flying and aquatic creatures, to this end, that having been captured and killed by men, they might yield to their consumption and use. But because the expression φυσικὰ γεγενημένα for φυσικῶς or φύσει γεγενημένα is extremely harsh and unusual (whence even Erasmus suspects that the participle γεγενημένα crept into the context from the margin of the book), therefore it is more correctly said that the little word φυσικὰ ought to be referred to the preceding things. Those as brute animals, natural, i.e., which are driven by Nature or by natural motions and concupiscences, but are not led by reason. For as ψυχικὸς ἄνθρωπος 1. Cor. 2. v. 14. is called he who has nothing excellent in himself except a rational soul, who follows the natural light of reason, and is not yet regenerated by the Spirit of GOD: so ζῶα φυσικὰ are those in whom natural impetus and impulse dominates, which do not possess reason, restraining and curbing natural affections and impetuses. The Syrian rendered it, they were [בכינא] in Nature, which name some derive from [כון] so that it is said as if it were the directress of all things.

Γενενημένα εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθορὰν, born for capture and destruction. Syrian [לחרבא ולחבלא] for slaughter and perdition. Some explain it actively concerning rapacious and harmful animals intent upon the plunder and destruction of others, such as terrestrial wolves and aquatic lions, vultures, hawks, etc., in whom it is implanted by Nature to capture and destroy other animals inferior in strength, so that the sense may be: those false teachers lie in wait for the simpler ones, and capture and destroy their souls, whence they are compared by Christ to thieves and robbers Iohann. 10. vers. 8. Paul Actor. 20. vers. 29. as also Christ Matth. 7. vers. 15. call them grievous and rapacious wolves. But because Peter compares φθορὰν of false teachers with φθορᾷ of these animals, it appears from this that these words εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθορὰν are rather to be taken passively, in this sense, that those brute animals were created for this reason, that they might yield as prey to others, by whom they are consumed and perish, and consequently it is signified that those false teachers, in the manner of brute animals destined for capture and slaughter, on the day of judgment as if by a certain snare are to be taken and dragged to destruction Luke 21. verse 35. when they have immersed themselves entirely like beasts in the mire of pleasures. Bede in this place Just as it is natural for irrational animals, for the sake of fodder, to fall more often ignorantly into capture and destruction: so heretics, compared to foolish beasts of burden, because of the desire to satisfy their own corruption, blaspheming the incorrupt and sound doctrine of the Catholic Church and life, weave for themselves the snares of eternal perdition with impious rashness. Luther in his commentary joins both the active and the passive exposition. And indeed both can be joined very well. For just as wild beasts capture others, and in turn are captured by others: so false teachers, when they have destroyed others with impious doctrine, they themselves also perish together with them. A parallel passage exists James 5. v. 5. You have nourished your hearts in luxuries, as in the day of slaughter.

Ἐν οἱς ἀγνοοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες. that is ἐν ἐκείνοις, ἅ ἀγνοοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες. βλασφημία it signifies not only blasphemy properly so called, that is, abuse against GOD, but also any evil-speaking, detraction, or reviling, so that it is the same as δυσφημία, to which is opposed εὐφημία. Augustine in On the Morals of the Manichaeans, chapter 2, defines blasphemy as when some evil things are said about good things; in this latter meaning the word βλασφημεῖν seems to be used in this place.

That phrase, blaspheming in those things which they are ignorant of, is less common, but it is understood from the parallel passage Jude v. 10. ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασι βλασφημοῦσι, they blaspheme those things which they do not understand. Therefore, 1. such a Hebraism can be established in this phrase, as is in those places in which ב is used for על Gen. 26. verse 12. His hand against all that is, against all and the hand of all against him that is, against him. Num. 12. v. 1. against Moses that is, against Moses. Isa. 21. verse 13. The burden against Arabia that is, against Arabia. Thus in this place, blaspheming in those things which they are ignorant of, that is, they pour out and vomit their blasphemies against those things which they are ignorant of. 2. Or such as is in those places in which the preposition ב and its corresponding ἐν circumscribes the accusative Psalm 20. v. 8. We will call upon in the name of the Lord, that is, the name of the Lord. Thus in this place, they blaspheme in those things which they are ignorant of that is, those things which they are ignorant of; which exposition agrees with the parallel passage Jude v. 10.

3. Some think ἐν is put for περὶ, for the Greeks speak thus, βλασφημεῖν περί τινος πράγματος. 4. Some apply here the rule, that the Hebrews construct verbs of contact, whether real, or mental, or verbal, such as to blaspheme, with the ablative by means of the preposition εν, as they say to strike in the face for to strike the face. Thus in this place. In these, which they do not know i. e. these which they do not know, they blaspheme. But the two former expositions are simpler.

Ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καταφθαρήσονται. Vulg. in their corruption they shall perish. But in the Greek there is a beautiful paranomasia of noun and verb, which Jerome in the said place expressed thus. In their corruption they shall be corrupted; Erasmus in their destruction they shall perish. The Syrian in the same way. [בחבלא דילהון נתחבלון] in their corruption they shall be corrupted, in their destruction they shall perish. Luther Sie werden von ihrem verderblichen Wesen umbkommen. The sense, however, is, they shall perish by that destruction, which they voluntarily bring upon themselves by their lost and corrupt morals: in their destruction i. e. they shall perish by the just judgment of GOD destined for them, just as he had said they were born as brute animals εἰς φθορὰν, the manner of the destination however varies, as we shall advise later.

Latin:

Connexio, 1. Pergit Apostolus superbam illorum falsorum doctorum, de quibus agit, audaciam exaggerare ab adiuncto stupore & caecitate, cuius respectu illos confert cum brutis animalibus, in perniciem suam ruentibus, quâ occasione falsis doctoribus tertiâ vice exitium praenunciat. 2. Posset etiam haec stupida caecitas accipi ut novum aliquod falsorum doctorum vitium ac nota, pergit enim Apostolus mores eorum corruptissimos describere.

Textus expositio. οὗτοι δὲ ὡς ἄλογα ζῶα φυσικὰ &c. οὗτοι δὲ, sc. ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι de quibus multis hactenus egit. Instituit oppositionem inter Angelos sanctos, qui non inferunt maledicum iudicium malis Angelis, etsi tale quid promeritis: & falsos illos doctores, qui etiam, quod ignorant, blasphemare non reformidant.

Ὡς ἄλογα ζῶα. Vulg. reddidit, velut irrationabilia pecora; Erasmus rectiùs, bruta animalia, quo modo ipse Vulg. Interp. in loco parallelo Iud. v. 12. reddidit. Syrus vertit [חיותא חרשתא] Etzel. animalia sylvarum, rectiùs, animalia muta, quo modo etiam quidam Codd. Latini legunt Iud. v. 12. brutum enim & rationis & sermonis est expers. Pococke ad Syriac. Paraph. h. l. sic annotat. Commune Syris cum Arabibus hoc videtur, ut irrationale mutum vocent, rationale autem loquens, quod nimirum loquela sit ê praecipuis animae rationalis actibus.

Φυσικὰ. Quidam hanc voculam coniungunt cum verbis sequentibus γεγενημένα εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν,ut nomenφυσικὰponatur pro adverbioφυσικῶς, ac sensus sit, naturaliter genita ad capturam ac internecionem. Erasmus in h. l. Naturalia ad captionem dixit, quemadmodum dicimus, natus ad discendum, pro eo, quod est Naturâ compositus. Hunc sensum sequi videtur Interpres vulgatus, qui duas voces φυσικὰ γεγενημένα reddidit unicâ voce naturaliter, uti etiam Lutherus, qui hunc locum sic vertit. Sie sind wie die unvernünfftigen Thier / die von Natur darzu geboren sind/ daß sie gefangen und geschlachtet werden.

Haec expositio, quoad rem substratam, de qua agitur, nihil absurdi continet. DEUS enim qui est Naturae creatae autor ac Natura naturans, ut loquuntur, bruta animantia tam qua drupeda, quàm volatilia & aquatilia eo fine creavit, ut ab hominibus capta & occisa cedant in eorum esum & usum. Sed quia perquam dura & insolens est locutio, φυσικὰ γεγενημένα pro φυσικῶς vel φύσει γεγενημένα (unde etiam Erasmus, suspicatur participium γεγενημένα ex albo libri in contextum irrepsisse) ideò rectiùs dicitur, voculam φυσικὰ referri debere ad praecedentia. Illi velut bruta animalia, naturalia i. e. quae â Naturâ sive naturalibus motibus & concupiscentiis aguntur, non autem ratione ducuntur. Ut enim ψυχικὸς ἄνθρωπος1. Cor. 2. v. 14. dicitur is, qui nihil in se eximium habet praeter animam rationalem, qui naturale rationis lumen sequitur, ac Spiritu DEI nondum est regeneratus: ita ζῶα φυσικὰ sunt, in quibus naturalis impetus & impulsus dominatur, quae non pollent ratione, affectus & impetus naturales coërcente ac refrenante. Syrus reddidit, fuerunt[בכינא]in Natura, quod nomen quidam deducunt â [כון] ut sic dicatur, quasi rerum omnium directrix.

Γενενημένα εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθορὰν,nata ad capturam & perniciem. Syrus [לחרבא ולחבלא]ad caedem & perditionem. Quidam exponunt activè de animalibus rapacibus ac maleficis in aliorum rapinam & perniciem intentis, qualia sunt lupi terrestres & aquatici leones, vultures, accipitres, &c. quibus Naturâ insitum est alia animalia viribus inferiora capere ac perdere, ut sit sensus: falsos illos doctores insidiari simplicioribus, eorumque animas capere ac perdere, unde â Christo furibus & latronibus conferunturIohann. 10. vers. 8. Paulus Actor. 20. vers. 29.ut & ChristusMatth. 7. vers. 15.vocant eos lupos graves ac rapaces. Sed quia φθορὰν falsorum doctorum cum φθορᾷ horum animalium Petrus confert, ex eo apparet, quod haec verba εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθορὰν potius passivè sint accipienda, hoc sensu, quod animalia illa bruta ideò condita sint, ut aliis cedant in praedam, â quibus consumta pereant, ac proinde significatur, quod falsi illi doctores more brutorum animalium capturae & occisioni destinatorum die iudicii tanquam laqueo quodam sint capiendi & in interitum trahendi Luc. 21. vers. 35. cùm totos se brutorum instar voluptatum ceno immerserint. Beda in h. l. Sicut irrationabilibus animantibus naturale est, causâ pabuli saepius in captionem & perniciem ignoranter incidere: ita haeretici comparati iumentis insipientibus ob appetitum suae corruptionis explendum, incorruptam sanamque Catholicae Ecclesiae doctrinam blasphemantes & vitam, sempiternae sibi perditionis laqueos impiâ temeritate nectunt. Lutherus in comm. utramque expositionem tam activam, quàm passivam coniungit. Et sanè utraque optimè coniungi potest. Quemadmodum enim ferae capiunt alias, & vicissim ab aliis capiuntur: sic falsi doctores cùm alios impiâ doctrinâ perdiderunt, ipsi quoque unà cum illis pereunt. Locus parallelus extat Iac. 5. v. 5.Enutriistis in luxuriis corda vestra, ut in die occisionis.

Ἐν οἱς ἀγνοοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες. h. e. ἐν ἐκείνοις, ἅ ἀγνοοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες. βλασφημία non tantum blasphemiam propriè dictam, h. e. convitium in DEUM significat, sed etiam quamlibet maledicentiam, obtrectationem, vituperationem, ut sit idem, quod δυσφημία, cui opponitur εὐφημία. August. de moribus Manich. cap. 2. blasphemiam definit, cùm aliqua mala dicuntur de bonis; in hac posteriore significatione verbum βλασφημεῖν hoc loco videtur usurpari.

Phrasis illa, in his, quae ignorant, blasphemantes, est minùs usitatata, intelligitur autem ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 10. ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασι βλασφημοῦσι,quae non intelligunt, blasphemant. Potest ergo 1. talis Hebraismus in hac phrasi statui, qualis est in illis locis, in quibus ב usurpatur pro עלGen. 26. vers. 12.Manus eius in omnes i. e. contra omnes & manus omnium in ipsum i. e. contra ipsum. Num. 12. v. 1.in Mosen i. e. contra Mosen. Esai. 21. vers. 13.Onus in Arabiam i. e. contra Arabiam. Sic h. l. blasphemantin iis, quae ignorant, h. e. blasphemias suas effundunt atque evomunt contra ea, quae ignorant. 2. Vel qualis est in illis locis, in quibus praepositio ב eique correspondens ἐν circumscribit accusativum Psalm. 20. v. 8.Nos invocabimus in nomine Domini, id est nomen Domini. Sic hoc loco, blasphemant in iis, quae ignorant i. e. ea, quae ignorant; quae expositio congruit cum loco parallelo Iudae v. 10.

3. Quidam existimant ἐνpositum esse proπερὶ,Graeci enim sic loquuntur,βλασφημεῖν περί τινος πράγματος. 4. Quidam huc applicant regulam, quod Hebraei verba contactus, sive realis, sive mentalis sive verbalis, qualis est blasphemare, construant cum ablativo mediante praepositioneεν,ut percutere in facie dicunt pro percutere faciem. Sic h. l. In his, quae ignorant i. e. haec quae ignorant, blasphemant. Sed duae priores expositiones sunt simpliciores.

Ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καταφθαρήσονται. Vulg. in corruptione sua peribunt. Sed in Graeco est pulchra nominis & verbi paranomasia, quam Hieronymus d. l. sic expressit. In corruptione sua corrumpentur; Erasmus in perditione suâ peribunt. Syrus eodem modo. [בחבלא דילהון נתחבלון]in corruptione sua corrumpentur, in interitu suo interibunt. Lutherus Sie werden von ihrem verderblichen Wesen umbkommen. Sensus autem, est, peribunt illo exitio, quod perditis & corruptis suis moribus sibi ipsis sponte accersunt: in suo interitu i. e. iusto DEI iudicio sibi destinato peribunt, sicut animalia bruta dixerat nata εἰς φθορὰν, modus tamen destinationis variat, ut postea monebimus.

## 2:13
Connection. 1. The Apostle had said that those false teachers, infamous for notorious crimes, would perish in their destruction. He indicates the justice of that destruction i. e. of the divine punishment, when he predicts that they will carry back the reward of their injustice.

2. He again touches upon their luxury and intemperance, since it is the tinder and nurse of those abominable lusts, of which he had treated in the preceding verse; to which luxury he also shows that fraudulence is joined by them, through which they milk the simpler sort of their money, so that it may abundantly suffice for their luxury.

Exposition of the text. Κομιούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας. The Syrian, joining this member with the following ones, casts darkness upon the text, for he renders it thus: With those in whom there is iniquity, the reward of iniquity is reckoned as sweetness, which is in the day. Perhaps he wished to signify that those false teachers, by the just judgment of GOD, fall from one sin into another, so that the later iniquity is the reward of the former. Blessed Luther in the German version joins this member more correctly with the preceding ones, which series of the text, approved also by Estius, is confirmed by the participle κομιούμενον. which coheres entirely with the preceding ones.

Furthermore, that κομιούμενοι the Vulgate version rendered receiving. The Greek properly has about to receive back in the future, by which word the same Vulgate Interpreter expresses the Greek κομίζεσθαι 1. Petr. 1. v. 9. as also Hebr. 10. v. 36. Luther most correctly. Sie werden umbkommen / und den Lohn der Ungerechtigkeit davon bringen.

By the name Ἀδικίας some understand in particular injury, brought against a neighbor contrary to the seventh commandment. But it is more correctly taken generally for any graver sins committed against the second table of the Decalogue, so that it also embraces foul lusts, and luxury, the tinder of them, as is gathered from the preceding and following parts of this passage. This general signification of the word ἀδικίας is frequent in the Scriptures. Luc. 13. vers. 27. ἐργάται τῆς ἀδικίας. Rom. 1. v. 18. ἀσέβεια καὶ ἀδικία are joined. The former expresses sins against the first, the latter sins against the second table of the Decalogue. 1. Ioh. 5. v. 17. πᾶσα ἀδικία ἁμαρτία ἐστι. The Syrian rendered it by [עולא] from the root [עול] he acted iniquitously, perversely. The sense, therefore, is that those flagitious men will receive back damnation as the reward of their crimes.

Ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν. Jerome seems to join the little word ἡδονὴν with the preceding ones, for he cites this passage thus, book 1 against Jovinian: And they shall receive the reward of iniquity, luxury. Bede in his commentary likewise warns that some join the little word ηβονην with the preceding words in this way: Receiving the reward of injustice, pleasure. Rom. 1. v. 24. & 27. But anyone sees that this is forced. The Greek Codices [have] the little word ἡδονὴν they join with the following words. Regarding the participle ἡγούμενοι, to some it seems that the pronoun οὗτοι. must be repeated from the preceding verse ἀπὸ κοινοῦ These are they who consider pleasure. But the sense maintains its integrity without that repetition.

Τρυφὴ signifies luxury and delights. Luc. 7. v. 25. The Syrian rendered it [בוסמא] from the root [בסם] he lived delicately, in luxury. Iac. 5. v. 5.

The phrase ἐν ἡμέρᾳ is explained in various ways. 1. Some establish that it is put for καθ' ἡμέραν daily, so that the sense is: They judge it to be the highest good and joy if they can live in delights and feast daily, as is said of the rich glutton Luc. 16. vers. 19. εὐφραινὸμενος καθ' ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς. Oecumenius in this place: Considering daily luxury as pleasure, that is, establishing true and lovable joy and pleasure in the daily enjoyment of the gullet: Erasmus in his paraphrase: Considering it as pleasure if they enjoy delights for the day. Beza in this place ἐν ἡμέρα, declares nothing else than Exod. 29. vers. 36. ליום for καθ' ἡμέραν. But if the Apostle had wished this, he would have said ἡμέραν εἰς ἡμέραν τρυφῶντες, as he speaks in v. 8. of this chapter, or τὴν καθ' ἡμέραν τρυφὴν ὑδονὴν ἡγούμενοι.

2. Bede in his commentary establishes that regard is had to the preconceived opinion of those voluptuaries. Pleasure, he says, is accepted both in good and in evil, etc. Good pleasure is called of the day, by which all the saints delight in the Lord. But the pleasure of the evil is of the night, when the reprobate are perversely delighted in performing the works of darkness. Well, therefore, he says of the unjust that they consider the pleasure of the day to be the delights of defilement and stain, because many are so perverse and shameless in their heart that, when they are free for the most impure and execrable delights, they nevertheless judge these to be the best and as it were light-flowing.

3. Some think that mention is made of the day notably, so that the impudence of those flagitious men may be expressed, because, having cast off all shame entirely, they do not fear to carouse and indulge in lusts in the clear light of day, when otherwise these things are accustomed to be done by the children of darkness at night. Rom. 13. v. 12. The night is far spent, the day is at hand, let us therefore cast off the works of darkness. v. 13. Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness. 1. Thessal. 5. v. 7. They that be drunken are drunken in the night.

4. It is most simply established that by τὴν ἡμέραν is understood the time of the present life, which, when compared to the day of eternity (concerning which in this Epistle cap. 3. v. 18.), is like a single day, in the same chapter v. 8.. Therefore, the Epicurean security of those wicked men is exaggerated, because, being little mindful of the final judgment and the coming age, they establish happiness in present delights, which nevertheless scarcely last for a little day, so that the sense may be: They think pleasure is daily delights, to be able to delight oneself for one or another day, to enjoy delights for a short time. Luth. Sie achtens für Wollust das zeitliche Wolleben.

Σπῖλοι καὶ μῶμοι. Some Latin Codices read in the Genitive of defilement and spot, which reading also occurs in Bede. From the Roman correction, today in most Latin Codices it is read, defilements and spots, which approaches more closely to the Greek text.

Σπῖλος properly signifies a spot, Eph. 5. v. 27. Among profane writers σπῖλος is used first for a spot on a garment, for σπῖλοι, as Gellius testifies, are spots from wine or ointment adhering to garments, which discolor them, so called from ἀσπᾶν & ὕλιν from drawing mud. Secondly for a mole on the face. Among Hesychius σπιλάδες is explained by μεμιασμένοι.. Jude in the parallel passage v. 12. of the Epistle uses the word σπιλὰς,; both are from σπιλέω I spot, I contaminate. Iac. 3. v. 6. Iud. v. 23. Sap. 15. v. 4. &c. The LXX use the cognate word σπιλώματος, which corresponds to the Hebrew צאה filth. Es. 28. v. 8. just as also in this place Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 24, rendered it filth.

Μῶμος properly signifies blame from the verb μωμᾶσθαι to blame, 2. Cor. 6. v. 3. cap. 8. v. 20. The LXX use it for מום which generally signifies something in the body or action of life, which incurs reproach, and is always taken in a bad sense, namely for a spot, a vice, filth, &c. Lev. 21. v. 16. cap. 22. v. 20. cap. 24. v. 20. Deut. 15. v. 21. Jerome in the said place μώμους rendered it spots. Among profane writers it is likewise taken for disgrace, reproach, infamy, ignominy, reprehension, vituperation. Hesychius explains it by ψύγον.. The Syriac σπίλους καὶ μώμους rendered [מכתמא ומליי מומא] which Ezelius translates defilements and sprinklings of moles. But he seems to have read otherwise, for these properly have, defiled and full of spots. Luth. Sie sind Schande und Laster / with the abstract, to wit, placed for the concrete μετωνυμικῶς on account of the emphasis, as is done also in the Greek text.

But why those false teachers are called spots and blemishes is clear both from the following and from the parallel passage in Jude v. 12. οὗτοι εἴσιν ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες, in your public feasts they are spots. that is, like spots, they practice in them things base and worthy of all reproach, and by this reason they show themselves to be defiled both in soul and body. In the abstract there is great emphasis, for just as we call an eminently wicked man a wickedness: so the Apostle calls false teachers, as being eminently spotted and defiled, spots and defilements. But especially both Apostles look to this, that they are spots and reproaches of the Church, whose members they wish to be considered and associate themselves with its assembly, and meanwhile expose the name of Christians, nay, of Christ himself, to the blasphemy of enemies. Luther in his commentary on this place They imagine for themselves that they adorn Christianity, just as the Sun and Moon decorate the heaven, that they are most precious κειμήλια, like gold and gems, but Peter calls them spots and defilements.

Ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὑτῶν. The Vulgate rendered it, Luxuriating in their feasts. From which it appears that for ἀπάταις it read ἀγάπαις, which reading agrees with the parallel passage in Jude v. 12. οὑτοι εἰσὶν ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες, where likewise, as in this place, is added συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν. The Syrian followed the same reading, because both in this place and in the Epistle ⬬Jude v. 12.⬬ it has [בניחתהון] in their refreshments. Similarly also Luther, who rendered it both ways. Sie prassen von euren Allmosen. Now ἀγάπαι were public feasts, instituted in the assembly of the Church, and accustomed formerly to be joined to the celebration of the Eucharist, for the fostering of brotherly love, from which also they were called ἀγάπαι that is, charities. An elegant passage exists concerning them in Tertullian in Apolog. chap. 39. Our supper shows the reason for its name from its name, for it is called ἀγάπη, that which is love among the Greeks. Whatever the cost may be, it is gain to make an expenditure in the name of piety, since we also help the needy with this refreshment. It admits nothing of baseness, nothing of immodesty. One does not recline before prayer to God is tasted beforehand. it is eaten, as much as the hungry can take, it is drunk, as much as is useful to the modest. They are so satisfied that they remember that God must be adored by them even through the night: they converse in such a way that they know the Lord is present. In these ἀγὰπαις those false teachers are called ἐντρυφῶντες. τρυφὴ, as we warned a little above, it signifies luxury and delights. ἐδέσματα τρυφῆς Sap. 19. v. 11. they are called delicate foods, the LXX use for עדן from which is the Greek ἡδονὴ pleasure, delights Gen. 2. v. 15. Ierem. 51. v. 34. Thren. 4. v. 5. Thence the verb τρυφᾶν and the compound ἐντρυφᾶν to live delicately, to delight, to indulge in pleasures, to be entirely given over and immersed in delights, for the preposition ἐν in composition intensifies the meaning. The LXX use for ענג to delight, Esai. 55. v. 3. cap. 57. v. 4. The sense therefore would be that those false teachers in their banquets, covered over with the specious name of ἀγάπων are entirely given over to luxury and pleasures.

But because the Greek Codices constantly read ἀπάταις, not ἀγάπαις, thence it is more correctly translated, delighting in their deceits, so that the sense may be that those false teachers through manifold frauds seek and heap up those things which they afterwards abuse for luxury and delights; and thus they procure delights by their frauds, and deceive others by their hypocrisy, while they pretend to be true teachers. Osiander in h. l. When they have deceived simple Christians with their lies and impostures and have fleeced them of money, they afterwards squander the same on splendid and sumptuous banquets, on gambling, magnificent structures, and harlots. This exposition is confirmed by the reciprocal pronoun αὑτῶν, which better agrees with ταῖς ἀπάταις, than ταῖς ἀγάπαις. For if they were called ἀγάπαις αὑτῶν, it would be claimed for those impious men, which belonged to the whole Church. For ἀγάπαι were not the property of those men, and therefore αὐτῶν could not be added, since they were common to the whole Church, which the following member also declares, συνευωχούμευοι ὑμῖν. Erasmus followed the same reading, except that he rendered it a little differently, namely in this way. Insulting you with their errors, because ἐντρυφᾶν with the dative signifies, to mock someone through delights and lasciviousness, to hold someone in derision. Lucian τοιαῦτα ἐντρυφῶσι, μᾶλλον δὲ ἐνυβρίζουσι τοῖς ἀποροῦσι οἱ πλούσιοι. ἐντρυφώμενος ὑπότιμος in Plutarch is held in derision and contempt by someone. See Budaeus p. 1071. but because the dative ὑμῖν not it is constructed with the participle ἐντρυφοῦντες, but with the participle συνευωχούμενοι, therefore the former exposition, by which ἐντρυφοῦντες is explained as those who are delighting, those who are abounding in delights, is more in agreement with the text, just as also in the parallel passage Iudae v. 12. Luther seems to have read ἐντυφῶντες, for thus he annotates in the margin of this passage. ἐντυφῶντες they are properly those who take things for a game and delights; who mock men to their great inconvenience, nor do they suffer themselves to be reproved for their sins. But the Greek codices consistently read ἐντρυφῶντες.

Συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν. Vulg. luxuriating with you, εὐωχία signifies a banquet, a feast, which most derive from ὀχὴ food. But Athenaeus prefers to derive it from εὐ & ἔχειν, for thus he writes in book 9. τὰς δε εὐωχίας ἐκάλουν οὐκ ἀπὸ τὴς ὀχῆς, ὅ ἔστι τροφῆς, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ τοῦ κατὰ ταύτας εὐ ἔχειν. Eustathius in one place puts the former derivation, in another he joins both. Pollux εὐωχίαν says it is a public banquet, which fits this passage beautifully. From the noun εὐωχία is formed the verb εὐωχοῦμαι I am received at a banquet, I feast, I banquet and the compound συνευωχοῦμαι I feast together, whence also Augustine in the book on faith and works chapter 25 συνευωχούμενοι rendered it feasting together. In the writings of the O.T. it is read only once Iudith. 1. v. 16. concerning Nebuchadnezzar: He was there (in Nineveh) ῥαθυμῶν καὶ εὐωχούμενος holding luxurious banquets. For although εὐωχοῦσθαι generally signifies to feast, to hold banquets, yet sometimes it signifies to feast luxuriously, to hold luxurious banquets, which meaning is gathered from the response of Gorgias the Sophist, who, as Lucian reports in the Macrobii, when asked whence he had arrived at such a long old age, for he had reached his one hundred and eighth year, replied, δὶα τὸ μηδέποτε συμπεριενεχθῆναι ταῖς ἄλλων εὐωχίαις. And this meaning of luxurious banquets also fits this passage, as is gathered from the parallel passage of Jude v. 12. συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν ἀφόβως they feast luxuriously with you, or rather from your resources, collected for the sustenance of the Ministry and the use of the poor, shamelessly, with the fear of God cast off, without any respect for the Ecclesiastical congregation and the Lord's Supper, which was accustomed to be celebrated in those ἀγάπαις. 1. Corinth. 11. v. 21. Luther translates 1. Sie prassen mit dem euern. in Jude. Sie prassen von euren Allmosen ohne Schew. For συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν in Peter is δημοσίαν ἐστίασιν the same as συνευωχούμενοι ἐν ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν, in Jude. The Syriac rendered the participle ἐντρυφῶντες by [מתבסמין] taking delight in themselves, from the root [בסם] lived delicately, was in luxury, or even took delight in themselves. The participle συνευωχούμενοι is rendered [מתפנקין] acting in delights, nourishing themselves delicately, from the root [פנק] he held delicately or nourished. Both are placed in Ithpael. Gagnaeus suspects that for συνευωχεύμενοι the Vulgate Interpreter read συνευοχευὸμενοι that is, practicing the sexual act together with you, and therefore translated it as living in luxury. Lorinus approves of this, although he is forced to admit that no example of this compound is given. But also the Greek Codices constantly read συνευωχούμενον.

Q. on this passage. 1. What is to be understood by κυριότητα, which false teachers are said to despise? Resp. 1. Lorinus, the interlinear Gloss, etc., explain it concerning the supreme dominion of Christ, which they despised, who substituted Angels as Mediators to God instead of Christ, which Paul calls θρησκείαν τῶν Ἀγγέλων. Col. 2. vers. 18. Cornelius à Lapide embraces this exposition on this passage. By κυριότητα, he says, Peter signifies the Divinity, by which he is dominant over all, that is, his supreme empire, dominion, right, power, will, authority, government, and providence over all things, which Simon Magus with his followers was taking away from Christ and arrogating to himself. But Peter had already said before in v. 1. that false teachers deny the Lord who bought them, which can be accommodated to the denial of the office of Christ the Mediator. 2. Oecumenius thinks that the Universal dominion of GOD shining forth in the creation and government of the world is signified, which those false teachers undermined through their aeons and other false dogmas. Estius thinks this sense approaches more closely than the others to the dogmas of the heretics of the Apostolic time. But Jude in the parallel passage in his Epistle vers. 4. had said that those false Teachers τὸν μόνον δεσπὸτην θεὸν καὶ Κύριον ὑμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν deny, and nevertheless he attributes to them in vers. 8. that κυριότητα ἀθετοῦσι. 3. Therefore it is most simply taken concerning the political Magistrate, to whom is attributed κυριεύειν Luke 22. v. 25.

1. Tim. 6. v. 15. and the Roman Emperor is called ὁ Κύριος Act. 25. v. 26. which exposition is confirmed from the subsequent words, which are the former ἐξηγητικὰ, δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφημεῖν.

Q. 2. What does the Apostle understand by τὰς Δόξας, which false teachers are said to blaspheme? Oecumenius brings forward a double exposition. 1. That some understand by δόξας divine virtues, by which name they think the holy Angels, ministers of God, are denoted by Oecumenius, who are said to have appeared most often ἐν δόξῃ in heavenly glory. Turrianus lib. 2. de Hierarch. ordinat. cap. 9. to which can be referred what Clement of Alexandria in the parallel passage Jude v. 7. understands by δόξας Angels. Estius confirms that from the fact that it is not truly unlikely, δόξας that those are called, whom Paul calls principalities, powers, dominions, thrones. Ephes. 1. v. 21. Coloss. 1. vers. 16. He could have added the passage 1. Petr. 3. v. 22. where Peter himself calls the Angels ἐξουσίας καὶ δυνάμεις. Others add, that the School of Simon and the Gnostics, whom the Apostle touches upon in this place, feigned wonders about the Angels and devised things altogether unworthy of them, as is evident from Irenaeus, Epiphanius, Theodoret, etc. They think that the same exposition is favored by what is held in Epist. Jude v. 9. concerning Michael the Archangel, not daring to bring against the Devil a judgment of blasphemy, and what follows in Peter v. 11. Angels, greater in virtue and strength, do not bear against themselves a blasphemous judgment from the Lord. But that it cannot be proven from the series of the text in Peter and Jude that the discourse here is about Angels, will be evident from the exposition of v. 11. The remaining arguments are of little moment. 2. That some understand by δόξας Ecclesiastical Principalities, namely Apostles and Bishops: which exposition Estius confirms from the fact that experience testifies that those who are established in the government of Churches are subject to the curses and calumnies of heretics. But it cannot be demonstrated from the Scriptures that Apostles and other Doctors of the Church are called dignities or powers. Luc. 22. vers. 25. Christ says to the Apostles, The kings of the Gentiles κυριεύουσι, and those who have power are called εὐεργέται v. 26. But you not so. 2. Cor. 1. v. 24. Paul says οὐ κυριεύομεν we do not lord it over your faith. 1. Petr. 5. v. 3. οὐ κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων. 3. Most simply, therefore, by τὰς δόξας are understood glories and majesties, that is, Kings, Princes, and others established in majesty and glory, who by political power and authority are powerful, as we have shown above. Erasmus confirms this from the word κυριότητος, which preceded and is indeed of less value than δόξα,, inasmuch as it is suitable for any lord, whereas the latter is otherwise used only for a Prince, against whom the crime of high treason is said to be committed.

Δόξα and δύναμις is of the essence of the political office and of Magistrates, since they are ordained by God for that purpose, that they may exercise power, whence they are also called ἐξουσιάζοντες. Paul Tit. 1. v. 10. calls those contemners of Magistrates ἀνυποτάκτους non-subordinated, who do not acknowledge the order of inferiors and superiors established by GOD. To this exposition it is opposed: 1. That inv. 12.Peter adds that those false teachers blaspheme what they do not understand, which Jude himself also asserts in the parallel passage.v. 10.But everyone understands that the power of Kings and Magistrates is from GOD, yet in the Apostles that ignorance could easily happen, since their power was not known to all. Resp. The little word ἀγνοοῦσι signifies not simple ignorance, but affected ignorance, because they do not wish to acknowledge that the power of Kings and Princes is from GOD.

2. That in the parallel passageJude v. 11.they are said to have perished in the contradiction of Korah. Just as therefore Korah did not perish because he contemned some political Magistrate, but because he spurned Moses the leader of the people of GOD.Num. 16. v. 1. & seqq.So also those of whom the Apostle speaks do not perish because they contemn political Magistrate, but because they contemned the Apostles, who were common men, yet endowed with singular power from GOD, and refused to obey them. Resp. Nay rather, Moses can be more conveniently compared with Kings than with Apostles, since he performed the office of King among the Israelite people. Deut. 33. v. 5. Add that this example can be accommodated to the purpose of the Apostle, even if the objects of the sins are different.
