3. Estius objects to this exposition, that those heretics of whom it is treated here did not contemn the Magistrate, nay rather that Simon Magus even flattered Nero to the point of adoration. Resp. Estius is forced to admit in the same place that many interpret this passage concerning the political Magistrate, to which exposition the argument brought forward does not stand in opposition. For whence does Estius prove that Peter is dealing in this place only with the Simonians? We have shown above that the Apostle is speaking of all those heretics to act, who conform themselves to those ψευδοδιδασκάλοις in doctrine and morals. Estius himself in the exposition of verse 1 warns, that Peter uses words of the future tense for this reason, because those who had already arisen as heretics were very few in comparison to those who were yet to arise; whence he concludes the exposition of verse 11 with these words. If, however, one should prefer to understand by glories men excelling in glory (rather than Angels) the exaggeration of the crime of those who speak evil of these, taken from the Angels, will nevertheless remain valid. Therefore, he does not reject the exposition concerning the Magistrate.

Q. 3. In what sense are the Angels said not to bring a blasphemous judgment against them? Resp. Fevardentius and Lorinus bring forward eight or even nine expositions of this passage. Some refer it to evil Angels, but others to good ones. Of those who belong to the former class, some refer it to the fault, others to the punishment of the evil Angels.

Those who think that regard is had to the fault of the evil Angels bring forward various expositions. 1. Bede in his commentary writes thus. That which he says, where, signifies in that, because they despise dominion. Because they are bold, because they are self-pleasing, etc. for by doing these things the Angels deserved to become Demons and to pay the penalties for their pride.

2. Arias Montanus elicits this sense. The evil Angels, even if they have fallen away from the obedience of GOD, nevertheless do not dare to refute the sentences of GOD and those first heads and precepts of virtue and piety, which the heretics nevertheless refute and despise both by their speeches and by their actions.

3. The same man also brings forward this exposition. Although the Demons are stronger to endure the punishments of hell, yet they do not dare to blaspheme God, the author of them, lest they be punished more severely by him. How then do heretics dare to blaspheme him?

4. Gagnaeus understands it thus, The Demons do not dare to curse and blaspheme the Prelates of the Church, even though they are opposed to them; indeed, in exorcisms they submit themselves to them, although compelled. How then do heretics dare to blaspheme them and attack them with insults?

5. Some explain it thus. The Demons do not speak evil of one another, nor do they blaspheme one another; how then do men, for instance heretics, dare to speak evil of and blaspheme one another?

6. Glossa ordin. & Hugo. Demons do not bear judgment against themselves that is they do not dare nor presume to raise themselves against GOD, pressed by the weight of punishments, as they presumed before the fall. The words of the Gloss are as follows. There the wicked will be tormented, where the evil Angels, who previously had been proud against God and were punished for it, now do not bear, but rather cast off the judgment of being proud against GOD, which is execrable against themselves, because for it they are gravely punished and terrified by the magnitude of the punishments they now desist from that judgment of presumption, but these wicked ones do not yet desist.

7. Those who determine that regard should be had for the punishment of evil Angels, most go into the opinion that the punishment of false teachers is exaggerated in these words, in the sense that the infernal torments, by which they are reserved, will be intolerable to them, since not even the Angels themselves, namely the evil ones who are by Nature more excellent and stronger than men, sustain the judgment of GOD against them, but as unbearable they are exercised and blaspheme. Lyranus in this place. Demons who are stronger for sustaining, can scarcely sustain the punishment of hell. Glossa Interlin. So great is the force of the punishments, that (as) even the evil Angels, who are greater in strength and more robust for enduring than men, do not bear it as an intolerable burden. Barradius Tom. 4. Concord. Evang. lib. 5. cap. 8. Since Angels surpass men in strength and power, they cannot bear the judgment and supplication, because it is intolerable to them and execrable, in Greek βλάσφημον for by blaspheming they execrate it. The vulgate version seems to follow the same opinion, as does Luther in the vernacular version, who rendered it thus. Sie ertragen nicht das lästerliche Gericht wider sich vom Herrn; and Osiander in comment.

8. Akin to this exposition is that apostate Angels are by no means said to bear as grave a judgment from the Lord as those worst seducers. Thomas, Hugo &c. If evil Angels on account of the enumerated sins, which they suggest, do not do for example that which is of luxury, are vexed in such an atrocious and unbearable way, much more so men, who perpetrate it by deed.

9. But from the whole context especially from the parallel passage of Jude v. 9. where mention is made of Michael the Archangel, it is gathered that the Apostle is not dealing here with evil, but with good Angels, which those who acknowledge, again go into diverse opinions. Gloss. ordin. thus he explains. Or they will be tormented there i. e. before GOD, where the good Angels do not endure, but avenge, if anything execrable is said against them, just as they overthrew the Sodomites,

10. Hugo accepts it thus. The good Angels do not bring judgment against them, although sometimes against others, rising up against others by the command of GOD.

11. Certain ones elicit this sense, that the Angels of GOD do not assail one another with insults, but each one diligently performs his duties in his turn according to the delegation of GOD and they assist one another. asDan. 10. v. 13.Apoc. 12. v. 7.it is to be seen.

12. Certain ones refer the relative pronoun αὐτῶν to δόξας in the preceding verse in this way. The good Angels, although they are greater in power & dignity, nevertheless do not bring a blasphemous judgment against Magistrates before the Lord, which those false teachers do not fear to do in the least, but if at any time the Angels bring forth anything worthy of reproach against Magistrates, they nevertheless do that with due reverence without insults cast against the order divinely sanctioned. For the Angels revere the civil polity established by the Lord, & they preside over the kingdoms even of the impious as ministers of GOD, as is evident fromDan. 10. & 11.nor in the sight of the Lord against Ahab, however impious a King, is any insult brought forth by them.1. Reg. 22. v. 20.

13. The best explanation of all & most conformable to the text is gathered from the parallel passage Iudae v. 9. which has it thus. But Michael the Archangel when contending against the Devil he disputed about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a railing judgment (against him) to bring in i. e. he abstained from bringing curses upon him, he did not wish to curse him, but said. The Lord rebuke you i. e. may God restrain you, & resist your attempts, which was not to curse, but to pray to GOD for the impediment of his evil attempt. For although Michael the Archangel knew that the Devil had turned himself away from God the creator through apostasy, & had sent a repudiation to Him, nevertheless he weighed that he was still by Nature a good creature of GOD, and therefore he did not wish to curse him. It was therefore just, & indeed far more just, for those false teachers to refrain themselves from heaping curses upon the Magistrate & to weigh that the Magistrate is a holy ordinance of GOD, not to be overwhelmed with contumelies & insults, but to be honored on account of GOD. The comparison of this parallel passage shows, first that Peter is not speaking about the wicked, but concerning the good Angels. Secondly, not to exaggerate the punishment, but the guilt of the false teachers; Thirdly, to understand by a blasphemous or railing judgment, curses and insults, in this sense. Those false teachers do not fear to attack majesties and Potentates with insults and curses, since not even the holy Angels themselves, who are far greater in strength and power than them (the false teachers), bring against them a blasphemous judgment, inasmuch as when the good Angels have a dispute with the evil ones (with whom they are of the same Nature), they do not cast railing words at them, nor do they rise up against them with curses. Jerome in chapter 3 to Titus The Devil deserved a curse, but blasphemy ought not to have come forth through the mouth of the Archangel. Oecumenius in 2 Peter 2. It is an argument from the greater in this manner. If the Devil, who is more worthy to be cursed, because he is nevertheless a participant in a certain glory, did not receive that from Michael the Archangel before the Lord, they certainly are not wise who so rashly pursue all glory with curses, when they are nevertheless established far below the dignity of the Angels. It is opposed to this exposition that προσδιορισμὸς added παρὰ Κυρίῳ does not suit them. Resp. παρὰ Κυρίῳ here is the same as before the Lord, as Erasmus translates, or before the judgment of GOD.

Q. 4. Whether φθορὰ in v. 12. is used for lust? Resp. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian cites this Apostolic passage with these words. Like irrational beasts they are prone to the belly and lust. Thence it seems to some that ἅλωσιν is placed for the gluttony of the belly which it fills with captured prey; φθορὰν for lust, which is often accustomed to be called corruption, & γεγενυμένα is placed for that which is to have a proneness of Nature. But this citation of Jerome is more correctly taken for an application than a translation.

Q. 5. What are those things which false Teachers blaspheme out of ignorance? Some take it specifically concerning δόξαις,, some generally concerning the mysteries of the Christian faith. Of the former, some explain it concerning the Angels, whose Nature, orders, and offices, since they exceed the grasp of the human mind, and only those things are known about them which God has willed to reveal in the Scriptures, it is not a wonder that false teachers, as being not content with the limits set in Scripture, blaspheme. But we have warned above that by δόξας Magistrates are more correctly understood, whose office is divinely that it is an institution and salutary for the human race, since they either do not acknowledge ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι to it, or do not weigh it sufficiently exactly, it is from this that the Magistrates blaspheme out of ignorance. But nothing stands in the way of this Apostolic κατηγορία being accepted in a general sense concerning the truth of heavenly doctrine, and concerning the mysteries of the Christian faith, which false teachers defile with their invented fables, and blaspheme the truth not yet sufficiently acknowledged with their evil sayings, by which reasoning another vice and mark of the false teachers would be proposed in these words.

Q. 6. What is that corruption in which those who blaspheme are said to be corrupted? Resp. 1. Some accept it concerning the corruption of life and morals, because those false teachers, immersing themselves deeply in the mire of pleasures, through foul and unnatural lusts, extremely dishonor and vitiate human Nature, since not even brutes follow such unspeakable Sodomies: in which meaning the word φθορᾶς is accepted cap. 1. v. 4. ἀποφυγόντες τῆς ἐν κόσμῳ ἐν ἐπιθυμία φθορᾶς. and cap. 2. v. 19. they promise liberty, when they themselves are slaves φθορᾶς of corruption. But because a comparison is instituted between φθορὰν of brute animals and between φθορὰν of false teachers, therefore so that ἀπόδοσις προτάσει may correspond, by φθορὰς it is more correctly understood as spiritual destruction, just as by φθορὰν of brutes their bodily destruction had been denoted, so that the sense may be that it will come to pass that the false teachers will fall from the spiritual death of sins into eternal death.

Q. 7. Whether Peter in this place and Jude in the parallel place speak of the φθορᾷ of those false Doctors, Epist. v. 10. Resp. The place of Jude parallel to this one of ours has it thus. But these (false teachers) blaspheme those things which indeed they do not know; but those things which they know naturally as irrational animals, in them they are corrupted. In the former member Jude looks back to that which he had said in v. 8. δόξας βλασφημοῦσιν, so that the sense may be. Michael the Archangel, resisting the attempts of Satan, abstained from reviling, nor did he dare to bring a railing judgment against him: But these instruments of Satan attack with curses those things which they do not know, even the very majesties, to be reverently honored by all. In the latter member Jude looks back to that which he had said in the same verse, σάρκα μιαίνουσι, so that the sense may be. Those things which they know naturally by the senses alone without the judgment of reason, as if they were brute animals, namely those things which pertain to the sensitive appetite, such as food, drink, sleep, the use of Venus, are corrupted in these through gluttony and nefarious lusts, dishonoring the dignity of their Nature through offenses against Nature and casting themselves down below the lot of brutes. From these it appears that the name φθορᾶς in Jude is taken concerning the corruption of guilt, but in Peter concerning the corruption of punishment.

Ἐναντιοφανεία Cant. 4. v. 7. it is said concerning the Church, you are all beautiful and there is no spot in you. But it is said in this place concerning false teachers v. 13. that they are spots in the Church.

Resp. 1. A distinction must be made between the external society of the Church or the visible Church, to which hypocrites are admixed; and between the internal society of the Church or the invisible Church, whose true and living members are all holy and immaculate. 2. A distinction must also be made between the spots of infirmities, which adhere to the saints in this life, but are covered by the righteousness of Christ imputed through faith; and between the spots of malice or of sins, committed against conscience, which are absent from the truly pious.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Because the Papacy is a sink of ancient heresies, as was demonstrated in the place concerning the Church §. 230, from there also the vices, which the Apostle touches upon in this place, are discovered to have reigned in the Roman Pontiffs and the Papal Clergy. The first is the Sodomitic crime, which we showed to be denoted by εὐφημισμὸν in vers. 10. from a collation of a parallel passage. Jude v. 6. That indeed, to say nothing of incests, adulteries, and rapes, no one will deny to reign in the Papacy. Jerome in book 2 against Jovinian complains, with the heresy of Jovinian flourishing, Rome had already in his own time been defiled by the filth of the Sodomitic crime: This was as it were a certain prelude of the state, which was to be in Rome at the time of the dominant Papacy. Ulrich, Bishop of Augsburg, in an Epistle to Nicholas 1 around the year 860 writes, Pontiffs, Bishops, and Papal Clerics are driven so headlong into lust, that they know not how to abhor the most shameful embraces of males, nor of beasts. Aeneas Sylvius also mentions this Epistle. Sixtus IV was a Sodomite, and granted that crime to be practiced by his familiar Cardinals for the three summer months of June, July, and August, as Wolff reports from M. Johannes Wessel in his tract on Indulgences, tom. 11. Memorab. p. 836. Julius 2, two boys, whom the Queen of France sent with a French Cardinal to Rome to be educated, he held in delights and besides a young German, hence the distich of Grebellius.

The German came into Italy remarkable for his rare character, he returned from a boy a woman.

Concerning Leo X, Paulus Iovius in his life, p. 192, writes thus: He was not free from the infamy of Sodomy, because he seemed to love some not very honestly and to joke with them more tenderly and freely. But let us grant something to the humanity of Leo, as one who in the highest license of a fervent age and prosperous health sustained the heat with great difficulty: then, other are the vices of a Prince, other of a man. Julius 3 is written to have cherished a certain Ganymede by the name of Innocent as Jupiter did, and to have approved the Apology for such a great crime adorned by Hieronymus Mutius, who defends Sodomy, according to Sleidan, book 21 of the History, Vergerius, Bale, Cent. 8, chap. 27, Appendix.

Concerning the Cardinals, the Venetian Citizens write thus in their reply to the exhortation of Baronius, p. 46: Which even the Heathens shudder at, among the Candidates of this purple there existed those who not only held the filth of preposterous lust in delights, but also adorned it with praises in poems, which was done in this very city by Ioh. Casa, Archbishop of Benevento, Legate of the Pope. Carolus Molinaeus in an oration on the excellence of Theology and Jurisprudence held at Tübingen: Not yet five years, since Iohannes della Casa, Archbishop of Benevento, Dean of the Papal Chamber and Legate a latere with Papal power in the whole dominion of the Venetians, while performing that legation at Venice, composed and published a book on the praises of Sodomy. In that book he affirms that that most execrable crime of Sodomy is an art and a divine work, and that he is delighted by no other Venus more. This book was openly printed and sold at Venice with the author's name prefixed by Troianus Naum, a public printer. Besides this Iohannes Casa, also Grappa and Anastasius Platus commended Sodomy in public writings, as reported by Wolff, vol. 2, Memorabil. p. 421. Petrus Paulus Vergerius in the History of the Lauretan idol among other things writes thus: There was in the memory of our fathers a certain Venetian Cardinal from the Pisani family, who among his other inner and hidden letters had two little books set aside, filled with various obscene pictures and detestable images of nefarious lusts. There existed in one of them several forms of the intercourse of a man with a woman, of every turpitude and full of filthiness, and altogether alien from Nature. In the other, the modes of that execrable Venus, which, because it is established to have been familiar to the Sodomites, they call Sodomitical, appeared expressed, distinct in the greatest variety. After the death of the Cardinal, when the library furniture which he had kept equipped in his house was shaken out, one of those two lascivious little books was found, published to the light by the press at Rome in the time of Pope Julius II, and finally publicly sold and distributed while Adrian VI held the Pontificate. In the year 1538 the Breviary of Things Discovered in Monasteries, Convents, Colleges, etc., from the English Registers came to light, in which it is recorded that, in the Visitation of Monasteries instituted by the order of Henry VIII, King of England, such a multitude of pederasts, sodomites, boy-lovers, Sodomites, and Ganymedes was found in the monasteries of the cowled ones and the colleges of the mass-priests, that in each one of them you would have believed a new Sodom to be present. Wolff. Tom. 2. Memorab. p. 424.

The second is the Onanitic crime, masturbation, effeminacy called by the Apostle. 1. Cor. 6. v. 9. That this crime is frequent in the Papacy, those who preside over the hearing of the Confessions of mass-priests, monks, and nuns can testify, a thing which must be accepted as caused by the laws of forced celibacy. Carolstad. in the preface to the book on celibacy and monasticism, published in the year 21. Would that a lowered voice could speak certain things into your ear; you would certainly shudder at those things which the auditors and judges of sins, whom they call Confessors, have learned from those confessing and have taught me, things more to be unlearned than learned. They think that they do not commit a sin when, in burrows and cells and in solitude, I know not what they accomplish by rubbing, etc. Concerning this abominable and silent crime (which Thomas rightly pronounces to be graver than both fornication and adultery), we shall bring forward no more; we shall only warn of this, that it approaches most closely to ἐπιθυμίαν μιασμοῦ, which Peter taxes in those false teachers in this place, which Toletus writes in book 5, Instruct. moral. chap. 13. If anyone desires to have a pollution to relieve the temptations of the flesh by which he is afflicted, it is not a sin.

The third is contempt of the Magistrate. That it reigns in the Papacy can be demonstrated by many things. 1. The Pontiff arrogates to himself supreme power among Emperors, Kings, and Princes, by which he can cast them from their throne if they are unwilling to comply with his pleasures. The Roman Emperor, the highest Monarch on earth, must kiss the feet of the Roman Pontiff; carry on his shoulders the chair in which the Pontiff is carried, give water for his hands, hold the stirrup, lead the horse by the hand, and thus he is ordered to perform the office of a groom to perform. Ceremonial book 3, title 2. Gregory VII plotted snares for the life of Emperor Henry III, and indeed in a sacred place. Alexander III placed his foot upon the neck of Frederick I, called Barbarossa, ordering the clergy meanwhile to acclaim: You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk. Paschal II stirred up sedition against Henry X, so that he was forced to fight for his life and his fortunes. See the book of Simon Schardius concerning the perfidy of the Popes against the Emperors. 2. They exempt all clerics from the power of the civil magistrate, whence they deny that the rebellion of a cleric against the magistrate is a crime of high treason. Even the lowest person in the clerical order, by the privilege of the tonsure, as they call it, spurns the authority of the political magistrate. Hence Luther, in his book against the falsely called estate of the spirituals, fol. iii. b., writes thus: The Pope has long since dared to trample kings and princes under his feet, to cast them down from their throne and excommunicate them, to curse the same unto the fourth, ninth, etc., generation; bishops and ecclesiastics in the Papacy are despisers of dominion and blasphemers of majesties; they do not wish to be subject to any magistrate, neither in respect of their body, nor of their goods, etc. 3. They teach that the magistracy is such a state of life in which someone can be saved only with difficulty, whence they persuade the magistrate to abdicate his office and enter a monastery. 4. They keep the magistrate away from the care of religion and the reading of Scripture.

The fourth are the insults cast at the Magistrate. Most of them against the Princes devoted to the Augsburg Confession are found poured out not by the peck, or by the three-peck measure, but by the whole granary in the slanderous writings of Johannes Nass, Christoph Ungersdorff, and others. Baronius everywhere attacks with curses those Princes who touch upon ecclesiastical matters, having dared to compare the ancient Kings of the Franks on that account to robbers in the woods, Ann. 855. Bellarmine in his Judgment on the Formula of Concord attributes to its authors an illustrious lie, criticizing those very Electors and Princes devoted to the Aug. Conf., under whose name the Formula of Concord came to light.

The fifth is αὐθαδεία.. Peter describes false teachers thus, that they are αὐθάδεις pleasing to themselves. This, however, applies most especially to the Roman Pontiffs, inasmuch as they so admire their own opinions and decrees that they do not fear to make them equal to Holy Scripture, nay, even to prefer them, as is witnessed by the decree concerning communion under one kind, concerning the celibacy of priests, etc.

2. But also that part of the description of false teachers, which is proposed in v. 13., to have been abundantly fulfilled in the Papal kingdom, History and αὐτοψία testify. Who, I ask, writes Luther in the book against the falsely called Spiritual estate, vol. 2, Jena, German, fol. 112, are those who live luxuriously from the goods of others? Who think it sufficient for themselves to have delicacies of every kind supplied? Does the text need a gloss? For it is known to the common people that luxury reigns first in the courts of the Pope, Cardinals, Bishops, and Prelates. Bernard, in sermon 33 on the Song of Songs, long ago complained about this matter. They are ministers of Christ, he says, and they serve Antichrist, they walk about honored with the goods of the Lord, to which Lord they do not defer honor. Hence that harlot-like splendor which you see daily, the theatrical attire, the royal equipment: hence gold on bridles, on saddles, on spurs, and spurs shine more than altars, hence splendid tables with both foods and cups, hence carousings and drunkenness, hence zithers and lyres and flutes, hence overflowing winepresses, and full storehouses, belching from this into another, etc. For the sake of such things they wish to be, and are, Provosts of Churches, Deans, Archdeacons, Bishops, Archbishops. Ecbert, Bishop of Cologne, once said, To be a Bishop is nothing else than to indulge the flesh, to walk about pompously, to aim at profit, and to live idly in luxury. Nicholas of Clemanges in the book on the corrupt state of the Church, page 22, If anyone today is slothful, if anyone is abhorrent of labor, if anyone wishing to live luxuriously in idleness flies to the Priesthood, which once accepted, he immediately joins himself to other Priests who are lovers of pleasures, who living more according to Epicurus than according to CHRIST and frequenting taverns diligently, spend all their time drinking, eating, feasting, carousing, and playing with dice and ball. Platina in the life of Gregory IV, The Ecclesiastical Order poured itself into every luxury and lust. You might see them now in scarlet and purple robes, not men, which perhaps would seem trivial, but horses and beasts of burden, with a great order of youths preceding them as they walk, and another order of Priests following: not on donkeys, as CHRIST, the author of our dogma and the unique example of living well on earth, but on very fierce and caparisoned horses, as if they were leading a triumph from a conquered enemy. It does not pertain to speak of silver vessels and their excellent furnishings, and of food, since both the feasts of Sicily and Attalic ornaments, and Corinthian vessels, if you look at these, could be said to be of no value. John Huss in the commentary on this place, Luxury and gluttony defile the soul and body of man, and alas in these Our Clergy is submerged, abounding as if in two sins above others. Cornelius Agrippa writes in De vanitate scient. cap. 61, No tyrant has ever equaled the pomp and pride of the Roman Pontiff. Salmero tom. 9. tract. 9. p. 57. Now in many Priests and Religious, who live from the patrimony of the crucified, that Prophetic saying is fulfilled: I fed them to the full, and they committed adultery, and in the house of the harlot they rioted. Ierem. 5. The Venetian Citizens in Resp. ad Paraen. Baronii p. 45. If any among these purple-clad Satraps (Cardinals) are of a milder disposition, once they have entered upon this honor, they believe that this alone is the business given to them, to recall from hell the luxury of the pagan gluttons.

Secondly. Nor is luxury absent from Monks who have professed poverty and chastity, whence Emperor Frederick once said of Monasteries, Visit a Monastery, if you wish to know luxury. Bernard in Epist. ad Guilielm. Abbat. Dishes are set upon dishes, and instead of meat alone, from which they abstain, the large bodies of fish are doubled. Giraldus Cambrensis in Speculo lib. 2. cap. 3. records, The Monks of Winchester had complained gravely that out of thirteen dishes, which were set before them at each lunch and dinner, three had been taken away from them, and he adds, The Monks were scarcely content with sixteen dishes: Erasmus in Methodo Theol. p. 139. Mixed into the very bowels of the world, they call themselves Monks, and while pursuing royal luxury, they pretend to mendicancy. But from where do they have that from which they institute such feastings and luxurious banquets? From alms, indeed, from those things which pious and devout men have consecrated to God from their goods for the sustenance of the Ministry and the poor. Luther in the margin at this place annotates thus: Alms are Canonries and prebends, which the idle consume, and furthermore they mock the founders.

Thirdly, if we should wish to speak of Papal frauds, the day would fail us sooner than the speech. Many have long since called Indulgences pious frauds. Caesar Borgia, the bastard of Alexander VI, when he had lost several thousands in a game of dice, collected from the Jubilee and Papal Indulgences, wittily said: What else have we lost, but the sins of the Germans? The doctrine concerning purgatory, concerning the value of Masses for the dead, concerning works of supererogation, to be communicated to others through the intervention of money, concerning votive offerings and other culinary dogmas are composed of frauds and lies. How many frauds have been employed in miracles to deceive the simpler folk. We have reviewed certain examples in the place concerning the Church §. 284. Compare Selneccer part. 4. Exam. pag. 537. How many Popes were fraudulent and perjured. Concerning Alexander VI, Machiavelli writes thus in his book on the Prince, chapter 18: He acted as nothing other than a deceiver of mortals, he exercised his mind for nothing other than malice and fraud, (so that he might deceive the race of men). But in asserting, who was more effective, or who swore an oath more speciously, and in turn who performed it less, there was no one ever.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. The Vulgate version, departing greatly from the sources, rendered that δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες thus: They do not fear to introduce sects, blaspheming, by which reasoning the unbridled and proud audacity of those false teachers would be censured, because they do not fear to scatter new and erroneous dogmas, and by this reasoning to introduce sects. This version, inasmuch as it was pronounced authentic in the Council of Trent, Papist interpreters also defend in this place by whatever means they can. Lorinus annotates on this place thus: That the noun δόξης signifies a sect or opinion, no one denies, etc. A pious narrator will strive with all his might to defend the authority of the Interpreter. The authority of Oecumenius does not move me, to whom I ought rather to prefer the Interpreter, approved by the Church. Cornelius à Lapide on this place: Our (Interpreter) better, understanding ἐπάγειν, translates, they do not fear to introduce sects, for this is proper to heretics, and the Greek δόξα signifies opinions and sects.

And yet. 1. In the Greek Codices, which alone are authentic, nothing about the introduction of sects is held in this place. Lorinus is absurd when he annotates on this place thus: In an equal case I ought to embrace the Latins more than the Greeks. But this is to prefer streams, and indeed turbid ones, to the fountains. The Greek Codices are the fountains, the Latin Interpreters and narrators are the streams. 2. Peter had already said before in v. 1. that those false teachers would introduce destructive sects, from which verse that seems to have been transferred here. 3. Some Latin Manuscript Codices also, as Erasmus mentions, do not have the word introduce. 4. Although δόξα signifies not only glory, but also opinion, it is nevertheless nowhere used for a sect. 5. And not even the Vulgate Interpreter explains that as sects elsewhere. 6. The following verse 11 shows that these words are to be accepted concerning blasphemy against those who are endowed with majesty.

2. Salmero in this place thunders against Luther, because consecrated to GOD He has joined a nun to himself in matrimony, and that he has permitted men, when their wives are ailing, to rush upon their slave-girls or maidservants. But what is to be judged concerning these ἐγκλήμασι was set forth in the treatise on Marriage.

3. Cornelius à Lapide brings forward certain sayings of Luther against the Magistrate, namely, that a wise Prince is a rare bird, a good Prince is still much rarer; that the Turk is ten times more prudent and upright than our Princes, that Scripture calls them beasts. Lorinus touches upon this hatefully, that he called Princes, nay Kings, the lice of his head. Resp. 1. It is one thing to tax the vices of Magistrates; another to disapprove of the office of the Magistrate itself and the order instituted by GOD. 2. Luther does not simply and absolutely disparage the authority of the Magistrate, but if they wish to oppose themselves to GOD and His word.

4. The same Cornelius à Lapide attributes the crime of αὐθαδείας and audacity to Luther on this account, that in his book against the King of England he wrote, Here I stand, here I remain, here I glory, here I insult the Papists, the Henricians, the Sophists, and all the gates of hell. The divine majesty is on my side, so that I care nothing if a thousand Augustines, a thousand Cyprians, a thousand Henrician Churches stood against me, my dogmas shall stand and the Pope with the Henricians shall fall. Resp. This is not a carnal αὐθάδεια, but a spiritual πληροφορία, and immovable confidence of a mind relying solely on the word of GOD. Nor does Luther speak of his own person, but of his doctrine.

5. The same Cornelius also rubs the crime of αὐθαδείας upon Luther on this account, that he said.

Thus I will, thus I command, let my will stand for a reason. Item. Living I was a plague, dying I shall be your death, O Pope.

But Luther is dead, says Cornelius, but the Pope and the Papacy live and flourish. Resp. The former ἔγκλημα they elicit from the Apologetic Epistle written for the version of the passage Rom. 3., but in that same one Luther sufficiently defends himself against all the bites of sycophants, for he opposes this only to the stubborn and incurable, who desire to admit or hear no reasons. The latter does not deal with the plenary extermination of the Papacy, which Luther teaches everywhere from 2. Thess. 2. vers. 8. will follow only on the day of the last judgment, but with the significant decline of the Papal kingdom.

6. Calvinists, from the fact that false teachers are compared to brute beasts born for capture and destruction, conclude that certain ones are destined for ruin and perdition by an absolute decree of reprobation.

Resp. 1. The reason for the bodily destruction of brutes and the spiritual and eternal destruction of the impious is different. The former depends on the absolute will of GOD, by which He created brute animals for this use, that they might be caught and slaughtered; but the latter, since it concerns men created in the image of GOD in Adam, and redeemed after the fall through Christ, therefore cannot be attributed to the absolute will of GOD. 2. The comparison therefore consists in the destination to destruction, but it is not to be extended to the manner of the destination, which is not the same in both cases, but far different.

7. Cornelius à Lapide on verse 12 annotates thus: That Luther, when he had dined sumptuously in the evening, driven by despair and the furies of the Demon at night, brought death upon himself by casting a noose, his servant asserted, who was later converted to the orthodox faith, as Thomas Bozius reports in De signis Ecclesiae, tom. 2. lib. 23. cap. 3.

Resp. 1. Not even Cochlaeus himself, most mendacious αὐτοχειρίαν, attributes this to Luther. Bellarmine, lib. 4. de Eccles. cap. 17. §. Lutherus &c. brings forward these things from Cochlaeus concerning the life of Luther: Luther was taken away by a sudden death. For when he had eaten a sumptuous dinner in the evening, happy and healthy, and had provoked everyone to laughter with his witticisms, he died that same night. 2. One must believe neither a friend praising nor an enemy disparaging. Therefore, neither Cochlaeus, nor Bozius, nor Bellarmine, nor Cornelius à Lapide, sworn enemies of Luther. 3. Who that servant of Luther was, to whose testimony Bozius appeals, he does not indicate by even a little word, nor could he even indicate it. These are the fabrications of idle, indeed, of slanderous men. 4. There exists a History of the death of Luther, written by men worthy of faith, who were themselves present with him, namely by Justus Jonas, Michael Coelius, and Johannes Aurifaber of Weimar, who testify before GOD and in the sight of Christ that they report the history of his passing with holy faith and a good conscience, which is held in Tom. 8. Ien. Germ. Sleidanus mentions the sum of all those things in lib. 16. Comment. pag. 488, where he also recounts the prayer sent up to GOD a little before the end of his life, which Surius himself also recites in Comm. rerum ab orbe gestarum pag. 474, edition of the year 66. 5. Jacob Augustus Thuanus in lib. 2. Hist. pag. 30 describes the death of Luther, but mentions nothing of αὐτοχειρία. Compare the tract de Ecclesia §. 297.

8. Lorinus, ibid., censures Luther because he confessed ignorance of the Hebrew and Greek language, in Colloq. tom. 1, f. 187, because he called Jerome the Presbyter of Lyon; Irenaeus of Stridon; because he wrote that the former lived in the year 414, the latter 422, Lyra 320, tom. 2, Colloq. fol. 138, because he asserted that the name of free will was most hateful to all the Fathers, tom. 1, fol. 42, that neither Jerome nor Ambrose thought anything about Purgatory, f. 65, that until Augustine no mention was made of original sin, fol. 98, 99, that Jerome treats of nothing concerning Christ, does not speak of faith, hope, charity, or the works of faith, fol. 137.

Resp. 1: The book of Table Talk was neither edited nor approved by Luther. 2. Luther, part 2, Postill. domest. Domin. Iubilate fol. 34. b. In S. Augustini Büchern findet man diel Sprüche die Fleisch und Blut geredt haben / und ich muss auch von mir bekennen / daß ich viel Wort rede / welche nicht Gottes Wort sind / wenn ich rede ausserhalb dem Predigampt / daheim über Tisch oder sonst. 3. The version of Scripture into the vernacular language shows that Luther was not moderately skilled in both the Hebrew and Greek language. 4. Let Lorinus seek ignorance among the mass-priests and monks, among whom the Brothers of Ignorance constitute a peculiar order, but one which wanders through all the remaining orders. You have taken good care, lest any letter be able to kill you, for no letter is known to you, as Buchanan jokes against an unlearned monk. 5. What kind of edition of the Table Talk Lorinus followed, we cannot know. In our Eisleben edition of the year 66, chapter 58, fol. 529, these things are held: Jerome, Presbyter and elder of Stridon, lived in the year 422, Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyon, in the year 175. It is indeed added that Lyra lived in the year 320. But here there is either a mistake μνημονευτικὸν in Aurifaber, the collector of this book, or σφάλμα a typographical one. For Luther knew well that Lyra, whom he had read not without diligence, was not older than Augustine. To the remaining things ἐγκλήματα it is answered elsewhere.

9. Salmero in comm. v. 13 establishes: Peter in this place abused the word reward, when he calls it the reward of unrighteousness, since a reward is properly of righteousness or of a good work. Lot in the same way: Reward is called by catachresis of punishment. Resp. Scripture does not observe this distinction between the reward of a good work and the punishment of an evil one. Act. 1. v. 18. it is called μισθός ἀδικίας. Rom. 1. v. 27. ἀντιμισθία πλάνης. 2. Petr. 2. v. 15. μισθός ἀδικίας. Jude verse 11. Βαλαάμ μισθοῦ &c.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Dixerat Apostolus, falsos illos doctores notoriis flagitiis infames in sua perditione perituros. illius interius h. e. poenae divinae iustitiam indicat, quando mercedem suae iniustitiae illos reportaturos praedicit.

2. Luxuriam & intemperantiam illorum denuò perstringit, quippe quae nefandarum istarum libidinum, de quibus versu praeced. egerat, fomes est ac nutricula; cui luxuriae etiam fraudulentiam ab illis coniungi ostendit, per quam simpliciores pecuniâ emungunt, ut luxui ipsorum abundè suppetat.

Textus expositio. Κομιούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας. Syrus hoc membrum coniungens cum sequentibus, tenebras offundit textui, sic enim reddit. Cum illis, quibus inest iniquitas, merces iniquitatis suavitas reputatur oblectatio, quae est in die. Fortè significare voluit, falsos illos doctores iusto DEI iudicio ex uno peccato in aliud incidere, ut posterior iniquitas prioris sit merces. B. Lutherus in vers. Germ. rectiùs coniungit hoc membrum cum praecedentibus, quam textus seriem etiam Estio probatam confirmat participium κομιούμενον. quod cum praecedentibus omninò cohaeret.

Coeterùm illud κομιούμενοι Vulg. versio reddidit percipientes. Graeca propriè habent reportaturi in futuro, quo verbo idem Vulg. Interpres exprimit Graecum κομίζεσθαι1. Petr. 1. v. 9. uti ettiam Hebr. 10. v. 36. Lutherus rectissimè. Sie werden umbkommen / und den Lohn der Ungerechtigkeit davon bringen.

Ἀδικίας nomine quidam in specie intelligunt iniuriam, proximo contra septimum praeceptum illatam. Sed rectiùs generaliter accipitur pro quibusvis gravioribus peccatis, contra secundam Decalogi tabulam commissis, ut etiam complectatur foedas libidines, earumque fomitem luxuriem, ut ex antecedentibus & consequentibus huius loci colligitur. Haec generalis significatio vocis ἀδικίας in Scripturis frequens est. Luc. 13. vers. 27.ἐργάται τῆς ἀδικίας.Rom. 1. v. 18.ἀσέβεια καὶ ἀδικία coniunguntur. Prius exprimit peccata contra primam, posterius peccata contra secundam Decalogi tabulam. 1. Ioh. 5. v. 17.πᾶσα ἀδικία ἁμαρτία ἐστι. Syrus reddidit per [עולא] â rad. [עול]iniquè, perversè egit. Sensus igitur est, flagitiosos illos damnationem pro mercede scelerum suorum reportaturos.

Ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν. Hieronymus voculam ἡδονὴν videtur coniungere cum praecedentibus, sic enim citat hunc locum, lib. 1. contra Iovinian. Recipientque mercedem iniquitatis luxuriam. Beda in comm. itidem monet, quosdam voculamηβονηνconiungere cum verbis praecedentibus hoc modo. Mercedem percipientes iniustitiae voluptatem.Rom. 1. v. 24. & 27. Sed quilibet videt, hoc esse coactum. Graeci Codd. voculam ἡδονὴν coniungunt cum verbis sequentibus. Circa participium ἡγούμενοι quibusdam ἀπὸ κοινοῦ ex versu praeced. repetendum videtur pronomen οὗτοι.Hi sunt, qui voluptatem existimant. Sed sensui sine illa repetitione sua constat integritas.

Τρυφὴ significat luxum & delitias.Luc. 7. v. 25. Syrus reddidit, [בוסמא] â rad. [בסם]delicatè, in luxu vixit.Iac. 5. v. 5.

Phrasis ἐν ἡμέρᾳ variis modis exponitur. 1. Quidam statuunt, positam esse proκαθ' ἡμέρανquotidiè, ut sit sensus. Iudicant esse summum bonum ac gaudium, si quotidiè in delitiis vivere & epulari possint, sicut de divite epulone diciturLuc. 16. vers. 19.εὐφραινὸμενος καθ' ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς. Oecumenius in h. l. Voluptatem quotidianum luxum aestimantes, hoc est, veram & amabilem laetitiam & voluptatem in quotidiana gulae fruitione constituentes: Erasmus in paraphrasi. Pro voluptate ducentes, si in diem delitiis fruantur. Beza in h. l. ἐν ἡμέρα,nihil aliud declarat, quàmExod. 29. vers. 36.ליום pro καθ' ἡμέραν. Sed si hoc voluisset Apost. dixisset, ἡμέραν εἰς ἡμέραν τρυφῶντες, ut loquitur in v. 8. huius cap. vel τὴν καθ' ἡμέραν τρυφὴν ὑδονὴν ἡγούμενοι.

2. Beda in comm. ad praeconceptam voluptuo sorum illorum opinionem respectum haberi statuit. Voluptas, inquit, & in bono accipitur & in malo &c. Voluptas bona diei vocatur, quâ sancti quique delectantur in Domino. Voluptas autem malae noctis est, cùm reprobi ad perficienda opera tenebrarum perversè delectantur. Benè ergo dicit de iniustis, quòd voluptatem existiment diei, delitias coinquinationis & maculae, quia multi in tantum suo corde perversi & inverecundi existunt, ut cùm delitiis impurissimis vacent & execrandissimis, has tamen ipsi optimas & quasi lucifluas iudicent.

3. Quidam existimant, diei notanter fieri mentionem, ut impudentia illorum flagitio sorum exprimatur, quòd exuto omni prorsus pudore non vereantur in clara diei luce comessari ac libidinibus indulgere, cùm alioqui â filiis tenebrarum isthaec noctu fieri consueverint.Rom. 13. v. 12.Nox praecessit, dies appropinquavit, abiiciamus ergo opera tenebrarum. v. 13. Sicut in die honestè ambulemus, non in comessationibus & ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus & impudicitiis.1. Thessal. 5. v. 7.Qui ebrii sunt, nocte ebrii sunt.

4. Simplicissimè statuitur, per τὴν ἡμέραν intelligi praesentis vitae tempus, quod ad diem aeternitatis (de quo in hac Epist. cap. 3. v. 18.) comparatum est unius diei instar, cap. eiusd. v. 8. Exaggeratur igitur flagitiosorum istorum epicuraea securitas, quòd novissimi iudicii ac venturi seculi parùm memores felicitatem statuant, in praesentibus delitiis, quae tamen vix per dieculam durent, ut sit sensus. Voluptatem existimant dieculares delitias, posse uno & altero die delitiari, brevi tempore delitiis perfrui. Luth. Sie achtens für Wollust das zeitliche Wolleben.

Σπῖλοι καὶ μῶμοι. Quidam Codd. Latini legunt in Genitivo coinquinationis & maculae, quae lectio etiam apud Bedam occurrit. Ex castigatione Romana hodie in plerisque Codd. Latinis legitur, coinquinationes & maculae, quod propiùs accedit ad Graecum textum.

Σπῖλος propriè significat maculam,Eph. 5. v. 27. Apud profanos scriptores σπῖλος usurpatur primò pro maculâ in veste,σπῖλοι enim, teste Gellio, sunt maculae ê vino vel unguine vestibus inhaerentes, quae eas decolorant, sic dictae âἀσπᾶν & ὕλινâ trahendo ceno. Secundò pro naevo in facie. Apud Hesychium σπιλάδες exponitur μεμιασμένοι. Iudas in loco parallelo v. 12. Epist. utitur voce σπιλὰς, utrumque est â σπιλέωmaculo, contamino.Iac. 3. v. 6.Iud. v. 23.Sap. 15. v. 4. &c. LXX. utuntur cognatâ voce σπιλώματος, quae respondet Hebr. צאהsordes.Es. 28. v. 8. sicut etiam h. l. Hieronymus l. 1. contra Iovin. c. 24. reddidit sordes.

Μῶμος propriè significat vituperium â verbo μωμᾶσθαιvituperare,2. Cor. 6. v. 3.cap. 8. v. 20. LXX. usurpant pro מום quod generaliter significat aliquid in corpore vel actione vitae, quod incurrit reprehensionem, & semper in malum accipitur, videlicet pro maculâ, vitio, sordibus &c. Lev. 21. v. 16.cap. 22. v. 20.cap. 24. v. 20.Deut. 15. v. 21. Hieronymus d. l. μώμους reddidit maculas. Apud Scriptores profanos itidem accipitur pro dedecore, probro, infamiâ, ignominiâ, reprehensione, vituperatione. Hesychius exponit per ψύγον. Syr. σπίλους καὶ μώμους redd. [מכתמא ומליי מומא] quod Ezelius vertit commaculationes & aspersiones naevorum. Sed videtur aliter legisse, haec enim propriè habent, inquinati & pleni maculis. Luth. Sie sind Schande und Laster / abstracto sc. posito pro concreto μετωνυμικῶς propter emphasin, uti fit etiam in textu Graeco.

Quare verò dicantur illi falsi doctores maculae & vituperia, patet tum ex sequentibus, tum ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 12. οὗτοι εἴσιν ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες,in conviviis vestris publicis sunt maculae. h. e. instar macularum, exercent in illis turpia & omni vituperatione digna, atque hac ratione sese & animo & corpore pollutos esse ostendunt. In abstracto est magna emphasis, ut enim hominem insigniter sceleratum vocamus scelus: sic Apostolos falsos doctores, utpote insigniter maculatos & inquinatos vocat maculas & inquinamenta. Cumprimis verò uterque Apostolus eò respicit, quòd sint maculae & probra Ecclesiae, cuius membra haberi volunt ac caetui eius sese associant, atque interim Christianorum, imò ipsius Christi nomen blasphemiae hostium exponunt. Lutherus in comm. h. l. Imaginantur sibi, quòd Christianismum ornent, sicut Sol & Luna caelum condecorant, quòd sint preciosissimaκειμήλια,sicut aurum & gemmae, sed Petrus eos vocat maculas & inquinamenta.

Ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὑτῶν. Vulg. reddidit, Delitiantes in conviviis suis. Ex quo apparet, quòd pro ἀπάταις legerit ἀγάπαις, quae lectio congruit loco parallelo Iud. v. 12. οὑτοι εἰσὶν ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες, ubi itidem, ut hoc loco additur συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν. Eandem lectionem secutus fuit Syrus, quia & h. l. & in Epist. Iudae v. 12. habet [בניחתהון]in refectionibus suis. Similiter & Lutherus, qui utrobique reddidit. Sie prassen von euren Allmosen. Erant autem ἀγάπαι convivia publica, in conventu Ecclesiae instituta, ac celebrationi Eucharistiae olim coniungi solita, ad fovendam fraternam caritatem, ex quo etiam, ἀγάπαι h. e. caritates dicta fuêrunt. Extat de illis elegans locus apud Tertullianum in Apolog. cap. 39. Cena nostra de nomine rationem sui ostendit, vocatur enimἀγάπη,id quod dilectio penes Graecos est. Quantiscunque sumtibus constet, lucrum est. pietatis nomine sumptum facere, siquidem inopes quoque refrigerio isto iuvamus, Nihil vilitatis, nihil immodestiae admittit. Non priùs discumbitur, quàm oratio ad Deum praegustetur: editur, quantum esurientes capiunt, bibitur, quantum pudicis est utile. Ita saturantur, ut qui meminerint, etiam per noctem adorandum Deum sibi esse: ita fabulantur, ut qui sciant Dominum adire. In hisce ἀγὰπαις falsi illi doctores dicuntur ἐντρυφῶντες. τρυφὴ, ut monuimus paulò superiùs, significat luxum & delitias. ἐδέσματα τρυφῆςSap. 19. v. 11. dicuntur cibi delicati, LXX. utuntur pro עדן â quo est Graecorum ἡδονὴvoluptas, delitiaeGen. 2. v. 15.Ierem. 51. v. 34.Thren. 4. v. 5. Inde verbum τρυφᾶν & compositum ἐντρυφᾶνdelicatè vivere, delitiari, voluptatibus indulgere, delitiis totum esse deditum & immersum, praepositio enim ἐν in compositione inten dit significationem. LXX. utuntur pro ענגdelitiari,Esai. 55. v. 3.cap. 57. v. 4. Sensus igitur foret, quòd falsi illi doctores in conviviis suis, specioso ἀγάπων nomine oblevatis, luxui & voluptatibus toti sint dediti.

Sed quia Graeci Codd. constanter legunt ἀπάταις, non ἀγάπαις, inde rectiùs vertitur, deliciantes in deceptionibus suis, ut sit sensus, falsos illos doctores per multiplices fraudes ea conquirere & coacervare, quibus postea ad luxum & delitias abutuntur; adeoque fraudibus suis delitias comparare, hypocrisi suâ alios decipere, dum se veros doctores simulant. Osiander in h. l. Cùm mendaciis & imposturis suis deceperint simplices Christianos & pecuniâ eosdem emunxerint, postea eandem in splendida & lauta convivia, in aleam, structuras magnificas, & scorta profundunt. Hanc expositionem confirmat pronomen reciprocum αὑτῶν, quod meliùs congruit ταῖς ἀπάταις, quàm ταῖς ἀγάπαις. Quòd si enim dicuntur ἀγάπαις αὑτῶν, impiis istis vendicaretur, quod totius Ecclesiae erat. Neque enim ἀγάπαι istorum hominum erant propriae, ac proinde αὐτῶν addi non potuit, cùm communes essent Ecclesiae totius, quod etiam declarat sequens membrum, συνευωχούμευοι ὑμῖν. Eandem lectionem secutus fuit Erasmus, nisi quod paulò aliter reddiderit, videlicet hoc modo. Erroribus suis vobis insultantes, quia ἐντρυφᾶν cum dativo significat, per delitias & lasciviam alicui illudere, aliquem ludibrio habere. Lucian. τοιαῦτα ἐντρυφῶσι, μᾶλλον δὲ ἐνυβρίζουσι τοῖς ἀποροῦσι οἱ πλούσιοι. ἐντρυφώμενος ὑπότιμος apud Plutarchum est ludibrio & contemtui ab aliquo habitus. Vide Budaeum p. 1071. sed quia dativus ὑμῖν non cum participio ἐντρυφοῦντες, sed cum participio συνευωχούμενοι construitur, ideò prior expositio, quâ ἐντρυφοῦντες exponitur per delitiantes, delitiis affluentes, magis congruit textui, uti etiam loco parallelo Iudae v. 12. Lutherus videtur legisse ἐντυφῶντες, sic enim ad marginem huius loci annotat. ἐντυφῶντεςpropriè sunt, qui pro ludo & delitiis habent; qui hominibus cum magno eorundem incommodo illudunt, nec patiuntur ob peccata sua sese argui. Sed Graeci Codd. constanter legunt ἐντρυφῶντες.

Συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν. Vulg. luxuriantes vobiscum,εὐωχία significat convivium, epulum, quod plerique deducunt ab ὀχὴcibus. Sed Athenaeus ab εὐ & ἔχειν derivari mavult, sic enim scribit lib. 9. τὰς δε εὐωχίας ἐκάλουν οὐκ ἀπὸ τὴς ὀχῆς, ὅ ἔστι τροφῆς, ἀλλ' ὑπὸ τοῦ κατὰ ταύτας εὐ ἔχειν. Eustathius in uno loco priorem derivationem ponit, in altero utramque coniungit. Pollux εὐωχίαν dicit esse δημοσίαν ἐστίασινconvivium publicum, quod pulchrè huic loco congruit. Ex nomine εὐωχία formatur verbum εὐωχοῦμαιconvivio excipior, convivor, epulor ac compositum συνευωχοῦμαιunà epulor, unde etiam Augustinus lib. de fid. & operibus cap. 25. συνευωχούμενοι reddidit coepulantes. In Scriptis V. T. semel tantum legitur Iudith. 1. v. 16. de Nabuchodonosore: Erat ibi (in Ninive) ῥαθυμῶν καὶ εὐωχούμενοςluxuriosa convivia agitans. Quamvis enim εὐωχοῦσθαι generaliter significet epulari, convivia agitare, tamen quandoque significat luxuriosè epulari, luxuriosa convivia agitare, quae significatio colligitur ex responso Gorgiae Sophistae, qui referente Luciano in Macobio interrogatus, unde ad tam longam senectutem pervenisset, nam centesimum & octavum annum attigerat, respondit, δὶα τὸ μηδέποτε συμπεριενεχθῆναι ταῖς ἄλλων εὐωχίαις. Atque haec conviviorum luxuriosorum significatio etiam huic loco congruit, uti colligitur ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 12. συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν ἀφόβωςluxuriantur vobiscum, vel potius de facultatîbus vestris, in sustentationem Ministerii & usum pauperum collatis, impudenter, excusso Dei timore, absque ullo congregationis Ecclesiasticae & Cenae Dominicae, in illis ἀγάπαις celebrari solitae, respectu. 1. Corinth. 11. v. 21. Lutherus vers. 1. Sie prassen mit dem euern. apud Iudam. Sie prassen von euren Allmosen ohne Schew. Nam συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν apud Petrum est idem quod συνευωχούμενοι ἐν ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν, apud Iudam. Syrus participium ἐντρυφῶντες reddidit per [מתבסמין]oblectantes se, ârad. [בסם]delicatè vixit, in luxufuit, vel etiam sese oblectavit. Participium συνευωχούμενοι redd. [מתפנקין]delicias agentes, delicatè se nutrientes, â rad. [פנק] delicatè habuit vel nutrivit. Utrumque ponitur in Ithpael. Gagnaeus suspicatur, proσυνευωχεύμενοι vulg. Interp. legisse συνευοχευὸμενοι h. e. unà vobiscum rem Veneream exercentes, ac proinde vertisse luxuriantes. Lorinus hoc approbat, quamvis fateri cogatur, nullum huius compositi dari exemplum. Sed & Graeci Codd. constanter legunt συνευωχούμενον.

Q. hoc loco. 1. Quid perκυριότητα,quam falsi doctores contemnere dicuntur, intelligatur? Resp. 1. Lorinus, Glossa interlin. &c. exponunt de suprema Christi dominatione, quam contemserunt, qui pro Christo Angelos ad Deum Mediatores substituerunt, quam Paulus vocatθρησκείαν τῶν Ἀγγέλων.Col. 2. vers. 18. Hanc expositionem amplectitur Cornelius â Lapide in h. l. Perκυριότητα, inquit, Petrus significat Divinitatem, quâ dominantem omnibus, puta summum eius imperium, dominium, ius, potestatem, arbitrium, autoritatem gubernationem & providentiam in res omnes, quam Christo adimebat, sibique arrogabat Simon Magus cum suis. Sed Petrus iam antè dixerat in v. 1. quòd falsi doctores eum, qui emit ipsos, Dominum negent, id quod ad officii Christi Mediatorii negationem accommodari potest. 2. Oecumenius significari putat Universalem DEI dominationem in creatione & gubernatione mundi relucentem, quam falsi illi doctores per suos aeonas & alia falsa dogmata labefactarint. Hunc sensum Estius putat propiùs quàm caeteros accedere ad dogmata haereticorum Apostolici temporis. Sed Iudas in loco parallelo Epist. vers. 4. dixerat, quòd falsi illi Doctores,τὸν μόνον δεσπὸτην θεὸν καὶ Κύριον ὑμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸνnegent, ac nihilominus illis tribuit vers. 8. quod κυριότητα ἀθετοῦσι. 3. Simplicissimè ergo accipitur de Magistratu politico, cui tribuitur κυριεύεινLuc. 22. v. 25.

1. Tim. 6. v. 15. ac Imperator Romanus vocatur ὁ ΚύριοςAct. 25. v. 26. quae expositio confirmatur ex verbis subsequentibus, quae sunt priorum ἐξηγητικὰ, δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφημεῖν.

Q. 2. Quid perτὰς Δόξας,quas falsi doctores dicuntur blasphemare, Apostolus intelligat? Oecumenius duplicem affert expositionem. 1. Quod quidam per δόξαςintelligant divinas virtutes, quo nomine putant ab Occumenio denotari sanctos Angelos, Dei ministros, qui saepiùs ἐν δόξῃ in gloria caelesti apparuisse dicuntur. Turrianus lib. 2. de Hierarch. ordinat. cap. 9. quò referri potest, quod Clemens Alexandr. in loco parallelo Iud. v. 7. per δόξας intelligit Angelos. Estius illud confirmat ex eo, quòd non sit vero absimile,δόξαςillos vocari, quos Paulus vocat principatus, potestates dominationes, thronos.Ephes. 1. v. 21.Coloss. 1. vers. 16. Potuisset addere locum. 1. Petr. 3. v. 22. ubi ipse Petrus Angelos vocat ἐξουσίας καὶ δυνάμεις. Addunt alii, Scholam Simonis & Gnosticorum, quos Apostolus h. l. perstringat, mirabilia finxisse de Angelis. & indigna prorsus de illis excogitasse, ut constat ex Irenaeo, Epiphanio, Theodoreto &c. Eidem expositioni favere putant, quod in Epist. Iudae v. 9. habetur de Michaele Arch Angelo, non auso inferre Diabolo iudicium blasphemiae, ac quod apud Petrum sequitur v. 11. Angelos virtute & fortitudine maiores non pertare adversum se â Domino blasphemum iudicium. Sed ex serie textus apud Petrum & Iudam non posse probari, quod de Angelis h. l. sermo sit, patebit ex v. 11. expositione. Reliqua argumenta momenti sunt exigui. 2. Quòd quidam perδόξαςintelligant Ecclesiasticos Principatus, videl. Apostolos & Episcopos: quam expositionem Estius confirmat ex eo, quod experientia testetur, illos, qui in regimine Ecclesiarum constituti sunt, maledictis & calumniis haereticorum esse obnoxios. At non poterit ex Scripturis demonstrari, Apostolos & alios Ecclesiae Doctores dignitates vel potestates appellari. Luc. 22. vers. 25. inquit Christus ad Apostolos. Reges gentiumκυριεύουσι,& qui habent potestatem vocanturεὐεργέταιv. 26.Vos autem non sic2. Cor. 1. v. 24. inquit Paulus οὐ κυριεύομενnon dominamur fidei vestrae.1. Petr. 5. v. 3.οὐ κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων. 3. Simplicissimè ergo per τὰς δόξας intelliguntur gloriae & maiestates h. e. Reges, Principes & alii in maiestate & gloria constituti, qui politicâ potestate & autotate pollent, ut superiùs ostendimus. Erasmus hoc confirmat ex voce κυριότητος, quae praecessit & minus quidem valet, quam δόξα, utpote conveniens cuivis hero, cùm haec aliàs Principi duntaxat, contra quem crimen laesae maiestatis committi dicitur.

Δόξα ac δύναμις est de essentia muneris politici ac Magistratuum, quippe qui â Deo ad illud ordinati sunt, ut potentiam exerceant, unde etiam ἐξουσιάζοντες vocantur. Paulus Tit. 1. v. 10. contemtores illos Magistratuum vocat ἀνυποτάκτους nonsubordinatos, qui non agnoscunt, ordinem inferiorum ac superiorum â DEO constitutum. Opponitur huic expositioni. 1. Quòd inv. 12.Petrus subiungat, falsos illos doctores blasphemare, quod non intelligunt, quod ipsum etiam Iudas asserit in loco parallelo.v. 10.Sed Regum & Magistratuum potentiam â DEO esse, omnes intelligunt, in Apostolis verò illa ignorantia facilè contingere poterat, quippe quorum potentia non erat omnibus nota. Resp. vocula ἀγνοοῦσι non ignorantiam simplicem, sed affectaram significat, quòd nolint agnoscere, potentiam Regum & Principum esse â DEO.

2. Qued in loco paralleloIudae v. 11.dicuntur periisse contradictione Core. Quemadmodum ergo Core non ideò periit, quòd Magistratum aliquem politicum contemneret, sed quia Mosen spernebat Dutem populi DEI.Num. 16. v. 1. & seqq.Sic etiam illi, de quibus Apostolus loquitur, non ideò pereunt, quòd Magistratum politicum contemnant, sed quia Apostolos, qui vulgares erant homines, singulari tamen potentiâ â DEO praediti contemnerent & illis parere recusarent. Resp. imò verò Moses commodiùs potest cum Regibus, quàm cum Apostolis comparari, cùm in populo Israëlitico functus fuerit officio Regis. Deut. 33. v. 5. Adde quòd possit hoc exemplum accommodari ad propositum Apostoli, etiamsi obiecta peccatorum sint diversa.

3. Estius huic expositioni obiicit, haereticos illos, de quibus hîc agitur, non contemsisse Magistratum, quinimò Simonem Magum usque ad adorationem Neroni fuisse assentatum. Resp. Estius ibidem fateri cogitur, multos hunc locum de Magistratu politico interpretari, cui expositioni allatum argumentum non adversatur. Unde enim probat Estius de solis Simonianis Petrum hoc loco agere? Ostendimus superiùs, de omnibus illis haereticis Apostolum agere, qui doctrinâ & moribus illis ψευδοδιδασκάλοις sese conformant. Estius ipse in exposit. vers. 1. monet, Petrum ideò uti verbis futuri temporis, quia qui iam exorti erant haeretici, pauci admodum erant, comparatione eorum, qui adhuc erant exorituri; unde expositionem vers. 11. hisce concludit. Si tamen per glorias quis intelligere maluerit homines gloriâ praecellentes (quàm Angelos) nihilominus valebit criminis eorum, qui his maledicunt, exaggeratio ab Angelis sumta. Ergo expositionem de Magistratu non repudiat.

Q. 3. Quo sensu Angeli negentur ferre adversus se iudicium blasphemum? Resp. Fevardentius & Lorinus octo vel etiam novem expositiones huius loci afferunt. Quidam referunt ad Angelos malos, quidam verò ad bonos. Qui ad priorem classem pertinent, eorum aliqui ad culpam, aliqui ad poenam malorum Angelorum referunt.

Qui ad culpam malorum Angelorum respectum haberi existimant, varias proferunt expositiones. 1. Beda in comm. sic scribit. Quod ait, ubi, significat in eo, quod dominationem contemnunt. quod audaces, quod sibi placentes sunt, &c. haec namque faciendo Angeli Daemonia fieri ac poenas suae superbiae solvere meruerunt.

2. Arias Montanus hunc elicit sensum. Angeli mali, etiamsi â DEI obsequio desciverint, tamen DEI sententias & illa prima virtutis ac pietatis capita & praecepta minimè refellere audent, quae nihilominus haeretici & orationibus & actionibus refellunt ac contemnunt.

3. Idem etiam hanc profert expositionem. Daemones licet fortiores sint ad perferendas inferni poenas, tamen non audent Deum earum autorem blasphemare, ne graviùs ab eo puniantur, Quomodo ergo eum blasphemare audent haeretici.

4. Gagnaeus sic accipit, Daemones non audent execrari & blasphemare Praepositos Ecclesiae, licet sibi adversos, imò in exorcismis eis sese subdunt, licet coacti, quomodo ergo haeretici eos audent blasphemare & convitiis incessere?

5. Quidam sic exponunt. Daemones sibi invicem non maledicunt, nec se mutuò blasphemant, quomodo ergo homines, puta haeretioi, audent sibi invicem maledicere & blasphemare.

6. Glossa ordin. & Hugo. Daemones non portant iudicium adversùm se h. e. non audent nec praesumunt se erigere contra DEUM, pressi mole poenarum, sicut praesumobant ante lapsum. Verba Glossae sic habent. Ibi cruciabuntur iniqui, ubi Angeli mali, qui priùs contra Deum superbierant & inde puniti sunt, iam non portant, sed potius abiiciunt iudicium superbiendi contra DEUM, quod ex execrabile adversus seipsos, quia pro illo graviter puniuntur & territi magnitudine poenarum iam ab illo iudicio praesumtionis desistunt, sed isti iniqui nondum desistunt.

7. Qui ad poenam malorum Angelorum respectum haberi statuunt, plerique in eam abeunt sententiam, quòd poena falsorum doctorum in his verbis exaggeretur, sensu eo, quòd tormenta infernalia, quibus ipsire servantur, futura sint ipsis intollerabilia, cùm nec ipsi Angeli, mali sc. qui Naturâ praestantiores & fortiores sunt hominibus, DEI adversus se iudicium sustineant, sed ut importabile exercentur & blasphement. Lyranus in h. l. Daemones qui sunt fortiores ad sustinendum, vix possunt sustinere poenam inferni. Glossa Interlin. Tanta vis est poenarum, quod (ut) & mali Angeli, qui sunt maiores fortitudine & robustiores ad perferendum quàm homines, non portent quasionus intolerabile. Barradius Tom. 4. Concord. Evang. lib. 5. cap. 8. Cùm Angeli superent homines robore & potentia, non possunt ferre iudicium & supplicium, quia intolerabile est illis & execrabile, Graecèβλάσφημονblasphemando enim illud execrantur. Eandem sententiam sequi videtur vulgata versio, ut & Lutherus in versione vernacula, qui sic reddidit. Sie ertragen nicht das lästerliche Gericht wider sich vom Herrn; ac Osiander in comment.

8. Affinis est huic expositioni ea, quod Angeli apostatici nequaquam tam grave iudicium â Domino perferre dicantur, quàm seductores illi pessimi. Thomas, Hugo &c. Si Angeli mali propter enumerata peccata, quae suggerunt, non faciunt verbi gratia id quod est luxuriae, tam atroci & importabili vexantur modo, multò magis homines, qui facto perpetrant.

9. Sed ex toto contextu praesertim ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 9. ubi Michaëlis Arch Angeli fit mentio, colligitur, Apostolum non de malis, sed de bonis Angelis hîc agere, quod ipsum qui agnoscunt, iterum in diversas abeunt sententias. Gloss. ordin. sic exponit. Vel torquebuntur ibi i. e. apud DEUM, ubi Angeli boni non sustinent, sed vindicant, si quid execrabile contra illos dicitur, sicut subverterunt Sodomitas,

10. Hugo sic accipit. Boni Angeli non portant iudicium adversus se, quamvis aliquando adversus alios insligentes aliis iussu DEI.

11. Quidam hunc eliciunt sensum, quod Angeli DEI non alii alios convitiis incessant, sed singuli suis vicibus secundùm delegationem DEI diligenter perfungantur ac alii aliis subveniant. utDan. 10. v. 13.Apoc. 12. v. 7.videre est.

12. Quidam pronomen relativum αὐτῶν referunt ad δόξας in v. praeced. hoc modo. Angeli boni, quamvis sint virtute & dignitate maiores, tamen non ferunt blasphemum iudicium adversùs Magistratus apud Dominum, quod tamen falsi illi doctores facere minimè reformidant, sed si quando Angeli contra Magistratus quidquam reprehensione dignum proferunt, faciunt tamen illud debitâ reverentiâ sine convitiis, in ordinem divinitus sancitum iactis. Reverentur enim Angeli politiam civilem â Domino constitutam, & regnis etiam impiorum custodiendis tanquam ministri DEI praesunt, ut constat exDan. 10. & 11.neque in conspectu Domini adversus Achabum, quantumvis imptum Regem, convitium allum ab ipsis profertur.1. Reg. 22. v. 20.

13. Omnium optima & textui maximè conformis explicatio colligitur ex loco parallelo Iudae v. 9. qui sic habet. Atque Michael Arch Angelus cùm adversus Diabolum certans disputaret de corpore Mosis, non est ausus iudicium maledicum (ei) inferre h. e. â maledictis ei inferendis abstinuit, noluit ei maledicere, sed dixit. Increpet te Dominus i. e. Deus te coërceat, & conatibus tuis resistat, quod non erat maledicere, sed mali conatus impedimentum â DEO ipsi imprecari. Quamvis enim Michaël Arch Angelus sciret, Diabolum per apostasian â Deo creatore sese avertisse, & repudium ei misisse, tamen expendit, ipsum Naturâ adhuc esse bonam DEI creaturam, ideoque ei maledicere noluit. Aequum igitur erat, & quidem longè magis aequum, falsos illos doctores â maledictis Magistratui ingerendis sibi temperare & expendere, quòd Magistratus sit sancta DEI ordinatio, non contumeliis & convitiis obruenda, sed propter DEUM honoranda. Collatio huius loci paralleli ostendit, primò Petrum non loqui de malis, sed de bonis Angelis. Secundò, non exaggerare poenam, sed culpam falsorum doctorum; Tertiò per iudicium blasphemum sive maledicum intelligere maledicta & convitia, hoc sensu. Falsi illi doctores non reformidant maiestates ac Dynastas conviciis & maledictis incessere, cùm nec ipsi Angeli sancti robore & potentiâ illis (falsis doctoribus) longè maiores non inferant sibi mutuò iudicium blasphemum, siquidem quando Angeli boni cum malis (cum quibus sunt eiusdem Naturae) disceptationem habent, non ingerunt illis verba maledica, nec adversus illos maledictis insurgant. Hieronymus in cap. 3. ad Tit. Merebatur Diabolus maledictum, sed per Arch Angeli os blasphemia exire non debuit. Oecumenius in 2. Petr. 2. Est â maiori argumentatio in hunc modum. Si Diabolus, qui dignior est, ut maledicatur. quia tamen gloriae cuiusdam particeps est, â Michaële Arch Angelo coram Domino id non est consecutus, illi sanè non sapiunt, qui ita temerè gloriam omnem maledictis prosequuntur, cum tamen multò post Angelorum dignitatem sint constituti. Opponitur huic expositioni, quod προσδιορισμὸς additus παρὰ Κυρίῳilli non conveniat. Resp. παρὰ Κυρίῳ hîc idem est, quod apud Dominum, ut vertit Erasmus, vel coram DEI iudicio.

Q. 4. Anφθορὰin v. 12. pro libidine usurpetur? Resp. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinianum locum hunc Apostolicum citat hisce verbis. Quasi irrationalia iumenta in ventrem & libidinem proni sunt. Inde quibusdam videtur, ἅλωσιν poni pro ingluvie ventris quem capta repleat praeda;φθορὰνpro libidine, quae crebrò dici solet corruptio, &γεγενυμέναpositum esse pro eo, quod est Naturae pronitatem habere. Sed haec Hieronymi citatio rectiùs pro applicatione, quam versione accipitur.

Q. 5. Quaenam sint illa, quae falsi Doctores ex ignorantia blasphemant? Quidam in specie accipiunt de δόξαις, quidam in genere de fidei Christianae mysteriis. Ex prioribus quidam exponunt de Angelis, quorum Naturam, ordines & officia cùm humanae mentis captum excedant, ac ea tantùm de illis nota sint, quae in Scripturis Deus revelare voluit, mirum non est, falsos doctores, ut pote limitibus in Scriptura positis non contentos blasphemare. Sed monuimus superius per δόξας rectiùs intelligi Magistratus, quorum officium divinitus institutum & humano generi salutare esse, cùm ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι illi vel non agnoscant, vel non satis exactè perpendant, inde est, quòd Magistratus ex ignorantia blasphement. Nihil verò obstat, quò minùs haec Apostolica κατηγορία in genere accipiatur de veritate doctrinae caelestis, ac de fidei Christianae mysteriis, quae falsi doctores confictis suis fabulis conspurcant, ac male dictis suis veritatem nondum satis agnitam blasphemant, quâ ratione aliud falsorum doctorum vitium ac nota in his verbis proponeretur.

Q. 6. Quae sit illa corruptio, in qua blasphemantes illi dicuntur corrumpendi? Resp. 1. Quidam accipiunt de corruptione vitae & morum, quod falsi illi doctores voluptatum ceno sese penitus immergentes per foedas & non naturales libidines Naturam humanam extremè dehonestent ac vitient, cùm ne bruta quidem nefandas eiusmodi Sodomias sectentur: in qua significatione voxφθορᾶς accipitur cap. 1. v. 4.ἀποφυγόντες τῆς ἐν κόσμῳ ἐν ἐπιθυμία φθορᾶς. & cap. 2. v. 19.libertatem promittunt, cum ipsi sint serviφθορᾶςcorruptionis. Sed quia collatio instituitur inter φθορὰν brutorum animalium & inter φθορὰν falsorum doctorum, ideò ut ἀπόδοσις προτάσει respondeat, per φθορὰς rectiùs intelligitur interitus spiritualis, sicut per φθορὰν brutorum denotatus erat interitus eorum corporalis, ut sit sensus, fore, ut falsi doctores ex morte peccatorum spirituali in mortem aeternam incidant.

Q. 7. An de eorum falsorum Doctorumφθορᾷloquantur Petrus hoc loco & Iudas in loco parallelo, Epist. v. 10. Resp. locus Iudae huic nostro parallelus sic habet. Hi verò (falsi doctores) quae quidem ignorant, blasphemant; quae verò naturaliter tanquam irrationalia animalia sciunt, in illis corrumpuntur. In priore membro respicit Iudas ad illud, quod dixerat v. 8. δόξας βλασφημοῦσιν, ut sit sensus. Michaël Arch Angelus Satanae conatibus resistens â convitiando abstinuit, nec fuit ei maledicere ausus: Sed haec Satanae organa, ea, quae non noverunt, maledictis incessunt, etiam ipsas maiestates, ab omnibus reverenter honorandas. In posteriore membro respicit Iudas ad illud, quod eodem versu dixerat, σάρκα μιαίνουσι, ut sit sensus. Quae naturaliter solis sensibus absque iudicio rationis, ac si essent bruta animalia cognoscunt, videlicet quae pertinent ad appetitum sensitivum, qualia sunt cibus, potus, somnus, Veneris usus, in iis per comessationem & nefarias libidines corrumpuntur, dignitatem Naturae suae per delicta contra Naturam dehonestantes ac infra brutorum fortem sese abiicientes. Ex his apparet, nomen φθορᾶς apud Iudam accipi de corruptione culpae, apud Petrum verò de corruptione poenae.

ἘναντιοφανείαCant. 4. v. 7.de Ecclesia dicitur, tota pulchra es & macula non est in te. Atqui de falsis doctoribus hoc loco dicitur v. 13. quòd sint maculae in Ecclesia.

Resp. 1. Distinguendum est inter societatem Ecclesiae externam sive Ecclesiam visibilem, cui admixti sunt hypocritae; atque inter societatem Ecclesiae internam sive Ecclesiam invisibilem, cuius vera & viva membra omnia sunt sancta & immaculata. 2. Distinguendum etiam inter maculas infirmitatum, quae in hac vita sanctis adhaerent, sed iustitiâ Christi per fidem imputatâ teguntur; & inter maculas malitiae sive peccatorum, contra conscientiam admissorum, quae â verè piis exulant.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Quia Papatus est haeresium antiquarum sentina, ut in loco de Ecclesia §. 230. fuit demonstratum, inde etiam vitia, quae hoc loco perstringit Apostolus, in Pontificibus Romanis & Clero Papali regnasse deprehenduntur. Primum est flagitium Sodomiticum, quod per εὐφημισμὸν in vers. 10. denotari ostendimus ex collatione loci paralleli. Iudae v. 6. Illud verò, ut de incestibus, adulteriis & stupris nihil dicamus, in Papatu regnare nemo inficias iverit. Hieronymus lib. 2. contra Iovinianum conqueritur, vigente haeresi Ioviniani iamdum suo tempore Romam Sodomitici sceleris spurcitiâ faedatam fuisse: Fuit hoc quasi praeludium quoddam statûs, tempore dominantis Papatus Romae futuri. Udalricus Episcopus Augustanus in Epist. ad Nicolaum 1. circa annum 860. scribit, Pontifices, Episcopos & Clericos Papales in libidinem ita agi praecipites, ut nec masculorum, nec pecudum turpissimos amplexus sciant abhorrere. Huius Epistolae etiam Aeneas Sylvius meminit. Sixtus IV. fuit Sodomita, & concessit illiud flagitium familiaribus Cardinalibus tribus aestivis mensibus Iunio, Iulio, & Augusto exercendum, uti ex M. Iohanne Wesselo tract. de Indulg. refert Wolff. tom. 11. Memorab. p. 836. Iulius 2. pueros duos, quos Galliae Regina cum Cardinali Gallo Romam misit informandos, in delitiis habuit & praeterea adolescentulum Germanum, inde Grebellii distichon.

Venit in Italiam spectabilis indole rarâGermanus, rediit de puero mulier.

De Leone X. Paulus Iovinus in ipsius vitap. 192. sic scribit. Non caruit Sodomiae infamiâ, quod parùm honestè nonnullos adamare & cum his teneriùs ac liberè iocari videretur. Sed demus aliquid humanitati Leonis, ut in summa licentia fervidae aetatis ac prosperae valetudinis aestum aegerrimè sustinenti: deinde alia sunt vitia Principis, alia hominis. Iulius 3. tanquam Iupiter Ganymidem quendam nomine Innocentium fovisse, ac Hieronymi Mutii, Sodomiam defendentis Apologiam pro tanto scelere adornatam adprobasse scribitur apud Schleidan. lib. 21. Hist. Vergerium, Balaeum Cent. 8. cap. 27. Append.

De Cardinalibus sic scribunt Cives Veneti in resp. ad paraenesin Baroniip. 46. Quod Ethnici quoque exhorrescunt, inter purpurae huius Candidatos extitêre, qui praeposterae libidinis sordes non modò in delitiis habuerunt, sed laudes etiam carminibus ornarent, quod in hac ipsa urbe â Ioh. Caso Archiepiscopo Beneventano Papae Legato factum. Carolus Molinaeus in orat. de Theolog. & Iurisprud. excellentia Tubingae habita. Nondum quinque anni, quod Iohannes della Casa Archiep. Beneventanui Papalis Camerae Decanus & in toto Venetorum dominio cum potestate Papali â latere Legatus, eâ legatione fungens Venetiis librum composuit & edidit de laudibus Sodomiae. In illo libro affirmat, execrandissimum illud Sodomiae scelus esse artem & opus divinum, seque non alia magis Venere delectari. Liber hic Venetiis praefixo autoris nomine per Troianum Naum publicum Chalcographum propalam excusus fuit & venditus. Praeter hunc Iohannem Casam, etiam Grappa & Anastasius Platus Sodomiam publicis scriptis commendarunt, referente Wolffio tom. 2. Memorabil. p. 421. Petrus Paulus Vergerius in Hist de idolo Lauretano inter caetera sic scribit: Fuit Paetrum nostrorum memoriâ Cardinalis quidam Venetus ê Pisana familia, qui inter reliquas suas interiores & reconditas literas duos libellos habuit sepositos, variis obscaenis picturis & detestandis nefariarum libidinum simulachris refertos. Extabant in eorum altero complures viri cum muliere concubitûs formae, omnis turpitudinis & foeditatis plenae, atque â Natura prorsus alienae. In altero execrabilis illius Veneris, quam, quia Sodomitis familiarem fuisse constat, Sodomiticam appellant, dissimiles summaque varietate distincti modi expressi videbantur. Post obitum Cardinalis excussâ librariâ supellectile, quam domi suae instructam habuerat, alter ê duobus illis libellis Venereis repertus, tempore Papae Iulii II. Romae typis in lucem evulgatus, denique Pontificatum gerente Adriano VI. publicè divenditus distractusque fuit. Anno 1538. in lucem prodiit Breviarium Compertorum in Monaesteriis, Conventïbus, Collegiis &c. ex Regestis Anglicis, in quo memoratur, in Visitatione Monasteriorum iussu Henrici IIX. Angliae Regis institutâ tantum paederastarum, pediconum, puerariorum, Sodomitarum, Ganymedum in Cenobiis cuculligerorum & Collegiis sacrificulorum inventam fuisse multitudinem, ut in unoquoque eorum credideris novam adesse Sodomam. Wolff. Tom. 2. Memorab. p. 424.

Alterum est scelus Onaniticum, mastuprium, mollities Apostolo dicta. 1. Cor. 6. v. 9. Scelus hoc in Papatu frequens esse, testari possunt, qui audiendis Confessionibus Sacrificulorum, Monachorum, Monialium praesunt, id quod coacti caelibatus legibus ferendum est acceptum. Carolstad. in praefat. libr. de caelibat. ac Monach. Ann. 21. editi. Utinam demissa vox in aurem tibi quaedam loqui posset, horreres certè illa, quae auditores & iudices peccatorum, quos Confessores vocant, â confitentibus didicerunt & me docuerunt, dedocenda magis quàm docenda. Opinantur, se non delinquere, cùm in cuniculis & cellis & solitudine haud scio, quid efficiant confricatione &c. De hoc abominando ac muto scelere, (quod & fornicatione & adulterio gravius esse, Thomas rectè pronunciat) plura non afferemus, hoc tantùm monebimus, ad ἐπιθυμίαν μιασμοῦ, quam Petrus h. l. in falsis illis doctoribus taxat, quàm proximè accedere, quod scribit Toletus lib. 5. Instruct. moral. cap. 13. Si quis desideret habere pollutionem ad levandas tentationes carnis, quibus affligitur, non est peccatum.

Tertium est contemtus Magistratûs. Illum in Papatu regnare, multis demonstrari potest. 1. Pontifex sibi arrogat supremam inter Imp. Reges & Principes potestatem, quâ eos ê solio deiicere possit, si placitis suis obsequi nolint. Imperator Romanus summus in terris Monarcha, pedes Rom. Pontif. osculari; sellam, in qua Pontifex vehitur, humeris suis portare, aquam manibus dare, stapedem tenere, equum manu deducere, adeoque stratoris officio fungi iubetur. Cerem. lib. 3. tit. 2. Gregorius VII. vitae Hernici III. Imp. insidias struxit, & quidem in loco sacro. Alexander III. Friderici 1. Barbarossae dicti collo pedem imposuit, acclamari interim â Clero sibiiubens. Super aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis. Paschalis 2. contra Henricum X. seditionem movit, ut devita & fortunis suis dimicare cogeretur. Vide librum Simonis Schardii de Paparum adversùs Impp. perfidia. 2. Clericos omnes potestati Magistratûs civilis eximunt, unde rebellionem Clerici adversùs Magistratum, negant esse laesae maiestatis crimen. Vel infimus quilibet in Ordine Clericali tonsurae, quam ita vocant, privilegio politici Magistratus imperium aspernatur. Inde Lutherus in lib. contra falsò dictum statum Spiritualium fol. iii. b. sic scribit. Pontifex iam olim ausus fuit Reges & Principes pedibus suus conculcare, de throno eos deiicene & excommunicare, iisdem maledicere in quartam, nonam &c. generationem, Episcopi & Ecclesiastici in Papatu sunt contemtores dominationis, & blasphematores Maiestatuum, nolunt ulli Magistratui subesse, nec ratione corporis, nec bonorum &c. 3.
