Docent, Magistratum esse talem vitae statum, in quo difficulter aliquis salvari possit, unde persvadent Magistratui, ut abdicato suo officio Monasterium ingrediatur. 4. Magistratum â cura religionis & Scripturae lectione arcent.

Quartum sunt convitia in Magistratum proiecta. Illorum plurima in Principes Augustanae Confessioni addictos non modio, vel trimodio, sed integro horreo effusa inveniuntur in maledicis scriptis Iohannis Nass, Christophori Ungersdorffii & aliorum. Baronius Principes illos, quires Ecclesiasticas attingunt, ubique maledictis incessit, ausus Reges veteres Francorum propterea comparare latronibus in sylvis, Ann. 855. Bellarminus in Iudicio de Formula Concordiae autoribus eius tribuit illustre mendacium, perstringens ipsos Electores & Principes Aug. Conf. addictos, sub quorum nomine Formula Concordiae in lucem prodiit.

Quintum est αὐθαδεία. Falsos doctores Petrus sic describit, quòd sintαὐθάδειςsibiipsis placentes. Id verò vel maximè competit Pontificibus Romanis, quippe qui sua placita ac decreta ita admirantur, ut non vereantur ea Scripturae sacrae exaequare, imò etiam anteferre, ut testatur decretum de communione sub una specie, de caelibatu Sacerdotum &c.

2. Sed & illam descriptionis falsorum doctorum partem, quae in v. 13. proponitur, in regno Papali abunde completam fuisse, Historia & αὐτοψία testantur. Quinam sunt quaeso, scribit Lutherus in lib. contra falsò dictum statum Spiritualium tom. 2. Ien. Germ. fol. 112. qui ex aliorum bonis luxuriosè vivunt? qui sufficere putant sibi omnis generis delitias suppetere? num textus indiget glossa? Nam primo in aulis Pontificis, Cardinalium, Episcoporum, ac Praelatorum luxum regnare, in vulgus notum est. Bernhardus serm. 33. in Cant. iam olim hac de re conquestus est. Ministri Christi sunt, inquit, & Antichristo serviunt, honorati incedunt de bonis Domini, cui Domino honorem non deferunt. Inde is, quem quotidiè vides, meretricius nitor, histrionicus habitus, regius apparatus: inde aurum in frenis, in sellis, calcaribus & plus calcaria, quàm altaria fulgent, inde splendidae mensae & cibis & scyphis, inde comessationes & ebrietates, inde cytharae & lyra & tibia, inde redundantia torcularia, & promtuaria plena, ex hoc in aliud eructantia &c. Pro huiusmodi volunt esse, & sunt Ecclesiarum Praepositi, Decani, Archidiaconi, Episcopi, Archiepiscopi. Ecbertus Coloniensis Episcopus olim dicebat, Episcopari nihil esse aliud, quàm carni indulgere, pompaticè incedere, quaestui intendere & delitiosè otiari. Nicolaus de Clemangis in lib. de corrupto Ecclesiae statu pag. 22. Si quis hodiè desidiosus est, si quis â labore abhorrens, si quis in otio luxuriari volens, ad Sacerdotium convolat, quo accepto statim se caeteris Sacerdotibus voluptatum amatoribus adiungit, qui magis secundùm Epicurum, quàm secundùm CHRISTUM viventes & cauponulas seduli frequentantes, potando, comessando, pransitando, convivando, cum tesseris & pila ludendo, tempora tota consumunt. Platina in vita Gregorii. IV. In omnem luxum & libidinem sese effudit Ecclesiasticus Ordo. Coccinatos & trabeatos nunc inspiceres, non homines, quod leve fortasse videretur, sed equos & iumenta, praecedente, dum incedunt, magno adolescentum & altero Presbyterorum ordine subsequente: non in asinis, ut CHRISTUS nostri dogmatis autor & benè vivendi unicum in terris exemplar, sed in equis praeferocibus & phaleratis, ac siex hoste devicto triumphum ducerent. De argenteis vasis & egregiâ eorum supellectile, deque cibariis non attinet dicere, cùm & Siciliae dapes & Attalica ornamenta, & vasa Corinthia, si haec inspicias, nussius precii dici possint. Iohannes Huss. in comm. h. l. Luxuria & gula animam & corpus hominis coinquinant, & proh dolor in his duobus peccatis quasi prae aliis affluens mergitur noster Clerus. Cornelius Agrippa de vanitate scient. cap. 61. scribit, Pontificis Romani pompam & fastum nullum unquam Tyrannorum aequavisse. Salmero tom. 9. tract. 9. p. 57. Modò in pluribus Sacerdotibus & Religiosis, qui de patrimonio crucifixi vivunt, illud Propheticum impletur. Saturavi eos & moechati sunt, & in domo meretricis luxuriabantur.Ierem. 5. Cives Veneti in Resp. ad Paraen. Baroniip. 45. Si qui inter purpuratos istos Satrapas (Cardinales) mitiore sunt ingenio, inito hoc honore hoc solùm sibi negotii datum credunt, ut Ethnicorum epulonum luxum ex orco revocent.

Secundo. nec â Monachis paupertatem & castitatem professis luxus abest, unde iam olim de Monasteriis Fridericus Imp. dixit, Vise Monasterium, si vis cognoscere luxum. Bernhardus in Epist. ad Guilielm. Abbat. Fercula ferculis apponuntur, & pro solis carnibus, â quibus abstinetur, grandia piscium corpora duplicantur. Giraldus Cambrensis in speculo lib. 2. cap. 3. memorat, Monachos Vintonienses graviter fuisse conquestos, quòd ex tredecim ferculis, quae singulis prandiis & cenis apponebantur, tria illis demta essent, & addit. Monachos vix sedecim ferculis fuisse contentos: Erasmus in Methodo Theol. p. 139. Ipsis mundi visceribus immixti Monachos se vocant, & Regium luxum assectantes mendicitatem praetexunt. Unde verò habent, ex quo eiusmodi comessationes & luxuriosa convivia instituunt? ex eleemosynis profectò, ex iis, quae pii ac devoti homines ad sustentationem Ministerii & pauperum de bonis suis Deo consecrarunt. Lutherus in marg. ad h. l. sic annotat. Eleemosyna sunt Canonicatus & praebendae, quas otiosi absumunt, & insuper fundatoribus illudunt.

Tertio, de fraudibus Papalibus si velimus dicere, dies nos citiùs quàm oratio deficeret. Indulgentias iam olim plurimi dixerunt esse pias fraudes. Caesar Borgia Alexandri VI. Spurius, cùm aliquot millia in lusu aleae perdidisset, ex Iubilaeo & Indulgentiis Papalibus collecta, salsè dixit: Quid aliud amisimus, quàm peccata Germanorum? Doctrina de purgatorio, de valore Missarum pro defunctis, de operibus supererogationis, interventu pecuniae aliis communicandis, de donariis votivis & alia dogmata culinaria ex fraudibus & mendaciis sunt composita. Quot fraudes in miraculis ad decipiendos simpliciores sunt adhibitae. Exempla quaedam recensuimus in loco de Eccles. §. 284. Confer Selneccerum part. 4. Exam. pag. 537. Quot Pontifices fraudulenti & periuri fuêre. De Alexandro VI. sic scribit Machiavellus lib. de Principe cap. 18. Nihil aliud, quàm mortalium impostorem egit, ad nihil aliud, quàm ad malitiam & fraudem, (quò hominum genus falleret) mentem suam exercuit. In asseverando autem qui magis fuerit efficax, aut qui speciosius iuraverit iuramentum, & vicissim qui minùs praestiterit, nemo unquam fuit.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Vulgata versio plurimùm discedens â fontibus illud δόξας οὐ τρεμοῦσι βλασφημοῦντες sic reddidit. Sectas non metuunt introducere blasphemantes, quâ ratione perstringeretur effrenata & superba falsorum istorum doctorum audacia, quòd non vereantur nova & erronea dogmata spargere, atque hac ratione sectas introducere. Hanc versionem, utpote in Concilio Tridentino pronunciatam authenticam, etiam hoc in loco Pontificii Interpp. quibus possunt modis, tuentur. Lorinus ad l. h. sic annotat, Nomenδόξηςsignificare Sectam sive opinionem, nullus negat &c. Pius enarrator studebit pro virili autoritatem Interpretis tueri. Oecumenii non me movet autoritas, cui praeferre potiùs Interpretem debeo, approbatum ab Ecclesia. Cornel. â Lapide ad h. l. Noster (Interpres) meliùs, subaudiensἐπάγειν,vertit, Sectas non metisunt introducere, hoc enim est proprium haereticorum, & Graecumδόξαopiniones & sectas significat.

Atqui. 1. In Codd. Graecis, qui soli sunt authentici, nihil de sectarum introductione hoc loco habetur. Absurdus est Lorinus quando ad h. l. sic annotat. In pari causa Latinos magis quàm Graecos Latinus debeo complecti. Hoc verò est rivulos & quidem turbidos praeferte fontibus. Codices Graeci sunt fontes, Latini Interpretes & enarratores sunt rivuli. 2. Petrus iam antè dixerat in v. 1. quod falsi illi doctores introducturi sint Sectas exitiales, ex quo versiculo illud huc videtur translatum. 3. Quidam etiam Latini Codd. Manuscripti, ut memorat Erasmus, non habent verbum introducent. 4. Quamvis δόξα non solùm gloriam, sed etiam opinionem significet, pro Secta tamen nuspiam usurpatur. 5. Ac ne quidem vulgatus Interpres Sectas illud alibi exponit. 6. vers. seqq. 11. ostendit, haec verba accipienda esse de blasphemia contra eos, qui maiestate praediti sunt.

2. Salmero h. l. detonat in Lutherum, quòd sacratam DEO Monacham in matrimonium sibi copulaverit, quòdque permiserit viris, ut cùm languent uxores, in servas velancillas irruant. Sed quid de his ἐγκλήμασι iudicandum sit, in tract. de Coniugio fuit expositum.

3. Cornelius â Lapide adducit quaedam Lutheri dicta contra Magistratum, utpote, quòdrara avis sit prudens Princeps, adhuc multò rarior Princeps bonus; quòd Turca sit decies prudentior & probior Principibus nostris, quòd Scriptura eos vocet bestias. Lorinus hoc odiosè perstringit, quòd Principes imò Reges appellaverit capitis sui lentes. Resp. 1. aliud est vitia Magistratuum taxare; aliud ipsum officium Magistratus & ordinem â DEO institutum improbare. 2. Lutherus non simpliciter & absolutè Magistratûs autoritatem elevat, sed si DEO & verbo eius se opponere velint.

4. Idem Cornelius â Lapide αὐθαδείας & audaciae crimen hoc nomine Luthero tribuit, quòd in lib. contra Regem Angliae scripserit, Hîc sto, hîc maneo, hîc glorior, hîc insulto Papistis, Henricistis, Sophistis, omnibus portis inferi. Divina maiestas mecum facit, ut nihil curem, si mille Augustini, mille Cypriani, mille Henricianae Ecclesiae contra me starent, dogmata mea stabunt & Papa cum Henricistis cadet. Resp. haec non est carnalis αὐθάδεια, sed spiritualis πληροφορία, ac immota animi verbo DEI unicè innitentis fiducia. Nec loquitur Lutherus de sua persona, sed de sua doctrina.

5. Idem Cornelius etiam hoc nomine Luthero αὐθαδείας crimen affricat, quod dixerit.

Sic volo, sic iubeo, sit pro ratione voluntas.Item. Pestis eram vivus, moriens ero mors tua Papa.

At mortuus est Lutherus, inquit Cornelius. sed vivit vigetque Papa & Papatus. Resp. prius ἔγκλημα eliciunt ex Epistola Apologetica pro versione loci Rom. 3. scripta, sed in eandem Lutherus adversùs omnes Sycophantarum morsus sese satis tuetur, pertinacibus enim & insanabilibus hoc duntaxat opponit, qui nullas rationes admittere vel audire cupiunt. Posterius non agit de plenario Papatûs exterminio, quod in die novissimi iudicii demum secuturum, Lutherus ex 2. Thess. 2. vers. 8. passim docet, sed de insigni regni Papalis inclinatione.

6. Calviniani ex eo, quòd falsi doctores conferuntur cum brutis ad capturam & perniciem natis, colligunt, quosdam absoluto reprobationis decreto adinteritum & perditionem esse destinatos.

Resp. 1. Dispar est ratio interitus brutorum corporalis, & interitus impiorum spiritualis & aeterni. Ille pendet ab absoluta DEI voluntate, quâ animalia bruta in eum usum creavit, ut capiantur & mactentur; hic verò cùm concernat homines in Adamo ad imaginem DEI conditos, & post lapsum per Christum redemtos, ideò non potest absolutae DEI voluntati tribui. 2. Comparatio ergo consistit in destinatione ad interitum, sed non est extendenda ad destinationis modum, qui utrobique non est idem, sed longè diversus.

7. Cornelius â Lapide vers. 12. sic annotat. Lutherum, cùm vespere lautè cenasset, noctu desperatione & furiis Daemonis actum sibi iniecto laqueo necem intulisse, asservit eius famulus, postea ad orthodoxam fidem conversus, utirefert Thomas Bozius de signis Ecclesiae, tom. 2. lib. 23. cap. 3.

Resp. 1. Ne ipse quidem Cochlaeus mendacissimus αὐτοχειρίαν Luthero tribuit. Bellarminus lib. 4. de Eccles. cap. 17. §. Lutherus &c. ex Cochlaeo de vita Lutheri haec adducit. Lutherus morte repentinâ sublatus est. Nam cùm vesperi opiparam cenam sumsisset laetus & sanus, & facetiis suis omnes ad risum provocasset, eadem nocte mortuus est. 2. Nec amico laudanti, nec inimico detrahenti credendum. Ergo nec Cochlaeo, nec Bozio, nec Bellarmino, nec Cornelio â Lapide iuratis Lutheri hostibus. 3. Quis fuerit ille Lutheri famulus, ad cuius testimonium Bozius provocat, ne verbulo quidem indicat, nec indicare etiam potuit. Figmenta haec sunt otiosorum, imò maledicorum hominum. 4. Extat Historia de morte Lutheri, â viris fide dignis, qui ipsimet praesentes ei fuêre, conscripta, videlicet à Iusto Iona, Michaele Caelio, Iohanne Aurifabro Vinariensi, qui coram DEO & in conspectu Christi testantur, quòd sanctâ fide & bonâ conscientiâ Historiam obitùs referant, quae habetur Tom. 8. Ien. Germ. Summam illorum omnium memorat Schleidanus lib. 16. Comment. pag. 488. ubi etiam recenset Orationem, paulò ante vitae finem ad DEUM ablegatam, quam ipse quoque Surius in Comm. rerum ab orbe gestarum pag. 474. edit. Ann. 66. recitat. 5. Iacob. Augustus Thuanus lib. 2. Hist. pag. 30. Lutheri obitum describit, sed de αὐτοχειρία nihil meminit. Confer. tract. de Ecclesia §. 297.

8. Lorinus. ibid. perstringit Lutherum, quòd fassus sit ignorantiam Hebraeae Graecaeque linguae, in Colloq. tom. 1. f. 187. quod Hieronymum vocaverit Presbyterum Lugdunensem; Irenaeum Stridonensem; quod scripserit illum anno vixisse 414. istum 422, Lyranum 320. tom. 2. Colloq. fol. 138. quod asserverit, nomen liberi arbitrii Patribus omnibus odiosissimum fuisse tom. 1. fol. 42. nec Hieronymum, nec Ambrosium de Purgatorio quidquam sensisse f. 65. originalis peccati usque Augustinum nullam mentionem factam fol. 98. 99. Hieronymum nihil de Christo tractare, de fide, spe, caritate, fidei operibus non loqui fol. 137.

Resp. 1: liber Convivalium sermonum â Luthero nec editus fuit, nec approbatus 2. Lutherus part. 2. Postill. domest. Domin. Iubilate fol. 34. b. In S. Augustini Büchern findet man diel Sprüche die Fleisch und Blut geredt haben / und ich muss auch von mir bekennen / daß ich viel Wort rede / welche nicht Gottes Wort sind / wenn ich rede ausserhalb dem Predigampt / daheim über Tisch oder sonst. 3. Versio Scripturae in linguam vernaculam ostendit, Lutherum & Hebraeae & Graecae linguae non mediocriter gnarum fuisse. 4. Ignorantiam inter Sacrificulos & Monachos Lorinus quaerat, inter quos Fratres Ignorantiae peculiarem constituunt ordinem, sed qui per reliquos ordines omnes vagatur. Cavisti benè tu, ne te ulla occidere possit Litera, nam nota est litera nulla tibi, ut in Monachum indoctum iocatur Buchananus. 5. Qualem Convivalium sermonum editionem Lorinus fuerit se cutus, scire non possumus. In nostra editione Islebiensi Ann. 66. cap. 58. fol. 529. haec habentur. Hieronymus Presbyter & senior Stridonensis vixit anno 422. Irenaeus Episcopus Lugdunensis Ann. 175. Additur quidem, quod Lyranus vixerit anno 320. Sed hîc vel est erratum μνημονευτικὸν in Aurifabro libri huius Collectore; vel σφάλμα Typographicum. Lutherus enim probè noverat, Lyranum, quem haud in diligenter legerat, non esse antiquiorem Augustino. Ad reliqua ἐγκλήματα alibi respondetur.

9. Salmero in comm. v. 13. statuit. Petrum hoc loco abusum esse mercedis vocabulo, quando mercedem iniustitiae vocat, cùm merces propriè sit iustitiae sive operis boni. Lot in us eodem modo. Catachresticè merces depoena dicitur. Resp. Scriptura discrimen hoc inter mercedem boni & poenam mali operis non observat. Act. 1. v. 18. vocatur μισθός ἀδικίας.Rom. 1. v. 27.ἀντιμισθία πλάνης.2. Petr. 2. v. 15.μισθός ἀδικίας. Iudae vers. 11. Βαλαάμ μισθοῦ &c.

## 2:14
Connection. He repeats and exaggerates the life and marks of the false teachers through a certain accumulation, namely their lusts, frauds, and avarice.

Exposition of the text. ὀφθαλμούς ἔχοντες μεστούς μοιχαλίδος The Vulgate rendered it, Having eyes full of adultery. In Cyprian or any other author in the book on the singularity of clerics it is rendered thus: Having eyes full of adulteries. In the Greek it is properly, having eyes full of an adulteress. The Syriac: Since there are to them eyes full of adultery. Luther in the same way. Sie haben Augen voll Ehebruchs.

Καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας. The Vulgate rendered it, and of unceasing sin, so that it may be referred to the preceding adjective full. Cyprian in the same place in almost the same way with unceasing sins. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian with insatiable lust. In Greek it is the accusative, which is referred to the preceding substantive ὀφθαλμούς in this sense. They have eyes that know not how to cease from sinning, restless from sin, that is, they do not desist from sin; as soon as they look upon a woman, they burn with flames of lust toward her, they cannot be satisfied by the sight of those things which provoke to lust. In certain Latin codices the accusative unceasing is held, which reading corresponds to the Greek text. The Syrian seems to have read not in the accusative ἀκαταπαὺστους but in the genitive ἀκαταπαύσου, for thus he rendered this passage. Since their eyes are full of adultery and sins, which do not cease. Luther Sie lassen ihnen die Sünde nicht wehren.

Δελεάζοντες ψυχάς ἀστηρικτούς The Vulgate enticing unstable souls. From the Latin version it cannot be known whether this refers to the eyes or to the false teachers, but from the Greek text it is manifest that it refers to the false teachers, which the following things also prove. Cyprian in the same place rendered it, capturing weak souls, δελεάζειν properly is to bait, to lie in wait by baiting, just as a fowler sets bait for birds, or a fisherman for fish, by which they are enticed into nets and a fish-trap. Athenaeus book 7 concerning a certain fish; οὖ δελεάζεται οὐτε σαρκὶ, οὔτε ἄλλῳ τινι ἐμψύχω. James chap. 1. v. 14. uses this word concerning depraved concupiscence enticing a man to sin. The Syrian has the word [שדל] to persuade with adulterous words, to entice. Luther most correctly. Sie locken an sich.

By souls ἀστηρίουτους are understood men not yet sufficiently founded and strengthened in faith and the study of piety, wavering and not yet sufficiently confirmed. Jerome in the same place rendered it, they deceive souls not yet robust in the charity of Christ. The Syrian [דלא סמיכן] not confirmed and founded. Luther Die leichtfertigen Seelen. The Apostle uses the same word in chap. 3. v. 16.

Καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίαις ἔχοντες. Vulg. having a heart exercised with covetousness. Some Greek codices read πλεονεξίας in the genitive singular. But the more approved and more numerous codices read πλεονεξίαις, in the dative plural, so that the sense is that they have a heart exercised with covetousnesses, where exercise denotes a mind uniquely intent upon gains, long accustomed to capturing gains, and thus an inveterate zeal and skill in capturing gains joined with fraud. The Syriac has the noun [עלובותא] which signifies iniquity, avarice, defrauding from the root [עבל] he treated with injury, he defrauded through injury, just as also πλεονεξία does not signify a bare desire of having more, but such a one by which someone seizes the things of others through force and frauds, whence Erasmus in this place rendered it by rapines. But the Apostle uses the plural number for this reason, to show that those seducers do not labor under one disease of avarice, nor are they skilled in only one art of heaping up riches through right and wrong, and of milking the simpler sort of their money. Therefore this passage agrees with that which he had said in v. 3, with covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you. For it is for this reason that false teachers bait others with their flatteries and draw them to themselves, so that they may procure their own advantages from them, and have that from which they may live luxuriously. Κατάρας τέκνα cursed children, that is, men cursed, worthy of the execration of all, by a customary Hebraism. The Royal Psalmist best explains the emphasis of this phrase Psal. 109 v. 17. and following. These are they who love cursing and it shall come unto them; and they love not blessing and it shall be far from them, and they clothe themselves with cursing like as with a garment, and it came into their inward parts like water, and like oil into their bones, and it shall be unto them as the garment which covereth them, and for a girdle wherewith they are girded continually.

Latin:

Connexio. Falsorum doctorum vita & notas per congeriem quandam repetit atque exaggerat, ipsorum sc. libidines, fraudet & avaritiam.

Textus expositio. ὀφθαλμούς ἔχοντες μεστούς μοιχαλίδος Vulg. reddidit, Oculos habentes plenos adulterii. Apud Cyprianum vel quemcunque alium autorem in lib. de singul. Clericorum sic redditur. Oculos habentes plenos moechationibus. In Graeco propriè est, oculos habentes plenos adulterae. Syrus. Cùm sint illis oculi pleni adulterio. Lutherus eodem modo. Sie haben Augen voll Ehebruchs.

Καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας. Vulg. reddidit, & incessabilis delicti, ut referatur ad praecedens adiectivum plenos. Cyprianus d. l. eodem fere modo incessabilibus delictis. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovin. insatiabili libidine. In Graeco est accusativus, qui refertur ad praecedens fubstantivum ὀφθαλμούς hoc sensu. Habent oculos â peccando cessare nescios, irrequietos â peccato h. e. non desistunt â peccato, quamprimùm feminam intuentur, flammis libidinis erga eam exardescunt, non possunt satiari intuitu eorum, quae ad libidinem provocant. In quibusdam Codd. Latinis habetur accusativus incessabiles, quae lectio textui Graeco respondet. Syrus non in accusativo ἀκαταπαὺστους sed in genitivo ἀκαταπαύσου legisse videtur, sic enim hunc locum reddidit. Cùm oculi sint illis pleni adulterio & peccatis, quae non cessant. Luth. Sie lassen ihnen die Sünde nicht wehren.

Δελεάζοντες ψυχάς ἀστηρικτούς Vulg. pellicientes animas instabiles. Ex Latina versione non potest sciri, an ad oculos, an ad falsos doctores hoc referatur, sed ex Graeco textu manifestum est, ad falsos doctores illud referri, quod ipsum etiam probant sequentia. Cyprian. d. l. reddidit, capientes animas infirmas,δελεάζειν propriè est inescare, inescando insidiari, sicut auceps avibus, vel piscator piscibus escam proponit, quâ in retia ac nassam illiciuntur. Athen. lib. 7. de quodam pisce; οὖ δελεάζεται οὐτε σαρκὶ, οὔτε ἄλλῳ τινι ἐμψύχω.Iacobus cap. 1. v. 14. utitur hoc verbo de prava concupiscentia hominem ad peccatum illiciente. Syrus habet verbum [שדל]verbis adulteratoriis persvadere, allicere. Lutherus rectissimè. Sie locken an sich.

Per animas ἀστηρίουτους intelliguntur homines in fide & pietatis studio nondum satis fundati ac firmati, nutantes & nondum satis confirmati. Hieronymus d. l. reddidit, decipiunt animas necdum Christi caritate robustas. Syrus [דלא סמיכן]non confirmatas & fundatas. Luth. Die leichtfertigen Seelen. Eadem voce utitur Apostolus in cap. 3. v. 16.

Καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίαις ἔχοντες. Vulg. cor exercitatum avaritiâ habentes. Quidam Codd. Graeci legunt πλεονεξίας ingenitivo singulari. Sed probatiores & plures Codd. legunt πλεονεξίαις, in dativo plurali, ut sit sensus, quod habeant cor exercitatum avaritiis, ubi exercitatio denotat animum ad lucra unicè intentum, lucris captandis diu assvetum, adeoque inveteratum studium & peritiam captandi lucra cum fraude coniunctam. Syrus habet nomen [עלובותא] quod significat, iniquitatem, avaritiam, defraudationem â rad. [עבל]iniuriâ affecit, per iniuriam defraudavit, sicut etiam πλεονεξία non significat nudam habendi plura cupiditatem, sed talem, quâ quis aliena per vim ac fraudes rapit, unde Erasmus h. l. reddidit per rapinas. Ideò verò Apostolus utitur numero plurali, ut ostendat, seductores illos non uno avaritiae morbo laborare, nec unam duntaxat artem callere divitias perfas, nefasque congerendi, ac simpliciores pecuniâ emungendi. Congruit ergo hic locus cum eo, quod dixerat v. 3. in avaritia fictis verbis de vobis negotiabantur. Ideo enim falsi doctores blanditiis suis alios inescant & ad se pertrahunt, ut sua ex illis parent commoda, & habeant, ex quo luxuriari possint. Κατάρας τέκναfilii maledictionis, h. e. homines maledicti, omnium execratione digni, per usitatum Hebraismum. Emphasin huius phraseos optimè exponit Psaltes Regius Psal. 109 v. 17. & seqq. Hi sunt, qui diligunt maledictionem & veniet eis; & nolunt benedictionem & elongabitur ab eis, & induunt maledictionem sicut vestimentum, & intravit sicut aqua in interiora eorum, & sicut oleum in ossibus eorum, & fiet eis sicut vestimentum, quo operiuntur, & Zona, quâ semper praestringuntur.

## 2:14-16 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. In what sense are the eyes of false teachers said to be μεστοί μοιχαλίδος full of an adulteress? Resp. 1. Certain ones join the noun μοιχαλίδος with the following noun ἁμαρτίας and by an interposed word ἀκαταπαύσους read ἀκαταπαύσου, in this sense, having degenerate eyes, and full of perpetual sin. But the Greek copies consistently read ἀκαταπαύσους ἁμαρτίας not ceasing from sin. But it is an unusual epithet in the Scriptures for μοιχαλίδος to be added to sin. 2. It is customary for the Hebrews for the concrete to be placed for the abstract. Thus Deut. 29. v. 19. drunken is placed for drunkenness, thirsty for thirst. Dan. 9. v. 29. נביא for נבואה Eph. 6. v. 12. πνευματικὰ πονηρίας are πνεύματα πονηρὰ. Thus therefore the noun adulteress is also placed in this place for adultery or the lust of committing adultery. 3. It could also not inconveniently be said that the Apostle wishes this, that these lustful men carry an adulteress in their very eyes, and look at nothing else but adulteresses for the sake of fulfilling their lust, who always have an adulteress before their eyes, nor do they cast their eyes elsewhere, than to look at an adulteress.

Cyprian, or whoever else the author is in the book on the simplicity of Prelates, beautifully expressed the emphasis of the phrase. They are utterly insane, they burn with desire for women, as many as do not yield to this prohibition: and gaping at obscenities they prefer to die, rather than be content to be torn away from the sides of women by any separation, so that to satisfy the gluttony of their greed they are not even for a point of time without the pleasure of a woman, and they have this fruit in women, that with their intention always fixed upon them they may satisfy the desires of their eyes, so that not even any moment passes when they are in need of what they crave. Thus integrity dies among them, where every dwelling together, whether by winking or by living together, is defiled by corrupt affections, whom Saint Peter designated, saying, Having eyes full of adultery. Oecumenius on this place: Moreover, while they feast with you, they do not do it out of charity, but so that they may find an opportunity to deceive women. For these, when they have eyes, look at nothing else but adulteresses, etc.

Q. 2. Why does the Apostle in describing the lust of adultery make mention specifically of the eyes? The answer is made for a twofold reason. First, through the eyes, as if through windows, that which excites and inflames lust enters. The Hebrews say: The eyes and the heart are the procurers of love. That saying of the Greeks is known: οὐκ τοῦ ὁρᾶν γίγνεται τὸ ἐρᾶν. As I saw, as I perished, as an evil error carried me away, says he in Maro: The eyes are leaders in love, in Propertius, book 2, Elegy 5. To this is adapted by some of the ancients that Prophetic saying: Jer. 9. v. 21. Death has entered through our windows. More correctly the following sayings are referred here: Job 31. v. 1. I made a covenant with my eyes, and what did I consider in a virgin? Ps. 119. v. 37. David, with his soul gravely wounded through his eyes, asked of GOD that he might turn them away, lest they see vanity. Prov. 6. v. 26. it is said of an adulteress, beware lest she catch you with her eyelids. Lam. 3. v. 51. My eye has plundered my soul, on which place Jerome comments thus: Through the eye of the body he brought about the plunder of the heart. Matt. 5. verse 28. He who looks at a woman to lust after her (that is, in such a way that he lusts after her, for the end of the looking is not signified, but the manner or result of the looking) has already committed adultery with her in his heart. On which place Salvian comments elegantly thus in book 3 on providence: From this we can clearly understand how chaste the Savior has commanded us to be, who even cut off the license of vision. For knowing that the light of the eyes is in a way the windows of our minds, and all wicked That desires enter into the heart through the eyes, as if through natural tunnels, he wished to extinguish them completely from the outside, lest they arise within and, with lethally growing fibers, perhaps grow strong in the soul if they had sprouted in the sight. Ambrose, book on Joseph, chapter 3. The first weapons of an adulteress are those of the eyes, the second of words, but he who is not captured by the eyes can resist the words. Jerome, on chapter 3 of Lamentations. Once the appearance of beauty is bound to the heart through the eyes, it is scarcely loosened by the hand of a great struggle. For in order that a clean mind may be preserved in thought, the eyes must be suppressed from the lasciviousness of their pleasure, as if they were certain robbers of guilt. Secondly, because the signs of lust shine forth most especially in the eyes. Basil, on true virginity. The eyes are the matchmakers of him whose touch is the minister. Augustine, in the Rule for Monks. Do not say that you have chaste minds if you have unchaste eyes, because an unchaste eye is the messenger of an unchaste heart. Concerning the wife of Potiphar Gen. 39. v. 7. it is said, that she cast her unchaste eyes upon Joseph, with which, as if with certain poisoned weapons, she had attempted to entice him into love for her and to inflame his heart. Ezech. 6. v. 9. mention is made of eyes committing fornication. It is indeed treated there of spiritual fornication, meanwhile the comparison is taken from bodily fornication. Sirac. 26. v. 12. The fornication of a woman shall be known in the haughtiness of her eyes and in her eyelids. Zaleucus, the legislator of the Locrians, sanctioned by law that the eyes of adulterers should be plucked out, as if they were the first adulterers in man, as Aelian reports in book 13 of Various History, chapter 24. Bernard joins both causes when he says in his book on the degrees of humility, that the eyes are the occasion of sin, the indication of committed guilt, and the cause of guilt to be committed.

Q. 3. Whether by πλεονεξίας insatiable desires of base pleasures in this place are they understood? Some establish it thus, bringing forward to prove that the Apostolic passage Eph. 4. v. 19. where the Apostle says concerning the Gentiles, they have delivered themselves up to τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσις ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ. Oecumenius approves this exposition from the words immediately preceding, having eyes full of adultery. But πλεονεξία is more correctly understood concerning the desire for riches, as is evident, both from the words immediately preceding, enticing unstable souls; and from the subject example of Balaam, and from the perpetual usage of Scripture, in which πλεονεξία is always taken for avarice, and for the defrauding of one's neighbor taking its origin from it, whence Oecumenius also joins this exposition to the former. The passage from Eph. 4. v. 19.

what is adduced does not prove the contrary, because the Apostle attributes both vices to the Gentiles, both impure lusts and avarice, so that ἐν is taken for with, as in this very Epistle cap. 1. v. 5.

Q. 4. Of what kind of seduction of unstable souls does the Apostle speak? Resp. 1. Some think that the Apostle is speaking either solely or chiefly of seduction through carnal pleasures, to which they accommodate that saying of Plato, that pleasure is the bait of evils, by which men are caught, as fish by a hook. 2. Some on the contrary maintain that the discourse here is chiefly of seduction through false doctrine. For first, those false teachers are called δελεάζειν τὰς ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους.. But who those ἀστήρικτοι, are, can be gathered from the following chapter 3. vers. 16. where ἀμαθεῖς καὶ ἀστήρικτοι are said to στρεβλεῖν the sacred Scriptures, from which it is manifest that by ἀστηρίκτους are understood those who are not sufficiently firm and grounded in the faith and knowledge of the truth. Secondly, the seduction through carnal pleasures is treated finally v. 18. seqq. δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκός ἐν ἀσελγείαις. Thirdly, ἀστηρίκτοις are opposed to these στερεοὶ ἐν πίστει firm and strong in the faith. 1. Petr. 5. v. 9. 3. But these expositions are not opposed, but subordinated, because those who embrace the doctrine of these false teachers are carried with the whole impulse of their mind toward carnal pleasures by their example; and conversely, those who follow the pleasures of the flesh, they allow themselves more easily to be persuaded to embrace the false doctrine of those Pseudo-Prophets.

Q. 5. Why are they called children of cursing? Resp. The name children according to Hebraism is used in various ways, some of which can be accommodated here. 1. They are called children who study and are vigilant about some thing. 2. Reg. 4. v. 38. If therefore by the curse μετωνυμιχῶς is understood cursed doctrine, children of cursing will be called those addicted to cursed Nature. 2. Just as children of strength are called robust men Deut. 3. v. 18. children of iniquity iniquitous and impious men Deut. 13. v. 13. children of the covenant those who are in the covenant Act. 3. v. 25. children of unbelief unbelieving men Col. 3. v. 6. children of obedience obedient men 1. Petr. 1. v. 14. Thus children of cursing are cursed men. 3. Just as children of death are called those who are worthy of death 1. Sam. 20. v. 21. 2. Sam. 12. v. 5. children of striking, worthy to be struck, Deut. 25. v. 2. Thus children of cursing are worthy of a curse, to which pertains the rule of the Hebraists. The words בן and υἱὸς joined to a genitive of virtue or vice denote those addicted to them; joined to a genitive of reward or punishment, they denote those worthy of them. 4. Just as children of wrath are those whom the wrath of GOD awaits Ephes. 2. v. 2. children of damnation, those whom damnation remains: Thus they are children of the curse, whom there awaits not only a temporal, but also an eternal curse, to be pronounced against them at some time on the day of judgment. Matt. 25. v. 41.

Q. 6. In what sense are false teachers said to follow the way of Balaam? Resp. 1. By reason of false doctrine; because as Balaam was disobedient to the mouth of the Lord, and went against His word to Balak, King of the Moabites: so false teachers desert the way of truth prescribed in the word of the Lord: 2. By reason of an impious life. Just as Balaam, out of a desire for his own advantage and for retaining royal favor, gave counsel to Balak that the daughters of the Moabite people should entice the Israelites into love for them, and at the same time also into idolatry: so false teachers are authors to others for following the license of the flesh and lusts. 3. By reason of avarice, because false teachers, just as Balaam, depart from the straight way of truth for the sake of returns, prebends, and dignities.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Balaam's ass is called ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον. v. 16. and yet it is immediately said to have spoken with a human voice. Resp. the former regards the Nature of this animal, but the latter the supernatural miracle performed in it; because it was brought about by divine power that an animal destitute of the faculty of speech by Nature should utter a voice similar to a human one. Dionysius the Carthusian, Lorinus, Estius, etc., think that by the ministry of an Angel this voice was formed in the mouth of the ass by GOD. But because Moses notably says, Jehovah opened the mouth of the ass Num. 22. vers. 28. therefore this miracle is to be attributed immediately to divine power.

2. The dumb beast of burden is said to have rebuked the transgression of Balaam, and to have restrained his folly. But in the words of the ass there does not occur an open reproof of that crime. For thus they have Num. 22. vers. 28. What have I done to you, that you have now struck me three times? v. 30. Am I not your ass upon which you have ridden from your previous time until this day? have I ever been accustomed to do so to you? Resp. 1. Ἔλεγξιν Peter does not expressly attribute it to the ass, but says absolutely that Balaam had a reproof of his transgression, which can and ought to be understood of the Angel of the Lord, who spoke with Balaam afterwards. 2. From that unusual and stupendous miracle of the speaking ass, Balaam could and ought to have understood that his way was perverse, and his folly rebuked by a brute animal. 3. Because God spoke to Balaam through the ass and through the Angel, and because the speech was as if opened by the Angel through the speech of the donkey, therefore Peter, joining all those things together, says that the foolishness of Balaam was restrained by the donkey.

3. Balaam knew that he was sitting upon a brute and mute animal: and yet he speaks with it as if it were a rational human. Resp. 1. The author of the Historia Scholastica says, Balaam, accustomed to monsters, did not tremble at the voice of the donkey. 2. Augustine, q. 50 in Numer., establishes that Balaam, blinded by anger and the desire for revenge, was not at all moved by the speech of the donkey, nor was he terrified. 3. Philo, in the book that God is immutable, establishes this cause, that he was overwhelmed by the waves of imprudence. 4. Dionysius the Carthusian, in chapter 22 of Num., teaches that Balaam spoke with the donkey with the intention that those things which he was saying might be understood as being spoken by the Devil through it, being indignant against it, and wishing to slaughter the donkey to its disgrace. 5. Our Apostle seems to attribute this to his foolishness.

4. Peter in this place calls Balaam a Prophet. But Moses calls him a soothsayer Num. 22. v. 5. by which name he is also called Ios. 13. vers. 22 Resp. 1. That Balaam was a Prophet of God, though greedy and wicked, is evident from the fact that Peter calls him a Prophet absolutely, and does not rebuke idolatry in him, but greed. 2. But especially that is evident from the Mosaic description, in which it is recorded that he sought and obtained his answers from the true God. Num. 22. vers. 8. I will answer you, as Jehovah shall speak to me. v. 13. Jehovah refused to grant me to go with you, v. 18. I shall not be able to transgress the mouth of Jehovah my God. v. 19. that I may know what Jehovah may add to speak to me. 3. If anyone should even very much wish to object, that Balaam indeed boasts that Jehovah speaks with him, but Moses, in describing the oracles given to Balaam, does not use the word Jehovah, but Elohim, which is also attributed to false Gods, as is evident from the whole cap. 22. Num. it can be answered that Moses Num. 23. v. 5. expressly says, that Jehovah put a word in the mouth of Balaam and again v. 16. Jehovah met Balaam and put a word in his mouth. 4. The oracle which he brought forth concerning the Messiah Num. 24. v. 17. is acknowledged by all to be divine and θεόπνευστον, whence he prefixes to the same such an opening v. 16. He said, hearing the utterances אל of God, and knowing the knowledge עליון of the Most High. He shall see the vision שדי of the Almighty, etc. 5. Num. 22. v. 5. in the Hebrew text there is nothing that corresponds to the name soothsayer. The words are as follows. And he sent (Balac) messengers to Balaam the son of Beor פתורה Targum לפתור ארם to Pethor of Syria, which is near נהר the river, Targum פרת the Euphrates, the land of his people, that is, from where Balac was born. The LXX retained the proper name. φαθούῤῥα except that ה they took the local for the feminine Benjamin in the Itinerary. באליץ Baliz formerly פתורה Pethor near the river Euphrates, where even to this day the tower of Balaam son of Beor is visited, built according to the calculation of the hours of the day. Certainly the Vulgate Interpreter who פתורה Num. 22. v. 5. translates soothsayer, took it for an appellative noun from the root פתר he interpreted, he explained dreams Gen. 40. v. 8. but in the parallel place Deut. 23. v. 4. He hired against you Balaam, the son of Beor מפתור from Pethor of Aram of the two rivers that is, from Mesopotamia of Syria, the same Vulgate Interpreter acknowledges it to be the proper name of a place. 6. Ios. 13. v. 22. the name קוסם is held, which is of middle signification, for it is not only taken in a bad sense for soothsayer, Magician, diviner Deut. 18. v. 10. but also in a good sense for one who knows future things beforehand Es. 3. v. 2. just as also the root קסם is not only taken in a bad sense so as to signify, he used juggling tricks, sorceries, divinations. 1. Sam. 28. v. 8. But also in a good sense so as to signify, he predicted future things, he prophesied Mich. 3. v. 11. hence the LXX rendered μάντιν prophet. 7. Meanwhile, however, it is not unlikely that Balaam, driven by the desire for gain, had sometimes also used illicit divinations, especially since he lived among infidels devoted to the worship of Demons. Num. 24. v. 1. it is said of him. He did not go, as had been done twice before, to meet נחשים auguries. Therefore he previously wished to elicit an oracle about cursing the Israelite people by Magical arts and incantations. cap. 23. v. 1. & following, he orders twice altars to be erected, and sacrifices to be offered, from which Ambrose lib. 6. Epist. 37. Gregory of Nyssa lib. on the life of Moses, Cyril lib. 6. on prayer, Augustine q. 48. in Num. Theodoret q. 40, & following, gather, that he was a Prophet of the Devil. Augustine or whoever else is the author of sermon 203. on the times, says of him, that he frequently turned opposing armies to flight by a cursing song and sorcery. The author of Phesichra 56. 4. calls him נביא שקר a lying Prophet. Jerome in the Hebrew questions from Num. 22. At first a holy man and Prophet of God. Afterwards through disobedience and the desire for gifts when he wishes to curse Israel, he is called by the name of a diviner (namely Iosuae 13. v. 22. where in the Hebrew it is קסם ) R. Mardochai Nathan in Concord. Hebraicis. קוסם is a magician, a diviner, a soothsayer. There are also those who explain it as an inspector of the stars, who foresees future things: others wish that it be a diviner of dreams, others a Pseudo-Prophet. Confer Drusius lib. 9. Praeteri. p. 386. Mafius in cap. 13. Iosuae 5. The donkey is said to have hindered the foolishness of the Prophet. But Num. 22. v. 20. The Lord had permitted Balaam to go to Balak, King of the Moabites. I respond: when the first royal legates came to Balaam and asked that he go with them to Balak and curse the Israelite people, Balaam consulted the mouth of the Lord and brought back a clear response v. 12. Do not go with them, nor curse the people (Israelite) because he is blessed. But when for a second time more and more honorable legates were sent by the King, and offered greater gifts to Balaam, driven by the desire of collecting money and obtaining dignity before the King, he finally wavers, and although he already had the will of GOD sufficiently perceived from the first oracle, nevertheless because he did not want to fall out of the King's favor and lack the offered largesse, he tempts the Lord by exploring a second time whether he might obtain through a different response than the former. Therefore, by the just judgment of GOD, he receives an ironic response. If these men have come to call you, arise and go with them, that is, at your own peril, since I see that you do not wish to acquiesce to my will already sufficiently known, but I command, that when you have come to the King, you say or do nothing, except what I shall have commanded you. For that GOD did not approve of Balaam's departure, nor hold it pleasing, is sufficiently manifest from the Angelic prohibition, as also from verse 22 immediately following. The fury of the Lord was angry because he walked with them. Add that he was setting out with the intention of cursing and harming, which God had nevertheless forbidden. The rule could be referred here, that imperatives are sometimes to be explained permissively, since they do not always signify a command, but sometimes συγχώρησιν. 1. Reg. 22. v. 22. 2. Reg. 2. 17. Matth. 8. v. 32. nay, in certain sayings of Scripture that is seen to be commanded, which nevertheless those who use that mode of speaking do not wish to be done. Iud. 10. v. 14. Call upon the Gods whom you have chosen Es. 21. v. 5. Prepare the table: Ez. 20. v. 39. Walk after your idols. Matt. 26, 45. Sleep and take your rest. Apoc. 22, 11. He who is in filth, let him become filthy still. But especially for the sake of comparison, it could be referred here that Christ says to Judas the traitor at the last supper Iohan. 13. v. 27. what you do, do quickly that is, because you have altogether determined to give effect to what you have proposed in your mind, and you securely reject all my warnings, not that I may further resist your attempts, do at your own peril what you so greatly desire to do; which formula of speaking contains an emphatic dissuasion rather than a permission, and certainly not an exhortation.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Luther in his book against the falsely called spiritual estate, vol. 2, fol. 112. b., writes thus: What are the eyes of an adulteress? Without doubt, a wanton, impudent, and forward life. Just as an impudent adulteress casts her eyes upon anyone and prostitutes herself to anyone: so the Papal Clerics are prone and headlong into lust, in which they live freely and securely without reproach. Indeed, that adulteries are frequent in the Papacy, the examples of the supreme Pontiffs demonstrate. Sergius III, a most filthy adulterer, begot John XII, later Pope, from Marozia, a most impure woman, as reported by Liutprand of Cremona l. 3. on the deeds of the Emperors, c. 12. John XIII was caught in adultery and stabbed to death, according to Sigebert, Year 963. John XXIII was accused at the Council of Constance of having committed incest with his brother's wife and with Nuns, of having deflowered virgins, and of having perpetrated adulteries with married women. The Vispergensis calls Clement V a public fornicator. The beastly lusts of Leo X are known to the whole world. Paul III committed various rapes and adulteries.

2. The same Luther in his commentary on this passage adapts that ἀκαπαύστους ἁμαρτίας to the Papacy in this way: The Pontiff has prohibited the secular Magistrate from punishing Ecclesiastical persons for crimes, and if a political Magistrate attempts such a thing, he is excommunicated, but this has been entrusted to the Bishops. But because they are immersed in sins on both ears, they therefore wink at the crimes of the Clerics. Thus, therefore, they have exempted themselves from the power of the political Magistrate, so that no one dares to resist their wantonness.

3. Concerning the avarice of the Roman Pontiffs and the Papal pecuniary nets, it was spoken of above in commentary on v. 3.

4. But also this part of the Apostolic prophecy, forsaking the right way they have gone astray, having followed the way of Balaam &c. has been abundantly fulfilled in the Papacy. For the Pontifical Doctors have forsaken the way of celestial truth revealed in the word, and have proposed human dreams to the people; many also have allowed themselves to be hired for a reward, so that they might defend superstitions and idol-manias, just as Erasmus was accustomed to say, that poor Luther has enriched many, namely those who, hired by money, wrote against him. See by all means Luther in his book against the falsely called Spiritual estate, vol. 2, Jena, German, f. 113.

where he compares the idolatrous worship of Baal-Peor, to which Balaam led the Israelites, with the human doctrines that reign in the Papacy. Item in the commentary on this place, in the same volume, folio 408 b.

5. Bede in the commentary on this place writes thus: Often heretics put forward such foolish dogmas, such execrable sacraments, that even the senses of the dull and of pagans, and of those who are entirely lacking in the reason of divine knowledge, detest their insanity, and by thinking more soundly, refute their distorted paths that are contrary to GOD; and what is worse, because it is more frequent, sometimes many Catholics love the wages of iniquity to such an extent that even the learned are deservedly torn apart by the unlearned, and the Clergy by the Laity, who are rightly compared to the Prophet who is rebuked by the words of an ass speaking against Nature, yet is not delayed from the purpose of his wicked journey. Salmero ibid. The ass of Balaam signifies a certain kind of men in the Church, humble and ignorant, and subject to the divine law and to GOD: and upon these the False Prophets rely, who indeed from the beginning capture many of this kind, and sit upon them, whom they lead into the way of cursing. But the Angel of GOD makes them safe; and they crush against the wall, which is Christ, the foot of the one sitting; and so it sometimes happens that the simpler ones by the example of their life rebuke their superiors. (Such were very many in times past and still are in the Papacy, whose ears are purer than the lips of those teaching, so that it is sought in vain where the Church was under the Papacy before the light of the Gospel arose.)

Ἐκδίησις. 1. The Vulgate version v. 15. has followed the way of Balaam from Bosor, as if Bosor were the name of a place, when in the Greek it is only τοῦ Βοσόρ, in that sense, that Balaam was the son of Βοσόρ. The Papists, for whom the Vulgate version was made authentic in the Council of Trent, in order to protect its authority, attempt to prove that Βοσόρ was the name of a place, but they depart into two different opinions. 1. Some establish that by Βοσόρ is denoted that place which is called by the Hebrews בצר Deut. 4. v. 43.Ios. 20. v. 8.1. Paral. 6. v. 78. which the LXX rendered Βοσόρ. The same name of a place also exists1. Maccab. 5. v. 26. But this opinion does not agree with the circumstances of the History of Balaam. For בצר or Βοσόρ in the texts cited is the name of a place in the land of Canaan in the tribe of Reuben. But Balaam, originating from the city of Pethor in Mesopotamia, says Deut. 23. v. 4.Num. 22. v. 5. whence he says of himself, Num. 23 v. 7. from Aram i.e. Syria Balac brought me, where Abulensis by a notable error understands by the name Aram Haran or Charras, the fatherland of Abraham. For that city, in which Abraham lived, the Hebrews write with ח at the beginning ן at the end חרן But Aram, from which Balaam was summoned, they write with א at the beginning & ם at the end ארם by which name Aram or Syria is called by the Hebrews. 2. Some therefore think Βοσόρ to be the name of that place, whichNum. 22. v. 5.is called פתור which city was the fatherland of Balaam. They demonstrate the agreement of the Hebrew word פתור with the Greek Βοσόρ, in this way, that the Jews ת commonly pronounce the raphated or aspirated as S lisping, and therefore for פתור read Peter Βεσόρ, & with the sheva changed, which is read as a very short e in o Βοσόρ, which Weigenmeier notes elsewhere among the ancients in his tables, page 5. 3. But indeed, because it is fitting that we be concerned not so much with the authority of the Vulgate version as with the integrity of the Greek text, which alone is authentic, and in truth no Greek codices read ἐκ τοῦ Βοσόρ, but simply τοῦ Βοσόρ, therefore it must be certain that by the little word Βοσόρ not the name of some place, but the parent of Balaam is denoted. 4. Nor does it conflict with this opinion, that the parent of Bileam,Num. 22. v. 5.Mich. 6. vers. 5.is called not Bosor, but בעור Beor. For so that we may say nothing about the fact that Augustine, q. 48 on Numbers, reciting this passage of Peter, and the Syriac version published by Pococke, likewise read Beor in this place according to the Hebrew pronunciation of the O.T., in which way it is also read in Luther's version in certain editions, it can be answered that either the parent of Bileam was διώνυμον of two names & בעור i.e. also βοσόρ called (which is frequent in the scriptures. Compare Gen. 26. v. 34. with Gen. 36. v. 2. Item Iudic. 6. v. 32. with 2. Sam. 11. v. 21. Item 1. Sam. 21. v. 2. with Marc. 2. v. 26. Item 1. Paral. 2. v. 6. with Ios. 7. v. 1. Item 2. Reg. 24. v. 6. with 1. Paralip. 3. v. 16. & Ierem. 22. v. 24.) or בעור was changed by the Interpreter into Βοσόρ, of which kind changes in names, especially proper ones, often happen, as Tiglath Pileser & Tilgath Pilneser 2. Reg. 15. vers. 19.1. Paral. 5. v. 6. Abigal & Abigail 2. Sam. 17. v. 25.1. Paral. 2. v. 16. Aram & Ram 1. Paral. 2. v. 9.Matth. 1. v. 3. Timnath-seres & Timnath-sera Iud. 2. v. 9.Ios. 24. v. 30. Bethbara & Bethabara Iud. 7. v. 24.Ioh. 1. v. 28. Nay, even in this very place, which Moses Num. 22. v. 5. & seqq. calls Bilham, Peter and Iudas v. 11. call him Balaam. The Syrian calls him Belham. 5. Thence Salmero, compelled by the brightness of truth, from The Vulgate version departs at this place. Bede, he says, thinks Βοσόρ is the name of the city which Balaam inhabited. Because, however, it is said in Greek Βαλαάμ τοῦ Βοσόρ, it is signified that Balaam was the son of Bosor, althoughNum. 22.he is called the son of Beor, and either the word Bosor is placed here for Beor, or he was called by both names.

2. Abulensis Num. 22. q. 10. rightly refutes the Hebrew delirium of the Rabbis concerning the ten things which were created in the evening of the Sabbath at the setting of the sun after the formation of man, among which in the third place they number the mouth of Balaam's ass for speaking.

Observations 1. It is customary in the Scriptures for idolatry and false doctrine to be compared to adultery and fornication, and consequently also for false teachers to be compared to harlots enticing others to lust. Apoc. 9. v. 8.cap. 17. v. 1. etc. Bede in this place: Harlots are accustomed to be called pellices, the word being taken from pollution, or from the beauty of their skin, by which they entice the unwary. They entice, therefore, unstable souls, whom by teaching badly they subject to the erroneous sects of various dogmas as if to the lusts of those who defile.

2. Spiritual and bodily fornication are for the most part joined. The devil is a liar.Ioh. 8. vers. 44. and the unclean spiritLuc. 11. v. 24. therefore impels one to scatter the lies of heresies and to follow impure lusts, those whom he holds bound in his snares. But also, how would he who does not keep faith with GOD keep faith with his spouse?

3. Sin is fruitful; it does not end where it begins. The following sin is for the most part the punishment of the preceding, and the preceding sin is the cause of the following.

4. Especially, however, luxury and idleness are accustomed to be followed by lasciviousness and obscene lusts. Prov. 30. vers. 15. Luxury never says, it is enough. Os. 4. v. 10. They have committed fornication and have not ceased. Concerning Messalina, Juvenal Satyr. 6: And wearied by men, she did not yet depart satisfied.

5. Those who are not yet sufficiently confirmed and founded in the doctrine of the faith are seduced by false teachers with easy effort. Eph. 4. v. 14. Let us not be children, fluctuating and carried about by every wind of doctrine in the wickedness of men, etc. 2. Tim. 3. v. 6. Always learning, never arriving at the knowledge of the truth.

6. False doctrine is for the most part compared to the snaring of money. Luther in his book against the falsely called spiritual estate vol. 2. f. 115. Was Menschen Ding ist/ das trägt Geld/ Gottes Wort träget nichts denn das Kreutz.

7. Greedy men are children of a curse. Acts 8. v. 20. The interest of money becomes the funeral of the soul for the greedy. Prosper, book 2, on the contemplative life, chapter 13. Those who wish to have riches do not find them without difficulty, do not keep them without care, do not possess them without anxious delight, do not lose them without pain.

8. Those who abandon the way of truth shown in the word are carried off into the various pathless wastes of errors.

9. Just as Peter says of Balaam in this place, that he loved the wages of iniquity, so also Luke Acts 1. v. 18. pronounces of Judas the traitor, that he acquired a field from the wages of iniquity. Both, driven and blinded by avarice, fell into a most grave sin.

10. Bede in his commentary on this place also applies the name of Balaam to false teachers. But also the name, he says, of Balaam himself, which is interpreted as vain people or casting them down, is fitting for such men. For those who of their own accord desert the way of truth once recognized, what are they if not a vain people? What are they if not those who send their hearers into a precipice, to whom they preach not salutary things that might correct them, but erroneous things that might delight them.

11. The donkey of Balaam, uttering a human voice, teaches that God is not bound to secondary causes, but can act even above Nature, indeed even against Nature.

12. He who was able to form a human voice in the mouth of a donkey, He is able to give to His confessors, even if they are ἰδιῶται καὶ ἀγράμματοι Acts 4. v. 13. a στόμα καὶ σοφίαν, which all adversaries cannot contradict and resist. Luke 21. v. 15.

13. Those who do not wish to hear GOD speaking with them in the word are sometimes rebuked by donkeys. Thus, sometimes the motions of Princes; simpler people rebuke the sins and errors of Pastors.

14. Augustine, question 50 on Numbers, interprets the speech of the donkey mystically concerning the foolish of the world, whom GOD was going to choose, that He might confound the wise. 1 Cor. 1. v. 27. Ambrose in chapter 19 of Luke concerning the Gentile people, who under the coming of the great Angel, when previously it was a donkey, ought to speak.

15. Gregory, part 3 of the Pastoral Care, admonition 13. An insane man is rebuked by a dumb beast, when a proud mind of humility. That it ought to hold, is remembered by the afflicted flesh; the flesh through sickness recalls the mind to the knowledge of itself, so that it may reform that which a healthy man usually casts aside, by the memory of infirmity.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quo sensu oculi falsorum doctorum dicanturμεστοί μοιχαλίδοςpleni adulterâ? Resp. 1. Quidam nomen μοιχαλίδοςconiungunt cum sequenti nomineἁμαρτίας& per interposita voceἀκαταπαύσουςleguntἀκαταπαύσου, hoc sensu, oculos habentes degeneres, perpetuique peccati plenos. Sed Graeca exemplaria consentienter legunt ἀκαταπαύσους ἁμαρτίαςnon desinentes à peccato. Sed in Scripturis insolens ephitheton μοιχαλίδος peccato addi. 2. Hebraeis usitatum concretum poni poni pro abstracto. Sic Deut. 29. v. 19.ebria ponitur pro ebrietate, sitiens pro siti. Dan. 9. v. 29.נביא pro נבואהEph. 6. v. 12.πνευματικὰ πονηρίας sunt πνεύματα πονηρὰ. Sic ergo adulterae nomen & h. l. ponitur pro adulterio vel adulterandi libidine. 3. Posset etiam haud incommodè dici, Apostolum hoc velle, quod libidinosi isti homines in ipsis oculis adulteram gestent, & nihil aliud quàm adulteras libidinis explendae causâ spectent, quae adulteram semper prae oculis habeant, nec aliò coniiciant suos oculos, quàm ut adulteram spectent.

Cyprianus, vel quicunque alius autor in lib. de simplicit. Praelatorum, emphasin phraseos pulchrè expressit. Insaniunt prorsus, ardent desiderio feminarum, quotquot huic interdictioni non cedunt: & obscoenitatibus inhiantes malunt mori, quàm contenti sint â lateribus mulierum aliquâ disiunctione divelli, ut ad explendam suae aviditatis ingluviem etiam puncto temporis non sint sine feminae voluptate, & hunc habent in mulieribus fructum, ut in illis semper defixâ intentione desideria satient oculorum, ne vel momentum aliquod transeat, quando indigeant, quod affectant. Sic inter eos integritas emoritur, ubi omnis commoratio sive connivendo, sive commanendo corruptis affectionibus inquinatur, quos sanctus Petrus designavit, dicens, Oculos habentes plenos moechationibus. Occumenius in h. l. Quin etiam dum vobiscum epulantur, non ob caritatem id faciunt, sed ut occasionem ad decipiendas mulieres nanciscantur. Hi enim cùm oculos habeant, non aliud quàm adulteras inspiciunt &c.

Q. 2. Quare Apostolus in describenda adulterand libidine oculorum in specie mentionem faciat? Resp. fit hoc duplici de causa. Primò per oculos velut per fenestras illud, quod libidinem excitat & inflammat, ingreditur. Hebraei dicunt. Oculi & cor sunt proxenetae amoris. Notum est illud Graecorum. οὐκ τοῦ ὁρᾶν γίγνεται τὸ ἐρᾶν.Ut vidi, ut perii, ut me malus abstulit error, dicit ille apud Maronem: Oculi sunt in amore duces, apud Propert. lib. 2. Eleg. 5. Eò â quibusdam veterum accommodatur illud Propheticum. Ier. 9. v. 21.Mors per fenestras nostras intravit. Rectiùs huc referuntur dicta sequentia. Iob. 31. v. 1.Foedus pepigì cum oculis meis, & quid consideravi in virgine.Psal. 119. v. 37. David laesâ graviter per oculos animâ petiit â DEO, ut eos averteret, ne viderent vanitatem.Proverb. 6. v. 26. de adultera dicitur, cave ne capiat te palpebris suis.Thren. 3. v. 51.Oculus meus depraedatus est animam meam, in quem locum Hieronymus sic commentatur. Per oculum corporis pertulit praedam cordis.Matth. 5. vers. 28.Qui aspicit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam (h. e. ita ut concupiscat eam, non enim significatur aspectûs finis, sed aspiciendi modus veleventus) iamdum moechatus est cum ea in corde suo. in quem locum eleganter sic commentatur Salvianus lib. 3. de provid. Hinc intelligere planè possumus, quàm castos nos esse Salvator iusserit, qui etiam licentiam visionis abscidit. Sciens enim, fenestras quodammodo esse nostrarum mentium lumen oculorum, & omnes improbas cupiditates in cor per oculos, quasi per naturales cuniculos introire, extinguere eas penitùs foris voluit, ne intus oriuntur & lethaliter crescentibus fibris convale scerent fortassè in animo, si germinassent in visu. Ambrosius lib. de Ioseph. cap. 3. Prima adulterae oculorum tela sunt, secunda verborum, sed qui non capitur oculis, potest verbis resistere. Hieron. in cap. 3. Threno. Semel species formae cordi per oculos alligata vix magni luctaminis manu solvitur. Ut enim munda mens in cogitatione servetur, à lascivia voluptatis suae deprimendi sunt oculi quasi quidam raptores ad culpam. Secundò, quia libidinis signa in oculis potissimùm relucent. Basilius de vera virginit. Oculi sunt pronubi eius, cuius tactus minister est. Augustinus in Regul. Monach. Ne dicatis vos habere animos pudicos, si oculos habetis impudicos, quia impudicus oculus est impudici cordis nuncius. De Potipharis coniuge Gen. 39. v. 7. dicitur, quod impudicos suos oculos in Iosephum coniecerit, quibus velut venenatis quibusdam telis in sui amorem ipsum pellicere, & cor eius inflammare fuit conata. Ezech. 6. v. 9. mentio fit oculorum fornicantium. Agitur quidem ibi de Spirituali fornicatione, interim comparatio à fornicatione corporali est petita. Sirac. 26. v. 12.Fornicatio mulieris in extollentiis oculorum & in palpebris suis cognoscetur. Zaleucus Locrensium legislator lege sanxit, ut adulteris oculi eruerentur, quasi primi in homine adulteri, ut refert Aelianus lib. 13. variar. Hist. cap. 24. Utramque causam coniungit Bernhardus, quando lib. de gradibus humilit. dicit, oculos esse occasionem peccati indicium commissae culpae, & causam committendae.

Q. 3. An perπλεονεξίαςturpium voluptatum insatiabiles cupiditates h. l. intelligantur? Ita quidam statuunt, ad probandum istud adducentes locum Apostolicum Eph. 4. v. 19. ubi de gentilibus dicit Apostolus, tradiderunt seipsosτῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσις ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ. Oecumenius hanc expositionem probat ex verbis proximè praecedentibus oculos habentes plenos adulterio. Sed πλεονεξία rectiùs intelligitur de cupiditate divitiarum, uti constat, tùm ex verbis proximè praecedentibus, illicientes animas instabiles; tùm ex subiecto Bileami exemplo, tum ex perpetuo Scripturae, in qua πλεονεξία pro avaritia, & ex ea originem ducente proximi defraudatione semper accipitur, unde etiam Oecumenius hanc expositionem priori coniungit. Locus ex Eph. 4. v. 19.

adductus non probat contrarium, quia utrumque vitium Apostolus gentilibus tribuit, tùm impuras libidines, tùm avaritiam, ut sic ἐν accipiatur pro cum, ut in hac ipsa Epistola cap. 1. v. 5.

Q. 4. De quali animarum instabilium seductione Apostolus loquatur? Resp. 1. Quidam existimant de seductione per voluptates carnales Apostolo vel unicè, vel praecipue sermonem esse, quò accommodant illud Platonis, quod voluptas sit esca malorum, quâ homines capiantur, ut hamo pisces. 2 Quidam contra statuunt, de seductione per falsam doctrinam praecipuè h. l. sermonem esse. Nam primò dicuntur illi falsi doctores δελεάζειν τὰς ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους. Quinam verò sint illi ἀστήρικτοι, colligi potest ex seqq. cap. 3. vers. 16. ubi ἀμαθεῖς καὶ ἀστήρικτοι dicuntur στρεβλεῖν Scripturas sacras, ex quo manifestum est, per ἀστηρίκτους intelligieos, qui in fide & cognitione veritatis non sunt satis firmati ac fundati. Secundò de seductione per voluptates carnales agitur demumv. 18. seqq. δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκός ἐν ἀσελγείαις. Tertiò ἀστηρίκτοις hisce opponuntur στερεοὶ ἐν πίστειfirmi ac fortes in fide.1. Petr. 5. v. 9. 3. Sed hae expositiones non sunt oppositae, sed subordinatae, quia qui doctrinam falsorum istorum doctorum amplectuntur, toto animi impetu ad voluptates carnales eorundem exemplo seruntur; & vicissim, qui voluptates carnis sectantur, illi facilius sibi persuaderi patiuntur, ut falsam illorum Pseudo Prophetarum doctrinam amplectantur.

Q. 5. Quare dicantur filii maledictionis? Resp. nomen filiorum iuxta Hebraismum variis modis usurpatur, quorum aliqui hûc accommodari possunt. 1. Filii dicuntur, qui student & invigilant alicui rei. 2. Reg. 4. v. 38. Quòd si ergò per maledictionem μετωνυμιχῶς intelligatur maledicta doctrina, filii maledictionis dicentur addicti maledictae Naturae. 2. Sicut filii roboris dicuntur homines robusti Deut. 3. v. 18.filii iniquitatis homines iniqui & impii Deut. 13. v. 13.filii foederis illi, qui sunt in foedere. Act. 3. v. 25.filii incredulitatis homines increduli Col. 3. v. 6.filii obedientiae homines obedientes 1. Petr. 1. v. 14. Sic filii maledictionis sunt homines maledicti. 3. Sicut filii mortis dicuntur, qui sunt digni morte 1. Sam. 20. v. 21.2. Sam. 12. v. 5.filii percussionis, digni qui percutiantur, Deut. 25. v. 2. Sic filii maeledictionis sunt digni maledictione, quò pertinet regula Hebraistarum. Vocesבן&υἱὸςiunctae genitivo virtutis velvitii iisdem deditum; genitivo praemii vel poenae his dignum denotant. 4. Sicut filii irae sunt, quos manet DEI ira Ephes. 2. v. 2.filii damnationis, quos manet damnatio: Sic filii maledictionis sunt, quos manet non solùm temporalis, sed etiam aeterna maledictio, in die iudicii contra ipsos aliquando proferenda. Matth. 25. v. 41.

Q. 6. Quo sensu falsi doctores dicantur sequi viam Balaami? Resp. 1. Ratione faelsae doctrinae; quia ut Balaam fuit ori Domini in oboediens, & contra ipsius verbum ad Regem Moabitarum Balacum abiit: sic falsi doctores viam veritatis in verbo Domini praescriptam deserunt: 2. Ratione impiae vitae. Sicut Balaam sui commodi & retinendae gratiae Regiae studio dedit Balaco consilium, ut filiae populi Mobitici in sui amorem, & simul etiam ad idololatriam pellicerent Israëlitas: sic falsi doctores ad licentiam carnis & libidines sectandas aliis sunt autores. 3. Ratione avaritiae, quia falsi doctores aequè ac Bileam us ob reditus, praebendas & dignitates â recta veritatis viâ decedunt.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Asina Bileami vocaturὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον. v. 16. & tamen statim dicitur humanâ voce locuta. Resp. prius respicit Naturam huius animalis, posterius verò miraculum supernaturale in eo editum; quòd divinâ potentiâ factum fuerit, ut animal loquendi facultate per Naturam destitutum vocem humanae similem ediderit. Dionysius Carthusianus, Lorinus, Estius &c. putant, ministerio Angeli hanc vocem in ore asinae â DEO fuisse formatam. Sed quia Moses notanter dicit, Iehovah aperuit os asinaeNum. 22. vers. 28. ideò hoc miraculum immediatè divinae potentiae tribuendum.

2. Subiugale mutum dicitur corripuisse Balaami transgressionem, & insipientiam eius prohibuisse. Atqui in verbis asinae non occurrit aperta reprehensio illius criminis. Sic en im habent Num. 22. vers. 28.Quid feci tibi, quod iam percussisti me tribus vicibus? v. 30. Nonne ego asina tua super quam equitasti â tempore praecedente tuo usque ad hanc diem? num consuescendo consuevi tibi sic facere? Resp. 1. Ἔλεγξιν Petrus disertè non tribuit asinae, sed absolutè dicit, quòd Balaamus habuerit redargutionem suae transgressionis, id quod de Angelo Domini, qui postea cum Balaamo locutus fuit, intelligi potest ac debet. 2. Ex insolito & stupendo illo asinae loquentis miraulo Balaamus intelligere potuit, ac debuit, viam suam esse perversam, ac suam insipientiam â bruto animali redargui. 3. Quia Deus per asinam & per Angelum Balaamo locutus, ac quia loquelae per Angelum aditus quasi patefactus per loquelam asinae, ideò Petrus, omnia illa coniungens, Balaami insipientiam per asinam prohibitam fuisse dicit.

3. Balaam noverat se insidere animali bruto ac muto: & tamen cum eo tanquam homine rationali loquitur. Resp. 1. Autor Historiae Scholasticae dicit. Balaamum assuetum monstris ad vocem asinae non trepidasse. 2. Augustinus q. 50. in Numer. statuit, Balaamum excaecatum irâ & vindictae cupiditate asinae sermone nihil commotum fuisse, nec expavisse. 3. Philo in lib. quod Deus sit immutabilis, causam statuit, hanc, quod imprudentiae fluctibus fuerit obrutus. 4. Dionysius Carthusianus in cap. 22. Num. docet, Balaam cum asina sic locutum eâ intentione, ut intelligerentur, quae dicebat â Diabolo loquente per eam, indignando contra illum, ac in illius dedecus volendo asinam trucidare. 5. Apostolus noster hoc videtur insipientiae eius tribuere.

4. Petrus hoc loco Balaamum vocat Prophetam. Sed Moses illum vocat ariolumNum. 22. v. 5.quo nomine etiâm appellaturIos. 13. vers. 22 Resp. 1. Balaamum fuisse Prophetam Dei, avarum tamen & improbum, constat ex eo, quod Petrus absolutè eum Prophetam vocat, nec reprehendit in eo idololatriam, sed avaritiam. 2. Cumprimis verò illud constat ex descriptione Mosaica, in qua responsa sua â vero Deo petiisse & impetrasse memoratur. Num. 22. vers. 8.Respondebo vobis, quemadmodum Iehovah ad me loquetur. v. 13. Renuit Iehovah concedere mihi, ut eam vobiscum, v. 18. Non potero transgredi os Iehovae Domini mei. v. 19. ut sciam, quid Iehovah mihi addat loqui. 3. Si vel maximè quis velit excipere, Balaamum quidem gloriari, quod Iehovah secum loquatur, Mosen verò, in describendis oraculis Balaamo datis, non uti voce Iehovah, sed Elohim, quae etiam falsis Diis tribuitur, uti constat ex totocap. 22. Num. responderi poterit, Mosen Num. 23. v. 5. expressè dicere, quod Iehovah posuerit verbum in ore Bileami & denuò v. 16. Occurrit Iehovah Bileamo & posuit verbum in ore eius. 4. Oraculum, quod de Messia protulit Num. 24. v. 17. ab omnibus agnoscitur esse divinum ac θεόπνευστον, unde eidem tale exordium praemittit v. 16. Dixit audiens eloquiaאלDei, & sciens scientiamעליוןAltissimi. Visionemשדיomnipotentis videbit &c. 5. Num. 22. v. 5. in textu Hebraeo nihil habetur, quod respondeat nomini arioli. Verba sic habent. Et misit (Balac) nuncios ad Bileam filium Beorפתורה Targum לפתור ארםin Petor Syriae, quae est iuxta נהרflumen, TargumפרתEuphratem, terram populi sui, h. e. unde Balac erat oriundus. LXX. retinuerunt nomen proprium. φαθούῤῥα nisi quod ה locale acceperint pro faeminino Beniamin in Itineratio. באליץBaliz quondamפתורהPethora iuxta Euphratem fluvium, ubi in hodiernum usque diem visitur turris Bileam filii Peor ad diei horarum rationes aedificata. Sanè vulgatus Interpres qui פתורהNum. 22. v. 5. vertit ariolum, accepit pro nomine appellativo à rad. פתרinterpretatus est, exposuit somniaGen. 40. v. 8. sed in loco parallelo Deut. 23. v. 4.Conduxit super te Bileam, filium Beorמפתורde Pethor Aram duorum fluviorum h. e. ex Mesopotamia Syriae idem ipse vulgatus Interpres agnoscit esse nomen proprium loci. 6. Ios. 13. v. 22. habetur nomen קוסם quod est mediae significationis, non solùm enim accipitur in malum pro ariolo, Mago, divinatoreDeut. 18. v. 10. sed etiam in bonum pro praescio futurorumEs. 3. v. 2. sicut etiam radix קסם non solum accipitur in malum ut significet, usus est praestigits veneficiis divinationibus.1. Sam. 28. v. 8. Sed etiam in bonum ut significet, futura praedixit, vaticinatus estMich. 3. v. 11. inde LXX. reddiderunt μάντινvatem. 7. Interim verò non est absimile, Balaamum lucri cupiditate impulsum, quandoque etiam illicitis divinationibus fuisse usum, praesertim cùm inter infideles Daemoniorum cultui deditos habitaverit. Num. 24. v. 1. de ipso dicitur. Non abiit, sicut antea duabus vicibus factum fuerat, in occursumנחשיםauguriorum. Ergò prius voluit Magicis artibus & incantationibus oraculum de maledicendo populo Israëlitico elicere. cap. 23. v. 1. & seqq. bis aras erigi, sacrificiaque efferri iubet, ex quo Ambrosius lib. 6. Epist. 37. Gregorius Nyssenus lib. de vita Mosis, Cyrillus lib. 6. de orat. Augustinus q. 48. in Num. Theodoretus q. 40, & seqq. colligunt, ipsum fuisse Diaboli Prophetam. Augustinus vel quicunque alius autor serm. 203. de temp. de ipso, dicit, quod frequenter carmine maledico & maleficio exercitus adversarios in fugam verterit. Autor Phesichrae 56. 4. vocat eum נביא שקרProphetam mendacem. Hieronymus in qq. Hebr. ex Num. 22.Primùm vir sanctus & Propheta Dei. Postea per inoboedientiam & desiderium munerum cùm Israël male dicere cupit, divini vocabulo nuncupatur (sc.Iosuae 13. v. 22. ubi in Hebraeo est קסם) R. Mardochai Nathan in Concord. Hebraicis. קוסםest Magus, divinator, hariolus. Sunt etiam qui exponunt inspectorem astrorum, qui futura prae videt: alii volunt, quod sit divinator somniorum, alii Pseudo Propheta. Confer Drusium lib. 9. Praeteri. p. 386. Mafium in cap. 13. Iosuae 5. Asina dicitur prohibuisse insipientiam Prophetae. At Num. 22. v. 20.Dominus permiserat Bileamo, ut abiret ad Balac Moabitarum Regem. Resp. cum primi Legati Regii ad Balaamum venirent ac peterent, ut secum ad Balacum iret, & populo Israëlitico malediceret, Bileamus os Domini consuluit, ac disertum tulit responsum v. 12. Noli ire cum eis, neque maledicas populo (Israëlitico) quia benedictus est. Cùm verò secundâ vicè Legati plures & honoratiores à Rege mitterentur, ac maiora donaria Bileamo offerrent, cupiditate pecuniae colligendae, ac dignitatis apud Regem obtinendae, impulsus tandem labascit, ac quam vis iam antè voluntatem DEI ex primo oraculo satis perspectam haberet, tamen quia gratiâ Regis excidere, & congiariis oblatis carere noluit, tentat Dominum secundâ vice explorando, an per diversum à priore responsum impetrare posset. Iusto ergo DEI iudicio ironicum responsum accipit. Si vocatum te venerint isti homines, surge & vade cum eis, tuo sc. periculo, cùm videam te voluntati meae iamdum satis cognitae nolle acquiescere, sed iubeo, ut ubi ad Regem veneris, nihil dicas velfacias, nisi quod tibi praecepero. Quod enim DEUS Bileami abitum non approbaverit, nec gratum habuerit, ex prohibitione Angelica satis manifestè constat, uti etiam ex vers. 22. immediatè sequente. Iratus est furor Domini, quod ambulaverit cum eis. Adde, quod animo maledicendi ac laedendi proficiscebatur, quod tamen Deus prohibuerat. Posset hûc referri regula, quod Imperativi quandoque exponendi sint permissivè, cùm non semper praeceptum, sed interdum συγχώρησιν significent. 1. Reg. 22. v. 22.2. Reg. 2. 17.Matth. 8. v. 32. quinimò in quibusdam Scripturae díctis videtur id iuberi, quod tamen fieri non debere volunt, qui eo loquendi modo utuntur. Iud. 10. v. 14.Invocate Deos, quos elegistisEs. 21. v. 5.Instrue mensam:Ez. 20. v. 39.Ambulate post idola vestra.Matt. 26, 45.Dormite & requiescite.Apoc. 22, 11.Qui in sordibus est sordescat adhuc. Cumprimis verò collationis gratiâ huc referri posset, quod Christus in cena novissima Iudae proditoridicit Iohan. 13. v. 27.quod facis, fac citius id est, quia omnino tibi constitutum effectum dare, quod animo proposuisti tuo, ac securè omnes admonitiones meas repudias, non amplius tuis conatibus obsistam, fac tuo periculo, quod facere tan topere expetis; quae loquendi formula emphaticam potiùs dehortationem, quàm permissionem, necdum exhortationem continet.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Lutherus in lib. contra falsò dictum statum spiritualium tom. 2. fol. 112. b. sic scribit. Quid sunt oculi adulterae? procul dubio proterva, impudens & procax vita. Sicut impudens adultera oculos in quosvis coniicit, & cuivis se prostituit: Sic Papales Clerici ad libidinem proni sunt ac praecipites, in quae liberè & securè sine reprehensione vivunt. Nimirum in Papatu adulteria esse frequentia, exempla summorum Pontificum demonstrant. Sergius III. ex Marozia faemina impurissima Iohannem XII. postea Papam spurcissimus adulter genuit, referente Luit prando Ticinensi l. 3. de gestis Impp. c. 12. Iohannes XIII. in adulterio deprehensus. & confossus est, teste Sigeberto Ann. 963. Iohannes XXIII. in Concilio Constantiensi accusatus est, quod cum uxore fratris sui, & cum Monialibus incestum commiserit, quod virgines stuprârit & cum coniugibus adulteria perpetrârit. Clementem V. Vispergensis vocat publicum fornicatorem. Leonis X. beluinae libidines toti orbi notae Paulus III. varia stupra & adulteria commisit.

2. Idem Lutherus in comm. h. l. illud ἀκαπαύστους ἁμαρτίας ad Papatum hoc modo accommodat. Pontifex prohibuit, ne secularis Magistratus personas Ecclesiasticas ob delicta puniat, ac si tale quid politicus Magistratus tentat, excommunicatur, Episcopis verò hoc demandatum. Sed quia illi peccatis in utramvis aurem sunt immersi, ideò connivent ad Clericorum scelera. Sic ergo potestati Magistratus politici sese eximerunt, ut proterviae ipsorum nemo resistere audeat.

3. De avaritia Romanorum Pontificum, ac de retibus pecunariis Papalibus dictum fuit superiùs in comm. v. 3.

4. Sed & haec pars Apostolici vaticinii, derelinquentes rectam viam erraverunt, secuti viam Balaami &c. in Papatu abunde fuit impleta. Pontificii enim Doctores viam veritatis caelestis in verbo patefactam reliquerunt, & humana somnia populo proposuerunt; multi etiam mercede se conduci passi fuêrunt, ut superstitiones & idolomanias propugnarent, sicut Erasmus dicere fuit solitus, quod pauper Lutherus multos ditaverit, eos sc. qui pecuniâ conducti contra ipsum scripserunt. Vide omnino Lutherum in lib. contra falsò dictum statum Spiritualium tom. 2. Ien. Germ. f. 113.

ubi idololatricum cultum Baalpeor, ad quem Bileam Israëlitas induxit, confert cum doctrinis humanis, quae in Papatu regnant. Item in comment. h. l. tom. eodem fol. 408 b.

5. Beda in comm. h. l. sic scribit. Plerunque haeretici tam stulta dogmata, tam execranda proferunt sacramenta, ut etiam hebetum sensus & paganorum, & qui ratione divinae cognitionis omnimodis carent, illorum detestentur insaniam, illorum distorta, & DEO contraria itinera saniùs sapiendo redarguant; & quod peius, quia frequentius est, nonnunquam multi Catholici in tantum mercedem amant iniquitatis, ut etiam docti ab indoctis, â Laicis Clerici meritò lacerentur, qui iure comparantur Prophetae, qui verbis asinae contra Naturam loquentis corripitur, nec tamen â proposito pravi itineris retardatur. Salmero ibid. Asina Balaami significat quoddam genus hominum in Ecclesia, humile & ignarum, divinaeque legi subditum ac DEO: & in his nituntur Pseudo Prophetae, qui ab initio quidem multos eiusmodi capiunt, ac illis insident, quos in viam maledictionis inducunt.
