Qui enim servus est peccati, is etiam servus est Diaboli & mortis; illius quidem, quia quando Diabolus hominem per peccatum vincit, in suos laqueos & in suam potestatem illum redigit; huius verò quia stipendium peccati mors estRom. 6. v. 23. ac Diabolus habet mortis imperiumHebr. 2. v. 14.dominans illis, qui per totam vitam timore mortis obnoxii sunt servituti. vers. 15.

Ἐναντιοφάνεια.Poena damnatorum aeterna describitur per caliginem tenebrarumv. 17. Atqui cruciabuntur damnati per ignem, qui non est caliginosus, sed lucidus. Resp. 1. Augustinus lib. 20. de Civ. Dei c. 16. rectè dicit, Cuiusmodi sit ignis ille infernalis hominem scire arbitror neminem, nisifortè cui Spiritus divinus ostendit. Proindè nondum exactè constat, an ignis ille infernalis futurus sit corporeus visibilis, & omnis materiae expers? Confer tract. de Inferno §. 68. 2. Qui ignem infernalem corporeum & materialem statuunt, existimant vim lucendi divinâ virtute ab eo separatum iri, relictâ solâ vi urendi ad cruciatum impiorum.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Quae in v. 17. Apostolus falsis doctoribus tribuit, illa omnia Papalibus doctoribus conveniunt. Illi enim relicto fonte aquae vivae, Scripturis sc. sacris cisternas humanarum traditionum extra verbum sectantur; illorum doctrinae non praebet firmam & solidam consolationem; iidem in suis opinionibus sunt inconstantes, ac variis modis inter se dissident. Lutherus in libr. contra falsò sic dictum statum Spiritualium tom. 2. fol. 112. Episcopus sine concionandi munere est fons sine aqua, nubes sine pluvia Episcopalem sedem tenet, sed nihil eorum, quae Episcopo incumbunt, praestat sicutπηγή ἄνυδροςest fontis loco, sed aquam non exhibet. Idem in comm. h. l. tom. eod. f. 409. Doctores in Scripturis vocantur fontes, utpote â quibus scaturire debet salutaris doctrina, per quam animae reficiantur. Ad hoc officium Episcopi uncti sunt. Sed quid agunt? planè nihil; Solus duntaxat titulus superest.

2. Apostolus disertè asserit v. 18. per vaniloquentiam falsorum doctorum etiam seduci eos; quiὄντωςreverâ effugerant ab illis, qui in errore conversantur. Falsum igitur est, quod cum Anabaptistis Calviniani docent, fidem veram semethabitam nullis flagitiis â verè renatis deperdi aut Spiritum sanctum ab ipsis excutiposse. Frivola etiam est exceptio, quod qui fidem amisisse dicuntur, eam tantùmδοκήσειsuâ & aliorum opinione habuerint, quia Apostolus dicit, eos non οἰομένως sed ἄντως fidem habuisse. Athanasius orat. 4. contra Arian. tom. 1. p. 270. edit. Commel. ὅτε γοῦν ἐκπίπτει τις ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος διὰ τίνα κακίαν, ἡ μέν χάρις ἀμεταμέλητος μένει τοῖς βουλομένοις, κἄν τις ἐκ πεσῶν μετανοῇ, οὐκετι δὲ ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος ὁ πεσῶν, διὰ τὸ ἀποστῆναι ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἅγιον καὶ παράκλητον πνεῦμα ἀλλ' ἐν ἐκείνῳ ἔσται, ᾧ ἑαυτὸν ὑπέταξε ἁμαρτάνων, quibus verbis ad hunc ipsum locum Apostolicum respicit.

Excipit. 1. Piscator in comm. h. l. Petri dictum intelligendum esseκατὰ τιsecundum iudicium caritatis, quae omnes in externo Ecclesiae caetu habet pro credentibus. Idem in cap. 10. Hebr. schol. 29. pag. 1345. apostatas dici sanctificatos nonκατ' ἀλήθειανsedκατὰ δόξαν. Id ipsum alii sic efferunt; esse hoc intelligendumδόξαστικῶς, κατὰ χρηστικῶςin facie Ecclesiae, iuxta illorum, qui excidunt & aliorum, de ipsis praeconceptam opinionem. Resp. 1. Imò verò Apostolus disertè asserit, illos ὄντως reverâ effugisse ab illis, qui in errore conversantur. Hoc non potest dici de illis, quae iudicio caritatis duntaxat tales sunt, quia caritas omnia credit, omnia sperat. 1. Cor. 13. v. 7. 2. Si ea, quae in Scripturis credenda proponuntur, licet κατὰ δόκησιν accipere, nihil ampliùs certi ex Scripturis poterit colligi. Marcion teste Tertulliano in lib. de carne Christi, Catholicis probantibus veritatem carnis Christi ex eo, quod natus passus, mortuus, sepultus &c. respondebat, φανταστικῶς καὶ κατὰ δόξανhaec fuisse facta, atque his consiliis, inquit Tertullianus, tot originalia Christi instrumenta delebat. 3. Hebr. 6. v. 4. quidam apostatae sic describuntur, quòd fuerint illuminati, quod gustaverint donum caeleste & participes facti sint Spiritus Sancti v. 5. quod gustaverint bonum DEI verbum, virtutesque futuri seculi. Haec certè non possunt eo sensu accipi, quod tantùm κατὰ τὸ δοκεῖσθαι tales fuerint.

2. Tossanus excipit, dictum Apostoli accipiendum esse de illis, qui veritatem cognoverant & ab idololatria recesserant, quam vis non fuerint verè renati & verâ fide praediti. Resp. 1. in v. seq. Apostolus asserit, quod illi, de quibus agit, per cognitionem Christi effugerint inquinamentamundi. Ergò non solùm fide Historicâ, sed etiam verâ & salvificâ fide praediti fuêre. Nam fides Historica hoc non praestat, ut per eam effugiamus inquinamenta mundi. 2. Si illi, qui fide duntaxat Historicâ praediti sunt, possunt dici effugisse inquinamenta mundi, consequens fuerit, etiam de Diabolo dici posse, quòd effugerit inquinamenta mundi, cùm & ipse cognoscat doctrinae caelestis veritatem. 3. Etiam de hypocritis mundo servientibus dici posset, quod mundi inquinamenta effugerint, cùm ipsi quoque fide Historicâ sint praediti. 4. Apostolus eos, qui inquinamentis mundi, quae effugerant, iterum implicantur vers. 22. confert suibus ad volutabrum ceni reversis, & canibus, ea quae vomuerant, resorbentibus. At quomodo hae similitudines illis possunt applicari, qui non fuêre verâ fide â mundi inquinamentis priùs purgati?

3. Est & haec Tossani exceptio, dictum Apostolicum accipiendum esse de illis, qui â falsis doctoribus seducuntur, sed â DEO iterum convertuntur. Resp. 1. Quòd iterum post suum relapsum ad Deum fuerint conversi, de eo nihil extat apud Apostolum. 2. Ac sic vel maximè fuerunt iterum conversi, tamen ante suam conversionem fuêre verâ fide destituti, quam tamen habuerant, cùm inquinamenta mundi effugerent. 3. Temporali non debet opponi verum, sed permanens; ac vero non debet opponitemporale, sed falsum. Fides est vel vera, vel falsa. Vera fides est vel temporalis vel permanens; temporalis ex vitio hominum; permanens ex gratia Dei, non quidem absoluta, sed ordinata. Nimirum verum dicitur tripliciter. Primò verum κατ' οὐσίαν, Scholasticis verum essentiae seu existentiae, cùm res habet, quicquid ad suam essentiam pertinet, actusque proprios exercere potest, huic opponitur falsum, fictum, apparens aut putativum. Secundò dicitur aliquid verum κατ' ἐπιμονὴν & ἐπίτευξιν sive respectu finis, quando videlicet finem suum, ad quem ordinatur actu consequitur, utcunque interim in cursu aliquando interrumpatur, quibusdam dicitur verum permanentiae seu perseverantiae; huic opponitur vanum, frustraneum, atque inutile. Tertiò dicitur verum κατ' ἐπίτασιν, verum tenaciae solitudinis, firmitudinis fixae; huic opponitur infirmum atque imbecillum. Quando quaeritur, an vera fides excidere possit, tùm quaestio accipienda de prima, non de secunda, vel tertia significatione.

4. Alii excipiunt, quosdam Codd. Graecos legereὀλίγον,qui paululum effugerunt, ut sit sensus, neophytos in religione nondum satis confirmatos â pseudo doctoribus faciliùs seduci. Resp. quid de hac lectione statuendum sit, exposuimus superiùs.

3. Apostolus dicit, falsos doctores esse servos corruptionis, quod confirmat ratione eâ, quia â quo quis victus est, huic & servus adictus est. Ex eo contra Synergistas & Pontificios colligimus, hominem post lapsum esse peccati servum, cùm sit â peccato victus & superatus; ac proindè voluntatem hominis in spiritualibus non ampliùs esse liberam, sed peccati servam. Augustinus in Enchir. cap. 30. Libero arbitrio malè utens homo & se perdidit & ipsum. Sicut enim qui se occidit, utique vivendo se occidit, sed se occidendo non vivit, nec seipsum poterit resuscitare, cùm occiderit: ita cùm libero peccaretur arbitrio, victore peccato amissum est liberum arbitrium; â quo enim quis devictus est, huic & servus addictus est. Petri enim Apostoli est ista sententia, quae cùm vera sit, qualis quaeso potest servi addicti esse libertas, nisi quando eum peccare delectat. Liberaliter enim servit, qui Domini sui voluntatem liber facit; ac per hoc ad peccatum liber est, qui peccati servus est. Basilius Seleuciensis homil. 2. de Adamo, hominem post lapsum vocat αἰχμάλωτον ἅρματος οἰκείου captivum proprii currus. Et posteà. παραδοϊς τή ῥαθυυίᾳ τήν δεσποτείαν γίνεται δούλος παθῶν,prodito per socordiam domino fit servus affectuum. Excipit Bellarminus lib. 5. de grat. & lib. arbitr. cap. 29. resp. ad 4. testim. Servitutem & libertatem generatim acceptam sine dubio opponi, sed non quamvis servitutem cuivis liberati opponi, alioqui non diceret ApostolusRom. 6. vers. 20.eos qui sunt servi peccati, liberos esse iustitiae, & contra liberatos â peccato servos esse iustitiae. Itaque servitutem peccati opponi liberatati â peccato, non libertati Naturae, quae propriè dicitur liberum arbitrium. Nam qui servus est peccati non potest suis viribus excutere iugum peccati, & ad libertatem iustitiae pervenire, potest tamen per liberum arbitrium adiuvante DEO liberari â peccato, & potest, si velit, per se manere in servitute peccati: Sicut etiam è contrario servitus Naturae, hoc est, naturaelis determinatio ad unum, qualis est in pecoribus, opponitur libertati Naturae, hoc est, libero voluntatis arbitrio, non tamen libertatis â peccato; imò quae carent libertate Naturae, hoc ipso quòd illâ carent, non possunt ullo modo servire peccato. Similia occurrunt apud Estium in annot. ad Rom. 6. v. 22.

Resp. 1. Confundit Bellarminus libertatem â coactione cum libertate rectitudinis; libertatem subiecti cum libertate obiecti. Si per libertatem Naturae intelligit ipsam voluntatis humanae essentiam vellibertatem subiecti, vel libertatem â coactione, libenter concedimus, eam perlapsum non esse amissam, adhuc enim homo liberè à nemine coactus agit malum. Si verò per libertatem Naturae intelligit libertatem rectitudinis vel libertatem obiecti, quà voluntas hominis aequaliter se habeat ad bonum vel malum eligendum, quò spectare videtur quod servitutem libertati Naturae oppositam desinit determinatione ad unum, dicimus eam omninò per lapsum amissam esse. 2. Idem nobiscum docet Scriptura, docent pii veteres. Augustinus de grat. & lib. arb. cap. 15. totum negotium nervosè sic explicat. Semper in nobis voluntas est libera, sed non semper est bona. Aut enim â iustitia est libera, quando servit peccato & tunc est mala; aut â peccato est libera, quando servit iustitiae & tunc est bona, Gratiâ verò Dei semper est bona, & per hane fit, ut homo sit bonae voluntatis, qui priùs fuit malae voluntatis. Bernhardus serm. 81. in Cantic. Premebatur iugo, non alio tamen, quàm voluntariae cuiusdam servitutis, & erat pro servitute quidem miserabilis, sed pro voluntate inexcusabilis. Voluntas enim est, quae se, cùm esset libera, servam fecit peccati, peccato assentiendo, voluntas nihilominus est quaese sub peccato tenet, voluntariè serviendo. 3. Nec potest contrarium ex Bellarmini distinctione probari. Vitiosè enim opponit Bellarminus liberum arbitrium determinationi ad uno, sub innuens non consistere cum libero hominis arbitrio sive cum libertate Naturae determinationem ad unum, cùm tamen fateri cogatur, imo operosè disputet lib. 3. de grat. & lib. arbit. c. 16. Deum esse liberi arbitrii, cuius tamen voluntas ad unum, videlicet ad bonum est determinata. Optimè Bernhardus lib. de grat. & lib. arbit. Nemo putet, ideò dictum liberum arbitrium, quod aequâ in bonum & malum potestate aut facultate versetur, alioqui nec Deus nec Angeli, sive boni, sive mali, liberi arbitrii esse dicerentur, sed ex eo potiùs liberum arbitrium dicitur, quod sive in bono, sive in malo, aequè liberam facit voluntatem. 4. Servitus peccati, cui omnes homines post lapsum ante suam conversionem sunt subiecti, non tollit libertatem Naturae, si per eam intelligatur prona illa ad malum inclinatio omnibus per Naturam corruptam insita atque innata; tollitautem libertatem Naturae, si per eam intelligatur concreata & Naturae humanae primitus insita libertas rectitudinis, quâ voluntas aequâ inter bonum & malum facultate versabatur. 5. Liberos iustitiae appellat Apostolus μεταφορικώςemancipatos imperio iustitiae seu vacuos iustitiae. At vacui iustitiâ non sunt liberi ad iustitiam, sed tantùm ad iniustitiam, nec ad bonum, sed tantùm ad malum. Hoc verò loco quaeritur non de libertate seu vacuitate iustitiae, sed de libertate voluntatis ad iustitiam, sive ad bonum sine gratia Et sanè res ipsa docet, libertatem iustitiae Apostolo nihil aliud esse quàm pravitatem Naturae & pronitatem ad iniustitiam. Quando ergò Bellarminus pro libertate iustitiae, h. e. pro libertate ad bonum pugnat, reipsâ pro Naturae pravitate & pronitate ad iniustitiam pugnat. 6. Insidiosè dicitur, posse hominem non renatum per liberum arbitrium, adiuvante DEO, liberari â peccato. Si enim assertio illa hoc modo intelligitur, quod DEI auxilium excitet sopitas liberi arbitrii vires, ut gratia DEI & voluntas hominis sint causae sociae conversionis, (quo sensu Bellarminus eam profert) tunc assertio est falsa; sin verò eo modo explicetur, quòd homo in eo differat â bruto, quòd adhuc post lapsum voluntate praeditus sit, in quam tanquam subiectum cadere possit conversionis gratia, quae in pecora non cadit, rectè dicitur. Distinguendum proinde inter ἐνέργειαν activam ad bonum, & inter capacitatem passivam conversionis. Illam homini post lapsum denegamus, hanc verò concedimus.

4. In Papalibus doctoribus etiam hoc impletur, quod turgida & fastuosa, quae tamen vana & inania, proferant. Lutherus in comment. h. l. Totumius Pontificium refertum est fastuosis & vanis eiusmodi gloriationibus. Cogitentur encomia, quae Pontifici suo tribuunt, quod sit Christi Vicarius, Ecclesiae Monarcha, quod unum Consistorium habeat cum Christo, quod omnia iura habeat in scrinio sui pectoris, quod errare non possit, & quae huius generis alia. Cogitentur encomia, quae tribuunt Episcopis. Episcopatum dicunt esse statum perfectionis, & tamen Episcopi ipsorum fermè nihil aliud agunt, quam quòd neglecta animarum curâ & praetermisso docendi munere luxuriantur & genio indulgent. Si quid sacri muneris peragere cupiunt, Missas decantant, templa & altaria consecrant, Moniales velant, campanas baptizant &c. Cogitentur encomia, quae tribuunt Monachatui, quod constituti in eo non solùm legem perfectè implere, sed etiam opera supererogationis praestare, eademque aliis communicare possint. Per ingressum Religionis h. e. Monastices professionem dicunt hominem ita mundari â peccatis, ut per Baptismum fuit mundatus; opera quae in hoc statu fiunt, etiam vilissima, praeferenda esse dicunt summis pietatis operibus, quae fiunt â coniugatis. Cogitentur encomia, quae tribuunt suis traditionibus, quòd contineant abstrusa quaedam mysteria, non omnibus promiscuè revelanda; quod verbo DEI scripto vel praeferendae sint, vel certè exaequandae. Cogitentur encomia, quae tribuunt Missae, votivis, peregrinationibus, aquae benedictae, rosariis &c. ac liquidò apparebit, haec omnia, cùm sint praeter & extra, imò contra Scripturam inventa, esseὑπερογκα ματαιότητος.

5. Sed & hoc in Papalibus doctoribus impletum, quod suâ doctrinâ pelliciunt homines ad carnis desideria & libidines. Papa per prohibitionem coniugii mundum replevit libidinibus & horrendis flagitiis carnalibus, inquit Glossa margin. h. l. Videmus, inquit, Lutherus in lib. contra falsum dictum statum spiritualium tom. 2. fol. 115. b. statum Ecclesiasticum latissimè patere, qui in eo vivunt, voto caelibatus omnes sunt obstricti, & tamen Scriptura unâ cum experientia testatur, continentiam virginalem esse donum singulare & supernaturale, quod paucis etiam ex insignium Sanctorum ordine datum: ipsi verò hoc donum tàm commune faciunt, ut panem quotidianum, pelliciunt iuniores in illum statum Ecclesiasticum ac Monasticum, qui per omnem vitam postea in impuritate haerent. Cogitentur ergò fructus, qui ex coacto caelibatu oriuntur, immanes scil. ac nefandae Sacrificulorum ac Monachorum libidines. Expendantur egregia illa Pontificiorum Scriptorum emblemata, quòd Sacerdos uxorem ducens graviùs peccet, quàm si centum concubinas domi alat; quod secundae nuptiae Sacerdotibus magis sint illicitae, quàm adulterium; quòd satiùs sit ustionum flammis torqueri, quàm coniugium contrahere, si scilicet quis votum caelibatûs emiserit. Convertantur etiam oculi ad lupanaria, quae in populosioribus urbibus pulicè excructa & privilegiis munita omnium conspectui obversantur.

6. Congruit etiam illud vaticinio Apostolico, quòd Papales doctores libertatem â peccato promittunt per indulgentias & Missas pecuniâ comparatas, per opera supererogationis, interventu certi precii communicata, per Bullas Papales, in gradibus prohibitis dispensationem concedentes &c.

7. Suspecti verò sint insuper omnes alii Ecclesiae doctores, qui vanâ quadam grandiloquentiâ abstrusa mysteria promittunt, non contenti simplicirate Scripturae, quales olim fuêre Simoniani, Nicolaitae, Gnostici (qui ut ipsum nomen fastuosum innuit, sibi solis scientiam vendicantes de rebus abstrusis non minore cum vanitate, quam superbiâ nugabantur) & huius furfuris alii: nostro verò seculo fanatici illi, qui revelationes iactitabant, ac sese caelestes Prophetas vocabant; Anabaptistae item ac in primis Enthusiastae, Methistae, Weigeliani &c. quorum doctrina fictis ac commentitiis revelationibus magnâ ex parte nititur.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Estius, ut vulgatam versionem in vers. 18. cum textu Graeco in gratiam redigat, veri simile esse statuit; Petrum scripsisse & Interpretem Latinum legisse nonασελγείαις,in dativo plurali, sedασελγείαςin genitivo singulari. 1. cùm Hieronymus libro 2. contra Iovin. legat luxuriae; Augustinus de fide & operibus cap. 25. impudicitiae. 2. Nec desint Graeci Codices, in quibus idem casus legatur. 3. Cùm facilima sit huius lectionis in alteram mutatio, solo iota addito. 4. ac denique vulgata Graecorum lectio commodum sensum non recipiat, nisi coniunctio addatur, & lasciviis. Idem placet Lorino in comment. h. l.

Sed argumentis hisce tantum robur non inest, ut propterea mendum aliquod in Graecis Codicibus statuere cogamur. Nam 1. & Hieronymus & Augustinus saepiculè citant vulgatam versionem. 2. Codices Graeci qui sic legunt, sunt recentiores ad Latinam versionem conformati. 3. Nulla hîc probari potest facta mutatio. 4. Nullâ necessitate coniunctionem καὶ addere cogimur, quia praepositio ἐν illius locum obtinet, ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκός, ἐν ἀσελγείαις h. e. εἰς ἐπιθυμίας σαρκός καὶ ἀσελγείας. Frustra ergo Estius est solicitus est de expositione vocis luxuriae in genitivo positae, quòd sc. referenda illa sit, vel ad propinquius, ut caro luxuriae phrasi Hebraicâ sit idem, quod caro luxuriosa & lasciva h. e. in luxum & lasciviam propensa: vel ad remotius, ut desideria luxuriae dicantur, quatenus voluptatem libidinosam pro obiecto habent; desideria carnis, quatenus ex parte sensitiva non oboediente rationi oriuntur.

2. Idem Estius ad v. 19. sic annotat. Quadrat locus iste (libertatem illis promittentes &c.) in haereticos nostri temporis, qui ex sola fide promittunt hominibus salutem, eamque certissimè consequendam, nullis obstantibus peccatis, quae quis post fidem semel susceptam patraverit. Lorinus eodem modo in comm. h. l. Qui solam exigunt fidem haeretici, summam offerunt libertatem, imò non verentur sanctos viros, quod carnis desideriis non servierint, inter reprobos collocare.

Resp. 1. Si de Calvinianis Estius haec vult intellecta, qui statuunt fidem semel acceptam nullis peccatis amitti posse, nihil ad nos, qui errorem illum detestamur. 2. Nos vero distinguimus inter peccata infirmitatis & malitiae sive contra conscientiam admissa. Illa cum fide consistere posse dicimus, haec vero minimè. 3. Non praedicamus libertatem peccandi vel licentiam carnalem, sed spiritualem libertatem â servitute peccati, & â reatu damnationis illis, qui verâ fide ad Christum liberatorem confugiunt, per Christum partam esse docemus, Ioh. 8. v. 36. Simul autem requirimus â renatis & in Christum credentibus mortificationem carnis h. e. pravarum concupiscentiarum; ac sanctificationum Spiritus, disertè docentes per peccata contra conscientiam fidem & Spiritum sanctum excuti. 4. Disertè etiam docemus, veram & vivam non posse â bonis operibus seiungi, sed per bona opera in lege Dei requisita sese exerere. 5. Falsò igitur nobis tribuitur, quòd ex fide solâ h. e. â bonis operibus separatâ promittamus hominibus salutem, nullis obstantibus peccatis, quae quis post fidem semel susceptam patraverit. Sic enim loquitur August. Confess. art. 12. Damnant (Ecclesiae nostrae) Anabaptistas, qui negant, semel iustificatos posse amittere Spiritum Sanctum.

Observationes. 1. Falsi doctores sunt fontes sine aqua & nubes sine pluvia, quia non proferunt efficaces ex verbo consolationes, quibus territae & afflictae conscientiae possint refici, nec instar aquae fontanae & pluvialis auditores in bonis operibus fertiles reddunt.

2. Gloss. interlin. & ex ea Iohannes Huss in hunc locum Ubi est fons sine aqua, ibi est lutum & limus: sic in istis non est aqua inundantis gratiae, sed lutum inquinantis malitiae. Nec mirum, quia dereliquerunt fontem aquae vitae. Sunt ergo fontes non inundantes, sed potiùs inquinantes, non calorem voluptatis sedantes, sed veriùs suscitantes; non reficientes, sed inficientes; non sanctificantes, sed polluentes.

3. Ut falsi doctores conferuntur fontibus sine aqua & nubibus sine pluvia: ita è contrario pii doctores conferuntur nubibus, salutari pluviâ fecundis. Esai. 60. vers. 8. Moses populi Israëlitici Doctor optabat, ut concresceret in pluviam doctrina sua, & flueret, ut ros, ut imber, ut stillae.Deut. 32. v. 2. Hebraeis non sine mysterio unum idemque verbum ירה significat & docuit & pluit.Ioël. 2. v. 23.Dabit nobis Doctorem iustitiae, & descendere faciet ad nos imbrem matutinum.

4. Quod falsi doctores comparantur nubibus à vento agitatis, illud Beda in comm. h. l. sic explicat, quòd turbinibus Daemonum atque vitiorum exagitentur, quia falsa doctrina est doctrina Daemoniorum1. Tim. 4. v. 1. & seminarium variorum peccatorum. Iohan. Huss in h. l. Nubes ventis agitatae tempestatem excitant & Solis splendorem obfuscant: sic haeretici mentium quietem turbant, seditiones excitant, tenebris errorum Solem iustitiae obfuscant.

5. Poena damnatorum describitur per caliginem tenebrarum, per procellam tenebrarum Iudae v. 13. dicuntur versari in terra tenebrarum & umbra mortis seu mortifera Iob. 10. v. 21. tribuuntur ipsis tenebrae exteriores h. e. extremaeMatth. 8. v. 12.cap. 22. v. 13.cap. 25. v. 30. Per has tenebras denotatur non solùm privatio lucis naturalis, quia infernus est tenebricosus, & horridus carcer, locus tenebrarumIob. 38. v. 19. sed etiam ac cumprimis 1. Caligo Spiritualis, coecitas mentis, ignorantia DEI. Esai. 42. v. 2.Luc. 1. v. 79.Ioh. 1. v. 5. quia damnati in extrema salutaris θεογνωσίας inopia versantur, distituuntur luce divinae cognitionis, habent cor excaecatum, adeoque sunt merae tenebrae. Eph. 5. v. 8. &c. 2. Perversitas voluntatis, proiecta impietas, omnis generis peccata, quae sunt opera tenebrarum. Eph. 5. v. 11. quia in damnatis non est sanata perversitas voluntatis, in qua & cum qua mortui olim fuêre. 3. Omnis generis calamitates, afflictiones & miseriae 2. Sam. 22. v. 26.Psal. 18. v. 29. &c. quia infernus est omnium miseriarum sentina.

4. Regnum Diaboli, quod vocatur potestas tenebrarumEph. 6. v. 12.Col. 1. v. 13. quia Diabolus in damnatos plenum & absolutum dominium obtinebit. 6. Homines flagitiosi in hac vita ambulant in tenebris peccatorum, inde de tenebris vitiorum praecipitantur in tenebras tormentorum. Dionysius Carthusianus in comm. h. l.

7. Tertullianus de praescript. cap. 41. de haereticis in genere sic loquitur. Omnes tument, omnes scientiam pollicentur, antè sunt perfecti Catechumeni quàm edocti. Ipsae mulieres haereticae quàm procaces! quae audeant docere, contendere, exorcismis ugere, curationes repromittere, forsan & tingere. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. Descripsit sermo Apostolicus Iovinianum loquentem buccis tumentibus & inflata verba trutinantem.

8. Hanc fastuosam falsorum doctorum & hypocritarum vaniloquentiam Spiritus sanctus etiam alibi graphicè depingit. 1. Sam. 2. v. 3.multiplicant loqui sublimia gloriantes.Psal. 12. v. 5.linguam suam magnificant.Psal. 73. v. 9.ponunt os in caelum.Psal. 131. v. 1.ambulant in magnis & in mirabilibus super se.

9. Multi peccatorum laqueis, ex quibus per DEI gratiam extricati erant, per falsa dogmata & flagitia iterum involvuntur. Luc. 11. v. 26.

10. Vera libertas Christiana non est carnalis pro lubitu quidvis impune agendi licentia, ut homines secuti & Epicuraei sibi persuadent; talis enim libertas carnalis est potiùs turpisima servitus. Liberi sunt pii, h. e. à servitute peccati, à potestate Diaboli, à maledictione legis & iugo Ceremoniarum Mosaicarum liberati Ioh. 8. v. 32.Rom. 6. v. 18.Gal. 5. v. 1. sed hac libertate non debent ad peccandi licentiam abuti, sed tanquam DEI servi in iustitia & sanctitate ipsi servire debent Luc. 1. v. 75.Rom. 6. v. 19.Gal. 5. v. 13.

11. Nulla turpior ac detestabilior servitus, quàm peccatis & carnis concupiscentiis liberè indulgere. Origenes homil. 23. in Genesin expendens illud Apostolicum Coloss. 2. vers. 14.Delens chirographum &c. sic scribit. Istud chirographum peccatorum nostrorum cautio fuit, unusquisque enim nostrûm in iis, quae de linquit, efficitur debitor & peccati sui literas scribit. Augustinus de honest mulier cap. 30. Quanta iniquitas, ut animam, quam Christus suo sanguine redemit, luxuriosus pro unius horae delectatione Diabolo vendat ac tradat? cuius venditionis syngrapham propriâ subscriptione munitam Diabolo tradit peccator. tract. 41. in Ioh. Erit voluntas tua libera, si fuerit pia, eris liber, sifueris servus; liber peccati servus iustitiae. serm. 13. de verb. Apost. Libera voluntas dicenda non est, quamdiu vincentíbus & vincientibus cupiditatibus est subdita.

12. Peccatum vocatur corruptio, tùm quia Naturam hominis corrumpit, defoedat atque contaminat: tùm quia hominem summo bono privat: tùm quia ad aeternam corruptionem hominem perducit.

13. Captivitas sub Diabolo est iusta peccati poena. Quia enim Diabolus per peccatum primos parentes superavit, inde ipsi cum omnibus posteris facti sunt peccati servi & Diaboli captivi. Augustinus Epist. 28. ad Hieronymum rectè monet, animas hominum, utpote rationales, non ita tradi servituti Daemonum, sicut porcos, qui bruta sunt & Naturâ Angelicâ longè inferiores, sed necessariô hîc intercedere peccatum. Nam etsi mortalis est homo, tamen est etiam rationalis & DEI capax, & ideò non Angelorum servus, sed conservus est, & DEO non per Angelos, sed per se famulatum praestat. Quare quod Diabolus Princeps huius mundi nominatur Iohan. 14. v. 30. & homines capitivos tenere dicitur ad suam voluntatem2. Tim. 2. vers. 26. quodque Christi opere indigemus, ut ex potestate Satanae liberemur, non potest aliunde, quàm ex peccato originem trahere.

14. Ephrem tom. 1. serm. exhort. ad piet. ex hoc loco Apostolico vilitatem peccati, rerumque omnium creatarum, si cum DEO conferantur; colligit, vehementer admirans, si quis sit, qui servire creaturae malit, quàm DEO creatoriRom. 1. v. 25.non solùm idola venerando, sed quodcunque gravius peccatum perpetrando.

15. Augustinus lib. 5. contra Iulian. cap. 13. probat ex h. l. unum peccatum esse poenam alterius peccati. Cùm dicitur, inquit, homo tradi desideriis suis, inde fit reus, quia desertus à DEO cedit eis, atque consentit, vincitur, trahitur, capitur, possidetur: à quo enim quis devictus est, huic & servus addictus est; & fit ei peccatum consequens poena praecedentis peccati.

## 2:18
Connection. 1. The Apostle explains the cause why he compared the false teachers to clouds and mists, namely because they indeed sound proud, but their smoke vanishes into the air.

2. The Apostle amplifies the over-swollen and proud empty-talking of the false teachers by a most pernicious effect, namely that through it men are to follow the concupiscences of the flesh. by enticing and promising them liberty with a vain promise, they cast them down into destruction.

3. He exaggerates the same effect from the antithesis of the former state of those who are ensnared and seduced by false teachers, namely that they had previously escaped the lusts of the vicious flesh, in which they are again entangled through this seduction.

Exposition of the text. ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεξγόμενοι. The Vulgate rendered it, Speaking great swelling words of vanity; or as other codices read, speaking with the pride of vanity. But the former reading agrees more with the Greek text. They are called, however: Great swelling words of vanity, by a Hebrew phrase, proud and puffed-up vanities, for the neuter adjective is placed for the substantive (Thus τὸ δοκίμιον τῆς πίστεως is tried faith 1. Petr. 1. v. 7. ἔσχατον τῶν ἡμερῶν are the last days 2. Petr. 3. v. 3. the slippery of age is slippery age, bitter of cares are bitter cares) and the preposition ὑπὲρ increases the meaning, vehemently boastful, as Erasmus rendered it; or above measure turgid. Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 24, rendered it, swelling words; book 2 against the same, chapter 2, grand. Bede on this passage, They speak grand things, and their whole discourse is pride. John Huss on this passage, He does not say teaching, but speaking, because their doctrine is loquacity, φθέγγεσθαι is to emit a sound. The Syriac rendered that ὑπέρογκα ματαιότητος as [גוחכא דסריקותא] ridicule of vanity, speaking the derision of vanity, for those boastful vain-talkers are accustomed to expose themselves to the mockery and derision of others. Luther Sie reden stoltze Worte / da nichts hinter ist / which beautifully agrees with the word [סריקותא] which signifies inanity and emptiness. The sense therefore is that with swelling words and full of pride, yet vain and empty, they ensnare those to whom they permit whatever they please. In the parallel passage Iudae vers. 16. that is expressed thus: τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα, with which agrees that Ps. 12. v. 5. they magnify their tongue, they crack sesquipedalian words.

Δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἐν ἀσελγείαις. The Vulgate rendered it, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness. But the Greek words properly have, in wantonnesses. Δελεάζειν signifies properly to ensnare and by ensnaring to take, the emphasis of which word we explained above in v. 14. Therefore, the Apostle compares in these words the false teachers with fishermen, who catch fish with a hook; and with bird-catchers, who bait birds, so that they may enclose them in a net. The lusts of the flesh are that bait of evils, by which they entice men. Concerning the word ἀσελγείας we have likewise treated above in v. 2, as also 1. Petr. 4. v. 3. The Syrian rendered it, they entice in the unclean lusts of the flesh. Luth. Sie reitzen durch Unzucht zur Fleischlichen Lust / by which reason ἐν ἀσελγείαις is accepted as placed for δι' ἀσελγειῶν and ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς for εἰς ἐπιθυμίας σαρκός. In the parallel passage Iudae v. 4. that is expressed thus. τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριν μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν they transfer the grace of God into lasciviousness, and therefore from its own proper end into an alien one, they abuse the doctrine concerning the grace of GOD and free remission on account of Christ unto carnal lasciviousness, and under the appearance of Christian liberty they permit others to exercise lusts.

Τούς ὄντως ἀποφυγόντας. The Vulgate rendered it, those who escape for a little. But a double deviation from the Greek text occurs here. 1. ὄντως does not signify a little, but in reality or truly. Erasmus and Vatablus think that the common Interpreter instead of ὄντως read οὗτως, which signifies among other things somehow, or a little. Iohann. 4. v. 6. ἐκαθέζετο οὗτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ. But concerning this signification of the little word οὗτως for a little, it is deservedly doubted. Chrysostom, Theophylact, and Euthymius explain the Johannine passage in two ways. 1. οὗτως i.e. as the road carried him. 2. οὗτως i.e. on the ground without a seat. Others accept δεικτικῶς or μιμητικῶς. There are those who think οὗτως in that place is the same as therefore, and so, on that account, so that the sense may be, that Christ was fatigued both from the labor of a three-day journey, and because the hour was almost the sixth, i.e. midday, and thus the greatest heat of the day, and on that account he sat down at the fountain. But even if that signification of the word οὗτως were granted, it would not yet be proven that the Interpreter read οὗτως, instead of ὄντως in certain Codices, since no copies support this reading. Therefore, some respond more probably that in certain Codices is read ὀλίγως a little or ὀλίγον a little, as in the Complutensian and Royal edition. In the same way read also the Syriac version, which has [במלא קליל] Almost or altogether a little, both the Arabic, and Jerome in book 2 against Jovinian, and Augustine on faith and works chapter 25. But the Greek codices, which read ὀλίγον are fewer and of less proven reliability. For almost all the rest have ὄντως, in which way Luther also translates, Die recht entrunnen waren/ 2. ἀποφυγόντας is not a participle of the present tense, but an aorist having the signification of the past, so that it should be rendered, those who have escaped, in which way also Jerome and Augustine in the stated places receive it. Gagnaeus suspects in vain, that formerly in the Greek text it was written ἀποφεύγοντας in the present, who are escaping. Furthermore, some judge this participle ἀποφυγόντας to be placed absolutely, and therefore either to be understood from verse 20 following τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου or something else similar, concerning which matter what should be determined will appear from the following.

Τούς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους. Vulg. who walk in error. 1. Some refer that to the more remote, namely to the participle φθεγγόμενοι in that sense, that those who entice others with their proud empty talk, walk in error. The Vulgate version seems to go that way, which rendered it in the nominative case, who walk in error. But the Greek text does not admit this exposition, since it is not read in the nominative οἱ ἀναστρεφόμενοι, but in the accusative τούς ἀναστρεφομενούς.

2. Some join that with the verb δελεὰζουσι in that sense, that false teachers entice those who walk in error. But false teachers do not entice those who are erring but those who have escaped idolatry, errors, and the lusts of the flesh, 1. to entangle them again in the same.

3. Some likewise join it with the verb δελεάζουσι, but bring forward another exposition, for they think that by these words is described the state of those of whom the Apostle speaks, after the seduction, so that the sense may be. They had indeed escaped (the pollutions of the world) but after they were seduced by false teachers, they now walk in a most grave error. Luther seems to have followed this sense, because he translates the passage thus. Die jenigen die recht entrunnen waren und nun in Irrihumb wandeln. But in the Greek the particle καὶ, is not added nor is an opposition made between the former and the present state through the inserted particle νῦν.

4. It is therefore more correctly said that this member is governed by the nearest participle ἀποφυγόντας in this sense. They entice those who had truly escaped from those who live in error, and thus through true repentance had escaped the errors of their former conversation, in which way the Syrian also rendered it, they flee from those who live in error.

They are said to live in error, both those who are still unbelievers established in Judaism or Gentilism, and those who, fascinated by heretical opinions, have been carried away into the pathless regions of errors; and those who, by freely and securely indulging in the lusts of the flesh, wander from the way of the divine commandments. From all those, they have fled and separated themselves who were converted to Christ by true faith, but were allowed to be seduced by false teachers.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Exponit Apostolus causam, cur falsos doctores nubibus ac nebulis comparaverit, nimirum quia fastuosa quidem sonent, sed in aërem istorum fumus abeat.

2. Amplificat Apostolus praetumidam ac fastuosam falsorum doctorum vaniloquentiam ab effectu maximè pernicioso, videlicet quòd per illam ad sectandas carnis concupiscentias homines illiciendo & libertatem vanâ pollicatione illis promittendo, in exitium eos praecipitent.

3. Exaggerat eundem effectum ab antithesi pristini status illorum, qui â falsis doctoribus inescantur ac seducuntur, videlicet quod vitiosae carnis concupiscentias priùs effugerint, quibus per hanc seductionem denuò involvantur.

Textus expositio. ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεξγόμενοι. Vulg reddidit, Superba vanitatis loquentes; vel ut alii Codices legunt, superbiâ vanitatis loquentes. Sed prior lectio magis congruit textui Graeco. Dicuntur autem: Superba vanitatis phrasi Hebraeâ superbae ac praetumidae vanitates, adiectivum enim neutrum ponitur pro substantivo (Sic τὸ δοκίμιον τῆς πίστεως est explorata fides 1. Petr. 1. v. 7.ἔσχατον τῶν ἡμερῶν sunt dies novissimi 2. Petr. 3. v. 3.lubricum aetatis est lubrica aetas, amara curarum sunt curae amarae) ac praepositio ὑπὲρ auget significationem, vehementer vastuosa, ut Erasmus reddidit; vel supra modum turgida. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. cap. 24. reddidit, verba tumentia; lib. 2. contra eund. cap. 2. grandia. Beda in h. l. Loquuntur grandia, & totus eorum sermo superbia est. Iohannes Huss. in h. l. Non dicit docentes, sed loquentes, quia doctrina eorum loquacitas est,φθέγγεσθαιest sonum edere. Syrus illud ὑπέρογκα ματαιότητος reddidit [גוחכא דסריקותא]ridiculum vanitatis, derisionem vanitatis loquentes, fastuosi enim illi vaniloqui aliorum ludibrio & irrisioni seipsos exponere solent. Luther. Sie reden stoltze Worte / da nichts hinter ist / quod pulchrè congruit voci [סריקותא] quae inanitatem & vacuitatem significat. Sensus igitur est, quòd verbis tumentibus ac fastu plenis, vanis tamen & inanibus eos inescent, quibus, quicquid ipsis libet, permittunt. In loco parallelo Iudae vers. 16. illud sic effertur: τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα, cum quo congruit illud Ps. 12. v. 5.linguam suam magnificant, crepant sesquipedalia verba.

Δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἐν ἀσελγείαις. Vulg. reddidit, pelliciunt in desideriis carnis luxuriae. Sed Graeca propriè habent, in laciviis.Δελεάζειν significat propriè inescare & inescando capere, cuius verbi emphasin exposuimus superiùs v. 14. Comparat ergò Apostolus his verbis falsos doctores cum piscatoribus, qui hamo pisces capiunt; & aucupibus, qui volucres inescant, ut reti eas concludant. Concupiscentiae carnis sunt esca illa malorum, quâ homines illiciunt. De voce ἀσελγείας itidem egimus superius v. 2. uti etiam 1. Petr. 4. v. 3. Syrus reddidit, pelliciunt in concupiscentiis immundis carnis. Luth. Sie reitzen durch Unzucht zur Fleischlichen Lust / quâ ratione ἐν ἀσελγείαις accipitur positum pro δι' ἀσελγειῶν ac ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς pro εἰς ἐπιθυμίας σαρκός. In loco parallelo Iudae v. 4. illud sic effertur. τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριν μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειανtransferunt Dei gratiam in lasciviam, ac proindè â fine suo proprio in alienum, abutuntur doctrinâ de gratia DEI & gratuita remissione propter Christum ad carnalem lasciviam, ac sub specie libertatis Christianae libidines exercere aliis permittunt.

Τούς ὄντως ἀποφυγόντας. Vulg. reddidit, eos qui paululùm effugiunt. At duplex hîc occurrit â textu Graeco deviatio. 1. ὄντως non significat paululùm, sed reverâ sive verè. Erasmus & Vatablus existimant vulgatum Interpretem proὄντωςlegisseοὗτως,quod significat inter alia utcunque, sive paululùm.Iohann. 4. v. 6.ἐκαθέζετο οὗτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ. Sed de hac significatione voculae οὗτως pro paululùm meritò dubitatur. Chrysostomus, Theophylactus & Euthymius locum Iohannaeum duobus modis explicant. 1. οὗτωςh. e. proutrursus ferebat. 2. οὗτωςh. e. humi sine sede. Alii δεικτικῶς vel μιμητικῶς accipiunt. Sunt, qui putent οὗτωςeo in loco idem esse, quod idcirco, itaque propterea, ut sit sensus, Christum fuisse fatigatum tùm ex labore itineris triduani, tùm quia instabat hora fermè sexta h. e. meridies, adeoque maximus diei aestus, ac propterea consedisse ad fontem. Quòd si vel maximè significatio illa vocis οὗτως concederetur, nondum tamen evictum foret, Interpretem pro ὄντως in quibusdam Codd. legisse οὗτως, cùm nulla exemplaria huic lectioni suffragentur. Quidam ergò probabilius respondent in quibusdam Codd. legi ὀλίγωςparumper velὀλίγονpaululùm, ut in Complutensi ac Regiaeditione Eodem modo legunt tùm versio Syriaca, quae habet [במלא קליל] propemodum seu omnino modicum, tùm Arabica, tùm Hieronymus lib. 2. contra Iovin. & Augustinus de fid. & operibus cap. 25. Sed Graeci Codices, qui legunt ὀλίγον pauciores sunt & fidei minùs probae. Plerique enim omnes habent ὄντως, quo modo etiam Lutherus vertit, Die recht entrunnen waren/ 2. ἀποφυγόντας non est praesentis temporis participium, sed aoristus praeteriti significationem habens, ut sit reddendum, eos qui effugerunt, quo modo etiam Hieronymus & Augustinus dictis locis excipiunt. Gagnaeus frustra suspicatur, olim in textu Graeco scriptum fuisseἀποφεύγονταςin praesenti, qui effugiunt. Caeterùm participium hoc ἀποφυγόντας quidam absolutè positum censent, ac proindè vel subintelligendum ex v. seq. 20. τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου vel aliud quidpiam consimile, quâ de re quid statuendum sit, parebit ex sequentibus.

Τούς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους. Vulg. qui in errore conversantur. 1. Quidam illud referunt ad remorius, videlicet ad participium φθεγγόμενοι sensu eo, quòd qui fastuosâ suâ vaniloquentiâ alios illiciunt, in errore versentur. Eò abire videtur vulgata versio, quae in nominandi casu reddidit, qui in errore conversantur. Sed Graecus textus hanc expositionem non admittit, cùm non legatur in nominativo οἱ ἀναστρεφόμενοι, sed in accusativo τούς ἀναστρεφομενούς.

2. Quidam illud coniungunt cum verbo δελεὰζουσι sensu eo, quod falsi doctores pelliciant eo, qui in errore conversantur. At falsi doctores non pelliciunt eos, qui errant sed qui effugerunt idololatriam, errores & carnis libidines, 1. eos rursus iisdem implicent.

3. Quidam itidem coniungunt cum verbo δελεάζουσι, sed aliam afferunt expositionem, putant enim his verbis describi statum eorum, de quibus loquitur Apostolus, post seductionem, ut sit sensus. Effugerant quidem (mundi inquinamenta) sed postquam â falsis doctoribus seducti sunt, in errore gravissimo iam versantur. Hunc sensum videtur secutus Lutherus, quia locum sic vertit. Die jenigen die recht entrunnen waren und nun in Irrihumb wandeln. Sed in Graeco non additur particula καὶ, nec fit oppositio inter pristinum & praesentem statum per insertam particulam νῦν.

4. Rectiùs ergò dicitur, quòd hoc membrum regatur â participio proximo ἀποφυγόντας hoc sensu. Pelliciunt eos, qui reverâ effugerant illos, qui in errore conversantur, adeoque per veram paenitentiam errores pristinae conversationis effugerant, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit, fugiunt ab illis, qui in errore conversantur.

Dicuntur autem in errore versari, tum qui adhuc infideles sunt in Iudaismo vel gentilismo constituti, tum qui haereticis opinionibus fascinati in errorum avia sunt abrepti; tum qui carnis concupiscentiis liberè ac securè indulgenda â via mandatorum divinorum aberrant. Ab illis omnibus fugerunt ac sese separaverunt, qui verâ fide ad Christum conversi fuêre, sed â falsis doctoribus sale passi fuerunt seduci.

## 2:19
Connection. 1. Just as in the verse immediately preceding he had exaggerated that pernicious effect, that false teachers by their vain talk, by enticing men to follow the lusts of the flesh, precipitate them into destruction, by the antithesis of the former state of those who are seduced by false teachers: so in this verse he exaggerates the same by a description of the present state of those who seduce others, and falsely promise them liberty, namely that they themselves are the slaves of corruption.

He proves that servitude of both the seducers and the seduced from the fact that they allow sin to reign in themselves, from which it follows spontaneously that that liberty which false teachers persuade themselves of, and which they promise to others with great audacity, is not true liberty, but the most miserable servitude of sin, and thus they falsely and mendaciously promise liberty.

Exposition of the text. Ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι αὐτοῖ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορὰς. Vulg. Promising them liberty, when they themselves are the slaves of corruption, The Apostle explains with these words the manner by which false teachers entice those whom they deceive to the luxury of a carnal life, namely that they promise liberty to them, that is, because under the pretext and appearance of the liberty obtained through Christ they introduce a license for crimes and outrages, and thus turn the grace of God into lasciviousnessIudae v. 4. The Apostolic sayings speak concerning this translation of liberty into carnal license Gal. 5. v. 13. For you have been called unto liberty, brethren; only do not give liberty as an occasion to the flesh, that is, beware, lest under the appearance of liberty you loosen the rein for the depraved concupiscences of the flesh 1. Petr. 2. v. 16. As free, and not as having liberty as a cloak of malice.

By φθορὰς, of which the false teachers are said to be slaves, some understand the corruptions of lusts, to which those of whom the Apostle speaks have addicted themselves as if into slavery. But it is more correctly taken in a general sense concerning the entire genus of depraved concupiscence, to which those false teachers indulge, and thus concerning all those vices and outrages of which he had hitherto made them guilty, in which signification the little word φθοράς is used in this very Epistola cap. 1. v. 4. and cap. 2. v. 12.

Ὧ γὰρ τις ἥττηται τούτῷ καὶ δεδούλωται. Vulg. for by whom anyone is overcome, of him he is also a slave. The Greek properly has, to him he is also made a slave, he is reduced into his slavery. August. lib. de fide & operibus cap. 25. cites it thus, to him he is also addicted as a slave. The Apostle had said that those false teachers, who falsely and mendaciously promise liberty to others, are themselves slaves of corruption. He proves that with an argument taken from the law of war. By whom anyone is overcome in war, by him he is reduced into slavery. Now, those false teachers have suffered themselves to be overcome by the Devil through the depraved concupiscences of the flesh. Therefore, they have been reduced by him into the slavery of sin and death. Christ uses almost the same argument Iohann. 8. v. 34. Whoever commits sin is the slave of sin. For there by τὸ committing sin, it is not understood to have or commit sin in any way 1. Iohann. 1. vers. 8. but to subject oneself to sin, to provide dominion to sin, and to be entirely given over to it 1. Iohann. 3. vers. 8. Whoever commits sin in that way, he is a slave of sin; it is not absurd to think that Peter wished to allude to these words of Christ in this place. Paul uses the same argument Rom. 6. v. 16. Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as slaves to obey, you are the slaves of him whom you obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness.

To which also, for the sake of illustration, the words of the Emperor Justinian may be referred, Instit. de iure person. lib. 4. §. 1. By the law of nations, slavery was thus introduced, while victors, having captured enemies in war, whom they could have killed, spared their lives and changed death into slavery.

The word ἥττηται the Syrian rendered by [זכא] which to the Chaldeans signifies to be pure and clean, but to the Syrians signifies to conquer, and thus the same as the Hebrew נצח whence it is that the LXX Interpreters Psal. 51. v. 6. translated the Hebrew תזכה that you may be pure by νικήση and you may conquer, which the Apostle retained. Rom. 3. v. 4.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Sicut in versu proximè praecedente perniciosum illum effectum, quod falsi doctores per suam vaniloquentiam ad sectandas carnis concupiscentias homines illiciendo in exitium eos praecipitant, exaggeraverat ab antithesi pristini status illorum, qui â falsis doctoribus seducuntur: ita in hoc versic. eundem exaggerat descriptione praesentis status illorum, qui alios seducunt, iisdemque libertatem falsò promittunt, videlicet quòd ipsimet sint servi corruptionis.

Servitutem illam tùm seducentium, tùm seductorum, probatex eo, quod peccatum in se patiantur regnare, ex quo sponte sequitur, quod libertas illa, quam falsi doctores sibi persuadent, & quam aliis magnà audaciâ promittunt, non sit vera libertas, sed miserrima peccati servitus, adeoque falsò & mendaciter libertatem promittant.

Textus expositio. Ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι αὐτοῖ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορὰς. Vulg. Libertatem illis promittentes cùm ipsi sint servi corruptionis, Exponit Apostolus his verbis modum, quo falsi doctores ad carnalis vitae luxuriam, eos, quos decipiunt, pelliciunt, videlicet quod libertatem illis promittant, h. e. quòd sub praetextu ac specie libertatis per Christum partae licentiam scelerum ac flagitiorum introducant, sicque Dei gratiam in luxuriam transferantIudae v. 4. De hac libertatis in carnalem licentiam translatione loquuntur dicta Apostolica Gal. 5. v. 13.Vos enim in libertatem vocati estis, fratres tantùm ne libertatem in occasionem carni sc. detis h. e. cavete, ne sub specie libertatis pravis carnis concupiscentiis frenum laxetis 1. Petr. 2. v. 16.Quasi liberi & non quasi velamen habentes malitiae libertatem.

Per φθορὰς, cuius servi dicuntur falsi doctores, quidam intelligunt libidinum corruptelas, quibus illi, de quibus Apostolus agit, sese velut in servitutem addixerint. Sed rectiùs in genere accipitur de universo pravae concupiscentiae genere, cui falsi illi doctores indulgent, adeoque de omnibus illis vitiis & flagitiis, quorum eos hactenus reos fecerat, in qua significatione vocula φθοράς usurpatur in hac ipsa Epistola cap. 1. v. 4. & cap. 2. v. 12.

Ὧ γὰρ τις ἥττηται τούτῷ καὶ δεδούλωται. Vulg. â quo enim quis victus est, huius & servus est. Graeca propriè habent, huic & servus factus est, in illius servitutem redactus est. August. lib. de fide & operibus cap. 25. sic citat, huic & servus addictus est. Dixerat Apostolus, falsos illos doctores, qui aliis libertatem falsò & mendaciter promittunt, ipsosmet esse corruptionis servos. Illud probat argumento ex iure belli desumto. A quo quis in bello superatur, ab eo in servitutem redigitur. Iam verò falsi illi doctores passi sunt â Diabolo per pravas carnis concupiscentias sese superari. Ergo ab eo in servitutem peccati & mortis sunt redacti. Eodem ferè argumento utitur Christus Iohann. 8. v. 34.Qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Ibi enim per τὸfacere peccatum, non intelligitur quovis modo habere, vel facere peccatum 1. Iohann. 1. vers. 8. sed peccato sese subiicere, peccato dominium praebere, ipsique totum deditum esse 1. Iohann. 3. vers. 8. Qui eo modo facit peccatum, is est peccati servus; ad quae Christi verba Petrum hoc loco alludere voluisse, haud absurdè cogitatur. Eodem argumento utitur Paulus Rom. 6. v. 16.Nescitis, quoniam cui exhibetis vos servos ad oboediendum, servi estis eius, cui oboeditis, sive peccati ad mortem, sive oboeditionis adiustitiam.

Quò etiam referri possunt illustrationis causâ verba Iustiniani Imperat. Instit. de iure person. lib. 4. §. 1. Iure gentium sic inducta est servitus, dum victores hostibus bello captis, quos occidere poterant, vitam condonârunt, necemque in servitutem commutârunt.

Verbum ἥττηται Syrus reddidit per [זכא] quod Chaldaeis significat purum ac mundum esse, Syris verò significat vincere, adeoque idem, quod Hebrae is נצח unde est, quod LXX. Interpp. Psal. 51. v. 6. Hebraeum תזכה purus sis verterunt per νικήση & vincas, quod Apostolus retinuit. Rom. 3. v. 4.

## 2:20
Connection. 1. After the Apostle had hitherto dealt with false teachers and seducers, he now proceeds to deal with the seduced, whose condition he shows to be far worse than it was before their conversion.

2. Some think that the Apostle proposes a certain dilemma, by which he wished to prove that those lying teachers are slaves. For either they have not yet truly known the power of Christ, and therefore they are slaves of sin and keep their disciples like themselves; or they have indeed known it, but having returned to their former ways they sin willingly, and thus they undergo a greater and more severe judgment. But the series of the text shows that the Apostle is not dealing with the seducers in these words, but with the seduced.

Exposition of the text. εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου &c. Vulg. For if they, having escaped the defilements of the world. But το αποφυγοντες, is an aorist participle, having the meaning of past time, as also in v. 18 preceding; therefore it must be translated, after they have escaped,

Τὰ μιάσματα are defilements; filthiness, pollutions. This little word does not occur elsewhere in the N. T., but the cognate μίασμος is used in this very chapter v. 10.Iudith. 9. v. 2. concerning defilement through the crime of fornication.v. 5. concerning defilement through the shedding of blood.Ezech. 33.v. 31. among the LXX Interpreters, it is used for defilement of the heart through avarice.Ierem. 32. v. 34. it is used for שקוצים for any more serious and abominable crimes. Budaeus, from Demosthenes and Lucian, shows that μίασμα is a piacular sacrifice, μιάστωρ, for he is one who, when he has contaminated himself with some crime, and has thus contracted a piacular guilt, renders others as if by a certain contagion liable to the same. This meaning fits this passage beautifully, because impious men, denoted by the name world in this place, are before GOD as if a piacular sacrifice, infecting and contaminating others by the contagion of their conversation. To physicians, μιάσματα are called seeds of pestilential plague in corrupt air. This meaning can likewise be accommodated to this place. For just as μιάσματα those creep secretly and where they fall upon a disposed subject, they infect it with their contagion: so also the seeds of every kind of vice and crime creep secretly in the world, which contaminate and infect men prone to those vices with easy business.

The Syrian rendered by [טנפותא] which signifies filth, uncleanness, pollution.

Ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. The Vulgate renders in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. But in the Greek, our is not added, but it is said simply in the knowledge of the Lord, which ἐμφατικώτερον. Moreover, the Apostle understands by ἐπίγνωσιν that salutary and saving knowledge of Christ, which we otherwise call justifying faith, since through it we escape the pollutions of the world and are cleansed from them. In the same signification the word ἐπιγνώσεως is used chap. 1. of this Epist. v. 2. 3. and 8. and the little word γνώσεως chap 3. v. 18.

Τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται. The Vulgate being entangled again in these, they are overcome. In the Greek is added the particle δὲ, which does not abound idly, as it seems to some, but is to be explained adversatively, but again they are entangled in them, namely, ensnared and seduced by false teachers.

The participle ἐμπλακέντες is very emphatic, for they are called ἐμπλέκεσθαι who are entangled in certain tricks and snares. Lucilius lib. 2. Epigramm. ἀράγνῃ τοὺς πόδας ἐμπλεχθεὶς ὕπτιος ἐκρεματο, entangled and ensnared by the feet in a spider's web. 2. Tim. 2. v. 4. he is called ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις ἐμπλέκεσθαι who is so involved and entangled in the business of life, that he cannot freely serve him to whom he has dedicated his labor. The LXX use it Prov. 28. v. 18. for נפל to fall, for those animals which are bound by tricks and snares fall on the way, which can be beautifully applied to these relapsed ones.

The verb ἡττῶνται has respect to the preceding verse in which it is said, that by whom anyone is overcome, to him also he is addicted into slavery. It signifies, therefore, that those seduced are again reduced into the slavery of sin and the Devil, from which they had gone out, and therefore it describes the double state of those of whom it treats. 1. Of conversion and παλιγγενεσίας that ἀληθῶς καὶ ὄντως, not δοξαστικῶς, truly and really, not putatively, they had escaped the pollutions of the world. 2. Of aversion and ἀποστασίας, that they were again entangled in those pollutions, turned backward from the holy commandment and were again overcome by the Devil through sin. γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων. The Vulgate the latter things are made worse for them than the former. The Greek properly has, The last things are made worse for them than the first. The Syrian; their end is made worse than the beginning. The Apostle took this from Matt. 12. v. 44.Luke 11. v. 26. where the same words are used by Christ.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Post quam Apostolus hactenus de falsis doctoribus ac seductoribus egerat, iam porrò de seductis agit, quorum conditionem longè deteriorem esse ostendit, quàm ante conversionem erat.

2. Quidam existimant, Apostolum dilemma quoddam proponere, quo evincere voluerit, magistros illos mendaces esse servos. Etenim aut Christi nondum verè noverunt virtutem, ideoque servi sunt peccati ac sibi similes discipulos conservant; aut noverunt quidem, sed ad priora reversi sponte peccant, sic verò maius graviusque iudicium subeunt. Sed series textus ostendit, non de seductoribus, sed de seductis Apostolum in hisce verbis agere.

Textus expositio. εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου &c. Vulg. Si enim refugientes coinquinationes mundi. Sed το αποφυγοντες, est participium aoristum, temporis praeteriti significationem habens, uti etiam in v. 18. praeced. vertendum igitur, postquam effugerunt,

Τὰ μιάσματα sunt inquinamenta; faeditates, sordes. Haec vocula alibi in N. T. non occurrit, sed cognatum μίασμος in hoc ipso cap. v. 10.Iudith. 9. v. 2. usurpatur de coinquinatione per flagitium scortationis.v. 5.de coinquinatione per effusionem sanguinis.Ezech. 33.v. 31. apud LXX. Interpp. de coinquinatione cordis per avaritiam.Ierem. 32. v. 34. usurpatur pro שקוצים pro quibusvis gravioribus & abominandis flagitiis. Budaeus ex Demosthene & Luciano ostendit, μίασμαesse piaculum,μιάστωρ,ením est, qui cum scelere aliquo sese contaminârit, atque ita piaculum contraxerit, caeteros velut contagione quadam eidem obnoxios reddit. Haec significatio pulchrè huic loco congruit, quia homines impii, mundi nomine h. l. denotati, coram DEO sunt quasi piaculum, contagione conversationis suae alios in ficientes & contaminantes. Medicis μιάσματα dicuntur seminaria luis pestilentialis in aëre corrupto. Haec significatio itidem huic loco accommodari potest. Quemadmodum enim μιάσματα illa occultè serpunt & ubi incidunt in subiectum dispositum, contagione suâ illud in ficiunt: ita quoque seminaria omnis generis vitiorum & flagitiorum in mundo occultè serpunt, quae homines ad vitia illa pronos facili negotio contaminant & inficiunt.

Syrus reddidit per [טנפותא] quod significat spurcitiem, immunditiem, pollutionem.

Ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Vulg. redd. in cognitione Domini nostri & Salvatoris Iesu Christi. Sed in Graeco non additur nostri, verùm simpliciter dicitur in cognitione Domini, quod ἐμφατικώτερον. Intelligit autem Apostolus per ἐπίγνωσιν Christi salutarem illam & salvificam Christi cognitionem, quam aliàs vocamus fidem iustificantem, quippe per quam coinquinationes mundi effugimus & ab illis mundamur. In eadem significatione usurpatur vox ἐπιγνώσεωςcap. 1. huius Epist. v. 2. 3. & 8. ac vocula γνώσεωςcap 3. v. 18.

Τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται. Vulg. his rursus implicati superantur. In Graeco additur particula δὲ, quae non otiosè red undat, ut quibusdam videtur, sed exponenda est adversativè, rursum autem illis implicantur, inescati scil. ac seducti à falsis doctoribus.

Participium ἐμπλακέντες est valde emphaticum, ἐμπλέκεσθαι enim dicuntur, qui tricis & laqueis quibusdam implicantur. Lucilius lib. 2. Epigramm. ἀράγνῃ τοὺς πόδας ἐμπλεχθεὶς ὕπτιος ἐκρεματο,implicatus & irretitus pedibus telâ araneae.2. Tim. 2. v. 4.ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις ἐμπλέκεσθαι dicitur, qui vitae negotiis ita involvitur & implicatur, ut non possit liberè servire ei, cui operam suam addixit. LXX. utuntur eo Prov. 28. v. 18. pro נפלcadere, quae enim animalia tricis ac pedicis constringuntur, in via concidunt, id quod pulchrè ad hosce relapsos accommodari potest.

Verbum ἡττῶνται respectum habet ad versum praeced. in quo dicitur, quod à quo quis victus, ei quoque in servitutem addictus sit. Significat ergo, seductos illos iterum in servitutem peccati & Diaboli, ex qua exierant, redigi, ac proinde geminum illorum, de quibus agit, describit statum. 1. Conversionis & παλιγγενεσίας quòd ἀληθῶς καὶ ὄντως, non δοξαστικῶς, verè & realiter, non putativè mundi inquinamenta effugerint. 2. Aversionis & ἀποστασίας, quòd inquinamentis illis rursum fuerint impliciti, retrorsum à sancto mandato conversi & à Diabolo per peccatum iterum fuerint victi. γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων. Vulg. facta sunt illis posteriora deteriora prioribus. Graeca propriè habent, facta sunt illis postrema peiora primis. Syrus; factus est finis eorum peior principio. Desumsit hoc Apostolus ex Matth. 12. v. 44.Luc. 11. v. 26. ubieadem à Christo usurpantur verba.

## 2:20-22 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Whether the Apostle is speaking about the seducers, or indeed about the seduced? Resp. Some affirm the former, since in the preceding verses there was speech about them, and since they themselves in Baptism had renounced the pleasures of this age, and through this Sacrament of initiation had been reborn, but afterwards had been again entangled in the defilements of false doctrine and impious life. But it is more correctly said that the Apostle is dealing with the seduced in this place. 1. Because in v. 18. the participle ἀποφυγόντες is used concerning the seduced, which the Apostle repeats in this v. 20.: and just as he says there, that they had escaped those who live in error: so in this place he says, that they had escaped the defilements of the world. 2. Lest anyone should think that false teachers and seducers are only servants of corruption, and draw destruction upon themselves, he shows that for those also who allow themselves to be seduced by false teachers, a most grave danger likewise looms, since they are not only dragged back into the slavery of sin, from which they had been freed, but are also thrust into a worse state than that in which they had been before their conversion to Christianity. It is to be noted, however, that the Apostle is not speaking here of just any seduced persons, nor of just any lapses by which a man is sometimes preoccupied, Gal. 6. v. 1., but rather of apostates, who, casting off sincere doctrine, afterwards blaspheme the same, and of those Epicurean contemners who, having cast off all shame, surrender themselves entirely to carnal concupiscences.

Q. 2. What are those defilements of the world by which the seduced are again entangled. Resp. They are 1. false and erroneous dogmas, which the Spirit that is in the world 1. Iohann. 4. v. 4. Prince of the world Iohan. 14. v. 30. God of this age 2. Cor. 4. v. 4. inspires in false teachers, so that through them they may seduce others. 2. Foul lusts and outrages of every kind, which infect others with their contagion. 3. Those various scandals and perverse examples which are everywhere obvious in the world, and with easy business draw others to imitation. Sap. 4. v. 11. He was snatched away, lest malice should change his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.

vers. 12.For the fascination of trifling obscures good things, and the inconstancy of concupiscence overturns a mind not evil.Rom. 16. vers. 18. concerning false teachers the Apostle says, that by χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐλογίας they seduce the hearts τῶν ἀκάκων.

Q. 3. How are the pollutions of the world escaped through the knowledge of Christ or faith in Christ? Resp. 1. The knowledge of Christ arises from the word of the Gospel. That indeed is the saving instrument, through which God cleanses us from all the filth of error and sin. Ioh. 15. v. 3.You are clean because of the word which I have spoken to you. 2. Faith in Christ seeks and finds perfect cleanliness, by which a man can stand before the judgment of GOD. Actor. 15. v. 9.purifying their hearts by faith. 3. While by faith the Holy Spirit is given to man, who begins to purge the filth of sin, and kindles in his heart a zeal for true holiness and cleanliness. 1. Cor. 6. v. 11.you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our GOD, where the Apostle opposes washing to filth, sanctification to pollution, justification to guilt; and attributes those benefits to Christ as the meriting cause, and to the Holy Spirit as the dispensing and applying cause.

Q. 4. Whence is the condition of those, who are again entangled in the pollutions of the world, which they had escaped, rendered worse? Resp. It happens.

1. Because of the condition of the sinner. He who sins in the light of faith and deserts the way of truth once acknowledged, he sins no longer out of ignorance, but knowingly and willingly. Now indeed the sin which one commits knowingly and willingly is graver than that which proceeds from ignorance. Luc. 12. v. 47.That servant, who knew the will of his Lord, and did not prepare himself, nor did his will, shall be beaten with many stripes. v. 48. But he who did not know and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few.

2. Because of the accumulation of sin. He who sins after Baptism and conversion, he adds ingratitude to the remaining sins, which adds no mediocre weight to them. Chrysostom homil. on the fall of the first man. Do not sin after forgiveness, do not be wounded after the cure, do not be dirtied after grace. Think, O man, that the fault is graver after forgiveness, the renewed wound is more painful after the cure, it is more troublesome for a man to be dirtied after grace. Wherefore he is ungrateful for the indulgence, who sins after forgiveness; he is unworthy of holiness, who himself, after he has been cured, wounds himself; nor does he deserve to be cleansed, who defiles himself after grace. And afterwards. It is grave for an instructed man to commit a fault; graver for an absolved man to sin; worse is the servant who offends his patron after liberty has been given; ungrateful for benefits is he who despises the giver with the arrogance of pride. Bernard, sermon 1 on the seven mercies, col. 280. Ingratitude is a peremptory thing, an enemy of grace, a foe of salvation. Ingratitude is an enemy of the soul, a dissipation of virtues, a loss of benefits. Ingratitude is a poisonous and fetid herb growing from three roots, lying, pride, injustice, whence also through ingratitude GOD is affected with the greatest ignominy, as is gathered fromLuke 17. v. 18.

3. On account of the loss of precious gifts. He who sins against conscience after illumination and conversion, and is again entangled in the pollutions of the world, he loses the grace of GOD, true faith, the Holy Spirit, righteousness, and eternal life. But the more precious those gifts are, the worse is their loss and the more deteriorated is the condition of him who has lost them. Basil, in the 289th of the shorter rules, notes, when someone relapses into sin, it is a sign that he had not previously departed from sin entirely, nor had he extirpated its root, but that the appetite and concupiscence of sin still resided secretly in his mind.

4. On account of the attainment of danger. He who sins after illumination and conversion either falls into apostasy in reality, or can fall into it with easy effort. For although not all who are again entangled in the pollutions of the world through sins against conscience immediately lose the knowledge of the truth at the same time and fall into heresies or apostasy, nevertheless they expose themselves to the danger of losing that knowledge. For since having lost a good conscience they have made shipwreck concerning the faith,1 Tim. 1. v. 19. from there it can happen with easy effort that whatever saving knowledge still remains in them is extinguished by the darkness of sins. Augustine, book 8 of the Confessions, chapter 5, says, from a perverse will was made lust; while lust is served, custom is made; while custom is not resisted, necessity is made. That is indeed true even before conversion, but much more so after a relapse.

5. On account of a more difficult conversion. Just as, as physicians teach, ὑποστροφὴ or relapse, that is, a disease renewed after an interval, as it were breaking out again, brings a far greater danger than the beginnings of diseases: so also in spiritual diseases the same thing we see happen in practice, namely that the healing of those who, having been freed by Christ from the spiritual diseases of the soul, relapse into them again, becomes more difficult. Satan, once expelled, if he is let back in through sins, brings with him seven other spirits who are more wicked than he is, who guard that atrium far more strongly than before. (Salmero and Cornelius à Lapide apply the sayings Heb. 6. v. 4.ch. 10. v. 26. to this. But those deal properly and directly with a certain special sin, namely the sin against the Holy Spirit.) And these are the principal reasons why Peter pronounces that the condition of those who are again entangled in the pollutions of the world, which they had escaped, is worse than that of those who have never known the way of righteousness. John Huss in his commentary on this passage assigns these causes. The first is the weakness for rising again, which is increased in the relapser, just as it happens in a relapsing bodily infirmity. 2. The breaking of the covenant entered into with the Lord. 3. A more grievous subjection to enemies. 4. The mocking of divine mercy. 5. Cruelty inflicted upon one's own soul. 6. The grieving of the Holy Spirit and the heavenly court, and the rejoicing of the demons. 7. Ingratitude for the forgiveness and grace already given and the glory promised. 8. Because the relapser, as much as is in him, repeats the passion of Christ.

Q. 5. What is the occasion of the proverbs brought forward by the Apostle? 1. The origin of the former proverb is this. A dog, when it has gorged itself too greedily on food, by eating a certain herb indeed induces vomiting, and by this --cto empties its stomach; but as it is an animal by nature imm --m and voracious, a little later it returns to the food rejected through vomiting, and laps it up again. Similar to such foul and shameless dogs are those who allow themselves to be entangled again in the pollutions of the world, which they had escaped through conversion to the faith of Christ. 2. The origin of the latter proverb is this. The pig is a friend of mud, according to Pliny book 8, Nat. Hist. ch. 51, Varro book 2, ch. 4, Columella book 7, ch. 9, Alexander of Aphrodisias book 1, q. 141. The unclean dog would have lived, or the sow a friend to mud, sings Horace book 2, Epist. 2. Hence it often happens that, having been washed and cleaned by the hands of men, it immediately returns to the mud and wallows in it. Similar likewise to those unclean pigs are those who, having been washed and cleaned from the impurities of this age, are again involved in the same. For both similitudes are accommodated to the same object and to the same goal.

Ἐναντιοφάνεια. It were better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But not to know the way of righteousness is not a good, but an evil. Resp. 'Better' is said in this place as that which is less evil, for two evils are compared, of which one is worse than the other. Others express that thus: 'Better' is said not positively, as if it were a greater good, since it is not even a good: but negatively, because it is a lesser evil, that is, the guilt of the unbeliever who is ignorant is less than that of the believer who knows, but afterwards relapses, whence the punishment also will be less. This explanation is gathered from the preceding verse, in which τα ἔσχατα of those men are called χείρανα πρώτων. Therefore also τὰ πρῶτα they were κακὰ. The Syriac has the word [פקח] it would be useful, it would be profitable for them, so that regard is had to the greater punishment of those who relapse and apostatize, just as Christ says concerning his betrayer, Matth. 26. v. 24. It had been good for that man if he had not been born.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. If those who through the knowledge of Christ have escaped the pollutions of the world can be entangled again in the same, it follows that Christ also suffered and died for those who, entangling themselves in the pollutions of the world, are involved in eternal destruction. The reason for the connection is this, because those who through the acknowledgment of Christ have escaped the pollutions of the world, they also were made partakers of the fruit of the passion and death of Christ, since deliverance from the pollutions of the world pertains to the fruits of the passion and death of Christ. But for those who have been made partakers of the fruit of the passion and death of Christ, Christ altogether suffered and died.

Polanus objects, that the knowledge of Christ is twofold, general and special; that in this place the discourse is not about special, but about general knowledge of Christ, such as can exist even in the demons themselves Marc. 1. v. 23.

Resp. The discourse here is about such a knowledge of Christ through which the pollutions of the world are escaped. But the pollutions of the world are not escaped through general knowledge, or through merely historical faith, but through special knowledge, through the fiducial apprehension of the merit of Christ.

2. If those who have escaped the pollutions of the world can be entangled again in the same, it follows that the regenerate can fall into sins against conscience, and through them lose faith and the grace of God again.

1. Tossanus objects, here it is a matter only of the recognition and confession of the truth, which may also fall to hypocrites. I answer: The Apostle attributes to those, whom he says are again entangled in the pollutions of the world: 1. The knowledge of Christ. 2. The knowledge of the way of righteousness. 3. An escape from the pollutions of the world, or a liberation from those pollutions. 4. He says of them that they turn from that which was delivered to them, the holy commandment. 5. He compares them to dogs returning to their vomit and to swine to the wallowing in the mire, all of which show that they had emerged from the mire of crimes by true faith in Christ, had cast off filth from themselves, and had been liberated from the pollutions of the world, to which sins especially pertain.

2. Others object, not all in whom some external amendment of morals appears and a departure from idolatry, are immediately the elect. I answer: 1. None of us says this; indeed, we say more, that not all in whom some external amendment of morals appears and a departure from idolatry, are immediately reborn, although by the law of charity they are held to be such. 2. But this is what we say, that those whom the Apostle in this place says are again entangled in the pollutions of the world, were truly reborn, because he pronounces of the same ones that they had previously escaped those pollutions through the knowledge of Christ, and indeed ὄντως, as is held in v. 18. 3. It is false what the Calvinists maintain, that all who are truly reborn are elect, and because these, of whom the Apostle speaks, were not elect, they infer from that that they were also not reborn. For the term of the reborn extends more widely than that of the elect, since while all the elect are indeed reborn, not all the reborn are elect. πρῶτον ψεῦδος consists in this, that with a strong, but nevertheless vain imagination, they have persuaded themselves that true faith is given to none except those elected by an absolute decree of God, and that faith once given cannot be lost again.

3. Augustine in the book De Fide et Operibus, chapter 24, refutes from this Apostolic passage those who promised salvation through fire to those who, even while believing, live most wickedly. What, he says, is still promised against this most manifest truth, a condition and something better for those who have known the way of righteousness, that is, the Lord Christ, and live wickedly, as if they had not known it at all, when it is most openly said: It was better for them not to know the way of righteousness, than after knowing it to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them. And afterwards: Therefore it is not promised the punishment of fire is transitory for those living basely and wickedly, because they knew the way of righteousness, for whom it would have been better not to know it, as the most truthful Scripture testifies.

4. Παραδόσεως the word in v. 21. is used concerning the doctrine of the Apostles, which they first preached by living voice, and afterwards by the will of God reduced into Scripture. Therefore, the true παράδοσις Apostolic is contained in Scripture, not in the word ἀγράφῳ, which the Papists have fabricated.

Ἐηδίκησις. 1. Estius gathers from v. 20, that a man imbued with faith and charity cannot be certain of his salvation, since faith and charity once possessed can be lost. Resp. 1. We concede that faith and charity once possessed can be lost, but we deny that uncertainty of salvation follows from that. 2 For we distinguish between present salvation and the fullest possession of the same, which will follow on the day of judgment. Present salvation is obtained by all who truly believe in Christ and are justified before GOD through faith. John 3. v. 36. He who believes in the Son has eternal life. Romans 4. v. 6. David μακαρισμὸν says that it is of that man, to whom GOD imputes righteousness without works. where observe, δικαίωσιν & μακαρισμὸν is taken by the Apostle as ἰσοδυναμοῦντα. 1. John 5. verse 11. GOD has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. verse 12. He who has the Son, has life. verse 13. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of GOD, that you have eternal life. If, therefore, those who truly believe can be certain of justification and the grace of GOD, as they absolutely can, then they can also be certain of present salvation. 3. As regards the certainty of the fullest possession of future salvation, we distinguish between absolute certainty and conditional certainty. Although absolute certainty is not given concerning the fullest possession of future salvation, nevertheless a conditional certainty is given concerning it, which we have explained above in the exposition of chap. 1. verse 10. 4. Between absolute certainty, i.e., that which depends on the absolute decree of election, which the Calvinists defend, and conjectural certainty, i.e., the uncertain persuasion which the Papists defend, there is a middle ground, namely conditional certainty, which has respect to the means through which GOD preserves in faith and leads to salvation.

2.
