Lorinus gathers from v. 21, that the mercy of God shines forth even in this, that the Gospel is not announced to all, lest those who do not believe should bear a heavier judgment, although the justice of the same is also to be admired, in that He did not wish it to be preached to many, who, if it had been preached to them, would have believed and brought forth fruit, as Tyre and Sidon.Matth. 11. v. 21. 22. Resp. 1. That the Gospel is not actually preached to certain peoples is not properly to be attributed to divine mercy, but to divine justice, because on account of the preceding contempt of the word, committed by their ancestors, their descendants are deprived of that preaching. 2. Although those to whom the Gospel has been actually preached, and yet who were unwilling to believe it, bear a heavier judgment than those to whom it was never preached, this is nevertheless not the true cause on account of which some are deprived of the actual preaching of the Gospel, but rather that which we have just explained.

3. Matth. 11. v. 21. 22. Christ is not speaking of the ordinary means of conversion, namely of the preaching of the word, but of that extraordinary benefit which includes an abundance of miracles and preaching in the very person of Christ.

3. From the fact that Peter says, some are turned from the holy commandment which was delivered unto them.v. 21. the Papists seem to be able to gather, that the Gospel, properly speaking, is a law, and therefore a doctrine of works. Resp. 1. By the name of commandment the Apostle understands the whole doctrine of Christ, or, which is the same thing, the Gospel γενικῶς taken, in which no one of us denies that the doctrine of works is contained. 2. The Gospel εἰδικῶς taken teaches faith in Christ, which we do not deny is required by divine command in a certain respect. 1. Iohann. 3. v. 23.And this is the commandment of GOD, that we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as he gave us commandment. 3. Although the Gospel does not directly and properly require works, yet it requires them consequently. For because true faith, which the Gospel requires, is not, and cannot be, without good works, thence the Gospel, by requiring faith, also consequently requires good works, as the fruits and testimonies of faith, so that nevertheless the Gospel, properly speaking, is not a doctrine of works and the norm and rule of the same, but a law distinguished from the Gospel. 4. Hence Augustine in his book on faith and works, chapter 25, writes thus concerning this commandment. For neither is that holy commandment to be understood in this place, by which It is commanded that we believe in God, although the whole is contained in that very thing, if we understand that faith of believers which works through love, but he openly expressed what he meant by the holy commandment that is by which it is commanded that, withdrawing from the defilements of this world, we live with a chaste conversation. For he says, not fleeing the ignorance of God, or fleeing the infidelity of the age or something of that sort, but the defilements of the world, in which is certainly every uncleanness of shameful acts. 4. The Novatians wished to gather from this place that for those who, after having received Baptism, deny the acknowledged truth in a time of persecution out of infirmity or fear of danger, the doors of grace, even if they knock upon them most earnestly in true repentance, are closed. Resp. 1. Peter, according to the opinion of some, does not treat here of just any fall, but of that voluntary ἀποστασία, which is done from a set purpose and is joined with blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, of which it is also treated in Hebr. 6. v. 4. and cap. 10. v. 26.. For those who in that manner fall away from the acknowledged truth out of voluntary malice are, by the just judgment of God, delivered into a reprobate mind and do not perform repentance, but continue in their blasphemies, and therefore do not arrive at grace. 2. But it is more correctly said that Peter is treating not only of the sin against the Holy Spirit, but of any more serious sins committed out of malice; therefore we answer that Peter indeed pronounces the condition of those who are again entangled in the defilements of the world, which they had escaped, to be worse, but he by no means adds that the way to repentance is not again open to them. 3. Nay rather, just as all promises are to be understood with the condition of faith, so all threats are to be understood with the condition of repentance.

Observations. 1. There are two kinds of spiritual defilements, of doctrine and of life. The defilements of doctrine are errors fighting against the divinely revealed doctrine of the Gospel. The defilements of life are pursuits and actions fighting against the norm of the divine law. We are freed from both kinds of spiritual defilements through the knowledge of Christ, inasmuch as it embraces not only notice and assent, but also trust, and with which the sanctification of the Spirit is joined in an individual bond.

2. Because it happens that some, after liberation from the defilements of the world, are again entangled in the same, therefore, having shaken off carnal security, let us walk cautiously and solicitously in the true fear of God. I have washed the feet my feet, how shall I defile them? says the Spiritual Spouse of Christ Cant. 5. v. 3. The same must be the voice of all the pious. Cyprian, book 3 to Quitinus. That he who has been baptized also loses the grace which he has attained, unless he preserves his innocence, is said in the Gospel according to John cap. 5. v. 14. Behold, you are made whole, sin no more, lest something worse happen to you. Jerome in his Epistle to Furia. Do brute animals and wandering birds not fall into the same snares and nets, and shall man, endowed with reason, fall again into the same snares of Satan which he once escaped?

3. To this pious solicitude of avoiding falls, we ought especially to be stirred by the fact that, as the Apostle teaches, the condition of those is worse who, after they have received the health of the soul from GOD, sin again and fall into a relapse. Bernard, sermon 3 on the Canticles, col. 500. If I shall again defile my feet which I had washed, will it be of any value to have washed anything? I lay for a long time, filthy with every kind of vice, in the mire of dregs, but it will undoubtedly be worse for one who relapses than for one who lies there. I remember that He who made me whole said to me: Behold, you are made whole, go, sin no more from now on, lest something worse happen to you, etc. For such a one I am not entirely content with the former grace, by which I am already penitent for my evils, unless I also receive a second, namely, that I may bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, and henceforth not return to my vomit. Dionysius the Carthusian on this passage. Just as from such a washing, after he returns to the mud, a pig is rendered filthier than he had been before: so from a relapse a man is more gravely defiled.

4. The first temple of Solomon was completed in seven years 1. Reg. 6. v. 38. but the second temple of Zerubbabel was built up only in the space of forty-six years. Ioh. 2. v. 20. Bede, book 2 on Ezra, chapter 8, mystically applies this thus. It is to be noted that Solomon completed the first temple in the very great peace of his kingdom, in a short time, with no one opposing; but now the sons of the transmigration, having destroyed it on account of their sins, insisting with great compunction of heart upon long labor, and very often delayed by enemies, at length, divinely aided, restored it. For it is easy for anyone converted to the faith and the acknowledgment of the truth to renounce the Devil, and to confess the living God, and to receive the sacraments of Christ, and to preserve the received innocence of life with His grace accompanying; but it is of much labor for him who despises the received Sacraments of the faith to recover his former dignity. Compare the same, book 3 of Ezra, chapter 20, where he likewise mystically applies it here, that when Jerusalem was first When it was being built by Solomon, there was no need for an apparatus of military instruments, but when it had to be repaired after the Babylonian captivity, half of the young men did the work, and half were prepared for war. And likewise one hand did the work, and the other held a sword. 2. Esdr. 4. v. 16.

5. August conc. 2. in Psalm. 30. When he says, it was better for them not to know the way of justice, did he not indicate that enemies placed outside are better than those living evilly within, by whom the Church is pressed and burdened?

6. The same or any other author of the book on the New Canticle. O evil to look back! For the wife of Lot, who was freed from Sodom, looked back against the command and was turned into a pillar of salt. The same in Psal. 88. Why was she turned into a pillar of salt, if not to season men, so that they may be wise? Therefore, having been freed from Sodom, let us not look back at our past life.

7. Salvianus lib. 4. de provid. Now because you have already acknowledged Christ, you who were received as if into the house of God through the acknowledgment of faith, you will be cast out through lukewarmness, which Peter also explained, speaking about the vicious and the lukewarm. It was better for them not to know the way of justice &c.

8. The canonical authority of the book of Proverbs is proved among other things by the argument from the allegation of this writing in the N. Testament. For besides the fact that Peter in this place Prov. 26. v. 11. alleges the sentence, this book is also cited elsewhere more often as Canonical by Christ and the Apostles. Compare Prov. 3. v. 7. with Rom. 12. v. 16. Item Prov. 3. v. 11. with Hebr. 12. v. 5. Item Prov. 3. v. 12 with Hebr. 12. v. 6. & Apoc. 3. v. 17. Item Prov. 10. v. 12. with 1. petri 4. v. 8. Item Prov. 11. v. 31. with 1. petr. 4. v. 18. Item Prov. 17. v. 13. with 1. Thess. 5. v. 15. & 1. Petr. 3. v. 9. Item Prov. 17. v. 27. with Iac. 1. v. 19. Item Prov. 20. v. 9. with 1. Ioh. 1. v. 8. Item Prov. 22. v. 20. with Matth. 15. v. 4. & Marc. 7. v. 10. Item Prov. 24. v. 23. with Iacob. 2. v. 1. Item Prov. 26. v. 6. with Luc. 14. v. 10. Item Prov. 25. v. 21. with Rom. 12. v. 20. It must be noted, however, that the canonical authority of any book cannot be proved from its sole allegation in the N. T., but the remaining things must also κριτήρια be present, namely that it be written by a Prophet and in the Prophetic language; that it exactly agree with the remaining Canonical books, that it enjoy the testimony of the Israelite Church &c.

I. August. in tract. de decem chordis compares the confession of sins with vomiting, looking back to this place of Peter; and he warns lest the sinner after confession, like vomit revealed from sins, in canine fashion to the vomit that is to the sins, which he cast out through confession, he returns. The same in the exposition of Psalm 83. The conscience of sins was pressing upon your breast; having received indulgence, you as it were vomited, and your sin was relieved (perhaps your breast) a good conscience was made from a bad conscience. Why do you turn back again to your vomit? If a dog doing this is horrible to your eyes, what will you be to the eyes of God? The same in sermon 2 on Psalm 30. See to what a horrible thing he has compared them? It is indeed a horrible thing to resorb one's own vomit, nor is it practiced by anyone even in the greatest hunger.

10. Gregory, part 3 of Pastoral Care, Admonition 31. Those who lament committed sins, yet do not abandon them, are to be admonished that they should know how to consider solicitously that they cleanse themselves in vain by weeping, who wickedly defile themselves by living, since they wash themselves with tears for this reason, that they may return clean to filth. For hence it is written: The dog returned to his vomit, and the sow washed to her wallowing in the mire. For a dog, when it vomits, indeed casts out the food which was pressing upon its chest: but when it returns to the vomit, it is again burdened from where it had been lightened. And those who lament committed sins, indeed cast out the wickedness with which they had been evilly sated, and which the habit of the mind was pressing upon the inmost parts, which, while they repeat it after confession, they resume. But a sow, when it is washed in the wallowing of the mire, is rendered filthier. And he who laments a committed sin, yet does not abandon it, subjects himself to a nearly graver fault, because he despises the very pardon which he could have obtained by weeping, and he rolls himself in muddy water, because while he withdraws the cleanliness of life from his weeping, he makes even the tears themselves dirty before the eyes of God. The same exists in just as many words in Bede in the commentary on this place.

11. Such dogs, who return to the vomit of former errors and sins, will at some time be outside the heavenly Jerusalem. Apoc. 22. v. 15. In such swine, who return to the mire of former outrages, the Devil is so delighted that he often appears in this form, and asked that power be given to him by Christ to enter the swine. Matth. 8. v. 31. but at length he casts them into the sea of destruction.

12. Just as Augustine, Gregory, and Bede adapt the former proverb about the dog returning to its vomit to those who after penance and confession return to former sins: so Gregory Nazianzen στηλιτευτ. α. page 285, the proverb The latter part concerning the sow washed returning to the wallowing place of mire he applies to Julian the Apostate, who had washed away holy Baptism with the impious blood of victims.

13. Just as Peter in this place joins dogs returning to their vomit and sows to the mire: so also Christ Matth. 7. v. 6. likewise joins those two unclean animals παροιμιακῶς. Do not, he says, give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, upon which words Chrysostom comments thus in homily 24 on Matthew, fol 235 Κύνας ἐν τᾶυθα τοὺς ἐν ἀσεβεία ζῶντας ἀνιάτῳ καὶ μεταβολῆς τῆς ἐπὶ τό κρεῖττον οὐκ ἔχοντας ἐλπίδα ἠνίξατο, καὶ χοίρους τοὺς ἐν ἀκολάστῳ διατρίβοντας διαπαντὸς etc. Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, Epistle 143, page 37. By dogs he understands the Jews, who have very often received the divine word, and return again to their vomit, or heretics, who betake themselves to true doctrine, and return again to their former perversity of opinion. By swine he understands τοὺς πάθεσι συμφυρομένους καὶ χοιρώδη βίον μετερχομένους those who wallow in vicious affections, and follow a swinish manner of life. Euthymius on this place: He named dogs and swine, because they are held by an incurable impiety; dogs indeed as barking at Christ, but swine as wrapped in the mud of perturbations.

14. Origen, homily 1 on Psalm 37, teaches that sinners are most aptly compared to swine, To swine, he says, are those said to be similar, who delight in the stenches of sins. Just as swine, who seek out every stench as if it were a most sweet odor, consider therefore the sinner, that he delights in his sins, and is happy in his evils, since he himself also wallows in the fetid dung and perceives no sense of its stench, which arises from the dung of sin, and as if in the highest pleasures and most grave delights he takes pleasure.

15. Drusius in the Appendix of the book of Praeterita. A sow washed into the wallowing place. It can be said of him, who having been washed, (for reformation is a certain washing) wallows himself again in Sophistic mud, to the great harm of youth and the Church. For whence arise these dissensions, if not from that mud? Similarly the dog returns to the vomit; who now again recalls into the Academies, and introduces Scholastic Theology, that bread, which proceeds from the mouth of God alone, mixing it with the leaven of the Philosophers. These turn the simplicity of believing into the curiosity and subtlety of disputing, devising new questions daily, most of which are useless, once unknown to the Prophets and Apostles, which nevertheless increase the number of disputants, which fills the Christian world today.

CHAPTER III.

Summary of the chapter. He predicts that Epicurean mockers, denying the final judgment and the destruction of the world, will arise, and he warns the faithful against them. The parts of the chapter are two. 1. Confirmation of the coming of Christ to judgment. 2. A graphic description of the destruction of the world. To each part is prefixed an introduction consisting of a transition; an epilogue is added, comprising a repetition of the principal exhortation and a doxology.

In the transition, he again indicates the scope of his writing, and he exhorts those to whom he writes to constancy in the doctrine of the Gospel confirmed by the testimonies of the Prophets and Apostles, v. 1. & 2.

In the former part of the chapter, these members are proposed. 1. A prediction concerning the Epicurean mockers who are to come. v. 3. 2. A recitation of their argument, by which they go about denying the coming of Christ to judgment and the destruction of the world. v. 4. 3. A refutation of that argument. v. 5. & 6. 4. A confirmation of the future destruction of the world by fire. v. 7. 5. A proleptic excuse for the delay. v. 8. & 9. In the latter part of the chapter, these members occur. 1. A description of the coming of Christ to judgment, both from the manner of the coming, that it will be sudden, and from the accompanying destruction of the world, which is explained in parts, v. 10. 2. An exhortation to the pursuit of piety, deduced from the manner of the coming of Christ and the destruction of the world. v. 11. 3. A repetition of the prediction concerning the destruction of the world. vers. 12. 4. A promise of new heavens and a new earth. v. 13. 5. A repetition of the exhortation to piety, and its confirmation from the Pauline Epistles. v. 14. 15. & 16.

The epilogue consists both of ἀποτροπῇ v. 17. and of προτροπῇ & δοξολογία. v. 18.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. An de seductoribus, an verò de seductis Apostolus loquatur? Resp. Quidam affirmant prius, cum in praecedentibus de illis sermo fuerit, cùmque ipsi in Baptismo voluptatibus huius seculi renunciaverint, ac per hoc initiationis Sacramentum renati fuerint, sed postmodùm inquinamentis falsae doctrinae & vitae impiae iterum involuti fuerint. Sed rectiùs dicitur, de seductis hoc loco Apostolum agere. 1. Quia in v. 18. participium ἀποφυγόντες usurpatur de seductis, quod in hoc v. 20. Apostolus repetit: ac sicut ibi dicit, illos effugisse eos, qui in errore versantur: ita hoc loco dicit, illos effugisse inquinamenta mundi. 2. Ne quis cogitaret, falsos doctores ac seductores tantùm esse servos corruptionis, ac sibi ipsis exitium attrahere, ostendit etiam illis, qui se â falsis doctoribus patiuntur seduci, itidem gravissimum periculum imminere, cùm non solùm in servitutem peccati, ex qua liberati erant, retrahantur, sed etiam in peiorem statum detrudantur, quàm in quo fuerant ante suam ad Christianismum conversionem. Notandum tamen, quod non de quibusvis seductis, nec de quibusvis lapsibus, quibus homo interdum praeoccupatur, Gal. 6. v. 1. Apostolo hîc sit sermo, sed tùm de apostatis, qui sincerae doctrinae repudium mittentes eandem postmodum blasphemant, tùm de Epicurae is contemtoribus, qui abiecto omni pudore totos sese carnalibus concupiscentiis tradunt.

Q. 2. Quaenam sint illa mundi inquinamenta, quibus seducti iterum involvuntur. Resp. Sunt 1. falsa & erronea dogmata, quae Spiritus qui est in mundo 1. Iohann. 4. v. 4.Princeps mundiIohan. 14. v. 30.Deus huius seculi2. Cor. 4. v. 4. falsis doctoribus inspirat, ut per ea alios seducant. 2. Foedae libidines & omnis generis flagitia, quae contagio suo alios inficiunt. 3. Varia illa scandala ac perversa exempla, quae in mundo ubivis sunt obvia, ac facili negotio alios ad imitationem pertrahunt. Sap. 4. v. 11.Raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum eius, aut dolus deciperet animam illius.

vers. 12.Fascinatio enim nugacitatis obscurat bona, & inconstantia concupiscentiae transvertit mentem non malam.Rom. 16. vers. 18. de falsis doctoribus dicit Apostolus, quòd per χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐλογίαςseducant cordaτῶν ἀκάκων.

Q. 3. Quomodo per cognitionem Christi sive fidem in Christum effugiantur mundi inquinamenta? Resp. 1. Cognitio Christi oritur ex verbo Evangelii. Illud verò est salutare organum, per quod Deus ab omnibus erroris & peccati sordibus nos mundat. Ioh. 15. v. 3.Vos mundi estis propter sermonem, quem locutus sum vobis. 2. Fides in Christo quaerit & invenit perfectam munditiem, quâ homo coram DEI iudicio consistere potest. Actor. 15. v. 9.fide purificans corda eorum. 3. Dum fide datur homini Spiritus sanctus, qui peccati sordes expurgare incipit, & studium verae sanctitatis ac mundiciei in corde eius accendit. 1. Cor. 6. v. 11.abluti estis, sanctificati estis, iustificati estis in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi & in Spiritu DEI nostri, ubi Apostolus sordibus opponit ablutionem, pollutioni sanctificationem, reatui iustificationem; ac beneficia illa tribuit Christo tanquam causae promerenti, & Spiritui sancto tanquam causae dispensanti & applicanti.

Q. 4. Unde conditio illorum, qui inquinamentis mundi, quae effugerant, iterum implicantur, reddatur deterior? Resp. Fit illud.

1. Propter peccantis conditionem. Qui in luce fidei peccat & viam veritatis agnitam deserit, ille non ampliùs ex ignorantia, sed sciens & volens peccat. Iam verò gravius est peccatum, quod quis sciens & volens committit, quàm quod ex ignorantia proficiscitur. Luc. 12. v. 47.Servus ille, qui cognovit voluntatem Domini sui, & non praeparavit se, nec fecit voluntatem eius, vapulabit multis. v. 48. Qui autem non cognovit & fecit digna plagis, vapulabit paucis.

2. Propter peccati accumulationem. Qui post Baptismum & conversionem peccat, ille reliquis peccatis adiicit ingratitudinem, quae non mediocre pondus illis addit. Chrysostomus homil. de lapsu primi hominis. Noli peccare post veniam, noli vulnerari post curam, noli sordidari post gratiam. Cogita, ô homo, graviorem esse culpam post veniam, renovatum vulnus peius dolore post curam, molestiùs hominem sordidari post gratiam. Quare indulgentiae ingratus est, qui post veniam peccat; sanctitate indignus est, qui semetipsum, postquam curatus est, vulnerat; nec mundari meretur, qui semetipsum post gratiam sordidat. Et postea. Grave est, hominem instructum delinquere; gravius, absolutum peccare; servopeior est, qui patronum post datam libertatem offendit; beneficiis ingratus est, qui datorem tumoris arrogantiâ despicit. Bernhardus serm. 1. de sept. miseric. col. 280. Peremtoria res est ingratitudo, hostis gratiae, inimica salutis. Ingratitudo inimica est animae, virtutum dissipatio, beneficiorum perditio. Ingratitudo est herba venenata & fetida ex tribus radicibus crescens, mendacio, superbia, iniustitia, unde etiam per ingratitudinem DEUS maximâ afficitur ignominiâ, ut colligitur exLuc. 17. v. 18.

3. Propter donorum preciosorum deperditionem. Qui post illuminationem & conversionem contra conscientiam peccat, ac mundi inquinamentis iterum involvitur, ille amittit gratiam DEI, veram fidem, Spiritum sanctum, iustitiam & vitam aeternam. Quò verò dona illa sunt preciosiora, eò peior est illorum amissio ac deterior illius, quiea amisit, conditio. Basilius regula 289 ex brevioribus notat, cùm quis relabitur in peccatum, signum esse, primitus eum à peccato non planè recessisse, nec eius radicem extirpasse, sed adhuc occultè in animo eius residere peccati appetitum & concupiscentiam.

4. Propter periculi consecutionem. Qui post illuminationem & conversionem peccat, in apostasiam vel reipsâ incidit, vel facili negotio incidere potest. Quamvis enim non omnes, qui per peccata contra conscientiam inquinamentis mundi iterum involvuntur, notitiam veritatis statim simul amittant ac in haere ses vel apostasian incidant, tamen amittendae illius notitiae periculo sese exponunt. Cùm enim bonam conscientiam amittentes circa fidem naufragium fecerint.1. Tim. 1. v. 19. inde facili negotio fieri potest, ut quicquid salutaris notitiae adhuc in ipsis superest, peccatorum tenebris extinguatur. Augustinus lib. 8. Confess. cap. 5. dicit, ex perversa voluntate factam libidinem; dum servitur libidini, factam consuetudinem; dum consuetudini non resistitur, factam necessitatem. Id quidem verum etiam ante conversionem, sed multò magis post relapsum.

5. Propter difficiliorem conversionem. Quemadmodum, docentibus Medicis, ὑποστροφὴ sive recidiva, h. e. morbus renovarus ex intervallo quasi recrudescens longè maius periculum affert, quàm morbi initia: ita quoque in morbis spiritualibus idem usu venire videmus, videlicet quòd difficilior fit illorum sanatio, qui â morbis animae spiritualibus per Christum liberati in eosdem denuò relabuntur. Satan semel expulsus, si denuò per peccata intromittitur, adducit secum septem alios Spiritus, qui ipso sunt nequiores, qui atrium illud longè fortiùs custodiunt, quám prius. (Salmero & Cornelius â Lapide hûc accommodant dict a Hebr. 6. v. 4.cap. 10. v. 26. Sed illa propriè & directè agunt de speciali quodam peccato, videlicet de peccato in Spiritum Sanctum) Atque hae sunt praecipuae rationes, propter quas Petrus pronunciat, conditionem illorum, qui inquinamentis mundi, quae effugerant, iterum implicantur, esse deteriorem, quàm est illorum, qui viam iustitiae nunquam cognoverunt. Iohannes Huss in comm h. l. hasce assignat causas. Prima est debilitas ad resurgendum, quae in recidivante augmentatur, sicut fit in recidivante infirmato corporali. 2. Ruptio foederis initicum Domino. 3. Inimicis subiectio gravior. 4. Divinae misericordiae subsannatio. 5. Crudelitas animae propriae illata. 6. Spiritus sancti & caelestis curiae contristatio, ac Daemonum laetificatio. 7. Ingratitudo veniae & gratiae iam datae & gloriae promissae. 8. Quia recidivans, quantum in eo est, Christi iterat passionem.

Q. 5. Quae sit occasio proverbiorum ab Apostolo adductorum? 1. Prioris proverbii origo haec est. Canis, ubi se avidiùs cibo ingurgitavit, herbâ quadam comesâ vomitum quidem ciet, atque hoc --cto ventriculum exonerat; verùm ut est animal Naturâ imm --m & vorax, paulò pòst ad cibos per vomitum reiectos revertitur, eosque resorbet. Illiusmodi foedis & impudicis canibus similes sunt, qui inquinamentis mundi, quae per conversionem ad fidem Christi effugerant, iterum sese patiuntur implicari. 2 Proverbii posterioris haec est origo. Sui lutum est amicum, teste Plinio lib. 8. Nat. Hist. cap. 51. Varrone lib. 2. cap. 4. Colummella lib. 7. c. 9. Alexandro Aphrodisaeo lib. 1. q. 141. Vixisset canis immundus, vel amica luto sus, canit Horatius lib. 2. Epist. 2. Inde saepe accidit, ut manibus hominum lota & mundata statim redeat ad lutum, inque eo sese volutet. Immundis istis porcis itidem similes sunt, qui ab immunditiis huius seculi abluti & mundati iisdem rursus involvuntur. Utraque enim similitudo ad idem obiectum, & ad eundem scopum accommodatur.

Ἐναντιοφάνεια.Melius erat illis, non cognoscere viam iustitiae, quàm ubi cognoverunt eam, converti â tradito illis sancto mandato. Atqui non cognoscere viam iustitiae, non est bonum, sed malum. Resp. melius hoc loco dicitur, quod est minùs malum, comparantur enim duo mala, quorum unum altero peius. Illud alii sic efferunt. Melius dicitur non positivè, quasi maius sit bonum, cùm nec sit bonum: sed negativè, quia minus malum, h. e. minor est infidelis ignorantis, quàm fidelis cognoscentis, sed postea relapsi, culpa, unde minor etiam erit poena. Haec explicatio colligitur ex vers. praeced. in quo τα ἔσχατα illorum hominum dicuntur χείρανα πρώτων. Ergo etiam τὰ πρῶταfuêreκακὰ. Syrus habet verbum [פקח]utile foret, conduceret illis, ut respectus habeatur ad maiorem relapsorum & apostatarum poenam, sicut de proditore suo Christus dicit, Matth. 26. v. 24.Bonum erat ei, si natus non fuisset, homo ille.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Si illi, qui per cògnitionem Christi effugerunt inquinamenta mundi, iisdem iterum implicari possunt, consequens est, Christum etiam pro illis esse passum & mortuum, qui inquinamentis mundi sese implicantes aeterno exitio involvuntur. Ratio connexionis haec est, quia qui per agnitionem Christi effugerunt inquinamenta mundi, illi etiam participes facti fuêre fructus passionis & mortis Christi, cùm liberatio ab inquinamentis mundi ad fructus passionis & mortis Christi, pertineat. Qui autem participes facti sunt fructus passionis & mortis Christi, pro illis Christus omninò fuit passus ac mortuus.

Excipit Polanus, cognitionem Christi esse duplicem, generalem & specialem; hoc loco non de speciali, sed de generali cognitione Christi sermonem esse, qualis etiam potest esse in ipsis DaemonibusMarc. 1. v. 23.

Resp. de tali cognitione Christi hîc sermo est, per quam effugiuntur inquinamenta mundi. Atqui inquinamenta mundi non effugiuntur per cognitionem generalem, vel per fidem merè Historicam, sed per cognitionem specialem, per fiducialem meriti Christi apprehensionem.

2. Si illi, qui effugerunt inquinamenta mundi, possunt iisdem iterum implicari, consequens est, renatos posse in peccata contra conscientiam incidere, ac per ea fidem & gratiam Dei iterum amittere.

Excipit 1. Tossanus, hîc agi de sola agnitione & confessione veritatis, quae etiam in hypocritas cadat. Resp. Apostolus illis, quos, inquinamentis mundi iterum implicari dicit, tribuit. 1. Christi cognitionem. 2. cognitionem viae iustitiae. 3. fugam ab inquinamentis mundi, sive liberationem ex illis inquinamentis. 4. dicit de illis, quòd convertantur ab eo, quod illis traditum est sancto mandato. 5. comparat eos canibus, ad vomitum & porcis ad volutabrum luti redeuntibus, quae omnia ostendunt, illos verâ in Christum fide ê luto scelerum emersisse, foeditates â se reiecisse, & ab inquinamentis mundi, ad quae cumprimis peccata pertinent, liberatos fuisse.

2. Excipiunt alii, non omnes, in quibus qualiscunque emendatio morum externa apparet & ab idololatria discessus, statim esse electos. Resp. 1. Nemo nostrûm hoc dicit, imò plus dicimus, non omnes, in quibus qualiscunque emendatio morum externa apparet & ab idololatria discessus, statim esse renatos, licet ex caritatis lege pro talibus habeantur. 2. hoc verò est, quod dicimus, illos, quos Apostolus h. l. inquinamentis mundi iterum implicari dicit, fuisse verè renatos, quia de iisdem pronunciat, quòd inquinamenta illa priùs per cognitionem Christi effugerint, & quidem ὄντως, ut habetur in v. 18. 3. Falsum est, quod Calviniani statuunt, omnes verè renatos esse electos, & quia hi, de quibus Apostolus loquitur, non fuerunt electi, ex eo colligunt, illos etiam non fuisse renatos. Renatorum enim terminus latiùs patet quàm electorum, cùm omnes quidem electi sint renati, non tamen omnes renati sint electi. πρῶτον ψεῦδος in eo consistit, quòd forti, sed vanâ tamen imaginatione sibi persuaserunt, veram fidem nullis dari, nisi absoluto Dei decreto electis, ac fidem semel datam non posse iterum amitti.

3. Augustinus libro de fid. & operibus cap. 24. ex hoc loco Apostolico refellit illos, qui promittebant salutem per ignem illis, qui etiam credentes pessimè vivunt. Quid, inquit, adhuc promittitur contra istam manifestissimam veritatem conditio & melior iis, qui cognoverunt viam iustitiae, h. e. Dominum Christum, & perditè vivunt, quasi omninò non cognovissent, cùm apertissimè dicatur. Melius erat illis, non cognoscere viam iustitiae, quàm cogno scentibus retrorsum reflecti â tradito sibi sancto mandato. Et postea. Non itaque promittitur poena ignis transitoria turpiter scelerateque viventibus, quia viam iustitiae cognoverunt, quibus melius erat non cognoscere, sicut veracissima Scriptura testatur.

4. Παραδόσεως vox in v. 21. usurpatur de doctrina Apostolorum, quam primùm quidem vivâ voce praedicarunt, postea per Dei voluntatem in Scripturam redegerunt. Ergo in Scriptura continetur vera παράδοσις Apostolica, non in verbo ἀγράφῳ, quod Pontificii confinxerunt.

Ἐηδίκησις. 1. Estius ex v. 20. colligit, hominem fide & caritate imbutum non posse esse certum de sua salute, cùm fides & caritas semel habita amitti possint. Resp. 1. Fidem & caritatem semel habitam amitti posse concedimus, sed quod ex eo salutis incertitudo sequatur, negamus. 2 Distinguimus enim inter salutem praesentem, & inter plenissimam eiusdem possessionem, in die iudicii secuturam. Salus praesens omnibus verè in Christum credentibus ac per fidem coram DEO iustificatis obtingit. Iohann. 3. v. 36.Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam.Roman. 4. v. 6.Davidμακαρισμὸνdicit esse illius hominis, ovi DEUS imputat iustitiam sine operibus. ubi observa, δικαίωσιν & μακαρισμὸν ab Apostolo ut ἰσοδυναμοῦντα accipi. 1. Iohann. 5. vers. 11.Vitam aeternam dedit nobis DEUS, & haec vita in Filio eius est. vers. 12. Qui habet Filium, habet vitam. vers. 13. Haec scripsi vobis credentibus in nomen Filii DEI, quoniam vitam habetis aeternam. Quòd si ergò verè credentes possunt esse certi de iustificatione & gratia DEI, uti omnino possunt, utique etiam pessunt esse certi de salute praesente. 3. Quod attinet certitudinem de plenissima secuturae salutis possessione, distinguimus inter certitudinem absolutam, & conditionatam. Quamvis de plenissima secuturae salutis possessione non detur certitudo absoluta, tamen datur de ea certitudo conditionata, quae quomodo comparata sit, exposuimus superiùs in enarratione cap. 1. vers. 10. 4. Inter certitudinem absolutam h. e. ex absoluto electionis decreto dependentem, quam propugnant Calviniani, & inter certitudinem coniecturalem i. e. incertam persuasionem, quam propugnant Pontificii, datur medium, videlicet certitudo conditionata, quae respectum habet ad media, per quae DEUS in fide conservat & ad salutem perducit.

2. Lorinus ex v. 21. colligit, elucere etiam in eo Dei misericordiam, quod non omnibus annuncietur Evangelium, ne gravius ferant iudicium non credentes, quamvis & admiranda eiusdem iustitia sit, ut praedicari noluerit multis, qui si praedicatum ipsis fuisset, credidissent & fructum fecissent, ut Tyrus, Sidon.Matth. 11. v. 21. 22. Resp. 1. Quòd quibusdam populis actu non praedicatur Evangelium, propriè non est misericordiae, sed iustitiae divinae tribuendum, quia propter antegressum verbi contemtum, â maioribus commissum, posteri praedicatione illâ destituuntur. 2. Quamvis gravius ferant iudicium, quibus Evangelium actu praedicatum est, & tamen ei credere noluerunt, quàm illi, quibus nunquam praedicatum est, haec tamen non est vera causa, propter quam actuali Evangelii praedicatione quidam destituuntur, sed illa potiùs, quam modò exposuimus.

3. Matth. 11. v. 21. 22. Christus non loquitur de ordinario conversionis medio, videlicet de verbi praedicatione, sed de extraordinario illo beneficio, quod copiam miraculorum & praedicationem in propria Christi persona complectitur.

3. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, quosdam converti â sancto, quodipsis traditum fuit mandato.v. 21. Pontificii colligere posse videntur, Evangelium propriè loquendo esse legem, & proinde doctrinam operum. Resp. 1. mandati nomine intelligit Apostolus totam Christi doctrinam, sive, quod idem est, Evangelium γενικῶς acceptum, in quo doctrinam operum contineri, nemo nostrûm negat. 2. Evangelium εἰδικῶς acceptum docet fidem in Christum, quam certo respectu mandato divino requiri non abnuimus. 1. Iohann. 3. v. 23.Hoc est mandatum DEI, ut credamus in nomen Filii eius Iesu Christi & diligamus alterutrùm, sicut dedit mandatum nobis. 3. Quamvis directè & propriè Evangelium non requirat opera, tamen consequenter eadem requirit. Quia enim vera fides, quam Evangelium requirit, non est, nec esse potest sine bonis operibus, inde Evangelium requirendo fidem, requirit etiam consequenter bona opera, tanquam fidei fructus & testimonia, ut tamen nihilominus Evangelium propriè loquendo non sit doctrina operum eorundemque norma & regula, sed lex ab Evangelio contradistincta. 4. Inde Augustinus lib. de fide & operibus cap. 25. de hoc mandato sic scribit. Neque enim illud hoc loco intelligendum est sanctum mandatum, quo praeceptum est, ut in Deum credamus, quanquam eo ipso totum continetur, si eam intelligimus fidem credentium, quae per dilectionem operatur, sed aperte expressit, quod diceret sanctum mandatum h. e. quo praeceptum est, ut ab huius mundi coinquinationibus recedentes castâ conversatione vivamus. Non enim, ait, refugientes ignorantiam Dei, aut refugientes infide litatem seculi vel tale aliquid, sed coinquinationes mundi, in quibus est utique omnis immunditia flagitiorum. 4. Novatiani ex h. l. colligere voluerunt, illis, qui post acceptum Baptismum tempore per secutionis ex infirmitate aut metu periculi agnitam veritatem abnegant, fores gratiae, si maximè eas in vera paenitentia pulsent, esse clausas. Resp. 1. Petrus iuxta quorundam sententiam non de quovis lapsu hîc agit, sed de voluntaria illa ἀποστασία, quae fit ex destinato consilio & cum blasphemia in Spiritum sanctum est coniuncta, de qua etiam Hebr. 6. v. 4. & cap. 10. v. 26. agitur. Qui enim eo modo ex voluntaria malitia ab agnita veritate deficiunt, iusto Dei iudicio in sensum reprobum traditi non agunt paenitentiam, sed in suis blasphemiis pergunt, ideoque ad gratiam non perveniunt. 2. Sed rectiùs dicitur, Petrum non tantùm de peccato in Spiritum sanctum, sed de quibusvis gravioribus peccatis ex malitiâ commissis agere, proinde respondemus, Petrum quidem pronunciare conditionem illorum, qui inquinamentis mundi, quae effugerant, iterum implicantur, esse deteriorem, nequaquam verò addere, illis non patere iterum aditum ad paenitentiam. 3. Quinimò ut omnes promissiones cum conditione fidei: sic omnes comminationes cum conditione paenitentiae sunt intelligendae.

Observationes. 1. Duplicis generis inquinamenta spiritualia dantur, doctrinae & vitae. Inquinamenta doctrinae sunt errores cum Evangelii doctrinam divinitùs revelata pugnantes. Inquinamenta vitae sunt studia & actiones cum norma divinae legis pugnantes. Ab utroque inquinamentorum spiritualium genere per cognitionem Christi liberamur, quippe quae non solùm notitiam & assensum, sed etiam fiduciam complectitur, & cum qua sanctificatio Spiritus est individuo nexu coniuncta.

2. Quia post liberationem ab inquinamentis mundi iisdem iterum implicari quosdam, contingit, ideò excussâ carnali securitate in vero Dei timore cautè & solicitè ambulemus. Lavi pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo illos? dicit Sponsa Christi Spiritualis Cant. 5. v. 3. Eadem debet esse vox omnium piorum. Cyprianus lib. 3. ad Quitinum. Baptizatum quoque gratiam perdere, quam consecutus sit, nisi innocentiam servet, in Evangelio secundùm Iohannemcap. 5. v. 14.dicitur, Ecce sanus factus es, iam noli peccare, ne quid tibi deterius fiat. Hieronymus in Epist. ad Furiam. Bruta animalia & vagae aves in easdem pedicas. retiaque non incidunt, homo ratione praeditus in eosdem Satanae laqueos, quos semel effugit, iterum incidet?

3. Ad piam hanc cavendi lapsus solicitudinem cumprimis nos excitare debet, quod Apostolo docente peior sit illorum conditio, qui postquam â DEO sanitatem animae perceperunt, iterum peccant & in recidivam incidunt. Bernhardus serm. 3. in Cant. col. 500. Si rursus pedes meos quos laveram, inquinavero, nunquid aliquid lavisse valebit? Sordens omni genere vitiorum iacui diu in luto fecis, sed erit sine dubio recidenti, quam iacenti deterius. Qui me sanum fecit, ipsum mihi dixisse recordor. Ecce sanus factus es, vade, iam ampliùs noli peccare, ne deterius quid tibi contingat &c. Pro huius modi non sum omninò contentus priori gratiâ, quâ iam malorum sum paenitens, nisi & secundam accepero, ut videlicet dignos faciam paenitentiae fructus, & deinceps non revertar ad vomitum. Dionys. Carth. in h. l. sicut ex tali lotione postquam ad cenum redit, porcus redditur sordidior, quam fuerat ante: ita ex recidiva graviùs homo coinquinatur.

4. Primum Salomonis templum septem annis fuit perfectum 1. Reg. 6. v. 38. sed secundum templum Zorobabelis non nisi quadraginta sex annorum spacio fuit exaedificatum. Ioh. 2. v. 20. Illud Beda lib 2. in Esdr. cap. 8. mysticè sic applicat. Notandum, quod prius templum Salomon in pace regni sui permaxima, tempore brevi, nullo contradicente perfecit: nunc autem destructum propter peccata filii transmigrationis in magna cordis compunctione labori longo insistentes, & saepissimè ab inimicis retardati, tandem divinitus adiuti restaurârunt. Facile namque est conversum quemque ad fidem, agnitionemque veritatis abrenunciare Diabolo, & confireri Deum vivum, sacramenta Christi percipere, atque acceptam vitae innocentiam comitante eius gratiâ servare; sed multi laboris est, eum, qui accepta fidei Sacramenta contemnit, pristinam recipere dignitatem. Confer eundem lib. 3. Esdrae cap. 20. ubi itidem mysticè huc applicat, quod cùm Hierosolyma primùm â Salomone aedificaretur, nullo opus fuerit militarium instrumentorum apparatu, sed cùm post Babylonicam captivitatem esset reparanda, media pars iuvenum faciebat opus, & media parata erat ad bellum. Itemque una manus faciebat opus, & altera tenebat gladium. 2. Esdr. 4. v. 16.

5. August conc. 2. in Psalm. 30. Cùm dicit, melius erat illis, non cognoscere viam iustitiae, nonne indicavit, meliores esse inimicos foris positos, quam intus malè viventes, quibus premitur & gravatur Ecclesia?

6. Idem vel quicunque alius autor lib. de Cantico novo. O malum retrospicere! Uxor enim Loth, quae liberata est â Sodomis, contra praeceptum retrospexit & in statuam salis conversa est. Idem in Psal. 88.Ut quid in statuam salis conversa est, si non homines condit, ut sapiant? Liberati ergo â Sodomis praeteritae vitae non respiciamus retrò.

7. Salvianus lib. 4. de provid. Nunc quia iam Christum agnovisti, qui susceptus es quasi intraos Dei per fidei agnitionem, proiicieris per teporem, quod etiam Petrus exposuit dicens de vitiosis & tepidis. Melius erat illis, non cognoscere viam iustitiae &c.

8. Canonica libri Proverbiorum autoritas probatur inter caetera argumento ex allegatione huius scripti in N. Test. Praeterquam enim, quod Petrus hoc loco Prov. 26. v. 11.Sententiam allegat, etiam alibi saepius hic liber ut Canonicus â Christo & Apostolis adducitur. Confer.Prov. 3. v. 7.cumRom. 12. v. 16.ItemProv. 3. v. 11.cumHebr. 12. v. 5.ItemProv. 3. v. 12cumHebr. 12. v. 6.&Apoc. 3. v. 17.ItemProv. 10. v. 12.cum1. petri 4. v. 8.ItemProv. 11. v. 31.cum1. petr. 4. v. 18.ItemProv. 17. v. 13.cum1. Thess. 5. v. 15.&1. Petr. 3. v. 9.ItemProv. 17. v. 27.cumIac. 1. v. 19.ItemProv. 20. v. 9.cum1. Ioh. 1. v. 8.ItemProv. 22. v. 20.cumMatth. 15. v. 4.&Marc. 7. v. 10.ItemProv. 24. v. 23.cumIacob. 2. v. 1.ItemProv. 26. v. 6.cumLuc. 14. v. 10.ItemProv. 25. v. 21.cumRom. 12. v. 20.Notandum tamen, quod ex sola allegatione in N. T. non possit Canonica alicuius libri autoritas probari, sed oportet etiam reliquaκριτήριαadesse, videlicet quod sit scriptus â Propheta & lingua Prophetica; quod reliquis libris Canonicis exactè consentiat, quod testimonio Ecclesiae Israeliticae gaudeat &c.

I. August. in tract. de decem chordis peccatorum confessionem comparat cum vomitu, respiciens ad hunc Petri locum; monetque ne peccator post confessionem tanquam vomitum revelatus â peccatis, canino more ad vomitum h. e. ad peccata, quae per confessionem proiecit, redeat. Idem in enarr. Psalm. 83.Premebat pectus conscientia peccatorum accepta Indulgentiâ quasi vomuisti, & relevatum est peccatum tuum (fortè pectus tuum) facta est bona conscientia ex mala conscientia. Quid rursus converteris ad vomitum tuum? Si canis hoc faciens horret oculis tuis, tu quid eris oculis Dei? Idem conc. 2. in Psalm. 30. Vide quàm horribili rei eos comparaverit? Horribilis profectò res est, proprium resorbere vomitum, nec in summa quidem fame â quoquam usurpatum.

10. Gregorius part. 3. Curae Pastoralis Admonit. 31. Admonendi sunt, qui admissa plangunt, nec tamen deserunt, ut considerare solicitè sciant, quia flendo inaniter se mundant, qui vivendo se nequiter inquinant, cùm idcircò se lachrymis lavant, ut mundi ad sordes redeant. Hinc enim scriptum est. Canis reversus ad suum vomitum, & sus lota in volutabro suti. Canis quippe cùm vomit, profecto cibum, qui pectus deprimebat, proiicit: sed cùm ad vomitum revertitur, unde levigatus fuerat, rursus oneratur. Et qui admissa plangunt, profectò nequitiam, de qua malè satiati fuerant, & quae mentis intima deprimebat consuetudo, proiiciunt, quam post confessionem, dum repetunt, resumunt. Sus verò in volutabro luti cùm lavatur, sordidior redditur. Et qui admissum plangit, nec tamen deserit, penè graviori culpae se subiicit, quia ipsam, quam flendo potuit impetrare veniam, contemnit, & quas in lutosa aqua semetipsum volvit, quia dum fletibus suis vitae munditiam subtrahit, ante Dei oculos sordidas ipsas etiam lachrymas facit. Eadem totidem ver bis extant apud Bedam in comm. h. l.

11. Illiusmodi canes, qui ad vomitum pristinorum errorum & peccatorum revertuntur, erunt aliquando foris extra caelestem Hierosolymam. Apoc. 22. v. 15. Illiusmodi porcis, qui ad cenum flagitiorum priorum redeunt, Diabolus adeò delectatur, ut & istâ saepe appareat formâ, & potestatem ingrediendi porcos â Christo sibi dari petierit. Matth. 8. v. 31. sed tandem in mare exitii illos praecipitat.

12. Quemadmodum Augustinus, Gregorius & Beda Proverbium prius de cane ad vomitum redeunte accommodant ad illos, qui post paenitentiam & confessionem ad priora peccata revertuntur: ita Gregorius Nazianzenus στηλιτευτ. α. pag. 285. proverbium posterius de sue lota ad volutabrum ceni redeunte accommodat ad Iulianum apostatam, qui sacrum Baptismum impio victimarum sanguine abluerat.

13. Sicut Petrus hoc loco canes ad vomitum & sues ad cenum redeuntes coniungit: ita quoque Christus Matth. 7. v. 6. itidem duo illa immunda animalia παροιμιακῶς coniungit. Nolite, inquit, sanctum dare canibus, neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos, in quae verba sic comment. Chrysostomus homil. 24. in Matth. fol 235 Κύνας ἐν τᾶυθα τοὺς ἐν ἀσεβεία ζῶντας ἀνιάτῳ καὶ μεταβολῆς τῆς ἐπὶ τό κρεῖττον οὐκ ἔχοντας ἐλπίδα ἠνίξατο, καὶ χοίρους τοὺς ἐν ἀκολάστῳ διατρίβοντας διαπαντὸς &c. Isidorus Pelusiotal. 1. Epist. 143. pag. 37. Per canes intelligit Iudaeos, qui divinum sermonem persaepe acceperunt, ac rursum ad vomitum suum revertuntur, aut haereticos, qui ad veram doctrinam sese conferunt, ac rursum ad priorem sententiae perversitatem redeunt. Per porcos intelligitτοὺς πάθεσι συμφυρομένους καὶ χοιρώδη βίον μετερχομένουςqui in vitiosis affectibus affectibus volutantur, ac porcinum vitae genus sequuntur. Euthymius in h. l. Canes & porcos nominavit, quod immedicabili tenentur impietate; canes quidem tanquam Christo oblatrantes, porcos verò perturbationum luto involutos.

14. Origenes homil. 1. in Psal 37. peccatores suibus aptissimè comparari docet, Porcis, inquit, similes dicuntur ii, qui peccatorum fetoribus delectantur. Sicut porci, qui fetorem omnem tanquam odorem suavissimum expetunt, Considera ergo peccatorem, quod peccatis suis delectatur, & laetus est in malis suis, quoniam & ipse in stercore fetido volutatur & nullum fetoris eius, qui ex peccati stercore oritur, percipit sensum, ac velut in summis voluptatibus & gravissimis delitiis delectatur.

15. Drusius in Appendice libri Praeteritorum. Sus lota in volutabrum. Dici potest de eo, qui lotus, (nam reformatio est quaedam lotio) se in luto Sophistico rursum volutat, magno iuventutis & Ecclesiae malo. Nam unde quae so haec dissidia, nisi ex illo luto? Similiter canis advomitum redit; qui nunc iterum in Academias revocat, introducitque Theologiam Scholasticam, panem illum, qui procedit ex ore solius Dei, miscens cum fermento Philosophorum. Hi simplicitatem credendi convertunt in curiositatem & subtilitatem disputandi, quaestiones novas quotidie excogitantes, quarum pleraeque inutiles sunt, Prophetis atque Apostolis olim ignoratae, quae lamen augent numerum disputantium, qui Christianum orbem hodie replet.

CAPUT III.

Summa capitis. Epicuraeos irrisores, iudicium extremum & mundi interitum negantes exurrecturos praedicit, ac contra illos fideles praemonet. Partes capitis duae. 1. Adventus Christi ad iudicium confirmatio. 2. Interitus mundi graphica descriptio. Utrique parti praemittitur exordium transitione constans; subiicitur Epilogus repetitionem principalis commone factionis & doxologiam complectens.

In transitione scriptionis suae scopum denuò indicat, & ad constantiam in doctrina Evangelii Prophetarum & Apostolorum testimoniis confirmata, eos, ad quos scribit, hortatur, v. 1. & 2.

In priore capitis parte haec proponuntur membra. 1. De venturis Epicurae is irrisoribus praedictio. v. 3. 2. Argumenti ipsorum, quo Christi ad iudicium adventum & mundi interitum negatum eunt, recitatio. v. 4. 3. Argumenti illius refutatio. v. 5. & 6. 4. Futuri interitus mundi per ignem confirmatio. v. 7. 5. Proleptica dilationis excusatio. v. 8. & 9. In parte capitis posteriore haec occurrunt membra. 1. Adventus Christi ad iudicium descriptio, tùm ex adventus modo, quòd futurus sit repentinus, tùm ex adiuncto mundi interitu, qui per partes exponitur, v. 10. 2. Ex modo adventus Christi & interitus mundi deducta exhortatio, ad studium pietatis. v. 11. 3. Praedictionis de mundi interitu repetitio. vers. 12. 4. Novorum caelorum ac novae terrae promissio. v. 13. 5. Exhortationis ad pietatem repetitio, eiusdemque ex Epistolis Paulinis confirmatio. v. 14. 15. & 16.

Epilogus constat tùm ἀποτροπῇv. 17. tùm προτροπῇ & δοξολογία.v. 18.

## 2:21
Connection. He proves what he had said in the preceding verse, that the condition of those who are seduced by false teachers is far worse than it had been before their conversion, by a comparison of unequals, namely, the lesser destruction of those who never knew the way of truth and righteousness.

Exposition of the text. Κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τήν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης. Vulg. For it were better for them, not to know the way of righteousness. The Greek has not to have known. By the way of righteousness is understood the doctrine of Christ, or the doctrine of the Gospel, in which is delivered the manner of obtaining righteousness valid before GOD and eternal life.

Ἤ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ἐπιστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς. Vulg. than after the acknowledgment to be turned back from that which was delivered to them, the holy commandment. The Greek properly has, than when they have known (to wit, the way of righteousness) to be turned from the holy commandment delivered to them.

For ἐπιστρέψαι some Greek Codices have, εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἀνακάμψαι to be turned back to the rear. But few Codices read thus and nothing is lost to the sense itself. By the holy commandment the Apostle understands the same thing which he did before by the way of righteousness, because the doctrine of Christ or the Gospel γενηκῶς received not only delivers the manner of obtaining true righteousness valid before God, but also prescribes the precepts of living justly and holily John 13. v. 34. A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another, As I have loved you, that ye also love one another. chap. 15. v. 12. This is my commandment, that ye love one another 1. John 3. v. 23. This is his commandment, that we should believe on the name of his Son and love one another, as he gave commandment to us. He calls this commandment holy, because it has proceeded from him who is the holy of holies Dan. 9. v. 24. because it contains nothing but what is holy and pure, because it is the medium through which God sanctifies man, and because it is opposed to the pollutions of the world, which defile and profane man. Some add, that it is also called holy for this reason, because it must be kept holily, because it has the holy God as its primary and formal object, and because the saints in eternal life are to fulfill it most perfectly. But the reasons previously adduced are the principal ones. Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian, adduces this Apostolic passage with these words: It were better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after the acknowledgment to turn back, and to leave the holy commandment which was delivered unto them.

Latin:

Connexio. Probat, quod versu praeced, dixerat, conditionem eorum, qui à falsis doctoribus seducuntur, esse longè deteriorem, quàm fuerat ante conversionem, per collationem imparium, videlicet minoris exitii illorum, qui viam veritatis & iustitiae nunquam cognoverunt.

Textus expositio. Κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τήν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης. Vulg. Melius enim erat illis, non cognoscere viam iustitiae. Graeca habent non cognovisse. Per viam iustitiae intelligitur doctrina Christi, sive doctrina Evangelii, in qua traditur modus consequendi iustitiam coram DEO valentem & vitam aeternam.

Ἤ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ἐπιστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς. Vulg. quàm post agnitionem retrorsum converti ab eo, quod illis traditum est, sancto mandato Graeca propriè habent, quàm ubi cognoverunt (scil. viam iustitiae) converti à tradito illis sancto mandato.

Pro ἐπιστρέψαι quidam Codd. Graeci habent, εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἀνακάμψαιad posteriora reflecti. Sed pauci Codd. ita legunt ac sensui ipsi nihil decedit. Per sanctum mandatum idem intelligit Apostolus, quod priùs per viam iustitiae, quia doctrina Christi sive Evangelii γενηκῶς accepti non solùm tradit modum consequendi veram coram Deo valentem iustitiam, sed etiam praescribit iustè & sanctè vivendi praecepta Ioh. 13. v. 34.Praeceptum novum do vobis, ut diligatis vos invicem, Sicut dilexi vos, ut & vos diligatis invicem.cap. 15. v. 12.Hoc est praecaeptum meum, ut diligatis invicem1. Ioh. 3. v. 23.Hoc est mandatum eius, ut credamus in nomen Filii eius & diligamus invicem, sicut mandatum dedit nobis. Hoc mandatum vocat sanctum, quia est profectum ab eo, qui est sanctus sanctorumDan. 9. v. 24. quia nihil nisi sanctum & purum continet, quia est medium, per quod Deus hominem sanctificat, & quia opponitur inquinamentis mundi, quae hominem contaminant & profanant. Quidam addunt, etiam ideò vocari sanctum, quod sit saenctè servandum, quod sanctum Deum proprimario & formali obiecto habeat, quod sancti in vita aeterna illud perfectissimè impleturi sint Sed priùs adductae rationes sunt principales. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. locum hunc Apostolicum his verbis adducit. Melius eis erat, non nosse viam iustitiae, quam post agnitionem retrorsum converti, & relinquere sanctum mandatum, quod eis traditum est.

## 2:22
Connection. The Apostle illustrates what he had said with two similitudes, namely, of the dog returned to its vomit and the sow that was washed returning to the wallowing in the mire.

Exposition of the text. συμβεβηκε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμὶας. Vulg. For it has happened unto them according to the true proverb i.e., that which is accustomed to be said by a true proverb. The Greek has an adversative. But it has happened unto them &c. meanwhile it cannot be denied that the adversative in this place performs the role of either a rational (examples of which signification occur John 17. v. 3.Luke 20. v. 38. whence Augustine, book on faith and works, chapter 25, cites the passage thus, For the thing of the true proverb has happened unto them.) or a copulative (whence Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 2, alleges the passage thus, And that most true proverb is completed in them) Luther, with the adversative omitted, rendered it. Es ist ihnen wiederfahren das wahre Sprich Wort.

By the name παροιμίας the Apostle looks back to the book of the Solomonic proverbs, from which the sentence that he adduces is taken, which to the Hebrews is משלי but to the Greeks παροιμίαι. Concerning this παροιμίας word Basil discourses thus in his homily on Proverbs. τὸ τῶν παροιμιῶν ὄνομα ἐπὶ τῶν δημοδεστέρων λόγων παρὰ τοῖς ἔξωθεν τέτακται, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς λαλουμένων, ὡς τὰ πολλὰ; οἶμος γὰρ ἡ ὁδος ὀνομάζεται. The name of proverbs is composed from that which is commonly said among outsiders (profane authors) and for the most part from those things which are said in the crossroads, οἰμος for it is called a way. Afterwards he adds a double παροιμίας definition. The former is thus, that it is ῥῆμα παρόδιον τετρυμμένον ἐν τῇ χρήσει τῶν πολλῶν καὶ ἀπὸ ὀλίγων ἐπὶ πλείονα ὅμοια ματαλυφθῆναι δυνάμενον, a word according to the way by the usage of many a common thing and one which can be transferred from a few to many similar things. The latter is this, that it is λόγος ὠφέλιμος μετ' ἐπικρύψεως μετρίας ἐκδεδοκμενος πολὺ μὲν τὸ αὐτοθεν χρήσιμον περιεχων, πολλὴν δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ βάθει τὴν διάνοιαν συγκαλύπτων, a useful discourse expressed under a moderate concealment, indeed exhibiting much utility, but covering much understanding in the depths or in the recess. Some, however, derive this word not from οἶμος, but from οἴμη, which signifies word, so that παροιμία corresponds to the Latin word proverb.

Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα. Vulg. The dog is returned to his own vomit, understand to be swallowed again. This sentence exists Prov. 26. v. 11. As a dog that returneth to his vomit, so is the fool that repeateth his folly. The LXX rendered it thus. ὥσπερ κύων ὅταν ἐπέλθη ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἔμετον, καὶ μισητὸς γένηται, οὕτως ἀφρωντῇ ἑαυτοῦ κακία ἀναστρέψας ἐπὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίαν. From which it appears, by the occasion that Peter had said concerning those seduced ones themselves ἐπιστρέψαι from the holy commandment and again to be entangled μιάσμασι in the pollutions of this world, he himself was led to that foul similitude and to the passage Prov. 26. v. 11.. Chrysostom, homily 5 on 1 Timothy 2, brings forward the same similitude in almost the same words in which it is described in the Proverbs of Solomon by the LXX Interpreters. Ἀνθρωπος he says, ἀποστρέφων ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας αὑτοῦ καὶ πάλιν πορευόμενος, καὶ τὰ αὐτὰ ποιῶν ὥσπερ κύων ἔστιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἴδιον ἔμετον ἐπιστρέφων.. But Peter in this place instead of τὸν ἔμετον placed τὸ ἐξέραμα, that which is evacuated or drawn out, because food is cast out and evacuated by vomiting. For ἐξέραμα ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐξερᾶν is derived to drain, to evacuate. The scholiast of Aristophanes says that word ἐξεράω was made ἀπὸ τῆς ἔρας that is τῆς γῆς, so that ἐξεράσαι may be εἰς τὴν γὴν μεταβάλλειν to cast upon the ground, whence also some Greek Codices for ἐξέραμα in this place read ἐξέρασμα. The Syrian has the noun [תיובא] from the root [תוב] to return, to go back, for vomiting is as it were a returning of food or a bringing back of it from the voice, which word Solomon also uses Prov. 26. v. 11.

Καὶ ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κύλισμα βορβόρου. Vulg. And the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire. In Greek into the wallowing place or to the wallowing place of mire, namely ἐπιστρέψασα which is to be repeated from the former proverb. Καὶ is placed absolutely, but it is to be understood likewise from the preceding words.

And that which is accustomed to be said in another true-word happens to them. For ὗς the Syrian places the noun [חזיררתא] signifying a sow, a pig from the root [חזר] to return, to turn back, because it is its characteristic to return to filth. Luther, looking to the sense, rendered it Die Sau weltzet sich nach der Schwemme wieder in Koth..

Latin:

Connexio. Illustrat Apostolus, qui dixerat, duabus similitudinibus, videlicet canis ad vomitum reversi & suis lotae ad volutabrum luti redeuntis.

Textus expositio. συμβεβηκε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμὶας. Vulg. Contigit enim eis illud veri proverbii h. e. quod vero proverbio dici solet. Graeca habent adversativam. Contigit autem illis &c. interim negari nequit, adversativam hoc loco fungi vice vel rationativae (cuius significationis exempla occurrunt Ioh. 17. v. 3.Luc. 20. v. 38. unde Augustin. l. de fide & operibus. cap. 25. locum sic citat, Contigit enim illis res veri proverbii.) vel copulativae (unde Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian cap. 2. locum sic allegat, Completumque est in eis verissimum illud proverbium) Lutherus omissâ adversativâ reddidit. Es ist ihnen wiederfahren das wahre Sprich Wort.

Nomine παροιμίας respicit Apostolus ad librum prover biorum Salomonaeorum, ex quibus sententia, quam adducit, est petita, qui Hebraeis משלי Graecis verò παροιμίαι. De hac παροιμίας voce sic disserit Basilius hom. in Prov. τὸ τῶν παροιμιῶν ὄνομα ἐπὶ τῶν δημοδεστέρων λόγων παρὰ τοῖς ἔξωθεν τέτακται, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς λαλουμένων, ὡς τὰ πολλὰ; οἶμος γὰρ ἡ ὁδος ὀνομάζεται.Proverbiorum nomen de eo, quod vulgariter dicitur apud externos (profanos autores) compositum est & de illis plerumque, quae in triviis dicuntur,οἰμοςenim via nominatur. Postea subiicit duplicem παροιμίας definitionem. Prior sic habet, quod sitῥῆμα παρόδιον τετρυμμένον ἐν τῇ χρήσει τῶν πολλῶν καὶ ἀπὸ ὀλίγων ἐπὶ πλείονα ὅμοια ματαλυφθῆναι δυνάμενον,verbum iuxta viam usu multorum tritum & quod à paucis ad plura similia transferri potest. Posterior haec est, quod sitλόγος ὠφέλιμος μετ' ἐπικρύψεως μετρίας ἐκδεδοκμενος πολὺ μὲν τὸ αὐτοθεν χρήσιμον περιεχων, πολλὴν δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ βάθει τὴν διάνοιαν συγκαλύπτων,sermo utilis sub occultatione mediocri expressus, multum quidem utilitatis exhibens, in fundo autem sive in recessu multam intelligentiam contegens. Quidam tamen non ab οἶμος, sed ab οἴμη, quod verbum significat, vocem hanc deducunt, ut παροιμία respondeat voci Latinae proverbium.

Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα. Vulg. Canis reversus ad suum vomitum, subintellige resorbendum. Extat haec sententia Prov. 26. v. 11.Sicut canis, qui revertitur ad vomitum suum, sic imprudens qui iterat stultitiam suam. LXX. sic reddiderunt. ὥσπερ κύων ὅταν ἐπέλθη ἐπὶ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἔμετον, καὶ μισητὸς γένηται, οὕτως ἀφρωντῇ ἑαυτοῦ κακία ἀναστρέψας ἐπὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτίαν. Ex quo apparet, occasione ea, quòd Petrus de seductis illis dixerat ipsosἐπιστρέψαιà sancto mandato & iterum implicariμιάσμασιinquinamentis huius mundi, ipsum ad foedam illam similitudinem & ad locum Prov. 26. v. 11. esse deductum. Chrysostomus homil. 5. in 1. Timoth. 2. iisdem ferè verbis, quibus haec similitudo in proverbiis Salomonae is à LXX. Interpp. describitur, eandem adducit. Ἀνθρωπος inquit, ἀποστρέφων ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας αὑτοῦ καὶ πάλιν πορευόμενος, καὶ τὰ αὐτὰ ποιῶν ὥσπερ κύων ἔστιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἴδιον ἔμετον ἐπιστρέφων.. Sed Petrus hoc loco pro τὸν ἔμετον posuit τὸ ἐξέραμα, id quod evacuatum seu eductum est, quia cibus vomitu reiicitur & evacuatur. Deducitur enim ἐξέραμα ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐξερᾶνexhaurire, evacuare. Scholiastes Aristophanis verbum illud ἐξεράω ait factum esseἀπὸ τῆς ἔρας h. e. τῆς γῆς, ut ἐξεράσαι sit εἰς τὴν γὴν μεταβάλλεινin terram proiicere, unde etiam quidam Graeci Codices pro ἐξέραμα h. l. legunt ἐξέρασμα. Syrus habet nomen [תיובא] à rad. [תוב]redire reverti, vomitus enim est quasi cibi reversio aut eius ex voce reductio, quâ voce etiam Salomon utitur Prov. 26. v. 11.

Καὶ ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κύλισμα βορβόρου. Vulg. Et sus lota involutabro luti. Graecè in volutabrum vel ad volutabrum luti, scilicet ἐπιστρέψασα quod ex priore paraemia repetendum. Καὶ ponitur absolutè, subintelligendum verò itidem ex verbis praecedentibus.

Et accidit eis illud, quod in altero veriverbio dici consuevit. Pro ὗς Syrus ponit nomen [חזיררתא] significans suem, porcum â rad. [חזר]redire, reverti, quòd eius proprium sit ad sordes redire. Lutherus ad sensum respiciens reddidit. Die Sau weltzet sich nach der Schwemme wieder in Koth.

## 3:1-2
Connection. 1. Before he forewarns and fortifies those to whom he writes against the scoffers denying the final coming of Christ to judgment, he again indicates the scope of this writing of his, which he had already done before, cap. 1. v. 12. namely, that he might confirm them in the doctrine of Christ, in which, as being confirmed by the testimonies of the Prophets and Apostles, they ought to remain constantly.

2. Thus, therefore, he briefly repeats the sum of those things which he had proposed in chapter 1 from verse 16 to the end of the chapter, for there also he had confirmed the doctrine of the Gospel by the testimonies of both the Apostles and the Prophets.

Exposition of the text. Ταύτην ἤδη ἀγαπητοὶ δευτέραν ὑμῖν γράφω ἐπιστολὴν. Vulg. This behold to you, dearest, I write the second Epistle to you. The Greek properly has. This now, beloved, I write the second Epistle to you. For ἤδη the Interpreter reads ἰδοὺ Behold. But all Greek codices constantly read ἤδη, which the Syrian also expressed [כדו] The name ἁγαπητοὶ the Syrian rendered, [חביבי] my beloved, as if it is in the Greek, ἁγαπητοὶ μου. Ἐν αἷς διεγείρω ὑμῶν ἐν ὑπομνήσει τὴν εἰλικρινῆ διάνοιαν. Vulg. in which I stir up your sincere mind in admonition. The word διεγείρειν cap. 1. vers. 13. he had rendered by to stir up, here he expresses it more correctly by to stir up, out of the lethargy of torpor, lukewarmness, and forgetfulness.

In the preceding there is the singular noun ἐπιστολὴν, with it the plural noun εν αις. does not seem to agree. Bede in his commentary answers thus. In which, he says in the Epistles or in them, to whom he writes the Epistles. But the latter anyone sees to be forced. Therefore some think there is something underlying here σολοικοφανὲς to avoid which they translate the words of Peter thus. These second letters I write to you. But far be it that we should attribute a solecism to the Holy Spirit speaking and writing through Peter. It is to be noted, therefore, that the construction refers to the sense, not to the words. For he who asserts that he is writing a second Epistle presupposes that a first was written by him, and thus in reality of two Epistles he makes mention. Something must therefore be understood in this way. I am now writing this second Epistle to you after the former, or besides the first. ἐν αἷς namely ἐπιστολαῖς, in which, that is, in both of which I stir up your sincere mind.

Εἰλικρινὴς is sincere, pure, unpainted, as if to say τῇ εἴλῃ or to εἴλην κρινόμενος examined and judged by the splendor of the Sun, because to εἴλην τὰ μεμιγμένα καὶ τὰ ἀμιγῆ with easy effort διακρίνεται. 1. Cor. 5. vers. 8. are joined εἰλικρίνεια καὶ ἀλήθεια truth opposed to all paint. 2. Cor. 1. v. 12. ἁπλότης καὶ εἰλικρίνεια, for what is sincere, that is simple and unmixed. The Syrian rendered it by [שפיר] elegant, beautiful, good; for what is sincere and pure, that is also beautiful. Therefore the Apostle attributes to those to whom he writes εἰλικρινῆ διάνοιαν, because he was persuaded that they were of a sincere mind and an open spirit. The little word ὑπομνήσεως shows that the Apostle establishes that they do not need more abundant information so much as serious admonition, which he expresses thus in more explicit words cap. 1. vers. 12. I will not neglect to always ὑπομιμνήσκειν remind you of these things, and indeed knowing and confirmed in the present truth. Moreover ἐν ὑπομνήσει is put for δι' ὑπομνήσεως by admonition, since it was the medium of excitation and exhortation to constancy in the faith. The interlinear gloss seems to have accepted it actively that I may admonish you and you may admonish others. In the same way Thomas, that being admonished you may be able to admonish 2. Cor. 1. v. 6. But the Apostle speaks properly and directly of his own admonition. The Syrian rendered [בעוהדנא] which Pococke translates in remembrance Phil. 1. v. 3. 2. Tim. 1. v. 5. But it can also be translated in admonition, or by calling back into memory, because [עהד] in Aphel signifies to make to remember, or to call back into memory. Erasmus for ἐν ὑπομνήσει reads ἐν ἐπιγνώσει in the same way also Luther seems to have read, for thus he rendered it. In welcher ich erwecke und erkenne euern lauteren Sinn.

Μνησθῆναι τῶν προειρημένων ῥημάτων ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων Προφήτων The Vulgate rendered, that you may be mindful of those words which I foretold by the holy Prophets. The Interpreter perverted and obscured the sense, which in the Greek is The text is sufficiently clear. For the little word τῶν προειρημένων is not to be referred to Peter writing, which the Vulgate Interpreter did, but to the Prophets, in this way: That you may be mindful of those words which were foretold by the holy Prophets, in which way the Syrian also rendered it, that you may remember the words [דקדמי אתאמרי] which were spoken before, or were foretold by the Prophets. Moreover, the Vulgate Interpreter himself rendered the parallel passage of Jude v. 17. in the same way: But you, most beloved, be mindful of the words τῶν προειρημένων ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀποστόλων, which were foretold by the Apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Καὶ τῆς τῶν Ἀποστόλων ἡμῶν ἐντολῆς τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος. Vulg. And of your Apostles of the commandments of the Lord and Savior. In the word ἡμῶν he changed the first person into the second. For because Peter himself is in the number of the Apostles, therefore it seemed absurd to him to translate of our Apostles, and so he changed it into the pronoun of the second person of your. But all Greek Codices, the Complutensian excepted, constantly read ἡμῶν in the first person. He also changed the singular τῆς ἐντολῆς into the plural τῶν ἐντολῶν,, although the singular is read likewise in all Greek Codices. The little word ἐντολῆς in this place is taken generally for doctrine, just as the Hebrew תורה likewise in general denotes doctrine.

Furthermore, concerning the genuine version and sense of the Greek text, three opinions occur.

1. Some render it thus: That you may be mindful of the commandment of the Lord and Savior, delivered to you by us the Apostles. They order and complete the text thus.

Καὶ τῆς τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἐντολῆς (δοθείσης or προειρημένης ὑπὸ) τῶν ἡμῶν Ἀποστὸλων. The Syrian expressed this sense, who rendered this passage thus: That you may be mindful of the commandment of our Lord and Savior [דביד] which was by the hand of the Apostles, that is, which was delivered to you by the ministry of the Apostles.

2. Some translate thus: That you may be mindful of the commandment, delivered to you both by the Apostles and by the Lord and Savior. They order the text thus: Καὶ τῆς τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἐντολῆς (καὶ) τῶν ἡμῶν Ἀποστόλων namely ἐντολῆς. to which it can be referred, which the Greek Scholia say, τὸ ὑπὸ serves for three, namely, τῶν προφητῶν Ἀποστόλων, Κυρίου Ιησοῦ.

3. Erasmus thinks it should be rendered thus. That you may be mindful of our commandment, who are Apostles of the Lord and Savior, that is, that you may be mindful of the commandment which you received from us, the Apostles of the Lord and Savior. According to this exposition, the text is to be ordered thus: καὶ τῆς ἐντολῆς ἡμῶν τῶν Ἀποστόλων τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος, in which way Luther also rendered it, Daß ihr gedencket an unser Gebot / die wir sind Apostel des Herrn und Heilandes.

4. Closely approaching this explanation is that by which the pronoun ἡμῶν is joined with the genitives κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος in this way, That you may be mindful τῆς ἐντολῆς τῶν Ἀποστόλοων τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν, of the commandment (viz. which you received) from the Apostles of our Lord and Savior (Jesus Christ.)

We prove this exposition, brought forward in the third place, from this, 1. that it inflicts no force upon the text, but only establishes a certain transposition of words, not infrequent in the Scriptures, especially also in the Petrine Epistles. Compare 1. Petr. 1. v. 11.cap. 3. v. 21.2. Petr. 1. v. 19.

2. That it exactly agrees with the former member, in which mention is made of the words foretold by the Prophets, so that by this reason the testimonies of the Prophets and Apostles concerning the doctrine of the Gospel are joined, just as they had also been joined in cap. 1. v. 16. & following.

3. That it corresponds to the parallel passage Jude v. 17. μνήσθητε τῶν ῥημάτων τῶν προειρημένων ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀποστόλων τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. The thing itself testifies that that passage is parallel to this one of ours, except that Jude makes mention only of the Apostles, but Peter, according to the reason of his institution, joins the Prophets to them.

Estius acknowledges that this exposition most greatly agrees with the Greek text, which he therefore embraces, having dismissed the Vulgate version. Bartholomaeus Petrus, successor to Estius in the professorship, who wrote additions to the same commentaries, attempts to reduce the Vulgate version to the same sense, but not without manifest force inflicted upon it. It approaches, he says, to this sense, which is in our Vulgate, if we order and distinguish it thus. That you may be mindful of those words spoken by the holy Prophets, which I have foretold in this very Epistle; likewise be mindful of the precepts, which we your Apostles gave to you, the same precepts of the Lord and Savior. But to whom, I ask, does this meaning come to mind for one reading the Vulgate version?

It is asked in this place. 1. Why does the Apostle say that he is stirring up their sincere mind by way of reminder in this and the former Epistle? Resp. So that he may win their goodwill for himself, and meet a silent objection. For those to whom he was writing could have objected: There was not such a need for us to be animated and stirred up to constancy in the Christian faith, since we are devoted to this doctrine with a sincere heart. The Apostle answers: I know indeed very well that you are of a sincere heart and a candid breast, nor do I suspect anything sinister about you; meanwhile, however, both by reason of my Apostolic office and by reason of the danger to be feared for you from false teachers and Epicurean mockers, I wished, nay, I even owed it, to stir you up to constancy in the doctrine by these letters of mine.

Q. 2. What commandment does Peter understand in this place? Resp. 1. Salmeron thinks that the commandments concerning the love of GOD and neighbor, to which all other things are referred, are understood. But from a comparison of chapter 1 of this Epistle, it is manifest that the Apostle wished to exhort and remind those to whom he writes not only of the holiness of life, consisting in the love of GOD and neighbor, but also of guarding the sincerity of the doctrine. 2. Some take it specifically concerning the commandment of constancy, that they ought to persist constant in the profession of the Christian faith, and to beware solicitously for themselves against all Pseudo-Prophets who attempt to lead them away from it, which commandment he had inculcated in chapter 1 and 2 to them. 3. But because the Apostle makes mention in general of those things which were said by the Prophets and Apostles, therefore the name of commandment is more correctly taken concerning the whole Christian doctrine, confirmed by the testimony of the Prophets and Apostles, which he calls back to their memory, having been preached to them before by living voice. For ἐντολή, corresponding to the Hebrew מצוה, signifies doctrine. cap. 2. vers. 21. 4. But in truth, there is not a great difference between these two latter opinions. For he calls those things which were said by the Prophets and Apostles for the confirmation of Christian doctrine back to their memory for this reason, that they may be constant in Christian doctrine and the profession of faith. 5. From the parallel passage Jude v. 18. it could seem to be gathered that by this Apostolic ἐντολὴν one ought to understand Pauline exhortations concerning avoiding the doctrines of demons 1. Tim. 4. v. 1. and fleeing the company of the impious who will exist toward the end of the world 2. Tim. 3. v. 1.. But the passage of Jude does not extend as widely as this one of ours.

Ἐναντιοφανεία. The Apostle says that he is writing this second Epistle. But the Apostles did not receive from Christ the command of writing, but of preaching. Marc. 16. v. 15. Response: in the parallel passage Matth. 28. v. 19. they are commanded to teach all nations, and indeed the duty of teaching is performed not only by the preaching of the living voice, but also by writing. Add that they are also commanded to teach all nations of the time to follow, as is evident from v. 20, a thing which they could by no means perform by living voice without writing. Compare Exeg. tom. 1. loc. 1. §. 23. and following.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. From the words of Peter, 'I write this second Epistle to you,' the opinion of Erasmus is convicted of falsehood, by which he maintains that Peter, before those two Epistles which still exist today, had written yet another Epistle to the same people, which perished through the injury of time. A thing which those eagerly embrace who strive to prove the imperfection of Scripture from certain lost divine and Canonical writings. But if Peter had written another before the first Epistle, he ought to have said that it was being written by him not as the second, but as the third. Deservedly, therefore, Estius at this place annotates thus: Blessed Peter, naming this second Epistle written to them, sufficiently signifies that he had previously given to the same people, not two, nor more, but one Epistle.

2. That Peter commends not only Apostolic precepts, but also Prophetic words to those to whom he writes, is to be opposed to the Anabaptists and Photinians, who judge those things which were written by the Prophets in the O. T. to be of less authority than those from the Apostles in the N. T. Schmalzius in refutation of Smiglecius p. 79: Little care is to be taken of what a Prophet of the O. covenant says about the worship of God. Theoph. Nicolaides against Midzibezium p. 68: This testimony is indeed received, but it would have been worth more if an Apostle had said it.

3. Since the Apostle assigns this end to both Epistles written by him, that they might be mindful of the words which were foretold by the Prophets, and of his own command, it is gathered from this that the Prophets and Apostles consigned to letters the very same doctrine which they delivered by living voice. For not only the faithful who in their time lived, they wished to make mindful of their doctrine, but also to transmit the same to posterity, so that those who were to live around the last times of the world might have a certain and immovable truth, which they once handed down by living voice.

4. Peter teaches in this place that the true and only fountain of salvation is the word of God comprised in the Prophetic and Apostolic writings. This is to be opposed to the Swencfeldians, Anabaptists, and Weigelians, who, having spurned the external word, await interior revelations and enthusiasms.

5. Peter absolutely calls Christ Κύριον καὶ σωτῆρα.. He is therefore the true God, because the word κύριος corresponds in the N. T. to the Hebrew IEHOVAH, which is the property of the only true God, and αὐποκρατορικῶς to save is likewise the work proper to the only true God, Esai. 45. v. 11. Beside me there is no Savior. This is to be opposed to the Photinians who deny the Deity of Christ.

Ἐκδίκησις. The Papists gather from the word ὑπομνήσεως, that the proper and chief end of Scripture is not that it should be the rule of faith, but that it should be a certain useful reminder for preserving the doctrine received from preaching. But what must be answered, we have explained above cap. 1. v. 12.

Observations. 1. It is a great benefit of GOD that men can communicate the thoughts of their minds to one another not only by voice, but also by writings. Aristot lib. περὶ ἑρμην. part. 1. cap. 1. ἔστι μὲν τὰ ἐν τῇ φωνῇ τῶν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ παθημάτων σύμβολα; καὶ τὰ γραφόμενα τῶν ἐν τῇ φωνῇ,

2. But it is by far the greatest benefit of GOD that He willed His holy word not only to be preached by the Prophets and Apostles by living voice, but also to be reduced to letters. This was required by the brevity of human life, the multitude of men, the unfaithfulness to be expected from tradition in custody, the weakness of human memory, the stability of heavenly doctrine, and the perversity of heretics. Confer. Exeges. tom. 1. Loc. 1. §. 19.
