A. chap. 11. that he was accustomed to say in a proverb, σπεῦδε βραδέως, admonishing that both the speed of industry and the slowness of diligence should be applied together to the matter at hand.

3. It is said most simply that the preposition εἰς is to be understood (such ellipses of prepositions are frequent in the Scriptures) in this way, expecting and hastening unto the coming, or as Augustine reads in his book on faith and works, chapter 14, unto the presence of the day of the Lord, in which way also the Prophetic passage Isa. 16. v. 5. can be accepted, σπεύδων εἰς δικαιοσύνην, since in the Hebrew it is מהר, which is intransitive. Thus, therefore, the sense will be: You ought not only to patiently expect the day of the Lord, and if the Lord should delay, nevertheless to endure, always prepared to receive him with joy when he comes Hab. 2. v. 3. Luke 12. v. 36. but also to hasten to the meeting of the Lord, and most eagerly to desire his coming, by the example of the virgins who in the Evangelical parable are said to have gone to meet the Bridegroom with lamps Matt. 25. v. 1. so that by this reasoning both members of the Apostolic exhortation are sought from the parables of Christ the Master. In the same sense Luther rendered Daß ihr wartet und eilet zu der Zukunfft des Tages des Herrn.

Τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ παρουσίας. In that way also the Syriac translates in the Pococke edition, but the other Syriac, upon which Dionysius commented, rendered: when you expect the day of the coming of God, as if it were in the Greek, Τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ παρουσίας. But the former reading is genuine.

Τὴν παρουσίαν Augustine in the said work translates presence, but it is more correctly rendered in this place by coming, as appears from v. 10. The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night. For θεοῦ in certain Latin Codices it is read, of the Lord, in which way also Luther rendered, Den Tag des Herrn. But the Greek Codices constantly read θεοῦ, which most Latin Codices also have. Estius suspects that the name of the Lord crept in for God because elsewhere it is called the day of the Lord everywhere, and because the day of God seems to have something cacophonous. But whether of God or of the Lord is read, it is manifest that Christ is understood, who is called both God Acts 20. v. 28. Tit. 2. v. 13. and Lord 1. Cor. 8. v. 6. and elsewhere passim. For it is his final coming to judgment that is treated here.

Δι' ἥν οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται. Vulg. by whom the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved. But in the Greek it is by which, i.e., the day or the coming, for the diversity of gender prevents it from being referred to God. Those who refer it to ἡμέραν establish that δι' ἥν is placed by Hebrew phrase for ἐν ἧ As inv. 10.the Apostle had said, The day of the Lord will come, ἐν ἧ in which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise. Luth. In welchem die Himmel vom Feuer werden zergehen . But it is more conveniently referred to παρουσίαν, so that the sense may be, that through the coming of that day, that is, by the power of that coming, this whole universe is to be destroyed, as is said in Apoc. 20. v. 11. And I saw a great white throne and him who sat upon it, from whose face the earth and heaven fled away, and there was no place found for them.

Πυρούμενοι is set on fire and inflamed, burning. The Syrian renders [בנורא מתבחרין] tested by fire, just as χρυσίον πεπυρωμένον ἐκ πυρὸς is gold tried in the fireApoc. 3. v. 18. which version favors the opinion concerning the change of the heavens only according to qualities, not a substantial destruction. The word λυθήσονται is accepted in the way in which the Apostle had spoken concerning the Elements in v. 10., στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα λυθήσονται and v. 11. τούτων οὐν πάντων λυομένων the Apostle had said v. 7. the heavens, which now are, and the earth are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment; here he shows, that at the coming of that day the heavens set on fire shall be dissolved.

Καὶ τὰ στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τακήσεται. Vulg. And the Elements shall melt with fervent heat. But in the Greek there is ηαυσυμενα, which properly signifies burning; and τακήσεται which is shall melt, with the metaphor drawn from wax brought near to fire, which immediately is loosened and melts together. In some Codices there is held the verb of the present tense τήκεται, which is placed through enallage of tense for τήξεται. But the Complutensian, the Royal, and most approved Codices have the future τακήσεται, which agrees more with the preceding verb λυθήσονται. Augustine in book 10 of the City of God, chapter 18, rendered it, shall be boiled down. The Vulgate version, which rendered, shall melt, draws the metaphor from that kind of disease which is called consumption, by which if any animals are consumed, they are near to destruction. The LXX use for בקע noise and with violence it dividesMich. 1. v. 4. τακήσονται, where it is added, as wax from the face of the fire; המס for liquidEsa. 64. v. 2. ὡς κηρὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου πυρὸς τήκεται, for כלה altogether ceased, failed.Iob. 11. v. 20.cap. 17. v. 5. for מוג is dissolved, is liquefiedEx. 15. v. 15.Psal. 74. v. 3. For מסס it melts, so that it flows down,Iud. 15. v. 14.Ps. 21. v. 15. for מקק wasted awayLev. 26. v. 39.Esai. 34. v. 4. etc. which passage is parallel to this one of ours, τακήσονται πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν. for נזל flowed downEsai. 64. v. 1. for קדח was kindled, was set on fireEsai. 64. v. 1. for התם consumed it was, which includes the total destruction of the thing to which it is attributed, Ezech. 24. v. 10. which all meanings agree with this passage. The Syrian rendered it by [נשחון] from the root [שח] or [שחא] for both are found, it is melted, which corresponds to the word τηκεται.. A comparison must indeed be instituted between this verse and the preceding one. 10. In v. 10. the Apostle says concerning the heavens, οἱ οὐρανοὶ ῥοιζηδὸν παρελευσονται; in this v. 12. οἱ οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται. In v. 10. he says concerning the Elements, στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα λυθήσονται, in this vers. 12. στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τακήσεται. From which it is gathered that the future destruction of the heavens and the Elements by fire will be the same. For lest anyone should think that the heavens would be free from the conflagration, because the Apostle had said of them in v. 10. simply, παρελεύσονται, therefore in v. 12. he adds πυρέμενοι λυθήσονται. Hence also Luther rendered both the word λυθήσονται in v. 10. and the word τακήσεται used in v. 12. concerning the Elements with one and the same term, Die Elemente werden für Hitze schmelzen oder zerschmeltzen. By equal reasoning he also rendered both the word παρελεύσονται in v. 10. and the word λυθήσονται used in v. 12. concerning the heavens with one and the same term. Die Himmel werden zergehen

Latin:

Connexio. Applicat exhortationem generalem in versu proximè praecedente propositam ad suum institutum, ac repetit descriptionem modi, quo mundum praedixerat interiturum.

Textus expositio. Προσδοκῶντας καὶ σπεύδοντας τὴν παρουσίαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας. Vulg. Expectantes & properantes in adventum dici Dei. Quod debeamus προσδοκᾷν expectare adventum diei Dei, illud desumsit Petrus ex parabola Magistri sui de servis expectantibus Dominum, quando revertatur à nuptiis Luc. 12. vers. 36. (quamvis ibi non habeatur verbum προσδοκᾷν, sed προσδέχεσθαι) ac verè pii Tit. 2. v. 13. sic describuntur, quòd sint προσδεχόμενοι τὴν μαρακίαν ἐλπίδα καὶ ἐπιφάνειαν τῆς δόξης τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ, qui locus huic nostro est parallelus.

Quòd autem debeamus non solùm προσδοκᾷν, sed etiam σπεύδειν illius diei adventum, illud, quo sensu accipiendum sit, tùm ratione phraseos, tùm ipsius rei, videtur cum quadam difficultate coniunctum.

1. Erasmus verbum σπεύδειν aequè, ac verbum προσδοκᾷν accipit transitivè, sic enim h. l. vertit. Expectantes & accelerantes adventum diei &c. quâ ratione foret sensus, quòd diligenti ac serio bo-norum operum studio id agere debeamus, ut novissimus Christi adventus acceleretur. Atqui. 1. verbum σπεύδειν nuspiam in N. Test. transitivè, sed semper intransitivè sive neutraliter accipitur, Luc. 2. v. 16.cap. 19. v. 5. & 6.Actor. 20. v. 16.cap. 22. v. 18. Apud LXX. Interpp. semel duntaxat cum accusativo rei construitur Esa. 16. vers. 5.σπεύδων δικαιοσύνειν, de quo loco idem statuendum, quod de nostro Apostolico. Apud profanos Scriptores σπεύδειν quandoque cum accusativo iungitur, ut γάμους σπεύδειν apud Homerum Odyss. T. sed tùm plerunque usurpatur pro incumbere in rem aliquam, contendere ad rem aliquam & anniti. Pindar. Pyth. 3. βίον ἀθάνατον σπεῦδε. Homerus Iliad. ν. ταῦτα χρὴ σπεύδειν. Eurip. σπεύδω σὸν ἀγαθὸν,incumbo in tuum commodum. 2. Petrus hoc loco non tribuit nobis accelerationem illius diei, sicut & nuspiam alibi in Scripturis ea piis tribuitur, sed potiùs ipsi Christo, de quo dicit, quòd non tardet promissum.

2. Quidam participium σπεύδοντες exponunt adverbialiter, expectantes properando, vel proporanterμετὰ σπουδῆςadventum diei Dei, ut sic expectatio patientem morae tolerantiam, properatio verò studium torpori oppositum significet, sicut de Augusto Imp. memorat Gellius lib. 10. N. A. cap. 11. quod proverbio dicere fuerit solitus,σπεῦδε βραδέως, admonens, ut ad rem agendam simul adhiberetur & industriae celeritas & diligentiae tarditas.

3. Simplicissimè dicitur, subaudiendam esse praepositionem εἰς (quales propositionum ellipses in Scripturis sunt frequentes) hoc modo, expectantes & properantes in adventum, vel ut Augustinus legit lib. de fide & operibus cap. 14. ad praesentiam diei Domini, quo modo etiam locus Propheticus Esa. 16. v. 5. accipi potest, σπεύδων εἰς δικαιοσύνην, cùm in Hebraeo sit מהר, quod est intransitivum. Sic ergò erit sensus. Non solùm patienter diem Domini debetis expectare, ac si moram fecerit Dominus, nihilo minùs perdurare, semper parati ad eum, quando venerit, cum gaudio excipiendumHab. 2. v. 3.Luc. 12. v. 36. sed etiam in occursum Domini properare, & adventum illius cupidissimè desiderare, exemplo virginum, quae in parabola Evangelica cum lampadibus Sponso obviam ivisse dicuntur Matth. 25. v. 1. ut hac ratione utrumque membrum Apostolicae exhortationis ex parabolis Christi Magistri sit petitum. Eodem sensu reddidit Luth. Daß ihr wartet und eilet zu der Zukunfft des Tages des Herrn.

Τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ παρουσίας. Eo quoque modo vertit Syrus in editione Pococke, sed Syrus alter, in quem Dionysius commentatus est, reddidit: cùm expectetis diem adventûs Dei, ac si in Graeco esset, Τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ παρουσίας. Sed prior lectio est genuina.

Τὴν παρουσίαν Augustinus d. l. vertit praesentiam, sed rectiùs hoc loco redditur per adventum, ut apparet ex v. 10.Veniet dies Domini, sicut fur in nocte. Pro θεοῦ in quibusdam Codd. Latinis legitur, Domini, quo modo etiam Luth. reddidit, Den Tag des Herrn. Sed Graeci Codd. constanter legunt θεοῦ, quod etiam habent plerique Codd. Latini. Estius suspicatur, nomen Domini pro Dei propterea irrepsisse, quod alibi passim vocetur dies Domini, quodque dies Dei cacophonum quid habere videatur. Sive autem Dei, sive Domini legatur, manifestum est, Christum intelligi, qui & Deus Act. 20. v. 28.Tit. 2. v. 13. & Dominus 1. Cor. 8. v. 6. & alibi passim appellatur. De eius enim novissimo ad iudicium adventu hîc agitur.

Δι' ἥν οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται. Vulg. per quem caeli ardentes solventur. Sed in Graeco est per quam sc. diem vel adventum, quo minùs enim referatur ad Deum, obstat generis diversitas. Qui ad ἡμέραν referunt, statuunt δι' ἥνphrasi Hebraicâ positum esse proἐν ἧ sicut inv. 10.Apostolus dixerat, Adveniet dies Domini,ἐν ἧin quâ caeli magno impetu transibunt. Luth. In welchem die Himmel vom Feuer werden zergehen. Sed commodiùs refertur ad παρουσίαν, ut sit sensus, per adventum diei illius h. e. virtute illius adventus totum hoc universum destructum iri, sicut Apoc. 20. v. 11. dicitur. Et vidi thronum magnum candidum & sedentem super eum, à cuius conspectu fugit terra & caelum, & locus non est inventus eis.

Πυρούμενοιest igne accensi & inflammati, conflagrantes. Syrus redd. [בנורא מתבחרין]igne probati, sicut χρυσίον πεπυρωμένον ἐκ πυρὸς est aurum igni exploratumApoc. 3. v. 18. quae versio favet sententiae de caelorum tantùm secundùm qualitates mutatione, non substantiali interitu. Verbum λυθήσονται eo modo accipitur, quo in v. 10. de Elementis dixerat Apostolus, στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα λυθήσονται & v. 11.τούτων οὐν πάντων λυομένων dixerat Apostolus v. 7. caelos, qui nunc sunt, & terram reservari igni in diem iudicii; hîc ostendit, in adventu illius diei caelos igni accensos dissolutum iri.

Καὶ τὰ στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τακήσεται. Vulg. Et Elementa ignis ardore tabescent. Sed in Graeco est ηαυσυμενα, quod propriè significat aestuantia; ac τακήσεται quod est liquescent, ductâ metaphorâ à cera igni admotâ, quae statim solvitur ac colliquescit. In quibusdam. Codd. habetur verbum praesentis temporis τήκεται, quod per enallagen temporis positum pro τήξεται. Sed Complutensis, Regius ac probati Codd. plerique habent futurum τακήσεται, quod magis congruit praecedenti verbo λυθήσονται. Augustinus d. l. 10. de C. D. cap. 18. reddidit, decoquentur. Versio vulgata, quae reddidit, tabescent, metaphoram ducit à specie illâ morbi, quae tabes vocatur, quâ si quae animalia conficiuntur, interitui sunt propinqua. LXX. utuntur pro בקעimpetu ac vi disciditMich. 1. v. 4.τακήσονται, ubi additur, sicut cera à facie ignis;המס pro liquidusEsa. 64. v. 2.ὡς κηρὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου πυρὸς τήκεται, pro כלהomninò cessavit, defecit.Iob. 11. v. 20.cap. 17. v. 5. pro מוגdissolutus est, liquefactus estEx. 15. v. 15.Psal. 74. v. 3. Pro מססliquescit, ut defluat,Iud. 15. v. 14.Ps. 21. v. 15. pro מקקcontabuitLev. 26. v. 39.Esai. 34. v. 4. &c. qui locus huic nostro prallelus est, τακήσονται πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν. pro נזלdefluxitEsai. 64. v. 1. pro קדחincensus, succensus fuitEsai. 64. v. 1. pro התםconsumtus fuit, quod includit omni modam rei, cui tribuitur, perditionem, Ezech. 24. v. 10. quae significationes omnes huic loco congruunt. Syrus reddidit per [נשחון] à rad. [שח] sive [שחא] utrumque enim reperitur, liquefactus est, quod respondet verbo τηκεται. Instituenda verò collatio inter hunc versiculum & praecedentem. 10. In v. 10. de caelis dicit Apostolus, οἱ οὐρανοὶ ῥοιζηδὸν παρελευσονται; in hoc v. 12.οἱ οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται. In v. 10. de Elementis dicit, στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα λυθήσονται, in hoc vers. 12.στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τακήσεται. Ex quibus colligitur, quod caelorum & Elementorum futurus sit idem per ignem interitus. Ne quis enim cogitaret, caelos à conflagratione fore liberos, quia de illis v. 10. simpliciter dixerat Apostolus, παρελεύσονται, ideò v. 12. subiungit πυρέμενοι λυθήσονται. Inde etiam Lutherus & verbum λυθήσονται in v. 10. & verbum τακήσεται in v. 12. de Elementis usurpatum unâ eâdemque voce reddidit, Die Elemente werden für Hitze schmelzen oder zerschmeltzen.Pari ratione & verbum παρελεύσονται in v. 10. & verbum λυθήσονται in v. 12. de caelis usurpatum unà eâdemque voce reddidit. Die Himmel werden zergehen

## 3:13
Connection. 1. To the destruction of the heavens which now are, that is, which we behold with bodily eyes, and of the earth which now is, that is, upon which we stand with our feet, he opposes the creation of a new heaven and a new earth, which he confirms with prophetic testimony, and at the same time indicates the most happy state of that new world.

2. He meets a tacit objection. For someone might have thought, if the heavens will pass away with a great noise and, set on fire, will be dissolved, if the burning elements will melt away, if the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up, will there therefore be no heaven anymore, will there be no earth anymore? The Apostle answers, we expect a new heaven and a new earth, in which, since righteousness is to dwell, therefore they will never be destroyed, but will endure forever.

Exposition of the text. Καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς καὶ γῆν καινὴν κατὰ τὸ ἐπάγγελμα αὐτοῦ προσδοκῶμεν. Vulg. But we expect new heavens and a new earth according to his promises. In some Latin codices it is read, and promises, which departs even further from the Greek text, in which it is, according to the promise in the singular. If it pleases anyone, says Estius on this passage, that reading of certain codices, and the promises themselves can be explained concerning the goods which Christ everywhere, as much in the Gospel as in the Apocalypse, promised to his elect, the glory of the resurrection, immortality, the fellowship of his kingdom, the vision of GOD, by which goods the blessedness of the elect is perfected.

But what need is there to be greatly concerned about a faulty reading? Estius himself writes thus concerning it in the preceding. That which is read in certain Latin Codices instead of according to the promises, and promises in the more approved manuscripts, which are among us, is not found, just as it is not found at all in the Greek ones existing today. The Royal Codex indeed has ἐπαγγέλματα, but that is without a doubt translated from the Latin into the Greek text. Although Jerome in his commentary Es. 65. brings forward the Petrine passage with these words; But we shall see new heavens and a new earth and its promise: nevertheless, that faulty reading of the Vulgate version cannot be proven from it, for anyone sees that it was not Jerome's intention to cite the Apostolic passage κατὰ πόδα, but to provide a paraphrastic explanation of the same. The Syriac Interpreter omitted προσδιορισμόν concerning the newness of the earth in the latter member, for he rendered the text thus. We expect new heavens and earth. But the Greek Codices consistently read γῆν καινὴν, which προσδιορισμόν is also required both by the thing itself and by the Prophetic promise, to which Peter refers us 1. Esai. 65. v. 17.Behold I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former shall not be remembered, nor shall they ascend upon the heart. cap. 66. v. 22.As the new heavens and the new earth, which I make to stand before me, says the Lord: so shall your seed and your name stand. The prophecy Esai. 30. v. 26. can also be referred to here The light of the Moon shall be as the light of the Sun, and the light of the Sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days in the day in which the Lord shall have bound up the wound of his people. The same promise concerning the new heaven and the new earth is found Apoc. 21. v. 1.I saw a new heaven and a new earth.

That the pronoun αὐτοῦ is to be referred to Christ the judge is clear from verse 12 preceding in which the day of the final coming of Christ is called the day of GOD, from v. seq. 14. where we are commanded to be found immaculate before him, namely the judge who is to come, in peace; and from v. 15. in which we are commanded to account the long-suffering of our Lord as salvation.

Ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ. Vulg. in which justice dwells. The Greek properly has, dwells in. That ἐν αὐτοῖς 1. Some refer to the promises. But the Greek text does not admit this exposition, in which the singular ἐπάγγελμα; is held, nor is it said conveniently enough, that justice dwells in the promises of GOD. 2. Some refer it to the word προσδοκῶμεν. Gagnaeus in this place In which, while we expect the promises, justice dwells, as if to say: We ought to hope in the promises, provided that we live justly.

Erasmus, Fevardentius, Caietanus, Catharinus, etc., likewise say that those in whom righteousness dwells are those who expect new heavens and a new earth. But anyone can see that this exposition is entirely forced. For if Peter had wished to say this, that righteousness dwells in those who expect new heavens, he would have fashioned his style thus: Καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς &c. προσδοκῶμεν ἡμεῖς, ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ. 3. Therefore, this must be referred entirely to the new heavens and the new earth, that righteousness is said to dwell in them, which exposition also agrees with the Prophetic prediction Isa. 65. v. 18. where to the promise concerning the creation of new heavens and a new earth is added: Rejoice and exult (or also you shall rejoice and exult, because Imperatives among the Hebrews are often placed for futures) forever and ever, in those things which I create. For from that indwelling of righteousness in the new heaven and new earth will arise the eternal and continuous exultation and glorification of those dwelling there.

By Δικαιοσύνην 1. Philippus Solitarius in book 3 of the Dioptra, chapter 6, understands God, who is the Sun of righteousness and righteousness itself, which exposition could be proven from Apoc. 21. v. 3. Behold the tabernacle of GOD with men, and He will dwell with men, where, however, in the Greek it is not κατοικήσει but σκηνώσει. 2. Most understand by righteousness μετωνυμικῶς,, the abstract being placed for the concrete according to the Hebrew idiom, righteous and holy men, so that by this reason the perfect righteousness and holiness of the elect might be signified. Apoc. 21. v. 27. There shall not enter into it (the heavenly Jerusalem) anything defiled or doing abomination and a lie. 3. But the proper meaning of the abstract can also be retained, so that the sense may be that, together with the destruction of heaven and earth, the kingdom of sin is to be utterly abolished, and the elect are to be adorned with perpetual righteousness.

The present κατοικεῖ is placed for the future according to the Hebrew idiom, both because of the certainty of the promised thing and because of the eternal and continuous act of indwelling; R. Solomon in chapter 12 of Isaiah: Every Prophetic tongue speaks of the future as if of the past, and this is because the word of GOD is held as a fact, according to the old opinion of the Talmudists.

Latin:

Connexio. 1. Caelorum, qui nunc sunt, h. e. quos oculis corporeis conspicimus, & terrae, quae nunc est h. e. cui pedibus insistimus, destructioni opponit creationem novi caeli & novae terrae, quam confirmat testimonio Prophetico, ac simul novi illius mundi felicissimum statum indicat.

2. Occurrit tacitae obiectioni. Potuisset enim quispiam cogitare, si caeli magno stridore transibunt ac igne succensi solventur, si Elementa aestuantia contabescent, si terra & quae in ea sunt, opera exurentur, nunquid ergò nullum ampliùs erit caelum, nulla ampliùs erit terra? respondet Apostolus, expectamus novum caelum & novam terram, in quibus cùm iustitia sit habitatura, ideò illa nunquam destruentur, sed in aeternum perdurabunt.

Textus expositio. Καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς καὶ γῆν καινὴν κατὰ τὸ ἐπάγγελμα αὐτοῦ προσδοκῶμεν. Vulg. Novos verò caelos & novam terram secundùm promissa ipsius expectamus. In quibusdam Codd. Latinis legitur, & promissa, quod adhuc longiùs à Graeco textu discedit, in quo est, secundùm promissum in singulari. Si cui placet, inquit Estius ad h. l. illa quorundam Codicum lectio, & promissa ipsa exponi poterit de bonis, quae Christus passim tàm in Evangelio, quàm in Apocalypsi suis electis promisit, resurrectionis gloriam, immortalitatem, regni sui societatem, DEI visionem, quibus bonis electorum beatitudo perficitur.

At quid opus de lectione vitiosa magnoopere solicitum esse? Estius ipse de ea in praecedd. sic scribit. Quod in Latinis quibusdam Codd. pro secundùm promissa legitur, & promissa in MStis probatioribus, quae apud nos sunt, non reperitur, uti nec omninò in Graecis hodiè extantibus. Regius quidem Codex habet ἐπαγγέλματα, sed illud dubio procul ex Latino in Graecum textum est translatum. Quamvis verò Hieronymus in comm. Es. 65. locum Petrinum his adducat verbis; Novos autem caelos & novam terram videbimus & repromissionem eius: tamen ex eo lectio illa vulgatae versionis vitiosa probari nequit, quilibet enim videt, Hieronymo non fuisse propositum, locum Apostolicum κατὰ πόδα citare, sed paraphrasticam eiusdem explicationem tradere. Syrus Interpres in posteriore membro omisit προσδιορισμόν de novitate terrae, sic enim textum reddidit. Novos caelos & terram expectamus. Sed Graeci Codd. constanter legunt γῆν καινὴν, quem προσδιορισμόν etiam requirit tùm res ipsa, tùm Prophetica promissio, ad quam Petrus nos remittit 1. Esai. 65. v. 17.Ecce ego creo caelos novos & terram novam, & non memorabuntur priores, nec ascendent super cor.cap. 66. v. 22.Sicut caeli novi & terra nova, quae ego facio stare coram me, dicit Dominus: sic stabit semen vestrum & nomen vestrum. Potest etiam huc referri vaticinium Esai. 30. v. 26.Lux Lunae erit sicut lux Solis, & lux Solis erit septempliciter, sicut lux septem dierum in die, quâ alligaverit Dominus contritionem populi sui. Eadem promissio de novo caelo & nova terra reperitur Apoc. 21. v. 1.Vidi caelum novum & terram novam.

Pronomen αὐτοῦ ad Christum iudicem referendum esse, patet ex versu praeced. 12. in quo dies novissimi adventûs Christi vocatur dies DEI, ex v. seq. 14. ubi iubemur immaculati coram eo, venturo sc. iudice, inveniri; & ex v. 15. in quo long animitatem Domini nostri salutem arbitrari iubemur.

Ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ. Vulg. in quibus iustitia habitat. Graeca propriè habent, inhabitat. Illud ἐν αὐτοῖς 1. Quidam referunt ad promissa. Sed hanc expositionem non admittit Graecus textus, in quo habetur singulare ἐπάγγελμα; nec satis commodè dicitur, in promissis DEI iustitiam inhabitare. 2. Quidam referunt ad verbum προσδοκῶμεν. Gagnaeus in h. l. In quibus nobis promissa expectantibus iustitia habitat, q. d. Sperare in promissis debemus, siquide iustè vivamus.

Erasmus, Fevardentius, Caietanus, Catharinus &c. itidem eos, in quibus iustitia habitat, aiunt, esse illos, qui expectant novos caelos & novam terram. Sed quilibet videt, hanc expositionem esse pranè coactam. Quòd si Petrus hoc voluisset dicere, in expectantibus caelos novos habitare iustitiam, sic stylum informasset. Καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς &c. προσδοκῶμεν ἡμεῖς, ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ. 3. Omninò igitur ad novos caelos & novam terram hoc referendum, quod in illis iustitia dicitur habitare, quae expositio etiam congruit vaticinio Prophetico Esa. 65. v. 18. ubi promissioni de creatione novorum caelorum & novae terrae subiungitur. Gaudete & exultate (vel etiam gaudebitis & exultabitis, quia Imperativi apud Hebraeos saepè ponuntur pro futuris) in seculum seculi, in his, quae ego creo. Ex illa enim iustitiae in novo caelo & nova terra inhabitatione orietur aeterna & continua inhabitantium exultatio & glorificatio.

Per Δικαιοσύνην 1. Philippus Solitarius lib. 3. Dioptrae cap. 6. intelligit Deum, qui est Sol iustitiae ac ipsa iustitia, quae expositio probari posset ex Apoc. 21. v. 3.Ecce tabernaculum DEI cum hominibus, & habitabit cum hominibus, ubi tamen in Graeco est non κατοικήσει sed σκηνώσει. 2. Plerique per iustitiamμετωνυμικῶς, abstracto iuxta idiotismum Hebraeum posito pro concreto, intelligunt homines iustos & sanctos, ut hac ratione perfecta electorum iustitia & sanctitas significetur.Apoc. 21. v. 27.Non intrabit in eam (coelestem Hierosolymam) aliquid coinquinatum aut abominationem faciens & mendacium. 3. Sed potest etiam propria significatio abstracti retineri, ut sit sensus, quod unà cum caeli & terrae destructione penitus abolendum sit regnum peccati, ac electi perpetuâ iustitiâ sint decorandi.

Praesens κατοικεῖ iuxta idiotismum Hebraicum ponitur profuturo, tùm propter rei promissae certitudinem, tùm propter aeternum & continuum inhabitationis actum; R. Salomo in cap. 12. Esaiae. Omnis lingua Prophetica loquitur de futuro, tanquam de praeterito, & hoc ideò, quia dictum DEI habetur pro facto, iuxta veterem, Thalmudistarum sententiam.

## 3:13-15 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. What is that righteousness which is said to dwell in the new heaven and the new earth? Resp. 1. Some accept this concerning the righteousness of Christ, which PaulPhil. 3. v. 9.describes thus. I count all things as dung, that I may gain Christ, and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith. For that is the eternal righteousnessDan. 9. v. 24.it is that shining and white linen, with which the Bride of Christ will be at the heavenly nuptials to be clothed.Apoc. 7. v. 8. 2. Some, however, understand it concerning the inherent righteousness of the elect. The present world is defiled by every kind of wickedness, but in the new heaven and new earth righteousness shall dwell. The inherent or habitual and actual righteousness of the pious in this life is imperfect, since the stain of sin still adheres to them; but in eternal life that inherent righteousness of the pious will be perfect and consummated, because sin with all its roots and fibers will have been torn out from their soul and body. 3. These two expositions are not opposed, but subordinated, therefore they can be joined for the best reason.

Q. 2. In what sense are we commanded to be found in peace before Christ the coming judge? Resp. Some refer to Christ the judge in this sense. Strive for innocence and holiness, so that you may experience the judge as peaceful and clement for your own good. But it is more correctly referred to those who are to be set before the tribunal of the judge, as the series of the text shows; and not to the participle προσδοκῶντες or to the noun ἀμώμητοι, but to the verb εὑρεθῆναι, as we showed in the exposition of the text. There is, however, a double, or even triple peace, which is required of the pious in the word of GOD. The first is peace with GOD i. e. reconciliation with GOD through the word of the Gospel apprehended by faith 2. Cor. 5. v. 20.Be reconciled to GOD. According to this meaning of peace, the sense will be: Strive that Christ, coming to judgment, may find you having peace with GOD, established in His grace, adopted as sons. For those who are such, and no others, He will receive into the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom Matth. 25. v. 34. The second is peace of conscience or with one's own heart; this arises from the preceding, namely from reconciliation with GOD Rom. 5. v. 1.Being justified by faith we have peace with GOD through our Lord Jesus Christ.1. Ioh. 3. v. 22.If our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence toward GOD. Conversely, however, it is said of the impious Esai. 57. v. 21.There is no peace for the impious, says the Lord. The third is peace with one's neighbor. This likewise arises from the preceding peace, because faith, through which we are reconciled to GOD, are adopted as sons, and obtain rest of conscience, exerts itself through love Gal. 5. vers. 6. The Holy Spirit likewise requires this peace from the pious Matth. 5. vers. 9.Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of GOD. (If sons, then certainly also heirs Rom. 8. vers. 17. and consequently they themselves shall hear from the coming judge: Come you blessed, enter into the inheritance of the kingdom, which has been prepared for youMatth. 25. v. 34.) Hebr. 12. v. 14.Pursue peace with all and holiness without which no one shall see GOD. These expositions can also be joined, since they are subordinate, and one kind of peace is the immediate fruit of the other.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. We look for new heavens. But Psal. 89. v. 30. it is said concerning the throne of the Messiah, that it shall be eternal like the days of heaven. If the days of heaven are eternal, therefore the heaven itself is also eternal.

Resp. By the name heavens is understood the blessedness of the elect in the future age, and thus that very new heaven, of which the Apostle makes mention in this place. The days of this heaven will be eternal, because the blessedness of the elect will be eternal, by which reason the days of this heaven are opposed to the days of the present earth. Gen. 8. v. 22. for the Apostle expressly testifies in this very chapter that the present heavens, or, as the Apostle speaks, τούς νῦν οὐρανοὺς shall perish.

2. We look for a new earth. But concerning the earth, which now is, it is said Eccl. 1. v. 4. The earth stands forever. with which that agrees Psalm. 104. v. 5. You have founded the earth upon its base, it shall not be inclined for ever and ever. Resp. The little word עולם in this place does not signify absolute and indeterminate eternity, but periodic and determinate, namely, some certain space of long time, the duration of which is hidden from the eyes of men. This meaning is gathered from the opposition: One generation passes away and another generation comes, that is, men dwelling upon the face of the earth die and arise, and there is a perpetual vicissitude of those coming into this world and departing from the world: But the earth remains stable and immovable, namely, until the limit divinely prefixed for its duration. Compare the treatise on the consummation of the age §. 17.

3. We look for new heavens and a new earth according to His promise. But the promise concerning the creating of new heavens and a new earth Esai. 65. v. 17. seems to treat of the kingdom of grace in this life, or of the state of the Christian Church in the New Testament, as the whole context shows.

Resp. It is solemn for the Prophets to make a transition from the description of the kingdom of grace to the description of the kingdom of glory; from the state of the kingdom of Christ in this world to the state of the kingdom of Christ in the other age, because the benefits of Christ are not only to be estimated from this, but also from the future life; and the kingdom of Christ is only begun here, it will be consummated in the future age. Hemming. in this place This Prophecy, although it speaks of the whole kingdom of Christ, nevertheless is to be referred most especially to its consummation. For when we shall have been most fully regenerated, heaven also and

the earth will be thoroughly renewed, and will receive its entire state. Lorinus on this passage: Although the testimonies of Isaiah concerning a certain new face and form of the militant Church can be understood literally, in the way that in broad matters new things seem to be made, Esth. 8. v. 16. the glory and happiness of the triumphant Church is not excluded, however, to which the militant Church tends through all those gifts which are communicated to it by the benefit and merit of the same Christ.

Ἔλεγχος. The Prophetic promise concerning new heavens and a new earth must be opposed to the heretics who were called Aeternales, who, as Augustine reports in De haeres. cap. 67, maintained that this world, even after the resurrection of the dead, would remain in the same state in which it now is, and would not be so changed that there would be a new heaven and a new earth, as the holy Scripture promises.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Those who maintain that the world will be renewed only according to qualities urge that the Apostle did not say, We expect other heavens and another earth, but new heavens and a new earth. Jerome on chapter 65 of Isaiah, Bede on this Apostolic passage.

Resp. 1. We showed above that the emphasis of the sayings of Scripture, which deal with the destruction of the world, leads us to a substantial φθορὰν. 2. New heavens are, which are not only new in qualities, but also different in substance itself, just as a garment is called new which is prepared from new cloth or silk. 3. New in the Scriptures sometimes signifies the same as other. Exod. 1. v. 8. Esth. 8. v. 5. Esai. 62. v. 2. (compare with this place Esai. 65. v. 15.) Matth. 26. v. 29. Marc. 16. v. 17. Iohan. 13. v. 34. etc. 4. In the parallel place Apoc. 21. v. 1. to those words, I saw a new heaven and a new earth, it is immediately added, the first heaven and the first earth passed away. But how did it pass away? The exposition is had in the preceding cap. 20. v. 11. From the sight of him who sat upon the throne the earth and heaven fled, and no place was found for them.

2. Estius on v. 13 comments thus: Peter does not take the heavens in this place otherwise than in the preceding ones. But in the preceding ones, according to Estius's hypothesis, he understood the aerial heavens.

Resp. 1. The parallel places Esai. 65. v. 17. cap. 66. v. 22. Apoc. 21. v. 1. show that the discourse here is about the ethereal heavens. 2. Which προσδιορισμὸς, itself proves: in which justice dwells. For how will justice dwell in the aerial heavens? 3. We invert the argument. Peter in the preceding ones understands by the name of heavens the ethereal heavens. Therefore, also in this place he understands the ethereal heavens.

The antecedent was confirmed above. Estius concedes the consequence. 4. Barradius lib. 9. Concord. Evang. cap. 11. p. 592. Those words, we expect new heavens, are to be explained not concerning the air, but concerning the superior heavens. Blasius de Viega in comm. Apoc. 21. acknowledges, that by new heavens are to be understood not aerial, but ethereal heavens. 5. Thence Estius himself, convinced by the brightness of the truth, adds. Although we do not deny, that Peter's doctrine has truth also concerning the superelementary heavens, in which the celestial lights are fixed.

3. The same Estius to the same verse annotates thus. Saying new, the Apostle wishes the earth to be understood at the same time as the water. For these two he had closely comprehended by the name of Elements, which, as if liquefied by fire, are to receive new qualities or forms, having cast off their old age. Similar things occur in Ribera in cap. 21. Apocal. Resp. 1. We read that a new earth is promised, therefore we believe it will be; we do not read that new water is promised either in this place or elsewhere in the Scriptures. 2. After John in the parallel place Apoc. 21. v. 1. had said. I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth passed away, he expressly adds. And the sea is no more. 3. From which Bede gathers, The element of water will perish entirely in the destruction of the world. 4. Estius excepts. John does not say, that water will no longer be, but the sea, i.e. as Augustine explains lib. 20. de C. D. This age turbulent and stormy with the life of mortals, which he figured by the name of the sea; or as some wish, the sea according to the position, which it now has in the universe, so that it may be signified that the sea will return to the place of the universe, which it had in the beginning, before the waters were gathered into certain bays, so that the dry land might appear; or rather the sea, insofar as it is impure, thick, salty, turbid and restless, for the word sea is accustomed to import qualities of this kind, and therefore it is not said that a new sea will be, but simply that it will no longer be. Resp. Augustine in the cited place doubts concerning the renewal of the sea. The words are thus. But what he says, and the sea is no more, whether it is dried up by that greatest heat, or whether it itself is turned into something better, I would not easily say. For we read that a new heaven and a new earth will be, but I do not recall having read anywhere that a new sea will be, unless what is found in this same book (of the Apocalypse) And a sea of glass like unto crystal. But then he was not speaking of that end of the age, nor does he seem to have said properly, sea, but as it were a sea. Andreas of Caesarea in comm. Apocal. cap. 21. expressly denies, that the sea will be in the new world; For thus d. l. writes. But it is to be noted concerning heaven and earth that he (John) says, it has passed away, that is, it has been changed, but concerning the sea he says: The sea will be no more. For what utility is there of the sea, when there is no need for men to navigate it? There is no great weight in that triple exposition which Estius brings forward. The first, brought forward from Augustine, is mystical. But if the name of the sea were to be taken mystically, the same would have to be said concerning the name of heaven and earth. The second exposition contradicts the opinion of those who establish that the new earth will be the dwelling place of men. For if water will surround the whole globe of the earth, how will men be able to dwell on the earth? The third exposition does not attain the emphasis of the Apostolic statement. For it is one thing for the sea to be no more, and another for it to be no longer such.

4. Lorinus on the same verse annotates thus. Luther ridiculously tom. 1. Colloq. mens. f. 61. asserts new, for example, dogs, whose skin is golden, the hairs made of pearls. Resp. 1. What is to be determined concerning the book of Table Talk, we have already warned before. 2. Luther imitates the style of Scripture, concerning which Otto of Freising lib. 8. chron. cap. 35. discourses thus. If anywhere Holy Scripture says that the senses of the blessed are refreshed by flowering and green fields, pleasant places, the chirping of birds, and fragrant things, such as cinnamon and balsam, this seems to be understood spiritually rather than carnally. 3. We have exposed the earthly and carnal thoughts of certain Papists concerning the joys, exercises, and dwellings of the blessed in the tract on eternal life §. 162. 4. Anselm in Elucid. and William of Paris in Dionysius the Carthusian 4. sent. Dist. 48. assert that flowers and similar things conciliating pleasure are to be germinated in the new earth. The words of Anselm are as follows. The earth, which cherished the body of the Lord in its bosom, will be entirely like Paradise, and because it has been irrigated by the blood of the saints, it will be perpetually adorned with fragrant flowers, lilies, roses, and violets, in an unfading manner. William of Paris speaks thus. Concerning the earth, some of the wisest of Christians have said that it is to be adorned like the earthly Paradise with ever-green grasses, and unfading flowers, and perpetual pleasantness.

5. Ambrosius Catharinus on the same verse comments thus. To what use is the new earth, if no one is to dwell in it? Therefore it is most congruously believed by many that those who by their own sin did not deserve hell, nor yet were received in Christ through grace, such as children dying without Baptism, will possess this new earth, much more beautiful and pure from all corruption and defilement, where they will perpetually praise the Lord God.

Alphonsus Salmero, Disputation 4 on this 2nd Epistle of Peter, page 140: Observe, the new earth is to be formed. But I beseech you, good GOD! for what use, unless that children who have departed without circumcision and without Baptism may possess it. Pineda in his commentary on Job 26:10: There has not been lacking one who piously and not improbably felt that children who dwell in limbo will inhabit this world. Lorinus on this passage of the Apostle: I would not dare to judge the opinion of Salmero and Pineda as entirely improbable, setting aside those things which Catharinus and Salmero assert concerning freedom from the power of the Devil, and concerning angelic visitations and revelations. This opinion is served by the fact that, as we warned a little earlier, some establish that that new earth will be most beautifully adorned with herbs and trees.

Response 1. Iodocus Coccius, part 2 of the Treasury, book 19, article 2, page 1047, lists this opinion of Ambrosius Catharinus among errors. 2. Bellarmine, book 6 on the loss of grace and the state of sin, chapter 2, describes a far different face of that new earth. It is entirely credible, he says, that after the day of the last judgment the Element of water will return to its natural place, and will cover the whole earth on all sides: for as the Theologian Doctors teach by common consent, after the day of judgment there will be no plants, no animals, no mixed bodies, with the exception of men alone. Wherefore, since water from the beginning of the world surrounded the whole earth, as its Nature seemed to demand, and then by the command of God was gathered into one place, so that there might be a place on earth for the generation of plants and animals, certainly with that generation removed, reason itself and the Nature of things demand that the water should return to its former place; therefore the place of infants dying without Baptism will be none other than hell. 3. Cornelius à Lapide in his commentary on this passage of the Apostle refutes Catharinus and Salmero by profession. Catharinus, he says, and Salmero think that children (not baptized) will be on the earth, as if in a certain earthly Paradise, and therefore are to be perfected in natural knowledge, so that they may surpass all Philosophers, etc., but they are mistaken while they think they will be blessed with natural blessedness, since, because they are to be condemned with the punishment of loss, although not of sense, namely by the lack of the beatific divine vision, etc., they are to be called damned rather than blessed. Otherwise, it is probable that they will lead a comfortable life on earth, for the limbo of children will not contain their bodies, which they will resume on the day of judgment. 4. Before them all, Thomas in the Supplement, question 91, article 5, distinguished thus: Plants and animals are of the perfection of the universe according to this state of mutability, not according to the state of newness. 5. The hypothesis is false that unbaptized Infants will be in a certain earthly place outside heaven and hell, which opinion the Church long ago disapproved in the Pelagians. 6. What that new heaven and that new earth will be like, the holy Scripture does not express, nor is it necessary for us to know in this life, therefore let us fear to scrutinize the secrets of the heavens too curiously.

6. Estius comments on v. 14 as follows. The Apostle infers from the renovation of the world, which he said would be the dwelling place of the just, that one must live in such a way that we may deserve to be received into it by Christ. Resp. 1. That the good works of the pious are not meritorious of eternal life, with the name of merit taken properly and strictly, is demonstrated in its own place. 2. Nor does Peter make mention of any merit in this place, but he requires this of the pious, that they should solicitously strive to be found immaculate before Christ the judge, namely, because faith exerts itself through good works, and is shaken off by sins against conscience.

Observations. 1. He who has faith in the divine promises, and all ought to have it, will be able to doubt in no way that new heavens and a new earth are to be created.

2. But what that new world will be like, we think that no man in this life can know. 1. Cor. 2. v. 9. Eye has not seen &c. on which passage Augustine in his Epistle to Dioscorus comments most beautifully as follows. Eye has not seen, because there is no color; nor has ear heard, because there is no sound: nor has it ascended into the heart of man, because the heart of man ought to ascend thither. That which GOD promises is not grasped by faith; it is not reached by hope, it is not comprehended by charity, it transcends desires and vows; it can be acquired, it cannot be estimated.

3. By the hope of that new world, in which perfect justice and perpetual joy will dwell, let us raise ourselves against all the miseries of this world. Let the faithful, agitated by so many hardships and deaths in this life, thinking of the reviving remains of the old world in the new heavens and new earth, remember that for the saints the losses of a fleeting life are likewise converted into the gains of immortality, and with the new heavens let them expect a new glorified body.

4. In this life all justice of the pious is imperfect and unclean, like the garment of a menstruous woman Esa. 64. v. 6. and both habitual and actual justice is far from perfection, but in eternal life the justice of the elect will be consummated. In these heavens of ours dwells mercy, tolerating sinners, but in the new heavens will dwell justice, which will not admit anything defiled.

5. Bede on this passage annotates thus: Justice dwells in the future age, because then to each of the faithful, according to the measure of his struggle, the crown of justice will be rendered, which in this life can by no means happen &c. Above the Sun are mansions, in which the just will receive the due rewards of their justice. This also, which he says, in which justice dwells, can be understood according to that of the Psalmist. This is the gate of the Lord, the just shall enter through it. And in the Apocalypse concerning the heavenly city, John says. There shall not enter into it anything defiled.

6. Just as Peter deduces an exhortation to the pursuit of holiness from the doctrine of the creation of a new heaven and a new earth: so all things in Theology are to be directed toward practice. Matth. 7. v. 21.Luc. 6. v. 46.Ioh. 13. v. 17. Justin in his exhortation, p. 25. Our religious matters consist not in words, but in deeds. Augustine, book 1 of Christian Doctrine, chapter 4. The whole of Theology is ordered to this end, that we may enjoy GOD.

7. It is truly the duty of the pious to apply themselves with the greatest zeal to this, that they may be found immaculate in the sight of Christ the judge. Basil in his commentary on Psal. 33. Blessed is he who, on the day of judgment, when the Lord shall come to illuminate the hidden things of darkness and to manifest the counsels of hearts, shall dare to stand under that light of reproofs, and fearless and without shame shall present an uncontaminated conscience, free from vices? Augustine in Soliloquies, chapter 14. A great necessity is placed upon us of living justly and rightly, we who do all things before the eyes of a judge who sees all things.

8. Bede on this v. 14 annotates thus: These are the holy vigils, of which the Lord says. Blessed are those servants, whom, when the Lord comes, he shall find watching. For he watches, who keeps himself immune from the filth of vices, who as much as is in him, has peace with all, who using most happy peace within himself, subjects all the allurements of the flesh to the rule of the Spirit.

9. They shall be found immaculate and in peace on the day of judgment, not those who have never sinned, but those who have performed serious repentance for their sins, to whom on account of Christ apprehended by true faith sins have been forgiven, who have been reconciled to GOD and have demonstrated their faith through charity, the pursuit of good works, and brotherly concord.

10. The pious ought not to be affected with weariness on account of the long delay of the Lord's coming, but to consider that the salvation of many is placed in it; but much less ought they to say in their heart with the evil servant, my Lord delays to come, therefore I desire to be injurious to my fellow servants, and to indulge my appetite. Matth. 24. v. 47. & 48.

11. It must be acknowledged and proclaimed with a grateful mind, that the long-suffering of GOD invites men to repentance. Rom. 2. v. 4.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quae sit illa iustitia, quae in novo caelo ac nova terra habitare dicitur? Resp. 1. Quidam hoc accipiunt, de iustitia Christi, quam PaulusPhil. 3. v. 9.sic describit. Omnia arbitror ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciam, ut & inveniar in illo non habens meam iustitiam, quae ex lege est, sed illam, quae est ex fide Christi, quae ex Deo est iustitia in fide. Illa enim est aeterna iustitiaDan. 9. v. 24.est byssinum illud splendens & candidum, quo Sponsa Christi in nuptiis caelestibus erit induenda.Apoc. 7. v. 8. 2. Quidam verò intelligunt de iustitia electorum inhaerente. Mundus praesens est omni scelerum specie inquinaetus, sed in novo caelo ac nova terra habitabit iustitia. Inhaerens sive habitualis & actualis piorum iustitia in hac vita est imperfecta, cùm peccati labes ipsis adhuc adhaereat; sed in vita aeterna inhaerens illa piorum iustitia erit perfecta, & consummata, quia peccatum cum omnibus radicibus ac fibris ex anima & corpore ipsorum erit evulsum. 3. Hae duae expositiones non sunt oppositae, sed subordinatae, ideò optimâ ratione coniungi possunt.

Q. 2. Quo sensu iubeamur coram Christo venturo iudice inveniri in pace? Resp. Quidam referunt ad Christum iudicem hoc sensu. Studete innocentiae & sanctitati, ut vestro bono iudicem pacificum & clementem experiamini. Sed rectiùs refertur ad illos, qui tribunali iudicis sunt sistendi, ut ostendit series textus; nec ad participium προσδοκῶντες vel ad nomen ἀμώμητοι, sed ad verbum εὑρεθῆναι, ut in expositione textus ostendimus. Duplex verò, vel etiam triplex pax est, quae à piis in verbo DEI requiritur. Prima est pax cum DEO i. e. reconciliatio cum DEO per verbum Evangelii fide apprehensum 2. Cor. 5. v. 20.Reconciliemini DEO. Iuxta hanc pacis significationem erit sensus. Studete, ut Christus ad iudicium veniens inveniat vos pacem cum DEO habentes, in gratia ipsius constitutos, in filios adoptatos. Qui enim tales sunt, illos & non alios in haereditatem regni caelestis recipiet Matth. 25. v. 34. Altera est pax conscientiae sive cum corde proprio, haec oritur ex praecedente, videlicet ex reconciliatione cum DEO Rom. 5. v. 1.Iustificati fide pacem habemus ad DEUM per D. N. I. C.1. Ioh. 3. v. 22.Si cor nostrum non reprehenderit nos, fiduciam habemus ad DEUM. Contrà verò de impiis dicitur Esai. 57. v. 21.Non est pax impiis, dicit Dominus. Tertia est pax cum proximo. Haec itidem oritur ex praecedente pace, quia fides, per quam DEO reconciliamur, in filios adoptamur, & quietem conscientiae consequimur, exerit se per dilectionem Gal. 5. vers. 6. Hanc pacem itidem Spiritus sanctus à piis requirit Matth. 5. vers. 9.Beati pacifici, quia filii DEI vocabuntur. (Si silii, utique etiam heredes Rom. 8. vers. 17. ac proinde ipsi à iudice venturo audient. Venite benedicti, hereditatem adite regni, quod paratum vobisMatth. 25. v. 34.) Hebr. 12. v. 14.Pacem sectemini cum omnibus & sanctimoniam absque quanemo videbit DEUM. Possunt & hae expositiones coniungi, cùm sint subordinatae, ac una pacis species sit immediatus alterius fructus.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Expectamus caelos novos. At Psal. 89. v. 30.de throno Messiae dicitur, quòd futurus sit aeternus sicut dies caeli. Si dies caeli sunt aeterni, ergò etiam ipsum caelum est aeternum.

Resp. Caeli nomine intelligitur beatitudo electorum in futuro seculo, adeoque ipsum illud novum caelum, cuius hoc loco mentionem facit Apostolus. Huius caeli dies erunt aeterni, quia beatitudo electorum erit aeterna, quâ ratione dies huius caeli opponuntur diebus terrae praesentis. Gen. 8. v. 22. praesentes enim caelos, sive, ut Apostolus loquitur, τούς νῦν οὐρανοὺς interituros Apostolus in hoc ipso capite disertè testatur.

2. Expectamus terram novam. At de terra, quae nunc est, diciturEccl. 1. v. 4.Terra in aeternum stat. cum quo congruit illudPsalm. 104. v. 5.Fundasti terram super basin suam, non inclinabitur in seculum seculi. Resp. vocula עולם h. l. non significat aeternitatem absolutam & indeterminatam, sed periodicam & determinatam, videl. certum aliquod diuturni temporis spacium, cuius duratio ab oculis hominum est abscondita. Colligitur haec significatio ex oppositione: Generatio praeterit & generatio advenit, h. e. homines super faciem terrae habitantes moriuntur & oriuntur, estque perpetua vicissitudo venientium in hunc mundum & ex mundo discedentium: Sed terra perseverat stabilis & immobilis, videl. usque terminum durationi suae divinitus praefixum. Confer tract. de consumm. seculi §. 17.

3. Expectamus novos caelos & novam terram secundùm ipsius promissionem. At qui promissio de creandis novis caelis & nova terraEsai. 65. v. 17.videtur agere de regno gratiae in hac vita, sive de statu Ecclesiae Christianae in N. T. ut ostendit totus contextus.

Resp. Solenne est Prophetis à descriptione regni gratiae transitum facere ad descriptionem regni gloriae; à statu regni Christi in hoc mundo ad statum regni Christi in altero seculo, quia beneficia Christi non solùm aestimanda sunt ex hac, sed etiam ex futura vita; & regnum Christi hîc duntaxat in choatur, in futuro seculo consummabitur. Hemming. in h. l. Haec Prophetia, etsi de toto regno Christi loquatur, tamen potissimùm ad eius consummationem referenda est. Quando enim nos fuerimus plenissimè regenerati, caelum etiam &

terra penitus renovabuntur, integrumque suum statum recipient. Lorinus ad h. l. Quamvis Esaiae testimonia de nova quadam facie ac forma Ecclesiae militantis ad literam intelligi possint, quo pacto in rebus latis nova videntur fieri omnia,Esth. 8. v. 16.non excluditur tamen triumphantis gloria ac felicitas, ad quam tendit militans per omnia illa dona, quae ipsi beneficio ac merito eiusdem Christi communicantur.

Ἔλεγχος. Promissum Propheticum de novis caelis & nova terra opponendum est haereticis, qui dicti fuêre Aeternales, qui referente Augustino de haeres. cap. 67. statuerunt, mundum hunc etiam post resurrectionem mortuorum in eodem statu, in quo nunc est, esse mansurum, neque ita esse mutandum, ut sit caelum novum & terranova, sicut fancta Scriptura promittit.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Qui mundum duntaxat secundùm qualitates renovatum iri statuunt, urgent, quòd Apostolus non dixerit. Expectamus alios caelos & aliam terram, sed novos caelos & novam terram. Hieronymus in cap 65. Esaiae, Beda in h. l. Apostolicum.

Resp. 1. Ostendimus superiùs, emphasin dictorum Scripturae, quae de mundi interitu agunt, ad substantialem φθορὰν nos deducere. 2. Novi caeli sunt, qui non solùm qualitatibus novi, sed ipsâ etiam substantiâ diversi, sicut nova vestis dicitur, quae ex novo panno vel serico parata. 3. Novum in Scripturis quandoque significat idem quod aliud.Exod. 1. v. 8.Esth. 8. v. 5.Esai. 62. v. 2. (confer cum hoc loco Esai. 65. v. 15.) Matth. 26. v. 29.Marc. 16. v. 17.Iohan. 13. v. 34. &c. 4. In loco parallelo Apoc. 21. v. 1. verbis illis, Vidi caelum novum & terram novam, statim subiungitur, primum caelum & prima terra abiit. Quomodo verò abiit? expositio habetur in praeced. cap. 20. v. 11.A conspectu sedentis super thronum fugit terra & caelum, & locus non est inventus eis.

2. Estius ad v. 13. sic commentatur. Petrus non aliter hoc loco caelos accipit, quàm in praecedentibus. Sed in praecedentibus iuxta Estii hypothesin intellexit caelos aëreos.

Resp. 1. Loca parallela Esai. 65. v. 17.cap. 66. v. 22.Apoc. 21. v. 1. ostendunt, de caelis aethereis hîc sermonem esse. 2. Quod ipsum comprobat προσδιορισμὸς,in quibus iustitia habitat. Quomodo enim in caelis aëreis habitabit iustitia? 3. Invertimus argumentum. Petrus in praecedentibus caelorum nomine intelligit caelos aethereos. Ergò etiam hoc loco caelos aethereos intelligit.

Antecedens superiùs fuit confirmatum. Consequentiam Estius concedit. 4. Barradius lib. 9. Concord. Evang. cap. 11. p. 592. Illa verba, expectamus novos caelos, non de aëre, sed de caelis superioribus explicanda sunt. Blasius de Viega in comm. Apoc. 21. agnoscit, per novos caelos accipiendos esse non aëreos, sed aethereos caelos. 5. Inde Estius ipsemet fulgore veritatis convictus subiicit. Quanquam non negamus, Petri doctrinam habere veritatem etiam de caelis superelementaribus, in quibus infixa sunt lumina caelestia.

3. Idem Estius ad eund. vers. sic annotat. Dicens Apostolus novam, terram simul aquam vult intelligi. Haec enim duo proximè nomine Elementorum comprehenderat, quae igne velut liquefacta novas, exutâ vetustate, qualitates ceu formas acceptura sint. Similia occurrunt apud Riberam in cap. 21. Apocal. Resp. 1. Terram novam promissam legimus, ideò eam futuram credimus; novam aquam promissam nec hoc loco nec alibi in Scripturis legimus. 2. Postquam Iohannes in loco parallelo Apoc. 21. v. 1. dixerat. Vidi caelum novum & terram novam, primum enim caelum & prima terra abiit, disertè subiungit. Et mare iam non est. 3. Ex quo Beda colligit, Elementum aquae in mundi destructione prorsus interiturum. 4. Excipit Estius. Iohannes non dicit, aquam non ampliùs futuram, sed mare, h. e. ut Augustinus exponit lib. 20. de C. D. Hoc seculum vitâ mortalium turbulentum & procellosum, quod maris nomine figuravit; vel ut quidam volunt, mare secundum situm, quem nunc habet in universo, ut significetur mare rediturum ad locum universi, quem habuit initio, prius quam aquae congregarentur in sinus quosdam, ut appareret arida; vel potiùs mare, quatenus impurum, crassum, salsum, turbidum & inquietum, nam huiusmodi qualitates importare solet vocabulum maris, ideoque non dicitur mare novum futurum, sed simpliciter non futurum ampliùs. Resp. Augustinus loco citato dubitat de maris renovatione. Verba sic habent. Quod autem ait, & mare iam non est, utrum maximo illo ardore siccetur, an & ipsum vertatur in melius, non facilè dixerim. Caelum quippe novum & terram novam futuram legimus, de mari autem novo aliquid me uspiam legisse non recolo, nisi quod in hoc eodem libro (Apocalypseos) reperitur. Tanquam mare vitreum simile crystallo. Sed tunc non de isto fine seculi loquebatur, nec propriè videtur dixisse, mare, sed tanquam mare. Andreas Caesariensis in comm. Apocal. cap. 21. disertè negat, mare in novo mundo futurum; Sic enim d. l. scribit. Notandum autem de caelo & terra eum (Iohannem) dicere, abiit, h. e. mutatum est, de mari autem ait: Mare non erit ampliùs. Quae enim utilitas maris, cùm non sit opus hominibus illud navigare? Triplici isti expositioni, quam Estius adducit, non inest magnum pondus. Prima ex Augustino adducta est mystica. Quòd si maris nomen mysticè accipiendum esset, idem dicendum foret de nomine caeli & terrae. Altera expositio repugnat sententiae eorum, qui statuunt, novam terram fore hominum habitaculum. Quod si enim aqua cinget totum terrae globum, quomodo in terra poterunt homines habitare? Tertia expositio non assequitur emphasin dicti Apostolici. Aliud enim est, mare non ampliùs esse, aliud non ampliùs tale fore.

4. Lorinus ad eund. vers. sic annotat. Ridiculè Lutherus tom. 1. Colloq. mens. f. 61. novos, verbi gratiâ, asserit canes, quorum cutis aurea, villi ex margaritis. Resp. 1. Quid de libro Colloq. mensal. statuendum, iam antè monuimus. 2. Imitatur Lutherus stylum Scripturae, de quo Otto Frisingensis lib. 8. chron. cap. 35. sic disserit. Sicubi Scriptura sacra floridis & virentibus campis, amoenis locis, garritu avium, odoriferis rebus, utpote cinamomo & balsamo sensus beatorum refici dicit, spiritualiter hoc potiùs, quàm carnaliter accipiendum videtur. 3. Terrenas & carnales quorundam Pontificiorum de gaudiis, exercitiis & habitaculis beatorum cogitationes exposuimus in tract. de vita aeterna §. 162. 4. Anselmus in Elucid. & Guilielmus Parisiensis apud Dionys. Carthusianum 4. sent. Dist. 48. flores & similia voluptatem conciliantia in nova terra germinanda asserunt. Verba Anselmi sic habent. Terra, quae in gremio suo corpus Domini fovit, tota erit ut Pamdisus, & quia sanctorum sanguine est irrigata, odoriferis floribus, liliis, rosis, violis, immarcescibiliter erit perpetuò decomta. Guilielmus Parisiensis sic loquitur. De term quidam ex sapientissimis Christianorum dixerunt, quòd graminibus sempervirentibus, & immarcescibilibus floribus, ac perpetuâ amoenitate instar Paradisi terrestris sit decoranda.

5. Ambrosius Catharinus ad eund. vers. sic commentatur. In quem usum nova terra, si nullus habitaturus sit in ea? Idcircò congruentissimè creditur à multis, eos, qui peccato proprio non merebantur infernum, nec tamen in Christo recepti fuerunt per gratiam, quales pueri absque Baptismo decedentes, hanc novam multò pulchriorem terram puram ab omni corruptione & inquinamem opossessuros, ubi perpetuò Dominum Deum laudabunt.

Alphonsus Salmero Disp. 4. in hanc 2. Epist. Petri pag. 140. Adverte, terram novam formandam. At quaeso, bone DEUS! in quem usum, nisi ut pueri, qui sine circumcisione & sine Baptismo decesserunt, eam possideant. Pineda in comm. Iob. 26. v. 10.Non defuit, qui piè neque improbabiliter sensit, pueros, qui in limbo agunt, in hoc mundo inhabitaturos. Lorinus in h. l. Apost. Salmeronis & Pinedae opinionem non ausim penitus improbabilem iudicare, demtis iis, quae asserunt Catharinus & Salmeron de libertate à potestate Diaboli, deque visitationibus & revelationibus Angelicis. Huic opinioni inservit, quod ut paulò antè monuimus, quidam statuunt, novam illam terram herbis & arboribus pulcherrimè fore exornatam.

Resp. 1. Iodocus Coccius part. 2. Thesauri lib. 19. art. 2. p. 1047. hanc Ambrosii Catharini sententiam recenset inter errores. 2. Bellarminus lib. 6. de amiss. gratiae & statu pecc. cap. 2. longè aliam novae illius terrae faciem describit. Omninò credibile est, inquit, post ultimi iudicii diem Elementum aquae ad locum suum naturalem esse rediturum, totamque terram undique cooperturum: nam ut Theologi Doctores communi consensu docent, post diem iudicii nullae erunt plantae, nulla animalia, nulla corpora mixta hominibus duntaxat exceptis. Quare cùm aquae ab initio mundi totam ambiret terram, ut Natura eius postulare videbatur, ac deinde iussu Dei in unum locum congregata fuerit, ut esset locus in terra generationi plantarum & animalium, certè generatione ista sublatâ ratio ipsa & Natura rerum postulat, ut aqua ad locum pristinum revertatur, proinde locus infantum sine Baptismo decedentium non alius erit, quàm infernus. 3. Cornelius à Lapide in comm. h. l. Apost. Catharinum & Salmeronem ex professo refellit. Catharinus, inquit, & Salmeron censent, pueros (non baptizatos) futuros in terra, quasi in quodam Paradiso terrestri, ideoque perficiendos in cognitione naturali, ut Philosophos omnes superent &c. sed falluntur, dum eos censent fore beatos beatitudine naturali, cùm enim damnandi sint poenâ damni, licet non sensus, puta carentiâ divinae visionis beatifica &c. damnati dicendi potiùs sunt, quàm beati. caeteroqui probabile est, eos in terra vitam commodam acturos, nam limbus puerorum eorum corpora, quae resument in die iudicii, non capiet. 4. Ante illos omnes Thomas in Additam. q. 91. art. 5. sic distinxit. Plantae & animalia sunt de perfectione universi secundùm statum istum mutabilitatis, non secundùm statum novitatis. 5. Falsa est hypothesis, quòd Infantes non baptizati in loco quodam terrio extra caelum & infernum sint futuri, quam opinionem in Pelagianis iam olim Ecclesia improbavit. 6. Quale futurum sit novum illud caelum ac nova ista terra, sacra Scriptura non exprimit, neque nobis in hac vita est scitu necessarium, ideò caelorum secreta curiosiùs scrutari vereamur.

6. Estius ad v. 14. sic commentatur. Infert Apostolus ex mundi renovatione, quem futurum dixit habitaculum iustorum, ita vivendum esse, ut in eum à Christo recipi mereamur. Resp. 1. Bona opera piorum non esse vitae aeternae meritoria, nomine meriti propriè & strictè accepto, suo loco demonstratur. 2. Nec Petrus ullius meriti hoc loco mentionem facit, sed hoc à piis requirit, ut solicitè studeant immaculati coram Christo iudice inveniri, nimirùm, quia fides exerit se per bona opera, & per peccata contra conscientiam excutitur.

Observationes. 1. Qui promissionibus divinis fidem habet, habere autem omnes debent, novos caelos, ac novam terram creandam esse, dubitare minimè poterit.

2. Qualis verò futurus sit novus ille mundus, illud in hac vita hominem arbitramur scire posse neminem. 1. Cor. 2. v. 9.Oculus non vidit &c. in quem locum Augustinus Epist. ad Dioscorum pulcherrimè sic commentatur. Oculus non vidit, quia non est color; nec auris audivit, quia non est sonus: nec in cor hominis ascendit, quia cor hominis debet illuc ascendere. Fide non capitur, quod DEUS promittit; spe non attingitur, caritate non comprehenditur, defideria & vota transgreditur; acquiri potest, aestimari non potest.

3. Spe novi illius mundi, in quo perfecta iustitia, & perpetua laetitia habitabit, erigamus nos adversùs omnes huius mundi miserias. Fideles tot aerumnis & mortibus in hac vita exagitati cogitantes revirescentes veteris mundi in novis caelis & nova terra exuvias, meminerint, sanctis pariter damna fugientis vitae in immortalitatis lucra converti, ac cum novis caelis novum expectent corpus glorificatum.

4. In hac vita omnis piorum iustitia est imperfecta & immunda, instar panni mulieris menstruataeEsa. 64. v. 6. & habitualis & actualis iustitia procul à perfectione abest, sed in vita aeterna electorum iustitia erit consummata. In caelis his ce nostris habitat misericordia, tolerans peccatores, in caelis verò novis habitabit iustitia, quae non admittet quidquam coinquinatum.

5. Beda ad h. l. sic annotat. Iustitia habitat in futuro seculo, quia tunc cuique fidelium pro modo sui certaminis reddetur corona iustitiae, quod in hac vita nequaquam fieri potest &c. Supra Solem sunt mansiones, in quibus iusti debita suae iustitiae praemia percipient. Potest & hoc, quod ait, in quibus iustitia habitat, etiam iuxta illud Psalmistae intelligi. Haec porta Domini, iusti intrabunt per eam. Et in Apocalypsi de civitate superna Iohannes. Non intrabit in eam aliquid coinquinatum.

6. Sicut Petrus ex doctrina de novi caeli & novae terrae creatione deducit exhortationem ad studium sanctitatis: sic omnia in Theologia ad praxin sunt dirigenda. Matth. 7. v. 21.Luc. 6. v. 46.Ioh. 13. v. 17. Iustinus in paraen. p. 25. Non in verbis, sed in factis res nostrae religionis consistunt. Augustinus lib. 1. de doctr. Christi. cap. 4. Universa Theologia eò ordinatur, ut DEO fruamur.

7. Verè piorum est, summo studio in id incumbere, ut conspectu Christi iudicis immaculati inveniantur. Basilius in comm. Psal. 33.Beatus, qui in die iudicii, quando venerit Dominus ad illuminandum abscondita tenebrarum, & manifestare consilia cordium, ausus erit sub luce illa redargutionum consistere, intrepidusque ac sine verecundia conscientiam incontaminatam, ac à vitiis liberam prae se feret? Augustinus in Soliloq. cap. 14. Magna nobis est indita necessitas iustè, rectèque vivendi, qui cuncta facimus ante oculos iudicis cuncta cernentis.

8. Beda ad hunc v. 14. sic annotat. Hae sunt vigiliae sanctae, de quibus Dominus ait. Beati servi illi, quos, cùm venerit Dominus, invenerit vigilantes. Vigilat namque, qui se à sordibus vitiorum immunem custodit, qui quantum in se est, cum omnibus pacem habet, qui in seipso pace felicissimâ utens omnes carnis illecebras Spiritus regimini subdit.

9. Immaculati & in pace in die iudicii invenientur, non qui nunquam peccaverunt, sed qui seriam de peccatis paenitentiam egerunt, quibus propter Christum verâ fide apprehensum peccata dimissa, qui DEO reconciliati ac fidem suam per caritatem, studium bonorum operum & fraternam concordiam demonstrârunt.

10. Pii non debent taedio affici ob diuturnam adventûs Dominici dilationem, sed in ea multorum salutem positam arbitrari; multò verò minùs cum servo malo in corde suo dicere debent, tardat Dominus meus venire, propterea in conservos iniurius esse, & genio indulgere cupio.Matth. 24. v. 47. & 48.

11. Gratâ mente agnoscendum & praedicandum, quod DEI longanimitas homines invitat ad paenitentiam.Rom. 2. v. 4.

## 3:14-15
Connection. He repeats the previous exhortation, and animates those to whom he writes both to the pursuit of piety and to patient hope.

Exposition of the text. Διὸ, ἀγαπητοὶ, ταῦτα προσδοκῶντες σπουδάσατε ἀσπιλοι καὶ ἄμωμοι αὐτῷ εὑρεθῆναι ἐν εἰρήνῃ. Vulg. Wherefore, dearly beloved, waiting for these things, be diligent that you may be found undefiled and unspotted in peace. Διό wherefore, therefore. Just as the Apostle had deduced an exhortation to the pursuit of piety and holiness from the prediction concerning the destruction of heaven and earth v. 11., so also he elicits a similar exhortation from the promise concerning the creation of a new heaven and a new earth. Because righteousness dwells in the new heaven and new earth, and access to this new dwelling is open only to the righteous and undefiled, therefore it is fitting to strive that we may be found undefiled before him.

Ἀγαπητοί. The Vulgate rendered dearly beloved. In the Greek it is beloved.

By ταῦτα he understands not only the new heavens and the new earth, but also the final coming of Christ, as appears both from the preceding v. 12. προσδοκῶντες καί σπεύδοντας τὴν παρούσιαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας, and from the words following in this very verse, to be found by him undefiled.

Προσδοκῶντες Luther rendered, Dieweil ihr darauff warren sollet. But in the Greek it is simply, because you expect these things.

Σπουδάσατε properly signifies give effort, strive, expend study and diligent effort upon it. chap. 1. of this Epist. vers. 10. & 15. The Syriac rendered [יפצו] be solicitous, have care for this matter. The root is [יצף] which the paraphrast sometimes uses for μεριμνᾶν Luke 10. vers. 41. 1. Cor. 7. v. 33. προνοεῖσθαι 2. Cor. 8. v. 21. ἐπιμελεῖσθαι Luke 10. v. 35. which all have the meaning of study and solicitude.

Ἄσπιλοι καὶ ἄμωμοι. Some Greek Codices read ἀμώμητοι, but without variation of sense. Just as ἄσπιλοι are those who lack σπίλοις; so ἄμωμοι are those who lack μώμοις. The Vulgate rendered less conveniently, unspotted; it is more correctly rendered undefiled, without stain and spot, and by consequence, irreprehensible. Such are called in the Scriptures those who live εὐσεβῶς, σωφρόνως καὶ δικαίως, Tit. 2. v. 12. who are from sins against conscience. they take heed to themselves, and whose life, as being free from stain, incurs no just reproach. 1. Tim. 6. vers. 14. they are joined ἄσπιλοι καὶ ἀνεπίληπτοι. Iac. 1. v. 27. pure and undefiled religion is called, to keep himself ἄσπιλον unspotted from this world 1. Petr. 1. v. 19. Christ is called a lamb ἄσπιλος καὶ ἄμωμος. Eph. 1. v. 4. cap. 5. v. 27. they are joined ἅγιοι καὶ ἄμωμοι Col. 1. v. 22. ἄμωμοι καί ἀνέγκλητοι The LXX use the word ἄμωμος for צדיק just Prov. 20. v. 7. but especially for תם and תמים whole, perfect, innocent, irreproachable Exod. 29. v. 2. Lev. 1. v. 3. etc. which they otherwise call τέλειον, ὅσιον, ἄκακον, ἄμεμπτον etc. Moreover, the Apostle in these epithets looks back to verse 13 of the preceding chapter, where he had called the false teachers, covered in every kind of wickedness, σπίλους καὶ μώμους, and to verse 10, where he had made mention of τῶν μιασμάτων τοῦ κόσμου, so that the sense may be: Do not give empty ears to ἐμπαίκταις who are perpetually repeating: Where is the promise of his coming? But with perpetual vigilance of faith, expecting the coming of Christ to judgment and the new heavens and the new earth at every moment, apply yourselves solicitously to this, that you may keep yourselves unspotted and harmless from the pollutions of the world, and may be found irreproachable before the judge who is to come.

The pronoun αὐτῷ has respect to Christ the judge, of whose coming the Apostle treated v. 12. and there is great emphasis in it. That judge, whose coming you expect, is just, therefore you ought to be zealous for justice; he is omniscient, he will bring even the most hidden things to light, therefore you ought to apply yourselves to this, that you may be found unspotted before him; he will render to everyone according to his works, therefore it ought to be your care that you be found fruitful in good works. Some render the Dative αὐτῷ as by him. But it is rendered more elegantly as before him, as appears from the parallel passage Luc. 21. v. 36. Watch at all times, praying, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of man, in which way also Luther rendered it in this place, Daß ihr für ihm unbefleckt und unsträflich erfunden werdet. Bede in his commentary on this place: Well, when he said: Be diligent to be found unspotted and inviolate, he added to him, that is, to the Lord, because he alone is perfectly clean, whence it is said in the praise of good spouses: They were both just before God. Well before God, because human judgments deceive. Interlinear Gloss: to him, that is, by him or to the honor of him coming and knocking.

John Huss in this place To Him, namely, to God the judge, not only to man, who only looks at those things which appear outwardly.

Ἐν εἰρήνῃ. Some refer this προσδιορισμὸν to the participle προσδοκῶντες, so that the sense may be, that they ought to await the coming of Christ with a quiet and undisturbed mind. Some to the noun ἀμώμητοι, so that the sense may be, that they ought to be found in peace, immaculate and irreprehensible, for not every peace is praiseworthy. But it is more correctly referred to the nearest verb, to which it is also joined, namely to the verb εὑρεθῆναι, so that the sense may be, that at the time of the final coming of Christ to judgment they ought to be found in peace; that they ought to strive that Christ, coming, may find them peaceful and pacified. There are those who think ἐν εἰρήνῃ is placed in the Hebrew phrase for μετ' εἰρήνης, but the proper meaning of the preposition ἐν can also be retained.

Καὶ τὴν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν μακροθυμίαν σωτηρίαν ἡγεῖσθε. Vulgate And account the long-suffering of our Lord as salvation. In the Greek εἶναι. must be understood Account the long-suffering of our Lord to be your salvation, i.e., to look to your salvation, to conduce to your salvation. The abstract could also be taken for the concrete, the substantive for the adjective, placed according to the customary Hebraism. Firmly establish that that long-suffering of your Lord, by which He delays His coming and does not immediately present Himself for judgment, is salutary for men, because, namely, the time of repentance is granted to them through this delay of the coming. v. 9. By the same phrase 2. Cor. 7. v. 10. μετάνοια εἰς σωτηρίαν is called μετάνοια σωτήριος salutary repentance. The Syrian in this place rendered it by [פורקנא] which signifies redemption, liberation, and salvation. Concerning the verb ἡγεῖσθε it is to be noted that in this place it signifies a certain persuasion of mind, in which sense it is also used Acts 26. v. 2.2. Cor. 9. v. 5.Phil. 2. v. 25.chap. 3. v. 8.1. Tim. 1. v. 12.

Latin:

Connexio. Exhortationem superiorem repetit, ac tùm ad studium pietatis, tùm ad patientem spem eos, ad quos scribit, animat.

Textus expositio. Διὸ, ἀγαπητοὶ, ταῦτα προσδοκῶντες σπουδάσατε ἀσπιλοι καὶ ἄμωμοι αὐτῷ εὑρεθῆναι ἐν εἰρήνῃ. Vulg. Propter quod, carissimi, haec expectantes satagite immaculati & inviolati ei inveniri in in pace.Διόpropter quod, propterea. Sicut ex praedictione de caeli ac terrae destructione deduxerat Apostolus exhortationem ad studium pietatis & sanctitatis v. 11. ita quoque ex promissione de novi caeli ac novae terrae creatione similem exhortationem elicit. Quia in novo caelo ac nova terra iustitia habitat, ac non nisi iustis & immaculatis ad novum hoc domicilium patet ingressus, ideò studere convenit, ut immaculati coram ipso inveniamur.

Ἀγαπητοί. Vulg. reddidit carissimi. In Graeco est dilecti.

Per ταῦτα intelligit non solùm novos caelos & novam terram, sed etiam novissimum Christi adventum, ut apparet tùm ex v. praeced. 12.προσδοκῶντες καί σπεύδοντας τὴν παρούσιαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας, tùm ex verbis sequentibus in hoc ipso versiculo, inveniri ipsi immaculati.

Προσδοκῶντες Lutherus reddidit, Dieweil ihr darauff warren sollet. Sed in Graeco est simpliciter, quia haec expectatis.

Σπουδάσατε propriè significat operam date, studete, studium & operam sedulam in id impendite.cap. 1. huius Epist. vers. 10. & 15. Syrus reddidit [יפצו]soliciti estote, curam huius rei habete. Radix est [יצף] quâ aliàs utitur paraphrastes pro μεριμνᾶνLuc. 10. vers. 41.1. Cor. 7. v. 33.προνοεῖσθαι2. Cor. 8. v. 21.ἐπιμελεῖσθαιLuc. 10. v. 35. quae omnia studii & solicitudinis significationem habent.

Ἄσπιλοι καὶ ἄμωμοι. Quidam Codd. Graeci legunt ἀμώμητοι, sed sine sensus variatione. Sicut ἄσπιλοι sunt, qui carent σπίλοις; sic ἄμωμοι sunt, qui carent μώμοις. Vulg. minùs commodè reddidit, inviolati; rectiùs redditur immaculati, sine labe & macula, & ex conseq. irreprehensibiles.
